issue_title: General MPS op coverage tracking issue
requirement: **Requirement: Maintain a Consolidated, Current Operator Coverage Tracker for the MPS Backend**  The project shall provide and maintain a single, authoritative tracking artifact that records the implementation status of every ATen operator supported by the MPS (Metal Performance Shaders) backend, so that users and contributors can determine which operations run natively on MPS, which fall back to CPU, and which are unsupported.  The tracker shall:  1. **List all operators** in the ATen operator set, including operator overloads where behavior differs, and identify each by its canonical name. 2. **Report per-operator status** using a defined set of values: `Implemented`, `Partially Implemented`, `CPU Fallback`, `Not Implemented`, and `Not Applicable`. 3. **Report supported data types** for each implemented operator (e.g., float32, float16, bfloat16, int32, int64, bool, complex types) and note any dtype-specific limitations. 4. **Link each entry** to its relevant implementation pull request, source file, and open issues describing known bugs or limitations. 5. **Record the minimum required platform or OS version** where an operator's behavior depends on it. 6. **Be generated or validated automatically** from the source registration of MPS kernels where feasible, so that the tracker cannot silently drift from the codebase. 7. **Be updated as part of the pull request process** for any change that adds, removes, or modifies MPS operator support, enforced through a CI check or contributor checklist item. 8. **Indicate the fallback behavior** of unimplemented operators, including whether the `PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK` (or equivalent) setting is required for execution to proceed. 9. **Be publicly accessible** from the project documentation and the MPS backend issue tracker, with a stated date or revision of last update. 10. **Provide a summary view** with counts of operators in each status category, updated with each revision.  Acceptance criteria: - Every operator registered for the MPS dispatch key appears in the tracker with a valid status. - A CI job fails if an MPS operator registration is added or removed without a corresponding tracker update. - The tracker is linked from the MPS backend documentation and from this tracking issue. - Users can identify, for any given ATen operator, whether it runs natively on MPS, falls back to CPU, or is unsupported, within one lookup.

issue_title: General MPS op coverage tracking issue
requirement: **Requirement Title:** MPS Backend Operator Coverage Tracking  **Problem Statement:** The MPS (Metal Performance Shaders) backend does not implement every operator available in the CPU and CUDA backends, and there is no centralized, up-to-date mechanism to track which operators are supported, partially supported, or unsupported. This makes it difficult to prioritize implementation work, measure progress, and communicate backend support status to users and contributors.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. The system shall provide a single, canonical tracking artifact that enumerates all public PyTorch operators and records their support status on the MPS backend, classified as: natively supported, supported via fallback/decomposition, unsupported, or not applicable. 2. The tracking artifact shall group operators by module category (e.g., `torch`, `torch.nn`, `torch.linalg`, `torch.special`, `torch.Tensor` methods) to enable targeted browsing and triage. 3. Each unsupported operator entry shall be individually actionable, allowing contributors to claim, implement, and reference the corresponding entry in associated pull requests. 4. The tracking artifact shall be regenerable from the current codebase state (e.g., derived from op registration data or test coverage results) so that it remains synchronized with the code and does not rely solely on manual updates. 5. An operator shall be marked as supported only if it produces results consistent with the CPU reference implementation, verified via the existing MPS backend test suites (e.g., OpInfo-based consistency tests with accepted tolerances). 6. The tracking mechanism shall support measurable progress reporting, including an overall coverage percentage and per-category coverage counts, updated as operators are implemented. 7. The tracking artifact shall be publicly visible in the project repository so that both maintainers and external contributors can consult and update it.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - A single source-of-truth listing exists that enumerates all PyTorch operators with their current MPS support status. - The listing can be regenerated from the codebase to reflect the current state without manual reconciliation. - Unsupported operators are clearly identifiable and linkable for implementation work. - Coverage status and percentage can be recomputed after each implementation change and remain consistent with test results. - The tracking process is documented such that new contributors can determine which operators remain unimplemented and how to add support for them.

Specifically:  1. **Hardware Detection:** The system shall automatically detect the presence and capabilities of the Apple Neural Engine (ANE) on ARM-based Mac devices at runtime.  2. **Execution Support:** When a compatible ANE is available, the system shall route supported operations (e.g., convolutions, matrix multiplications, activations) to the Neural Engine, falling back gracefully to GPU (Metal) or CPU execution for unsupported operations.  3. **Configuration:** The system shall provide a configuration option allowing users to explicitly enable, disable, or set preference levels for Neural Engine execution (e.g., `ANE_PREFERRED`, `ANE_ONLY`, `CPU_ONLY`).  4. **Performance:** On supported workloads, execution on the 16-core Neural Engine shall not degrade model accuracy relative to CPU/GPU execution, and shall reduce inference latency and energy consumption compared to CPU-only execution.  5. **Compatibility:** The feature shall support macOS 11.0 (Big Sur) and later on ARM64 (Apple Silicon) architecture, and shall be a no-op (with appropriate logging) on Intel-based Macs or platforms lacking a Neural Engine.  6. **Diagnostics:** The system shall expose diagnostics or logging indicating when the Neural Engine is actively being used, including the portion of the model offloaded to the ANE.

issue_title: General MPS op coverage tracking issue
requirement: ## Requirement: MPS Op Coverage Tracking  **Background** The MPS backend supports only a subset of the framework's operators. Today there is no single, authoritative view of which ops are implemented, which are missing, and how well each is tested, so gaps are discovered ad hoc (user reports, failing tests) and coverage silently regresses over time.  **Requirement** The project shall maintain a machine-readable and human-readable inventory ("op coverage table") of all framework operators with respect to the MPS backend, and shall treat the inventory as a first-class, continuously validated artifact.  Specifically:  1. **Inventory of ops**    - The coverage table shall enumerate every operator in the framework's public operator set (including operators added after the table was created) and record, for each op, whether it is: implemented on MPS, intentionally unsupported (with a documented reason and any fallback/error behavior), or pending implementation.    - Each entry shall link to the implementing source file and, where applicable, to the upstream issue tracking its implementation.  2. **Completeness checks in CI**    - A CI job shall run on every change to the operator registry and shall fail if a newly added op is absent from the coverage table.    - The same job shall fail if the table's declared implementation status for an op disagrees with the actual backend dispatch (i.e., the table claims an op is implemented but no MPS kernel/dispatch entry exists, or claims it is unsupported while a dispatch entry exists).  3. **Test coverage linkage**    - Each op marked as implemented shall be linked to at least one test that executes on the MPS device; the CI job shall verify this linkage and report ops that lack MPS-side test coverage.    - Tests that are skipped or xfailed on MPS shall be recorded explicitly in the table together with the reason for the skip.  4. **Backward compatibility and regression detection**    - Changes that remove or disable an op previously marked as implemented on MPS shall be detected and surfaced (as a CI failure or an explicitly approved table update) so that coverage regressions cannot occur unnoticed.  5. **Reporting**    - CI output shall publish a coverage summary (counts and percentages of implemented, unsupported, pending, and tested ops) as a build artifact, and the summary shall be surfaced in the pull request that changed coverage.    - The table and summary shall be reproducible from a single, documented command so contributors can check coverage locally before opening a pull request.  6. **Maintenance**    - The coverage table shall live in the repository in a documented format, with instructions for adding a new op, updating an existing op's status, and annotating a test as an MPS skip.    - Any op intentionally left unsupported on MPS shall document the expected error message or fallback path so behavior is consistent and user-visible.  **Acceptance criteria** - A single documented command regenerates/validates the coverage table and prints the coverage summary. - CI fails on: new op missing from the table, table status mismatching backend dispatch, implemented op with no linked MPS test, and removal of previously implemented op support without an explicit table update. - A coverage summary artifact is produced for every build. - The table includes, for every op, its implementation status, implementation location, linked issue (if unsupported/pending), and linked MPS test (if implemented).

Tensor operations shall infer output shapes and reject incompatible shapes, ranks, axes, or broadcasting rules with clear diagnostics identifying the operation and offending dimensions. issue_title: [FYI] NestedTensor Project Progress

issue_title: [Poll] Support DistributedDataParallel (DDP) in PyTorch C++ API (libtorch)
requirement: The LibTorch C++ API shall provide first-class DistributedDataParallel (DDP) support equivalent to Python’s `torch.nn.parallel.DistributedDataParallel`, allowing C++ users to wrap `torch::nn::Module` instances and perform multi-process, multi-device training with automatic gradient synchronization over an initialized process group. The API shall support standard DDP configuration options such as device IDs, output device, buffer broadcasting, unused-parameter detection, and gradient/bucket behavior where applicable; integrate with existing C++ optimizers and autograd; support common backends such as Gloo and NCCL; and include documentation and examples demonstrating multi-process C++ training.

issue_title: [Proposal] Data reading framework for PyTorch (Hive, MySQL, S3 etc.)

issue_title: [RFC] PT2-Friendly Traceable, Functional Collective Communication APIs
requirement: The project shall provide PT2-friendly collective communication APIs that are functional and traceable, enabling distributed collective operations such as all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, broadcast, and send/receive to be expressed as pure functions with explicit inputs and outputs that can be captured by PyTorch 2 tracing and compilation (e.g., torch.compile and torch.export) without graph breaks, while preserving correct distributed semantics and supporting autograd where applicable.

issue_title: [RFC] TorchStore - A Shared-Memory Tensor Store
requirement: TorchStore shall provide a shared-memory tensor store that enables multiple processes on the same host to create, store, retrieve, and share PyTorch tensors without copying tensor data, with safe lifetime management and cleanup of shared-memory segments.

issue_title: Feature request: INT4 format support
requirement: The system shall support the INT4 data format, enabling 4-bit integer tensors/values to be created, loaded, stored, converted, and processed through the relevant APIs and execution paths with correct numerical behavior and interoperability with existing supported formats.

issue_title: [RFC] RPC Based Distributed Model Parallel
requirement: Provide an RPC-based distributed model parallel capability that allows a model to be partitioned across multiple processes or machines, supports remote forward and backward execution through RPC, enables distributed autograd for cross-worker gradient propagation, and integrates a distributed optimizer for parameter updates, so that models exceeding single-device memory can be trained efficiently.

issue_title: DataLoader with option to re-use worker processes
requirement: The DataLoader shall provide an opt-in option to reuse its worker processes across epochs/iterations, avoiding the overhead of spawning and terminating workers each time. When enabled, worker processes shall remain alive between iterations and be cleanly shut down when the DataLoader is destroyed or the option is disabled. The default behavior shall remain unchanged.

issue_title: Zero-copy on shared memory of NVIDIA Jetson devices
requirement: The software shall support zero-copy access to data in shared memory on NVIDIA Jetson devices, enabling CPU and GPU components to use the same buffers without explicit memory copies while preserving correctness and existing behavior on non-Jetson platforms.

issue_title: Return attention weights in nn.Transformer
requirement: The PyTorch `nn.Transformer` module and its encoder/decoder components shall support an optional mode that returns the attention weights computed by each attention layer in addition to their normal outputs. This mode shall expose per-layer attention weights with documented shapes, support optional head averaging consistent with `nn.MultiheadAttention`, preserve existing behavior when disabled, and maintain backward compatibility.

issue_title: non-negative least squares solver feature request
requirement: The system shall provide a non-negative least squares (NNLS) solver for real-valued linear systems. Given an \(m \times n\) matrix \(A\) and an \(m\)-dimensional vector \(b\), the solver shall compute an \(n\)-dimensional vector \(x\) that minimizes the Euclidean norm \(\|Ax - b\|_2\) subject to the constraint \(x \ge 0\). The solver shall support overdetermined, underdetermined, and rank-deficient systems, and shall return the solution vector, the residual norm, and a convergence status. It shall accept user-configurable convergence tolerance and maximum iteration count, and shall reject inputs with incompatible dimensions or non-finite values by returning a clear error.

issue_title: Code Push / Hot Update / out of band updates
requirement: The system shall support code push / hot update / out-of-band update delivery, enabling application code and bundled assets to be updated on deployed clients without requiring a full release or app-store update, while preserving version compatibility and allowing rollback to a previous known-good version.

issue_title: Implement `numpy.random.choice` equivalent
requirement: The software shall implement a random sampling function equivalent to `numpy.random.choice(a, size=None, replace=True, p=None)`. It shall accept a one-dimensional array-like population or an integer `a` (treated as `numpy.arange(a)`), sample uniformly by default, and support optional non-uniform probabilities `p` that match the population length, are non-negative, and sum to 1 within numerical tolerance. It shall return a single element when `size is None`, otherwise an array of the requested integer or tuple shape. Sampling with replacement shall be the default; with `replace=False`, each population element may be selected at most once and an error shall be raised if the requested sample size exceeds the population size. Invalid inputs—such as an empty population, negative size, length-mismatched or invalid `p`, or impossible no-replacement requests—shall raise errors consistent with `numpy.random.choice`.

issue_title: Feature Request: Easier to extend base RNN implementation
requirement: The base RNN implementation shall be refactored to provide well-defined extension points, enabling developers to implement custom RNN variants by subclassing the base class and overriding only the cell-specific computation, while the base class retains responsibility for shared sequence iteration, state management, and output handling.

issue_title: Improve the indexability (SEO) of Flutter apps on the web
requirement: Flutter web builds shall emit crawlable, semantically meaningful HTML for app content—including text, headings, links, route-specific titles/descriptions, and canonical URLs—so search engine crawlers can discover and index Flutter web applications, including crawlers that do not execute JavaScript, without breaking Flutter’s rendering or interactivity.

issue_title: Implement PlatformView support on Windows
