Given an unreachable or rejecting license server, when the app initializes the controller, a descriptive error is delivered through the controller's error listener within a bounded timeout. - Given a DRM type unsupported on the current platform, when the app initializes the controller, initialization fails with an explicit "unsupported DRM scheme" error. - Given a non-DRM media URL, when the app initializes the controller without DRM configuration, playback behaves exactly as before this feature.

issue_title: Apple CarPlay / Android Auto support?
requirement: The application shall provide Apple CarPlay and Android Auto support, enabling users to launch and use the application’s core functionality from a compatible vehicle infotainment display. The integration shall: - Expose the app in the CarPlay home screen and Android Auto launcher when a compatible iPhone or Android phone is connected. - Support platform-approved input methods, including touchscreen, rotary controller, hardware buttons, and voice assistant where available. - Enforce Apple and Google driver-distraction guidelines by restricting complex or text-heavy interactions while the vehicle is in motion. - Handle connection, disconnection, and reconnection automatically without data loss or crashes. - Comply with current Apple CarPlay and Android Auto design, technical, and review requirements.

issue_title: Support soft hyphenation (line breaks at U+00AD plus rendering a hyphen at the end of the line)
requirement: **Requirement: Soft Hyphen (U+00AD) Line Breaking and Rendering**  The text layout and rendering system shall treat U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN as a conditional hyphenation point. U+00AD shall be invisible and zero-width when no line break occurs at its position. The line-breaking algorithm shall consider a U+00AD position as a valid break opportunity when the line cannot fit without breaking. If a line break is made at a U+00AD position, the system shall render a visible hyphen glyph at the end of the line before the break and shall not render U+00AD at the start of the next line. If no line break is made at U+00AD, the system shall not render a hyphen or any other visible glyph for that character. The visible hyphen glyph shall be the configured hyphenation glyph, defaulting to U+2010 HYPHEN, with U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS as a fallback when U+2010 is unavailable.  Acceptance Criteria: - A string containing U+00AD rendered on a line that fits without breaking displays no visible hyphen and no visible U+00AD. - A string containing U+00AD rendered on a line that must break at the U+00AD position displays a hyphen at the end of the preceding line and continues the text on the next line without a leading U+00AD. - U+00AD does not cause a line break when the line fits without breaking. - The hyphenation behavior is consistent across all supported text rendering paths.

issue_title: Add structs in GDScript
requirement: GDScript shall support user-defined structs as first-class value types. A struct declaration shall use the `struct` keyword and define a named type with typed fields, optional default values, and optional methods and constructors. Struct instances shall use value semantics: assignment, argument passing, and return values copy the instance; `==` and `!=` compare fields by value; mutating a copy shall not affect the original. Structs shall be usable as static type hints, in `is` and `as` expressions, in typed arrays and dictionaries, in signals, and in `@export` properties with serialization of their fields. Structs may be nested within scripts or classes and referenced across scripts. Structs shall not support inheritance, `extends`, or polymorphic substitution. The feature shall preserve existing GDScript syntax and behavior except that `struct` becomes a reserved keyword.

issue_title: Allow release mode builds to run on simulators
requirement: # Requirement: Release-Mode Builds on Simulators  ## Summary The build and run tooling SHALL support building and launching mobile applications in release mode on simulator/emulator targets, in addition to the currently supported debug and profile modes.  ## Motivation Release-mode behavior (optimized code, tree-shaking, disabled assertions, release-only configuration and error handling) often differs materially from debug-mode behavior. Developers currently cannot validate release-mode behavior without a physical device, which slows down diagnosis of release-only defects (e.g., rendering, performance, plugin, and networking issues) and increases reliance on CI or device hardware.  ## Functional Requirements  1. **Mode–Target Compatibility**    - The toolchain SHALL treat release mode as a valid build mode for simulator and emulator targets.    - Invoking a run/build command with release mode and a simulator target SHALL NOT fail with a "release mode not supported for simulators" error.  2. **Artifact Generation**    - The build pipeline SHALL produce a release-mode application bundle that is installable and launchable on the target simulator/emulator.    - Where the target architecture cannot support the standard release compilation strategy, the pipeline SHALL select an appropriate supported compilation strategy and document which optimizer/compilation configurations are unavailable.  3. **Runtime Semantics**    - A release-mode simulator build SHALL exhibit release-mode semantics: assertion checks disabled, debug-only instrumentation absent, debug banners absent, and optimization-level behavior consistent with release builds on physical devices.    - Any semantic differences that cannot be reproduced on simulators SHALL be reported to the user before or during the run, identifying the affected capabilities.  4. **Configuration**    - Release-mode-specific configuration, entry points, and environment definitions (e.g., release flavor/variant settings) SHALL be applied identically on simulator targets as on device targets, except where explicitly unsupported.  5. **User Feedback**    - If a requested release-mode simulator build cannot proceed (unsupported host, simulator runtime, or dependency constraint), the tooling SHALL fail with a clear, actionable message stating the specific unsupported element and the recommended alternative.    - Where a release-mode simulator build succeeds but with degraded fidelity relative to device release builds, the tooling SHALL emit a non-fatal notice enumerating the differences.  6. **Diagnostics**    - Release-mode simulator runs SHALL support the standard attach/detach, structured logging, and crash/stack-trace symbolication paths available for device release builds, to the extent the platform permits.  ## Non-Functional Requirements  - **Performance:** Release-mode simulator builds SHALL reflect the optimizations applicable to the selected compilation strategy; documented performance characteristics SHALL be published where they diverge from device release builds. - **Compatibility:** Existing debug and profile simulator workflows, and existing release-mode device workflows, SHALL remain unaffected. - **Documentation:** User-facing documentation SHALL state supported mode/target combinations and any known fidelity gaps for release-mode simulator builds.  ## Acceptance Criteria  1. Running the application on an iOS Simulator in release mode completes successfully and launches the app. 2. Running the application on an Android Emulator in release mode completes successfully and launches the app. 3. The launched release-mode simulator build reports release mode, with assertions disabled and debug-only UI elements absent. 4. A failure case (unsupported configuration) produces a message identifying the specific unsupported element. 5. Debug and profile simulator builds, and release device builds, continue to behave as before.  ## Out of Scope  - Changes to platform vendor simulator/emulator limitations that are outside the project's control. - Guaranteeing bit-for-bit identical behavior or performance between simulator release builds and device release builds.

issue_title: [path_provider] Add support for web
requirement: **Requirement: Web Platform Support for path_provider**  The `path_provider` plugin shall add first-class support for the Flutter web platform through an endorsed federated implementation that is automatically registered when the application runs on web. The plugin shall provide a web-compatible public API that compiles and runs without `dart:io`, while preserving existing source compatibility and runtime behavior on Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, and Windows. On web, the plugin shall expose non-empty, stable, per-origin storage locations for the temporary, application support, and application documents directories, backed by browser storage such as the Origin Private File System (OPFS) or IndexedDB. Methods that have no meaningful web equivalent—`getLibraryDirectory`, `getDownloadsDirectory`, `getExternalStorageDirectory`, `getExternalCacheDirectories`, and `getExternalStorageDirectories`—shall throw `UnsupportedError` with a descriptive message. Documentation shall specify supported methods, storage locations, persistence semantics, and unsupported methods. Automated tests shall verify web compilation, supported getters, unsupported getter errors, and non-web regression.  **Acceptance Criteria** 1. A Flutter web application can depend on `path_provider` and compile without errors related to unavailable `dart:io` APIs. 2. On web, supported getters return non-empty, per-origin path strings or URIs that can be used with browser file system APIs. 3. Unsupported getters throw `UnsupportedError` with a clear message. 4. Non-web platforms return the same values and types as before. 5. Documentation and tests are updated to cover web support.

issue_title: AVIF codec support
requirement: The software shall add AVIF (AV1 Image File Format) codec support so users can read, display, process, and write AVIF images through existing application workflows. The implementation shall: - detect AVIF files by `.avif` extension and `image/avif` MIME type; - decode still AVIF images and animated AVIF sequences when the application supports animation; - preserve alpha transparency, ICC color profiles, and Exif/XMP metadata where the application’s data model supports them; - encode/export AVIF images with lossy and lossless options and configurable quality; - handle unsupported AVIF profiles or missing codec dependencies with a clear user-facing error and no crash; - include automated tests with representative AVIF fixtures for decoding, encoding, metadata, alpha, animation, and error handling.  Acceptance criteria: AVIF files load and render correctly; exported AVIF files are valid and readable by standard AVIF-compatible software; existing image-format behavior is not regressed.

issue_title: Add public/private access modifiers to GDScript and autocompletion improvements
requirement: GDScript shall implement `public` and `private` access modifiers for all class members (including variables, constants, functions, and signals), with `public` as the default access level when no modifier is specified. The static analyzer shall enforce access control by raising an error when a `private` member is accessed from outside its declaring class. Additionally, the code editor's autocompletion system shall be enhanced to respect these access modifiers, ensuring that only accessible members are suggested based on the current scope (i.e., `private` members are suggested only within the declaring class).

issue_title: Add union types to Typed GDScript
requirement: Typed GDScript shall support union types in static type annotations using `|` between two or more types, e.g. `var value: int | String` and `func f(x: Node | Resource) -> int | String`. A value shall be assignable to a union type when it is assignable to at least one member type. Union types shall be supported in variable, parameter, return, signal, property, and nested generic annotations; shall integrate with type inference, autocomplete, type hints, member access, method calls, and existing `is`-based narrowing rules; shall normalize duplicate and nested unions; and shall produce clear diagnostics for malformed or unsupported unions. The feature shall preserve existing runtime behavior for valid code and include documentation and automated tests covering parsing, type checking, inference, narrowing, error cases, and backward compatibility.

issue_title: [Desktop] - Splash screen or background color customization
requirement: Requirement: The desktop application shall allow users to customize the splash screen background color and/or the main application background color. The application shall provide this option in Settings/Preferences, offer predefined colors plus custom HEX/RGB input, include Default/System and Reset options, validate input, persist selections across restarts in the user configuration, apply main-window background changes immediately, apply splash-screen background changes on next launch, and ensure that all text and UI controls maintain accessible contrast. The splash screen and main window background colors shall be independently configurable, and the feature shall work across all supported desktop platforms without overriding OS high-contrast/accessibility settings unless explicitly chosen by the user.

issue_title: Add a Trait system for GDScript
requirement: # Feature Requirement: Trait System for GDScript  ## Summary Add first-class support for traits to GDScript: a declaration construct that lets a script reuse a named, statically-checked bundle of members (methods, constants, signals, and properties) without using single inheritance. Traits are composed into a script at compile time via a `uses` clause, and the GDScript parser, analyzer, compiler, and editor tooling must all understand them.  ## Motivation GDScript currently supports only single inheritance (`extends`) plus inner classes. There is no sanctioned way to share implementation across unrelated classes, forcing code duplication or deep, brittle inheritance chains. A trait system provides horizontal code reuse while preserving GDScript's static analysis guarantees.  ## Functional Requirements  ### R1 — Trait declaration 1. A new top-level keyword `trait` shall declare a trait: `trait TraitName:` followed by an indented body. 2. A trait body shall permit the same member kinds as a class body: methods, constants, signals, properties (with getters/setters), and nested inner classes, subject to R6. 3. A trait shall support an optional `extends TraitName` clause to inherit from another trait (trait-to-trait inheritance only). 4. A trait shall not be instantiable; `TraitName.new()` shall be a parse/analysis error. 5. A trait shall not be usable as a type annotation; using a trait name where a type is expected shall produce an analysis error.  ### R2 — Trait composition 1. A class (or inner class) shall compose traits using a `uses TraitA, TraitB` clause placed after the optional `extends` clause. 2. `uses` shall accept one or more trait names separated by commas. 3. A trait may itself include a `uses` clause; traits are therefore transitively composable. Composition shall be resolved to a fixed set of members per class at analysis time (no runtime dispatch indirection required). 4. A class that `uses` a trait shall be assignable to and from that trait's own base classes where applicable (i.e., trait inheritance contributes its inherited members, but does not alter the using class's `extends` chain). 5. Circular trait composition (`A uses B`, `B uses A`) shall be detected and reported as an analysis error.  ### R3 — Member resolution 1. Members declared directly in the using class shall take precedence over members supplied by traits. 2. A member supplied by exactly one used trait shall be added to the class automatically. 3. If two used traits supply a member with the same name, and the class does not define it, this shall be a compile-time error naming both traits and the conflicting member. 4. The conflict in R3.3 may be resolved by the class defining the member itself, or by an explicit alias directive `use TraitName.Member as OtherName` within the class body. 5. Constants, signals, and property names shall follow the same conflict and precedence rules as methods.  ### R4 — Semantics of composed members 1. `self` inside a trait method shall refer to the instance of the using class. 2. Trait methods shall be able to call methods and access members defined by the using class, resolved at analysis time; referencing a member that no using class provides shall be reported as an error at the point where analysis can determine it, or deferred to composition-time checking. 3. Traits may declare abstract method requirements (a method signature with no body). Every class that `uses` such a trait must provide a concrete implementation, either directly or through another used trait; otherwise analysis shall fail. 4. Trait properties shall behave as if declared in the using class, including their getters, setters, and initializers. 5. `_init` and `_static_init` shall not be permitted in a trait body; a class's own initializers remain the only initialization entry points.  ### R5 — Reflection and tooling 1. A script shall expose a `get_traits()` method (or equivalent) returning the names of directly used traits; static analysis should expose the same information to the editor. 2. The editor shall provide go-to-definition, documentation lookup, and completion for members contributed by traits, attributing each member to its source trait. 3. The built-in documentation generator shall document traits and list, for each class, the traits it uses.  ### R6 — Restrictions 1. Traits shall not declare `class_name`; they are referenced by their script path or by name within the same file. 2. Traits shall not be `@tool`-qualified independently; `@tool` behavior is governed by the using class. 3. Traits shall not participate in `is`/`as` type checks as standalone types; the existing `extends` chain is unchanged. 4. Serialization, signal connections, and property replication shall operate on the using class's composed member set exactly as if those members had been written in the class.  ## Non-Functional Requirements 1. The feature shall preserve GDScript's existing static-typing guarantees: all trait member resolution exceptions shall be surfaced at parse/analysis time, not at runtime. 2. Composing traits shall not introduce per-call runtime lookup overhead beyond what an equivalent method declared directly in the class would incur. 3. Existing scripts without `uses` clauses shall parse and behave identically; the feature must be backward compatible. 4. Error messages for trait misuse (duplicate members, circular use, unimplemented abstract methods, non-instantiable traits) shall identify the trait, member, and source location.  ## Out of Scope - Runtime/dynamic trait addition or removal. - Traits as generic type parameters. - Multiple inheritance of classes. - Trait support in GDExtension/C# scripts.  ## Acceptance Criteria 1. A script declaring `trait Walkable:` with a `walk()` method, used via `uses Walkable`, compiles and exposes `walk()` on instances; calling `walk()` from a caller dispatches to the class instance. 2. Two traits defining the same method name produce an analysis error unless the class overrides the method or aliases one trait's member with `use`. 3. A trait that `extends` another trait contributes both sets of members to the using class, and `self` inside inherited trait methods resolves to the using instance. 4. A trait declaring an abstract method fails analysis on a using class that does not implement it, and passes on one that does. 5. `TraitName.new()` and a trait name used as a type hint each produce a clear analysis error. 6. Editor completion and go-to-definition resolve trait-contributed members to their defining trait. 7. A project with no `uses` clauses builds unchanged, and the GDScript test suite passes.

issue_title: Implement PlatformView support on macOS
requirement: # Requirement: PlatformView Support on macOS  ## Summary Flutter on macOS shall support PlatformView, enabling Flutter applications and plugins to embed native AppKit views (`NSView`) directly in the Flutter widget tree. The feature shall include the required framework APIs, macOS embedder support, plugin registration APIs, rendering/compositing, input handling, lifecycle management, accessibility integration, and documentation.  ## Functional Requirements  - **FR-1:** The macOS embedder shall implement PlatformView registration and creation APIs consistent with Flutter’s existing PlatformView architecture. - **FR-2:** Plugins shall be able to register native view factories with the macOS plugin registrar using a `viewType` identifier. - **FR-3:** The Flutter framework shall expose macOS-compatible PlatformView widgets, including `AppKitView` and support through `PlatformViewLink` / `PlatformViewSurface`. - **FR-4:** Dart code shall be able to create a platform view by `viewType`, optionally passing creation parameters and a codec. - **FR-5:** The macOS embedder shall create the corresponding `NSView`, add it to the native view hierarchy, and associate it with the Dart-side platform view instance. - **FR-6:** Platform views shall participate in Flutter layout: their native frames shall match the widget’s size, position, transforms, clipping, and visibility as closely as the macOS compositing model permits. - **FR-7:** Platform views shall support correct z-ordering relative to Flutter-rendered content, including overlapping and clipping scenarios where supported. - **FR-8:** Input events — including mouse, trackpad, scroll, keyboard, text input, and accessibility events — shall be routed to the native view when appropriate. Flutter gesture recognizers configured on the platform view shall be able to intercept or participate in hit testing. - **FR-9:** Platform view lifecycle shall be managed correctly: creation, reuse where applicable, disposal when removed from the widget tree, and cleanup on hot restart. Native resources shall not leak. - **FR-10:** Multiple platform views shall be supported simultaneously in a single Flutter view hierarchy. - **FR-11:** Platform views shall function in debug, profile, and release modes. - **FR-12:** Documentation and at least one example shall be provided showing how to implement a macOS platform view plugin.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - **AC-1:** Given a macOS Flutter app and a plugin registering a platform view factory, when Dart renders `AppKitView(viewType: 'example')`, the registered native `NSView` is created and displayed at the expected location and size. - **AC-2:** Resizing the macOS window updates the platform view’s native frame to match the Flutter widget bounds. - **AC-3:** Mouse clicks, drags, scroll events, and keyboard input reach the native view when the platform view is focused or hit-tested. - **AC-4:** Flutter gesture recognizers attached to the platform view can receive gestures according to the documented hit-test behavior. - **AC-5:** Two or more platform views can be displayed simultaneously and maintain correct ordering relative to Flutter widgets and each other. - **AC-6:** Removing the platform view widget from the tree disposes the native view and releases associated resources. - **AC-7:** Hot restart and hot reload do not leave orphaned native views or crash the application. - **AC-8:** VoiceOver and other accessibility features can access the native view, or any limitation is explicitly documented. - **AC-9:** Integration tests exist and pass on macOS for creation, layout, input, disposal, and multiple-view scenarios. - **AC-10:** Existing macOS rendering, input, and plugin behavior are not regressed.  ## Non-Functional Requirements  - **NFR-1:** The implementation shall follow existing Flutter PlatformView API conventions for consistency with Android and iOS. - **NFR-2:** The feature shall not introduce continuous CPU or GPU usage when platform views are idle. - **NFR-3:** The implementation shall avoid memory leaks and native resource leaks. - **NFR-4:** The feature shall be supported on macOS versions covered by Flutter’s current macOS support policy. - **NFR-5:** Public APIs shall be documented and covered by tests.  ## Dependencies  - Flutter framework - Flutter engine - macOS embedder - AppKit / Cocoa - Flutter plugin registration APIs  ## Out of Scope  - PlatformView support on Windows, Linux, or web. - Changes to Android or iOS PlatformView behavior. - Full parity with Android hybrid composition if the macOS compositing model requires documented differences.

issue_title: Create a Swarm/Mob/Flock/etc system for managing large amounts of entities
requirement: **Requirement:** The system shall provide a general-purpose entity grouping and simulation subsystem for managing large numbers of entities as coherent groups such as swarms, mobs, flocks, packs, crowds, or similar formations.  The subsystem shall: - Support creation, configuration, deletion, and querying of entity groups. - Allow entities to be added to, removed from, and transferred between groups at runtime. - Support pluggable group behavior policies so that swarm, mob, flock, and other behaviors can be implemented without changing the core grouping system. - Provide lifecycle management for groups and their entities, including spawning, despawning, enabling, disabling, and cleanup. - Support spatial queries and neighbor lookup sufficient for group behaviors that depend on nearby entities. - Provide deterministic and configurable update ordering for group simulation. - Support serialization and restoration of group state and membership. - Expose a documented public API for creating groups, configuring behavior, querying group state, and controlling updates. - Provide configuration for capacity limits, update rates, level-of-detail behavior, and graceful degradation under load. - Include observability for group counts, entity counts, update durations, and capacity/limit violations. - Include automated tests covering group lifecycle, membership changes, behavior-policy integration, serialization, and high-entity-count scenarios.  Acceptance criteria: - A caller can create a group with a selected behavior policy, add and remove entities, run updates, query membership, and delete the group through the public API. - The system supports multiple simultaneous groups and large entity counts within documented performance targets, with configurable limits and graceful degradation when limits are exceeded. - Group state can be saved and restored without loss of membership or configuration. - Behavior policies can be added or replaced without modifying the core grouping subsystem. - The feature is covered by documentation and automated tests, and does not regress existing entity-management behavior.

issue_title: Add a "Mask2D" node (and/or a "mask_parent" property for Sprite2D)
requirement: **Requirement: Built-in 2D Sprite Masking**  The engine shall provide a built-in 2D masking mechanism that allows `Sprite2D` and other `CanvasItem` nodes to be masked by another 2D texture or node without custom shaders. The feature shall be exposed through at least one of the following APIs:  1. **`Mask2D` node** — a new `Node2D`-derived node that masks its child `CanvasItem` nodes using the alpha channel of its rendered texture/shape. 2. **`mask_parent` property on `Sprite2D`** — a `NodePath` property that references a `Mask2D` or other `CanvasItem` whose rendered alpha channel defines the visible region of the `Sprite2D`.  **Functional requirements:** - Masking shall use the mask node’s alpha channel. By default, final pixel alpha shall be `source_alpha × mask_alpha`. An optional binary/clip mode may apply an adjustable alpha cutoff threshold. - The mask shall respect its own transform, rotation, scale, modulate, z-index, and canvas layer. - Pixels outside the mask texture/shape shall be fully transparent. - Only designated nodes shall be affected: children of a `Mask2D`, or nodes referencing a mask via `mask_parent`. Unrelated sibling/non-designated nodes shall not be affected. - Nested masks shall compose multiplicatively. - The feature shall work identically in the editor and at runtime, updating immediately when the mask or masked node is moved, animated, or modified. - The implementation shall not require per-frame CPU readback and should preserve batching where possible. - Existing projects shall remain unaffected unless the new node/property is used. - Documentation and automated tests shall be provided.  **Acceptance criteria:** - A `Sprite2D` masked by a `Mask2D` displays only within the mask’s alpha region. - Changing the mask’s transform, rotation, scale, or texture updates the masked result immediately in the editor and at runtime. - A `Sprite2D` with `mask_parent` set to a valid mask node produces the same masked output as the `Mask2D` child-node approach. - Disabling the mask node renders masked items unmasked, or follows the documented behavior for mask activation. - The feature is usable from GDScript and C# and is configurable through the editor inspector.

issue_title: Add support for global plugins/universal addons
requirement: The system shall support global plugins (also referred to as universal addons) that can be installed and configured once at the user or application level and are then automatically discoverable, loadable, and usable across all projects and supported environments without per-project installation. Users shall be able to manage global plugins—install, list, enable, disable, update, and uninstall—through the standard plugin management interface/CLI/API, with documented per-project configuration overrides and explicit opt-in/opt-out behavior. Plugin resolution shall follow a defined precedence order in which project-local plugins override global plugins for the same identifier or capability unless the project explicitly configures otherwise. Global plugins shall use the same plugin API, lifecycle hooks, dependency handling, permission model, and sandboxing as local plugins, shall not compromise project isolation or reproducibility, and shall emit clear, non-fatal diagnostics when they are incompatible, unavailable, or fail to load.

issue_title: Allow explicitly defining interfaces in GDScript
requirement: # Requirement: Explicit Interface Definition in GDScript  ## Summary GDScript shall support the explicit declaration of **interfaces** — named contracts that specify a set of required method signatures (and optionally properties/signals) — and shall support statically verifying that any class declaring an interface fully implements it. Interfaces shall be usable as types for variables, parameters, return values, and exported properties.  ## Motivation GDScript currently expresses contracts only through duck typing, informal conventions, or abstract base classes. There is no way to declare a named contract that a class explicitly "implements," nor to type a value as "any object that fulfills this contract." As a result, contract violations surface only at runtime, tooling/autocompletion is limited, and expected APIs are poorly documented. An explicit interface construct enables earlier error detection, better editor tooling, and self-documenting APIs.  ## Functional Requirements  **FR-1 — Interface declaration** - GDScript shall provide syntax to declare an interface as a named, first-class language construct (e.g., `interface IFoo:`). - An interface body shall contain method signatures with typed parameters and typed return values. - An interface shall contain no implementation bodies. - An interface may declare required properties and/or signals. - An interface may extend one or more other interfaces and shall inherit all of their requirements.  **FR-2 — Interface implementation** - A class shall be able to explicitly declare that it implements one or more interfaces. - A class may implement multiple interfaces. - An implementing class must provide a concrete implementation for every method signature declared by the interface(s), with compatible parameter and return types.  **FR-3 — Static verification** - The GDScript compiler shall verify at parse/compile time that every class declaring an interface satisfies all interface requirements. - A missing or signature-incompatible member shall produce a compile-time error that identifies the interface and the offending member.  **FR-4 — Interfaces as types** - Interfaces shall be usable as types for variables, function parameters, function return values, and exported properties. - Assigning a value to an interface-typed location shall require the value's class to implement that interface; the check shall be performed statically where determinable, otherwise at runtime. - The `is` and `as` operators, and type casting, shall accept interface types.  **FR-5 — Introspection** - The engine shall expose whether a class or object implements a given interface through reflection/introspection APIs.  **FR-6 — Editor tooling** - The editor shall provide autocompletion, documentation, and error highlighting for interfaces and their members.  ## Constraints and Non-Functional Requirements - **Backward compatibility:** The feature is additive; all existing GDScript projects must continue to compile and run unchanged. - **Performance:** Static verification shall impose no runtime overhead; runtime interface checks shall be efficient. - **Integration:** The construct shall interoperate with the existing inheritance model and the `class_name` registration system.  ## Acceptance Criteria 1. A script can declare an interface containing method signatures. 2. A script can declare that it implements one or more interfaces and is accepted only when all required members are implemented. 3. A variable, parameter, return value, or exported property can be typed as an interface and accepts any object whose class implements it. 4. Omitting or mismatching a required member produces a clear compile-time error naming the interface and member. 5. `is`/`as` checks and casts against interface types behave correctly at runtime. 6. Introspection APIs correctly report interface implementation. 7. All pre-existing GDScript code compiles and runs without modification.

issue_title: Replace GridMap with an improved TileMap3D node (inspired by the new 2D TileMap)
requirement: # Software Requirement: Replace GridMap with an Improved TileMap3D Node  ## Summary Replace the existing `GridMap` node with a new node named `TileMap3D` that adopts the architecture and workflow of the redesigned 2D `TileMap` node. The new node shall become the standard mechanism for building grid-based 3D level geometry, and `GridMap` shall be deprecated and eventually removed.  ## Motivation `GridMap` currently relies on the legacy `MeshLibrary` resource, which lacks the modularity, layering, terrain/autotiling, and editing ergonomics introduced by the redesigned 2D `TileMap`/`TileSet` system. Unifying 2D and 3D tile-based workflows reduces duplication in the engine, lowers the learning curve for users moving between 2D and 3D, and enables richer 3D level-authoring features already available in 2D.  ## Functional Requirements  1. **New Node: `TileMap3D`**    - Provide a new `Node3D`-derived class named `TileMap3D` for placing tiles on a 3D grid.    - The node shall mirror the conceptual API and behavior of the 2D `TileMap` node, adapted to three dimensions.  2. **TileSet-Based Resource Model**    - `TileMap3D` shall be driven by a `TileSet3D` resource, structured analogously to the 2D `TileSet`.    - `TileSet3D` shall support:      - Tile sources (equivalent to `TileSetScenesCollectionSource`, atlas-style sources, and mesh-based sources).      - Per-tile metadata, custom data layers, and collision information.      - Per-tile configuration of mesh instances, materials, and transforms.    - Existing `MeshLibrary` resources shall be convertible to `TileSet3D` via an import path or migration tool.  3. **Layering**    - `TileMap3D` shall support multiple independently configurable tile layers.    - Each layer shall expose: visibility, Z-index/ordering, transform, collision enable/disable, and per-layer cell size and origin.  4. **Terrain and Autotiling**    - `TileSet3D` shall support terrain sets equivalent to the 2D terrain/autotile system (bitmask and/or minimal matching modes).    - `TileMap3D` shall support automatic terrain painting consistent with 2D behavior.  5. **Editing Workflow**    - The TileMap3D editor shall provide painting, erasing, line, rectangle, and bucket-fill tools, mirroring the 2D TileMap editor.    - The editor shall support pattern selection, randomization, and probability-weighted placement.    - The 3D editor shall support snapping to grid cells and previewing tiles in the viewport.  6. **Runtime API**    - Provide runtime methods equivalent in intent to 2D `TileMap`: `set_cell`, `get_cell_source_id`, `erase_cell`, `clear_layer`, `map_to_local`/`local_to_map`, `set_layer_*`, and cell coordinate conversions between 2D grid coordinates and 3D positions.    - Support efficient bulk operations and dirty-region updates to avoid full relayouts.  7. **Compatibility and Migration**    - `GridMap` shall be marked deprecated and remain available for at least one release cycle.    - Provide a documented migration path from `GridMap`/`MeshLibrary` to `TileMap3D`/`TileSet3D`, including automated conversion where feasible.  ## Non-Functional Requirements - Performance for large maps (e.g., tens of thousands of cells) shall be at least on par with `GridMap`. - API naming and semantics shall remain consistent with the 2D `TileMap`/`TileSet` to the extent the 3D domain permits. - Documentation shall cover the new node, resource, migration, and editor usage.  ## Acceptance Criteria - A `TileMap3D` node can be added, associated with a `TileSet3D`, painted in the editor, and rendered correctly at runtime. - Terrain/autotiling functions in 3D as it does in 2D. - Multiple layers render and collide independently per their configuration. - A `GridMap` scene can be migrated to `TileMap3D` without manual reconstruction of tile data. - Existing `GridMap` projects continue to load and run while deprecation remains in effect.

issue_title: Add array unpacking/destructuring to GDScript
requirement: **Requirement:** GDScript shall support array unpacking/destructuring in variable declarations and assignment statements. The left-hand side of a declaration or assignment may be a bracketed pattern of assignable targets, such as `var [a, b, c] = [1, 2, 3]` and `[a, b] = [b, a]`. At runtime, each target shall receive the source array element at the corresponding index; extra source elements shall be ignored, and if the source array contains fewer elements than the pattern requires, execution shall raise a clear runtime error. Nested array patterns shall be supported recursively, e.g. `var [a, [b, c]] = [1, [2, 3]]`. The feature shall integrate with GDScript’s parser, analyzer, type checking, and runtime, preserve existing type inference where possible, report clear parse/analyzer errors for invalid patterns and non-array right-hand sides, and be documented and covered by automated tests.

issue_title: Add support for multiple displays/screens/monitors in Godot editor
requirement: **Requirement:** The Godot editor shall support multiple connected displays/screens/monitors, allowing users to place, move, resize, maximize, and fullscreen the main editor window and detachable editor panels (e.g., Scene, Inspector, FileSystem, Output) on any available display. The editor shall detect display configuration, respect per-monitor DPI scaling and coordinate systems, and persist the multi-monitor layout—including display assignment, window/panel positions, sizes, docked/floating state, and maximized/fullscreen state—across editor sessions. When displays are added, removed, resized, or their DPI/primary status changes, the editor shall update the layout, relocate any off-screen windows/panels to a visible display, and avoid crashes, lost panels, or unusable UI. The editor shall remain fully functional on a single display and shall provide a reset/recover default layout action. Multi-monitor behavior shall be configurable in Editor Settings and shall not affect project runtime behavior unless explicitly enabled by the project.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - A user can move/dock editor panels to a secondary monitor and continue using them normally. - The editor restores the exact multi-monitor layout after restart. - Disconnecting a monitor moves affected editor windows/panels to a visible display without data loss. - Single-display users experience no regression in editor layout or usability.

issue_title: Expose a zero allocation API to Godot C# bindings
requirement: **Requirement ID:** C#-BINDINGS-ZERO-ALLOC-API  **Title:** Zero-allocation API for Godot C# bindings  **Statement:** The Godot C# bindings shall expose a public, documented, and supported zero-allocation API that enables C# code to call engine methods, access properties, emit and connect signals, and create, read, write, and convert `Variant` and common Godot types without managed heap allocations during steady-state execution. The API shall support cached `StringName` and `Callable` handles, caller-provided buffers, spans, or stack-allocated storage; return values shall be written to caller-provided destinations or returned as value types without boxing. It shall coexist with existing allocating APIs without breaking source or binary compatibility, be usable in editor and exported projects, and include automated tests proving zero managed allocations per operation after warm-up. Documentation shall cover usage, lifetime, threading, and disposal rules. Existing allocating convenience APIs shall remain available.  **Acceptance Criteria:** 1. Public zero-allocation API is available and documented for method calls, property access, signal operations, and `Variant`/type conversion. 2. Representative operations allocate zero managed bytes per call after warm-up, verified by automated tests using `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread()` or equivalent. 3. No unbounded managed or native memory growth occurs under repeated documented use. 4. Existing C# code compiles and runs without modification. 5. API works in editor and exported projects on supported Godot platforms.

issue_title: Add procedural and parametrizable audio support
requirement: The audio system shall support procedural audio generation and runtime-parametrizable audio sources.  - Procedural audio generators shall be definable through the public API and/or configuration without requiring pre-recorded audio assets. - Each generator shall expose named, typed parameters with defaults, valid ranges, and optional modulation/animation support. - Parameters shall be settable at runtime and changes shall take effect without restarting playback unless explicitly scheduled or configured otherwise. - Procedural sources shall integrate with the existing audio pipeline, including mixing, buses, effects, spatialization, and lifecycle management. - Generator instances shall support creation, start, stop, disposal, configurable polyphony, and safe handling of invalid parameter values. - Generator definitions and parameter values shall be serializable and loadable through the existing configuration/persistence mechanisms. - Generators shall support an optional deterministic seed so identical parameters and seed produce reproducible output.  Acceptance criteria: 1. A developer can define a procedural generator, start playback, adjust its parameters at runtime, and observe the resulting audio change. 2. Procedural sources can be mixed and routed through the same buses/effects as existing audio sources. 3. Invalid parameter values are rejected or clamped without crashing the audio system. 4. Generator configuration and parameter values can be saved and restored. 5. Multiple generator instances can run concurrently up to a configured polyphony limit and are correctly cleaned up when disposed.

issue_title: Obfuscate GDScript in production export
requirement: The Godot export system shall provide an optional, per-export-preset setting to obfuscate GDScript in production/release exports. When enabled, the exporter shall transform exported GDScript to make it harder to read and reverse engineer—such as renaming safe identifiers, stripping debug/source metadata, and encoding compiled script data—while preserving runtime behavior, public script APIs, exported properties, signals, RPCs, annotations, and platform compatibility. The option shall be disabled by default, available for all supported platforms, and documented in the export documentation.

issue_title: Add literal quoted strings with embedded variables (f-strings) to GDScript
requirement: **Requirement:** GDScript shall support f-string literals. An f-string is any single-line or multiline single- or double-quoted GDScript string literal prefixed with `f` or `F`; within it, each `{expression}` segment shall be evaluated in the enclosing scope at the point where the f-string literal is evaluated, converted to a string using the same conversion rules as `str()`, and inserted at that position. Literal braces shall be written as `{{` and `}}`, and existing string escape sequences shall remain valid without being treated as interpolation delimiters. Interpolation expressions may be any valid GDScript expression and shall be evaluated left to right. An f-string with unbalanced braces, an empty interpolation expression, an invalid expression, or an undefined identifier shall produce a parse/compile error that identifies the f-string location. Non-f-string literals and all existing string-literal behavior shall remain unchanged.

issue_title: Add "refactor" tooling to rename symbols in the script editor
requirement: **Requirement: Script Editor Symbol Rename Refactoring**  The script editor shall provide a refactoring tool that allows users to rename a symbol—including variables, constants, functions, methods, classes, signals, enums, enum values, properties, and parameters—and automatically update all references to that symbol within the selected scope. The tool shall be accessible via a “Refactor” menu or submenu, the editor context menu, the command palette, and a configurable keyboard shortcut when the caret is on or a symbol is selected.  **Acceptance Criteria**  1. Invoking “Rename Symbol” opens an inline edit field or dialog pre-filled with the current symbol name. 2. The new name is validated against the scripting language’s identifier rules and checked for conflicts with existing symbols in the applicable scope; invalid or conflicting names prevent completion and display a clear error. 3. The user can select the refactoring scope: current script, open scripts, or entire project, where supported by the language and project structure. The default scope is the current script. 4. The tool identifies and updates all static references to the symbol in the selected scope, including declarations and usages, while preserving formatting, comments, and string literals unless the user explicitly opts to update them. 5. A preview of all affected files and changes is shown before applying, with the ability to include or exclude individual occurrences. 6. Applying the refactoring updates all selected occurrences atomically and records the change as a single undoable and redoable operation. 7. If a reference cannot be safely resolved—such as dynamic access, reflection, or an ambiguous symbol—the tool skips that occurrence and reports a warning listing unresolved or potentially affected locations. 8. The refactoring command does not modify files outside the selected scope or unrelated symbols. 9. The feature is covered by automated tests for valid renames, name conflicts, scope selection, preview, undo/redo, and error handling.

issue_title: Add WebGPU support
requirement: Requirement: Add WebGPU support as an optional, runtime-selectable backend for the project’s graphics/compute operations. The system shall detect WebGPU availability, provide a configuration option to enable, disable, or auto-select WebGPU, use WebGPU when selected and supported, and transparently fall back to the existing WebGL/WebGL2/Canvas backend when WebGPU is unavailable, disabled, or fails to initialize. The WebGPU path shall preserve existing public APIs, functional behavior, visual output, and error semantics; handle adapter/device request failures, device loss, and resource cleanup; and include documentation and automated tests covering capability detection, backend selection, fallback, and device-loss recovery. Acceptance criteria: existing tests pass without regression; new tests verify WebGPU initialization, fallback, and recovery; supported browsers/platforms are documented; and no breaking changes are introduced for users not using WebGPU.

issue_title: Implement a Rendering Compositor
requirement: **Requirement: Rendering Compositor**  The system SHALL implement a rendering compositor that accepts one or more rendered layers, composites them into a single output frame, and presents that frame through the active display/rendering backend. The compositor SHALL:  1. Maintain a mutable ordered layer list or tree. Each layer SHALL define at least: unique identifier, source surface/texture, bounds, z-order, visibility, opacity, transform, clip rectangle, and blend mode. 2. Composite layers in back-to-front z-order using source-over alpha blending with premultiplied alpha. Unsupported blend modes SHALL be rejected or fall back to source-over with a logged warning. 3. Apply per-layer transforms, clipping, and opacity before blending. Clipping SHALL constrain both sampling and output to the clip rectangle. 4. Support atomic layer updates: add, remove, reorder, show/hide, and property changes. Changes SHALL take effect on the next composited frame without restarting the compositor. 5. Track damage regions per layer where provided. If damage tracking is available, recomposite only affected regions; otherwise, composite the full output frame. The compositor SHALL never display partial or torn frames. 6. Synchronize composition and presentation with the rendering backend's frame/vsync mechanism. Layer mutations from other threads SHALL be synchronized so the compositor never reads partially updated layer state. 7. Prefer GPU-accelerated composition when available. Provide a CPU fallback path for environments without GPU support. Both paths SHALL produce visually equivalent output within the project's defined color and format tolerances. 8. Expose a programmatic API to create, update, remove, reorder, and query layers, and to start/stop the compositor. 9. Handle errors gracefully: invalid layer properties, missing source surfaces, unsupported formats, and backend failures SHALL be logged and SHALL NOT crash the process. If the primary backend fails, the compositor SHALL attempt fallback or stop cleanly. 10. Meet the project's frame budget on the documented reference hardware: composite and present a 1920x1080 frame at 60 Hz (16.6 ms/frame) with compositor overhead not exceeding 25% of the frame budget. Lower resolutions and refresh rates SHALL scale accordingly. 11. Include unit tests for z-ordering, alpha blending, opacity, transforms, clipping, damage-region updates, and error handling; and an integration test that composites multiple layers and verifies the final output against a reference image. 12. Document the compositor's layer model, API, supported blend modes and formats, and backend fallback behavior.  Acceptance criteria: the compositor builds and runs on supported platforms; the integration test passes; no tearing or crash occurs during layer mutation; the performance target is met on reference hardware; and CPU and GPU outputs match within the defined tolerance.

issue_title: Godot C# GDExtension Roadmap Discussion
requirement: Godot shall provide official, first-class C# support via GDExtension, enabling developers to create, build, package, distribute, and load C#-based GDExtensions without rebuilding the engine; these extensions shall support registration and exposure of Godot classes, methods, properties, signals, enums, and virtual methods; interoperate with Godot’s Variant system, object lifecycle, and memory management; run on supported .NET runtimes across all Godot-supported platforms and export templates; support debugging and optional hot reload; and be delivered with stable APIs, documentation, examples, and a published roadmap covering version compatibility, ABI/API stability, and migration from the existing C# module.

issue_title: Add proper and complete support for multi-pass shaders
requirement: **Requirement:** Add first-class, complete support for multi-pass shaders. The system shall allow a shader to declare an ordered sequence of passes, where each pass defines its own shader stages, uniforms/parameters, input/output resources, render targets, and render state (including blending, depth, stencil, culling, viewport, and scissor). The system shall compile, link, validate, and execute all passes in the declared or dependency-resolved order, automatically allocating and releasing intermediate render targets and transient resources. Shared parameters shall be available to every pass, with per-pass overrides supported; pass-local parameters shall not leak between passes. The system shall detect and report invalid pass configurations, cyclic dependencies, missing inputs, and resource conflicts with clear, actionable diagnostics. Multi-pass shaders shall work consistently across all supported rendering backends and remain backward compatible with existing single-pass shaders. Documentation and automated tests shall cover pass ordering, parameter propagation, resource lifetime, per-pass render state, and error handling.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - A multi-pass shader with N ordered passes executes each pass exactly once in the correct order. - Intermediate outputs from one pass can be consumed as inputs by later passes without manual render-target management. - Shared uniforms update all passes; per-pass uniforms affect only their pass. - Invalid pass definitions fail with clear errors and do not crash or silently misrender. - Existing single-pass shaders continue to work unchanged. - Automated tests validate multi-pass behavior on all supported rendering backends.

issue_title: Implement namespaces in GDScript
requirement: GDScript shall implement namespaces as a compile-time symbol-organization mechanism. A script shall be able to declare a namespace scope, including nested namespaces, and declare namespace-eligible symbols such as `class_name`, constants, enums, and static members within that scope. Namespaced symbols shall be accessible through fully qualified names and, where unambiguous, through unqualified names from within the same namespace. The implementation shall provide import or alias syntax for referencing namespaced symbols without repeated qualification, and name resolution shall be deterministic, reporting missing-symbol and ambiguity errors during parsing or analysis. Existing unnamespaced `class_name` declarations and global identifiers shall remain source-compatible. The parser, analyzer, editor autocomplete, documentation generation, and diagnostics shall understand namespaces. Namespaces shall have no runtime representation or runtime performance cost and shall affect only symbol registration and resolution. Acceptance requires tests covering namespace declaration, nesting, qualified and unqualified access, imports/aliases, name collisions, error diagnostics, and backward compatibility, along with updated language documentation.

issue_title: Improve the performance of the GDScript VM
requirement: Requirement REQ-GDSCRIPT-VM-PERF-001: Improve GDScript VM Performance  The GDScript virtual machine (VM) shall be optimized to significantly increase the execution speed of GDScript code in the Godot Engine while preserving existing language semantics, API compatibility, and runtime stability.  Scope: - Optimize interpreter hot paths, including but not limited to bytecode dispatch, stack operations, function and method calls, property access, arithmetic and comparison operations, loop execution, and typed instruction handling. - Use profiling and representative benchmarks to identify bottlenecks and validate improvements. - Avoid changes that alter GDScript syntax, semantics, error behavior, or serialized script compatibility.  Performance targets: - Achieve at least a 20% improvement in overall execution time on the official or agreed-upon GDScript benchmark suite compared to the pre-change baseline on the same hardware and software configuration. - No individual benchmark in the suite shall regress by more than 5%. - GDScript compilation and loading time shall not regress by more than 5% on average. - Runtime memory usage for GDScript execution shall not increase by more than 5% on average.  Acceptance criteria: - Benchmark results demonstrate the required execution-time improvement and show no significant regressions. - All existing GDScript and Godot Engine automated tests pass. - Behavior of valid GDScript programs remains identical, including deterministic execution and error reporting. - No new crashes, hangs, or platform-specific failures are introduced on supported platforms. - Benchmark methodology and results are documented.

issue_title: A new compiler flag: "link everything statically or die, dammit!"
requirement: The compiler shall provide a command-line flag that forces every library and runtime component to be linked statically. When this flag is enabled, the linker must not fall back to dynamic linking for any dependency; if any required library or object cannot be linked statically, the compilation or link step shall fail with a clear diagnostic identifying the non-static dependency. The flag shall be documented and covered by tests that verify both successful fully static linking and the expected failure when static versions of required libraries are unavailable.

issue_title: Implement a code formatter for GDScript in the script editor
requirement: **Requirement:** The GDScript script editor shall provide a built-in code formatter that formats GDScript source code according to the official GDScript style guide.  **The formatter shall:** - Be accessible from the script editor UI and via an editor command/shortcut for the active GDScript file. - Support formatting either the entire active script or the current selection. - Normalize indentation, spacing around operators and punctuation, blank lines, and statement layout without changing program behavior. - Preserve comments, string literals, annotations, and existing line endings. - Leave source unchanged and report an error when the script cannot be parsed safely. - Integrate with the editor’s undo/redo history and modified-state tracking. - Be idempotent: formatting already formatted code shall produce no further changes. - Operate locally without requiring external formatter binaries or network access.  **Acceptance criteria:** A user can invoke formatting on a valid GDScript file or selection, receive correctly formatted code that preserves semantics and comments, undo the operation in one step, and safely format invalid code without source loss.

issue_title: Rework the Tilemap terrain system to improve its usability
requirement: **Requirement:** The TileMap terrain system shall be reworked to make terrain creation, editing, and application intuitive, consistent, and efficient for both new and experienced users. The reworked system shall:  - Provide a visual, discoverable workflow for defining terrain sets, terrain types, and autotile transition rules from an existing tileset, with sensible defaults and minimal required configuration. - Allow users to paint, erase, and replace terrain directly on a TileMap using configurable brush sizes, live preview, undo/redo, and support for single-tile, random, and weighted tile variants. - Automatically resolve valid terrain transitions, including edges, corners, and diagonals, for supported tileset layouts, while allowing manual overrides for custom rules. - Preserve backward compatibility with existing TileMap and terrain data or provide a documented migration path that prevents data loss for user-created terrains. - Surface clear validation messages and guidance when terrain configurations are incomplete, invalid, or incompatible. - Include updated user documentation, in-editor tooltips/help, and examples covering common terrain workflows.  **Acceptance criteria:** A user can create a terrain set from a tileset, assign terrain types, paint terrain onto a TileMap, and observe correct autotiling in a new project without external guidance; existing projects with terrain data continue to load and render correctly; and no regressions occur in TileMap rendering, collision, or performance.

issue_title: Implement a Set primitive to complement Dictionary and Array
requirement: **Requirement: Implement a first-class Set primitive.**  The system shall provide a built-in `Set` type as a core primitive alongside the existing `Array` and `Dictionary` types. The `Set` shall represent a collection of unique values, complementing `Array` (ordered sequence) and `Dictionary` (key-value mapping) by providing efficient uniqueness, membership testing, and set-algebra operations.  **Functional requirements**  1. **Construction**    - A `Set` shall be constructible as empty, from an iterable such as an `Array`, or as a copy of another `Set`.    - A typed `Set` shall be constructible with an element type constraint, and an untyped `Set` shall accept any supported value type.  2. **Uniqueness**    - A `Set` shall not contain duplicate elements.    - Adding an element that is already present shall leave the `Set` unchanged and shall not increase its size.  3. **Core operations**    - The `Set` shall support adding, removing, and checking membership of an element.    - The `Set` shall expose its size, emptiness state, and a clear operation.    - The `Set` shall support iteration over its elements exactly once per element.  4. **Set algebra**    - The `Set` shall support union, intersection, difference, and symmetric difference.    - The `Set` shall support subset, superset, and disjointness checks.    - Set-algebra operations shall return new `Set` instances without mutating their operands unless an explicitly named in-place variant is used.  5. **Equality and comparison**    - Two `Set` instances shall be equal if and only if they contain the same elements, independent of insertion or iteration order.    - Iteration order shall be deterministic for a given `Set` instance and implementation, but shall not affect equality.  6. **Typed sets**    - A typed `Set` shall enforce its element type at runtime.    - Adding an element of an incompatible type to a typed `Set` shall raise an error consistent with existing typed `Array` and `Dictionary` behavior.  7. **Serialization and Variant integration**    - A `Set` shall be serializable and deserializable as a Variant without data loss, preserving its elements and type metadata.    - A `Set` shall be usable in the same contexts as `Array` and `Dictionary`, including scripting, engine APIs, property inspection, and documentation.  8. **Interoperability**    - A `Set` shall be convertible to and from an `Array`.    - Conversion from an `Array` containing duplicates shall produce a `Set` with duplicates removed.  9. **Performance**    - Membership testing, insertion, and removal shall have average-case time complexity no worse than O(1) for supported hashable element types.  10. **Error handling**     - Invalid operations, including type violations and unsupported element values, shall report errors consistently with existing collection types.  **Acceptance criteria**  - A `Set` can be created, populated, iterated, and serialized/deserialized without data loss. - Adding duplicate elements does not increase the `Set` size. - Union, intersection, difference, symmetric difference, subset, superset, and disjointness operations produce correct results. - Typed `Set` instances reject elements of incompatible types. - `Set` equality is order-independent and correct for identical element collections. - The `Set` type is documented, tested, and available through the same public APIs as `Array` and `Dictionary`.

issue_title: Implement Terrain
requirement: **REQ-TERRAIN-001: Implement Terrain**  The system shall provide a terrain subsystem that enables users to create, generate, render, edit, query, save, and load 3D terrain. The subsystem shall: 1. Represent terrain as a heightmap with configurable width, depth, height scale, and resolution, and support optional splat maps, normal maps, and material layers. 2. Generate terrain procedurally using configurable noise functions (e.g., Perlin, Simplex) with seed, frequency, amplitude, octaves, persistence, and lacunarity. 3. Render terrain using chunked meshes with level-of-detail, frustum culling, texture blending, and configurable materials. 4. Provide runtime editing operations—raise, lower, smooth, flatten, and paint texture—with undo/redo support. 5. Expose query APIs for terrain height at a world position, surface normal, and raycasting against terrain. 6. Persist terrain data and metadata in documented formats (e.g., PNG heightmap, raw binary, JSON metadata) with validation and error handling. 7. Provide public APIs and extension points for custom generators, materials, importers, and exporters. 8. Include documentation, an example scene, and automated unit and integration tests. 9. Maintain performance consistent with project benchmarks for target terrain sizes and hardware, using chunking and LOD to avoid frame-rate regressions.  **Acceptance Criteria:** A user can create a new terrain, generate it with a seed, edit it, save it, reload it, query heights and normals, and render it in the application without errors. All public APIs are documented and covered by tests. Performance meets or exceeds the project’s defined benchmarks for the reference terrain size and hardware.

issue_title: Linking with LLD
requirement: The system shall allow users to create, view, update, and remove links between an issue and one or more Low-Level Design (LLD) documents. Each link shall store the LLD identifier or URL, an optional description, and creation metadata. Linked LLDs shall be displayed on the issue detail view and exposed through the API. The system shall validate link targets, enforce access permissions for linked LLDs, and report clear errors for invalid or inaccessible links. Removing a link shall not delete the issue or the LLD.

issue_title: Add function to make paths absolute, which is different from canonicalization
requirement: The system shall provide a path utility function that returns an absolute path for a given path-like input without canonicalizing it. If the input is relative, the function shall make it absolute by combining it with the current working directory; if the input is already absolute, the function shall return it unchanged. The function shall not resolve symbolic links, collapse or resolve `.` or `..` components, normalize redundant or trailing separators, or require the path to exist. Its result shall be guaranteed only to be an absolute path, and the function shall be documented as distinct from canonicalization or realpath behavior.

issue_title: rustdoc support for per-parameter documentation
requirement: # Requirement: Rustdoc Support for Per-Parameter Documentation  **Identifier:** RUSTDOC-PARAM-DOC-001 **Status:** Proposed **Priority:** Medium  ## 1. Summary  The Rust compiler and rustdoc shall support attaching documentation to individual parameters of callable items and shall render that documentation as structured, addressable output in generated documentation.  ## 2. Problem Statement  Parameter semantics can currently only be explained as free-form prose in an ad hoc `# Arguments` Markdown section of the item's doc comment. Such prose is not associated with any parameter by the compiler or by rustdoc, cannot be validated for coverage or staleness, cannot be located by readers or tooling at the point of use, and is not represented in rustdoc's machine-readable output.  ## 3. Scope  **In scope:** value parameters, pattern parameters, and the `self` receiver of functions, inherent and trait methods, trait implementations, and `extern` declarations; rendering in rustdoc HTML and rustdoc JSON; related lints and documentation.  **Extended scope (should):** generic type parameters, lifetime parameters, and const generic parameters.  **Out of scope:** documentation of closure parameters, fn-pointer-type parameters, tuple struct/variant fields, and non-Rust documentation pipelines.  ## 4. Functional Requirements  **FR-1 — Authoring syntax.** Doc comments (`///`, `/** … */`) and equivalent `#[doc = "…"]` attributes written immediately before a parameter in a callable's signature shall be parsed by the compiler and attached to that parameter. The construct shall no longer be rejected with an error, and shall not be silently discarded or treated as an unused doc comment.  **FR-2 — Coverage.** FR-1 shall apply to free functions, inherent methods, trait methods, trait implementation methods, and foreign (`extern`) functions, including `async`, `unsafe`, `const`, and `extern "ABI"` variants, and to the `self` receiver where a receiver is written.  **FR-3 — Compilation neutrality.** Parameter documentation shall have no effect on name resolution, type checking, lowering, MIR, or code generation. Well-formed input shall not produce new compiler errors or warnings.  **FR-4 — HTML rendering.** Rustdoc shall render per-parameter documentation on the item page, associated with the corresponding parameter of the rendered signature, using the same Markdown pipeline as item documentation. Each rendered parameter shall expose a stable, linkable anchor so that a specific parameter's documentation can be referenced in a URL.  **FR-5 — Non-identifier parameters.** Documentation shall be accepted and rendered for parameters whose pattern does not supply a simple identifier (including `_`, tuple patterns, and destructuring patterns); where no name is rendered, the documentation shall still be reachable and attributable to the correct positional parameter.  **FR-6 — JSON output.** Rustdoc JSON shall carry per-parameter documentation in the representation of the corresponding argument. Any schema change shall follow the rustdoc JSON format's existing versioning and stability policy.  **FR-7 — Markdown and linking.** Parameter documentation shall support the Markdown feature set available to item documentation, including intra-doc links to types, traits, and functions, preformatted blocks, and HTML passthrough.  **FR-8 — Doctests.** Content in parameter documentation shall not generate doctests.  **FR-9 — Lints.** The behavior of `missing_docs` shall be unchanged by default. An allow-by-default rustdoc lint shall be provided to warn when a parameter is undocumented. `unused_doc_comments` shall not fire for parameter documentation.  **FR-10 — Extended scope.** Type parameters, lifetime parameters, and const generic parameters shall be documentable and renderable by the same mechanism.  **FR-11 — Documentation.** The accepted syntax shall be specified in the Rust Reference, and rendering, JSON representation, and lint behavior shall be documented in the rustdoc book.  ## 5. Non-Functional Requirements  - **Performance:** Compilation time and rustdoc time for crates with large public APIs shall show no measurable regression attributable to the feature. - **Compatibility:** Since the construct was previously a hard error, no currently compiling source code shall change behavior. - **Cross-crate propagation:** Parameter documentation on `pub` items shall be available to downstream crates through metadata and rendered in rustdoc for dependents, subject to `#[doc(hidden)]` and `--document-private-items` handling consistent with existing item documentation.  ## 6. Acceptance Criteria  1. A documented parameter compiles without error and its documentation appears in rustdoc HTML adjacent to that parameter. 2. Every rendered parameter exposes a distinct, stable anchor that resolves to the parameter's documentation. 3. The documentation appears in rustdoc JSON at the correct positional argument, under the versioned schema. 4. Intra-doc links inside parameter documentation resolve, and broken links are reported by `rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links`. 5. Parameter documentation produces no doctests and no `unused_doc_comments` warnings. 6. The opt-in parameter-documentation lint fires for undocumented parameters and is silent by default. 7. Trait methods, trait impl methods, foreign functions, and `async`/`unsafe`/`const` items behave as specified in FR-2. 8. A documented parameter on a `pub` item is rendered in a dependent crate's documentation. 9. Output for an undocumented parameter on an otherwise unchanged item is byte-identical to the pre-change output.  ## 7. Assumptions and Dependencies  - The exact spelling of the lint name and of the rendered parameter anchor scheme is fixed at implementation time and recorded in the rustdoc book. - Implementation depends on the parameter representation in rustc's HIR/AST retaining attached documentation attributes through to rustdoc's `clean` model and to metadata encoding.

issue_title: Add ability to ignore tests at runtime.
requirement: The test framework SHALL provide a documented runtime mechanism to ignore selected tests without modifying test source files. The mechanism SHALL accept one or more test identifiers or patterns via a supported interface (e.g., CLI flag, environment variable, or configuration), apply before test execution, mark matched tests as skipped/ignored in output, prevent their setup, test body, and teardown from executing, and not cause the test run to fail solely because tests were ignored. The feature SHALL be covered by documentation and automated tests.

issue_title: Add support for variadic functions (varargs) to GDScript
requirement: # Software Requirement: Variadic Function Support in GDScript  ## Summary  GDScript shall support user-defined variadic functions that accept a variable number of arguments at call time. The language shall provide defined syntax for declaring a variadic parameter and a defined mechanism for accessing surplus arguments within the function body.  ## Motivation  GDScript functions currently have fixed arity, modifiable only by default parameter values. Developers requiring variable arguments must rely on workarounds such as explicit `Array`/`Dictionary` parameters or `callv()`. First-class variadic support improves ergonomics, readability, and interoperability for wrapper, forwarding, logging, and utility APIs.  ## Functional Requirements  1. **Declaration syntax.** The language shall provide syntax to declare that a function accepts additional arguments beyond its named parameters. All surplus arguments shall be captured into a single ordered container accessible within the function body.  2. **Access to variadic arguments.** Inside a variadic function, the captured surplus arguments shall be accessible as an ordered, indexable collection that preserves call order.  3. **Minimum arity.** A variadic function may declare zero or more leading named parameters; only arguments beyond those named parameters are collected as variadic. Required named parameters shall be validated under existing rules.  4. **Call semantics.** A variadic function shall be callable with any number of extra arguments, including zero. Extra arguments shall be appended to the variadic collection in call order.  5. **Type support.** The variadic collection may be untyped or typed. If a type is declared, each surplus argument shall be validated/converted under existing parameter type rules, producing runtime errors consistent with current typed-parameter behavior.  6. **Interaction with default parameters.** Default values shall continue to apply to named parameters preceding the variadic parameter. The variadic parameter shall not require a default value.  7. **Forwarding / spreading.** The language shall provide a defined means to forward or expand a variadic collection into another callable's argument list (or document the supported alternative) so that transparent wrapper functions can be written without loss or reordering.  8. **Uniform callable behavior.** Variadic functions shall be invocable through all existing call paths—direct calls, `call()`/`callv()`, callables, signals, and reflection—with consistent behavior.  9. **Introspection.** Variadic functions shall report their variadic nature through the reflection/metadata APIs so that tooling and bindings can detect them.  10. **Lambdas and signals.** Variadic syntax shall be usable with lambdas and signal callback handlers wherever function syntax is permitted, with behavior consistent with named functions.  11. **Built-in interoperability.** The runtime shall expose a documented mechanism for built-in/native methods to declare variadic parameter behavior consistent with script-level variadic functions.  12. **Editor support.** The editor shall provide syntax highlighting, autocompletion, and inline documentation for variadic declarations and calls.  13. **Documentation.** User-facing documentation and examples shall be provided.  ## Error Handling  - Declaring more than one variadic parameter shall be a parse/compile error. - Placing the variadic parameter anywhere other than the final position shall be a parse error. - Passing arguments that violate a declared variadic type shall raise a runtime error consistent with existing typed-parameter errors. - Misuse of the forwarding/spread construct shall produce clear compile or runtime diagnostics.  ## Non-Functional Requirements  - No measurable regression in call performance for non-variadic functions. - Variadic calls shall have performance overhead comparable to existing dynamic-argument mechanisms. - The feature shall be backward compatible; existing scripts shall continue to parse and run unchanged. - Implementation shall not break existing method binding, reflection, or GDExtension interoperability.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - A function declared with named parameters plus a variadic parameter can be called with zero, one, or many surplus arguments and receives the expected values. - A wrapper function can forward its variadic arguments to another function without loss or reordering. - Typed variadic parameters raise the expected runtime error on invalid argument types. - Static analysis and editor tooling recognize variadic declarations. - Behavior is covered by automated tests and documented.  ## Out of Scope  - Overload resolution based on variadic arity. - Named or keyword argument support.

issue_title: Inclusive version of take_while
requirement: The iterator API shall provide `take_while_inclusive` as an inclusive variant of `take_while`, with the signature `fn take_while_inclusive<F>(self, predicate: F) -> TakeWhileInclusive<Self, F> where F: FnMut(&Self::Item) -> bool`. The adapter shall yield each element for which `predicate` returns `true`; upon the first element for which `predicate` returns `false`, it shall yield that element and then terminate.
