issue_title: x/tools/gopls: support for bazel-based projects
requirement: gopls (x/tools/gopls) shall support Go projects built with Bazel as a first-class build system. When a workspace is Bazel-based, gopls shall obtain Go package, file, import, and dependency metadata from Bazel instead of relying only on `go list`/`go.mod`, and shall use that metadata to provide standard language features—completion, go-to-definition, find references, hover, document/workspace symbols, rename, formatting, and diagnostics—for Bazel `go_library`, `go_binary`, and `go_test` targets and their dependencies. Support shall include: detection of Bazel workspaces via `WORKSPACE`, `WORKSPACE.bazel`, `MODULE.bazel`, and `BUILD`/`BUILD.bazel` files containing rules_go targets; acquisition of build metadata through Bazel query/cquery/aquery or an equivalent stable Bazel interface; mapping of Bazel labels to Go import paths and source files; inclusion of generated Go files from `bazel-bin`/`bazel-out`; resolution of external dependencies from Bazel external repositories; correct handling of Bazel convenience symlinks and execroot paths without duplicate packages; respect for build tags, cgo, and platform constraints; cache invalidation when `BUILD`, `WORKSPACE`, `MODULE.bazel`, or generated files change; configuration for Bazel executable, workspace root, and query flags; and graceful degradation with actionable errors when Bazel metadata is unavailable. Acceptance is met when, in a rules_go/gazelle Bazel workspace without `go.mod` or GOPATH layout, go-to-definition on imports resolves to the correct Bazel target or external source, completion includes dependency and generated symbols, diagnostics align with `bazel build` for the target, and editing a `BUILD.bazel` dependency updates gopls behavior without restart.

issue_title: cmd/go: subcommand as git merge tool for go.mod merge conflicts
requirement: **Requirement: Add `go mod merge` as a Git merge driver/tool for `go.mod`**  `cmd/go` must add a `go mod merge` subcommand that semantically merges conflicting `go.mod` files. It must resolve merge conflicts without network access and be usable as both a Git merge driver and a Git mergetool.  **Command-line interface** - `go mod merge [-o output] <base> <local> <remote>`: parse three module files and write the merged result to `output`, defaulting to `local`. - Git merge-driver mode: accept `%O %A %B %L %P` (base, current, other, marker size, path), merge into `%A`, and use the remaining arguments only for diagnostics. - Git mergetool mode: accept `$BASE $LOCAL $REMOTE $MERGED`, merge into `$MERGED`. - Document the Git configuration recipe:   - `.gitattributes`: `go.mod merge=go`   - `git config merge.go.driver 'go mod merge %O %A %B %L %P'`  **Merge behavior** - Parse all inputs with the same parser used by `go mod edit`. Invalid input must produce a diagnostic and non-zero exit. - Merge `module`, `go`, and `toolchain` as scalar directives: take a one-sided change, accept identical changes, and report an unresolved conflict when both sides change differently. - Merge `require`, `exclude`, `replace`, and `retract` as keyed sets using the base to distinguish one-sided changes from concurrent changes. - Include additions from either side and honor removals when the other side did not change the same entry. - For a `require` entry changed on both sides to different versions, resolve to the higher version. For any other entry changed on both sides to different values, report an unresolved conflict. - Preserve comments where practical and format output canonically as `go mod edit -fmt` would. - Never emit Git conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`). - Must not access the network, run `go mod tidy`, or modify `go.sum`.  **Exit and error behavior** - Exit 0 after writing a valid merged `go.mod`. - On unresolved conflicts, leave the output file unchanged, write a diagnostic naming the conflicting directives to stderr, and exit non-zero. - On usage or parse errors, write a diagnostic to stderr and exit non-zero.  **Acceptance criteria** - Tests cover clean merges, one-sided additions/removals/updates, concurrent identical edits, concurrent conflicting edits, comment preservation, and Git integration. - Documentation covers Git merge-driver and mergetool setup, limitations, and standalone use with three files. - `go mod merge` operates correctly without Git when invoked directly on base, local, and remote files.

issue_title: cmd/compile: implement powerpc 32-bit backend (ppc32)
requirement: # Requirement: Implement PowerPC 32-bit (ppc32) Backend in `cmd/compile`  ## Description The Go compiler (`cmd/compile`) shall support generating correct machine code for 32-bit big-endian PowerPC (`GOARCH=ppc`) on Linux, enabling the Go toolchain to build and run Go programs for `linux/ppc`.  ## Functional Requirements 1. Add an architecture-specific compiler backend for ppc32 (e.g., `src/cmd/compile/internal/ppc`) that implements SSA lowering, instruction selection, register allocation, stack frame layout, calling convention/ABI, and object file emission. 2. The compiler shall accept `GOOS=linux GOARCH=ppc` and shall report `linux/ppc` in `go tool dist list`. 3. Generate correct code for all Go language constructs and runtime features on ppc32, including goroutines, channels, select, defer, panic/recover, interfaces, maps, slices, strings, closures, reflection, 64-bit integer and floating-point operations, complex numbers, atomics, and memory synchronization. 4. Conform to the 32-bit PowerPC ELF ABI for Linux, including endianness, alignment, register usage, stack layout, and calling conventions. 5. Integrate with `cmd/internal/obj`, `cmd/asm`, `cmd/link`, and the runtime as required to produce valid ppc32 ELF executables. 6. Support cross-compilation to `linux/ppc` from supported host platforms. 7. Ensure the Go standard library builds for `linux/ppc` with only documented platform-specific exclusions. 8. Preserve existing compiler behavior and ensure all currently supported architectures continue to build and pass tests.  ## Acceptance Criteria - `GOOS=linux GOARCH=ppc go build` compiles a representative Go program into a valid 32-bit PowerPC ELF executable. - The resulting executable runs correctly on a ppc32 Linux system or emulator and produces expected output. - `GOOS=linux GOARCH=ppc go test -short std` passes, or any failures are limited to documented unsupported platform-specific tests. - Architecture-independent compiler tests and ppc32-specific tests pass. - `go tool dist list` includes `linux/ppc`. - All existing supported architectures continue to build and pass tests.  ## Out of Scope - 32-bit little-endian PowerPC (`ppcle`) and non-Linux ppc32 operating systems, unless separately specified.

issue_title: cmd/go: allow verifying vendored code
requirement: The `go` command (cmd/go) shall provide a supported way to verify vendored code. When a module uses a `vendor` directory, `go mod verify` must not fail solely because vendor mode is active; it shall verify that every vendored dependency listed in `vendor/modules.txt` matches the integrity information recorded for that module, using `go.sum` and `vendor/modules.txt`. If existing vendoring metadata is insufficient to verify the vendored file set, `go mod vendor` shall record the additional per-module integrity metadata needed for later verification. Verification shall detect modified, missing, or extra files in vendored dependencies; report each affected module and file path; exit with a non-zero status if any vendored dependency cannot be verified; and exit successfully when all vendored dependencies are verified. It shall operate offline and shall not modify the `vendor` directory.

issue_title: Support multiple windows for desktop shells
requirement: Desktop shells must support creating and managing multiple application windows simultaneously, rather than being limited to a single window.

issue_title: Implement PlatformView support on macOS
requirement: The framework must support `PlatformView` on macOS, allowing applications to embed and interact with native macOS views in their UI.

requirement: The application shall support Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, allowing users to access its supported features through compatible vehicle infotainment systems.

issue_title: DataLoader with option to re-use worker processes
requirement: The DataLoader shall provide an option to keep worker processes alive after an iteration completes, allowing them to be reused by subsequent iterations and reducing process startup overhead. When disabled, workers shall retain the existing shutdown behavior.

issue_title: [RFC] RPC Based Distributed Model Parallel
requirement: Add RPC-based distributed model parallelism that allows a model to be partitioned across multiple workers and its components to communicate during execution via RPC.

issue_title: OpenCL 3.0 support: support every GPU on earth through rusticl
requirement: Rusticl must implement OpenCL 3.0 support for GPUs supported by its drivers, exposing the corresponding OpenCL 3.0 APIs and capabilities.

issue_title: Feature Request: Easier to extend base RNN implementation
requirement: The base RNN implementation should provide a clear, modular interface that makes it easier for developers to extend its behavior without modifying core code.

issue_title: Code Push / Hot Update / out of band updates
requirement: The application shall support over-the-air code updates so users can receive and apply hot fixes and other out-of-band updates without reinstalling the app or waiting for an app store release.

issue_title: Enable "hot reload" (not just "hot restart") for Flutter Web
requirement: Flutter Web must support hot reload, applying code changes to a running app without a full restart and preserving its current state.

issue_title: Return attention weights in nn.Transformer
requirement: Extend `nn.Transformer` to optionally return the attention weights produced by its attention layers alongside the standard output.

requirement: Add a global GPU flag that lets users enable or disable GPU acceleration for all supported operations.

issue_title: Customizable project structure (platforms)
requirement: The system shall allow users to customize the project structure for each supported platform, including the organization and naming of platform-specific files and directories.

requirement: Flutter Web should support running `compute` callbacks on a separate background thread, such as a Web Worker, so computation does not block the UI thread while preserving the existing API and result behavior.

issue_title: Implement PlatformView support on Windows
requirement: Windows must support the PlatformView API, allowing applications to create, display, interact with, and manage the lifecycle of native platform views.

issue_title: encoding/xml: add support for xml version 1.1
requirement: The encoding/xml package shall support XML 1.1 in addition to XML 1.0. The decoder shall accept an XML declaration with version="1.1", apply XML 1.1 character validity rules by accepting character references to restricted characters, rejecting literal restricted characters, and rejecting NUL, and normalize XML 1.1 line endings (#xD#xA, #xD, #x85, #x2028) to #xA. The encoder shall allow callers to select XML 1.1 output and shall emit a matching XML declaration, escaping restricted characters as character references. Existing XML 1.0 behavior, APIs, and error handling shall remain backward compatible.

issue_title: cmd/go: allow serving module under the subdirectory of git repository
requirement: The `go` command must support fetching and resolving Go modules whose source code resides in a subdirectory of a Git repository. To enable this, the `go-import` meta tag must accept an optional `<subdir>` field in the format `<import-prefix> <vcs> <repo-root> [<subdir>]`. When `<subdir>` is present, the `go` command must treat the specified subdirectory as the module root within the repository; when absent, the repository root is the module root. For direct VCS operations, the `go` command must use `<subdir>` to locate the module's `go.mod`, to filter version tags prefixed with `<subdir>/` (e.g., `sub/v1.0.0`), and to extract the module contents from the correct subdirectory. The module proxy protocol must also support module paths that include subdirectories, allowing proxies to serve such modules by mapping the module path to the repository root and subdirectory. The `go` command's documentation must be updated to describe the optional `<subdir>` element and the behavior for modules in subdirectories.

issue_title: Support home and lock screen widgets
requirement: The app must support widgets that users can add to their device’s home screen and lock screen.

issue_title: Support soft hyphenation (line breaks at U+00AD plus rendering a hyphen at the end of the line)
requirement: Text layout must treat U+00AD (soft hyphen) as a discretionary line-break point: keep it invisible when no break occurs, and render a hyphen at the end of the line when a break occurs there.

issue_title: Add support for visionOS
requirement: The project shall support visionOS as a target platform, allowing it to be built and run on compatible devices.

issue_title: reflect: NamedOf
requirement: **Requirement: `reflect.NamedOf`**  The `reflect` package shall add a public function `NamedOf(pkgPath, name string, t Type) Type` that constructs and returns a `reflect.Type` representing a defined (named) type. The returned type shall have `PkgPath() == pkgPath`, `Name() == name`, and `Kind() == t.Kind()`, and its underlying type shall be `t` (if `t` is a named type, its underlying type shall be used). The function shall return the same `reflect.Type` value for repeated calls with identical `pkgPath`, `name`, and `t`. If a named type with the given `pkgPath` and `name` already exists with a different underlying type, the function shall panic. The function shall panic if `pkgPath` or `name` is invalid. The returned type shall be usable in all contexts that accept a `reflect.Type`, including `reflect.New`, `reflect.Zero`, `reflect.SliceOf`, `reflect.StructOf`, and as an element in composite type construction. The function shall be safe for concurrent use.

issue_title: Add structs in GDScript
requirement: GDScript shall support user-defined struct types that group named fields and can be instantiated and accessed as a single value.

issue_title: Add support for nullable static types in GDScript
requirement: GDScript should support nullable static types, allowing variables and parameters with declared types to explicitly accept `null` while preserving static type checking.

issue_title: AVIF codec support
requirement: The software shall support reading and writing images in the AVIF format.

issue_title: Add a Trait system for GDScript
requirement: GDScript shall support defining and composing traits—reusable sets of methods and properties that classes can adopt to share behavior without relying on inheritance.

issue_title: Allow explicitly defining interfaces in GDScript
requirement: Add support for explicitly declaring interfaces in GDScript, allowing classes to implement them and enabling type checking against interface-defined members.

issue_title: Create a Swarm/Mob/Flock/etc system for managing large amounts of entities
requirement: Provide a Swarm/Mob/Flock system that enables users to group and manage large numbers of entities as a collective.

issue_title: Expose a zero allocation API to Godot C# bindings
requirement: Godot C# bindings shall expose an API that allows callers to perform supported operations without allocating managed memory.

issue_title: Allow release mode builds to run on simulators
requirement: The build system shall support building and running applications in release mode on simulators.

issue_title: Add a "Mask2D" node (and/or a "mask_parent" property for Sprite2D)
requirement: Add 2D masking support so a `Sprite2D` can use another node, such as a parent, as a mask that clips its visible content. This may be implemented with a `Mask2D` node, a `mask_parent` property on `Sprite2D`, or both.

issue_title: Add public/private access modifiers to GDScript and autocompletion improvements
requirement: Add explicit `public` and `private` access modifiers to GDScript members and methods, and improve autocompletion to support the modifier syntax and respect symbol visibility.

issue_title: Implement a Rendering Compositor
requirement: Implement a rendering compositor that combines rendered layers in the correct order into a single final output, supporting configurable layer ordering and compositing behavior.

issue_title: Replace GridMap with an improved TileMap3D node (inspired by the new 2D TileMap)
requirement: Replace the GridMap node with an improved TileMap3D node that brings the design and workflow of the new 2D TileMap to 3D tile-based scene creation.

issue_title: Add "refactor" tooling to rename symbols in the script editor
requirement: The script editor shall provide a rename-symbol refactoring tool that renames a selected symbol and updates its references throughout the relevant script.

issue_title: Add array unpacking/destructuring to GDScript
requirement: GDScript shall support array unpacking, allowing multiple variables to be declared or assigned from the elements of an array in a single statement.

issue_title: Add proper and complete support for multi-pass shaders
requirement: The rendering system shall support multi-pass shaders by allowing shaders to define ordered passes, configure each pass’s resources and render state, pass intermediate outputs between dependent passes, and use the final pass’s output for rendering, while preserving support for existing single-pass shaders.

issue_title: Add support for global plugins/universal addons
requirement: The system shall support global plugins (universal add-ons) that can be installed once and made available across all applicable projects or workspaces.

issue_title: Add support for multiple displays/screens/monitors in Godot editor
requirement: The Godot editor must support multi-monitor setups, allowing users to arrange and use editor windows and panels across connected displays.

issue_title: Implement Terrain
requirement: The system shall support terrain by providing a terrain representation that can be created, loaded, and used by the application.

issue_title: Add union types to Typed GDScript
requirement: Typed GDScript shall support union types, allowing variables, parameters, and return values to accept values matching any one of multiple declared types; type checking must reject values that match none of them.

issue_title: Calinou doesn't sleep
requirement: The system should allow Calinou to sleep when needed.

issue_title: Godot C# GDExtension Roadmap Discussion
requirement: The project should define and publish a roadmap for C# support in Godot GDExtension, outlining planned capabilities, milestones, and current status.

issue_title: Need negative trait bound
requirement: The language should support negative trait bounds, allowing generic constraints to require that a type does not implement a specified trait, and enforce those constraints during type checking.

issue_title: Crate local state for procedural macros?
requirement: Provide procedural macros with state that is shared across invocations within a crate, isolated from other crates, and reset for each compilation.

issue_title: Include images in rustdoc output
requirement: Rustdoc shall include images referenced in documentation and display them in the generated HTML output.

issue_title: Provide a means of turning iterators into fixed-size arrays
requirement: Add an API for collecting an iterator’s elements into a fixed-size array of a specified size.

issue_title: Add function to make paths absolute, which is different from canonicalization
requirement: Add a function that converts a relative path to an absolute path using the current working directory without canonicalizing it; it must not resolve symlinks or otherwise require filesystem canonicalization. Absolute paths should be returned unchanged.

issue_title: Proc macros: ability to refer to a specific crate/symbol (something similar to `$crate`)
requirement: Provide procedural macros with a way to reference a specific crate or symbol hygienically, similar to `$crate`, so generated code resolves to the intended definition regardless of the caller’s scope or dependency renaming.

issue_title: Using std::io::{Read, Write, Cursor} in a nostd environment
requirement: Provide `no_std`-compatible `Read`, `Write`, and `Cursor` APIs so they can be used in environments where `std` is unavailable.

issue_title: Initializing array of Option<T> using [None; n] syntax should not require std::marker::Copy for T
requirement: Allow `[None; n]` to initialize an array of `Option<T>` without requiring `T: Copy`, since `None` contains no `T` value to copy.

issue_title: Inclusive version of take_while
requirement: Add an inclusive `take_while` iterator adapter that yields elements while the predicate is true and also yields the first element for which it is false, then stops.

issue_title: [libs] Add `TcpStream::keepalive` and `TcpStream::set_keepalive`
requirement: Add `TcpStream::keepalive` and `TcpStream::set_keepalive` methods to query and configure the TCP keepalive setting for a stream.

issue_title: Support Windows kernel mode for driver development
requirement: The software must support creating, building, and debugging Windows kernel-mode driver projects.

issue_title: Add ability to ignore tests at runtime.
requirement: The test framework shall allow individual tests to be marked as ignored at runtime, skipping their execution and reporting them as skipped.

issue_title: Struct initializer `..x` syntax should work for other structs with structurally equal subset of fields
requirement: Allow `..x` in a struct initializer when `x` has a structurally matching subset of the destination struct’s fields, copying those fields into the initialized struct.

issue_title: Feature request: Use 'trampolines' to make most of the body of a generic function non-generic
requirement: The system should support trampolines that let generic functions delegate most of their work to a shared non-generic implementation, reducing duplicated code while preserving type-specific behavior.

issue_title: Subslice search
requirement: The search API shall support searching within a specified subslice, considering only elements in that subslice and reporting any match relative to its bounds.

issue_title: Use mold as default linker?
requirement: Configure the build system to use mold as the default linker.

issue_title: Add Vec::contains_ref which is worse for inference but less restrictive than Vec::contains
requirement: Add `Vec::contains_ref` to test whether a vector contains a value by reference, allowing element types to be compared with a different query type than `Vec::contains` permits, even if this broader generic signature makes type inference less reliable.

issue_title: Scan is overly specialized
requirement: Generalize the scan functionality so it can support a broader range of inputs and use cases rather than being tied to a single specialized scenario.

issue_title: rustdoc: `--enable-index-page` integration with cargo?
requirement: Cargo should expose `rustdoc`’s `--enable-index-page` option through `cargo doc` and forward it to rustdoc when generating documentation.

issue_title: lint against unexpectedly late drop for temporaries in match scrutinee expressions
requirement: Add a lint that warns when a temporary created while evaluating a `match` scrutinee is dropped only after the selected arm finishes, since this extended lifetime can cause surprising behavior.

issue_title: encoding/json: no way to preserve the order of map keys
requirement: Provide an option or data type in `encoding/json` that preserves JSON object key order when decoding and re-encoding, instead of losing the order in maps.

issue_title: plugin: add Windows support
requirement: The plugin must support Windows, including installation, loading, and operation on supported Windows environments, while preserving its existing functionality.

issue_title: cmd/compile: implement powerpc 32-bit backend (ppc32)
requirement: The `cmd/compile` compiler must support the 32-bit PowerPC architecture (ppc32), including generating code for ppc32 targets.

issue_title: Make `pub` in a binary equivalent to `pub(crate)` for diagnostics
requirement: For visibility-related diagnostics in binary crates, treat `pub` items as equivalent to `pub(crate)` items.

issue_title: runtime: implement WASM-GC
requirement: The runtime shall support the WebAssembly Garbage Collection (WASM-GC) proposal, allowing modules that use GC types and operations to be loaded and executed.

issue_title: net/http: support HTTP/3
requirement: The `net/http` package should support HTTP/3 for sending and serving HTTP requests.

issue_title: Provide UnixPath and WindowsPath (ditto PathBuf) on all platforms
requirement: Expose `UnixPath`, `UnixPathBuf`, `WindowsPath`, and `WindowsPathBuf` on every supported platform, so callers can work with either platform’s path types regardless of the host OS.

issue_title: database/sql: missing escape functions
requirement: Add a standard API to `database/sql` for safely escaping values embedded in SQL statements, avoiding the need for driver-specific escape functions.

issue_title: x/tools/gopls: support change signature refactoring
requirement: gopls should support change-signature refactoring for Go functions and methods, allowing users to modify parameters or results and automatically update all affected declarations and call sites consistently.

issue_title: x/tools/gopls: annotations for implementations of interfaces
requirement: gopls should annotate interface declarations with the concrete types that implement them, so users can discover implementations directly in their editor.

issue_title: x/pkgsite: API for pkg.go.dev
requirement: pkg.go.dev should provide a documented API that allows clients to programmatically retrieve package and module information available on the site.

issue_title: x/pkgsite: generate static docs
requirement: The `x/pkgsite` tool should support generating static HTML documentation for Go packages that can be served without running the pkgsite application.

requirement: The `cmd/link` tool must support reading and linking object files produced by Microsoft Visual C++ (MSVC), including their symbols and relocations.

issue_title: plugin: Add support for closing plugins
requirement: The plugin system shall provide a way to close an active plugin, stopping its activity and releasing its resources.

issue_title: cmd/go: 'go mod why' should have an answer for every module in 'go list -m all'
requirement: `go mod why -m all` must report an explanation for every module listed by `go list -m all`, including modules that are not needed by any imported package.

requirement: The `cmd/fix` command should automatically detect simple, well-defined deprecations and rewrite them to their recommended replacements while preserving behavior.

requirement: The `go` command should provide a way to verify that vendored dependencies match the versions and contents expected by the module, and report missing or modified vendored files.

issue_title: proposal: database/sql: support a way to perform bulk actions
requirement: Extend `database/sql` with a standard way to execute a statement for multiple sets of arguments as a single bulk operation, allowing drivers to perform the work efficiently and report errors through the API.

requirement: Add a `reflect.NamedOf` API that returns the `reflect.Type` for a specified named type, including instantiated generic types, without requiring a runtime value.

issue_title: [Feature request] Let DistributedSampler take a Sampler as input

requirement: The system shall include an embedding layer and positional encodings in the Transformer architecture.

requirement: The system shall support integration of DeepSpeed with PyTorch Distributed for distributed model training.

Specifically:  1. When a module path includes a path suffix that corresponds to a subdirectory within a Git repository (e.g., a module path of `example.com/repo/sub/module` where the repository is at `example.com/repo` and the module resides in `sub/module`), the `go` command shall locate the repository, check out the appropriate revision, and use the contents of that subdirectory as the module root.  2. Version tags for such modules shall be recognized using the subdirectory-prefixed form (e.g., `sub/module/v1.2.3`) in addition to the standard form, consistent with the Go modules tagging conventions for nested modules.  3. Module zip archives and module source trees produced for such modules shall contain only the files within the subdirectory, with paths relative to the module root.  4. `go get`, `go mod download`, and `go list -m` shall correctly resolve versions, download, and verify such modules, including honoring the module's `go.mod` file located in the subdirectory.  5. The go command shall reject or report an error when the specified subdirectory does not exist at the requested revision or does not contain a valid `go.mod` file.  6. Existing behavior for modules located at the repository root shall remain unchanged.

When a `Sampler` is provided, `DistributedSampler` shall use the indices produced by that `Sampler` as the pool of indices to be partitioned among the distributed processes, instead of enumerating indices from the `Dataset`. 2. All ranks within the same distributed run shall receive the identical index sequence from the wrapped `Sampler`, ensuring that the resulting per-rank partitions are disjoint and their union covers the full index set without duplication or omission. 3. Existing behavior shall be preserved: if no `Sampler` is provided, `DistributedSampler` shall continue to operate on the `Dataset` as it currently does, maintaining backward compatibility with existing code and the current constructor signature. 4. The implementation shall validate that the input is mutually exclusive where applicable (i.e., a `Sampler` is supplied in place of direct dataset index enumeration), and shall raise a clear, informative error if the provided object is not a valid `Sampler`. 5. Padding behavior (replicating indices to evenly divide the index pool across ranks) shall apply equivalently whether the index pool originates from the `Dataset` or from the provided `Sampler`. 6. The new functionality shall be documented in the API reference for `DistributedSampler`, including usage examples demonstrating how to wrap a custom `Sampler` for distributed training.

issue_title: Feature Requst: Add regex support to test filters
requirement: ## Feature Requirement: Regular Expression Support for Test Filters  ### Summary Test filters currently support only simple matching (exact names, literal substrings, and glob-like patterns). Users need the ability to select tests using regular expressions, so that large suites can be narrowed by patterns that literal matching cannot express (e.g., `^Suite::.*_smoke$`, `.*[Ff]laky.*`, alternation across several test names).  ### Motivation Selecting a subset of tests by pattern is a core daily workflow. Without regex, users must resort to multiple filters, broad literals that over-select, or external scripting. Regex support makes test selection expressive and precise, and reduces the number of filters needed for a single run.  ### Functional Requirements  1. **Filter syntax**    - Each filter option that currently accepts a literal or glob pattern (e.g. test name, file path, tag/label) must additionally accept a regular expression.    - A filter is interpreted as a regex when it is explicitly marked as such (e.g. a dedicated `regex:` prefix or a separate `--filter-regex` style option). Literal/glob behavior must remain the default so existing configurations are unaffected.  2. **Matching semantics**    - Regex matching is applied against the full identifying string of the test (e.g. the fully qualified test name, including suite/class and file path components as defined by the existing filter contract).    - Matching shall be unanchored by default: a pattern matches if it is found anywhere in the target string. Users shall be able to anchor explicitly with `^` and `$`.    - Case sensitivity shall be configurable; the default must match the behavior of existing filters (case-sensitive unless the existing option already provides a case-insensitive mode).  3. **Engine and portability**    - Use the standard regular expression syntax of the host language/runtime, and document the exact flavor supported (e.g. PCRE, ECMAScript, POSIX ERE, Go RE2), including which constructs are unsupported.    - The chosen engine must be a linear-time engine (no catastrophic backtracking) so that pathological user patterns cannot hang the test runner.  4. **Combination with existing filters**    - Regex filters must compose with all existing filter types using the same precedence and conjunctive/disjunctive rules that literal filters use today.    - Multiple regex filters of the same type must be OR-ed together (a test matching any one is selected), consistent with current multi-value filter semantics.  5. **Error handling and validation**    - An invalid regular expression must be detected before the test run starts and must produce a clear error message identifying the offending pattern, the reason it is invalid, and the filter/option that supplied it.    - An invalid regex must cause the run to fail fast with a non-zero exit status rather than silently matching nothing or aborting mid-run.  6. **Reporting**    - The run output must report how many tests were selected by each filter and the total selected, so users can confirm their pattern behaves as expected.    - When a filter selects zero tests, the existing "no tests matched" behavior must be preserved (including any configured failure or warning policy).  7. **Documentation**    - Document regex filter syntax, the supported regex flavor, matching semantics, examples, and precedence relative to other filter options.    - Provide at least one worked example showing a literal filter and its equivalent regex filter.  ### Non-Goals - Adding new filter target types (e.g. filtering on test duration or runtime output) beyond enabling regex on existing targets. - Supporting regex in assertion or matcher expressions.  ### Acceptance Criteria - A user can select tests with a pattern such as `^integration::api::.*_test$` using only filter configuration, with no source-code changes. - A pattern that matches nothing yields the documented zero-match behavior and message. - An invalid pattern (e.g. `*[`) is rejected at startup with an actionable error message and a non-zero exit code. - Existing configurations and scripts that use literal/glob filters continue to produce identical results. - Automated tests cover: valid match, no match, anchored and unanchored patterns, case-insensitive mode, multiple regex filters, invalid pattern handling, and precedence when regex and literal filters are combined.

issue_title: Implement namespaces in GDScript
requirement: **Requirement: Namespace Support in GDScript**  **Summary:** GDScript shall support namespaces so that classes, functions, constants, and enums declared in different modules or scripts can share the same identifier without collision, and so that related symbols can be grouped and referenced in a qualified form.  **Description:** Currently, all global class names (`class_name`) and autoloaded singletons share a single flat global scope. As projects and add-ons grow, name collisions occur, and third-party plugins cannot safely reuse common names. The language shall provide a namespace mechanism that:  1. Allows a script to declare the namespace it belongs to. 2. Allows symbols within a namespace to be referenced using qualified names (e.g., `Namespace.ClassName`). 3. Allows importing or aliasing a namespace to shorten qualified references within a script. 4. Preserves full backward compatibility: existing scripts without namespace declarations shall compile and behave identically.  **Functional Requirements:**  - FR-1: A script shall be able to declare a namespace, and all `class_name` declarations within it shall be registered under that namespace. - FR-2: Two classes with the same name in different namespaces shall coexist without error or ambiguity. - FR-3: Qualified references (`Namespace.Symbol`) shall resolve to the correct symbol at parse time where possible, and report a clear error when the symbol is not found. - FR-4: Unqualified references shall resolve first to the current namespace, then to imported namespaces, then to the global scope; ambiguous unqualified references shall produce a compile-time error. - FR-5: Namespaces shall support nesting (e.g., `A.B.C`). - FR-6: An import or alias mechanism shall allow a script to bring a namespace into local scope with an optional alias. - FR-7: Namespaces shall apply to functions, constants, enums, and inner classes, not only top-level classes. - FR-8: The editor shall provide autocompletion and go-to-definition for namespaced symbols. - FR-9: Namespace information shall be preserved in exported/serialized script resources and in `.tscn`/`.tres` references so that saved scenes resolve correctly after reload.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  - NFR-1: Scripts without namespace declarations shall produce identical bytecode and runtime behavior to the current implementation. - NFR-2: Namespace resolution shall occur at parse/analysis time and shall not add measurable overhead to function calls at runtime. - NFR-3: Error messages for namespace-related issues shall identify the file, line, column, and the conflicting or missing symbol.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - AC-1: Two plugins each defining `class_name Node` inside distinct namespaces load together without conflict. - AC-2: Referencing an undefined qualified symbol produces a compile error naming the namespace and symbol. - AC-3: An unqualified reference matching symbols in two imported namespaces produces an ambiguity error. - AC-4: The existing GDScript test suite passes unchanged. - AC-5: A scene referencing a namespaced script loads correctly after the project is closed and reopened. - AC-6: Editor autocompletion lists members of a namespace after typing `Namespace.`.  **Out of Scope:** Changes to C# or GDExtension name resolution; runtime dynamic namespace creation; automatic migration of existing projects to use namespaces.

issue_title: lint against unexpectedly late drop for temporaries in match scrutinee expressions
requirement: ## Requirement: Lint against unexpectedly late drop of temporaries in a `match` scrutinee  ### Motivation  Temporaries that are created while evaluating the scrutinee of a `match` expression are kept alive until the *end of the whole `match` expression* — i.e. after the selected arm's body (and after any match guards) has run — rather than being dropped at the end of the scrutinee evaluation. This is frequently surprising, especially for types with meaningful `Drop` implementations such as `MutexGuard`, `Ref`/`RefMut`, `File`, `String`, `Vec`, or custom RAII types, because the user may reasonably expect the resource to be released before the arm body executes (e.g. to avoid holding a lock while doing work, or to release a file handle before the "done" message is printed).  The linter should make this behavior visible so that users can either accept it explicitly or restructure the code by hoisting the temporary into a `let` binding before the `match`.  ### Behavior  * The linter must inspect `match` expressions and determine whether the scrutinee expression creates one or more temporary values that:   * implement `Drop` (directly or transitively), and   * are not moved out of / bound by the match arms (i.e. are still owned by the temporary scope at the end of the `match`). * When such temporaries exist, a warning must be emitted, pointing at the offending temporary in the scrutinee. * The diagnostic message must state that the temporary is dropped at the end of the `match` expression (after the arm body/guard), and must suggest hoisting it into a `let` binding before the `match` if earlier release is intended. * The lint must be `allow`-by-default (e.g. in the `nursery`/`pedantic` group), and must be configurable through the standard lint attribute and configuration mechanisms (`#[allow(clippy::...)])`, `#[warn(...)]`, `#[deny(...)]`, and the `-A/-W/-D` command-line flags), including for the whole crate or a specific module. * The lint must not fire when:   * the scrutinee contains no temporaries with drop semantics (e.g. `match x { ... }` where `x: Copy` or is a plain binding);   * the temporary is explicitly bound by the arm patterns (e.g. `match mutex.lock().unwrap() { g if g > 0 => ... }` where the guard value is moved into the pattern) — in that case ownership is transferred and no late drop occurs;   * the temporary is explicitly dropped or `mem::forget`-ed by the user;   * the scrutinee is a `let`-bound variable or otherwise contains no temporary expression at all. * The lint should also recognize the equivalent `if let` and `while let` scrutinee temporaries, which exhibit the same late-drop behavior, or at minimum must not report false positives for them.  ### Examples  Lint (warning expected):  ```rust fn example(m: &Mutex<i32>) {     // The MutexGuard temporary is dropped only at the end of the `match`,     // i.e. after the arm body has run.     match m.lock().unwrap() {         0 => println!("zero"),         _ => println!("other"),     } } ```  No lint:  ```rust fn example(m: &Mutex<i32>) {     let guard = m.lock().unwrap(); // dropped at the end of this statement     match *guard {         0 => println!("zero"),         _ => println!("other"),     } } ```  No lint (value moved into the pattern, so no late drop):  ```rust fn example(m: &Mutex<i32>) {     match m.lock().unwrap() {         g if *g > 0 => println!("positive"),         _ => println!("other"),     } } ```  ### Implementation notes  * The check must be based on the typed AST/HIR of the scrutinee: collect the temporaries created in the scrutinee expression, keep only those whose type needs dropping, and exclude those whose ownership is moved by the arm patterns. * Temporaries that are dropped in a nested closure or in an inner scope must not be reported. * The diagnostic should be emitted once per offending scrutinee (not once per temporary) to avoid duplicate noise. * The lint must be documented in the linter's lint list with a clear title, explanation, and the before/after example above.

issue_title: [webview_flutter] Add Windows support
requirement: **Requirement ID:** REQ-WEBVIEW-001 **Title:** Windows Platform Support for `webview_flutter`  **Requirement Statement:** The `webview_flutter` plugin shall support the Windows platform (Windows 10 and later), enabling Flutter applications to embed, display, and interact with web content on Windows using the plugin's existing platform-agnostic Dart API without code changes.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. The Windows implementation shall use Microsoft Edge WebView2 as the underlying web content engine. 2. The implementation shall conform to the `webview_flutter_platform_interface` contract, including WebView widget creation, URL loading, navigation (load, back, forward, reload), navigation delegation, JavaScript execution, JavaScript channel messaging, and cookie management. 3. Windows-specific configuration options (e.g., WebView2 user data folder path) shall be exposed through the plugin's existing platform-specific configuration mechanism. 4. The Windows implementation shall be registered automatically via standard Flutter plugin tooling, such that adding `webview_flutter` to `pubspec.yaml` is sufficient for a Windows build. 5. If the WebView2 Runtime is not present on the host machine, the plugin shall fail with a clear, actionable error message rather than an unhandled exception.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - A Flutter application targeting Windows using `webview_flutter` compiles and runs without manual native project configuration. - Platform interface conformance tests pass on Windows. - Core operations — loading a URL, navigating history, and evaluating JavaScript — behave as defined by the platform interface.

issue_title: Add a Trait system for GDScript
requirement: The GDScript language parser, compiler, and runtime shall implement a trait-based composition system that enables modular, reusable behaviors across classes independent of single-inheritance hierarchies. The system shall:  1. Provide syntax for declaring traits that can define method signatures, default method implementations, and required property declarations. 2. Provide syntax for classes to consume one or more traits, binding the trait implementations directly into the consuming class scope. 3. Enforce deterministic conflict resolution rules when multiple applied traits share identical method or property identifiers, requiring explicit resolution or overriding by the consuming class. 4. Integrate with GDScript's static analyzer to validate that consuming classes satisfy all required property and method dependencies at parse/compile time. 5. Support runtime and static type checking to verify trait conformance, enabling script instances to be evaluated against applied traits using the `is` keyword and language reflection APIs.

issue_title: [Proposal] Data reading framework for PyTorch (Hive, MySQL, S3 etc.)
requirement: # Requirement: Unified Data Reading Framework for PyTorch  ## 1. Title  Unified Data Reading Framework for PyTorch — multi-backend data source access (Hive, MySQL, S3, local filesystem)  ## 2. Motivation  PyTorch training pipelines currently require bespoke, hand-written data loaders per storage backend. Reading from Hive tables, relational databases (MySQL/PostgreSQL), or object stores (S3-compatible) typically means implementing custom `torch.utils.data.Dataset`/`IterableDataset` subclasses, duplicating logic for schema decoding, sharding across ranks, batching, shuffling, caching, credentials handling, and retries for every project. This results in duplicated code, inconsistent behavior across distributed workers, poor failure semantics, and tight coupling of training code to infrastructure details.  A single, declarative data reading framework is required that abstracts storage backends behind a common interface, exposing records to PyTorch as standard `Dataset`/`IterableDataset` objects so that training code remains backend-agnostic.  ## 3. Goals  1. Provide a single, stable Python API for reading training/inference data from heterogeneous backends (Hive, MySQL, S3, local filesystem) with no change to training code when switching backends. 2. Expose read results through standard PyTorch constructs (`torch.utils.data.Dataset`, `torch.utils.data.IterableDataset`, `DataLoader`) including native multi-worker and distributed (DDP/FSDP) support. 3. Support declarative configuration (Python API + YAML/JSON config file) so pipelines are reproducible and versionable. 4. Support distributed-aware sharding, deterministic ordering, and reproducible shuffling across ranks and workers. 5. Support schema inference and type conversion (SQL types ↔ Python types ↔ `torch` dtypes), plus composable record-level transformation pipelines. 6. Support pluggable backends so that new sources can be added without modifying framework core code.  ## 4. Non-Goals (Out of Scope)  - Not a data processing/compute engine (no Spark-like query planning, joins, or aggregation). - Not a replacement for `torch.utils.data.DataLoader`; the framework integrates with it rather than reimplementing it. - Not a feature store, dataset versioning system, or model/data governance platform. - Not a distributed training framework; it must be compatible with existing PyTorch distributed launchers. - Backend-specific advanced features (e.g., Hive ACID transactional semantics, MySQL stored procedures) are out of scope.  ## 5. Functional Requirements  ### 5.1 Core Abstraction  - **FR-1.** The framework shall define a `DataSource` abstract base class representing a readable data source, with at minimum:   - `schema` property returning a resolved schema (column name → type, nullable flag);   - `read(...)` / iteration method yielding batches of records;   - `get_reader(config)` returning a configured reader instance. - **FR-2.** The framework shall define a `Reader` interface responsible for producing batches for a given `DataSource`, split/shard specification, and runtime context (rank, world size, worker id). - **FR-3.** The framework shall define a `Backend` plugin interface with methods `open()`, `read_batch(...)`, `close()`, `infer_schema()`, enabling third-party extension by subclassing and registering via an entry point/decorator. - **FR-4.** The framework shall provide a public factory function (e.g., `read(source_spec)` / `build_dataset(spec)`) that returns a `torch.utils.data.Dataset` or `IterableDataset` object based on the source type and configuration. - **FR-5.** All public classes, functions, and configuration keys shall be importable from a single top-level package namespace with stable, documented names and semantic versioning guarantees.  ### 5.2 Backend Connectors  - **FR-6. Hive.** Support reading from Hive tables via ThriftServer/metastore or JDBC. Requirements:   - Column selection and predicate pushdown (partition predicates, WHERE clauses) where supported;   - Partition-aware scanning (e.g., `dt=YYYY-MM-DD`) with partition pruning;   - Schema inference from metastore with explicit type override support;   - Support for ORC/Parquet/sequence-file underlying formats via HiveServer2 or direct object-store access. - **FR-7. MySQL.** Support reading from MySQL tables/views. Requirements:   - Connection pooling with configurable pool size and lifetime;   - Cursor-based streaming reads (server-side unbuffered cursors) to avoid loading full result sets into memory;   - Support for `WHERE`, `ORDER BY`, `LIMIT/OFFSET` clauses passed through from configuration;   - Consistent snapshot reads within a single reader instance where isolation level is configurable. - **FR-8. S3.** Support reading from S3 and S3-compatible object stores (MinIO, Ceph, R2). Requirements:   - Prefix/glob-based listing with optional recursive traversal;   - Support for CSV, JSON/JSONL, Parquet, and compressed variants (`.gz`, `.zst`, `.bz2`);   - Support for reading directly via `s3://` URIs in Hive/Hadoop-backed sources. - **FR-9. Local filesystem.** Support reading local files/directories using the same format handling as S3 for parity of behavior. - **FR-10.** Each backend shall be implemented as an independent plugin module; enabling/disabling a backend shall not require modification of framework core code or of other backends. - **FR-11.** Backends requiring optional third-party dependencies shall import them lazily and raise a clear, actionable error (naming the missing package and install command) rather than failing at package import time.  ### 5.3 Schema, Types, and Transformations  - **FR-12.** Schema inference shall be supported for all backends, with the ability to explicitly declare a schema in configuration to override inference. - **FR-13.** A type-mapping layer shall convert backend-native types to Python types and to `torch` dtypes, covering at minimum: integers (signed/unsigned, 8/16/32/64-bit), floats (16/32/64), booleans, strings/bytes, dates, timestamps, and nullable variants. - **FR-14.** Null values shall be represented consistently (e.g., `None`) and shall be convertible to framework-appropriate sentinels (e.g., `NaN`, `0`, or a configurable value) for numeric tensor columns. - **FR-15.** The framework shall provide a composable record-level transformation pipeline: `map`, `filter`, `select/rename`, `cast`, `fill_null`, `shuffle_buffer`, and `batch`. - **FR-16.** Transformations shall be composable in declaration order, and each stage shall be individually testable and inspectable. - **FR-17.** User-defined transformation callables shall receive a structured record/dict and return a dict, or a tensor/batch, and shall support both map-style (indexable) and iterable-style pipelines.  ### 5.4 PyTorch Integration  - **FR-18.** The framework shall return objects that are subclasses of, or fully interoperable with, `torch.utils.data.Dataset` and `torch.utils.data.IterableDataset`. - **FR-19.** Map-style datasets shall support `__len__` and `__getitem__` with configurable index-based or range-based access, including optional in-memory caching of the index metadata (e.g., row offsets) to avoid repeated scans. - **FR-20.** Iterable datasets shall implement `__iter__` yielding individual samples, and be compatible with `DataLoader(batch_size=..., collate_fn=...)`. - **FR-21.** The framework shall not require users to supply a `collate_fn` for common cases; a default collate supporting dict-of-lists and dict-of-tensors shall be provided, with the ability to override. - **FR-22.** Existing user-defined `collate_fn`, `sampler`, and `transform` hooks of `DataLoader` shall continue to work unchanged. - **FR-23.** The framework shall support `torch.utils.data.DataLoader` with `num_workers > 0`, including correct handling of worker seeding, per-worker reader instances, and cleanup of connections/cursors on worker termination. - **FR-24.** The framework shall support PyTorch DistributedDataParallel (and FSDP) by providing rank-aware sharding: each rank reads only its shard by default, with configurable sharding strategies (`by_row`, `by_file`, `by_partition`, `by_hash`, `round_robin`, `none`). - **FR-25.** Each dataset shall expose `set_epoch(epoch)` (and/or `__setstate__`/state-dict) so that shuffling and resharding can be made deterministic and distinct per epoch.  ### 5.5 Distributed Sharding and Determinism  - **FR-26.** Sharding shall be deterministic given `(source, split_spec, rank, world_size, epoch)`, producing a reproducible partition of records with no overlap and no omissions (verified by the test suite). - **FR-27.** A global seed shall control shuffling; the same seed with the same world size and epoch shall reproduce the same data order. - **FR-28.** Files/partitions shall be distributed across ranks in a balanced manner, and the framework shall expose per-rank record counts for verification. - **FR-29.** Support for reading a source once and broadcasting/broadcast-sharding to all ranks (e.g., small datasets) shall be provided via an explicit configuration option.  ### 5.6 Performance  - **FR-30.** Batch reads shall be supported natively by all backends (Hive fetch size, MySQL cursor fetch size, S3 range/list batching) to minimize per-record overhead. - **FR-31.** An optional bounded shuffle buffer and optional local disk cache/materialization layer shall be provided to improve throughput and reduce repeated remote reads. - **FR-32.** The framework shall expose read throughput metrics (records/sec, bytes/sec, latency percentiles) via an optional callback/logging interface. - **FR-33.** Where the backend supports it, predicate and column pushdown shall be used to reduce I/O; the framework shall not silently drop unsupported predicates but raise an explicit error when a requested predicate cannot be applied.  ### 5.7 Configuration  - **FR-34.** All sources and pipeline options shall be configurable via a declarative schema (Python dataclasses and/or YAML/JSON) covering: source type, connection parameters, credentials references, path/table patterns, format, read options, split/shard config, sampling, shuffling, caching, transformations, and batching. - **FR-35.** Secrets shall not be required to be stored inline in configuration files; the framework shall support environment-variable and external secret-provider references for credentials. - **FR-36.** Configuration validation shall occur at build time (before the first read) and shall raise a single aggregated error listing all invalid or missing fields. - **FR-37.** A resolved configuration object shall be serializable and printable (e.g., `to_dict()`/YAML dump) with secrets redacted, enabling logging of the effective configuration.  ### 5.8 Reliability and Error Handling  - **FR-38.** Transient failures (network errors, connection resets, throttling, 5xx responses) shall be retried with configurable exponential backoff and jitter, with a maximum retry count. - **FR-39.** Non-retryable errors (authentication failure, missing table/path, permission denied, malformed configuration) shall fail fast with clear messages that include the source identifier and the underlying cause. - **FR-40.** Readers shall implement proper resource cleanup (closing connections, cursors, file handles) on normal completion, exception, and worker shutdown; leaked resources shall not occur across repeated epochs. - **FR-41.** The framework shall emit structured warnings/errors for data-quality issues such as schema mismatch between inferred and actual data, truncated records, or parse failures, with a configurable policy to skip, quarantine, or abort.  ### 5.9 Observability and Logging  - **FR-42.** The framework shall integrate with the Python `logging` module and provide a consistent log format including source identifier, rank, worker id, and epoch. - **FR-43.** Optional progress reporting (records read, bytes read, ETA) shall be available via callback hooks and shall be safe to call from multiple workers (rank-0 aggregated by default).  ### 5.10 Extensibility  - **FR-44.** Third-party backends shall be registerable via a documented mechanism (decorator or `entry_points` group) without modifying framework source. - **FR-45.** A documented reference implementation of a custom backend shall be included, including a test harness, to lower the barrier for extension. - **FR-46.** The framework shall expose stable public interfaces such that internal refactoring does not break user code, enforced by semantic versioning and an API compatibility test.  ## 6. Non-Functional Requirements  - **NFR-1.** Python 3.9+ support; package shall be installable via `pip` and shall publish to PyPI. - **NFR-2.** Core framework shall depend only on `torch` and the standard library; each backend's third-party dependencies shall be optional extras (e.g., `pip install framework[hive]`, `[mysql]`, `[s3]`). - **NFR-3.** The framework shall not require a GPU and shall be usable in CPU-only environments. - **NFR-4.** Unit test coverage of ≥85% for core modules, and 100% coverage of sharding/splitting logic. - **NFR-5.** The framework shall maintain a documented minimum latency overhead per batch relative to a hand-written loader (≤10% for Parquet/CSV local reads). - **NFR-6.** All public APIs shall carry docstrings; user-facing documentation shall include quickstart, backend-specific configuration reference, distributed usage guide, and troubleshooting section. - **NFR-7.** CI shall run tests on Linux (and macOS/Windows where supported) across supported Python versions, including a distributed multi-process integration test using `torchrun`.  ## 7. Acceptance Criteria  1. A single configuration file can define a Hive table, a MySQL query, and an S3 prefix, and the same training script shall consume all three via `DataLoader` with only the configuration changing. 2. A user-written `collate_fn` and custom `torch.utils.data.Dataset` composition shall work without framework-specific code. 3. With `world_size=4` over a dataset of 1,000,000 rows, the union of shards read by all ranks contains each row exactly once, verified by an automated test. 4. Running the same configuration with the same seed twice produces byte-identical sample ordering. 5. A missing optional dependency (e.g., `pyarrow` for S3 Parquet) produces an actionable error message and does not prevent importing the framework or other backends. 6. Adding a new custom backend via the documented plugin interface requires no changes to framework core, and passes the supplied backend conformance test suite. 7. Credentials are never printed in logs or serialized configuration output.  ## 8. Deliverables  - Core package: source abstraction, reader abstraction, plugin registry, schema/type system, transformation pipeline, sharding/splitting, caching, config system, metrics/logging. - Backend plugins: `hive`, `mysql`, `s3` (with `local` filesystem support). - Public PyTorch integration API returning `Dataset`/`IterableDataset` implementations. - Configuration schema + YAML/JSON loader with validation and secret redaction. - Test suite: unit, integration (against local MySQL/Hive/MinIO test fixtures or mocks), distributed, and conformance tests for third-party backends. - Documentation: quickstart, backend guides, distributed guide, custom backend guide, troubleshooting, and an example project demonstrating end-to-end training over all supported backends.

issue_title: cmd/link: support msvc object files
requirement: **Requirement: MSVC COFF Object File Support in cmd/link**  The `cmd/link` tool shall support parsing, resolving, and linking Microsoft Visual C++ (MSVC) COFF (Common Object File Format) object files (`.obj`) to enable mixed-language linking scenarios, particularly for cgo on Windows platforms.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. **COFF Parsing**: The linker must parse COFF object files conforming to the Microsoft PE/COFF Specification, supporting architectures AMD64 (x86-64), 386 (x86), ARM, and ARM64. 2. **Section Handling**: Process standard COFF sections (`.text`, `.data`, `.rdata`, `.pdata`, `.xdata`, `.bss`, `.debug$*`, etc.), including COMDAT/section groups for proper deduplication of inline functions and template instantiations. 3. **Symbol Resolution**: Parse COFF symbol tables (including external, static, and section symbols with auxiliary entries) and integrate them with Go's symbol resolution system, ensuring correct handling of weak externals and common symbols. 4. **Relocations**: Support all relevant COFF relocation types per architecture (e.g., `IMAGE_REL_AMD64_ADDR64`, `IMAGE_REL_AMD64_REL32`, `IMAGE_REL_I386_DIR32`, etc.) and apply them during the linking phase. 5. **Import Handling**: Resolve references to the Import Address Table (IAT) and external DLL symbols for dynamic linking scenarios. 6. **Integration**: Seamlessly combine MSVC object files with native Go object files in the same link operation, maintaining existing dead code elimination and symbol visibility rules.  **Non-Functional Requirements:** - **Performance**: COFF parsing overhead shall not exceed 10% of equivalent native Go object file processing time. - **Safety**: Strict validation of all file offsets, sizes, and relocation targets to prevent memory corruption when processing malformed or untrusted input. - **Error Reporting**: Emit descriptive error messages indicating specific unsupported COFF features, architectures, or relocation types when encountered.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - `cmd/link` successfully links a Go executable containing calls to C functions compiled by `cl.exe` (MSVC) via cgo on windows/amd64, windows/386, and windows/arm64. - Object files containing COMDAT sections link without duplicate symbol errors. - All standard COFF relocation types are correctly resolved in the final binary. - The linker rejects LTCG (Link Time Code Generation) and managed object files with clear error messages. - Unit tests cover parsing of MSVC-generated object files for all supported architectures, including edge cases (empty sections, long symbol names, debug sections).  **Constraints:** - Implementation must be pure Go without external C dependencies. - Must conform to Microsoft PE/COFF Specification version 8.0+. - Must maintain backward compatibility with existing Go object file formats and other supported input formats (e.g., Mach-O, ELF).

issue_title: Add support for global plugins/universal addons
requirement: **REQ-XXX: Support for Global (Universal) Plugins/Addons**  **Description:** The system shall support installing, managing, and loading plugins/addons that are available globally, independent of any individual project, workspace, or environment. A global plugin is installed once per user or per machine and is automatically made available to all compatible projects without requiring per-project installation or configuration.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **Installation scope:** The system shall allow a user to install a plugin at a global scope (per-user and, where permissions allow, per-machine). 2. **Automatic availability:** Globally installed plugins shall be loaded automatically in every project or session that the current user runs, unless explicitly disabled for that project. 3. **Precedence:** When a project-level plugin and a global plugin share the same identifier, the project-level plugin shall take precedence, and the system shall log or report the override. 4. **Per-project opt-out:** The user shall be able to disable a specific global plugin for a specific project without uninstalling it globally. 5. **Management commands:** The system shall provide commands or UI to list, install, update, enable, disable, and remove global plugins, and to show each plugin's scope and status. 6. **Configuration:** Global plugins shall read configuration from a user-level configuration location, with optional project-level overrides. 7. **Compatibility check:** The system shall verify that a global plugin is compatible with the installed core version before loading it, and shall skip and report incompatible plugins without failing startup. 8. **Isolation:** A failure in a global plugin (load error, exception at runtime) shall not prevent the core system or project-level plugins from functioning. The error shall be reported with the plugin name and version.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  - **Performance:** Loading global plugins shall add no more than 200 ms to startup time for up to 10 installed global plugins. - **Portability:** Global plugin support shall work on all platforms the core system supports (Linux, macOS, Windows). - **Security:** Global plugins installed per-machine shall require elevated privileges. Plugin sources shall be verified (e.g., checksum or signature) before installation. - **Documentation:** User documentation shall describe global vs. project scope, precedence rules, and the opt-out mechanism.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - A plugin installed globally is active in at least two separate projects without per-project installation. - Disabling a global plugin in Project A does not affect its behavior in Project B. - A project-level plugin overrides a global plugin with the same identifier, and the override is reported. - A global plugin that fails to load is reported, and the application starts successfully. - Global plugin list, install, enable, disable, and remove commands work on Linux, macOS, and Windows. - Automated tests cover installation scope, precedence, opt-out, incompatible-version handling, and load-failure isolation.

issue_title: Add procedural and parametrizable audio support
requirement: The audio system shall support procedural synthesis in addition to existing asset-based playback. Applications shall be able to configure sound generators through a documented API using parameters such as waveform, frequency, amplitude, duration, timing, envelope, and effects. Parameters shall be validated, invalid values shall produce clear errors, and supported parameters shall be adjustable during playback. Generated audio shall integrate with existing playback, mixing, and export paths and support both real-time output and offline rendering, producing identical results for identical inputs and random seeds. Existing audio functionality shall remain backward compatible, and the new capabilities shall be documented and covered by automated tests.

issue_title: Allow release mode builds to run on simulators

Specifically, the build and run tooling shall be updated so that applications compiled in release configuration (with optimizations enabled) can be launched and run on simulator environments (e.g., iOS Simulator or Android Emulator) without build-time or run-time errors, enabling developers to perform performance-representative testing locally without requiring physical devices.

issue_title: Implement similar PyTorch function as model.summary() in keras?
requirement: Implement a public PyTorch model-summary utility equivalent to Keras’s `Model.summary()`.  The utility shall: - Accept a `torch.nn.Module` and, when required for shape inference, a sample input or input-shape specification. - Print a hierarchical table, in module registration order, showing each module’s name, type, output shape(s), total parameter count, and trainable parameter count, followed by totals for all parameters and trainable parameters. - Support nested modules and models with multiple inputs or outputs. - Avoid modifying model parameters, training/evaluation mode, or gradient state during inspection. - Raise a clear, actionable error when output shapes cannot be inferred and no additional input information is provided. - Include automated tests covering sequential models, nested modules, multiple-input/output models, non-trainable parameters, and shape-inference failures.

issue_title: cmd/link: support msvc object files
requirement: **Requirement: Support MSVC-Generated Object Files in the Go Linker (cmd/link)**  The Go linker (`cmd/link`) shall accept and correctly link COFF object files produced by the Microsoft Visual C++ toolchain (MSVC `cl.exe`) when building Go programs for Windows targets (`GOOS=windows`, `GOARCH` amd64 and 386 at minimum, and arm64 where supported).  The linker shall:  1. Parse MSVC-produced COFF `.obj` files, including their section, symbol table, string table, and relocation records, without error. 2. Resolve external and weak symbol references between Go objects and MSVC objects, including symbols with MSVC-specific name decorations (e.g., `_` prefixes for 32-bit x86 cdecl, `@n` suffixes for stdcall, and `?` C++ mangled names) as referenced from cgo or external linking. 3. Apply all COFF relocation types emitted by MSVC for the target architecture, producing the same final addresses as the MSVC linker would for equivalent code. 4. Handle COMDAT sections and section selection attributes (`IMAGE_COMDAT_SELECT_*`) emitted by MSVC, deduplicating or retaining sections according to their selection rules. 5. Tolerate and preserve or safely ignore MSVC-specific debug and metadata sections (e.g., `.debug$S`, `.debug$T`, `.drectve`) without causing link failure; directives in `.drectve` that affect linking (such as `/DEFAULTLIB` and `/EXPORT`) shall be honored or reported as unsupported with a clear diagnostic. 6. Emit a clear, actionable error message naming the object file and the unsupported construct when an MSVC object uses a feature the linker does not yet support, rather than failing with an internal error or producing a corrupt binary. 7. Work in both internal and external linking modes, and when linking through the system C toolchain (`-linkmode=external`) it shall pass MSVC objects through without modification. 8. Include regression tests using checked-in or generated MSVC `.obj` fixtures covering at least: plain function references, data symbols, COMDAT functions, and cgo interoperation, runnable on Windows builders. 9. Not regress linking of existing GCC/MinGW-produced COFF objects or Go-generated objects on any supported platform.

issue_title: plugin: add Windows support
requirement: **Requirement: Windows Platform Support for Plugin**  **Description:** The plugin shall be extended to fully support the Windows operating system, enabling installation, execution, and all core functionality on Windows environments with parity to existing supported platforms.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **Installation:** The plugin shall provide an installation path for Windows users, including a documented installation procedure compatible with standard Windows package/dependency management workflows. 2. **Build Compatibility:** The plugin's build system shall be configured to compile and package successfully on Windows (including CI builds for Windows runners), producing distributable artifacts for the Windows platform. 3. **Runtime Functionality:** All existing plugin features shall function correctly on Windows, including initialization, execution, and interaction with the host application. 4. **Path Handling:** All file and directory operations shall use platform-independent path handling, ensuring correct behavior with Windows path conventions (backslashes, drive letters, case-insensitive filesystems). 5. **Platform-Specific Code Paths:** Any platform-dependent logic (e.g., shell commands, environment variables, process management) shall be abstracted or branched so that Windows-specific implementations are used when running on Windows.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  1. The plugin shall support actively maintained Windows versions (Windows 10 and later, and Windows Server equivalents, as applicable). 2. Automated tests shall be extended to run on Windows in the project's CI pipeline to prevent future regressions. 3. Documentation shall be updated to reflect Windows as a supported platform, including any Windows-specific configuration steps, known limitations, or troubleshooting guidance.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - The plugin installs successfully on a clean Windows environment following the documented procedure. - All existing test suites pass on Windows in CI. - All documented plugin features are verified as working on Windows with no functional regressions relative to other supported platforms. - Documentation includes Windows-specific setup instructions and any known limitations.

issue_title: x/vuln: add support for suppressing vulnerabilities by ID
requirement: **REQ-VULN-001: Suppress vulnerabilities by ID**  **Statement:** The x/vuln tooling shall support suppressing (excluding) specific vulnerabilities from analysis results by their vulnerability identifiers (e.g., GO-2021-0113).  **Acceptance Criteria:** 1. Users shall be able to specify one or more vulnerability IDs to suppress via a command-line option and/or a configuration file, so the suppression list is reusable across invocations (including CI/CD pipelines). 2. Any detected vulnerability whose ID matches an entry in the suppression list shall be omitted from the primary findings output. 3. Suppressed vulnerabilities shall not contribute to the tool's failure determination or non-zero exit status. 4. The tool shall validate each supplied ID against the canonical Go vulnerability ID format and shall emit a warning (without aborting the scan) for IDs that are malformed or do not correspond to a vulnerability in the database at scan time. 5. Suppressions shall be auditable: in verbose and JSON output modes, the tool shall indicate which vulnerability IDs were suppressed so users can review and maintain the suppression list over time. 6. Suppression shall be applied by vulnerability ID only; suppression by package, module, or symbol is out of scope for this requirement.
