issue_title: Include images in rustdoc output
requirement: ## Requirement: Include images in rustdoc output Rustdoc shall support images referenced in crate-level, module-level, and item-level documentation and include them in generated HTML documentation. ### Functional requirements - Standard Markdown image syntax (`![alt text](url "optional title")`) shall be recognized in doc comments and in Markdown included through `#![doc = include_str!("...")]`. - Each recognized image shall produce an HTML `` element containing the resolved `src`, an `alt` attribute, and a `title` attribute when one is provided. - Remote image URLs, including HTTP and HTTPS URLs, shall be preserved and referenced directly. - Relative image paths shall be resolved against the source document, validated during documentation generation, and copied into the generated documentation output. The copied asset shall not depend on files remaining in the source tree. - Generated asset paths shall avoid collisions and shall not reference locations outside the documentation output directory. - Missing or unreadable image files shall produce a diagnostic identifying the documentation source and image path; images shall not be silently omitted. - Existing Markdown rendering, HTML sanitization, link resolution, and non-HTML rustdoc output shall remain backward compatible. ### Acceptance criteria - A doc comment containing `![Architecture](images/architecture.png)` generates an `` element with `alt="Architecture"`, and the referenced file is available in the generated output. - A crate-level document loaded with `include_str!` renders both local and remote Markdown images correctly. - A broken local image path reports the source document and missing path while allowing rustdoc to continue generating documentation.

issue_title: cmd/compile: thread support for webassembly
requirement: # Requirement: `cmd/compile` — WebAssembly Threads Support  ## 1. Background / Problem  The Go toolchain's WebAssembly target currently supports only single-threaded execution. The WebAssembly threads proposal (shared linear memory + atomic instructions) is not implemented, so Go programs that rely on `sync/atomic`, `sync.WaitGroup`, `sync.Mutex` contention, or any parallel goroutine execution cannot be compiled and run correctly on `GOOS=wasip1` / `GOARCH=wasm`.  The compiler (`cmd/compile`) is the component that must recognize and emit the instruction set required by the threads proposal, coordinate the ABI/memory layout with `cmd/link` and the runtime, and keep the existing (non-threads) WebAssembly output byte-for-byte compatible unless the feature is explicitly enabled.  ## 2. Scope  In scope: `cmd/compile` (including `cmd/compile/internal/ssagen`, `cmd/compile/internal/wasm`, `cmd/compile/internal/obj`, `cmd/compile/internal/syntax`, `cmd/compile/internal/types2` as needed) and the minimum coordination changes in `cmd/link` and `runtime` required to produce a working threads-enabled binary.  Out of scope: host-side thread-pool scheduling policy, `GOOS=js` specific host integration beyond enabling the same instruction support, and any user-visible API changes.  ## 3. Functional Requirements  ### FR-1 — Atomic instruction generation (backend)  When compiling for `GOARCH=wasm` with threads enabled, the backend must lower the Go atomic operations to the corresponding WebAssembly threads instructions:  - `i32.atomic.load`, `i32.atomic.store`, `i64.atomic.load`, `i64.atomic.store` - `i32.atomic.rmw.add`, `.sub`, `.and`, `.or`, `.xor`, `.xchg` - `i64.atomic.rmw.add`, `.sub`, `.and`, `.or`, `.xor`, `.xchg` - `i32.atomic.rmw.cmpxchg`, `i64.atomic.rmw.cmpxchg` - `memory.atomic.fence` (for `atomic` fence / memory barrier semantics) - `memory.atomic.wait32` / `wait64` / `notify` where required by the runtime's blocking primitives.  Go's `sync/atomic` API exposes no memory-ordering parameters; all operations must be compiled as sequentially consistent. The compiler must not weaken or reorder atomic operations relative to one another or relative to the surrounding program order.  ### FR-2 — Alignment and fault behavior  Atomic loads/stores/rmw must be emitted only for naturally aligned addresses (1/2/4/8 bytes as appropriate for the width). If the compiler cannot prove alignment for a value whose address is not statically known, it must either:  - emit a guarded check that traps deterministically (`unreachable`) on misalignment, or - guarantee alignment via the type system/layout rules,  and must never silently produce a misaligned atomic access.  ### FR-3 — Non-atomic accesses to shared memory  Ordinary (non-atomic) loads and stores to shared memory must continue to be emitted as plain `i32.load`/`i64.load`/`i32.store`/`i64.store` instructions, which remain valid against shared memory under the threads proposal. The compiler must not reject or rewrite them.  ### FR-4 — Feature gating / build configuration  The threads instruction set must be gated behind an explicit, documented build configuration knob (e.g. a `GOEXPERIMENT` such as `wasmthreads`, or an equivalent compiler/linker flag) so that:  - the default build of `GOOS=wasip1`/`GOARCH=wasm` continues to emit the current, threads-free instruction stream and remains fully backward compatible; - the feature can be enabled for `GOOS=wasip1` and any other wasm-based `GOOS` that adopts it; - `cmd/compile` and `cmd/link` must reject or agree on mismatched settings (e.g. compile with threads enabled, link without) rather than producing an invalid binary.  ### FR-5 — `sync/atomic` and runtime integration  The compiler must make the threads-capable implementations of `sync/atomic` (and any runtime primitives requiring atomics, e.g. `runtime.futex`, hash map sharding, timers) selectable when the feature is enabled, and the non-threads implementations selectable otherwise. Build constraints used for this selection must be resolvable by `cmd/compile`'s own build-constraint evaluation without ambiguity.  The compiler and runtime must agree on:  - the wasm linear memory being created as **shared** (`shared` flag on the memory declaration), - the size of the linear memory and the reserved address space layout being identical between threads and non-threads builds (so a binary built with one setting is not loadable with the other), - the maximum number of wasm threads/memory pages requested at instantiation time.  ### FR-6 — Assembler, object file, and debug info  - The compiler's wasm assembler and object writer must accept and encode the new atomic opcodes, including their memory-immediate operands and alignment hints. - `cmd/internal/obj`/`cmd/internal/goobj` encodings used for wasm must be extended compatibly (new opcodes must not change the encoding of existing opcodes). - DWARF/debug information generated for instructions containing new opcodes must remain valid; unknown-opcode assertions in the compiler must be updated so that the compiler does not panic on the new instructions.  ### FR-7 — SSA rewriting / correctness  `cmd/compile`'s SSA rewrite rules must correctly lower `sync/atomic` intrinsics (`AtomicAdd`, `AtomicCompareAndSwap`, `AtomicLoad`, `AtomicStore`, `AtomicXchg`, `AtomicAnd/Or/Xor`, and any `SYNC/ATOMIC` fence operations) to the wasm atomic instruction sequence, with the correct operand order and width, and must not leave unlowered generic operations in the final instruction list.  ### FR-8 — Traps and panic behavior  Operations that would trap in wasm (misaligned atomic, out-of-bounds access, `unreachable` from failed runtime checks) must surface as Go panics/crashes with the existing wasm trap-mapping behavior, not as silent corruption.  ## 4. Non-Functional Requirements  - **NFR-1 — Compatibility:** With the feature disabled, the generated wasm code and the resulting binary must be unchanged from the current behavior (no new opcodes, no layout change). - **NFR-2 — No regression:** Compile-time and code-size overhead for non-wasm targets and for wasm builds with the feature disabled must be negligible. - **NFR-3 — Portability of the flag:** The configuration knob must be settable via `GOEXPERIMENT`/`GOFLAGS` in a way that is honored consistently by `go build`, `go test`, `cmd/compile`, and `cmd/link`. - **NFR-4 — Determinism:** Compiling the same input twice with the same settings must produce identical output.  ## 5. Acceptance Criteria  1. `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm` with the threads feature enabled builds a program that uses `sync/atomic` (add/CAS/load/store/xchg) and `sync.WaitGroup`/`sync.Mutex` under contention, and the program produces correct results when executed on a threads-capable wasm host. 2. The emitted wasm module contains the expected atomic instructions and declares its memory as shared. 3. A `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm` build with the feature disabled produces a module identical to the pre-change output and contains no atomic instructions. 4. Mismatched compiler/linker feature settings fail with a clear diagnostic instead of producing an unloadable module. 5. `go test cmd/compile` and the wasm-target test suite pass; new unit tests cover opcode lowering, alignment handling, and feature gating. 6. `cmd/compile` does not panic ("unknown opcode"/"unsupported") when compiling any Go source that exercises the new instructions, including with `-race`-style instrumentation or `-N -l` optimization levels.  ## 6. Open Questions  - Should the feature be exposed as a `GOEXPERIMENT` or as a per-`GOOS` default (e.g. automatically on for `wasip1` in a future release)? - Is `memory.atomic.wait`/`notify` to be emitted directly by `cmd/compile`, or provided by the runtime via assembly only? - What alignment-checking strategy (compile-time proof vs. runtime trap) is preferred for `atomic.Pointer` and struct-embedded atomics?

issue_title: Replace GridMap with an improved TileMap3D node (inspired by the new 2D TileMap)
requirement: The system shall implement a `TileMap3D` node and an associated `TileSet3D` resource to supersede the legacy `GridMap` system, providing a modernized 3D cell-based level design framework aligned with the 2D `TileMap` architecture. The implementation shall support:  1. **Multi-Layer 3D Grid Architecture**: Enable independent, stackable 3D grid layers with configurable cell sizes, axes, origins, and per-layer visibility/modulation settings. 2. **Comprehensive TileSet3D Resource**: Provide a resource definition system supporting multi-mesh library integration, per-tile collision shapes, navigation meshes, occlusion data, alternative tile transforms (rotation and flipping), and user-defined custom metadata layers. 3. **Advanced Editor Painting Tools**: Deliver an interactive 3D editor toolset featuring continuous brush painting, line and rectangle fill modes, bucket fill, random tile scatter, saved tile patterns, and terrain/autotiling connection rules. 4. **Performance Optimization**: Utilize automated MultiMesh chunking, static batching, and level-of-detail (LOD) handling to minimize draw calls for large-scale 3D grid layouts. 5. **Runtime API & Migration**: Provide runtime methods for querying, modifying, and procedurally generating 3D tiles dynamically, along with an automated migration/conversion tool for existing `GridMap` and `MeshLibrary` assets.

issue_title: Enable "hot reload" (not just "hot restart") for Flutter Web
requirement: The Flutter development toolchain shall support stateful hot reload for web compilation targets, allowing developers to inject updated source code directly into an active browser runtime session and refresh the UI while preserving the application's current runtime state.

issue_title: Customizable project structure (platforms)
requirement: The system shall allow users to customize the project structure for supported platforms.

issue_title: Support Windows kernel mode for driver development
requirement: ## Requirement: Windows Kernel‑Mode Support for Driver Development  ### 1. Motivation  The project is currently usable only from user-mode processes (Windows applications/services). A significant class of consumers develop Windows kernel-mode drivers (WDM or KMDF) and need to link the project's functionality directly into a `.sys` driver image — for example to intercept I/O, provide a virtual device, or run the project's core logic inside the kernel. Such consumers currently have no supported way to do this: the code relies on Win32 user-mode APIs and user-mode CRT facilities that are unavailable (or unsafe) in kernel mode.  ### 2. Scope  Add a first-class Windows kernel-mode build/runtime path for the project so that its core functionality can be embedded in a WDM/KMDF driver, while keeping the existing user-mode build fully functional and source-compatible.  In scope: - A kernel-safe platform abstraction layer that isolates all user-mode-only dependencies. - Kernel-mode driver entry, device creation, IRP dispatch, IOCTL control interface, and unload/PnP handling. - Build-system integration with the Windows Driver Kit (WDK) / MSBuild so the project can be compiled as a kernel-mode static library (`.lib`) and linked into a driver. - A sample/reference kernel-mode driver demonstrating integration, plus a user-mode test client. - Documentation, limitations, and compatibility statements.  Out of scope: - Adding new user-mode features unrelated to kernel-mode enabling. - Signed production driver packages (signing guidance is documented, but the project does not ship certificates).  ### 3. Functional Requirements  **FR-1 Build configurations** - The build must expose an explicit kernel-mode configuration (e.g. a build target/flag such as `windows-kernel` or `MODE_KERNEL`) that is mutually exclusive with the user-mode configuration and selectable without editing source files. - Kernel-mode builds must succeed with the WDK toolchain for x64 (and, where the WDK supports it, ARM64), in both Debug and Release, with `/WX` (warnings as errors), `/GS` buffer-security checks, and SAL (`__In`, `_Out_`, `_When_`) annotations enabled. - Any dependency that is not usable in kernel mode must be excluded from the kernel build, replaced by a kernel-safe substitute, or moved behind an abstraction interface with a documented "not available in kernel mode" behavior.  **FR-2 Kernel-safe platform abstraction** - Provide a unified internal API for: memory allocation (nonpaged/paged pool with a project-specific pool tag, and `ExAllocatePoolWithTag`-equivalent), zeroed allocation, buffers, string conversion (`RtlUnicodeString`/`ANSI`), synchronization (spinlocks, interlocked operations, events, `ERESOURCE`), timers, worker queues (`ExInitializeWorkItem`/`IoQueueWorkItem`), and logging/tracing (WPP tracing or `DbgPrintEx`-based, with compile-time gating of verbose logging). - All abstraction entry points must be noinline-free of floating point, must not call Win32 APIs unavailable in kernel mode, and must be safe to call at `PASSIVE_LEVEL`, `DISPATCH_LEVEL`, or `APC_LEVEL` as documented per API. - Memory allocated in kernel mode must be freed deterministically; the implementation must not rely on the CRT, the registry, or user-mode environment services.  **FR-3 Driver integration surface** - Provide a documented integration entry point that a driver author calls from `DriverEntry`, which registers an IRP dispatch table and performs initialization/teardown. - Support the following IRPs at minimum: `IRP_MJ_CREATE`, `IRP_MJ_CLOSE`, `IRP_MJ_READ`, `IRP_MJ_WRITE`, `IRP_MJ_DEVICE_CONTROL`, `IRP_MJ_PNP` (start/stop/remove), and `IRP_MJ_POWER`/system callback registration where applicable. - Expose a control interface via IOCTLs for configuration, status/query, and administrative operations, using `METHOD_BUFFERED` and `METHOD_NEITHER` where required, with input/output structures that are versioned and validated (size checks, magic/version fields, range checks) before use. - Handle asynchronous I/O correctly: honor `IRP_MJ_*` cancellation (`CancelRoutine`), `IoCallDriver` completion, and pending-status propagation. - Provide device creation with a caller-selectable device name, optional symbolic link, and security descriptor; support exclusive (non-shareable) opens. - Implement a clean unload path: stop new I/O, cancel outstanding work items/timers, free all pool allocations, delete the device/symbolic link, and unregister callbacks with zero resource leaks.  **FR-4 Safety and robustness** - All data crossing the user/kernel boundary must be validated: `ProbeForRead`/`ProbeForWrite` usage, `METHOD_NEITHER` buffer validation, access checks against the security descriptor, and rejection of malformed or oversized inputs. - Use structured exception handling (`__try/__except`) around operations that may raise kernel exceptions from user-supplied data, with documented fallback behavior. - Must pass the Windows Driver Verifier with standard rulesets (including pool/memory checks, I/O completion, deadlock detection, and strict I/O) with zero reported errors during test runs. - No uninitialized-memory use, no use of the stack in a way that can overflow (bounded recursion/stack usage documented).  **FR-5 Multi-processor and IRQL correctness** - Shared state must be protected with appropriate synchronization primitives; reference counting on request/context objects must use interlocked operations. - The implementation must be documented with respect to maximum IRQL for each entry point.  **FR-6 Compatibility** - Support Windows 10 (1809 and later) and Windows 11 with WDK 10, for both WDM-style and KMDF-style drivers. - The user-mode build and its public API must remain unchanged (no behavioral regressions), verified by the existing test suite.  **FR-7 Testing** - Ship a minimal sample kernel-mode driver that links the project and exercises the main code paths (create/read/write/IOCTL/unload). - Ship a user-mode test client (and/or a kernel-mode test using the WDK test framework) that validates IOCTL round-trips, error paths, invalid-input rejection, and unload-time cleanup. - CI must build the kernel-mode target and the sample driver on every change, and run the sample driver under Driver Verifier on a test host.  **FR-8 Documentation** - Provide a "Kernel-Mode Integration Guide" covering: prerequisites (WDK version, supported architectures), how to add the kernel build to an existing WDM/KMDF project, code samples for `DriverEntry`, IOCTL definitions and structures, supported vs. unsupported features in kernel mode, IRQL and lifetime rules, pool tags used, troubleshooting (Verifier errors, build errors), and how to report kernel-mode-specific defects. - Document known limitations (e.g., features requiring user-mode services, logging verbosity differences, lack of floating-point use).  ### 4. Non-Functional Requirements  - The kernel-mode build must not increase the size of the user-mode binary, and user-mode dependencies must not be pulled into the kernel image. - No new mandatory runtime dependency for user-mode consumers; kernel-mode-specific dependencies are limited to documented WDK/SDK libraries. - Licensing of the project and all kernel-mode-specific code must remain compatible with the existing license and with Windows kernel-mode driver distribution. - The kernel-mode code path must be maintainable by contributors without access to physical hardware, via emulated/verifier-based CI.  ### 5. Acceptance Criteria  1. `build --config windows-kernel` (or the equivalent documented command) produces a kernel-mode static library that links successfully into a WDM and a KMDF sample driver with `/WX` enabled and no warnings. 2. The sample driver loads on Windows 10 1809+ and Windows 11 x64, exposes a device, successfully services create/read/write/IOCTL requests, and unloads with no resource leaks. 3. Running the sample driver under Driver Verifier (default + pool checking) completes all test cases with zero verifier errors. 4. All user-mode tests continue to pass with the kernel-mode configuration disabled, and the user-mode public API is unchanged. 5. The Kernel-Mode Integration Guide is published and covers every item in FR-8.

issue_title: Struct initializer `..x` syntax should work for other structs with structurally equal subset of fields
requirement: Requirement: The system shall support struct initializer `..x` syntax for structs that contain a structurally equal subset of fields.

issue_title: Expose a zero allocation API to Godot C# bindings
requirement: The Godot C# bindings shall expose an API surface that permits C# code to interact with the engine—including calling methods, getting/setting properties, marshaling common types (e.g., Variant, built-in structs, NodePath, StringName), invoking callables, and connecting/emitting signals—without triggering any managed heap allocations, so that performance-critical game code does not incur garbage collection pressure. This allocation-free behavior must hold on the hot path for repeated calls, and the allocation-free members should be clearly identified and documented so users can distinguish them from the existing allocating counterparts.

issue_title: Improve the indexability (SEO) of Flutter apps on the web
requirement: **Requirement: Enhanced Search Engine Indexability for Flutter Web Applications**  The system shall provide mechanisms to enable search engine crawlers to discover, index, and rank content within Flutter web applications, including: (1) static pre-rendering capability to generate HTML snapshots of application routes for crawler consumption without requiring client-side JavaScript execution; (2) server-side rendering (SSR) support to serve fully rendered semantic HTML content in the initial response; (3) dynamic injection of SEO meta tags (title, description, Open Graph, Twitter Cards, and canonical URLs) per route that are present in the server response; (4) semantic HTML fallback content accessible to crawlers when the Flutter engine is not yet initialized; (5) automatic generation and serving of XML sitemaps reflecting application routes at the domain root; and (6) progressive enhancement architecture ensuring text content and navigation links are visible to crawlers prior to client-side framework execution.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - Search engine crawlers (e.g., Googlebot, Bingbot) can retrieve meaningful text content and hyperlinks from any application route without executing JavaScript - Route-specific meta tags are dynamically updated and present in the initial HTML document head - Pre-rendered HTML snapshots accurately reflect the visual and textual state of the application - `sitemap.xml` is accessible at the domain root and dynamically reflects current application routes - Canonical link elements are present to prevent duplicate content indexing across URL variants

issue_title: CPU version of PyTorch on PyPI
requirement: The project shall publish CPU-only builds of PyTorch on PyPI, allowing users to install and use PyTorch without requiring GPU or CUDA dependencies.

issue_title: [Desktop] - Splash screen or background color customization
requirement: **Requirement ID:** REQ-DESKTOP-001 **Title:** Splash Screen and Background Color Customization **Type:** Functional Requirement **Component:** Desktop Application **Priority:** Should-Have  **Description:** The desktop application shall provide users with the ability to customize the visual appearance of the application during startup and in the main interface. Specifically, the system shall:  1. Support display of a splash screen during application startup, whose appearance (background color and logo) can be customized through the application preferences. 2. Allow users to set a custom background color for the application window, eliminating the default (e.g., white flash) background shown during launch and while the interface loads.  **Rationale:** Users currently have no control over the startup visual experience. A default background color can produce an unpolished appearance (e.g., a white flash on dark-themed systems) and may cause visual discomfort. Enabling splash screen and background color customization improves perceived startup quality, supports personalization and accessibility needs (e.g., reduced glare, dark-mode consistency), and allows alignment with user or organizational branding.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - AC1: The application preferences shall include an option to enable/disable the splash screen. - AC2: The user shall be able to select a splash screen background color via a color picker or preset palette. - AC3: The user shall be able to select a custom background color for the main application window via a color picker or preset palette. - AC4: The configured background color shall be applied during the startup/loading phase so that no default color (e.g., white) is displayed before the interface renders. - AC5: Customization settings shall persist across application restarts. - AC6: The application shall provide a "Reset to default" option restoring the original splash screen and background color settings.  **Constraints:** - Splash screen must not extend application startup time beyond current startup duration by more than 200 ms. - Custom colors must meet minimum contrast requirements for any text or logo displayed on the splash screen.

issue_title: compress/bzip2: implement bz2 encoder
requirement: # Requirement: `compress/bzip2` — bzip2 (`.bz2`) encoder  ## 1. Summary  Add a **bzip2 compressor** to the `compress/bzip2` package. The encoder must emit standards‑compliant `.bz2` streams that:  * are decompressed correctly by the package's existing `Reader` (round‑trip), * are decompressed correctly by libbz2 (`bzip2`/`bunzip2` CLI) and other third‑party implementations, * pass libbz2's integrity check (`bzip2 -t`), * are produced in a fully streaming fashion (no buffering of the whole input).  The implementation must be pure Go, stdlib‑only (no cgo, no external module dependencies).  ## 2. Context / Motivation  `compress/bzip2` currently implements **decompression only**. Applications that need to *produce* `.bz2` data must either shell out to the `bzip2` binary or link against libbz2 via cgo. A native encoder removes both dependencies and completes the package's API surface.  ## 3. Scope  **In scope**  * A new streaming encoder API in package `compress/bzip2` (same package as the existing reader). * A complete bzip2 format encoder: RLE1 → BWT → MTF + RLE2 → multi‑table Huffman coding → block framing → stream framing. * Compression levels 1–9, mapping to bzip2 block sizes of 100 KiB … 900 KiB. * Unit tests, interoperability tests, fuzz targets and benchmarks.  **Out of scope (non‑goals)**  * Any change to the existing decoder behaviour (it must keep working unchanged). * Multi‑stream support (concatenated `.bz2` files): the encoder writes exactly **one** stream. * The deprecated "randomised block" feature: the encoder never emits it; the decoder's existing support for it must be preserved. * Native/assembly acceleration or SIMD; no specific performance target beyond "practically usable" (see §7). * New compression features beyond the bzip2 format (no zstd/lzma-style extensions, no custom framing).  ## 4. Public API  The API must follow the conventions of the package's existing `ReaderConfig`/`NewReader` and of the other `compress/*` packages.  ```go // WriterConfig configures a Writer. type WriterConfig struct { 	// Level is the compression level: 1 (fastest, smallest ratio) … 9 (best ratio). 	// Valid values are 1–9. The zero value selects the default level (9). 	Level int }  // NewWriter returns a Writer that compresses data written to it and writes // the resulting .bz2 stream to w. func NewWriter(w io.Writer, conf *WriterConfig) (*Writer, error)  type Writer struct{ … }  func (w *Writer) Write(p []byte) (int, error) func (w *Writer) Close() error func (w *Writer) Reset(w io.Writer) ```  Requirements on the API:  * `NewWriter` **must not** write anything to `w` before the first `Write`/`Close`. * `NewWriter` returns an error when `conf != nil` and `conf.Level` is outside `1..9`. `conf == nil` and `conf.Level == 0` select the default level (9). * `Write` accepts an arbitrary amount of data, compresses it into the current block, and returns `len(p)` on success. It must not retain `p` after returning. * `Write`/`Close` must surface errors from the underlying `io.Writer`; such errors are sticky and are returned by all subsequent calls. * `Close` flushes the final block, writes the end‑of‑stream marker and combined CRC, and finalises the stream. It is a no‑op returning `nil` if already closed. **The stream is incomplete until `Close` is called.** * `Reset` discards all buffered state and re‑arms the writer for a new, independent stream on `w` (a fresh stream header is written for the new stream). * The `Writer` is **not** safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines (document this).  ## 5. Functional Requirements  ### 5.1 Normative reference  The bzip2 file format as implemented by **libbz2** is normative for all bit‑level details. The summary below states the elements that the implementation must get right; where a detail is not spelled out here, libbz2's `compress.c`/`decompress.c` (and the bzip2 format documentation) define it.  ### 5.2 Stream framing  * **Stream header:** the 4 bytes `'B'`, `'Z'`, `'h'`, followed by the ASCII digit `'1'`…`'9'` denoting the block size in units of 100 KiB. The digit **must** equal the configured level. * A stream consists of: header, zero or more compressed blocks, end‑of‑stream marker. * The encoder writes blocks of at most `level × 100 KiB` bytes of **original (pre‑RLE) input**. * **Empty input** produces a valid stream containing only the header and the end‑of‑stream marker (matching libbz2's output for an empty file, 14 bytes).  ### 5.3 Block encoding pipeline  For each block, the following stages must be applied **in this order**:  1. **RLE1 (first run‑length encoding).** Runs of ≥ 4 identical bytes are encoded as 4 literal bytes followed by a count byte holding `runLength - 4`; a run is limited to 255 bytes per encoded group, longer runs are split into consecutive groups. Runs shorter than 4 bytes are emitted literally. The RLE1 count bytes are part of the block's byte stream for all later stages (BWT, symbol map). 2. **BWT (Burrows–Wheeler transform).** Transform of the RLE1‑encoded block, yielding the sorted rotations and the primary index. The result must be *identical* to libbz2's transform for the same input. Must be implemented with a suffix‑array/suffix‑sort based algorithm of O(n log n) or better (an O(n²) implementation is not acceptable for 900 KiB blocks). 3. **MTF + RLE2 (move‑to‑front, then second run‑length encoding).** Apply move‑to‑front to the BWT output. Runs of MTF value 0 (i.e. repeated bytes) are encoded with the two special symbols `RUNA` (digit 1) and `RUNB` (digit 2) in bijective base 2, **least‑significant digit first** (run length = Σ dᵢ·2^(i‑1), dᵢ ∈ {1,2} in stream order). Non‑zero MTF values are emitted as literal symbols. 4. **Huffman coding.** Build between 2 and 6 Huffman tables over the block alphabet, assign one table per group of 50 symbols, and emit: number of tables (3 bits, value 2–6), number of selectors (15 bits), the MTF‑encoded selectors, the table definitions, and the Huffman‑coded symbol stream — exactly as specified by libbz2. EOB terminates the symbol stream.  ### 5.4 Alphabet and symbol map  * Alphabet size is `nInUse + 3`, where `nInUse` is the number of distinct byte values occurring in the **RLE1‑encoded** block:   * symbol `0` = `RUNA`, symbol `1` = `RUNB`,   * symbols `2 … nInUse+1` = literal MTF values `1 … nInUse`,   * symbol `nInUse+2` = `EOB`. * **Symbol map:** a 16‑bit bitmap marking which of the 16 groups of 16 byte values are used, followed by a 16‑bit bitmap for each used group. The map covers the byte values present in the RLE1‑encoded block (including RLE1 count bytes).  ### 5.5 Block framing  Each block is emitted as:  1. 48‑bit magic `0x314159265359`; 2. 32‑bit **block CRC** over the block's *original* (uncompressed, pre‑RLE1) data, using the CRC‑32/BZIP2 variant: polynomial `0x04C11DB7`, MSB‑first, init `0xFFFFFFFF`, final XOR `0xFFFFFFFF`; 3. the compressed block payload (symbol map, Huffman tables, symbol stream).  Blocks are **not** byte‑aligned: the next block header follows immediately after the previous block's payload bits.  ### 5.6 Stream termination  * 48‑bit end‑of‑stream magic `0x177245385090`; * 32‑bit **combined CRC**, initialised to 0 and updated per block as   `combined = rotateLeft32(combined, 1) XOR blockCRC`; * zero padding to the next byte boundary.  ### 5.7 Streaming behaviour  * The encoder must never buffer more than one block plus the BWT working structures; peak memory must stay bounded (≈ ≤ 10 MiB for level 9) regardless of input size. * Completed blocks are written to the underlying writer as soon as they are finished; the writer does not need to wait for `Close` to emit earlier blocks. * A `Write` spanning several block boundaries must be split across blocks correctly. * `Close` emits the final (possibly empty) partial block — but **no** block at all if no input bytes were ever written — followed by the end‑of‑stream marker.  ## 6. Non‑Functional Requirements  * **Dependencies:** standard library only; no cgo; no new entries in `go.mod`. * **Determinism:** the same input and level must always produce byte‑identical output (no map iteration order or randomness leaking into the output). * **Correctness of data handling:** `Write` must not modify the caller's slice; no data may be lost or duplicated across block boundaries; the round‑trip must be byte‑exact for binary data. * **Go conventions:** doc comments on all exported identifiers; package documentation updated to state that the package now implements compression as well as decompression; errors wrapped with `%w`; no panics on malformed input paths (the encoder's own inputs are trusted, but the package must remain safe under fuzzing of the decoder). * **Code quality:** the implementation must pass `go vet`, `gofmt -l`, and `go test -race`.  ## 7. Performance  * The BWT must not be implemented in O(n²); a suffix‑array based transform is required. * Provide `BenchmarkWriter` for representative inputs (highly compressible text, incompressible random data) at several levels. * No hard wall‑clock target is imposed, but compressing multi‑hundred‑megabyte inputs must be feasible in a single process without excessive memory growth.  ## 8. Testing & Acceptance Criteria  The change is accepted when all of the following hold:  1. **Round‑trip tests** (compress with `Writer`, decompress with the package's `Reader`) pass for at least:    * empty input; single byte; all 256 byte values;    * runs of identical bytes longer than 255 bytes (exercising RLE1 split and RLE2 bijective base‑2 coding);    * long runs of `0x00` and `0xFF` (exercising the BWT zero‑run path);    * incompressible random data;    * data of exactly one block size, one block size ± 1 byte, and several blocks (multi‑block stream);    * data written in many small `Write` calls vs. one large call (identical output). 2. **Interoperability tests** (skipped, not failed, when the external tools are unavailable):    * `bzip2 -t` accepts the produced stream and `bzip2 -d` recovers the original data;    * the package's `Reader` decompresses the output of `bzip2 -c` (including streams produced with all levels 1–9). 3. **Format tests** assert:    * the 4‑byte header is `"BZh"` + the configured level digit;    * the 48‑bit block magic and the 48‑bit end‑of‑stream magic are present at the expected bit positions;    * the combined CRC equals the value computed independently by the test;    * no block exceeds the configured block size;    * the output of an empty input is 14 bytes. 4. **Fuzz targets** are added: one that compresses arbitrary input and decompresses it back (must round‑trip), and one that feeds arbitrary bytes to the decoder (must not panic). 5. `go test -race ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass; benchmarks are committed.  ## 9. Open Questions / Decisions to be Confirmed  * Level API shape: `WriterConfig{Level int}` (symmetric with the existing `ReaderConfig`) is the recommended choice; an alternative `NewWriterLevel(w, level)` helper may be added if reviewers prefer the `compress/flate` style. * Default level when `conf == nil` or `conf.Level == 0`: recommended value 9 (best ratio), consistent with the bzip2 CLI default. * Whether to add a `Flush() error` method: not required — bzip2 has no flush semantics — but the encoder must emit completed blocks eagerly so that long‑running writers make progress.

issue_title: Support multiple windows for desktop shells
requirement: The desktop shell shall support the creation and concurrent management of multiple independent window instances, enabling users to open, switch between, and separately control (minimize, maximize, resize, reposition, and close) each window without affecting the state or content of other active windows. The system shall provide window management interfaces—such as a taskbar, dock, window list, or keyboard shortcuts—to facilitate navigation and organization of open windows, and each window instance shall maintain its own persistent session state, configuration, and UI layout.

issue_title: Transformer Lack of Embedding Layer and Positional Encodings
requirement: The Transformer implementation shall include a built-in token embedding layer and positional encoding mechanism. The embedding layer shall map input token IDs to dense vectors of configurable dimension, and positional encodings shall be added to these embeddings to inject token order information, supporting both fixed sinusoidal and learnable encoding schemes. Both components shall be configurable (e.g., vocabulary size, embedding dimension, maximum sequence length) and integrated such that the Transformer can accept raw token sequences directly, eliminating the need for users to implement embeddings or positional encodings externally.

issue_title: Support soft hyphenation (line breaks at U+00AD plus rendering a hyphen at the end of the line)
requirement: The application shall support soft hyphenation by treating the soft hyphen character (U+00AD) as a permitted line-break point in text layout: when a line break occurs at a soft hyphen, a hyphen shall be rendered at the end of the first line; when no break occurs at that position, the soft hyphen shall remain invisible.

issue_title: [Desktop] - Splash screen or background color customization
requirement: The desktop application shall allow users to customize the splash screen and the background color.

issue_title: [path_provider] Add support for web
requirement: The system shall provide support for the path_provider plugin on the web platform, so that applications using path_provider can retrieve directory paths when running in a browser.

issue_title: Support soft hyphenation (line breaks at U+00AD plus rendering a hyphen at the end of the line)
requirement: The system shall support soft hyphenation by allowing line breaks at U+00AD and rendering a hyphen at the end of the line.

issue_title: Table > TableRow > TableCell colspan
requirement: The `TableCell` component within a `TableRow` shall support a `colSpan` property that accepts a positive integer, allowing the rendered cell to horizontally span across the specified number of columns within the `Table` component.

issue_title: cmd/go: allow verifying vendored code
requirement: The go command shall provide a mechanism to verify the integrity of vendored dependencies, comparing the contents of the `vendor` directory against cryptographic hashes recorded in `go.sum` (or an equivalent vendor manifest) to detect unauthorized modifications, and shall fail relevant operations when discrepancies are found.

issue_title: Allow Hero widgets to have transitions within the same screen
requirement: The system shall enable Hero widget transitions within the same screen.

issue_title: Obfuscate GDScript in production export
requirement: **Requirement: GDScript Obfuscation for Production Export**  The Godot export pipeline shall provide an option to obfuscate GDScript source code when exporting a project for production builds.  **Details:**  1. **Configuration:** The export preset shall include a toggle (e.g., "Obfuscate GDScript") that enables or disables obfuscation for the exported project. The option shall default to disabled.  2. **Scope:** When enabled, all GDScript files included in the export shall be converted to a form that makes the original source code unreadable or significantly harder to reverse-engineer, while preserving identical runtime behavior.  3. **Compatibility:** Obfuscation shall not alter script functionality, signals, exported variables, or any behavior dependent on script names, node paths, or reflection-based calls unless explicitly documented as a limitation.  4. **Debug builds:** Obfuscation shall not be applied to debug exports unless explicitly requested, so that stack traces and debugging remain usable during development.  5. **Reproducibility:** Given the same project state and export settings, the obfuscated output shall be deterministic or the randomization seed shall be configurable.  6. **Documentation:** The feature shall document its limitations, including that obfuscation is not a substitute for security-critical server-side logic and that it does not guarantee protection against determined reverse engineering.

issue_title: Support multiple windows for desktop shells
requirement: The system shall provide multi-window support for desktop shells, enabling applications to create, configure, and manage multiple concurrent and independent windows.

issue_title: Implement similar PyTorch function as model.summary() in keras?
requirement: Add a utility function for PyTorch models that prints a formatted architecture summary analogous to Keras’s `model.summary()`, showing layer names, output shapes, parameter counts, trainable/non-trainable parameters, and total model parameters.

issue_title: AVIF codec support
requirement: The system shall implement native support for the AVIF (AV1 Image File Format) codec, conforming to the ISO/IEC 23008-12 (HEIF) container specification and the AV1 compression standard, to enable both decoding and encoding of still images (MIME type `image/avif`, extension `.avif`) and image sequences (MIME type `image/avif-sequence`, extension `.avifs`).  The implementation shall: - Detect AVIF content via ISOBMFF file signature ( `ftyp` box with `avif` or `avis` major brand) and register appropriate file extensions and MIME types in the format registry; - Decode AVIF images supporting 8-bit and 10-bit color depths, YUV 4:2:0, 4:2:2, and 4:4:4 chroma subsampling, grid-based tiled images, and alpha channels; - Encode AVIF images with configurable quality parameters (lossy CRF/QP values or lossless mode), speed/quality presets, and multi-threaded processing where supported by the underlying AV1 codec; - Preserve metadata (EXIF, XMP, ICC color profiles) through decode/encode round-trips; - Expose AVIF-specific options (quality, lossless toggle, effort/speed) through the application's configuration interface (API, CLI, or GUI); - Return explicit "unsupported format" error codes when AVIF capability is not compiled in or disabled, rather than generic decode failures; - Enforce configurable memory limits during decode to prevent excessive allocation on malformed or malicious files; - Maintain bitstream compatibility and interoperability with reference AVIF implementations (encoders: libaom, SVT-AV1, rav1e; decoders: dav1d, libaom, libgav1).

issue_title: A new compiler flag: "link everything statically or die, dammit!"
requirement: The compiler shall provide a command-line option that requires fully static linking of the output, including all dependencies. If any dependency cannot be linked statically or the target does not support fully static linking, compilation shall fail with a diagnostic rather than falling back to dynamic linking.

issue_title: Add support for global plugins/universal addons
requirement: **Requirement: Support for Global Plugins / Universal Addons**  The system shall provide a mechanism for installing and loading plugins (addons) that are globally available across the application, rather than being scoped to a single project, workspace, or user context.  **Details:**  1. **Global Installation:** Users shall be able to install a plugin once in a system-wide or user-wide location, making it available to all projects without requiring per-project installation.  2. **Automatic Discovery and Loading:** Global plugins shall be discovered and loaded automatically at application startup, subject to any enable/disable settings.  3. **Precedence Rules:** When a global plugin and a project-local plugin share the same identifier, the system shall apply a defined precedence rule (project-local overrides global by default) and shall log or report the conflict.  4. **Management Interface:** The system shall provide commands or UI to list, install, enable, disable, and remove global plugins.  5. **Configuration Scope:** Global plugins shall support both global default settings and per-project overrides.  6. **Compatibility Checks:** The system shall verify plugin version compatibility with the host application before loading and report incompatible plugins without crashing the application.  7. **Isolation:** A failure in a global plugin (load error or runtime exception) shall not prevent the application or other plugins from functioning.

issue_title: Return index of the first visible item in ListView
requirement: The system shall provide a method to return the index of the first visible item in a ListView.

issue_title: Add Vec::contains_ref which is worse for inference but less restrictive than Vec::contains
requirement: Add a `contains_ref` method to `Vec<T>` with signature `fn contains_ref<U>(&self, x: &U) -> bool where T: PartialEq<U>`, which returns `true` if the vector contains an element equal to the provided reference. This method shall provide less restrictive type constraints than `Vec::contains` by permitting comparison against a different type `U`, while accepting weaker type inference as a trade-off.

issue_title: net/http: support HTTP/3
requirement: The net/http package shall provide native support for HTTP/3 (RFC 9114) over QUIC transport, including server and client APIs that enable HTTP/3 communication while maintaining compatibility with existing HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 interfaces, and supporting protocol negotiation via Alt-Svc discovery or explicit configuration.

issue_title: Proc macros: ability to refer to a specific crate/symbol (something similar to `$crate`)
requirement: Support a mechanism in procedural macros that allows referring to the proc-macro crate itself and its exported items by a stable path, analogous to the `$crate` metavariable available in declarative macros. This should enable proc-macro-generated code to unambiguously reference the defining crate's functions, types, and re-exports regardless of how the crate is renamed or referenced by downstream users (e.g., via Cargo rename or dependency aliasing).

issue_title: Add support for global plugins/universal addons
requirement: The system shall support global (universal) plugins/addons that can be installed once at the application level and are automatically available and loaded across all projects and workspaces, eliminating the need for per-project installation. Users shall be able to install, enable, disable, and uninstall global plugins from a central management location, and project-level plugin configuration shall be able to extend or override global plugin behavior where conflicts arise.

issue_title: [RFC] TorchStore - A Shared-Memory Tensor Store
requirement: **Requirement: TorchStore — A Shared-Memory Tensor Store**  **Overview** The system shall provide TorchStore, a shared-memory tensor store service that enables multiple processes (e.g., distributed training workers, data loaders, inference servers) to share PyTorch tensors efficiently through a common, zero-copy shared-memory backing store.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **Tensor Storage API**    - The system shall expose APIs to `put` tensors into the store under a unique key and `get` tensors by key, returning a tensor view backed by the shared memory without copying data.    - The system shall support storing tensors of arbitrary dtype, shape, and stride, including non-contiguous and quantized tensors.  2. **Shared-Memory Backing**    - Tensors shall be allocated in a shared-memory region (e.g., POSIX shared memory or file-backed memory) so that any process attached to the store can access the same tensor data without serialization or IPC copy.    - The system shall support lazy allocation of shared memory regions as tensors are inserted, and shall release memory back to the OS when explicitly deleted.  3. **Multi-Process Access**    - Multiple independent processes shall be able to attach to the same store instance, discover existing tensors, and read/write them subject to the access rules.    - The store shall support concurrent access from multiple processes, including concurrent readers.  4. **Lifecycle Management**    - The system shall provide reference-counting or explicit ownership semantics so that memory is reclaimed only after all processes have detached from a tensor or the store has been closed.    - The system shall support graceful shutdown and cleanup of stale or orphaned shared-memory regions (e.g., after a process crash).  5. **Metadata and Synchronization**    - The store shall maintain metadata (dtype, shape, strides, dtype, device) alongside tensor data, consistent across processes.    - The system shall provide a synchronization mechanism (e.g., versioning, flags, or notifications) so that a producer process can signal that a tensor has been updated and a consumer can wait for or detect availability of a specific tensor.  6. **Storage Backend Extensibility**    - The store design shall allow pluggable backing stores (e.g., in-process memory, shared memory on disk, or a remote store) behind a common interface, while the initial implementation shall target shared memory.  7. **Performance Requirements**    - `put` and `get` operations shall incur zero-copy data transfer between processes sharing the same memory region.    - The store shall minimize per-operation overhead (e.g., metadata lookup) to support high-throughput data pipelines.  8. **Compatibility and Integration**    - The store shall integrate with PyTorch tensor APIs, allowing returned tensors to be used directly in standard PyTorch operations (e.g., autograd, CUDA transfers where applicable).    - The store shall work on Linux and macOS, with support for other platforms considered as follow-up work.  **Non-Functional Requirements** - The implementation shall be robust against process crashes, ensuring no permanent memory leaks in shared memory. - The API shall be documented, including usage examples for producer/consumer patterns. - The implementation shall include unit and integration tests covering multi-process access, crash recovery, and memory reclamation.

issue_title: Subslice search
requirement: **Subslice Search Requirement**  The system shall provide a subslice search operation that, given a slice (the haystack) and a subslice (the needle), determines whether the needle occurs as a contiguous sequence within the haystack.  1. **Input:** The operation accepts two sequences of the same element type: a haystack and a needle. 2. **Match semantics:** A match requires all elements of the needle to appear in the haystack in the same order, with no gaps. Element comparison uses the element type's equality semantics. 3. **Output:** The operation returns the zero-based index of the first occurrence of the needle in the haystack, or a not-found indicator (such as -1) if no occurrence exists. 4. **Empty needle:** An empty needle matches at index 0 for any haystack, including an empty haystack. 5. **Empty haystack:** A non-empty needle against an empty haystack returns not-found. 6. **Needle longer than haystack:** Returns not-found without error. 7. **Multiple occurrences:** The operation returns only the first match. An optional variant may return all starting indices of matches. 8. **Non-mutation:** The operation does not modify either input. 9. **Complexity:** The operation shall run in worst-case O(n·m) time, where n is the haystack length and m is the needle length.

issue_title: Implement Terrain
requirement: The software shall implement a terrain system that generates and renders three-dimensional terrain. The system shall support constructing terrain from heightmap data as well as procedural generation using configurable noise-based algorithms, and shall produce a polygonal terrain mesh with adjustable size and resolution. Terrain surfaces shall be shaded or textured based on elevation and/or slope, and the terrain module shall integrate with the existing rendering pipeline. Generation parameters (e.g., dimensions, resolution, roughness, seed) shall be user-configurable, and the feature shall include documentation and example scenes demonstrating usage.

issue_title: Add support for multiple displays/screens/monitors in Godot editor
requirement: **Requirement: Multi-Display Support in the Godot Editor**  **Summary:** The Godot editor shall support being used across multiple displays, monitors, or screens, allowing users to position, detach, restore, and scale editor windows and panels on any connected display, including mixed-DPI configurations.  **Background:** Developers commonly work with two or more monitors, such as an editor on one display and a running game or reference material on another. The editor currently does not reliably support this workflow, leading to lost window positions, incorrect scaling, and difficulty placing floating panels or the game window on a secondary screen.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **Window placement:** The editor main window and any floating editor windows (docks, dialogs, the game/embedded window when detached) shall be movable to any connected display. 2. **Position persistence:** The editor shall save each window's position, size, and the display it was on, and restore them on the next launch. If the saved display is no longer connected, the window shall be moved to the primary display and kept fully visible. 3. **Monitor change handling:** Hot-plugging or disconnecting a monitor while the editor is running shall not leave any editor window off-screen or unreachable. Affected windows shall be relocated to a visible display. 4. **Per-display scaling:** The editor shall correctly apply each display's DPI/scale factor to its windows, including when windows move between displays with different scale factors, without requiring an editor restart. 5. **Game window placement:** The user shall be able to launch or direct the running game window to a specific display, and the chosen display shall be remembered per project or per run configuration. 6. **Fullscreen behavior:** Fullscreen or maximized editor and game windows shall apply to the display they currently occupy, not always to the primary display. 7. **Screen selection in settings:** Editor settings shall provide an option to select the preferred display for new windows and the game window.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - On a two-monitor setup with different DPI scales, the editor and a floating dock can be moved between monitors with correct rendering and no restart required. - After closing the editor on monitor 2 and relaunching with monitor 2 connected, all windows reopen on monitor 2 at their previous positions and sizes. - After closing the editor on monitor 2 and relaunching with monitor 2 disconnected, all windows open fully visible on the primary display. - Disconnecting a monitor while windows are on it moves those windows to a visible display without crashing or losing unsaved work. - Launching the game from the editor places the game window on the display selected in settings or the project's run configuration. - Behavior is verified on Windows, macOS, and Linux (X11 and Wayland, where the platform supports client-side positioning), with documented limitations for any platform or compositor that restricts window placement.  **Out of Scope:**  - Changes to the rendering pipeline or per-display rendering of a single viewport in the running game. - Multi-display support for exported game builds, which is handled by the project's display settings. - Wayland compositor-specific positioning guarantees beyond what the platform API allows.

issue_title: Add structs in GDScript
requirement: ## Requirement: User-Defined Structs in GDScript  ### Summary GDScript currently offers only two user-definable composite types: classes (requiring a separate script file and an explicit `new()` call) and dictionaries (untyped). There is no way to declare a lightweight, fixed-layout data type whose shape is known at compile time and whose values can be created inline as plain values. This feature adds **structs**: user-declared, statically-typed record types that hold a fixed set of typed fields and behave as value types.  ### Functional Requirements  1. **Struct declaration**    - A `struct` keyword block shall be supported at the top level of a script and as a nested member of a class or another struct.    - Syntax: `struct Name:` followed by an indented body of member declarations, mirroring the existing `class` block syntax.    - Members shall support typed declarations with optional default values, e.g.      ```gdscript      struct Stats:          var health: int = 100          var mana: int = 50          var label: String = ""      ```    - Structs shall support methods and constants in addition to fields, consistent with `class` bodies.  2. **Type usage**    - A struct name shall be usable as a type annotation on variables, parameters, return values, and typed array element declarations (e.g. `var s: Stats`, `func f(s: Stats) -> Stats`, `var list: Array[Stats]`).    - Member accesses shall be statically checked: assigning a value of an incompatible type to a member, or accessing a non-existent member, shall raise a script parse/compile error.    - The declared type of a member shall be respected at runtime.  3. **Construction and value semantics**    - A struct value shall be constructible inline without a separate script resource or `load()` call, e.g. `var s := Stats.new(100, 50)` and/or `var s := Stats { health = 100, mana = 50 }`.    - Structs shall have **value semantics**: copying a struct (assignment, passing to a function, appending to an array) shall produce an independent copy, so mutating the copy shall not affect the original.    - Unspecified members shall be initialized to their declared default values.    - Assignment of a struct to a differently-named struct with an identical member layout shall be permitted (structural compatibility), consistent with GDScript's general duck-typing conventions for classes.  4. **Nesting and composition**    - Structs shall be nestable (a struct may contain members of another struct type) and may be used inside `class` declarations and inside arrays/dictionaries.    - Recursive or mutually recursive struct definitions shall be detected and reported as an error.  5. **Compatibility and tooling**    - Existing GDScript code, projects, and `.gd` files shall continue to compile and run without change; `struct` shall not conflict with any existing reserved word in a way that breaks current scripts (a migration note for any new reserved identifiers shall be provided).    - The editor shall provide autocompletion, member lookup, type hints, and documentation for struct types and their members.    - The GDScript parser, analyzer, and byte-code compiler shall handle struct declarations and usages; `class_name`-style global registration of a struct for use across files shall be supported.    - Structs shall be usable in exported/serialized properties and shall round-trip through `Resource`/scene serialization where the underlying member types are serializable.  6. **Error reporting**    - Invalid struct declarations (duplicate member names, unsupported member kinds, missing type on an untyped member where a type is required, cyclic definitions) shall produce clear, localized error messages identifying the script, line, and offending member.  ### Non-Goals - Binary layout guarantees or interop with C `struct` memory layout. - Reference (pointer) semantics for structs; structs are value types by design.  ### Acceptance Criteria - A script declaring a struct with typed members and defaults compiles without error. - A variable annotated with the struct type accepts a constructed struct value and rejects a value with an incompatible member type. - Mutating a struct obtained from an assignment does not affect the source struct. - Nested structs and `Array[Struct]` declarations parse, type-check, and execute correctly. - The existing GDScript test suite passes with no regressions, and new automated tests cover declaration, construction, copying, nesting, and error cases.

issue_title: Inclusive version of take_while
requirement: **Requirement: Add an Inclusive Variant of `take_while`**  1. The library shall provide a function or iterator adapter named `take_while_inclusive` (or the project's idiomatic equivalent) that accepts an iterable (or iterator) and a predicate.  2. The adapter shall yield elements from the source in their original order, as long as the predicate returns true for each element.  3. When the predicate first returns false for an element, the adapter shall yield that element as well, then stop. No elements after it shall be yielded or evaluated.  4. If the predicate returns true for every element, the adapter shall yield all elements and terminate when the source is exhausted.  5. If the source is empty, the adapter shall yield no elements and shall not invoke the predicate.  6. The adapter shall evaluate lazily. It shall pull elements from the source one at a time, only as needed by the consumer, and shall not consume more source elements than the first failing element requires.  7. The predicate shall be called exactly once per element examined, in source order.  8. The adapter shall not alter, buffer, or copy the yielded elements beyond what the existing `take_while` does.  9. The documentation shall include the function's behavior, a contrast with `take_while` showing that the first failing element is included, and at least one example for each of the following: a predicate that fails partway through, a predicate that never fails, and an empty source.  10. The test suite shall cover items 2 through 7, including the boundary case where the first element fails the predicate (the result is that single element).

Calls that violate the function’s declared parameter requirements shall produce an appropriate error.

issue_title: [google_maps_flutter] Support Widgets as markers
requirement: Requirement: Support Custom Widget Markers in google_maps_flutter  The google_maps_flutter plugin shall allow developers to define map markers using Flutter widgets rather than being limited to static image assets or default marker icons.  Functional requirements:  1. A developer shall be able to supply a Flutter widget as the visual representation of a marker, and the plugin shall render that widget as the marker icon on the map. 2. Widget-based markers shall be created through the existing marker API (e.g., a Marker object with an associated icon), without requiring a separate map overlay system. 3. The plugin shall capture the widget's rendered output (e.g., by rasterizing it to a bitmap) and provide it to the native map SDK as the marker icon. 4. Developers shall be able to update a widget-based marker's appearance (for example, when state changes) and have the change reflected on the map. 5. The rendering of widget markers shall support a configurable logical size and device pixel ratio so markers appear consistently across screen densities. 6. Widget markers shall respond to the same interaction callbacks as standard markers (onTap, draggable behavior, info window anchoring) where the underlying platform supports them. 7. Widget marker rendering shall not block the main UI thread for extended periods, and shall be cached so unchanged widgets are not re-rasterized on every map frame.  Non-functional requirements:  8. The feature shall work on Android, iOS, and web, or document any platform-specific limitations explicitly. 9. Existing marker APIs (BitmapDescriptor-based icons) shall remain unchanged and backward compatible. 10. Documentation and an example app demonstrating widget markers shall be provided.

issue_title: DataLoader with option to re-use worker processes
requirement: Requirement: Persistent Worker Processes for DataLoader  The DataLoader shall provide an option (e.g., `persistent_workers`) that, when enabled, keeps its worker processes alive across iterations over the dataset instead of terminating and respawning them at the start of each epoch.  Details:  1. Configuration: A boolean parameter `persistent_workers` is accepted by the DataLoader constructor. The default value is `False`, preserving existing behavior.  2. Behavior when enabled:    - Worker processes are created once, on the first iteration, and remain alive for subsequent iterations.    - Each new iteration reuses the existing workers without re-forking or re-initializing them.    - Worker state set up in the worker initialization function (`worker_init_fn`) persists across iterations.  3. Behavior when disabled: Worker processes are created at the start of each iteration and shut down when the iteration completes, as currently implemented.  4. Constraints:    - Requires `num_workers > 0`; setting `persistent_workers=True` with `num_workers=0` shall raise a `ValueError`.    - Workers shall be shut down cleanly when the DataLoader is garbage-collected or when its iterator is explicitly released.    - Worker processes shall not leak after the DataLoader is destroyed.  5. Error handling: If a worker process crashes, the DataLoader shall raise an error identifying the failure, consistent with the non-persistent case.  6. Compatibility: Existing DataLoader usage without the new parameter shall behave identically to prior versions.

issue_title: [webview_flutter] Add Windows support
requirement: **Requirement: Windows Platform Support for webview_flutter**  The `webview_flutter` plugin shall provide a Windows implementation so that Flutter applications built for Windows can embed and control web content using the same public API used on other supported platforms.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **Platform Integration**    1.1. The plugin shall register a Windows platform implementation discoverable through Flutter's federated plugin architecture (`webview_flutter_platform_interface`).    1.2. The Windows implementation shall be included in the plugin's `pubspec.yaml` under the `flutter.plugin.platforms` section with the `windows` key.  2. **WebView Rendering**    2.1. The plugin shall render web content in a `WebViewWidget` on Windows using a Windows-compatible browser engine (WebView2 is the expected backend).    2.2. The plugin shall support embedding multiple independent WebView instances within a single Flutter application.  3. **Navigation and Loading**    3.1. The plugin shall support `loadRequest` for URLs with GET and POST methods, including custom headers and request bodies.    3.2. The plugin shall support `loadHtmlString` and `loadFile`/`loadFlutterAsset` where applicable.    3.3. The plugin shall support `goBack`, `goForward`, `reload`, `canGoBack`, and `canGoForward`.    3.4. The plugin shall emit page lifecycle callbacks: `onPageStarted`, `onPageFinished`, `onProgress`, `onWebResourceError`, and `onNavigationRequest`, allowing the application to allow or prevent navigation.  4. **JavaScript Support**    4.1. The plugin shall support enabling and disabling JavaScript via `setJavaScriptMode`.    4.2. The plugin shall support `runJavaScript`, `runJavaScriptReturningResult`, and `addJavaScriptChannel` for bidirectional communication between Dart and web content.  5. **Other Controller Features**    5.1. The plugin shall support setting the user agent via `setUserAgent`.    5.2. The plugin shall support clearing the cache and local storage via `clearLocalStorage` and related cache-clearing APIs where the backend permits.    5.3. The plugin shall support `setBackgroundColor` and `scrollTo`/`scrollBy` where feasible, and shall document any unsupported methods explicitly.    5.4. The plugin shall support cookie management through the platform cookie manager (`WebViewCookieManager`).  6. **Dependencies and Runtime Requirements**    6.1. The plugin shall document the minimum Windows version and the required WebView2 Runtime version.    6.2. The plugin shall detect the absence of the WebView2 Runtime and surface a descriptive error to the Dart layer rather than failing silently.    6.3. The plugin shall build and run with the Flutter Windows toolchain (Visual Studio C++ build tools) without requiring additional manual native configuration beyond documented steps.  7. **Testing and Quality**    7.1. The Windows implementation shall include unit tests for the Dart platform interface and integration tests exercising navigation, JavaScript execution, and channel communication.    7.2. An example application under `example/` shall run on Windows and demonstrate core features.    7.3. The plugin's README and API documentation shall describe Windows-specific behavior, limitations, and setup requirements.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  - The Windows implementation shall conform to the existing `webview_flutter_platform_interface` contract so that application code requires no platform-specific branching for supported features. - Performance overhead of the Windows implementation shall be comparable to other desktop/mobile implementations for page load and JavaScript round-trip latency. - The implementation shall be licensed consistently with the rest of the plugin (BSD-3-Clause).  **Acceptance Criteria**  - A Flutter app targeting Windows can load a URL, receive navigation events, execute JavaScript, and exchange messages through a JavaScript channel using only the public `webview_flutter` API. - Running the example app on a supported Windows machine with WebView2 installed succeeds without errors. - Missing WebView2 Runtime produces a clear, catchable error.

requirement: **Requirement:** The system shall provide a scalable serving framework to host and serve trained PyTorch models via standardized inference APIs. The framework must support loading models from TorchScript archives (`.pt`/`.pth`) or serialized `state_dict` checkpoints, expose HTTP/REST and gRPC endpoints for synchronous and asynchronous inference requests, implement dynamic request batching to optimize throughput, handle automatic serialization/deserialization of tensors to/from JSON or Protobuf payloads, manage GPU/CPU device placement and memory, support versioned model registry with zero-downtime hot-reload capabilities, provide pluggable pre-processing and post-processing hooks, and expose health, readiness, and metrics monitoring endpoints. The framework shall ensure thread-safe handling of concurrent requests and return structured error responses for invalid inputs, missing models, or inference failures.

issue_title: cmd/go: 'go mod why' should have an answer for every module in 'go list -m all'
requirement: ## Requirement: `go mod why` must explain every module in the build list  ### Background  `go list -m all` reports every module in the main module's build list, including modules that are present only because the module graph (MVS) requires them and are never imported. Today, `go mod why` can only produce an import-based explanation, so for many of those modules it has no answer: it either prints an empty/omitted chain, or fails outright with an error such as `module <path>: not a known dependency`, even though the module is listed by `go list -m all`. Users (and tools) therefore cannot tell *why* a given module is in the build list.  ### Required behavior  1. **Complete coverage.** Running `go mod why -m all` must produce exactly one explanation for every module reported by `go list -m all`. The command must not fail, and must not omit or leave blank any module's entry.  2. **Two kinds of explanations.**    - If the module is needed to build packages in the main module (i.e., some package of the module is imported, transitively, by the main module or by one of its dependencies), `go mod why` must print the existing chain of imports/requirements leading from the main module to that package, e.g.:      ```      main/module      main/module/pkg      example.com/needed@v1.2.3      example.com/needed/pkg      ```    - If the module is **not** imported by anything in the main module's import graph, `go mod why` must still answer, using the module requirement graph: it must report the chain of module requirements (`go mod graph` edges) that brings the module into the build list, e.g.:      ```      main/module      example.com/intermediate@v1.0.0      example.com/unused@v1.1.0      ```      or, if no requirement path exists, it must state explicitly that the main module does not need the module and give the reason it is nevertheless in the build list (for example, it is required for the module graph only / by a test-only or indirect dependency).  3. **Per-module queries.** `go mod why -m <module>` for a module that appears in `go list -m all` must return a non-empty explanation of the same form described above (import chain, requirement path, or an explicit "not needed, and here's why it is in the build list" statement). It must not report the module as unknown when it is present in the build list.  4. **Consistency.** The set of modules for which `go mod why` returns an explanation must be identical to the set reported by `go list -m all`; the two commands must agree on the build list and on the selected versions of each module.  5. **Output stability.** The explanation must be deterministic (stable ordering of modules and of the chains) so that the output can be diffed and consumed by tooling.  ### Acceptance criteria  - For a main module whose `go.mod` requires a module that is never imported, `go mod why -m all` lists that module with a requirement-path explanation rather than an empty line or an error. - `go mod why -m all` exits with status 0 and prints one line-block per module in `go list -m all`, with no blank or missing entries. - `go mod why -m <mod>` succeeds for every module in `go list -m all`. - Existing import-chain output for needed modules is preserved (no regression in format or content). - The behavior is covered by `cmd/go` tests (e.g., `script/mod_why.sh`) including a test module with an unimported requirement.

issue_title: format_args! is slow
requirement: ## Requirement: Optimize the `format_args!` macro  ### Problem  The `format_args!` macro, which builds a `std::fmt::Arguments` value for use with formatting APIs such as `format!`, `write!`, `println!`, and `panic!`, is currently expensive. Expanding it produces a large amount of generated code (format-spec parsing machinery, per-argument handler thunks, and a stack-allocated `Arguments`/`Pieces` structure), which increases compile times, bloats binary size, and imposes measurable runtime overhead even for trivial format strings such as `format_args!("hello")` or `format_args!("{}", x)`.  ### Requirement  `format_args!` must be reworked so that constructing a `fmt::Arguments` value is effectively free unless formatting actually takes place, while preserving all observable behavior.  Specifically:  1. **Low-overhead expansion** — the code generated for a `format_args!` invocation must be substantially smaller than today. The common cases (no arguments, a single literal string, and a small number of primitive arguments) must not emit the full generic formatting machinery. 2. **No unnecessary work at construction time** — building the `Arguments` value must not perform format-string parsing, allocation, or handler dispatch eagerly. Parsing of the format string must be done at compile time wherever possible, and any remaining runtime work must be proportional to the actual formatting performed. 3. **Cheap common paths** — formatting a `Arguments` value that contains only literal text, or text plus simple primitive types, should avoid dynamic dispatch and heap allocation, and should be measurably faster than the current implementation. 4. **Preserved semantics** — the following must remain unchanged:    - All existing formatting traits and specifiers behave identically, including `{}`, `{0}`, named arguments, width/precision, `{:?}`, `{:#?}`, `{:x}`, `{:#x}`, fill/align, and custom `Display`/`Debug`/`LowerHex`/`UpperHex` implementations.    - The lifetime and borrow semantics of the produced `fmt::Arguments` (borrowing from the format string and the arguments) are unchanged.    - Compile-time errors for malformed format strings are still reported, and error messages remain helpful.    - `format_args!` results may still be stored in a `let` binding and passed to functions taking `fmt::Arguments`, and may still be used directly as a formatting argument. 5. **Compatibility** — the optimization must not require changes to user code and must not break downstream crates, `no_std` targets, or `const`-context usage patterns that are currently supported.  ### Success criteria  - Benchmarks of `format!`/`write!`/`println!`-style calls with 0–3 arguments show a clear reduction in runtime and in allocation count compared to the current implementation. - Binary size of a program using `format_args!` in typical ways is reduced. - Compile time of crates using `format!`/`println!` extensively is reduced. - The existing test suite, including formatting-trait and compile-fail tests, passes unchanged.

issue_title: Add a Trait system for GDScript
requirement: **Requirement: Trait System for GDScript**  GDScript shall support traits as a reusable, composable unit of behavior that can be shared across classes without inheritance.  1. **Declaration:** A developer can declare a trait in a script or resource, containing method definitions and optionally properties and signals. 2. **Composition:** A class can include one or more traits using a dedicated keyword or annotation. Included members become part of the class as if they were declared in it. 3. **Conflict handling:** If two included traits, or a trait and the class itself, define a member with the same name, the parser shall report a compile-time error unless the conflict is explicitly resolved by the developer. 4. **Required members:** A trait may declare abstract methods that any including class must implement. Omitting a required member shall produce a compile-time error. 5. **Type and reference behavior:** Trait membership shall not alter the class's inheritance chain. `is` checks and type hints shall work against traits, and `self` within trait methods shall refer to the including instance. 6. **Tooling:** The editor shall provide autocompletion and error highlighting for trait members within including classes. 7. **Compatibility:** Existing GDScript code without traits shall behave unchanged, and the feature shall not add runtime overhead to classes that do not use traits.
