issue_title: Implement a code formatter for GDScript in the script editor
requirement: ## Requirement: GDScript Code Formatter for the Script Editor  ### 1. Overview  The Script Editor shall provide a built-in formatting capability that reformats the currently open GDScript source file according to a defined, configurable set of style rules, using the engine's existing GDScript parser to guarantee that formatting never changes program semantics.  ### 2. Functional Requirements  **FR-1 — Invocation** - The formatter shall be invocable from the Script Editor via a menu command (e.g. `Script > Format Script` / `Format`), a toolbar button, and a keyboard shortcut. - The command shall operate on the active script editor tab and be disabled (greyed out) when no GDScript file is open or when the editor is in read-only mode. - The formatter shall be a user-callable action only; it must not run automatically on file open, save, or paste unless the user explicitly enables such an option.  **FR-2 — Scope of reformatting** - When invoked, the formatter shall replace the entire contents of the editor buffer with the formatted result. - The formatter shall format the whole file, not a selection or cursor region. - Formatting shall apply to all supported GDScript constructs: imports, class declarations and inheritance, `extends`, `class_name`, signals, enums, constants, `@export`/`@onready`/other annotations, variables, functions (including static, virtual/overridden, and constructors), inner classes, `if`/`elif`/`else`, `match`, `for`, `while`, `break`/`continue`/`pass`/`return`, `await`, expressions, arrays/dictionaries, lambda (`func` literals), and comments. - Trailing whitespace shall be removed from all lines; the file shall end with exactly one newline character.  **FR-3 — Formatting rules (configurable style)** The formatter shall implement, at minimum, the following rules: - **Indentation:** tab characters by default (configurable to spaces, with configurable indent width); block bodies indented one level relative to their parent; continuation lines of multi-line expressions/statements indented consistently. - **Whitespace around operators and keywords:** exactly one space around binary/unary assignment and comparison operators, after commas, after colons, and around `=` in keyword arguments; no space before commas or colons; no space inside parentheses or brackets. - **Keyword and builtin spacing:** one space after keywords such as `if`, `elif`, `while`, `for`, `return`, `var`, `const`, `func`, `in`, `not`, `and`, `or`, `assert`; `func` declarations shall use `func name(args):` with no space before the opening parenthesis. - **Blank lines:** at most one consecutive blank line within a function body or class body; blank lines between top-level declarations shall be preserved up to a configurable maximum; no leading blank lines at the start of the file or immediately before a closing brace-less block terminator beyond the configured maximum. - **Line length:** lines exceeding a configurable maximum length (default 100 characters) shall be wrapped where a safe, unambiguous break point exists (e.g. after commas in argument lists and array/dictionary literals, before binary operators); if no safe break exists, the line shall be left intact rather than truncated or syntactically altered. - **Comments:** comment markers shall be normalized to a single leading space (`# text`), preserving the comment text; comments shall retain their relative position and association with the following or preceding declaration.  **FR-4 — Configuration** - Formatting options (indent style, indent width, max line length, max consecutive blank lines, spacing rules) shall be exposed in the Editor Settings / Script Editor settings dialog. - A "Restore defaults" action shall be available. - Settings shall persist across editor sessions.  **FR-5 — Safety and correctness** - The formatter shall parse the script with the GDScript parser before applying changes. If the script contains syntax errors, the formatter shall abort, leave the buffer unmodified, and report the error to the user (e.g. via an editor notification/dialog identifying the error location). - Formatting shall be idempotent: running the formatter twice in succession on the same input shall produce byte-identical output. - Formatting shall be semantics-preserving: string literals (including multi-line strings, raw strings, and triple-quoted strings), escape sequences, and comment content shall never be modified beyond whitespace outside of them. - Formatted output shall re-parse successfully with the GDScript parser; the formatter shall verify this before committing the change and abort with an error if the result would not parse.  **FR-6 — Undo/redo and editor integration** - Applying formatting shall be a single undoable editor operation (one entry in the undo history), so `Ctrl+Z` restores the original text in one step. - If the buffer has unsaved modifications, the formatter shall use the current in-editor content as its input. - After formatting, the cursor position and editor scroll position shall be adjusted so the caret remains on a logically equivalent location, and the script shall be re-highlighted with no reported errors.  ### 3. Non-Functional Requirements  - **Performance:** formatting a 5,000-line script shall complete in under 500 ms on a typical development machine; the editor UI shall not freeze visibly during the operation. - **Compatibility:** shall support Godot 4.x GDScript syntax and shall be developed as a module/editor plugin that compiles against the engine's `GDScriptParser`/`GDScriptTokenizer` APIs. - **Extensibility:** the rule set shall be implemented as discrete, individually testable rule objects so that additional rules can be added without modifying the driver. - **Testing:** unit tests shall cover each formatting rule, idempotency, syntax-error abort, and preservation of string literals and comments; the test suite shall run in CI via the engine's headless test runner.  ### 4. Out of Scope (v1)  - Formatting other script languages (C#, GLSL, or resource files). - Automatic "fix on save" or "format on paste" behaviour beyond the optional user-enabled setting noted in FR-1. - Refactoring, code linting diagnostics, or style violation squiggles separate from the formatter's own safety checks. - Full bidirectional preservation of user-authored line breaks in free-form multi-line expressions beyond wrapping to the configured maximum line length.  ### 5. Acceptance Criteria  1. Opening a GDScript file containing mixed indentation, inconsistent spacing, and trailing whitespace and invoking `Format Script` produces output matching the configured style rules. 2. A script with a syntax error is left unchanged and an error is displayed to the user. 3. Formatting the same input twice yields identical output (verified by a unit test). 4. String literals and comment text containing sequences resembling code formatting (e.g. `var x = 1` inside a string) are preserved verbatim. 5. A single `Undo` restores the pre-format buffer contents exactly. 6. All formatting options can be changed in Editor Settings and take effect on the next format invocation without restarting the editor.

issue_title: Feature Request: Easier to extend base RNN implementation
requirement: **REQ-RNN-EXT-001: Modular Extension Points for Base Recurrent Neural Network Implementation**  The base RNN class shall provide a modular architecture with explicitly defined extension points that enable developers to customize recurrence dynamics, state management, and output generation through subclassing or dependency injection, without requiring modification of the core forward-pass implementation.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. The base implementation shall decompose the per-timestep computation into discrete, overridable protected methods: `compute_cell_transition(input_t, hidden_state_prev)`, `update_hidden_state(cell_state, hidden_state)`, and `project_output(hidden_state)`, allowing subclasses to alter specific aspects of the recurrence without rewriting the iteration loop. 2. The class shall expose hook methods (`pre_timestep_hook`, `post_hidden_update_hook`, `pre_output_hook`) that are invoked at precise stages of the forward pass (before input processing, after state update, before output emission) to support injection of custom logic such as attention mechanisms or adaptive gating. 3. Internal state tensors (hidden state and cell state, where applicable) shall be accessible via protected properties during the forward pass to enable custom state manipulation and external memory integration. 4. The forward method shall accept an optional `step_function` callable parameter that, when provided, replaces the default recurrence computation for that instance, supporting functional composition without subclassing. 5. The extensibility API shall maintain full compatibility with the framework's automatic differentiation system, ensuring gradients propagate correctly through any custom operations defined in overridden methods or hooks. 6. Multi-layer and bidirectional configurations shall inherit these extension capabilities, allowing per-layer customization of the recurrence logic while preserving the existing stacking API.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - A new RNN variant can be implemented by subclassing the base class and overriding only the specific methods relevant to the customization (e.g., a modified LSTM with custom forget-gate computation) without duplicating time-step iteration or batching logic. - Existing `RNN`, `LSTM`, and `GRU` implementations continue to function as subclasses of the extensible base class with no breaking changes to their public APIs or numerical behavior. - Unit tests verify that hooks execute in the correct sequence relative to state updates and that gradients flow through custom hook implementations. - Technical documentation includes at least two working examples demonstrating: (a) creation of a custom cell type via method overriding, and (b) runtime injection of per-timestep behavior via hooks.

issue_title: RFC: Introduce `setup`, `teardown`, and `fixture` attributes for `cargo test`
requirement: **REQ-ID:** FEAT-TEST-001  **Title:** Introduce `setup`, `teardown`, and `fixture` attributes for `cargo test`  **Requirement Description:** The Rust test framework (as invoked via `cargo test`) shall provide first-class support for test lifecycle management through the `#[setup]`, `#[teardown]`, and `#[fixture]` attributes, enabling automated per-test initialization, guaranteed cleanup, and dependency injection of reusable test context.  **Functional Requirements:**  - **FR-1:** The framework shall recognize `#[setup]`, `#[teardown]`, and `#[fixture]` attributes applied to functions within test code (`cfg(test)` modules and integration test crates). - **FR-2:** A function annotated with `#[setup]` shall execute automatically immediately before each test function in the same module. Its return value, if any, shall be passed to each test function as an argument. - **FR-3:** A function annotated with `#[teardown]` shall execute automatically immediately after each test function in the same module completes, regardless of whether the test passes, fails, or panics. - **FR-4:** `#[teardown]` functions shall receive the state produced by the corresponding `#[setup]` and any fixtures constructed for that test, so that all allocated resources can be released. - **FR-5:** A function annotated with `#[fixture]` shall define a reusable test fixture: test functions may declare parameters whose types match a fixture's return type, and the framework shall construct and inject a fresh fixture value for each test invocation. - **FR-6:** Fixtures shall support composition — a fixture may declare parameters resolved from other fixtures — and shall be importable and reusable across modules subject to standard Rust visibility rules. - **FR-7:** If a `#[setup]` function or fixture constructor fails or panics, the affected test shall be reported as failed, and any fixtures already constructed for that test shall be torn down. - **FR-8:** Panics or errors occurring inside `#[teardown]` shall be captured and reported as test failures without masking the original test outcome. - **FR-9:** The compiler/test harness shall report compile-time errors for: (a) ambiguous fixture resolution (multiple applicable fixtures of the same type in scope), (b) unresolved fixture parameters, and (c) application of these attributes outside a valid test context. - **FR-10:** All existing tests that do not use the new attributes shall compile and execute with unchanged behavior (full backward compatibility).  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  - **NFR-1:** Fixture and parameter resolution shall occur at compile time with zero runtime reflection overhead. - **NFR-2:** Test execution overhead introduced by the lifecycle hooks shall be negligible; tests not using the attributes shall exhibit no measurable performance change.  **Scope:** Per-test semantics only for this requirement. Suite-level one-time hooks and async runtime variants are explicitly out of scope.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - **AC-1:** `cargo test` executes `#[setup]` before and `#[teardown]` after every test in scope, including tests that panic. - **AC-2:** A test declaring a fixture-typed parameter receives a newly constructed fixture instance for each test run. - **AC-3:** Official documentation and usage examples for all three attributes are provided.

issue_title: [video_player] Support DRM content
requirement: **Requirement: Support DRM-Protected Content Playback in video_player**  The video_player plugin shall support playback of DRM-protected video content, specifically content encrypted with Widevine (Android) and FairPlay (iOS).  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **R1 – DRM Configuration API:** The video_player API shall expose an optional DRM configuration parameter when creating a player instance, allowing the caller to specify:    - The DRM scheme type (e.g., Widevine, FairPlay, ClearKey).    - The license server URL from which decryption keys are acquired.    - Optional DRM-specific request headers and license request parameters.  2. **R2 – Encrypted Stream Playback:** The player shall successfully decrypt and play encrypted media streams (e.g., DASH with Widevine, HLS with FairPlay) when a valid DRM configuration is provided, without degradation of standard playback features (play, pause, seek, buffering, and playback position reporting).  3. **R3 – Unencrypted Content Compatibility:** The player shall continue to play unencrypted media content without requiring any DRM configuration, preserving full backward compatibility with the existing API.  4. **R4 – Error Handling:** The player shall report DRM-related failures (e.g., license acquisition failure, unsupported DRM scheme, missing device-level DRM support) through the existing error-handling mechanisms, with error codes distinguishing DRM failures from general playback errors.  5. **R5 – Capability Detection:** The plugin shall provide a mechanism to query whether the current device supports a given DRM scheme, so applications can adapt content delivery accordingly.  6. **R6 – Platform Parity:** The DRM functionality shall be implemented consistently across supported platforms (Android, iOS, and web where feasible), with any platform-specific limitations documented.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - A Widevine-protected DASH stream can be played on Android using a license server URL. - A FairPlay-protected HLS stream can be played on iOS using a license server URL. - Existing unencrypted playback use cases behave identically to previous versions. - DRM failures surface as descriptive errors rather than silent playback failures.

issue_title: Obfuscate GDScript in production export
requirement: **Requirement: Obfuscation of GDScript in Production Exports**  The Godot export pipeline shall provide an option to obfuscate GDScript code included in production (release) builds so that the exported game's script logic is difficult to read or reverse-engineer.  **Functional Requirements**  1. The export preset dialog shall include a toggle, disabled by default, to enable GDScript obfuscation for release exports. 2. When enabled, the exporter shall transform all GDScript files included in the PCK, including autoloads and scripts embedded in scenes and resources, so that original identifiers (class, function, variable, and signal names) are not recoverable from the exported output. 3. Obfuscation shall be applied only to release and production export templates. Debug exports shall retain readable symbols to support debugging and stack traces. 4. Obfuscation shall not alter runtime behavior. Exported projects with obfuscation enabled shall pass the same automated test suite as non-obfuscated exports. 5. Identifiers referenced dynamically (for example, through `call()`, `has_method()`, `get()`/`set()` with string names, `@export` properties, signal connections made in the editor, node paths, and resource references) shall be excluded from renaming or mapped consistently so that they continue to resolve at runtime. 6. The exporter shall generate a mapping file that links obfuscated names to original names. The mapping file shall be written to a location excluded from the distributed build and shall be available to developers for crash report symbolication. 7. The exporter shall allow developers to specify identifiers or files to exclude from obfuscation, via the export preset or a project-level configuration file. 8. The exporter shall log a warning listing any identifiers it could not safely obfuscate due to dynamic reference patterns.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  1. Obfuscation shall add no more than 20% to export time for a project of 1,000 GDScript files on reference hardware, to be defined and documented by the maintainers. 2. Obfuscation shall be deterministic for a given project state and configuration, so that repeated exports produce identical obfuscated output. 3. Obfuscation shall be documented as a deterrent, not a security guarantee. Documentation shall state that it does not protect against determined reverse engineering and that it complements, but does not replace, script encryption (Encrypt Exported PCK) for protecting code.  **Acceptance Criteria**  - Exporting a release build with obfuscation enabled produces a PCK in which searching for original function and variable names returns no matches in the compiled script data. - A debug export with the same project retains original identifiers. - A release build with obfuscation enabled runs without errors across the existing test project suite, including scenes using `@export`, signals, autoloads, and dynamic method calls. - The mapping file allows a stack trace from an obfuscated release build to be translated back to original file names and line numbers. - Excluded identifiers and files appear unchanged in the output.

issue_title: [Poll] Support DistributedDataParallel (DDP) in PyTorch C++ API (libtorch)
requirement: ## Requirement: DistributedDataParallel Support in the PyTorch C++ API (libtorch)  ### 1. Overview  The C++ frontend of PyTorch (`libtorch`, `torch/csrc/api`) currently provides no way to replicate a module across multiple processes and synchronize gradients during training. This feature requires exposing a C++ implementation of DistributedDataParallel (DDP) so that native C++ applications can perform distributed data-parallel training using the same semantics and configuration options as the existing Python `torch.nn.parallel.DistributedDataParallel` class.  ### 2. Functional Requirements  **FR-1 — Class and construction** A public C++ type `torch::nn::DistributedDataParallel` shall be provided in a header under the `torch::nn` namespace, movable/copyable according to the conventions of other `torch::nn` modules, and constructible with: - The wrapped module (`std::shared_ptr<Module>`), which must not be null. - A `DistributedDataParallelOptions` struct supporting at minimum: the process group to use (defaulting to the default process group), the communication backend (e.g. `gloo`, `nccl`), whether to broadcast buffers at the start of each forward pass, the maximum bucket size in megabytes for gradient bucketing, whether to compute unused parameters (`find_unused_parameters`), whether gradients are exposed as views into communication buckets (`gradient_as_bucket_view`), and whether to join the module's parameters to the communication bucket view.  **FR-2 — Gradient synchronization** During the backward pass, gradients of the wrapped module's parameters shall be all-reduced across all ranks of the process group and divided by the world size (unless gradient scaling is disabled), matching Python DDP semantics. The reduction shall be bucketed so that gradients are coalesced into contiguous buffers of the configured maximum size before transmission, and a single collective operation shall be used per bucket.  **FR-3 — Forward behavior** Calling the module's `forward()` shall execute the wrapped module's forward pass. When `broadcast_buffers` is enabled, buffers (e.g. BatchNorm running statistics) shall be broadcast from rank 0 to all other ranks before the forward computation.  **FR-4 — Parameter and buffer management** The wrapped module's parameters and buffers shall be registered with the DDP module so that they are discoverable through the standard `torch::nn::Module` API (`parameters()`, `buffers()`, `named_parameters()`, `state_dict()`, `load_state_dict()`), and shall be accessible through accessors (e.g. `module()` returning the wrapped module).  **FR-5 — Checkpointing** `state_dict()` and `load_state_dict()` shall include DDP-specific metadata sufficient to resume training from a checkpoint saved by either the C++ or Python DDP implementation, and the implementation shall be interoperable with Python DDP checkpoints, including the ability to load a Python-saved DDP state dict into the C++ DDP module (ignoring or validating the Python-specific `module.` prefix appropriately).  **FR-6 — Autograd hooks / reducer integration** The implementation shall hook into the autograd engine (or use an equivalent mechanism) so that gradient readiness is detected as parameters complete backward, gradients are accumulated into buckets, and the all-reduce is issued without requiring user intervention.  **FR-7 — Process group dependency** The feature shall rely on the existing `c10d`/`torch::distributed` process group APIs (`ProcessGroup`, `Allreduce`, `Broadcast`) and shall support both the Gloo and NCCL backends.  **FR-8 — Python parity** The C++ DDP implementation shall expose the same configuration options and observable behavior as `torch.nn.parallel.DistributedDataParallel` for the supported option set, and shall be usable in a mixed environment where some ranks run Python and others run C++ within the same process group.  ### 3. Non-Functional Requirements  - The implementation shall be header/source compatible with the `libtorch` build system and distributed build (`USE_DISTRIBUTED`), and shall compile without errors when distributed support is disabled (with the type or its constructor reporting an informative error if a process group is unavailable). - Performance of gradient synchronization shall be comparable to the Python DDP implementation for the same bucket size and backend. - Code shall follow the project's existing style, naming conventions, and documentation standards for the C++ API.  ### 4. Out of Scope  - Implementations of `DistributedDataParallel` variants beyond the standard DDP (e.g., FSDP, DeepSpeed, or ZeRO stages 1–3). - Distributed inference or model-parallel APIs. - Additional optimizations not present in the Python DDP implementation.  ### 5. Acceptance Criteria  1. A C++ program can initialize a process group, wrap an `nn::Linear`/`nn::Conv2d` module in `torch::nn::DistributedDataParallel`, run forward and backward passes, and observe gradients that are identical across all ranks after the backward pass. 2. `state_dict()` output from the C++ DDP module can be loaded by Python `DistributedDataParallel.load_state_dict()` and vice versa, with parameter values matching. 3. All options listed in FR-1 are settable via `DistributedDataParallelOptions` and produce the documented effect. 4. The implementation builds and passes the project's unit tests, including at least one multi-process (gloo) test covering forward/backward and checkpoint round-tripping.

The mechanism shall:  1. Allow a prepared statement to be executed repeatedly with multiple sets of arguments as one batched operation, without requiring the caller to issue each execution separately. 2. Work across supported database drivers, with drivers that lack native batch support falling back to sequential execution while preserving the same API semantics. 3. Return results for the batch, including per-statement row-affected counts where the driver provides them, and surface errors that identify the failing argument set. 4. Respect the existing Context-aware execution model, so that batches can be canceled or time out via context. 5. Execute within the caller's transaction when one is in use, and roll back or leave the transaction state under the caller's control in the event of failure. 6. Be exposed through an API that is consistent with existing Exec, Query, and Prepare methods and does not break backward compatibility with current driver interfaces.

issue_title: [google_maps_flutter] Support Widgets as markers
requirement: **Requirement: Support Custom Widget-Based Markers in google_maps_flutter**  The google_maps_flutter plugin shall allow developers to define map markers using Flutter widgets, in addition to the existing bitmap-based marker icons, so that marker appearance can be composed from arbitrary Flutter widget trees.  **Functional Requirements**  1. The plugin shall provide an API that accepts a Flutter widget as the visual representation of a marker, identified by a `MarkerId` and positioned by a `LatLng`. 2. The plugin shall render the supplied widget off-screen, convert it to a bitmap, and display the resulting image as the marker icon on the native map (Google Maps SDK for Android and iOS, and Google Maps JavaScript API for web). 3. The widget-based marker API shall accept a configurable logical size and device pixel ratio so that the rendered bitmap is sharp across screen densities. 4. The plugin shall support updating a widget marker's appearance by supplying a new widget for an existing `MarkerId`, re-rendering the bitmap and refreshing the map marker without recreating the marker. 5. The plugin shall support existing marker properties (position, anchor, info window, alpha, rotation, flat, draggable, visibility, zIndex, onTap) for widget-based markers, consistent with the current `Marker` API. 6. The plugin shall allow widget markers to be removed and updated in batches, consistent with the existing `GoogleMapController` marker operations. 7. The plugin shall cache rendered bitmaps keyed by widget identity or an explicit cache key, so that unchanged widgets are not re-rendered on every map update. 8. The plugin shall provide a mechanism to specify a fallback or placeholder bitmap displayed while the widget is being rendered.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  1. Rendering a widget marker shall not block the UI thread for longer than one frame where avoidable; rendering shall be asynchronous. 2. Widget marker rendering shall work with the existing platform-specific map implementations without requiring changes to the native Google Maps SDK. 3. Memory consumption from cached bitmaps shall be bounded, with a configurable cache size limit. 4. The feature shall be documented with examples, including performance guidance for large numbers of widget markers. 5. Existing bitmap-based marker APIs shall remain unchanged and backward compatible.  **Acceptance Criteria**  1. A developer can add a marker whose appearance is a custom widget (e.g., a rounded container with text and an icon), and it renders correctly on the map on Android, iOS, and web. 2. Updating the widget for an existing marker changes its rendered appearance without removing and re-adding the marker. 3. Widget markers respond to tap events and honor all standard marker properties. 4. Rendering uses the device pixel ratio so markers appear crisp on high-density displays. 5. Existing tests for bitmap markers continue to pass, and new unit and integration tests cover widget marker creation, update, removal, and caching.

When the function is called, this parameter shall contain an `Array` of all additional positional arguments, in their original order. Fixed parameters shall retain their existing type-checking, default-value, and argument-count behavior. Passing zero variadic arguments shall be valid, while passing surplus arguments to a function without a variadic parameter shall continue to produce an argument-count error.  Variadic functions shall behave consistently when invoked directly, through `Callable`, or through `callv()`. An `Array` of variadic arguments shall be expandable at the call site using GDScript’s existing `...` spread syntax. Type annotations on variadic parameters, where provided, shall be enforced for every collected argument. The language reference shall document the syntax and behavior.

issue_title: Add a Trait system for GDScript
requirement: # Requirement: Trait System for GDScript  ## Summary GDScript shall provide a trait mechanism that allows developers to define reusable, composable units of behavior—methods and contracts—and apply them to classes independently of the inheritance hierarchy, enabling behavior sharing across unrelated classes without duplicate code or forced base-class coupling.  ## Functional Requirements  **FR-1 — Trait declaration.** Users shall be able to declare a trait using dedicated language syntax (illustrative: `trait Name:`) in a `.gd` file. A trait may contain: - concrete methods with implementations, - abstract methods (signature only, no body), - constants and static functions.  Traits shall be stateless: they shall not declare instance member variables or constructors.  **FR-2 — Trait application.** A class shall be able to apply one or more traits using explicit syntax (illustrative: `implements TraitA, TraitB`). All members provided by an applied trait shall be accessible on instances of the applying class as if declared in the class itself. A trait shall be applicable to any class regardless of its base class.  **FR-3 — Contract enforcement.** When a trait declares abstract methods, the applying class shall provide concrete implementations (directly or via inheritance); otherwise, the analyzer shall report an error identifying each missing method. Concrete trait methods shall be inherited by the applying class unless explicitly overridden.  **FR-4 — Conflict resolution.** - Members defined by the applying class shall take precedence over identically named trait members. - If two applied traits declare the same member and the class does not define it, the analyzer shall report an ambiguity error.  **FR-5 — Orthogonality to inheritance.** A class may simultaneously extend a base class and apply traits. Trait application shall not modify the class's inheritance chain and shall not change `is` semantics with respect to base classes.  **FR-6 — Typing and runtime integration.** Trait names shall be usable as types in variable, parameter, and return-type annotations. The system shall provide a runtime conformance check (illustrative: `instance is TraitName`) consistent with static analysis results. Trait members shall be visible to reflection APIs and editor tooling.  **FR-7 — Diagnostics.** All trait-related errors (missing implementations, ambiguous conflicts, invalid trait usage) shall produce clear, actionable analyzer messages referencing the source file and line.  ## Constraints - The feature shall be implemented within the GDScript module (tokenizer, parser, analyzer, code generation) without breaking changes to existing scripts. - Trait scripts shall load, export, and behave identically in editor (`tool`), debug, and release builds.  ## Acceptance Criteria 1. A trait with a concrete method applied to two unrelated classes is callable on instances of both. 2. Applying a trait with an unimplemented abstract method produces an analyzer error naming the missing method. 3. A same-named member contributed by two applied traits, not overridden by the class, produces an ambiguity error. 4. A class that both extends a base class and applies a trait exposes inherited and trait-provided members without conflict. 5. Autocompletion, goto definition, and documentation display trait-provided members on applying classes. 6. Runtime trait-conformance checks return results consistent with static analysis.

requirement: GDScript shall support array destructuring (unpacking), enabling multiple variables to be declared or assigned from the elements of an array in a single statement (e.g., `var a, b = [1, 2]` and `a, b = my_array`). The feature shall also support nested destructuring patterns (e.g., `var a, [b, c] = [1, [2, 3]]`) and destructuring in for-loop headers when iterating over arrays of arrays (e.g., `for key, value in pairs:`). If the number of target variables does not match the number of array elements, the parser/analyzer shall report a clear error where statically detectable; otherwise, a descriptive runtime error shall be raised. issue_title: A new compiler flag: "link everything statically or die, dammit!"
requirement: **Requirement: Strict Static Linking Flag**  The compiler shall provide a new command-line flag (e.g., `-static-strict`) that requires all linked libraries, including the C/C++ runtime and all transitive dependencies, to be linked statically.  1. **Enforcement:** When the flag is enabled, the toolchain shall link every library statically. It shall not fall back to dynamic linking for any library. 2. **Failure on unavailability:** If any required library has no static archive (e.g., `.a` or `.lib`) available in the search paths, the link step shall fail with a nonzero exit status. 3. **Diagnostics:** The failure message shall identify each library that could not be statically linked, the search paths checked, and the reason for failure. 4. **Distinction from existing behavior:** The flag shall be stricter than any existing `-static` option. Where `-static` may silently produce a dynamically linked binary, `-static-strict` shall never produce one. 5. **Dynamic-loading exceptions:** Libraries that inherently require dynamic linking on the target platform (for example, glibc NSS modules or platform system frameworks) shall be reported as errors unless the user explicitly whitelists them through a documented option. 6. **Platform support:** The flag shall be supported on all platforms where static linking is technically possible. On platforms where it is not, the compiler shall reject the flag with a clear error at invocation time rather than ignoring it. 7. **Documentation:** The flag, its behavior, its failure modes, and its platform limitations shall be documented in the compiler's manual and `--help` output. 8. **Testing:** Automated tests shall cover successful fully static builds, failure when a static archive is missing, failure when a dependency is only available as a shared object, and correct exit codes and diagnostics for each case.

issue_title: Expo like tool for flutter
requirement: **Requirement: Expo-Like Managed Workflow and Tooling for Flutter**  **Summary** Provide an opinionated, integrated command-line tool and supporting services that simplify the creation, development, testing, building, and distribution of Flutter applications, comparable in scope to Expo for React Native.  **Background** Flutter developers must currently assemble their own toolchain for project scaffolding, device provisioning, over-the-air updates, build signing, and store submission. This fragmentation raises the barrier to entry and slows iteration. A unified tool should reduce this overhead while remaining compatible with standard Flutter projects and the Dart SDK.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **Project scaffolding:** The tool shall create a new Flutter project from versioned templates (e.g., blank, navigation starter, authentication starter) with a single command. 2. **Development server:** The tool shall run a local development server that serves the app to physical devices and emulators via QR code or URL, with hot reload and hot restart supported. 3. **Device and SDK management:** The tool shall detect and validate installed Flutter SDK, Android SDK, Xcode, and CocoaPods versions, and report actionable remediation steps for missing or incompatible dependencies. 4. **Configuration abstraction:** The tool shall manage app metadata (name, bundle identifier, package name, version, icons, splash screens, permissions) from a single declarative configuration file, generating platform-specific files as needed. 5. **Cloud build service:** The tool shall build Android (AAB/APK) and iOS (IPA) artifacts on remote build infrastructure without requiring local Xcode or Android Studio installation. 6. **Credential management:** The tool shall securely create, store, and reuse signing certificates, provisioning profiles, and keystores, with options for local-only storage and encrypted remote storage. 7. **Over-the-air updates:** The tool shall publish JavaScript-equivalent Dart asset updates or hot-patch bundles to installed apps without a store resubmission, subject to Apple and Google policy constraints, and shall support rollback to a prior release. 8. **Release channels:** The tool shall support named channels (e.g., development, staging, production) mapping builds and updates to distinct audiences. 9. **Store submission:** The tool shall upload build artifacts to Google Play Console and App Store Connect via CLI, including metadata and screenshot upload where supported by the store APIs. 10. **Plugin compatibility check:** The tool shall verify that declared pub.dev dependencies are compatible with the target Flutter SDK version and platform before building. 11. **Dependency upgrade assistant:** The tool shall provide a command to upgrade the Flutter SDK and dependencies, listing breaking changes and offering automated migration where feasible. 12. **Standard project compatibility:** The tool shall operate on existing Flutter projects without requiring structural rewrites, and shall allow ejecting to a plain Flutter project with no proprietary runtime dependency.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  - **Compatibility:** Support the current stable Flutter release and the two prior stable releases on macOS, Windows, and Linux hosts. - **Performance:** Initial project creation completes in under 60 seconds on a broadband connection; hot reload latency is unchanged from the native Flutter tooling. - **Security:** Credentials are never stored in plaintext in the project repository; all remote transfers use TLS 1.2 or higher. - **Transparency:** All generated native code and configuration is readable, version-controlled, and documented. - **Open source:** The core CLI and configuration schema are released under an OSI-approved license. Hosted services may be optional and separately licensed. - **Extensibility:** A documented plugin API allows third parties to add commands and build hooks.  **Acceptance Criteria**  - A developer with only the Flutter SDK installed can run one command to create, run on a physical device, and produce a signed Android build of a new project within 15 minutes. - A developer can produce a signed iOS build without a local Mac by using the cloud build service. - An update published to the production channel reaches a test device within 5 minutes and can be rolled back with one command. - Running the tool against an existing standard Flutter project succeeds without modifying source files unless the user explicitly opts in. - Documentation covers installation, each command, the configuration schema, and the ejection procedure.  **Out of Scope (Initial Release)**  - Web and desktop target builds through the cloud service - Proprietary runtime that replaces the Flutter engine - Visual drag-and-drop UI builder  **Priority:** High **Labels:** enhancement, tooling, developer-experience, cli

issue_title: Create a Swarm/Mob/Flock/etc system for managing large amounts of entities
requirement: ## Requirement: Scalable Swarm/Mob/Flock Entity Management System  ### Objective  The project shall provide a reusable subsystem for organizing and controlling large populations of entities. The subsystem shall support swarms, mobs, flocks, and other group-oriented formations through configurable group types and behaviors.  ### Functional Requirements  1. **Group Management**    - Entities shall be assignable to named groups at runtime.    - Groups shall support adding, removing, transferring, and bulk-updating members.    - Group membership shall not require duplicating or replacing entity state.    - Destroying a group shall release its resources without affecting entities that are not owned by the group.  2. **Group Types and Behaviors**    - The system shall support multiple concurrent group types, including swarm, mob, and flock configurations.    - Behaviors shall be pluggable and configurable, including parameters such as formation, cohesion, separation, alignment, leader-following, movement speed, and target selection.    - Shared calculations shall be computed once per group where possible and reused by member entities.    - Groups shall optionally support a leader and role-based membership.  3. **Lifecycle Integration**    - The system shall use the project’s existing entity creation, destruction, registration, and world-update lifecycle.    - Entities shall be automatically removed from all relevant groups when destroyed.    - The system shall provide an efficient bulk-spawn or bulk-assignment path for large populations.  4. **Queries and Inspection**    - Developers shall be able to query a group’s members, group count, membership count, leader, state, and associated metadata.    - Spatial or radius-based queries shall be available for entities managed by a group.    - Debug tooling shall display active groups, membership, behavior state, and population counts.  5. **Configuration and Extensibility**    - Group definitions, behavior parameters, capacity limits, and update settings shall be configurable through the project’s established configuration mechanism.    - Public APIs shall allow creation and management of groups without requiring direct access to internal state.    - The system shall remain compatible with existing entity-management workflows.  6. **Observability**    - The system shall expose metrics for managed entity count, group count, membership changes, update duration, and memory usage.    - Errors such as invalid behavior configuration, capacity violations, or operations on nonexistent groups shall be reported through the project’s standard error mechanism.  ### Performance and Reliability Requirements  - Group updates shall not perform all-pairs comparisons between unrelated entities; neighbor-dependent behaviors shall use spatial partitioning or an equivalent acceleration structure. - Bulk membership operations shall scale with the number of affected entities rather than the total managed population. - Steady-state group updates shall avoid unnecessary per-entity and per-frame memory allocations. - The management layer shall use O(n) memory overhead for n managed entities. - Removing an entity from the system shall leave no dangling group membership or behavior references. - Population limits and performance targets shall be documented and verified through automated benchmarks.  ### Acceptance Criteria  - A developer can create multiple group types, populate them efficiently, assign behaviors, update them through the main entity tick, inspect their state, and remove them through public APIs. - Dynamic membership changes take effect without recreating unaffected entities or groups. - A benchmark demonstrates that the supported large-entity population can be updated without quadratic performance degradation. - Automated tests cover group creation, membership lifecycle, bulk operations, behavior execution, invalid configuration, entity destruction cleanup, and integration with the existing entity system.

issue_title: [Poll] Support DistributedDataParallel (DDP) in PyTorch C++ API (libtorch)
requirement: **Requirement: Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) Support in the PyTorch C++ API (libtorch)**  **Summary:** The PyTorch C++ API (libtorch) shall provide a native implementation of DistributedDataParallel (DDP) equivalent in functionality to the Python `torch.nn.parallel.DistributedDataParallel`, enabling multi-process, multi-device data-parallel training of `torch::nn::Module`-based models without requiring Python.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **Module wrapping:** Provide a C++ class (e.g., `torch::nn::parallel::DistributedDataParallel`) that wraps a `torch::nn::Module` and manages its replication and gradient synchronization across processes. 2. **Process group integration:** Integrate with `c10d` process groups (at minimum NCCL and Gloo backends) for initialization, using the same rendezvous mechanisms (e.g., environment variables `MASTER_ADDR`, `MASTER_PORT`, `RANK`, `WORLD_SIZE`, or a `FileStore`/`TCPStore`). 3. **Gradient synchronization:** Automatically all-reduce parameter gradients during the backward pass, with bucketing of gradients to overlap communication with computation, matching the performance characteristics of the Python implementation. 4. **Parameter broadcast:** Broadcast initial parameters and buffers from rank 0 to all other ranks upon construction to ensure identical starting state. 5. **Buffer synchronization:** Support optional synchronization of module buffers (e.g., BatchNorm running statistics) across ranks. 6. **Unused parameter handling:** Support a `find_unused_parameters` option that detects parameters not participating in the forward pass and excludes them from reduction without deadlocking. 7. **Gradient accumulation:** Support `no_sync()`-style context to skip gradient synchronization during accumulation steps. 8. **Device placement:** Support single-device-per-process placement (one CUDA device per rank), with explicit device specification via `torch::Device`. 9. **State handling:** Provide access to the underlying wrapped module (e.g., `module()`), and support saving and loading state dicts consistent with the non-distributed module's state dict format. 10. **Error handling:** Surface communication and configuration errors as `c10::Error` exceptions with descriptive messages (e.g., mismatched parameter shapes across ranks, uninitialized process group).  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  1. **Performance:** Throughput and scaling efficiency on multi-GPU NCCL setups shall be within a defined tolerance (e.g., ≥90% of Python DDP on the same hardware and model). 2. **Compatibility:** The API shall work with existing `torch::nn` modules and optimizers (`torch::optim`) without modification to user model code. 3. **Consistency:** Numerical results after N training steps shall match a single-process run with equivalent effective batch size within floating-point tolerance. 4. **Documentation:** Public API shall be documented in the libtorch reference, with a minimal end-to-end example (multi-process launch, training loop, checkpointing). 5. **Testing:** Unit and integration tests shall cover NCCL and Gloo backends, CPU and CUDA devices, unused-parameter handling, gradient accumulation, and state dict round-trips, runnable in CI. 6. **Build:** Feature shall be available in standard libtorch distributions on Linux and be gated behind build flags where backend dependencies (e.g., NCCL) are absent, without breaking builds.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - A libtorch example trains a model across ≥2 GPUs on one node and across ≥2 nodes, producing loss curves matching the Python DDP reference within tolerance. - Gradient synchronization is verified to occur exactly once per iteration (or be skipped under `no_sync()`). - All functional requirements above have passing automated tests.

For each module M in the output of `go list -m all`, `go mod why -m M` must print one of the following:    - **A shortest import chain:** a sequence of package imports starting at the main module and ending at a package provided by M, in the same format used for modules that are currently explained.    - **An explicit no-dependency statement:** a message that the main module does not need M, including the parenthetical form already used for unneeded modules (for example, `(main module does not need module M)`), when no package in the module graph imported by the main module's packages (including tests as covered by the `all` pattern) is provided by M. 2. The command must not exit silently, print an empty result, or omit M from its output for any module in `go list -m all`. 3. The explanation must be consistent with the package set that `go list -m all` and `go mod graph` use, so a module that appears in `go list -m all` is never reported as unneeded by `go mod why -m` unless it is also absent from the packages those commands consider. 4. When multiple modules are passed, or `-m` is used with `-vendor`, the same guarantee applies to each module individually. 5. The exit status must be 0 for all modules in `go list -m all`, whether the result is a dependency chain or a "does not need" message.  **Acceptance criteria**  - For a module graph containing modules required only transitively, only by test dependencies, or only through pruned module graph entries, `go mod why -m` for each listed module returns a non-empty, correct explanation. - A test script in `cmd/go/testdata/script` verifies that for a representative set of modules, every entry in `go list -m all` has a corresponding `go mod why -m` answer, and that the output matches the expected chain or "does not need" message. - Existing `go mod why` output for modules that already receive an answer is unchanged. - Documentation for `go mod why` in `cmd/go/internal/modcmd/why.go` (or the equivalent help text) is updated to state this guarantee.

issue_title: Support multiple windows for desktop shells
requirement: **REQ-SHELL-001: Multiple Window Support for Desktop Shells**  The desktop shell shall support the concurrent creation, display, and independent management of multiple windows, including multiple windows belonging to the same application.  Specifically, the shell shall:  1. Allow any number of windows to be open at the same time, limited only by available system resources. 2. Maintain independent content, geometry (position, size), and state for each window, so that changes to one window do not affect any other. 3. Provide standard per-window management operations — open, close, move, resize, minimize, maximize, restore, and raise/lower (z-order) — which affect only the targeted window. 4. Route keyboard and pointer input exclusively to the currently focused window, and allow the user to change focus via direct interaction (e.g., clicking a window) and via a window-switching mechanism (e.g., Alt-Tab). 5. Correctly render overlapping windows according to focus and stacking order. 6. Reflect all open windows in the shell's window-management interface (e.g., window list, taskbar, or overview), enabling the user to identify, select, and activate any open window. 7. Ensure that the creation, closing, or failure of one window does not interrupt, terminate, or degrade any other open window.  **Constraints and verification:** - Single-window behavior and performance shall not regress as a result of this feature. - On the reference hardware platform, the shell shall remain responsive with at least 10 windows open concurrently, with input latency and rendering performance within existing targets. - Verification shall be by demonstration and automated tests covering: opening multiple windows, overlapping and stacking, independent focus and input routing, per-window management operations, and correct representation of all windows in the window-management interface.

issue_title: Subslice search
requirement:
# Requirement: Subslice Search  **Document status:** Draft for review **Feature ID:** FEAT-SUBSLICE-SEARCH **Priority:** Medium **Affected component:** Sequence/string search utilities (core search library)  ---  ## 1. Introduction / Summary  The search library currently supports finding a pattern in a complete sequence (`haystack`) or string (`text`). There is no way to restrict a search to a *region* of the input without first copying that region out of the source container (e.g., `&text[start..end].to_string()`, or building a temporary `Vec` of the sub-range).  **Subslice Search** adds the ability to search for a pattern inside a bounded sub-range ("subslice") of a haystack, returning match positions expressed as offsets into the **original, full** haystack. The sub-range is searched in place, with no copying of the underlying data.  ---  ## 2. Motivation / Problem Statement  Callers frequently need to search only a portion of a larger buffer:  - Searching a single record or line inside a memory-mapped file buffer. - Searching a delimited region (e.g., between header and body markers) of a protocol frame. - Searching a bounded window of a log buffer or ring buffer. - Searching a sub-range of a large slice without incurring an O(n) copy/allocation.  Today these use cases require either an explicit copy of the region (time and memory cost proportional to the region size) or ad-hoc, inconsistently-implemented manual loop code with off-by-one error risks.  ---  ## 3. Terminology  | Term | Definition | |---|---| | **Haystack** | The full sequence/string being searched. | | **Needle** | The pattern being searched for. | | **Range** | The half-open interval `[start, end)` of the haystack that is searched. | | **Match position** | The index of the first element/byte of a match, expressed as an offset from the beginning of the **full haystack** (absolute index), not relative to `start`. | | **Subslice** | The view of the haystack covered by the range. |  ---  ## 4. Scope  ### 4.1 In scope  - Searching a pattern within an arbitrary half-open sub-range of a sequence or string. - Returning absolute match offsets. - Single-match and all-matches (iterator and collected) variants. - Overlapping-match option. - Range validation and defined behavior for invalid/edge-case inputs. - Public API documentation, examples, unit tests, and property/fuzz tests.  ### 4.2 Out of scope  - Reverse-search, regex, or fuzzy matching (existing capabilities remain unchanged). - Changing the semantics or performance characteristics of existing full-haystack search functions. - Multi-pattern / simultaneous multi-needle search across different ranges. - Searching across non-contiguous, disjoint regions in a single call.  ---  ## 5. Functional Requirements  ### FR-1 — Public API surface  The library shall expose subslice search through new, clearly named public functions/methods, one per supported data shape:  - **Generic sequence (e.g., `&[T]` where `T: PartialEq`):**   - `find_in(haystack, needle, start, end) -> Option<usize>` — returns the position of the leftmost match fully contained in `[start, end)`.   - `find_all_in(haystack, needle, start, end) -> impl Iterator<Item = usize>` — yields the positions of successive matches. - **Text (`&str`):**   - `find_in_str(text, needle, start, end) -> Option<usize>` — byte offset of the leftmost match.   - `find_all_in_str(text, needle, start, end) -> impl Iterator<Item = usize>` — byte offsets of successive matches.  Existing full-haystack APIs (`find`, `find_all`, etc.) shall remain source-compatible and behaviorally unchanged.  ### FR-2 — Absolute indexing  All returned positions shall be offsets into the **full haystack**. For a match that begins at relative position `r` within the range, the returned value shall be `start + r`. Callers shall never need to add `start` themselves.  ### FR-3 — Containment rule  A match shall only be reported if it lies **entirely** within `[start, end)`. A needle that begins inside the range but extends past `end` shall not be reported.  ### FR-4 — Match ordering and semantics  - `find_in` shall return the **leftmost** (lowest-index) match. - `find_all_in` shall yield matches in ascending order of position. - `find_all_in` shall return **non-overlapping** matches by default (after a match of length `m`, the next search resumes at `match_pos + m`). - An `overlapping` variant (e.g., `find_all_overlapping_in`) shall yield every match position, including those that overlap a previous match (after a match, the next search resumes at `match_pos + 1`).  ### FR-5 — Range validation  - If `start > end`, or `end > haystack.len()`, the API shall treat this as a **caller programming error** and shall fail fast with a clear, documented panic message (Rust) or a documented error return (other languages). The chosen behavior shall be consistent across all subslice entry points and documented in rustdoc/API docs. - The API shall never read out of bounds, never panic with an index-out-of-bounds message, and never produce undefined behavior.  ### FR-6 — Edge-case behavior (normative table)  Let `n = haystack.len()`, `m = needle.len()`, and the range be valid (`start <= end <= n`).  | # | Condition | Required result | |---|---|---| | E1 | `m == 0` (empty needle) | `find_in` → `Some(start)`. `find_all_in` → yields `start` once, then terminates. (Consistent with existing empty-needle semantics of the full-haystack API.) | | E2 | `start == end` (empty range), `m > 0` | `None` / empty iterator. | | E3 | `m > end - start` (needle longer than range) | `None` / empty iterator. | | E4 | `m > n` | `None` / empty iterator. | | E5 | Range covers the whole haystack (`start == 0 && end == n`) | Identical results to the existing full-haystack search API. | | E6 | Match begins exactly at `start` | Reported at position `start`. | | E7 | Match ends exactly at `end` | Reported (matches are inclusive of the last element in the range). | | E8 | Match would extend past `end` | Not reported (see FR-3). | | E9 | Multiple identical matches within range | Leftmost returned by `find_in`; all returned in ascending order by `find_all_in`. | | E10 | `&str` haystack with non-ASCII (UTF-8 multi-byte) content | Offsets returned are **byte** offsets into the full string, consistent with existing `str::find` semantics. `start`/`end` shall be valid UTF-8 character boundaries; passing a non-boundary index is a caller error per FR-5. |  ### FR-7 — Zero-copy guarantee  The implementation shall operate directly on the borrowed haystack and shall not copy the searched region (or the haystack) into a temporary buffer. No allocation shall occur as part of the search itself, other than allocations required to materialize results by the caller.  ### FR-8 — Composability / reuse  The subslice variants shall be implemented as a thin layer over the existing core search routine so that algorithm improvements, optimizations, and bug fixes benefit both full-haystack and subslice paths. The core routine shall accept an explicit search window.  ### FR-9 — Consistency with existing API  Naming, argument order, documentation style, error/panic conventions, and iterator-vs-collected return styles shall match the conventions already established by the library for its existing search functions.  ---  ## 6. Non-Functional Requirements  ### NFR-1 — Performance  - Searching a range of length `L` with a needle of length `m` shall complete in `O(L × m)` worst-case time or better, and shall not be more than a constant factor slower than an equivalent full-haystack search restricted to the same window. - `find_all_in` shall be **lazy** (iterator-based) and shall not allocate proportional to the number of matches unless the caller collects. - Overlapping-match enumeration shall not degrade to `O(n²)` in the number of matches.  ### NFR-2 — Memory  Zero heap allocation during a single search (see FR-7). Stack usage shall be `O(1)` with respect to haystack length.  ### NFR-3 — Safety  The implementation shall be free of `unsafe` code, or, if `unsafe` is required for performance, it shall be isolated, documented, and covered by `Miri` in CI.  ### NFR-4 — Thread safety  All new APIs shall be `Send`/`Sync`-safe (no interior mutability, no global mutable state) and shall be usable concurrently on disjoint or shared immutable haystacks.  ### NFR-5 — Backward compatibility  No existing public API shall change signature, semantics, or performance characteristics. The change shall be purely additive (semver-minor).  ### NFR-6 — Observability / diagnostics  Panic messages (or error values) for invalid ranges shall name the offending function and include the offending `start`, `end`, and haystack length.  ---  ## 7. Usage Examples (normative intent)  ``` // Search "needle" in the first 100 bytes of a buffer; result is an absolute offset. let buf: &[u8] = b"....needle....needle.."; if let Some(pos) = find_in(buf, b"needle", 0, 100) {     assert_eq!(pos, 4);              // absolute, not relative to start }  // Restrict to a region of a string; returns byte offsets into `text`. let text = "alpha
beta
gamma"; let body_start = text.find('
').unwrap() + 1; let hits: Vec<usize> = find_all_in_str(text, "a", body_start, text.len()).collect(); // hits are byte offsets into `text`  // Empty range yields no non-empty matches. assert_eq!(find_in(b"abc", b"b", 2, 2), None);  // A match extending past `end` is not reported. assert_eq!(find_in(b"abcdef", b"def", 0, 3), None); ```  ---  ## 8. Acceptance Criteria  The feature is considered complete when all of the following are true:  1. **AC-1:** `find_in`, `find_all_in`, `find_in_str`, and `find_all_in_str` are public, documented, and exported from the crate's public module. 2. **AC-2:** Every row of the FR-6 edge-case table has an automated test that asserts the specified result. 3. **AC-3:** A property-based/fuzz test asserts, for random haystacks, needles, and ranges, that the subslice results are **exactly equal** to the results of a brute-force reference implementation that scans the range element-by-element. 4. **AC-4:** A test asserts that subslice search over the full haystack (`start = 0`, `end = len`) produces results identical to the pre-existing `find`/`find_all` APIs. 5. **AC-5:** A test asserts that all returned offsets are within `start..=end` and that each reported match's content equals the needle. 6. **AC-6:** Invalid ranges (`start > end`, `end > len`) fail fast with the documented diagnostic; a test covers each case for each entry point. 7. **AC-7:** `cargo miri test` (or equivalent) passes for the new code paths, including the `&str`/UTF-8 boundary cases. 8. **AC-8:** A benchmark demonstrates that subslice search over a range is not slower than a full-haystack search over the same data by more than 10%, and that no allocation occurs during a search (allocation counter test). 9. **AC-9:** `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass; all new public items have rustdoc comments including a `# Panics` section where applicable. 10. **AC-10:** The crate's `CHANGELOG`/release notes document the addition as a minor-version feature.  ---  ## 9. Risks and Mitigations  | Risk | Impact | Mitigation | |---|---|---| | Off-by-one errors in range/containment logic | Incorrect results, silent data corruption in callers | FR-3 containment rule, FR-6 normative table, brute-force property tests (AC-3) | | Confusion between relative and absolute offsets | Caller bugs | FR-2 absolute indexing; documented explicitly; example asserts absolute value | | Regression in existing search performance | Downstream slowdown | FR-8 reuse of core routine; AC-8 benchmark gate | | Invalid range handling differs between APIs | Inconsistent, hard-to-debug behavior | FR-5 single documented policy enforced across all entry points; AC-6 |  ---  ## 10. Open Questions  1. Should invalid ranges **panic** (Rust idiom, caller error) or return `Result`? *Proposed default:* panic, matching existing library conventions; revisit if the library already prefers `Result` for input validation. 2. Should an `overlapping` variant ship in the initial release, or be deferred? *Proposed default:* ship both, with non-overlapping as the default. 3. Should the generic-sequence API support a custom equality/comparison predicate (e.g., case-insensitive) in v1? *Proposed default:* no; defer to a follow-up requirement.

issue_title: Feature Request: Easier to extend base RNN implementation
requirement: # Software Requirement Specification  **Requirement ID:** REQ-RNN-EXT-001 **Title:** Improved Extensibility of the Base RNN Implementation **Type:** Functional (with Maintainability/Usability impact) **Priority:** High **Source:** User feature request — "Easier to extend base RNN implementation"  ---  ## 1. Problem Statement The current base RNN implementation couples core recurrence logic with layer-level concerns (sequence iteration, state management, masking), forcing developers who wish to implement custom RNN variants to duplicate large portions of code or rely on private/internal APIs.  ## 2. Requirement Description The base RNN implementation shall be refactored to expose clearly defined, documented, and supported extension points, enabling developers to create custom RNN layers and cells by overriding only the behavior that differs from the default, while inheriting all standard functionality from the base class.  ## 3. Functional Requirements - **FR-1:** The base RNN class shall expose public, documented, overridable methods for the recurrent computation step, state initialization, state transition, and output generation. - **FR-2:** A user-defined RNN cell shall be able to customize cell behavior (e.g., activations, weight usage, bias handling) without reimplementing sequence iteration or state management logic. - **FR-3:** Activation functions, kernel/recurrent weight initializers, and bias configurations shall be configurable via constructor parameters or overridable hooks on the base class. - **FR-4:** Custom RNN cells derived from the base implementation shall automatically inherit support for masking, variable-length sequences, multi-step unrolling, and serialization/checkpointing. - **FR-5:** All existing public APIs and previously written RNN subclasses shall remain backward compatible; no breaking changes are permitted. - **FR-6:** Project documentation shall include an extension guide with at least one complete worked example of implementing a custom RNN cell using the new extension points.  ## 4. Acceptance Criteria - **AC-1:** A functional custom RNN cell (behaviorally equivalent to a standard variant, e.g., GRU) can be implemented by overriding only the cell-step logic, with zero modifications to core RNN source files. - **AC-2:** All existing unit and integration tests for current RNN implementations pass without modification. - **AC-3:** New tests demonstrate that custom cells inherit masking, state management, and serialization behavior from the base class. - **AC-4:** The extension guide and its example code execute successfully against the released API.  ## 5. Constraints / Non-Functional Requirements - **NFR-1:** The refactoring shall introduce no more than 5% performance degradation in existing RNN training and inference benchmarks. - **NFR-2:** The implementation shall conform to the project's established coding style and public API design guidelines.

issue_title: Table > TableRow > TableCell colspan
requirement:
# Requirement: Support `colspan` on TableCell ## 1. Summary Add support for a `colspan` (column span) property to the `TableCell` component, which is rendered inside a `TableRow` inside a `Table`. A cell with `colspan = n` must occupy `n` grid columns of its row, allowing authors to build tables with merged/irregular columns without resorting to raw HTML or workarounds. ## 2. Motivation Today, a `TableRow` renders a fixed set of `TableCell` children, each occupying exactly one column. Real-world data frequently requires a cell to span multiple columns — e.g., a header cell covering two or three data columns, a summary/total row where a label cell spans several columns, or a grouped-category header. Without `colspan` support, authors must either split data into redundant columns or bypass the component library entirely. ## 3. API ```tsx Plain cell Spans two columns Plain cell
``` ### 3.1 `TableCell` props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `colspan` | `number` | `1` | Number of columns the cell should span. Must be a positive integer (`>= 1`). | | `colSpan` (alias) | `number` | — | Optional camelCase alias accepted for React convention parity. If both are provided, `colspan` wins; a `console` warning is emitted in development when they conflict with different values. | The same prop is available on all cell variants exposed by the library (`TableCell`, `TableHeaderCell`/`TableHead`, etc.), so both `` and `` semantics are supported. ### 3.2 `TableRow` behavior - A row's **effective column count** is computed as the sum of the `colspan` values of its cells (cells with no explicit `colspan` count as `1`). - `TableRow` must not clamp, pad, or truncate cells based on a fixed column count. If the sum of spans in a row is greater than the table's column count, the extra span is still rendered (browser/grid behavior resolves it) rather than being silently dropped. - `Table` derives its total column count from the maximum effective column count across all rows, so a row containing a `colspan={3}` cell establishes a 3-column table even if other rows have more cells. ## 4. Behavior Specification 1. **Rendering.** The `colspan` value is forwarded to the underlying DOM element as the native `colspan` attribute on ``/``. When `colspan` is `1` or unset, no `colspan` attribute is written (preserving current markup output byte-for-byte for existing consumers). 2. **Validation.** Values that are not a positive integer (`0`, negative, fractional, `NaN`, `Infinity`, non-numeric strings) are rejected: in development the component logs a warning and falls back to `colspan = 1`; in production it falls back to `1` silently. 3. **Composition.** `colspan` is independent of existing cell features — content alignment, variant/styling, sorting, and sticky/header behavior must all continue to work for spanning cells. 4. **Server-side rendering / hydration.** The rendered markup must be identical on server and client, and the `colspan` attribute must survive hydration without mismatch warnings. 5. **Type safety.** The prop must be exposed in the public TypeScript declarations so `colspan` is autocompleted and type-checked; `colspan={2}` must not raise a type error, and `colspan={"2"}` must. ## 5. Acceptance Criteria - **AC-1** Given a `TableRow` with cells `colspan` values `1, 2, 1`, when rendered, the second cell's DOM element has attribute `colspan="2"`. - **AC-2** Given a `TableCell` with no `colspan` prop, when rendered, the DOM element has **no** `colspan` attribute and the rendered output is unchanged from the pre-feature behavior. - **AC-3** Given `colspan={0}`, `colspan={-1}`, or `colspan={1.5}`, when rendered in development, a warning is logged and the cell renders with `colspan = 1` semantics. - **AC-4** Given a `TableRow` whose cells sum to 3 columns via spans, and a `Table` whose other rows have 2 cells, when rendered, the table exposes a 3-column grid and the spanning cell visually covers columns 2–3. - **AC-5** Given `colspan` and `colSpan` both set to different values, when rendered in development, a warning is logged and `colspan` takes precedence. - **AC-6** Existing snapshot/unit tests for `Table`, `TableRow`, and `TableCell` continue to pass without modification. - **AC-7** Public type declarations include `colspan?: number` (and `colSpan?: number`) on the cell component(s). ## 6. Non-Goals - `rowspan` support (row spanning) is out of scope for this requirement; the DOM attribute is not exposed or managed by the library. - Automatic layout algorithm changes (e.g., CSS Grid-based table layout) are out of scope; the implementation continues to rely on native table layout semantics. - Row/column headers association (`headers` attribute) and scope management are out of scope.

issue_title: x/net/http2: support consuming PUSH_PROMISE streams in the client
requirement: **Requirement: Client-side support for consuming HTTP/2 PUSH_PROMISE streams in golang.org/x/net/http2**  The x/net/http2 client transport shall support receiving, validating, and exposing server-initiated PUSH_PROMISE streams to applications in accordance with RFC 7540 §8.2.  1. **Opt-in configuration:** The client shall provide a documented mechanism (e.g., a Transport option and/or callback) enabling applications to explicitly accept server push. By default, server push shall be disabled; in this state, every received PUSH_PROMISE shall be answered with RST_STREAM(REFUSED_STREAM) without disrupting concurrent in-flight requests.  2. **Protocol validation:** When server push is enabled, the client shall validate PUSH_PROMISE frames, including: promised stream IDs that are idle and monotonically increasing, complete header blocks spanning CONTINUATION frames, and presence/validity of the pseudo-header fields `:method`, `:scheme`, `:authority`, and `:path`. Violations shall produce a stream or connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR as specified by RFC 7540.  3. **Application-facing API:** The client shall expose each pushed response to the application, providing access to the promised request metadata, the association with the originating client-initiated request, and a means to read the pushed response body.  4. **Lifecycle management:** The client shall send RST_STREAM(CANCEL) for any pushed stream the application does not consume, and shall propagate cancellation of the parent request (e.g., context cancellation) to all pushed streams associated with it.  5. **Flow control:** Pushed streams shall participate in connection- and stream-level flow control identically to client-initiated streams.  **Acceptance criteria:** - An opted-in client successfully receives and reads a pushed response from a compliant HTTP/2 server. - A non-opted-in client refuses all PUSH_PROMISE frames and completes its own requests unaffected. - Malformed, out-of-order, or incomplete PUSH_PROMISE frames trigger correct PROTOCOL_ERROR handling. - Cancelling the initiating request cancels and releases all associated pushed streams.

issue_title: Feature Requst: Add regex support to test filters
requirement: **Requirement: Regular Expression Support for Test Filters**  The system shall allow users to specify test filters using regular expressions, in addition to the existing exact-match filter syntax.  1. **Functional Requirements**    1.1. Users shall be able to include tests matching a user-supplied regular expression when running tests (inclusion filter).    1.2. Users shall be able to exclude tests matching a user-supplied regular expression when running tests (exclusion filter).    1.3. The regular expression syntax shall conform to the standard regex library used by the implementation language (e.g., ECMA-262 regex, PCRE, or Python `re`), and this syntax shall be documented.    1.4. Regular expressions shall be applied to the fully qualified test names (including namespace, class, and method name) as well as to display names where applicable.    1.5. Multiple regular expression filters may be supplied in a single invocation; a test shall be included if it matches at least one inclusion filter, and excluded if it matches at least one exclusion filter. Exclusion filters shall take precedence over inclusion filters.    1.6. The feature shall be available through all supported interfaces: command-line options, configuration files, and API calls where filters are currently supported.  2. **Behavioral Requirements**    2.1. A filter argument that is not a valid regular expression shall cause the test run to terminate with a clear, descriptive error message indicating the invalid filter and the position of the syntax error, and shall exit with a non-zero status code.    2.2. If no tests match the provided regular expression filters, the system shall report zero matched tests and, unless configured otherwise, exit with a non-zero status code indicating no tests were run.    2.3. Regex matching shall be performed as a partial match (search) by default; users may anchor patterns with `^` and `$` for full-match behavior.    2.4. Filter behavior shall be deterministic and case-sensitive by default, with case-insensitive matching available via standard regex flags (e.g., `(?i)`).  3. **Documentation Requirements**    3.1. The user documentation shall describe regex filter syntax, usage examples, and limitations, including any differences from the existing exact-match filter behavior.    3.2. The documentation shall clearly distinguish between exact-match and regex filter modes and explain how users select each mode.  4. **Non-Functional Requirements**    4.1. Regex filtering shall not degrade overall test startup time beyond a negligible overhead (target: < 5% compared to exact-match filtering) for typical test suites.    4.2. The feature shall be covered by automated tests covering inclusion, exclusion, precedence, invalid patterns, and no-match scenarios.

issue_title: Transformer Lack of Embedding Layer and Positional Encodings
