issue_title: Allow explicitly defining interfaces in GDScript
requirement: # Requirement: Explicit Interface Declarations in GDScript  **Component:** GDScript language / Godot Script parser, analyzer, compiler, and editor tooling **Type:** Language feature (syntax + static analysis + runtime type information)  ---  ## 1. Problem Statement  GDScript currently offers no first-class way to express a *contract* that a set of unrelated classes must fulfil. Type conformance is determined solely by inheritance from a common base class, or left entirely to duck typing (the analyzer accepts any object for an untyped or structurally-compatible assignment, and `is` only tests inheritance chains).  This forces developers into one of two undesirable patterns:  1. **Artificial base classes** — e.g. `class_name Damageable extends Reference` used purely as a marker, adding runtime overhead, an unwanted base type, and a misleading "is-a" inheritance relationship in the class hierarchy. 2. **Convention-only contracts** — interfaces exist only as documentation comments, so a missing or mis-signatured method is discovered at runtime as a crash deep in unrelated call code, or never.  There is no compile-time verification that a class provides the members it promises to provide, no editor autocomplete for such contracts, and no way to type a variable as "any object that satisfies this set of members" in a nominal sense.  ## 2. Goals  - G1. Allow a developer to **explicitly declare an interface** (a named set of required members) directly in GDScript source. - G2. Allow a class to **declare that it implements** one or more interfaces. - G3. **Verify conformance at compile/parse time** with precise, actionable diagnostics. - G4. Allow **interface-typed variables, parameters, and return values**, with the analyzer treating interface types as nominal types for assignment checks and enabling narrowing. - G5. Allow runtime **`is` / `as` tests against interfaces**. - G6. Provide **editor support**: autocomplete, member lookup through the interface, documentation, and visible "Implements" metadata. - G7. Remain fully **backwards compatible** with existing GDScript code and with the existing inheritance model.  ## 3. Non-Goals  - N1. Implementing **abstract classes** (classes with unimplemented methods) — this is a separate, complementary feature and must not be introduced by this requirement. - N2. **Multiple inheritance of implementations.** A class still has exactly one base class; `implements` adds contracts only. - N3. **Generic interfaces** (type parameters on interfaces). - N4. Changing the semantics of duck typing for classes that do *not* declare an interface. - N5. Runtime dispatch tables, vtables, or `call()`-style late binding — interface method calls resolve through the normal dynamic method lookup. - N6. Interfaces that carry state or executable method bodies.  ---  ## 4. Terminology  | Term | Definition | |---|---| | **Interface** | A named declaration of required members (properties, methods, signals, constants) with no storage and no implementation. | | **Implementing class** | A class that declares `implements Interface` and provides concrete definitions for every required member. | | **Interface inheritance** | An interface may declare that it extends one or more other interfaces, thereby inheriting their required members. | | **Conformance** | The property that a class provides all members required by the interfaces it declares, with compatible signatures. | | **Contract member** | A member declared inside an interface body. |  ---  ## 5. Language Syntax  ### 5.1 Declaring an interface  ``` interface <Name>[: <Parent>[, <Parent>...]]:     <contract members> ```  `interface` becomes a **reserved keyword** in GDScript.  Permitted contract members:  | Member kind | Syntax | Notes | |---|---|---| | Property | `var <name>: <Type>` | Optional initializer is **not** permitted (an interface declares no storage). A default value of `null` typed as the interface's type is implicitly assumed. | | Method | `func <name>(<params>) -> <ReturnType>:` with **empty body** | Parameters must be typed. Default parameter values are not part of the contract (see FR-3.4). | | Signal | `signal <name>[(<params>)]` | Parameters must be typed. | | Constant | `const <name> := <value>` | The implementing class must define a constant of the same name with an equal value. |  A whole-interface body may be empty (`interface Marker:` with no members) to express a pure marker type.  Example:  ```gdscript # res://interfaces/damageable.gd class_name Damageable extends RefCounted          # optional: gives the interface script a resource identity  interface Damageable:     var health: int     var max_health: int     func take_damage(amount: int) -> void     func is_alive() -> bool     signal died ```  An interface may also be declared as an **inner** declaration inside a class body:  ```gdscript class Inventory:     interface Slot:         var item_id: String         func clear() -> void ```  ### 5.2 Implementing interfaces  ``` class_name Enemy extends Character implements Damageable, Saveable:     ... ```  Rules: - The `implements` clause appears after the `extends` clause (or after `class_name`/`extends` if no base) and before the member body. - The clause takes a comma-separated list of interface references. - An interface reference is resolved in this order: (1) an inner `interface` declaration visible in the current scope, (2) a `class_name` global interface, (3) a preloaded script constant whose script declares a top-level interface with the matching name, e.g. `implements preload("res://interfaces/damageable.gd").Damageable` or, when the script's top-level interface shares the script's `class_name`, `implements DamageableScript` where `const DamageableScript = preload(...)`. - The implementing class must ultimately derive from `Object` (i.e. it must have a valid `extends` chain); implementing an interface is not a substitute for a base class.  ### 5.3 Interface inheritance  ```gdscript interface Entity:     var id: int  interface Damageable extends Entity:     func take_damage(amount: int) -> void ```  - An interface may extend multiple interfaces. - Contract members of all ancestors are inherited transitively. - Cycles in interface inheritance are a compile-time error.  ---  ## 6. Functional Requirements  ### FR-1 — Parser support - **FR-1.1** The GDScript tokenizer shall recognize `interface` and `implements` as keywords. - **FR-1.2** The parser shall accept top-level, inner-class, and function-local? — **no**: interfaces shall be declarable only at script top level and inside class bodies (not inside function bodies). A function-local `interface` declaration shall produce the error `Local interfaces are not supported.` - **FR-1.3** `interface` and `implements` shall be added to the list of reserved words. Existing scripts that use these identifiers shall fail to parse and must emit an explicit error naming the reserved word (e.g. `Identifier "interface" is a reserved keyword.`). This breaking change shall be documented in the release notes and in the GDScript upgrade guide. - **FR-1.4** A file that contains only an interface declaration (and optionally a `class_name`) shall be a valid, loadable script resource.  ### FR-2 — Interface declaration semantics - **FR-2.1** An interface declaration shall create a named type in the global class registry when it carries a `class_name`, or a scoped inner type otherwise. - **FR-2.2** Interface types are usable as static types for variables, constants, parameters, return values, and typed array element types (e.g. `var all: Array[Damageable]`). - **FR-2.3** An interface type shall not be instantiable. `Damageable.new()` shall be a compile-time error: `Cannot instantiate an interface.` - **FR-2.4** Interfaces shall not be usable as an `extends` base for a class. `extends Damageable` where `Damageable` is an interface shall be a compile-time error directing the author to use `implements`. - **FR-2.5** An interface shall not declare a base class with storage-bearing semantics; `extends` on an interface (as a script base) is permitted only to give the interface script a resource identity (e.g. `extends RefCounted`) and shall not impose implementation requirements on implementers.  ### FR-3 — Conformance checking (compile time) - **FR-3.1** When a class declares `implements I`, the analyzer shall verify that the class (including members inherited from its base class chain) provides every contract member of `I` and of all interfaces `I` extends. - **FR-3.2** A missing member shall be a **compile-time error**, reported with the interface name, the member name, and the implementing class name:   `Class "Enemy" does not implement member "take_damage(amount: int) -> void" required by interface "Damageable".` - **FR-3.3** A member with an incompatible signature shall be a compile-time error:   - Method arity mismatch → `Method "take_damage" of interface "Damageable" expects 1 argument, but "Enemy.take_damage" accepts 0.`   - Parameter type mismatch → `Parameter "amount" of "Enemy.take_damage" has type "String", expected "int".`   - Return type mismatch → `Return type of "Enemy.take_damage" is "void", expected "int".`   - Property type mismatch → `Property "health" of "Enemy" has type "float", expected "int" declared by interface "Damageable".`   - Member kind mismatch (property vs. method) → `Member "health" declared in interface "Damageable" is a property, but "Enemy.health" is a method.` - **FR-3.4** Default parameter values in the implementation are permitted and are not part of the contract; a mismatch of defaults shall not be an error. Parameter *names* in the implementation may differ from the interface; the analyzer shall not error on name mismatch. - **FR-3.5** A constant declared in an interface shall be satisfied by an identically named constant in the implementing class with an equal value; a mismatch shall be a compile-time error. - **FR-3.6** A class shall be considered to implement an interface `I` if it declares `implements I`, or if its base class implements `I`, or if it implements an interface that extends `I`. - **FR-3.7** Conformance checking shall be performed at script-analysis time so that errors surface in the editor (with the error attached to the offending member) and abort `load()`/`preload()` of an invalid script at runtime. - **FR-3.8** Errors shall be reported for every distinct violation (not only the first) so that a single editor pass reveals all problems.  ### FR-4 — Interface types in the type system - **FR-4.1** Assigning a value to an interface-typed variable shall require the value's static type to implement that interface. A non-conforming assignment shall be a compile-time error:   `Cannot assign a value of type "Resource" to a variable of type interface "Damageable".` - **FR-4.2** The analyzer shall support **narrowing**: after `if enemy is Damageable:`, accesses within the branch shall resolve members through the `Damageable` interface in addition to the value's static type. - **FR-4.3** Within a function whose parameter or return type is an interface, calls to that interface's members shall resolve and be autocompleted. - **FR-4.4** Interface types shall be usable with `Array[Interface]` and `Dictionary` values (dictionary keys/values typed as an interface). - **FR-4.5** A class implementing an interface shall remain assignable to its own type and to any base type it already was.  ### FR-5 — Runtime `is` / `as` with interfaces - **FR-5.1** `value is <Interface>` shall return `true` at runtime if the value's script (or any script in its inheritance chain) declares implementation of that interface, directly or transitively through interface inheritance. - **FR-5.2** `value as <Interface>` shall return the value if it implements the interface, otherwise `null`, mirroring the existing behaviour of `as` with classes. - **FR-5.3** Runtime checks shall be **O(1)**-ish: the implementation shall cache the set of implemented interface identifiers on the script (e.g. a per-script list of interface type IDs including inherited ones), rather than performing deep reflection traversal per check. The per-instance overhead shall be zero additional bytes. - **FR-5.4** `is` against an unknown (non-existent) identifier shall be a compile-time error, consistent with existing `is` behaviour.  ### FR-6 — Editor and tooling support - **FR-6.1** Autocomplete shall suggest interface names in `implements` clauses, in type positions, and after `is` / `as`. - **FR-6.2** The editor's "Create New Script"/script inheritance dialog shall list interfaces separately from classes so that a user can select an interface as the type to implement. - **FR-6.3** The documentation generator (`DocTools`) shall produce a documentation page for each interface listing its contract members, and the class documentation page shall list the interfaces a class implements. - **FR-6.4** The class reference / "Class DB" style browser shall indicate whether a registered script type is an interface, a class, or an abstract class. - **FR-6.5** Renaming an interface (via `class_name` rename refactoring) shall update all `implements` clauses and type references. - **FR-6.6** The script editor's member list for a class implementing an interface shall indicate inherited-from-interface members distinctly from inherited-from-base-class members. - **FR-6.7** `@tool` scripts shall support interfaces without restriction.  ### FR-7 — Backwards compatibility - **FR-7.1** All existing valid GDScript files shall continue to compile and run unchanged, except for files using `interface` or `implements` as identifiers (FR-1.3). - **FR-7.2** The existing behaviour of structural/duck typing for classes that do not declare `implements` shall be unchanged. - **FR-7.3** `class_name` registration of a script whose top-level declaration is an interface shall register it as an interface type, and shall not conflict with class registration of the same name (duplicate names remain an error).  ---  ## 7. Non-Functional Requirements  - **NF-1 Performance:** Scripts that use no interfaces shall incur no additional runtime cost. Scripts that do use interfaces shall incur only the memory of a small per-script list of interface identifiers. - **NF-2 Diagnostics:** All errors shall name the interface, the implementing class, and the offending member, and shall link (via click) to the offending line. - **NF-3 Consistency:** The feature shall integrate with GDScript's existing static-typing mode (`UNSAFE`/`SAFE`/`STRICT` debug modes) — conformance errors are always reported regardless of mode, since they are definition errors, not usage errors. - **NF-4 Documentation:** The GDScript reference manual shall gain a section describing interfaces, with the syntax, semantics, and examples; the migration guide shall note the new reserved keywords. - **NF-5 Portability:** The implementation shall be architecture-agnostic and shall not require changes to the GDScript bytecode beyond representing interface type information and the `implements` metadata.  ---  ## 8. Acceptance Criteria  | # | Criterion | |---|---| | AC-1 | A script declaring `interface Damageable:` with a property and a method parses, loads, and appears in the global class list as an interface. | | AC-2 | A class declaring `implements Damageable` and providing all members compiles with no errors; calling `take_damage()` through a `Damageable`-typed variable dispatches to the class implementation. | | AC-3 | A class declaring `implements Damageable` but omitting `take_damage()` fails to load with the error from FR-3.2, and the error is shown in the editor at the `implements` line. | | AC-4 | A class declaring `implements Damageable` with `func take_damage(amount: String) -> void` fails to load with the error from FR-3.3. | | AC-5 | `var d: Damageable = enemy` compiles when `Enemy` implements `Damageable`, and fails to compile for a class that does not. | | AC-6 | `if node is Damageable:` returns `true` for a node whose script implements `Damageable` (directly or via a base class or via an interface that `Damageable` extends), and `false` otherwise. | | AC-7 | `node as Damageable` returns the node when conforming and `null` otherwise. | | AC-8 | `interface A extends B:` compiles; a class implementing `A` must also provide `B`'s members, and omitting them is a compile-time error. | | AC-9 | `Damageable.new()` and `class X extends Damageable` both produce compile-time errors with the specified messages. | | AC-10 | A cyclic interface inheritance (`A extends B`, `B extends A`) produces a compile-time error. | | AC-11 | Autocomplete in an `implements` clause offers all registered interfaces; documentation for an interface lists its contract members. | | AC-12 | All existing GDScript test suite scripts still compile and pass (except intentionally-updated tests for the two new reserved keywords). | | AC-13 | A script that uses `interface` as a variable name fails to parse with `Identifier "interface" is a reserved keyword.` |  ---  ## 9. Example Usage  ```gdscript # res://scripts/enemy.gd class_name Enemy extends Character implements Damageable, Saveable:  var health: int = 100 var max_health: int = 100  func take_damage(amount: int) -> void:     health = max(health - amount, 0)     if health == 0:         died.emit()  func is_alive() -> bool:     return health > 0  signal died ```  ```gdscript # res://scripts/combat.gd func apply_damage(target: Damageable, amount: int) -> void:     target.take_damage(amount)      # resolved through the interface contract  func try_damage(node: Node) -> void:     if node is Damageable:         (node as Damageable).take_damage(10) ```  ```gdscript # res://scripts/player.gd class_name Player extends Character implements Damageable:     # Compiler error: Class "Player" does not implement member     # "take_damage(amount: int) -> void" required by interface "Damageable".     var health: int = 100 ```  ---  ## 10. Future Considerations (out of scope for this requirement)  - Optional/default members in interfaces (partial conformance). - Abstract classes and abstract methods as a companion mechanism. - Generic interfaces with type parameters. - Interface-scoped `static`/`const` blocks shared across implementers. - Compile-time structural (duck-typed) conformance checking for classes that opt in without declaring `implements`.

issue_title: [RFC] RPC Based Distributed Model Parallel
requirement: ## RFC Requirement: RPC-Based Distributed Model Parallel Execution  The system shall provide an opt-in distributed execution mode that partitions a single model across multiple worker processes or hosts and coordinates model-parallel execution using remote procedure calls (RPC). Distributed execution shall present the same public inference interface as local execution.  ### Functional Requirements  1. **Model partitioning and placement**    - The system shall allow model layers or execution submodules to be assigned to separate workers through configuration.    - Each worker shall load only the model components assigned to it.    - The system shall support workers running on different hosts.  2. **RPC execution**    - The system shall expose each assigned model stage through a versioned RPC interface.    - RPC requests and responses shall carry tensor data and required metadata, including tensor shape, data type, and execution options.    - Intermediate activations shall be transferred between workers through RPC without requiring shared memory.  3. **Execution coordination**    - A coordinator shall validate worker readiness, dispatch the initial input to the first stage, forward intermediate results, and return the final output to the caller.    - The coordinator shall propagate request identifiers, deadlines, and cancellation signals across stage boundaries.    - The execution mode shall support both single-request and batched request submission.  4. **Configuration and compatibility**    - Configuration shall specify worker addresses, model-stage assignments, RPC timeouts, and distributed-execution enablement.    - Existing local execution shall remain available and shall not require distributed-execution configuration.  5. **Failure handling**    - RPC failures, worker disconnections, and timeouts shall terminate the affected request within the configured timeout.    - Errors shall identify the failed operation and worker stage.    - A failed request shall not leave the coordinator or healthy workers in an indefinitely blocked state.  6. **Observability**    - The system shall expose per-stage execution latency, RPC transfer size, and failure information through its existing logging or metrics facilities.  ### Acceptance Criteria  - A supported model partitioned across two or more workers shall complete inference and produce results numerically equivalent, within the project’s defined tolerance, to local execution. - Killing or disconnecting an active worker shall cause the affected request to fail with a stage-specific error rather than hang. - Enabling or disabling distributed execution shall not change the public inference API. - Integration tests shall cover successful multi-worker execution, stage-to-stage tensor transfer, worker startup and shutdown, RPC timeout, and mid-request worker failure.

issue_title: RFC: Introduce `setup`, `teardown`, and `fixture` attributes for `cargo test`
requirement: The Rust test harness (`libtest`) and `cargo test` runner shall support declarative test lifecycle management through `#[setup]`, `#[teardown]`, and `#[fixture]` attributes:  1. **`#[fixture]`**: The framework shall allow defining reusable fixture functions that construct state, pass initialized resources as parameters into test functions, and manage the scope and lifetime of associated test dependencies. 2. **`#[setup]`**: The framework shall support annotating functions to execute preparation logic immediately prior to the execution of associated test cases or test modules. 3. **`#[teardown]`**: The framework shall support annotating functions to execute cleanup logic immediately following test execution, guaranteeing execution even in the event of test assertion failures or panics. 4. **Execution and Isolation**: Fixture, setup, and teardown lifecycles shall integrate with standard multi-threaded test execution while preserving isolation between individual test invocations.

requirement: The system shall provide a simple and efficient method to compute gradients of each element of a sum.

issue_title: Inclusive version of take_while
requirement: **REQ-001: Inclusive take-while operation**  **Statement** The library shall provide a `take_while_inclusive` function that behaves like the existing `take_while`, except that the first element failing the predicate is included in the result.  **Functional behavior** 1. Given an input sequence and a predicate, the function shall yield input elements in order while the predicate evaluates to true. 2. The function shall additionally yield the first input element for which the predicate evaluates to false; this element shall be the last element of the output, and iteration shall stop after it. 3. If the predicate evaluates to true for every input element, the output shall contain the entire input sequence. 4. If the input sequence is empty, the output shall be empty. 5. If the predicate evaluates to false for the first element, the output shall contain exactly that single element. 6. The predicate shall be evaluated at most once per element and shall not be evaluated for any element after the first failing (terminating) element. 7. The function shall be lazy (streaming): it shall not consume elements from the input beyond the terminating element. 8. The function shall not modify the input sequence.  **Acceptance criteria** - `take_while_inclusive([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], x < 3)` → `[1, 2, 3]` - `take_while_inclusive([1, 2, 3], x < 10)` → `[1, 2, 3]` - `take_while_inclusive([4, 5, 6], x < 3)` → `[4]` - `take_while_inclusive([], x < 3)` → `[]`

issue_title: cmd/compile: implement powerpc 32-bit backend (ppc32)

This implementation MUST include instruction selection and SSA lowering rules for the 32-bit PowerPC ISA, register allocation utilizing the PPC32 register set, adherence to the 32-bit PowerPC ABI calling convention, and integration with the linker (cmd/link) and runtime to produce executable binaries capable of passing the standard Go test suite.

issue_title: Implement similar PyTorch function as model.summary() in keras?
requirement: **Requirement ID:** FR-MODEL-SUMMARY-001  **Title:** Model Summary Function for PyTorch  **Requirement Statement:** The system shall provide a `summary()` method for PyTorch `nn.Module` models that generates and displays a formatted tabular report equivalent to Keras's `model.summary()` output.  **Functional Specifications:**  1. The `summary()` method shall accept an optional argument specifying either an input shape (tuple) or a sample input tensor, which shall be used to perform a forward pass for layer output shape inference. 2. The generated report shall list, for every layer/module in the model's forward execution order:    a. The layer/module name;    b. The output shape of the layer;    c. The number of trainable parameters in the layer;    d. The number of non-trainable parameters in the layer. 3. The report shall conclude with aggregate totals: total number of parameters, total trainable parameters, and total non-trainable parameters. 4. The report shall indicate the approximate model size in memory (e.g., in MB) based on total parameter count and default dtype. 5. The method shall correctly handle models containing nested and hierarchical modules, representing sub-modules with hierarchical indentation. 6. The method shall support models with multiple inputs and models with conditional forward logic, falling back to module-level enumeration (without output shapes) when a forward pass cannot be completed without the optional input argument. 7. If no input shape or sample input is provided and shape inference is not possible, the method shall still produce a report containing layer names and parameter counts, and shall not raise an error. 8. The method shall be callable on any `nn.Module` subclass without requiring modification of user-defined model code.

issue_title: [FYI] NestedTensor Project Progress
requirement: ## Requirement: NestedTensor Project Progress Tracking  ### Background NestedTensor is an experimental PyTorch extension providing a tensor subclass for nested (ragged/irregular) tensor data, with support for `torch.compile`, autograd, and distributed training primitives. As the project evolves, contributors and users need a single, discoverable source of truth describing where the project stands, what has recently landed, what is currently in flight, and what is planned next.  ### Functional Requirements 1. The NestedTensor repository shall contain a persistent, human-readable project progress document (e.g., `PROGRESS.md` at the repository root, mirrored to the project wiki or documentation site). 2. The document shall be organized into clearly labeled sections:    - **Status Summary** — one-paragraph current state of the project, its maturity level (experimental/beta/stable), and supported features.    - **Milestones / Release History** — list of released versions with dates and headline changes.    - **In-Progress Work** — active branches/PRs with a short description, owner, and target release.    - **Known Issues & Blockers** — open defects, upstream PyTorch dependencies, and limitations.    - **Roadmap** — planned features and upcoming milestones, ordered by priority.    - **Recent Activity** — notable merged PRs, issues resolved, and community contributions since the previous update. 3. Each tracked item shall carry a status marker (e.g., `Planned`, `In Progress`, `In Review`, `Done`, `Blocked`, `Dropped`) and, where applicable, a link to the corresponding GitHub issue, pull request, or milestone. 4. The document shall be updated at a defined cadence — at minimum once per minor release and whenever a milestone is completed, blocked, or abandoned — and each update shall be dated. 5. The progress document shall be referenced from the repository `README.md` and the project documentation index so that it is discoverable within a single click from the project landing page. 6. The format shall be plain Markdown using tables and checklists, renderable on GitHub without external tooling, and shall not require generated assets or build steps.  ### Non-Functional Requirements - Content shall be accurate as of the stated update date; stale entries must be revised rather than appended indefinitely. - The document shall remain concise: the status summary shall not exceed one paragraph, and no single section shall exceed roughly 200 lines, so that it is readable in a single sitting. - Entries shall use stable issue/PR identifiers so that historical updates remain traceable after items close. - Additions and edits to the document shall be reviewable via the same pull-request process as code changes.  ### Acceptance Criteria - A `PROGRESS.md` (or equivalent) file exists in the repository root, is linked from the `README.md`, and contains all six sections listed above. - Every listed in-progress item links to an open GitHub issue or pull request and shows a status marker. - The document displays a last-updated date consistent with the most recent release or significant merged PR. - The file renders correctly as Markdown on GitHub and passes a repository Markdown-lint check, if one is configured. - A contributor can add or update a progress entry in a single pull request without modifying build configuration or scripts.

issue_title: Add function to make paths absolute, which is different from canonicalization
requirement: ## Requirement: Add `absolute()` — Convert a path to an absolute path without canonicalization  ### Summary  The path utilities module shall provide a new function, `absolute()`, that converts a given path into an absolute path. This operation is explicitly **not** the same as canonicalization: `absolute()` performs no filesystem access, does not resolve symbolic links, does not collapse `..` across symlink boundaries, and does not require the path (or any part of it) to exist. It only anchors the path to a known absolute base and produces a lexically absolute result.  ### Motivation  Users currently have only two options for obtaining an absolute path, and both are inappropriate in different situations:  - **Canonicalization** (`canonicalize()`) resolves symlinks, requires the path to exist, and touches the filesystem. It therefore fails for paths that are about to be created, and it can return an unexpected location when a symlink is involved. - **Manual concatenation** with the current working directory is error-prone: it does not account for relative paths whose base is not the process CWD, and it produces results containing `.`/`..` segments that are not lexically clean.  `absolute()` fills the gap: it is a pure, non-filesystem, lexical operation that guarantees the result is an absolute path, useful for configuration handling, path comparisons, logging, and building paths for files that do not yet exist.  ### API  ```rust /// Makes `path` absolute against `base`, without touching the filesystem. /// /// - If `path` is already absolute, it is returned unchanged (lexically normalized). /// - If `path` is relative, it is joined to `base`. /// - `base` must be absolute; if `base` is relative, it is interpreted relative to ///   the process current working directory. pub fn absolute<P: AsRef<Path>, B: AsRef<Path>>(path: P, base: B) -> Result<PathBuf, Error>;  /// Convenience overload that uses the process current working directory as the base. pub fn absolute_from_cwd<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> Result<PathBuf, Error>; ```  If the library is not Rust-based, the equivalent signature in the host language shall be used, preserving the semantics below. The function shall be exported from the crate's public API and documented in the public API reference alongside `canonicalize()`.  ### Normative behavior  1. **Already-absolute input is preserved.** If the input path is absolute, the output shall be the input path, with only lexical normalization applied (`.` segments removed, duplicate separators collapsed, trailing separator removed except for the root). No error shall be raised, and no filesystem lookup shall occur. 2. **Relative input is joined to the base.** If the input path is relative, the output shall be `base` joined with the input path, with lexical normalization applied to the result. 3. **Base resolution.** The base shall be used as supplied. If the base is relative, it shall first be made absolute against the process current working directory. The current working directory shall be read once, at call time, and the value used shall be consistent for the whole call. 4. **No filesystem access.** The function shall not stat, open, read, or otherwise query the filesystem for the existence of the input path, the base, or any intermediate component. It shall not follow symbolic links. 5. **No `..` resolution beyond lexical joining.** The function shall not collapse `..` segments, because doing so correctly requires filesystem knowledge (a preceding segment may be a symlink). A `..` segment shall be preserved in the output, unless it is trivially removable as the immediate parent of the current directory (i.e., `foo/../bar` retains `..`). *Note: the library's existing normalization rules for `..` shall be documented explicitly on the function so that behavior is unambiguous.* 6. **No change to path semantics beyond absoluteness.** The function shall not alter case, extension, filename, or the order/nature of components; it shall not add or remove a filename extension, and it shall not strip a trailing separator from the root path (`/`). 7. **Empty input.** An empty path shall be treated as the base directory, yielding the absolute base path. 8. **Determinism.** For a given `(path, base)` pair the function shall always return the same result, independent of filesystem state at the time of the call.  ### Examples  | Input path | Base | Output | |---|---|---| | `foo/bar.txt` | `/tmp` | `/tmp/foo/bar.txt` | | `/foo/bar.txt` | `/tmp` | `/foo/bar.txt` | | `foo/../bar.txt` | `/tmp` | `/tmp/foo/../bar.txt` (see rule 5) | | `./foo/./bar.txt` | `/tmp` | `/tmp/foo/bar.txt` | | `foo` | `/tmp/` | `/tmp/foo` | | `""` | `/tmp` | `/tmp` | | `foo` | (CWD = `/home/u`) | `/home/u/foo` |  ### Error handling  - The function shall return an error (or the language's equivalent error mechanism) only for conditions that prevent producing a result, e.g. the current working directory cannot be determined when it is required, or an invalid path encoding is encountered. - Absence of the target path on disk shall **not** be an error. - Errors shall carry a message identifying the offending input and base.  ### Documentation requirements  - The public documentation for `absolute()` shall state prominently that it differs from `canonicalize()` and shall enumerate the differences: no filesystem access, no symlink resolution, no existence requirement, `..` handling. - The documentation shall include the behavior table above and at least one usage example. - The crate's README/API index shall list the new function.  ### Acceptance criteria  1. `absolute()` exists in the public API and is documented. 2. Unit tests cover every row of the examples table and the empty-input case. 3. A test verifies that the function succeeds for a path that does not exist on disk. 4. A test verifies that a symlinked base directory is **not** resolved by `absolute()`, and that the equivalent call to `canonicalize()` **does** resolve it — demonstrating the documented difference. 5. A test verifies that the result of `absolute()` is always absolute. 6. Existing `canonicalize()` behavior and tests remain unchanged. 7. The implementation performs no filesystem metadata calls for the input path (verifiable via an instrumented filesystem or by inspection).  ### Non-goals  - Symbolic-link resolution. - Existence checks or validation of the resulting path. - Case normalization, Unicode normalization, or Windows-specific long-path/UNC handling beyond what the library already provides. - Any change to the behavior of existing path functions.

issue_title: Using std::io::{Read, Write, Cursor} in a nostd environment
requirement: **Requirement: no_std-compatible Read, Write, and Cursor abstractions**  The library shall provide `Read`, `Write`, and `Cursor` I/O abstractions that compile and function in `#![no_std]` environments without depending on `std::io`. These abstractions shall:  1. Be available when the `std` feature is disabled, and shall not require the standard library or an operating system. 2. Expose `Read` and `Write` traits with method signatures matching the semantics of `std::io::Read` and `std::io::Write` (including `read`, `read_exact`, `write`, `write_all`, and `flush`), using a no_std-compatible error type. 3. Provide a `Cursor<T>` type that wraps in-memory buffers (`&[u8]`, `&mut [u8]`, and `Vec<u8>` when the `alloc` feature is enabled), supports `Read`, `Write`, and `Seek` operations, and tracks its position with the same semantics as `std::io::Cursor`. 4. Report errors through a no_std-compatible error type that includes at least an unexpected-end-of-input kind and a write-zero or out-of-capacity kind, and that can be converted to or from `core::fmt::Error` where applicable. 5. Be implemented on top of `core` (and optionally `alloc`), so that `std::io` types are re-exported or interoperable when the `std` feature is enabled, without breaking existing `std` users. 6. Be verified by unit tests run under `cargo test --no-default-features` and by a `no_std` build check for a bare-metal target (e.g., `thumbv7em-none-eabihf`) in CI. 7. Be documented, including which features are required for each capability and any behavioral differences from `std::io`.

issue_title: Subslice search

The function shall work for any element type supporting equality comparison, shall treat an empty pattern as matching at index 0, shall return "not found" when the pattern is longer than the source, and shall be implemented with an efficient algorithm (e.g., two-way search or KMP) providing linear worst-case time complexity O(n + m). A companion variant shall return the starting indices of all (including overlapping) occurrences, or an iterator over them.

The feature must be toggleable so the existing linear-memory GC remains available, and the resulting binaries must run correctly on WASM-GC-capable engines.

issue_title: Godot C# GDExtension Roadmap Discussion
requirement: **REQ-GDE-CS-001 — C# Language Support Delivered as a GDExtension**  The Godot Engine shall implement C# language support as a GDExtension-based module that is fully decoupled from the engine core, enabling the engine to be built, distributed, and used with or without C# support, and enabling the C# extension to be independently versioned, released, and installed.  The system shall:  1. Expose the complete public Godot API to C# through generated GDExtension bindings, achieving functional parity with GDScript and other GDExtension languages (classes, signals, properties, methods, and constants). 2. Produce engine builds that contain no .NET/Mono runtime dependency when C# support is excluded, without degrading any other engine functionality. 3. Distribute the C# extension as a separate, versioned package that can be installed per-project (e.g., via the Asset Library or addon mechanism) without recompiling the engine, with each extension release publishing its compatible Godot major.minor version and target .NET runtime. 4. Preserve editor-integrated C# tooling when the extension is installed, including solution/project generation, MSBuild compilation, script attach/detach, debugger attach points, and assembly hot-reload. 5. Support exporting C# projects to all platforms covered by the standard export templates, including packaging of the required runtime assemblies and data files for each target. 6. Provide documented migration guidance for projects using the legacy built-in C# (Mono) module, covering breaking changes, updated project configuration, and required tooling versions.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - A Godot build compiled without the C# module runs all non-C# features with no errors or missing-functionality regressions. - Installing the C# GDExtension package into a project enables creating, editing, building, running, debugging, and exporting C# scripts with no engine recompilation. - Every released extension version ships with a compatibility matrix mapping it to supported Godot versions and .NET runtimes. - All core classes accessible to GDScript are invocable from C# via the extension bindings, verified by an automated API-coverage test suite.

issue_title: Add support for nullable static types in GDScript
requirement: **Requirement: Nullable Static Types in GDScript**  GDScript shall support declaring variables, parameters, and return values with static types that explicitly permit a `null` value. Such nullable static types shall be expressed through a clear, documented syntax (for example, a `?` suffix or an equivalent annotation on the type name).  Specifically, the feature shall:  1. Allow a variable, parameter, or function return type declared as nullable to hold either a value of its declared static type or `null`. 2. Continue to enforce static type checking at compile time for all non-null assignments, rejecting assignments of incompatible types. 3. Reject assignment of `null` to variables or parameters declared with a non-nullable static type, at compile time where determinable and at runtime otherwise, with an error message identifying the variable and expected type. 4. Permit nullable static types on built-in types, engine classes, user-defined classes, and inner classes. 5. Emit a runtime error with a descriptive message when a nullable-typed value is dereferenced or used in an operation requiring a non-null value while it is `null`, consistent with existing null-handling behavior in GDScript. 6. Preserve backward compatibility: existing code without nullable annotations shall behave identically to its current behavior. 7. Ensure that the static type information for nullable types is available to the analyzer, autocompletion, and static warnings, so that tooling reflects nullability.

issue_title: Crate local state for procedural macros?
requirement: **Requirement: Crate-Scoped Persistent State for Procedural Macros**  The procedural macro system shall provide a mechanism that allows multiple procedural macro invocations within the same crate compilation to read and write shared state that is scoped to that crate.  1. **Scope isolation:** State shall be visible only to macro invocations within the crate being compiled. State from one crate shall not be accessible to macros in another crate, including dependent crates. 2. **Lifetime:** State shall persist across all macro expansions within a single crate compilation session and shall be discarded when that compilation completes. 3. **Access API:** The macro API shall expose a defined interface for storing, retrieving, and updating crate-local values, with keys or types that prevent collisions between independent macros. 4. **Ordering:** The system shall document the expansion order guarantees that apply to state reads and writes, and shall make clear whether state written by one invocation is guaranteed to be visible to later invocations. 5. **Determinism:** Given identical source input, the state-dependent expansion output shall be deterministic and independent of the host's thread scheduling or parallel expansion behavior. 6. **Incremental compilation:** The mechanism shall define how crate-local state interacts with incremental compilation, including invalidation when the source changes, so that stale state cannot produce incorrect expansions. 7. **Concurrency safety:** Concurrent expansions that access crate-local state shall not cause data races or undefined behavior. Access shall be synchronized or the API shall prohibit concurrent mutation. 8. **Backward compatibility:** Existing procedural macros that do not use crate-local state shall compile and behave identically, with no measurable compile-time regression when the feature is unused. 9. **Diagnostics:** Misuse of the API, such as type mismatches on retrieval or access outside a valid compilation context, shall produce clear compile-time errors.

issue_title: Implement Terrain
requirement: **REQ-TERRAIN-001: Terrain System**  **Title:** Implement 3D terrain system  **Description:** The application shall provide a terrain system that supports the creation, rendering, and interactive use of 3D terrain environments.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **Terrain Generation:** The system shall construct terrain geometry from heightmap data, supporting both imported heightmaps (16-bit grayscale images) and procedural generation via configurable noise (e.g., Perlin/Simplex) with adjustable frequency, amplitude, octaves, and seed.  2. **Terrain Composition:** Terrain shall be organized into a configurable grid of chunks (default chunk size: 64×64 vertices) to enable efficient streaming, updating, and rendering.  3. **Terrain Editing:** The system shall expose runtime editing operations — raise, lower, flatten, and smooth — applied via brush tools with adjustable radius and strength, and shall support both editor-time and runtime modification.  4. **Texturing:** The system shall support texture splatting with a minimum of four texture layers, blended using user-editable masks and/or automatic weighting by height and slope.  5. **Physics Integration:** The system shall generate a collision surface matching the terrain heightfield, such that character controllers and rigid bodies interact accurately with the visible terrain.  6. **Level of Detail:** The system shall automatically reduce mesh resolution for distant terrain chunks based on camera distance, with seamless transitions (no visible popping or cracks).  7. **Object Placement:** The system shall support scattering of objects (e.g., trees, rocks, grass) on terrain surfaces via density rules constrained by height, slope, and texture mask.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  1. The system shall maintain a target frame rate of 60 FPS with a terrain of at least 1 km² (1,024×1,024 heightmap) on mid-range hardware. 2. Terrain chunk loading and unloading shall occur asynchronously without frame hitches exceeding 5 ms. 3. All terrain data shall be serializable to and loadable from a project file format.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  1. A terrain of at least 1,024×1,024 units can be generated from a heightmap and from procedural noise, and renders correctly from all camera angles. 2. Height edits made at runtime are reflected visually and in physics collision within one frame. 3. Texture layers blend smoothly with no hard seams at mask boundaries. 4. LOD transitions are imperceptible at normal viewing distances. 5. All functionality is covered by automated tests, and documentation includes usage examples for generation, editing, and object placement.

issue_title: Replace GridMap with an improved TileMap3D node (inspired by the new 2D TileMap)
requirement: # Requirement: Replace GridMap with an improved TileMap3D node  The engine shall provide a new `TileMap3D` node as the recommended way to create tile-based 3D levels, replacing `GridMap` and adopting the resource and authoring conventions of the 2D `TileMap`.  ## Functional requirements  1. **TileSet-based data model**    - `TileMap3D` shall reference a `TileSet` containing reusable 3D tile definitions.    - Tiles shall be definable from meshes or scenes and may define materials, collision shapes, navigation polygons, custom data layers, and alternative or terrain-based tile variants consistent with the 2D `TileMap` workflow.    - Each occupied cell shall store its source tile, orientation, and custom data without requiring a separate node for every mesh tile.  2. **3D editor tooling**    - The editor shall provide a tile palette and tools for painting, erasing, filling rectangular or line-shaped regions, and transforming selected cells.    - Editing shall support undo/redo, grid snapping, and updates to collision and navigation data.    - Tile placement and orientation shall remain consistent between editor and runtime.    - The editor shall display occupied cells and their custom data for inspection and debugging.  3. **Runtime and serialization**    - The runtime API shall support setting, retrieving, and erasing cells; querying occupied cells by tile source; reading and writing cell transforms and custom data.    - Changes shall update rendering, collision, and navigation without recreating unaffected portions of the map.    - TileMap3D data shall be saved and restored in scene files, including all cell contents and custom properties.  4. **Collision and navigation**    - Collision shapes and navigation polygons defined by tiles shall be instantiated automatically.    - Navigation data shall be generated or baked from the map and refreshed after relevant tile edits.    - Physics layers, collision masks, and navigation layers shall be configurable per tile.  5. **Performance**    - Mesh-based tiles shall be batched using an efficient rendering representation such as `MultiMesh`.    - Scene-based tiles shall preserve scene behavior and may be represented by instantiated nodes.    - The implementation shall use spatial partitioning or octants for visibility culling and incremental updates.    - Performance and memory usage shall be comparable to or better than `GridMap` for equivalent maps.  6. **Compatibility and migration**    - `GridMap` shall remain functional for existing projects but shall be marked deprecated with an editor warning and migration guidance.    - A conversion tool shall migrate a `GridMap` to `TileMap3D`, preserving occupied cells, positions, orientations, tile assignments, custom data, and collision and navigation configuration.    - The conversion tool shall report any information that cannot be represented by `TileMap3D`.  7. **Documentation**    - The API reference shall document `TileMap3D`, its `TileSet` resources, runtime methods, and editor workflow.    - Documentation shall include a `GridMap` migration guide and examples covering mesh tiles, scene tiles, collision, navigation, and custom data.  ## Acceptance criteria  - A user can create a `TileSet`, paint a 3D level in the editor, save it, reopen it, and obtain identical tile placement, orientation, and custom data. - Mesh and scene tiles render correctly and are correctly excluded by frustum culling. - Tile-defined collision and navigation are present and update after painting or erasing cells. - A representative `GridMap` containing at least 100,000 occupied cells converts to `TileMap3D` without loss of supported map data and remains editable and navigable. - The editor displays a deprecation warning for `GridMap` and links to the migration documentation.

issue_title: x/tools/gopls: support for bazel-based projects
requirement: **Requirement: Bazel Workspace Support in gopls**  gopls shall support Go projects built with Bazel (including those using `rules_go` and Gazelle) as a first-class workspace type, without requiring a `go.mod` file at the workspace root.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **Workspace detection:** gopls shall identify a Bazel workspace by the presence of a `WORKSPACE`, `WORKSPACE.bazel`, `MODULE.bazel`, or `BUILD`/`BUILD.bazel` file at the workspace root, and shall apply Bazel-specific package loading when no `go.mod` is present.  2. **Package loading:** gopls shall obtain package metadata (file-to-package mapping, import graph, build constraints, and compiled file lists) from Bazel, either by invoking a `go/packages`-compatible driver such as `rules_go`'s `gopackagesdriver` or by querying Bazel directly (for example, via `bazel query` and `bazel aquery`).  3. **Configuration:** Users shall be able to configure the Bazel driver path, the Bazel executable, target patterns, and additional Bazel flags through gopls settings (for example, `gopls.env` or a dedicated `gopls.bazel` settings group). Default behavior shall work with no configuration in a standard `rules_go` setup.  4. **Language features:** For Go files within Bazel packages, gopls shall provide the following with the same behavior as in module-mode workspaces: diagnostics, go-to-definition, find references, hover, completion, rename, and imports organization. Cross-package and external-repository references resolved through Bazel shall be supported.  5. **Generated code:** gopls shall include files produced by Bazel genrules and `go_library` generated sources in analysis when they are declared as inputs of the target being analyzed.  6. **Build tags and platform selection:** gopls shall respect `go_*` rule attributes and `--platforms` or configuration flags that affect build constraints, so that files excluded by the active Bazel configuration are not reported as errors.  7. **Incremental updates:** When a `BUILD`, `.bzl`, `WORKSPACE`, or `MODULE.bazel` file changes, gopls shall refresh affected package metadata without requiring a restart of the language server.  8. **Performance:** Metadata queries to Bazel shall run asynchronously and shall not block editor features on already-loaded packages. Results shall be cached between sessions where Bazel's query output is unchanged.  9. **Error reporting:** If Bazel is unavailable, a target fails to analyze, or the driver returns an error, gopls shall surface a diagnostic or log message that identifies the failing command and its output, and shall continue to serve features for unaffected packages.  **Acceptance Criteria**  - A sample Bazel workspace using `rules_go` and Gazelle opens in a supported editor with gopls and reports no spurious "package not found" or "no required module provides package" errors for targets it builds. - Go-to-definition and find-references work across at least two packages and one external repository dependency. - Editing a `BUILD` file to add a dependency makes the new import resolvable within a few seconds without restarting gopls. - Existing module-mode and GOPATH-mode behavior is unchanged; all existing gopls tests pass. - Documentation describing Bazel setup and configuration options is added to the gopls documentation.

issue_title: AVIF codec support
requirement: **Requirement: AVIF Image Codec Support**  The system shall support reading (decoding) and writing (encoding) images in the AVIF (AV1 Image File Format) codec, including:  1. **Decoding:** The system shall decode AVIF images conforming to the AVIF specification (AV1-based still image format), including 8-bit and 10-bit color depths, and alpha (transparency) channels. 2. **Encoding:** The system shall encode images to AVIF format, providing a configurable quality setting and a lossless mode. 3. **Metadata:** The system shall preserve EXIF, XMP, and ICC color profile metadata when reading and writing AVIF files, where present. 4. **Format detection:** The system shall identify AVIF files by their content signature (ISOBMFF `ftyp` box with `avif` or `avis` brand) rather than solely by file extension (`.avif`). 5. **Animated AVIF:** The system shall support decoding animated AVIF image sequences (`avis` brand) into their constituent frames, with per-frame timing preserved. 6. **Error handling:** The system shall report a descriptive error, without terminating the host process, when an AVIF file is malformed, truncated, or uses an unsupported feature. 7. **Dependency handling:** AVIF support shall be provided through a documented, optional codec backend (e.g., libavif with an AV1 encoder/decoder such as libaom, dav1d, or SVT-AV1), and the system shall build and run without AVIF support when the backend is absent, reporting AVIF as unavailable. 8. **Compatibility:** Encoded AVIF files shall be readable by mainstream AVIF-capable software (current major web browsers and libavif-based tools).  **Acceptance criteria:** - Round-trip encode/decode of a reference image set yields output within the configured quality tolerance (lossless mode yields bit-identical pixel data). - Files with `.avif` extension but non-AVIF content are rejected with a format error. - Build and test pass both with and without the AVIF backend enabled.

issue_title: proposal: database/sql: support a way to perform bulk actions
requirement: **Requirement ID:** REQ-DBSQL-BULK-001 **Title:** Bulk Operation Support in `database/sql`  **1. Description** The `database/sql` package shall provide a first-class, driver-agnostic API for executing bulk database operations (e.g., batch INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE), allowing an application to submit a collection of parameter sets for a single statement in one logical call.  **2. Problem Statement** Currently, applications that must insert, update, or delete many rows must either (a) execute one statement per row, incurring per-statement overhead (network round trips, re-parsing/re-planning), or (b) manually construct multi-row SQL strings, which is error-prone, non-portable across databases, and risks SQL injection when values are interpolated by hand.  **3. Functional Requirements** 3.1. The package shall expose a function or type that accepts a prepared statement (or statement text) and a collection of parameter sets, and executes them as a single logical bulk operation. 3.2. The API shall accept parameter sets supplied as a slice or iterator of argument tuples, with each set corresponding to one row execution. 3.3. The API shall support `context.Context` for cancellation and timeouts, consistent with existing `database/sql` conventions. 3.4. If the underlying driver and database support native batch or multi-row execution, the implementation shall use it. If not, the package shall transparently fall back to sequential execution of the parameter sets while preserving the API contract. 3.5. The API shall return the total number of affected rows and, where the driver supports it, per-row results (e.g., generated keys via `LastInsertId` or `RETURNING`). 3.6. When a bulk operation fails partway through, the API shall report the failure along with the index or identity of the failing parameter set where the driver exposes this information. 3.7. The API shall define an optional new driver interface (e.g., `driver.Batcher`) that drivers may implement to opt into native bulk execution; existing `driver.Driver`/`driver.Stmt` implementations shall continue to work unmodified via the fallback path. 3.8. All parameter values shall be passed as bound arguments; the API shall not require or encourage string interpolation of values into SQL text.  **4. Non-Functional Requirements** 4.1. Bulk execution shall reduce round trips and/or statement preparation overhead relative to per-row execution when native driver support is available. 4.2. The API shall be safe for concurrent use consistent with existing `database/sql` guarantees. 4.3. The design shall not break backward compatibility: no existing exported API may change behavior or be removed.  **5. Acceptance Criteria** 5.1. A caller can insert, update, or delete N rows using a single API call with N parameter sets. 5.2. Behavior is fully documented for both native-batch drivers and fallback (non-batch) drivers. 5.3. The implementation includes tests covering at least one driver implementing the optional bulk interface and one driver relying on the sequential fallback, including partial-failure scenarios.  **6. Constraints and Assumptions** 6.1. The solution must comply with the Go compatibility promise for the standard library. 6.2. Transaction semantics (atomicity or partial commit of the batch) shall be explicitly specified and documented; if atomicity is desired, callers may wrap the bulk call in an explicit transaction. 6.3. Final API naming and signatures shall be determined during design review, subject to the Go proposal process.

issue_title: [Feature request] Let DistributedSampler take a Sampler as input

issue_title: Implement `numpy.random.choice` equivalent
requirement: **Requirement: Implement a `numpy.random.choice`-Equivalent Random Sampling Function**  **Summary** Provide a function that randomly draws samples from a population, either from an integer range or an array-like input, with optional sampling with or without replacement and optional non-uniform probability weights. The behavior must match `numpy.random.choice` for equivalent inputs.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **Population input**    - If `a` is a positive integer `n`, sample from the integers `0` to `n-1`.    - If `a` is a non-empty 1-D array-like, sample elements from it.    - If `a` is a scalar that is not a positive integer, or is an empty array-like, raise `ValueError`.    - If `a` is multi-dimensional, raise `ValueError`.  2. **Output shape (`size`)**    - `size=None` returns a single sample as a scalar.    - `size` as an integer `k` returns a 1-D array of length `k`.    - `size` as a tuple returns an array with that shape.    - A zero or negative `size` dimension must follow NumPy conventions: zero yields an empty array; negative raises `ValueError`.  3. **Replacement (`replace`)**    - `replace=True` (default) allows repeated samples.    - `replace=False` samples without repetition.    - If `replace=False` and the requested number of samples exceeds the population size, raise `ValueError`.  4. **Probability weights (`p`)**    - `p=None` implies uniform sampling.    - If provided, `p` must have the same length as the population, contain only non-negative finite values, and sum to 1 within a floating-point tolerance (e.g., `1e-8`). Otherwise raise `ValueError`.    - When `replace=False` with `p`, sampling must proceed sequentially, renormalizing probabilities after each draw, so that selected elements are not repeated.    - Elements with zero probability must never be selected.  5. **Random state**    - Accept an optional random generator or seed so that results are reproducible across runs with the same seed.    - Use the project's standard RNG mechanism; do not rely on global mutable state unless it is the project's established convention.  6. **Return type**    - Return a NumPy array (or scalar when `size=None`) whose dtype matches the population's dtype when sampling from an array, and an integer dtype when sampling from an integer range.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  - **Statistical correctness:** Over large sample counts, empirical frequencies must converge to the specified probabilities (or uniform distribution when `p` is `None`). - **Performance:** Sampling with replacement and no `p` must run in O(k) time for k samples. Sampling with `p` must be O(k log n) or better using precomputed cumulative probabilities. - **Compatibility:** For identical inputs and seeds, outputs should match `numpy.random.choice` where the underlying algorithm is the same, or be documented as differing if the algorithm differs.  **Acceptance Criteria**  - Unit tests cover every parameter combination: integer and array population, each `size` form, `replace` True/False, and `p` with and without normalization errors. - Tests verify all error conditions listed above raise the specified exception type. - Tests confirm zero-probability elements are never returned across at least 10,000 draws. - Tests confirm reproducibility: the same seed produces identical output. - A statistical test confirms that observed frequencies over 100,000 draws fall within a tolerance of expected probabilities. - Documentation includes a docstring with parameters, return values, raised exceptions, and at least one usage example.

issue_title: Support multiple windows for desktop shells

issue_title: Support for `uint16`, `uint32`, and `uint64`
requirement: **Requirement: Unsigned Integer Type Support (uint16, uint32, uint64)**  The system shall extend its supported data types to include the unsigned integer types `uint16`, `uint32`, and `uint64`.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. The system shall provide first-class support for the `uint16` type, representing unsigned 16-bit integers with a valid range of 0 to 65,535.  2. The system shall provide first-class support for the `uint32` type, representing unsigned 32-bit integers with a valid range of 0 to 4,294,967,295.  3. The system shall provide first-class support for the `uint64` type, representing unsigned 64-bit integers with a valid range of 0 to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615.  4. The new unsigned integer types shall support the same operations (e.g., creation, arithmetic, comparison, conversion, serialization) available to the system's existing integer types, at parity in behavior and API.  5. The system shall support safe conversion between the new unsigned integer types and existing numeric types, including:    - Implicit or explicit conversion (as consistent with the system's existing conversion semantics) between signed and unsigned integer types.    - Well-defined overflow/underflow behavior (wrapping, error, or saturation) consistent with the system's policies for existing integer types, applied when values fall outside the target type's valid range.  6. Arithmetic operations on `uint16`, `uint32`, and `uint64` values shall conform to standard two's-complement-free unsigned integer semantics, and results shall never produce negative values.  7. The new types shall be integrated into all relevant subsystems, including but not limited to:    - Type inference and type checking (where applicable).    - Parsing and formatting of literal values (e.g., decimal and hexadecimal literals with appropriate suffixes).    - Serialization/deserialization and interchange formats.    - Documentation, error messages, and diagnostics.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - Users can declare, assign, and manipulate values of types `uint16`, `uint32`, and `uint64` without workarounds. - Operations on each type behave correctly at boundary values (0, maximum value) and on overflow/underflow per the defined policy. - Conversions between these types and existing numeric types behave consistently and are covered by tests. - All new types are documented and covered by the project's test suite.

issue_title: compress/bzip2: implement bz2 encoder
requirement: The `compress/bzip2` package shall provide a `Writer` implementation that conforms to the `io.WriteCloser` interface to enable data compression using the bzip2 format. The implementation must:  1. Provide a constructor function (e.g., `NewWriter(w io.Writer) *Writer`) that writes bzip2-compressed streams to an underlying `io.Writer`. 2. Provide configurable compression levels via a secondary constructor (e.g., `NewWriterLevel(w io.Writer, level int) (*Writer, error)`), supporting block sizes from level 1 (100k) through level 9 (900k), plus standard default constants. 3. Ensure the generated bitstream strictly adheres to the bzip2 format specification and is fully interoperable with standard bzip2 decompressors, including the package's existing `Reader`. 4. Properly flush buffered data, write appropriate CRC checksums and stream footers, and release allocated memory upon invocation of `Close()`.

issue_title: crypto/tls: add PSK support
requirement: ## Requirement: `crypto/tls` — Pre-Shared Key (PSK) Support  ### Background  Go's `crypto/tls` package currently authenticates peers exclusively with X.509 certificates (and, for TLS 1.3, via session tickets or session-ID-based resumption). It provides no way for a client and server to establish a mutually-authenticated TLS session using a shared secret that was provisioned out of band. Many constrained/embedded deployments, and protocols layered on TLS (e.g. QUIC-style session resumption, device provisioning), need this capability.  ### Requirement  Extend `crypto/tls` so that a client or server can authenticate and establish a TLS session using a **pre-shared key (PSK)** instead of — or in addition to — certificates.  #### Functional requirements  1. **PSK key exchange (TLS 1.3)**    - Support the TLS 1.3 PSK key exchange modes defined by RFC 8446: `psk_ke` (PSK only) and `psk_dhe_ke` (PSK combined with (EC)DHE).    - The specific mode is selected automatically by the server from the ciphersuite the client offers; the client must accept any offered PSK-capable ciphersuite.    - PSK-only handshakes must complete successfully **without** any certificate being presented, requested, or validated, and without the connection failing due to a missing certificate.  2. **PSK identity and secret provisioning API**    - Provide an idiomatic API in the `Config` type allowing an application to:      - supply the PSK identity and secret to use when acting as a client; and      - look up the secret associated with an offered PSK identity when acting as a server.    - The API must support multiple concurrent PSK identities on the server side, and must allow the application to reject an identity (returning a distinct, inspectable error) rather than only receiving a generic handshake failure.    - The API must be usable with `tls.Client`/`tls.Server` over arbitrary `net.Conn`s, and must not require any change to the `net/http` server's default configuration other than what the application explicitly opts into.  3. **PSK-based session resumption**    - When a TLS 1.3 connection is resumed using a PSK (as opposed to a ticket or session ID), the PSK identity and the associated secret/binder used for the resumption must be communicated and matched correctly, and must not be confused with the ticket-based resumption path.    - A server must be able to accept a resumption PSK that differs from the one originally used for the full handshake, provided the identity resolves to the same secret.  4. **Correctness and security properties**    - PSK secrets must be compared in constant time and must not be leaked through error messages, logs, or `tls.ConnectionState` output.    - PSK material held in `Config` or returned by user callbacks must be zeroed by the library when it is no longer needed, and the API must document that the application remains responsible for protecting the secrets it stores.    - A PSK must be long enough for the negotiated ciphersuite/hash as required by RFC 8446 (at least 32 bytes of keying material for the default hash); shorter secrets must be rejected with a clear error rather than silently accepted.    - Unknown PSK identity on the server ⇒ the server must abort the handshake with an appropriate TLS alert (`unknown_psk_identity` for TLS 1.3) and must not fall back to certificate-based authentication for that identity.    - PSK handshakes must interoperate with, and be interoperable from, other RFC 8446-conformant implementations (verified against at least one external TLS 1.3 implementation in tests).  5. **Scope decision for TLS 1.2**    - Support for the legacy TLS 1.2 PSK ciphersuites (RFC 4279 `PSK_WITH_*`) is **not** required by this change; it may be added separately. TLS 1.2 connections continue to work as they do today (certificate-based, with tickets/session IDs), and PSK configuration must not alter TLS 1.2 behavior.    - If TLS 1.3 is disabled or not negotiated, any configured PSK must simply go unused.  6. **Non-PSK behavior must be unchanged**    - When no PSK is configured, all existing behavior — ciphersuite negotiation, certificate verification, session tickets, session-ID resumption, `ConnectionState` fields, `net/http` integration — must remain byte-for-byte compatible with the previous release.    - `ConnectionState` must expose whether the connection was authenticated by PSK and, where applicable, the PSK identity used, so applications can make authorization decisions.  #### Quality requirements  - New exported API must follow Go API conventions (doc comments on all exported identifiers, no unnecessary new exported types, `Config` fields consistent with existing style) and pass `go vet` and the standard `API`/`gofmt` checks. - The package must have unit tests covering, at minimum: successful PSK-only handshake; successful PSK + DHE handshake; server rejecting an unknown identity; client rejecting a mismatched secret; PSK resumption; interaction with certificates when both are configured; and behaviour with TLS 1.2/1.3 version negotiation. - The new handshake paths must be covered by the existing `crypto/tls` fuzz targets and must not introduce new findings. - `crypto/tls` documentation (package doc and `Config` doc) must describe PSK usage, the security model, and the relationship between PSK and certificate-based authentication.

issue_title: Feature request: Use 'trampolines' to make most of the body of a generic function non-generic
requirement: **Requirement: Reduce Code Duplication in Generic Functions via Trampolines**  The compiler or runtime shall support a trampoline mechanism that lets most of a generic function's body be compiled once as non-generic code, instead of once per type instantiation.  1. A generic function shall be split into a thin generic wrapper and a non-generic implementation. The wrapper performs only the type-dependent work (such as conversions, dispatch, or type-specific setup) and forwards control and arguments to the shared implementation. 2. The non-generic implementation shall be emitted once and shared across all instantiations whose type-dependent behavior is identical after the wrapper's work. 3. The split shall preserve the observable behavior of the original function, including return values, side effects, error and exception behavior, and argument evaluation semantics. 4. The mechanism shall apply automatically or through a clearly documented annotation, so that existing generic code requires no changes to its public interface. 5. The number of generated instances of the non-generic body shall not grow with the number of distinct type instantiations of the wrapper. 6. Compile time and generated code size for programs that instantiate the function with many types shall be measurably reduced compared with the unsplit version. 7. Runtime performance shall not regress significantly for hot paths. The added forwarding indirection shall be small, and the mechanism shall allow inlining where it is beneficial. 8. Debugging and introspection tools (such as stack traces, profilers, and reflection) shall continue to report meaningful function names and locations.

issue_title: Initializing array of Option<T> using [None; n] syntax should not require std::marker::Copy for T
requirement: The system shall support initializing arrays of Option<T> using the [None; n] syntax without requiring T to implement the std::marker::Copy trait.

issue_title: Support home and lock screen widgets
requirement: The system shall provide home screen and lock screen widgets that display key application information and allow users to access core features directly from the device's home or lock screen.

issue_title: Support soft hyphenation (line breaks at U+00AD plus rendering a hyphen at the end of the line)
requirement: Text rendering shall support soft hyphenation using U+00AD (SOFT HYPHEN). When a line break occurs at a soft hyphen, the renderer shall end the preceding line with a visible hyphen and shall not display the U+00AD character as a separate glyph. When no break occurs at that position, the soft hyphen shall remain invisible and occupy no width. Existing line-breaking and rendering behavior shall otherwise remain unchanged.

issue_title: Customizable project structure (platforms)
requirement: **REQ-001: Customizable Platform-Specific Project Structure**  The system shall provide users with the ability to configure, extend, and reorganize the directory layout and file organization for platform-specific components within a project.  1. The system shall allow users to override default source directories for each supported target platform (e.g., iOS, Android, Web, macOS, Windows, Linux), enabling arbitrary custom paths within the project root. 2. The system shall support configuration of platform-specific asset, resource, and configuration file locations, allowing these artifacts to reside in user-defined directories rather than platform-conventional locations. 3. The system shall permit the definition of additional custom platform targets beyond the default set, each associated with its own configurable directory structure and build configuration. 4. The system shall maintain full backward compatibility with standard project layouts when no custom configuration is provided, ensuring existing projects continue to function without modification. 5. The system shall validate all custom path configurations during project initialization and build processes, rejecting invalid paths, circular references, or conflicts with system-reserved directories, and providing actionable error messages identifying the specific configuration issue. 6. All development tools, including build systems, code generators, hot-reload mechanisms, and dependency resolvers, shall dynamically resolve platform-specific files and resources according to the user-defined directory structure rather than hardcoded paths. 7. The system shall provide a declarative configuration file (e.g., project manifest) where custom platform structures are defined, supporting version control and team-wide consistency.

requirement: Requirement: The system shall provide support for procedural and parametrizable audio generation.

requirement: The system shall redesign the Tilemap terrain system to improve its usability.

requirement: The system shall allow release mode builds to be run on simulators.
