issue_title: [RFC] DataLoader architecture updates and TarDataset implementation
requirement: # Software Requirement Specification  **ID:** REQ-DL-001 **Title:** Composable DataLoader Architecture Refactor and TarDataset Implementation **Type:** Functional Enhancement (Architectural) **Status:** Proposed (RFC) **Priority:** High  ---  ## 1. Background & Motivation  The current DataLoader couples data reading, transformation, batching, and parallel execution within a single monolithic component. This limits extensibility, prevents substitution of custom storage backends (e.g., remote or archive-based sources), and forces users to fully extract archived datasets (e.g., `.tar` files) to local disk before training — wasting disk space and I/O time, especially on shared filesystems that perform poorly with many small files.  ## 2. Objective  Refactor the DataLoader into a composable, pluggable pipeline, and introduce a `TarDataset` that provides random-access reading of files directly from (optionally compressed) tar archives without extraction to disk.  ## 3. Functional Requirements  - **FR-1:** The DataLoader shall separate reading, shuffling/sampling, transformation, collation, batching, and parallel dispatch into independently replaceable modules with well-defined interfaces. - **FR-2:** The DataLoader shall support pluggable storage backends (local filesystem, remote/HTTP(S), cloud object storage, tar archives) selectable without changes to user pipeline code. - **FR-3:** The refactored DataLoader shall preserve full backward compatibility with the existing public API (`Dataset`, `Sampler`, `batch_size`, `num_workers`, `collate_fn`, `pin_memory`) such that existing user code runs unmodified. - **FR-4:** `TarDataset` shall accept one or more archive paths (`.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.xz`) and expose a standard `Dataset` interface mapping indices or keys to file contents within the archive. - **FR-5:** `TarDataset` shall support lazy, random access to archive members without extracting the archive to disk. - **FR-6:** `TarDataset` shall construct a member index (offset, size, key) on first access, persist it at a user-specifiable or default location (e.g., `<archive>.index`), and reuse a valid cached index on subsequent runs. - **FR-7:** `TarDataset` shall support gzip/bzip2/xz decompression; for non-seekable compressed streams, it shall provide configurable read strategies (sequential iteration or bounded in-memory caching). - **FR-8:** `TarDataset` shall integrate with the DataLoader such that it supports shuffling, batching, multi-worker parallel loading, and both map-style and iterable-style semantics. - **FR-9:** The pipeline shall allow users to insert, replace, or reorder per-sample transforms, filters, and batching policies at any stage via a documented composition API. - **FR-10:** The system shall raise informative, typed errors for corrupt/truncated archives, missing members, and stale indexes, and shall propagate worker exceptions with original tracebacks.  ## 4. Non-Functional Requirements  - **NFR-1 (Performance):** Random access to a member of an uncompressed archive shall be O(1) after indexing; DataLoader throughput shall not regress more than 5% versus the current implementation on equivalent workloads. - **NFR-2 (Memory):** `TarDataset` shall not load entire archives into memory unless explicitly configured; per-worker memory overhead shall be bounded and configurable. - **NFR-3 (Compatibility):** The implementation shall support all currently supported Python versions and behave consistently across Linux, macOS, and Windows. - **NFR-4 (Quality):** All new components shall include unit/integration tests meeting project coverage standards, plus API documentation and usage examples.  ## 5. Acceptance Criteria  1. All existing DataLoader tests and benchmarks pass with no public API breakage. 2. A dataset stored as a single `.tar.gz` trains end-to-end without prior extraction, within 10% of the extracted-file throughput baseline. 3. Second-run startup with a cached index takes < 1 second for archives with ≥ 100,000 members. 4. Composition API and `TarDataset` documentation, examples, and tests are merged.  ## 6. Out of Scope  - Write/append operations on tar archives. - Distributed, cross-node index synchronization. - New archive formats beyond tar and its common compressed variants.

issue_title: proposal: database/sql: support a way to perform bulk actions
requirement: Requirement: Bulk Operation Support in database/sql  The database/sql package shall provide a mechanism for executing multiple statement executions as a single bulk operation, so that callers can submit a set of parameter sets for one prepared statement and receive aggregate results without issuing a separate round trip per row.  Functional requirements:  1. The API shall allow a caller to execute a prepared statement (or equivalent statement handle) against a batch of argument sets in one call, returning an aggregate result (such as total rows affected) and any error encountered. 2. The API shall be exposed through existing database/sql types (e.g., DB, Tx, Stmt, Conn) without breaking the signatures of current methods. 3. Drivers shall be able to opt in to native bulk execution by implementing an optional interface; when a driver does not implement it, database/sql shall fall back to executing the statement once per argument set within the same operation. 4. When executed inside a transaction, the bulk operation shall honor the transaction's commit and rollback semantics, such that a failure in any element either causes the whole batch to be rejected (atomic behavior when inside a transaction) or is reported in a manner the caller can inspect, as documented. 5. The API shall respect context cancellation and deadlines, stopping further execution of batch elements once the context is done and returning the context error. 6. Errors shall identify the index of the argument set that failed, when determinable, so callers can locate the offending input. 7. The API shall accept an empty batch and return a zero result without error and without contacting the server.  Non-functional requirements:  8. Argument sets shall be passed without requiring the caller to concatenate SQL text, preserving parameter binding and protection against SQL injection. 9. The feature shall add no measurable overhead to existing single-execution paths. 10. Behavior shall be documented in the package godoc, including the fallback behavior for drivers without native bulk support. 11. Existing drivers and code using Exec, Query, and Prepare shall continue to compile and behave unchanged.

issue_title: Implement a Rendering Compositor
requirement: ## Rendering Compositor  The rendering pipeline shall provide a compositor that combines already-rendered layers into a single final output image for presentation or subsequent post-processing. The compositor shall not render scene content itself.  ### Functional Requirements  1. **Layer inputs** — The compositor shall accept an ordered collection of zero or more render layers. Each layer shall reference a valid image or render target and support:    - Visibility state.    - Opacity in the range `[0.0, 1.0]`.    - Blend mode.    - A destination rectangle within the output, allowing layers of different dimensions to be positioned and scaled. The default destination rectangle shall fill the output. 2. **Composition order** — Layers shall be composited from back to front in their configured order. Changing the order or layer properties shall take effect on the next composited frame without requiring source layers to be re-rendered. 3. **Blend modes** — The compositor shall support at minimum:    - **Normal / alpha-over**    - **Additive**    - **Multiply** 4. **Alpha and color correctness** — Blending shall use premultiplied alpha and the renderer’s configured working color space, converting to the output color space only when writing the final result. For premultiplied source and destination colors, normal blending shall use:    - `Cout = Cs + Cb × (1 - As)`    - `Aout = As + Ab × (1 - As)`      Layer opacity shall be applied to the source alpha before blending. 5. **Output** — The compositor shall produce one output surface with the configured dimensions, pixel format, and color-space encoding. If no visible layers are submitted, the output shall contain the configured clear color. 6. **Viewport handling** — Content outside a layer’s destination rectangle or outside the output bounds shall be clipped. Scaling shall use the renderer’s standard texture sampling behavior. 7. **Resource lifecycle** — The compositor shall expose operations to create, configure, update, execute, and release its resources. Temporary resources shall be reused across frames where practical, and output-target resizing shall be handled without leaking resources. 8. **Validation and errors** — Invalid layer references, unsupported formats, invalid opacity values, invalid blend modes, and incompatible configurations shall produce a clear error through the rendering system’s existing error mechanism. The compositor shall not crash or present a partially written frame.  ### Acceptance Criteria  - An opaque blue layer composited beneath an opaque red layer produces red; reversing the order produces blue. - A 50%-opaque red layer over an opaque blue layer produces the expected alpha-over result within the output format’s rounding tolerance. - Additive and multiply blending produce results matching their specified formulas. - Hidden layers and layers with zero opacity contribute no pixels. - Reordering layers changes the result according to the new back-to-front order. - A layer with dimensions different from the output is mapped to its configured destination rectangle and is clipped correctly. - An empty layer list produces the configured clear color. - Invalid configurations return an error and leave the previous valid output unchanged. - Repeated create, render, resize, and release cycles do not leak graphics or CPU resources.  ### Quality Requirements  - When source layers and the output are graphics-API resources, composition shall occur without CPU readback or avoidable intermediate full-frame copies. - The compositor shall not allocate full-frame temporary buffers on every frame. - Blending operations shall have unit-test coverage, and ordering, output, and lifecycle behavior shall have integration-test coverage.

issue_title: non-negative least squares solver feature request
requirement: # Feature Requirement: Non-Negative Least Squares (NNLS) Solver  **Summary:** Add a solver that finds the vector **x** minimizing ‖**Ax** − **b**‖₂² subject to **x** ≥ 0 (componentwise), where **A** is an m×n real matrix and **b** is an m-vector.  **Motivation:** Many scientific and engineering workflows require coefficients that are physically meaningful only when non-negative, such as spectral unmixing, concentration estimation, nonnegative matrix factorization subproblems, image deblurring, and constrained regression. Users currently must implement these solutions manually or use unconstrained least squares followed by clipping, which yields incorrect solutions. A built-in solver provides a correct, tested, and reusable implementation.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **FR-1 (API):** Provide a public function (e.g., `nnls(A, b, *, max_iter=None, tol=None)`) that accepts a dense 2-D array-like `A` of shape (m, n) and a 1-D array-like `b` of shape (m,), and returns a 1-D array `x` of shape (n,) and the residual norm ‖**Ax** − **b**‖₂. 2. **FR-2 (Constraint):** The returned solution must satisfy x_i ≥ 0 for all i, with no negative components, including values within floating-point rounding (exact zeros are permitted). 3. **FR-3 (Optimality):** The solution must satisfy the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions within tolerance: the gradient **w** = **Aᵀ**(**b** − **Ax**) satisfies w_i ≤ tol for all i, and w_i · x_i ≈ 0 (complementary slackness). 4. **FR-4 (Algorithm):** Implement the Lawson-Hanson active-set algorithm (or an equivalent exact method) as the default. The algorithm must terminate in a finite number of iterations for well-posed inputs. 5. **FR-5 (Input handling):** Accept `A` with m ≥ n or m < n. Accept `b` as a vector only; reject mismatched shapes with a clear `ValueError` naming the expected and received dimensions. 6. **FR-6 (Validation):** Reject inputs containing NaN or infinite values with a `ValueError`. 7. **FR-7 (Edge cases):** Correctly handle: `b` with all non-positive entries (solution should be x = 0 when **Aᵀb** ≤ 0 componentwise); zero matrix **A**; rank-deficient **A**; and n = 1. 8. **FR-8 (Convergence control):** Expose `max_iter` (default scales with n, e.g., 3n) and `tol` (default based on machine epsilon and matrix norm). On reaching `max_iter`, raise a convergence warning or error, configurable by the caller, and return the best iterate found. 9. **FR-9 (Optional, sparse input):** Accept `scipy.sparse` matrices when the backing library supports it, or document that only dense input is supported in this release. 10. **FR-10 (Optional, weights):** Optionally accept a weight vector w ≥ 0 to solve the weighted problem minimizing ‖diag(w)(**Ax** − **b**)‖₂² with **x** ≥ 0. (Mark as out of scope if not needed for the initial release.)  **Non-Functional Requirements**  - **NFR-1 (Correctness):** Results must match a reference implementation (e.g., `scipy.optimize.nnls`) to within 1e-8 relative error on the provided benchmark suite. - **NFR-2 (Performance):** For m = 1000, n = 100 dense inputs, the solver must complete in under 1 second on a standard desktop CPU. - **NFR-3 (Numerical stability):** Use orthogonal factorization (QR or Householder updates) for subproblem solves; do not form **AᵀA** explicitly when it would degrade the condition number. - **NFR-4 (Dependencies):** No new mandatory third-party dependencies beyond the project's existing numerical stack. - **NFR-5 (Compatibility):** Support the project's supported Python versions and floating-point dtypes (float32 and float64 at minimum).  **Acceptance Criteria**  - AC-1: All unit tests pass, including tests for each edge case in FR-7. - AC-2: Property-based tests confirm non-negativity and KKT conditions on at least 500 randomly generated problems across varied shapes and conditioning. - AC-3: Benchmark results against the reference implementation are included in the PR and meet NFR-1 and NFR-2. - AC-4: API documentation includes a docstring with parameters, return values, raised exceptions, a worked example, and a reference to Lawson & Hanson (1974), *Solving Least Squares Problems*. - AC-5: The function is exported from the appropriate public module and listed in the changelog.  **Out of Scope (initial release)**  - Bounded-variable least squares (lower and upper bounds beyond zero). - Regularized NNLS (e.g., L1 or L2 penalties), unless requested separately. - GPU execution.

requirement: GDScript shall support the declaration of struct types using a `struct` keyword, defining value-semantic data types with the following characteristics:  *   **Value Semantics**: Struct instances shall be passed by value (copied) during variable assignment, function argument passing, and return values, rather than by reference as with class instances. *   **Member Support**: Structs may contain member variables (with optional default values) and member functions/methods. *   **No Inheritance**: Structs shall not support inheritance from classes or other structs, ensuring predictable value semantics and preventing object slicing. *   **Value Equality**: The equality operator (`==`) shall perform member-wise comparison of all fields to determine equality between two struct instances. *   **Instantiation**: Structs shall be instantiable via constructor syntax (e.g., `MyStruct.new(...)`) or default initialization using member default values. *   **Container Storage**: When stored within Arrays, Dictionaries, or other containers, struct values shall be stored inline (copied) rather than as references.

issue_title: Add structs in GDScript
requirement: **Requirement: Support User-Defined Structs in GDScript**  GDScript shall provide a first-class `struct` construct that lets developers define named, lightweight composite types with a fixed set of typed fields.  1. **Declaration:** Developers can declare a struct at script or class scope using a `struct` keyword, specifying a name and a list of named fields, each with an optional static type and optional default value. 2. **Instantiation:** Struct instances can be created by naming the struct and providing values for its fields, either positionally or by field name. Fields without explicit values take their declared defaults. 3. **Field access:** Fields are read and written using dot notation (`instance.field`). Accessing an undeclared field is a parse-time error when the type is statically known and a runtime error otherwise. 4. **Type checking:** When a field has a declared type, assignments to it are validated against that type using the same rules as typed variables. 5. **Value semantics:** Assigning a struct instance to another variable, or passing it as an argument, copies the instance so that modifying one does not affect the other. Structs do not carry methods or inheritance. 6. **Interoperability:** Struct instances can be used as dictionary keys only if all their fields are hashable, and they can be converted to and from `Dictionary` values explicitly. They can be serialized by existing variant serialization mechanisms. 7. **Editor and tooling:** Structs are recognized by the parser, static analyzer, and autocompletion, and their fields appear in code completion and documentation. 8. **Compatibility:** Existing GDScript code that does not use the `struct` keyword continues to parse and run without changes.

issue_title: Crate local state for procedural macros?
requirement: **Requirement: Crate-Local State for Procedural Macros**  The compiler shall provide a mechanism that allows procedural macros to maintain state that is scoped to the crate being compiled, so that a macro invoked multiple times within the same crate can share and access data across invocations.  Specifically:  1. The system shall expose an API through the `proc_macro` crate that enables a procedural macro to define and access crate-local state, such as a keyed, typed storage area (e.g., a `static` variable or an equivalent map accessible during macro expansion).  2. State created by a procedural macro during expansion shall be visible only within the compilation of the crate in which the macro is invoked; it shall not leak into, or be shared with, other crates or other concurrent compilations (including parallel invocations of the same macro in different crates).  3. The system shall guarantee that accesses to crate-local state are performed in a deterministic order consistent with the order in which the macro invocations are expanded, so that macro behavior is reproducible across builds.  4. The compiler shall ensure that crate-local state is fully reset between compilations, so that cached builds (e.g., incremental or re-compiled crates) do not observe stale state from previous compilations.  5. The system shall detect and prevent, or at minimum warn about, any use of crate-local state that would make the expansion result depend on global state (e.g., environment variables, filesystem contents), since such behavior is unsupported and non-deterministic.  6. The feature shall operate correctly with the compiler's parallel execution model, including scenarios where multiple macro invocations may be expanded concurrently within the same crate; any concurrent access to crate-local state shall be data-race-free.  7. The mechanism shall be usable without requiring the macro author to depend on external crates (e.g., `std::sync::OnceLock` patterns relying on process-global state), while remaining sound under the compiler's threading and isolation guarantees.  8. The system shall document the semantics, lifetime, and limitations of crate-local state, including its unsuitability for caching values derived from anything other than the macro's own inputs, so that macro authors can use it correctly.

issue_title: Support multiple windows for desktop shells
requirement: **Requirement: Multi-Window Support for Desktop Shells**  The desktop shell shall support the creation, management, and display of multiple application windows concurrently.  **Functional Requirements**  1. The shell shall allow users to open more than one window for the same application where the application supports multiple instances. 2. The shell shall allow windows from different applications to be open simultaneously. 3. The shell shall provide a means to switch focus between open windows using keyboard shortcuts and pointer input. 4. The shell shall display a representation of all open windows (e.g., taskbar entries, window list, or overview mode) such that each window can be identified and selected. 5. The shell shall allow windows to be minimized, maximized, restored, moved, and resized independently of one another. 6. The shell shall preserve the stacking (z-order) of windows and update it consistently when a window is focused, raised, or lowered. 7. The shell shall allow windows to be grouped or associated with a specific workspace or virtual desktop, where workspaces are supported. 8. The shell shall retain window state (position, size, and minimized/maximized status) across window close and reopen actions within the same session, where the application permits. 9. The shell shall gracefully handle the closing of any individual window without affecting other open windows.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  1. Opening or switching between windows shall not produce perceptible latency under normal load, with a target response time consistent with the shell's existing interaction benchmarks. 2. Resource consumption shall scale predictably with the number of open windows, and the shell shall remain responsive with a configurable upper bound tested at a minimum of 20 concurrent windows. 3. Multi-window behavior shall be consistent across supported display configurations, including multi-monitor setups.  **Acceptance Criteria**  - Two or more windows of the same application can be opened, focused, and closed independently. - All open windows are listed in the shell's window list or taskbar and selectable from it. - Focus switching via keyboard (e.g., Alt+Tab equivalent) cycles through all open windows in a defined order. - Closing one window does not terminate or alter the state of other open windows. - Window positions and sizes persist across close and reopen within the same session.

issue_title: [feature request] Global GPU Flag
requirement: **Requirement: Global GPU Flag**  **Title:** Provide a global configuration flag to enable or disable GPU usage across the entire application.  **Description:** The system shall support a single, globally scoped flag (e.g., `--gpu` as a command-line argument, with a corresponding `use_gpu` setting in the configuration file) that controls whether GPU acceleration is used for all supported operations.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. FR-1: The system shall accept a global flag `--gpu` (boolean, default: `false`) applicable at the top level of the CLI, which overrides any per-operation GPU settings. 2. FR-2: When the global GPU flag is enabled and a compatible GPU device is available, all supported computations (training, inference, preprocessing, etc.) shall execute on the GPU without requiring per-component configuration. 3. FR-3: When the global GPU flag is disabled, the system shall execute all operations on CPU, regardless of GPU availability. 4. FR-4: The flag shall also be settable via the configuration file and/or environment variable (e.g., `USE_GPU`), with precedence: command-line argument > environment variable > configuration file > default value. 5. FR-5: If the flag is enabled but no compatible GPU or required GPU drivers/libraries are detected, the system shall emit a clear warning and fall back to CPU execution rather than terminating. 6. FR-6: The system shall report the active compute device (GPU model/CUDA version or CPU) at startup via a log message when verbose logging is enabled. 7. FR-7: The global flag's effective value shall be queryable through an introspection command or API (e.g., `--show-config`) so users can verify the current device selection.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - AC-1: Running the application with `--gpu` on a machine with a supported GPU routes all supported operations to the GPU. - AC-2: Running the application with `--gpu` on a machine without a GPU produces a warning and completes successfully on CPU. - AC-3: Running the application without the flag defaults to CPU execution with no behavior change relative to current functionality. - AC-4: Precedence rules in FR-4 are enforced and documented in the user documentation.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  - NFR-1: Enabling or disabling the flag shall not require code changes; it must be controllable entirely through runtime configuration. - NFR-2: Documentation shall be updated to describe the flag, its precedence, and fallback behavior.

issue_title: Feature request: INT4 format support
requirement: **REQ-INT4-001: INT4 Quantization Format Support**  The system shall implement native support for INT4 (4-bit signed integer) data format for model weight storage and inference computation to enable memory-efficient deployment while preserving model accuracy.  **Functional Requirements:** - The system shall provide APIs and CLI tools to convert FP32/FP16/BF16 model weights to INT4 representation, supporting per-tensor, per-channel, and group-wise quantization (configurable group sizes: 32, 64, 128) with both symmetric and asymmetric schemes including zero-point calibration. - The system shall execute inference using INT4 data types, performing on-the-fly dequantization to FP16/BF16 during computation or utilizing hardware-accelerated INT4 matrix operations (e.g., GPU tensor cores, CPU AVX-512 VNNI, ARM NEON) where available. - The system shall support mixed-precision execution, allowing selective application of INT4 quantization to specific layers or tensor types (e.g., attention QKV projections, MLP weights) while maintaining other components in higher precision. - The system shall serialize and deserialize INT4-quantized models using standard formats (GGUF, ONNX with quantization operators, or safetensors with quantization metadata), preserving scale and zero-point parameters. - The system shall provide post-training quantization (PTQ) calibration tools that accept calibration datasets to compute optimal quantization scales minimizing accuracy degradation.  **Non-Functional Requirements:** - **Memory Efficiency:** INT4 models shall consume ≤ 25% of the memory footprint of equivalent FP16 models and ≤ 12.5% of FP32 models. - **Performance:** INT4 inference shall deliver minimum 2x throughput improvement and ≤ 50% latency compared to FP16 inference on supported hardware accelerators. - **Accuracy:** INT4 quantization shall maintain model performance within 1% of the FP16 baseline on standard benchmarks (e.g., perplexity on WikiText-2 for LLMs, top-1 accuracy on ImageNet for vision models, BLEU score for translation).  **Acceptance Criteria:** - [ ] End-to-end inference succeeds on INT4-quantized reference architectures (Transformer-based LLMs, ResNet, BERT) with measured accuracy degradation ≤ 1% versus FP16. - [ ] Memory profiling confirms model size reduction to approximately 4 bits per parameter plus negligible overhead for scales/zero-points. - [ ] Benchmark suite demonstrates ≥ 2x speedup over FP16 on target hardware (NVIDIA Ampere+ GPUs, Intel Xeon with AVX-512, or ARM v9). - [ ] Export/import round-trip preserves model outputs within numerical tolerance (±1e-5). - [ ] Documentation specifies supported hardware backends, quantization schemes, and configuration parameters (group size, symmetric/asymmetric, calibration method).

issue_title: Proc macros: ability to refer to a specific crate/symbol (something similar to `$crate`)
requirement: ## Requirement: Proc macros must be able to refer to a specific crate/symbol (an analogue of `$crate`)  ### Problem  Declarative (`macro_rules!`) macros can refer to items belonging to their own crate via the special `$crate` metavariable, which expands to a hygienic, always-correct path to the defining crate. Procedural macros currently have no equivalent facility: a proc macro that needs to emit a reference to an item defined in a particular crate must hard-code an absolute path such as `::my_crate::my_module::my_function`.  This is fragile in practice because:  - the crate name in the hard-coded path does not match the name the dependency was actually given in `Cargo.toml` (renamed dependencies, `[dependencies] alias = { package = "my-crate" }`), - the crate may be reachable only through a re-export or under a different path in the consumer's dependency graph, - the same path is wrong when the macro is used from within the defining crate itself versus from an external crate.  ### Requirement  Provide proc macros with a way to emit a path to a specific crate/symbol that is resolved correctly at expansion time, semantically equivalent to `$crate` in declarative macros.  Specifically:  1. There must be a mechanism (either in the proc-macro API itself, e.g. via the compiler-provided crate-root path, or in the accompanying path/quoting helper library) to obtain the fully-qualified path of the crate in which the macro is being expanded / the crate that defines the macro. 2. Using that mechanism, a proc macro must be able to construct a syntactically valid absolute path to any item in that crate (module, function, type, constant, trait, etc.), and to items reached through re-exports. 3. The resulting generated code must compile and behave identically regardless of:    - whether the dependency was renamed in `Cargo.toml`,    - whether the macro is invoked from inside the defining crate or from a downstream crate,    - the crate's actual hyphen/underscore name form. 4. The mechanism must interoperate with the existing token-generation facilities so that the produced path can be spliced into the macro's output without additional manual path bookkeeping.  ### Acceptance criteria  - A proc macro can emit `some::path::to::item` where `some` is resolved automatically to the defining crate, and the expansion compiles in a downstream crate that renames the dependency. - The same macro expands to a path that resolves to the local crate when used inside the defining crate (no unnecessary self-qualification that would break privacy). - The feature is documented, including how it relates to `$crate` and how it interacts with crate renaming and re-exports.

issue_title: Implement `numpy.random.choice` equivalent
requirement: # Requirement: Implement `random.choice` — Functional Equivalent of `numpy.random.choice`  **Type:** Feature / API compatibility  ## 1. Summary  The library shall provide a random-sampling function `choice`, exposed in its random-number module consistently with the existing random API (callable on the default/global generator and on user-held generator instances), that is functionally equivalent to `numpy.random.choice`: it draws random samples from a 1-D population — specified either as an integer range `[0, a)` or as an explicit 1-D array of values — with or without replacement, under a uniform or user-specified probability distribution, returning samples with a caller-defined shape.  ## 2. Required API  ``` choice(a, size=None, replace=True, p=None) -> scalar or array of samples ```  | Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---|---| | `a` | `int` or 1-D array-like | required | Population: if int `n`, population is `{0, 1, …, n−1}`; otherwise the elements of the 1-D array. | | `size` | `None`, `int`, or tuple of `int` | `None` | Output shape. `None` → a single sample; `int` → 1-D array; tuple → array of that shape with `prod(size)` samples. | | `replace` | `bool` | `True` | `True` → independent draws (elements may repeat); `False` → all samples distinct. | | `p` | 1-D array-like of float | `None` | Per-element selection probabilities; `None` → uniform distribution. |  *Scope note:* the `axis` and `shuffle` parameters of `numpy.random.Generator.choice` (NumPy ≥ 1.26, n-D sampling) are out of scope for this requirement and may be addressed in a follow-up; a multi-dimensional `a` shall raise `ValueError`.  ## 3. Functional Requirements  **FR-1 — Population handling** - FR-1.1: If `a` is a non-negative integer `n`, samples shall be drawn from `{0, 1, …, n−1}` and returned using the library's default integer dtype. - FR-1.2: If `a` is array-like, it shall be treated as a 1-D array of elements; the result dtype shall match the dtype of `a`, and returned values shall be copies, not views, of the input. - FR-1.3: If `a` is an array with more than one dimension, the function shall raise `ValueError`.  **FR-2 — Output shape** - FR-2.1: `size=None` shall return a single sample as a scalar. - FR-2.2: `size` as an integer `k` shall return a 1-D array of `k` samples. - FR-2.3: `size` as a tuple shall return an array of exactly that shape containing `prod(size)` samples; dimensions equal to 0 shall yield an empty array. - FR-2.4: Non-integer `size` (e.g., float) shall raise `TypeError`; negative dimensions shall raise `ValueError`.  **FR-3 — Replacement semantics** - FR-3.1: With `replace=True`, draws shall be independent and identically distributed; an element may appear multiple times. - FR-3.2: With `replace=False`, all returned samples shall be distinct (a random subset of the population). If the requested sample count exceeds the population size, the function shall raise `ValueError`.  **FR-4 — Probability weighting** - FR-4.1: If `p is None`, every population element shall have equal selection probability. - FR-4.2: If `p` is provided, it shall satisfy: length equal to the population size; all entries finite and ≥ 0; sum equal to 1 within an absolute tolerance of `sqrt(eps)` (≈ 1.49e-8 for float64). Each draw shall select element `i` with probability `p[i]`. - FR-4.3: With `replace=False` and `p` provided, sampling shall proceed without replacement with probabilities proportional to the remaining (not-yet-selected) weights — equivalent to sequential draws that renormalize after each selection.  **FR-5 — Error handling** (`ValueError` unless stated otherwise; error messages shall be analogous to NumPy's for the corresponding conditions) - FR-5.1: `a` is a non-integer scalar → `TypeError`; `a` is a negative integer → `ValueError`. - FR-5.2: Empty population (`a <= 0` or empty array) while at least one sample is requested → `ValueError`. When zero samples are requested (e.g., `size=0`), the call shall succeed and return an empty array of the appropriate shape. - FR-5.3: Length of `p` differs from the population size → `ValueError`. - FR-5.4: `p` contains NaN or negative entries, or its sum deviates from 1 beyond tolerance → `ValueError`. - FR-5.5: `replace=False` with requested sample count > population size → `ValueError`.  **FR-6 — Randomness and reproducibility** - FR-6.1: All random draws shall be obtained from the library's canonical RNG mechanism (the default/global generator or the generator instance on which the method is invoked), so the function participates in the library's seeding scheme. - FR-6.2: For a fixed generator state and fixed arguments, the function shall be deterministic; results shall be reproducible across runs on the same version/backend. Any cross-backend (e.g., CPU vs. GPU) stream differences shall be documented.  ## 4. Non-Functional Requirements  - NFR-1: Implementations shall use vectorized algorithms (e.g., cumulative-sum + searchsorted / inverse-CDF for weighted with-replacement sampling; partial Fisher–Yates for uniform without-replacement sampling), not per-sample host-language loops. - NFR-2: Complexity targets: O(k) for uniform with replacement; O(n + k) for uniform without replacement; O(k log n) or better for weighted with replacement; O(n + k) for weighted without replacement. - NFR-3: The function shall be documented with a docstring mirroring `numpy.random.choice` semantics (parameters, returns, raises, examples) and exported at the library's standard random-API location.  ## 5. Acceptance Criteria  - **AC-1:** Outputs conform to the shape rules of FR-2 and dtype rules of FR-1 for integer `a`, float array `a`, integer array `a`, and for `size` ∈ {None, int, tuple, tuple containing 0}. - **AC-2:** For `replace=False` across many seeds, outputs contain no duplicates; for uniform `p=None`, the subset distribution matches uniform random subset selection (statistical test). - **AC-3:** With `p = [0.5, 0.3, 0.2]` and 100,000 with-replacement samples, empirical frequencies are within ±0.01 of `p` and a chi-square goodness-of-fit test passes at the 99% confidence level; with `p=None`, frequencies are approximately uniform. - **AC-4:** Each condition in FR-5 raises the specified exception type (parameterized tests over all cases). - **AC-5:** Identical seed and arguments produce identical outputs; distinct seeds produce distinct outputs. - **AC-6:** The function is accessible at the documented API path with a complete docstring, and all documented examples execute correctly.

issue_title: [libs] Add `TcpStream::keepalive` and `TcpStream::set_keepalive`
requirement: ## Requirement  Add TCP keepalive inspection and configuration methods to `std::net::TcpStream`:  ```rust pub fn keepalive(&self) -> io::Result<Option<std::time::Duration>>; pub fn set_keepalive(&self, keepalive: Option<std::time::Duration>) -> io::Result<()>; ```  ### Behavior  - `keepalive()` reports the effective TCP keepalive timeout:   - `Ok(None)` when keepalive is disabled.   - `Ok(Some(duration))` when keepalive is enabled, using the value actually applied by the operating system after any platform-specific rounding or normalization. - `set_keepalive(None)` disables TCP keepalive. - `set_keepalive(Some(duration))` enables TCP keepalive and configures the idle timeout after which keepalive probes are sent. - Durations must be applied using the finest resolution supported by the target platform. Any resulting effective value must be observable through `keepalive()`. - Configuration changes must apply to the underlying socket and therefore be visible to clones of the same `TcpStream`. - Both methods take `&self` and must be safe to call concurrently on a shared `TcpStream`.  ### Errors and portability  - Operating-system failures must be returned as `std::io::Error`; the methods must not panic or silently ignore failures. - If the target platform does not support querying or configuring TCP keepalive, the method must return an appropriate I/O error rather than causing a compilation failure on otherwise supported targets. - Platform limitations, supported duration granularity, and unsupported-platform behavior must be documented.  ### Validation  Tests must cover:  - Querying the initial disabled or enabled state. - Enabling keepalive with a timeout and verifying the effective value through `keepalive()` within platform resolution. - Updating an existing keepalive timeout. - Disabling keepalive and verifying that `keepalive()` returns `None`. - Error propagation for invalid configurations and unsupported platforms. - Behavior through cloned streams, confirming that the underlying socket configuration is shared.

issue_title: Make `pub` in a binary equivalent to `pub(crate)` for diagnostics
requirement: **Requirement: Treat `pub` as `pub(crate)` in binary targets when computing diagnostics**  Diagnostic visibility and reachability must be evaluated using the target's actual API surface. For items belonging to a binary target (`bin`, `example`, `test`, `bench`), a `pub` declaration must be treated as having `pub(crate)` visibility, because a binary exposes no externally consumable public API. Library targets must continue to treat `pub` as fully public.  Acceptance criteria:  1. Effective-visibility/reachability calculations used by diagnostics must downgrade `pub` to crate-level visibility for all items in binary targets, and leave `pub` unchanged for library targets. 2. Unused-item (dead code) diagnostics: an unused `pub` item in a binary target must be reported as never used, identically to an equivalent item declared `pub(crate)`; library targets must retain the current behavior where publicly reachable items are not reported. 3. Public-reachability diagnostics (e.g., reporting `pub` items that are unreachable/publicly unnameable) must not flag items in binary targets solely because they are declared `pub`; such diagnostics remain active for library targets. 4. Diagnostics that compare an item's visibility against the visibility of entities in its signature (e.g., private-in-public checks) must use the same downgraded visibility. 5. The change applies only to the diagnostic visibility model; user-written code is not rewritten, and non-diagnostic IDE behavior (navigation, completion, symbol indexing) is out of scope for this requirement.

issue_title: plugin: Add support for closing plugins
requirement: **Requirement: Support Explicit Closing of Plugins**  The plugin framework shall provide a mechanism to close (deactivate and release resources held by) a loaded plugin without requiring the host application to terminate.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  1. A caller can request closing of a specific loaded plugin by its identifier through a documented API, command, or interface. 2. Upon a close request, the framework invokes the plugin's shutdown or cleanup hook, if one is defined, before releasing the plugin. 3. Closing a plugin releases its associated resources, including event listeners, registered callbacks, background tasks, file handles, and network connections, so that none remain active after closing. 4. A closed plugin no longer receives events, hooks, or invocations from the host application. 5. Closing a plugin that is not loaded or is already closed returns a clear, non-fatal result or error and does not affect other plugins or the host application. 6. If the plugin's cleanup hook fails or times out, the framework logs the failure, still performs forced release of the plugin's registered resources, and reports the failure to the caller. 7. Closing one plugin does not alter the state, configuration, or availability of other loaded plugins. 8. The plugin's closed state is observable through the framework's status or query interface. 9. Closing is reversible in that the plugin can be loaded again after being closed, provided its load conditions are still met. 10. Unit and integration tests cover normal close, close of an unloaded plugin, close with a failing cleanup hook, and reload after close.

requirement: The standard library shall provide a `contains_ref` method on slices `[T]` (and thus accessible on `Vec<T>` via deref coercion) with the signature `pub fn contains_ref<U: ?Sized>(&self, x: &U) -> bool where T: PartialEq<U>`, which returns `true` if any element `e` in the collection satisfies `e == *x` under the `PartialEq<U>` implementation of `T`, and `false` otherwise. This method shall be documented as a less restrictive alternative to `Vec::contains` (which requires `x: &T` with `T: PartialEq<T>`), enabling containment checks with search values of type `U` distinct from the element type `T` whenever `T: PartialEq<U>`, while explicitly noting that the additional generic parameter `U` may result in worse type inference at call sites compared to `contains`.

issue_title: Feature Requst: Add regex support to test filters
requirement: Requirement: Regular Expression Support in Test Filters  The test runner shall support regular expression patterns in test filter arguments so that users can select tests whose names match a given pattern.  Functional requirements:  1. The test filter option shall accept a regular expression as its argument, in addition to any existing plain-text or glob-style matching behavior. 2. A test shall be selected for execution if its full name (including any suite or group name, as applicable) matches the supplied regular expression. 3. Matching shall be performed as a search (the pattern may match any substring of the test name) unless the pattern is explicitly anchored by the user with standard regex anchors such as ^ and $. 4. Regex syntax shall follow a widely recognized dialect, and the dialect used shall be documented. 5. If the supplied pattern is syntactically invalid, the test runner shall terminate without running any tests and shall display a clear error message identifying the invalid pattern and the reason for the failure. 6. Multiple filter patterns, where supported, shall be combined so that a test is selected if it matches any of the provided patterns. 7. Matching shall be case-sensitive by default, with an option available to enable case-insensitive matching. 8. When no test names match the supplied pattern, the test runner shall report that zero tests were selected and exit according to its existing behavior for empty test selections. 9. Existing filter behavior shall remain unchanged for users who do not use regex features, and no existing command-line options shall be broken.

issue_title: Add "refactor" tooling to rename symbols in the script editor
requirement: **Feature: Symbol Rename Refactoring in the Script Editor**  The script editor shall provide a refactoring tool that renames a symbol (such as a variable, function, class, or constant) and updates all of its references within the project.  **Requirements:**  1. **Invocation:** Users shall be able to trigger rename from the editor via a context menu entry, a keyboard shortcut, and the command palette. The action shall apply to the symbol under the caret or the current selection.  2. **Input:** Upon invocation, the editor shall display an input field pre-populated with the current symbol name, with the text selected for immediate overwriting.  3. **Scope of Changes:** The rename shall update the symbol's declaration and all references to it that resolve to the same definition. References that merely share the same identifier text but resolve to a different symbol (e.g., shadowed variables, same-named members in unrelated classes) shall not be modified.  4. **Cross-File Support:** Where the symbol is accessible from other files in the project, the rename shall update references in those files as well.  5. **Validation:** Before applying changes, the tool shall verify that the new name:    - is a valid identifier for the script language,    - is not a reserved keyword,    - does not conflict with an existing symbol in the same scope.    If validation fails, the tool shall display an error message and make no changes.  6. **Preview:** The tool shall show a preview of all affected locations (file, line, and surrounding text) before applying, allowing the user to confirm or cancel.  7. **Atomicity:** All changes shall be applied as a single undoable operation. If any file fails to write, the entire operation shall be rolled back and the user notified.  8. **Unsaved Files:** Open files with unsaved modifications shall be included in the rename, and their in-editor buffers updated without requiring a save.  9. **Feedback:** After completion, the editor shall report the number of occurrences and files changed.  **Non-Goals:** Renaming of files or directories, and renaming across external dependencies outside the project, are out of scope for this feature.

issue_title: encoding/xml: add support for xml version 1.1
requirement: ## Requirement: Add XML 1.1 support to `encoding/xml`  The `encoding/xml` package shall support parsing documents whose XML declaration specifies `version="1.1"`, using the existing decoder APIs without requiring a new public API or opt-in flag.  ### Functional requirements  1. **XML 1.1 declarations:** `xml.Decoder.Token`, `xml.Decoder.Decode`, and `xml.Unmarshal` shall accept XML declarations containing `version="1.1"` instead of reporting an unsupported-version error. 2. **Version-specific parsing:** Within the package’s existing feature set, the decoder shall apply XML 1.1 character validation and normalization rules when processing an XML 1.1 document, and retain XML 1.0 rules for XML 1.0 documents.    - XML 1.1 numeric character references for permitted restricted control characters shall be accepted.    - Literal restricted control characters shall be rejected in XML 1.1 documents.    - The NUL character shall remain invalid.    - XML 1.1 line-ending normalization shall be applied as specified by the XML 1.1 standard. 3. **Invalid input:** XML declarations specifying an unsupported version shall continue to be rejected with a non-nil error. XML 1.1 input containing characters or references prohibited by the standard shall also be rejected. 4. **Scope:** This requirement does not introduce DTD processing, custom entity expansion, or other XML capabilities that `encoding/xml` does not currently provide. 5. **Compatibility:** Existing XML 1.0 parsing behavior, error handling, and public APIs shall remain backward compatible.  ### Acceptance criteria  - A minimal XML 1.1 document decodes successfully through `Decoder`, `Decode`, and `Unmarshal`. - Tests cover XML 1.1-specific character-reference behavior, rejection of prohibited literal characters, and XML 1.1 line-ending handling. - Tests verify that unsupported versions remain rejected. - Existing XML 1.0 and malformed-input tests continue to pass.

issue_title: Inclusive version of take_while
requirement: Requirement: Inclusive take_while Operation  Provide an inclusive variant of the take_while operation that returns elements from the start of a sequence (or iterable) up to and including the first element for which the given predicate returns true, after which iteration stops.  Behavior: - Input: a sequence or iterable and a predicate function. - Output: a sequence or iterator yielding each element in order while the predicate has not yet matched, including the first element that satisfies the predicate. - Once an element satisfies the predicate, no further elements are consumed or yielded. - If no element satisfies the predicate, all elements are yielded. - If the input is empty, the output is empty. - The predicate is evaluated lazily, element by element, so that infinite or lazily generated inputs are supported when a match occurs. - The original input is not modified.  Contrast with take_while: the standard take_while excludes the matching element; this variant includes it.

issue_title: Expo like tool for flutter
requirement: ## Requirement: Expo-Like Development and Distribution Tool for Flutter  ### Objective  Provide a Flutter-native toolchain that gives developers a managed, Expo-style workflow for creating, previewing, building, and updating mobile applications. The tool must integrate with the standard Flutter SDK and `pub` ecosystem without requiring developers to replace Flutter or manually configure common native project settings.  ### Functional Requirements  1. **Project and Configuration Management**    - Provide a CLI to create, initialize, and configure Flutter projects.    - Support a declarative configuration file for application identifiers, display names, icons, splash screens, permissions, environment variables, and native plugins.    - Generate and update Android and iOS project configuration from the manifest.    - Preserve application-specific native code when regenerating managed configuration.  2. **Development and Preview**    - Build and run applications on Android emulators, iOS simulators, and physical devices.    - Support hot reload, hot restart, device logs, and a development menu.    - Provide an installable development client capable of loading the project configuration and compatible development builds.  3. **Build and Release**    - Produce debug, profile, and release artifacts, including Android App Bundles/APKs and iOS IPAs.    - Integrate signing credentials and configuration for reproducible release builds.    - Validate configuration and dependencies before starting a release build.    - Allow integration with CI systems and, where supported, managed build infrastructure.  4. **Over-the-Air Updates**    - Publish Dart code and asset updates to existing installations without requiring a new store submission.    - Sign update artifacts and validate compatibility against the target Flutter runtime and application version.    - Support rollout controls, update history, and rollback.    - Reject updates that require native binary or dependency changes.  5. **Compatibility and Extensibility**    - Support current stable Flutter and Dart releases.    - Remain compatible with standard Flutter packages and plugins.    - Allow developers to add or extend native functionality through configuration or custom native projects.    - Document installation, configuration, development, build, signing, publishing, and update-management workflows.  ### Acceptance Criteria  - A developer can create a Flutter project, configure a native plugin and permissions, and run it on an emulator or simulator using only documented CLI commands. - A developer can produce a signed, store-ready Android or iOS release artifact from the same project. - A published over-the-air update reaches an eligible installed application without store resubmission, while an incompatible update is rejected. - A failed build or update does not replace the last known-good application version. - Existing Flutter applications can adopt the tool without rewriting application source code.

The feature shall not break existing documentation builds. 6. **Tooling:** Per-parameter documentation shall be available in rustdoc JSON output so that downstream tools can consume it. 7. **Lint behavior:** Undocumented parameters shall not produce errors by default; an optional lint may be provided to warn on missing parameter documentation.

issue_title: Expose a zero allocation API to Godot C# bindings
requirement: **Requirement: Zero-Allocation API for Godot C# Bindings**  The Godot C# bindings shall provide an API surface that allows callers to perform engine operations without incurring managed heap allocations on the hot path. Specifically:  1. Methods that currently return newly allocated managed objects (such as arrays, strings, collections, or wrapper structs) shall offer overloads or alternative signatures that write results into caller-provided buffers, spans, or pre-allocated instances. 2. Where applicable, these APIs shall use `Span<T>`, `ReadOnlySpan<T>`, `Memory<T>`, or `ref`/`out` parameters to pass data without copying or allocating. 3. Existing allocating APIs shall remain available and unchanged for backward compatibility. 4. The zero-allocation APIs shall not introduce additional allocations in steady-state usage, including boxing, closures, temporary arrays, or implicit string creation. 5. Documentation shall identify which APIs are zero-allocation, describe their usage patterns (such as buffer reuse), and note any remaining allocation sources. 6. Correctness shall be verified by tests that measure managed allocations (e.g., via GC allocation counters) during invocation of the zero-allocation APIs and assert zero bytes allocated after warm-up.

issue_title: cmd/go: subcommand as git merge tool for go.mod merge conflicts
requirement: **Requirement: Git Merge Driver for go.mod and go.sum Conflicts**  The `go` command shall provide a subcommand that can be registered as a Git custom merge driver to automatically resolve merge conflicts in `go.mod` and `go.sum` files.  1. **Invocation:** The subcommand shall accept the three file arguments Git passes to a merge driver (ancestor `%O`, current `%A`, other `%B`) and, where applicable, the conflict marker size (`%L`) and merge path (`%P`).  2. **Merge behavior for `go.mod`:** The subcommand shall perform a semantic three-way merge of module directives, including `require`, `exclude`, `replace`, `retract`, `go`, `toolchain`, and `godebug`, rather than a line-based text merge. It shall:    - Combine non-conflicting additions and removals from both sides.    - Resolve a `require` conflict on the same module path by selecting the higher required version when both sides only upgraded the version, consistent with Minimal Version Selection.    - Report an unresolvable conflict (for example, both sides set incompatible `replace` directives for the same module) by exiting with a nonzero status and leaving conflict markers or an explicit error.  3. **Merge behavior for `go.sum`:** The subcommand shall union the checksum entries from both sides, remove duplicate lines, and sort the result in the canonical order used by `go mod tidy`.  4. **Post-merge normalization:** After merging `go.mod`, the subcommand shall reformat the file to canonical form. It shall not perform network access by default. An optional flag shall allow running `go mod tidy` equivalent logic when explicitly requested.  5. **Exit status:** The subcommand shall exit with status 0 when the merge fully succeeds and a nonzero status when manual resolution is required, so Git marks the file as conflicted.  6. **Configuration support:** Documentation and a helper (such as a `go mod merge-driver install` or equivalent) shall show how to add the driver to `.gitattributes` (for example, `go.mod merge=gomod`) and `.git/config` or `~/.gitconfig` (`merge.gomod.driver`).  7. **Compatibility:** The subcommand shall work on all platforms supported by the `go` command and with Git versions that support custom merge drivers, and it shall not change the behavior of existing `go` subcommands.  8. **Testing:** Automated tests shall cover non-overlapping edits, same-version upgrades, conflicting replace directives, `go.sum` union with duplicates, and the nonzero exit path for unresolvable conflicts.

issue_title: Improve the performance of the GDScript VM
requirement: **Requirement: Improve GDScript Virtual Machine Performance**  The GDScript VM shall execute scripts with lower CPU time and memory overhead than the current implementation, without changing observable language semantics.  **Scope** - Reduce per-instruction dispatch and operand-handling overhead in the bytecode interpreter. - Reduce overhead from common runtime operations, including function calls, member and property access, variant type conversions, and arithmetic and comparison operations on built-in types. - Reduce unnecessary allocations and copies during script execution.  **Requirements** 1. All existing GDScript language behavior, including results, error messages, and error conditions, must remain unchanged. The existing test suite must pass without modification to expected outputs. 2. A benchmark suite covering representative workloads (tight loops, recursive function calls, property access, and array and dictionary manipulation) must be established before optimization, and used to measure results before and after each change. 3. Each optimization must show a measurable improvement on at least one benchmark. Changes with no measurable benefit or with a regression on other benchmarks must not be merged. 4. Performance must not regress on any benchmark in the suite beyond an agreed tolerance. 5. Memory usage during script execution must not increase for any benchmark workload. 6. Optimizations must not compromise debuggability: breakpoints, stack traces, and script error reporting must continue to function correctly. 7. Optimizations must work across all supported platforms and build configurations, including debug and release builds.  **Acceptance Criteria** - The benchmark suite shows a documented, reproducible speedup over the baseline on the target workloads. - All existing automated tests pass on all supported platforms. - No new memory leaks or undefined behavior are introduced, as verified by sanitizer runs.

issue_title: Enable "hot reload" (not just "hot restart") for Flutter Web
requirement: ## Requirement: Hot Reload Support for Flutter Web  The Flutter SDK shall provide hot reload for applications running on the web as a distinct operation from hot restart.  ### Functional requirements  - The standard `flutter run` workflow for supported web devices, including browser and `web-server` targets, shall accept the existing hot reload command (`r`). - When hot reload is requested, the SDK shall recompile changed Dart source code as needed and apply those changes to the running web application. - Hot reload shall not be implemented as an alias for hot restart or as a full application restart that discards runtime state. - Hot reload shall preserve application state in the same manner as hot reload on supported native Flutter targets, including the current route, navigation state, and widget or application state not invalidated by the source change. - The existing hot restart command (`R`) shall remain available for web applications and shall continue to reset application state. - Compilation or hot-reload failures shall produce actionable diagnostics and leave the last successfully running application usable. - Terminal output shall clearly distinguish a successful hot reload from a hot restart. - The capability shall apply to web targets and browsers supported by the SDK. Any documented limitations shall be reported when the workflow starts.  ### Acceptance criteria  1. A developer can start a web application with `flutter run`, navigate to a screen, modify Dart application or widget code, and press `r` to see the changes without manually refreshing the browser. 2. After hot reload, the current route and applicable runtime state remain intact. 3. Pressing `R` still performs a hot restart and resets application state, demonstrating that hot reload and hot restart are separate operations. 4. Introducing a compilation error during hot reload reports the error without terminating the previously working application. 5. Release builds and existing hot reload behavior on native Flutter targets are unaffected.

requirement: **Requirement: Support for Unsigned Integer Types `uint16`, `uint32`, and `uint64`**  The software shall support the unsigned fixed-width integer types `uint16`, `uint32`, and `uint64` as first-class data types. Specifically:  1. **Type availability:** Users shall be able to declare, store, and manipulate values of type `uint16`, `uint32`, and `uint64` wherever existing numeric types are supported. 2. **Value range:** Each type shall represent the full unsigned range of its width, i.e., 0 to 65,535 for `uint16`, 0 to 4,294,967,295 for `uint32`, and 0 to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615 for `uint64`. 3. **Arithmetic and comparison:** The standard arithmetic, bitwise, and comparison operations defined for integer types shall be supported for these types, with well-defined wraparound (modular) behavior on overflow and underflow. 4. **Conversion:** Explicit conversion between these types and other integer and numeric types shall be supported. Conversions that cannot represent the source value shall follow a documented, consistent behavior (e.g., truncation or raising an error) rather than undefined behavior. 5. **Serialization and interoperability:** Values of these types shall be correctly serialized and deserialized in all supported input/output formats, and shall be usable in any interfaces that accept integer parameters or return values. 6. **Error handling:** Invalid literals or out-of-range values supplied as input shall be rejected with a clear error message. 7. **Documentation and testing:** The new types shall be documented, and automated tests shall cover range boundaries, overflow behavior, conversions, and serialization for each type.

issue_title: Support Firefox as a browser in flutter run
requirement: ## Requirement: Support Firefox as a run/debug target in `flutter run`  ### Motivation Flutter web applications can only be launched and debugged in a browser context from the CLI via Chrome (and, indirectly, Edge). Developers who use Firefox as their primary browser — and users of platforms where Chrome is unavailable or restricted — have no way to run, hot-reload, or debug a Flutter web app in Firefox from `flutter run`. Flutter should treat Firefox as a first-class web browser device.  ### Scope Add a Firefox web browser device to the Flutter tool's device discovery and run/debug flow, on all supported host platforms (macOS, Linux, Windows).  ### Functional requirements  1. **Device discovery**    - `flutter devices` must report a Firefox device when a supported Firefox installation is detected on the host (e.g. via the standard install locations / `which firefox` / registry lookup on Windows).    - The device entry must be clearly identified as Firefox and distinguish it from other web devices (Chrome, Edge, `web-server`).  2. **Run and launch**    - `flutter run -d firefox` must build the web application for the web (`web`/`wasm`) target, start the local development server, and launch a Firefox browser window pointing at the served application.    - The launched Firefox instance must use a dedicated, isolated temporary profile directory so that the user's existing Firefox profile, extensions, and settings are not modified or corrupted. The profile must be cleaned up when the run session ends.    - The launch must honor the existing web run options, including `--web-hostname`, `--web-port`, `--web-launch-url`, and the VM-service port/device-id options, with the same semantics as the Chrome device.  3. **Hot reload / hot restart**    - Source-code edits must trigger a hot reload in the running Firefox instance, and `r` / `R` in the CLI must trigger hot restart, with the same reliability and latency characteristics as the existing Chrome device.  4. **Debugging and DevTools**    - The tool must attach to the Dart VM service exposed by the application running in Firefox, enabling breakpoints, stepping, inspect/widget inspection, and the "open DevTools" / `flutter attach` workflow.    - Debugging must work through the standard VM service connection path used for other web devices (no Firefox-specific plugin required).  5. **Compatibility of the built artifact**    - The generated web application must be built in a form that runs correctly in Firefox: the default web renderer used by `flutter run` must be supported by Firefox, and renderer selection flags (e.g. `html`, `canvaskit`, `skwasm`) must be validated so that an unsupported combination fails fast with an explanatory message instead of a blank page.  6. **Error handling**    - If no Firefox installation is found, `flutter run -d firefox` must fail with a clear, actionable message stating that Firefox was not detected and how to install it or how to specify an explicit executable path.    - If a Firefox executable is explicitly provided (e.g. via an environment variable or flag), that executable must be used in preference to auto-detection.  7. **Non-regression**    - Existing behavior for `flutter run -d chrome`, `-d edge`, `-d web-server`, and `flutter run -d <device>` on mobile/desktop must be unchanged.    - Existing web tooling (build, serve, `flutter build web`) must not be affected.  ### Acceptance criteria - On a host with Firefox installed: `flutter devices` lists a Firefox device; `flutter run -d firefox` compiles the app, launches Firefox with an isolated profile, and displays the running application. - Editing a widget's source triggers an automatic hot reload in the Firefox window; `r` and `R` perform hot restart. - Setting a breakpoint in a Dart file and relaunching hits the breakpoint and exposes correct variable values via the VM service / DevTools. - On a host without Firefox: `flutter run -d firefox` exits with a non-zero status and a message explaining how to install Firefox or point to an explicit executable. - `flutter run -d chrome` and `flutter run -d web-server` continue to behave as before on all supported host platforms.  ### Out of scope - Native Firefox (Gecko) rendering of Flutter desktop applications. - Firefox for Android / iOS as a `flutter run` target. - Installing or updating Firefox on the user's machine automatically.

issue_title: non-negative least squares solver feature request
requirement: **Requirement: Non-negative Least Squares (NNLS) Solver**  The software shall provide a solver for the non-negative least squares problem:  minimize ‖Ax − b‖₂ subject to x ≥ 0,  where A is an m×n real-valued matrix, b is a length-m real-valued vector, and x is the unknown length-n solution vector.  Specific requirements:  1. **Interface.** The solver shall expose a callable of the form `nnls(A, b, maxiter=None, atol=None)` that accepts:    - `A`: array-like of shape (m, n), the design/coefficient matrix.    - `b`: array-like of shape (m,), the target vector.    - `maxiter`: optional positive integer limit on iterations, defaulting to a sensible value derived from problem size (e.g., 3·n).    - `atol`: optional positive convergence tolerance on the change in the objective/residual, defaulting to machine-precision-scaled value.  2. **Return values.** The solver shall return:    - `x`: array of shape (n,) satisfying x ≥ 0 to within numerical tolerance.    - `rnorm`: the Euclidean norm of the residual ‖Ax − b‖₂ at the returned solution.    - A termination status/message indicating success, iteration limit exceeded, or invalid input.  3. **Algorithm.** The solver shall implement the Lawson–Hanson active-set algorithm (or a mathematically equivalent method) that terminates in a finite number of iterations and returns a solution satisfying the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions (feasibility, stationarity, complementarity) up to numerical precision.  4. **Robustness.** The solver shall handle rank-deficient and ill-conditioned A by returning a valid non-negative solution and shall detect and report failure to converge within `maxiter` without raising an unhandled exception.  5. **Input validation.** The function shall raise descriptive errors for non-finite entries (NaN/Inf), dimensionally incompatible `A` and `b`, empty inputs, or non-positive `maxiter`/`atol` values.  6. **Documentation.** The feature shall include a complete docstring covering parameters, returns, algorithmic references (Lawson & Hanson, *Solving Least Squares Problems*, 1974/1995), notes on computational complexity, and at least one usage example.  7. **Testing.** The implementation shall be accompanied by unit tests verifying: (a) exact recovery of known non-negative solutions; (b) correctness on random dense problems by checking KKT conditions; (c) boundary cases including b = 0, x = 0 solutions, and n > m; and (d) proper error handling for invalid inputs.

issue_title: Add Vec::contains_ref which is worse for inference but less restrictive than Vec::contains
requirement: **Requirement: Add `Vec::<T>::contains_ref` as a more permissive alternative to `Vec::contains`**  The standard library shall provide a method `contains_ref` on `Vec<T>` with the signature:  ```rust pub fn contains_ref<U: ?Sized>(&self, x: &U) -> bool where     T: PartialEq<U>; ```  1. **Behavior:** `contains_ref` returns `true` if any element `e` in the vector satisfies `e == *x` using `PartialEq<U>` for `T`, and `false` otherwise. It shall return `false` for an empty vector. 2. **Relationship to `contains`:** `contains_ref` shall accept every call that `contains` accepts, and it shall additionally accept comparisons where `T: PartialEq<U>` with `U != T` (for example, `Vec<String>` searched with `&str`). `Vec::contains` remains unchanged. 3. **Inference:** The method may require explicit type annotations in cases where `U` cannot be uniquely determined from the argument. This tradeoff is accepted and shall be documented. 4. **Bounds:** The method shall not require `T: Clone`, `T: Sized` beyond what `Vec<T>` already implies, or any additional trait beyond `PartialEq<U>`. 5. **Documentation:** Rustdoc shall state that `contains_ref` is less restrictive but less inference-friendly than `contains`, and shall include an example using a type pair with a cross-type `PartialEq` impl. 6. **Stability:** The method shall be introduced behind a feature gate until its naming and API are approved through the standard library API process. 7. **Testing:** Tests shall cover an empty vector, a matching element, a non-matching element, and a cross-type comparison (e.g., `Vec<String>` with `&str`). Tests shall also include a case that fails to compile with `contains` and compiles with `contains_ref`.

issue_title: Rework the Tilemap terrain system to improve its usability
requirement: ## Requirement: Reworked Tilemap Terrain System  ### Summary The terrain (autotiling / terrain-brush) functionality of the Tilemap must be reworked so that authoring terrain-based maps is straightforward, discoverable, and error-resistant. The current terrain workflow requires users to assemble and maintain terrain rules manually in a way that is difficult to understand and produces silent or cryptic failures. The rework must preserve the ability to define terrain rules and to have tiles automatically select the correct art based on neighboring terrain.  ### Goals 1. **Simplify terrain definition.** Provide a single, coherent place in the editor to define terrain sets, terrain members, and their matching rules, instead of scattering this data across unrelated resources and dialogs. 2. **Make rule semantics explicit.** Users must be able to read, at a glance, what a rule matches (e.g. corners only, edges only, corners and edges, any neighbor) and how conflicting or overlapping rules are resolved. 3. **Improve the painting experience.** Terrain painting must be responsive, support brush sizes and rectangular fills, show the resulting tile art while dragging, and never require the user to guess what will be applied. 4. **Prevent silent mistakes.** Unresolvable or contradictory rule configurations must be detected and reported with an actionable message (including which terrain and which neighbor is problematic) rather than producing arbitrary or blank output. 5. **Support undo/redo and non-destructive edits.** All terrain authoring operations — rule changes, terrain set edits, and painting — must be fully undoable and redoable.  ### Functional Requirements - **FR-1 Terrain sets:** A terrain set is a named, ordered collection of terrains. A terrain declares a tile, a display name, and the list of rules that determine when the tile is drawn. - **FR-2 Rule model:** A rule specifies a matching mode and a per-side/per-corner expectation of acceptable neighbor terrains (or "ignore" / "any"). Supported modes must at minimum include: match corners, match sides, match corners and sides, and match any. - **FR-3 Rule ordering and conflict resolution:** The precedence of overlapping rules must be deterministic and documented. When no rule matches, the behavior must be configurable (fallback tile, keep existing tile, or leave empty) and stated explicitly in the UI. - **FR-4 Live preview:** While configuring a rule or dragging the terrain brush, the editor must preview the tile art that would be selected. - **FR-5 Validation:** On applying or editing a terrain set, the editor must validate all rules and report errors and warnings (e.g. no matching rule for the base terrain, unreachable terrains, duplicate or contradictory rules) with a clear location and description. - **FR-6 Bulk and pattern operations:** Users must be able to apply a terrain to a single cell, a rectangular region, a stroke, or the entire map, and to fill holes/infer missing terrain boundaries in a region. - **FR-7 Performance:** Terrain recomputation for a region edit must complete without perceptible stalls on maps of the project's target size, and must be incremental where only the affected region is re-evaluated. - **FR-8 Compatibility:** Existing terrain sets and maps authored with the previous terrain system must load without data loss, either directly or via an explicit, documented conversion step.  ### Non-Functional Requirements - The terrain workflow must be usable without reading documentation; required concepts must be labeled in plain language with tooltips. - Configuration and rule data must be serialized in a versioned, human-readable format suitable for version control. - Any behavior changes relative to the previous system must be covered by automated tests, including rule-matching unit tests and regression tests for previously authored maps.  ### Acceptance Criteria 1. A new user can create a terrain set, define two terrains with a corner-and-sides rule, and paint terrain on a map that automatically selects the correct corner/edge/inner tiles — without consulting external instructions. 2. A rule that cannot match any terrain in the set is reported as an error naming the offending rule and terrain. 3. Painting a terrain, editing a rule, and reordering rules are all undoable and redoable, and undo restores the exact previous map and terrain-set state. 4. Every terrain set saved by the previous system loads and renders identically after the rework, or the user is given an explicit, actionable conversion prompt. 5. Automated tests cover each matching mode, tie-breaking between overlapping rules, and the "no rule matched" fallback behavior.
