issue_title: Provide UnixPath and WindowsPath (ditto PathBuf) on all platforms
requirement: # Requirement: Platform-Specific Path Types Available on All Platforms  ## Summary  The path-handling library shall provide the platform-specific path types `UnixPath`, `WindowsPath`, `UnixPathBuf`, and `WindowsPathBuf` on **every** supported compilation target, rather than exposing them only on their "native" platform (i.e. no `#[cfg(unix)]` / `#[cfg(windows)]` gating). The types shall always behave according to their platform's path semantics, regardless of the host OS on which the code is compiled or executed.  ## Motivation  Today, code that must handle foreign-platform paths (e.g. a build tool normalizing Windows paths on Linux, a tool archiving artifacts produced for another OS, a cross-platform configuration parser) cannot use strongly-typed path abstractions: it must fall back to raw `OsStr`/`String` manipulation or to `cfg`-gated code with duplicated logic. Making the typed variants universally available removes the need for duplicated, error-prone string-based path handling and enables shared, testable path logic.  ## Detailed Requirements  ### 1. Unconditional availability  * `UnixPath`, `UnixPathBuf`, `WindowsPath`, and `WindowsPathBuf` shall be exported from the crate root (and from any submodule currently re-exporting them) on all targets, including Linux, macOS, Windows, and non-Unix/non-Windows targets (e.g. WASI, embedded/`no_std` targets if supported). * No public item's existence shall depend on the host OS at compile time, except the explicitly documented native aliases described in §3. * The crate's public API surface shall be identical on all targets so that downstream crates can be compiled once and run anywhere without conditional compilation.  ### 2. Semantics fixed by the *type*, not by the host  * `UnixPath` / `UnixPathBuf` shall always interpret `/` as the only path separator. A `\` shall be treated as an ordinary filename character. Drive letters, UNC prefixes, and verbatim (`\\?\`) prefixes shall never be recognized or special-cased. * `WindowsPath` / `WindowsPathBuf` shall always interpret both `\` and `/` as path separators, shall recognize drive prefixes (`C:`), drive-relative paths (`C:foo`), rooted-but-drive-less paths (`\foo`), UNC shares (`\\server\share`), and verbatim/device prefixes (`\\?\C:\`, `\\.\`), and shall treat `:` as a reserved character outside of a valid drive prefix. * `is_absolute`, `is_relative`, `has_root`, `components`, `parent`, `file_name`, `file_stem`, `extension`, `strip_prefix`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `join`, `push`, `pop`, `set_extension`, `with_file_name`, `with_extension` shall follow the semantics of the type's own platform on every host. * Component iteration shall normalize `.` and `..` per the respective platform rules (no `..` collapsing across a root or symlink-free assumptions beyond platform rules; `..` after a root shall be dropped on Unix-style roots and on Windows roots). * Non-UTF-8 input bytes shall be preserved losslessly; `to_str` shall return `None` for invalid sequences and `to_string_lossy` shall replace them, on all hosts.  ### 3. Relationship to the native path types  * `Path` and `PathBuf` (or their equivalents in the library) shall remain available on all targets with unchanged behavior and layout. * On Unix targets, the native path type shall be an alias of (or a zero-cost newtype over) the Unix variant; on Windows targets, of the Windows variant. `Path::new(...)`, `PathBuf::from(...)`, `Path::join`, and all existing methods shall continue to compile and behave exactly as before, with no observable behavioral change for existing users. * Lossless, allocation-free conversions shall exist in both directions between the native path type and each platform-specific type, e.g. `AsRef<UnixPath>`, `AsRef<WindowsPath>`, `From<&Path> for UnixPathBuf`, `From<PathBuf> for WindowsPathBuf`, and the inverse conversions back to the native type, plus `as_str`/`as_os_str`-style accessors that expose the underlying representation without copying. * Conversion between a Unix path and a Windows path shall **not** be provided implicitly (semantics differ); explicit, documented conversion helpers may be added but shall not silently reinterpret separators.  ### 4. API completeness and parity  * The four types shall expose a complete, documented API mirroring the native path API: construction (`new`, `from`, `with_capacity`), inspection (`as_os_str`, `to_str`, `to_string_lossy`, `to_path_buf`, `parent`, `ancestors`, `file_name`, `file_stem`, `extension`, `components`, `iter`), mutation for the owned variants (`push`, `pop`, `set_extension`, `set_file_name`, `clear`, `reserve`), and queries (`is_absolute`, `is_relative`, `has_root`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `strip_prefix`, `exists`-style helpers if the library provides them). * `Display`, `Debug`, `Clone`, `Copy` (for the borrowed variants), `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `PartialOrd`, `Ord`, `Hash`, `Default`, `Send`, `Sync`, and `UnwindSafe`/`RefUnwindSafe` shall be implemented consistently on all targets. * Optional integrations (e.g. serialization) shall support all four types on all targets, serializing as the platform-appropriate path string/byte representation.  ### 5. Compatibility, performance, and footprint  * The implementation shall not regress the performance or memory footprint of the native path types; the borrowed variants shall remain thin wrappers over the same underlying string representation with no allocation. * The change shall not modify the behavior of existing public functions, nor introduce new `unsafe` code, nor require any new mandatory dependency. * Existing downstream code that only uses the native path types shall continue to compile and pass its tests without modification.  ### 6. Documentation and testing  * Documentation shall explicitly state that the platform-specific types are available on all platforms and describe the separator/prefix rules each type follows. * The crate's test suite shall run on at least Linux, macOS, and Windows in CI, and shall include target-independent tests asserting cross-platform semantics (e.g. `WindowsPath::new(r"C:\foo/bar").is_absolute()` and `UnixPath::new(r"C:\foo/bar").file_name() == Some("bar")`). * Tests shall cover edge cases: UNC and verbatim Windows prefixes, drive-relative paths, trailing separators, `.`/`..` sequences, empty paths, and invalid UTF-8 byte sequences.  ## Acceptance Criteria  1. `use <crate>::{UnixPath, UnixPathBuf, WindowsPath, WindowsPathBuf};` compiles on every supported target with no `cfg` attributes or feature flags required. 2. A program compiled on Linux and executed on Linux/Windows (and vice versa) produces identical results for all `UnixPath`/`WindowsPath` operations listed in §2. 3. All existing tests for the native path types pass unchanged on all platforms. 4. The public API of the four types is documented and covered by the test matrix described in §6.  ## Non-Goals  * Replacing or deprecating the native `Path`/`PathBuf` types. * Providing implicit cross-platform path conversion (Unix ↔ Windows) with separator rewriting. * Changing path *resolution* semantics beyond the documented per-platform rules (e.g. no new symlink or `..` resolution behavior).

issue_title: Implement namespaces in GDScript
requirement: ## Requirement: Namespaces in GDScript  GDScript shall provide compile-time namespaces for organizing related classes and constants without requiring globally unique unqualified names.  - The language shall support namespace declarations using dot-separated identifiers and an indented declaration block:   ```gdscript   namespace Game.Combat:       const DEFAULT_HEALTH := 100        class Enemy:           extends Node2D           var health := DEFAULT_HEALTH   ``` - Namespace blocks shall be valid at script top level and shall support classes, constants, enums, and nested namespace declarations. Nested blocks and dotted declarations shall be equivalent:   ```gdscript   namespace Game:       namespace Combat:           class Enemy:               extends Node2D   ``` - Declarations in a namespace shall be addressable by their fully qualified names, such as `Game.Combat.Enemy` and `Game.Combat.DEFAULT_HEALTH`. - Namespaced classes shall be usable anywhere a class identifier is accepted, including inheritance, type hints, instantiation, static member access, and `extends`. - Name resolution shall search the current namespace, its enclosing namespaces, and then the global scope. Ambiguous references and references to unknown namespace members shall produce compiler errors with the relevant file, line, and column information. - Namespace member classes shall be registered and persisted in the global script-class cache under their fully qualified names and remain available after project reloads. - A namespace, namespace member, or fully qualified class name that conflicts with another global declaration or namespace path shall be rejected with a clear compiler error. - Namespaces shall be compile-time organizational constructs only. Creating or referencing a namespace shall not instantiate a runtime object, add a scene-tree node, or change resource paths and scene serialization. - Existing `class_name` behavior shall remain backward compatible. Unqualified global class names may coexist with namespaced classes, subject to namespace-path conflict checks. - The editor shall provide completion for namespace names and members, hover documentation, go-to-definition support, and namespace-aware symbol lookup. - The implementation shall include parser, compiler, runtime, project-reload, error-handling, and editor integration tests covering declaration syntax, qualified access, nested namespaces, name resolution, collisions, and backward compatibility.
