issue_title: Server-side rendering for Flutter web
requirement: **REQ-FLUTTER-WEB-SSR-001 — Server-Side Rendering for Flutter Web**  The Flutter web framework shall provide an opt-in server-side rendering (SSR) mode that generates, on the server, standards-compliant HTML representing the application's initial UI state and serves this HTML as the initial page response, so that meaningful content is visible to users and indexable by search engines before the Flutter engine finishes loading.  Acceptance criteria: 1. SSR shall be enabled only through explicit build/serving configuration and shall not alter the behavior, output, or performance of applications built with SSR disabled. 2. The server-rendered HTML shall accurately reflect the initial route's layout, visible text content, and images (including alternative text), and shall preserve accessibility semantics (ARIA roles, labels, heading structure). 3. The server response shall include document-level metadata (page title, meta description, Open Graph tags) suitable for search engine indexing and link previews. 4. Upon client-side initialization, the interactive Flutter application shall replace the server-rendered content with no perceptible flicker and a cumulative layout shift (CLS) of ≤ 0.1. 5. If JavaScript is disabled or the Flutter engine fails to load, the server-rendered content shall remain fully visible and legible in the browser. 6. The SSR generation step shall add no more than 100 ms median latency to the initial HTML response under representative production server load.

issue_title: Add array unpacking/destructuring to GDScript

The implementation shall support optional static type hints for unpacked variables, validate identifier bindings, emit a compile-time error when the number of target variables does not match the element count of a statically resolvable array literal, and raise a runtime error when the evaluated array length does not match the number of target variables during execution.

issue_title: Add support for variadic functions (varargs) to GDScript
requirement: # Requirement: Variadic Functions in GDScript  GDScript shall support variadic functions and methods that accept any number of trailing positional arguments.  ## Declaration syntax  - A variadic parameter shall be declared using the `...` prefix and shall always be the final parameter:   ```gdscript   func log_values(prefix: String, ...values: Array):   ``` - The same syntax and semantics shall apply to named functions, static functions, instance methods, constructors, and lambda functions. - A function shall not declare more than one variadic parameter, place a variadic parameter before other parameters, or assign a default value to a variadic parameter. Each of these cases shall produce a compile-time error with the relevant source location. - The `...` token shall not be valid in any other context and shall produce a compile-time error when misused.  ## Calling semantics  - Fixed parameters shall be matched to positional arguments according to the existing GDScript rules, including support for default values. - All arguments supplied beyond the fixed parameters shall be collected, in order, into an `Array` bound to the variadic parameter. - The variadic parameter shall always be initialized, including when no additional arguments are supplied; in that case it shall be an empty array. - Each invocation shall create a new array so that mutations of the variadic parameter do not affect the caller or subsequent invocations. - Supplying fewer arguments than required by the fixed parameters shall produce the existing call-argument-count runtime error. - The variadic parameter may be untyped or typed as `Array` or `Array[T]`. A non-array type hint shall produce a compile-time error. - When `Array[T]` is specified, every collected argument shall be checked against `T` at runtime. A type mismatch shall produce a runtime error identifying the invalid argument’s position and expected type.  ## Argument expansion and dynamic invocation  - Passing an array as a normal positional argument shall treat it as a single variadic value:   ```gdscript   log_values("x", [1, 2]) # values == [[1, 2]]   ``` - Existing `Object.callv()` and `Callable.callv()` APIs shall expand the supplied array into individual arguments when invoking a variadic GDScript function:   ```gdscript   log_values.callv(["x", 1, 2]) # values == [1, 2]   ``` - Direct calls, `Object.call()`, `Callable.call()`, `Object.callv()`, `Callable.callv()`, bound callables, and `super` calls shall all apply the same argument-matching rules to variadic GDScript functions. - Calls to `super` shall match the parent method’s signature, including collection of excess arguments by a variadic parent method.  ## Metadata and compatibility  - Variadic GDScript methods shall be identified as variadic in method metadata exposed through `get_method_list()`, using the vararg flag used for variadic built-in methods. - Existing fixed-arity GDScript functions, built-in functions, and scripts shall retain their current behavior. Adding variadic support shall not require changes to existing valid source files.  ## Documentation and tests  - The GDScript language reference shall document variadic declaration syntax, argument collection, type hints, array expansion through `callv()`, and the associated error cases. - The GDScript test suite shall cover:   - Functions with and without fixed parameters.   - Calls with zero, one, and multiple variadic arguments.   - Untyped, `Array`, and `Array[T]` variadic parameters.   - Type-mismatch and insufficient-argument errors.   - Invalid declarations, including misplaced, duplicated, and defaulted variadic parameters.   - Invocation through direct calls, `call()`, `callv()`, bound callables, and `super`.   - Isolation of the collected array between invocations.

issue_title: cmd/compile: implement powerpc 32-bit backend (ppc32)
requirement: Requirement: Add a 32-bit PowerPC (ppc32) backend to the Go compiler.  The cmd/compile toolchain shall support generating code for the 32-bit PowerPC architecture as a new target, identified by GOARCH=ppc (big-endian) and, where applicable, the corresponding little-endian variant. The backend shall:  1. Be integrated into the existing SSA-based compilation pipeline, including architecture registration, machine-specific SSA rewrite rules, instruction selection, register allocation, and code emission. 2. Correctly lower all Go types and operations on 32-bit word-sized values, including 64-bit integer arithmetic and comparisons implemented via multi-word sequences, as well as pointer and address computations using 32-bit addresses. 3. Follow the PowerPC 32-bit ABI conventions for calling, stack frame layout, register usage, and function prologue/epilogue generation, so that generated code interoperates with the runtime and assembly routines for the target. 4. Support the runtime requirements of the target, including goroutine stack management, garbage collection write barriers, atomic operations, and the memory model guarantees required by the language. 5. Provide floating-point support consistent with the target's hardware or software floating-point options. 6. Pass the existing Go compiler and runtime test suites (including codegen, run, and test directories) when built and run for the ppc32 target, with no regressions to other architectures. 7. Be selectable through the standard GOARCH build mechanism and be documented alongside other supported architectures.

issue_title: Inclusive version of take_while
requirement: The system shall provide an iterator adapter `take_while_inclusive` that yields elements from a source iterator while a given predicate returns `true`, additionally yields the first element for which the predicate returns `false` (if such an element exists), and terminates immediately thereafter. If the source iterator is exhausted before the predicate evaluates to `false`, all elements shall be yielded. The predicate shall be evaluated exactly once per element.

issue_title: Implement a Set primitive to complement Dictionary and Array
requirement: **Requirement: Introduce a Set Collection Type**  The language's standard library shall provide a first-class `Set` collection type that stores distinct values of a hashable type, complementing the existing `Dictionary` and `Array` collection types.  Functional requirements:  1. **Uniqueness**: Each element in a `Set` must be unique; inserting an element that is already present shall have no effect on the collection's contents. 2. **Unordered**: A `Set` shall not guarantee any particular iteration order of its elements. 3. **Hashable membership**: The element type must conform to a `Hashable` protocol to support efficient membership testing. 4. **Core operations**: The `Set` type shall support:    - Insertion (`insert`), removal (`remove`), and membership testing (`contains`);    - Fast membership lookup with expected average-case O(1) complexity;    - Set algebra operations, including union, intersection, symmetric difference, and subtraction (both as mutating and non-mutating forms, with corresponding operators such as `∪`-style methods or named functions);    - Subset/superset/disjointness predicates (`isSubset(of:)`, `isSuperset(of:)`, `isDisjoint(with:)`, including strict variants). 5. **Collection conformance**: `Set` shall conform to the standard collection protocols, supporting iteration, `count`, `isEmpty`, and other common collection operations. 6. **Literals and interoperability**: `Set` shall be constructible via array-like literals (e.g., `[1, 2, 3]` with explicit type context) and shall interoperate with `Array` and `Dictionary` through standard conversion mechanisms. 7. **Value semantics**: `Set` shall exhibit value semantics consistent with `Array` and `Dictionary` (copy-on-assignment behavior).  Non-functional requirements:  1. Performance of lookup, insertion, and removal shall be comparable to `Dictionary` (expected O(1) average case). 2. The API and naming shall be consistent with existing standard library collection types. 3. The implementation shall not require changes to the core language beyond existing protocol infrastructure (i.e., it shall be implementable as a standard library type).

issue_title: Customizable project structure (platforms)
requirement: **Requirement ID:** REQ-STRUCT-001 **Title:** Customizable Project Structure (Platforms)  **Statement:** The system shall allow users to customize the structure of a project by defining, adding, renaming, reordering, and removing platform-specific sections (e.g., desktop, web, mobile, console) within the project. Each platform section shall support its own set of source files, resources, settings, and build/export configurations, managed independently of other platforms. Users shall be able to modify the default project structure and save the customized layout as a reusable template for future projects.  **Functional Details:** 1. The system shall provide a project settings interface through which users can add or remove platform entries from a project. 2. The system shall persist all customizations to the project structure across sessions and reflect them consistently in the project view, build system, and export/deployment workflows. 3. The system shall prevent duplicate platform names or conflicting paths and shall display a validation warning when such conflicts occur. 4. The system shall build and export only the platforms currently enabled in the project structure, resolving all file paths according to the customized layout. 5. The system shall allow a platform to be removed or disabled without affecting the files, settings, or configurations of other platforms in the project.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - A user can add a new platform to an existing project and configure its files and settings. - A user can rename or reorder platforms, and the change is reflected everywhere the project structure is displayed or used. - A user can remove a platform, and the project builds and exports successfully with the remaining platforms. - Custom structure changes persist after closing and reopening the project. - Duplicate platform names or paths are rejected with a clear validation message.  **Priority:** High **Dependencies:** Project management module; build/export system.

issue_title: cmd/fix: automate migrations for simple deprecations
requirement: **FR-FIX-001 — Automated migration for simple deprecations**  The `cmd/fix` tool shall automatically migrate source code away from deprecated APIs when the deprecation has a simple, well-defined replacement. Specifically, the tool shall:  1. **Detect** — Identify all occurrences of a supported deprecated construct (identifier, function, type, or pattern) within the packages or files targeted on the command line, including those marked deprecated in their documentation. 2. **Rewrite** — Replace each occurrence with its documented, unambiguous replacement while preserving program semantics and, where possible, the original code formatting. 3. **Operate non-interactively** — Apply all supported migrations automatically in a single pass, without requiring user confirmation for each individual rewrite. 4. **Provide user control** — Expose command-line options to run in report-only (dry-run) mode and to enable or disable individual migrations. 5. **Report results** — Emit a summary listing (a) each migration applied, including file, position, and the deprecated construct and its replacement, and (b) each deprecated construct encountered that lacks a direct replacement or requires human judgment, so the user can address it manually.  **Constraints:** - The tool shall not modify a file unless every applicable migration within that file can be applied completely and safely (e.g., valid syntax, unambiguous replacement, no name collisions). - Deprecations that require human judgment, depend on context the tool cannot resolve, or have no direct replacement shall be excluded from automated rewriting and reported to the user instead. - Every migration performed shall be verifiable: the resulting code must compile and exhibit behavior identical to the original, except for the use of the replacement API.

issue_title: Add WebGPU support
requirement: **Requirement: WebGPU Rendering Backend Support**  **Description:** The system shall implement native support for the WebGPU API (Web Graphics Processing Unit) as a selectable rendering backend to enable high-performance 3D graphics and general-purpose GPU (GPGPU) computation in web browsers, providing capabilities such as compute shaders, reduced driver overhead, and explicit resource management compared to legacy WebGL backends.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. The system shall perform runtime feature detection of WebGPU availability via `navigator.gpu` and automatically fall back to the existing WebGL backend when WebGPU is unavailable, disabled, or fails to initialize. 2. The system shall implement WebGPU device acquisition, adapter selection with appropriate power preference options, and command queue management compliant with the W3C WebGPU specification. 3. The system shall support WebGPU Shading Language (WGSL) for vertex, fragment, and compute shader compilation, including pipeline state object creation and render/compute pipeline management. 4. The system shall implement GPU resource lifecycle management for buffers (vertex, index, uniform, storage), textures (2D, 3D, cubemaps, arrays), samplers, and bind groups with proper memory allocation and disposal. 5. The system shall support command encoding, render passes (including multi-pass rendering and viewport/scissor management), compute passes, and command buffer submission to the device queue. 6. The system shall handle device loss, validation errors, and uncaptured error scopes gracefully, providing diagnostic information and attempting recovery where possible. 7. The system shall expose a configuration option allowing users or developers to explicitly select the WebGPU backend, WebGL backend, or automatic selection based on capability detection.  **Non-Functional Requirements:** 1. **Performance:** The WebGPU backend shall achieve frame rates equal to or greater than the WebGL backend for equivalent rendering workloads on supported hardware, with specific benchmarks defined for vertex-heavy and fragment-heavy scenes. 2. **Compatibility:** The implementation shall function correctly on browsers with stable WebGPU support (Chrome/Edge 113+, Firefox 141+, Safari 26+) and shall degrade gracefully on unsupported platforms. 3. **Memory Efficiency:** GPU memory consumption shall not exceed the WebGL backend by more than 15% for identical scene complexity. 4. **Stability:** The system shall maintain stable operation without GPU device loss or memory leaks during continuous rendering sessions of at least 24 hours duration.  **Acceptance Criteria:** 1. Given a browser with WebGPU enabled, when the application initializes with WebGPU selected, then a valid `GPUDevice` shall be acquired and the render loop shall execute without validation errors. 2. Given a standard reference scene (defined by project test assets), when rendered via WebGPU, then the visual output shall match the WebGL reference render within a 1% per-pixel difference tolerance (using standard perceptual comparison metrics). 3. Given a browser without WebGPU support, when the application initializes, then the system shall automatically instantiate the WebGL fallback backend within 500ms of startup and display identical visual output to the WebGPU path. 4. Given compute shader workloads (e.g., particle simulation or physics calculation), when executed via WebGPU compute passes, then results shall match CPU-computed reference values within IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point tolerance. 5. All WebGPU code paths shall be exercised by automated unit and integration tests executing on CI infrastructure using cross-platform WebGPU implementations (e.g., Dawn, SwiftShader, or lavapipe) to ensure correctness across operating systems without requiring physical GPU hardware.

issue_title: Apple CarPlay / Android Auto support?
requirement: **REQ-001: Apple CarPlay and Android Auto Integration**  **Overview:** The application shall support Apple CarPlay (iOS 12+) and Android Auto (Android 6.0+) platforms, enabling users to access core application functionality through compatible vehicle infotainment systems via the vehicle's display, physical controls, and audio system.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. **Platform Connectivity:** The system shall establish connection via USB/Lightning (CarPlay) and USB/Bluetooth/Wi-Fi (Android Auto), automatically detecting and launching on supported vehicle head units. 2. **Interface Rendering:** The system shall render a driver-optimized, simplified UI on the vehicle display compliant with Apple CarPlay Human Interface Guidelines and Android Auto Design Guidelines, featuring large touch targets (≥44pt), limited navigation depth (≤5 taps to any function), and high-contrast glanceable layouts. 3. **Input Handling:** The system shall support vehicle touchscreen input, rotary controller/knob input, steering wheel controls, and voice commands via Siri and Google Assistant. 4. **Audio & Microphone Routing:** The system shall route audio output (media, navigation prompts, notifications) to the vehicle speaker system with proper audio ducking, and capture microphone input for voice commands and hands-free calling. 5. **Navigation Integration:** If applicable, the system shall provide turn-by-turn navigation, real-time ETA, and map rendering on the vehicle display, including lane guidance and points of interest where supported. 6. **Lifecycle Management:** The system shall persist session state across vehicle ignition cycles, auto-reconnect within 5 seconds of connection loss, and gracefully background when disconnected or when the vehicle powers off.  **Non-Functional Requirements:** 1. **Performance:** The interface shall initialize and render within 3 seconds of connection; input latency shall not exceed 100ms. 2. **Reliability:** The system shall maintain stable connectivity during vehicle operation (0-130 mph) and handle hot-plug events without crashing. 3. **Safety Compliance:** The implementation shall comply with NHTSA Driver Distraction Guidelines and platform-specific safety requirements, disabling complex text input and video playback while the vehicle is in motion.  **Constraints:** 1. **Certification:** The application must obtain Apple CarPlay certification and pass Google Play's Android Auto/Automotive quality review prior to distribution. 2. **Technical:** iOS implementation requires CarPlay entitlements and use of the CarPlay framework; Android implementation requires the Android Auto App Library (or Android Automotive OS SDK for native support) and automotive app category declaration in Google Play Console. 3. **Security:** All data transmission shall use encrypted protocols; sensitive data (credentials, precise location, personal content) shall require re-authentication after vehicle power cycles exceeding 5 minutes.  **Acceptance Criteria:** 1. When connected to a certified vehicle, the application appears in the CarPlay/Android Auto app launcher and launches to a functional home screen. 2. Users can execute primary workflows (media playback, navigation initiation, content browsing) using only vehicle-native controls without removing hands from the wheel for more than 2 seconds per interaction. 3. Audio output is clearly audible through vehicle speakers with correct priority handling for navigation prompts over media. 4. Siri and Google Assistant successfully trigger at least five core application actions via voice command. 5. The application passes third-party certification (Apple CarPlay/Google Android Auto) with no critical safety or stability violations.

issue_title: Add support for splitting linker invocation to a second execution of `rustc`
requirement: ## Requirement: Split the linker invocation into a second execution of `rustc`  ### Summary `rustc` must support an opt-in mode in which the final linker invocation is not performed by the compiling process, but is instead performed by a second, separate execution of `rustc`. The first execution performs compilation and code generation and produces the intermediate artifacts; the second execution consumes those artifacts and invokes the linker exactly once, with the same effective linker configuration that the current single-invocation flow uses.  ### Motivation Build systems and toolchains need the link step to be separable from the compile step so that it can be executed, observed, cached, sandboxed, or retried independently, and so that linkers that cannot be expressed as a single command invocation (e.g. due to command-line length limits or the need to alter the link environment) can be supported.  ### Functional requirements 1. **Opt-in only.** The behavior must be enabled by an explicit option; the default single-process compile-and-link flow must remain unchanged in behavior, output, and performance characteristics. 2. **First execution (compile phase).** Must perform the same compilation, code generation, and LTO work as today, must **not** invoke the linker, and must retain the intermediate artifacts (object files, bitcode, native library metadata) together with the fully resolved link plan: linker executable, linker flavor/features, complete argument list, ordering of inputs, environment variables, working directory, and output paths. 3. **Second execution (link phase).** Must reuse the artifacts produced by the first execution, must **not** re-run code generation or recompile the crate, and must perform exactly one linker invocation using the recorded link plan. 4. **Linker-relevant configuration must be honored.** At minimum: `-C linker`, `-C linker-flavor`, `-C linker-features`, `-C link-arg`, `-C link-args`, `-C link-dead-code`, `-C relocation-model`, `-C target-feature`, LTO/`-C lto` settings, debuginfo settings, panic strategy, crate types, target triple, `+crt-static`, and all library/link directives contributed by the crate, its dependencies, and build scripts (`-l`, native library search paths, `#[link]`/`#[link_args]` attributes). 5. **Consistency between executions.** Both executions must agree on all identity-critical inputs (target, sysroot, crate name, crate hash/disambiguator, edition, `cfg` flags, opt/debug settings, `RUSTFLAGS`/environment). The second execution must validate the link plan against the artifacts it receives and must fail with a clear diagnostic on any mismatch, rather than silently producing an incorrect binary. 6. **Linker coverage.** The split must work for all supported linker flavors (GNU `ld`/`lld`, MSVC `link.exe`, `wasm-ld`, and platform-provided linkers) and must work with cross-compilation and incremental compilation. If a given configuration cannot be split, `rustc` must emit an explicit diagnostic and fail instead of silently linking in the first process. 7. **Diagnostics and exit status.** Compilation errors from the first execution and linker errors from the second must be reported in normal `rustc` diagnostic format with the correct non-zero exit status. Failure of the second execution must be propagated to the caller of the first execution and must clearly identify which invocation failed. 8. **Output equivalence.** The artifacts produced via the split flow must be equivalent to those produced by the current single-invocation flow for the same inputs (bit-identical where deterministic). The linker must never be invoked twice for a single compilation unit. 9. **State transfer.** The data passed between the two executions must be a well-defined, versioned artifact (e.g. a link-plan/session file) written by the first execution and consumed by the second, so that the second execution can be launched independently by an external build tool as well as by `rustc` itself.  ### Command-line interface - The first execution must accept an option to request the split and to specify how the second execution is launched (at minimum: perform the link in a spawned second `rustc` process; optionally: write the link plan and defer linking to an externally launched second `rustc`). - The second execution must accept an option identifying the link plan/session to execute and must perform only the link step. - The options must be documented in `rustc --help`/`rustdoc`, and, if initially unstable, must follow the standard `-Z` unstable-option conventions.  ### Acceptance criteria - A test with a recording/fake linker confirms that, with the split enabled, the first `rustc` execution performs zero linker invocations and the second performs exactly one. - A build of the same crate with and without the split produces identical output artifacts. - Tests cover: successful split link; compile error in phase one; linker error in phase two (non-zero exit, propagated diagnostic); mismatched or stale link plan (explicit error); and a linker flavor that cannot be split (explicit diagnostic). - Tests run against at least one GNU-like and one MSVC-like linker configuration (mocked where not natively available), and for a cross-compilation target.  ### Non-goals - Changing the default build behavior of `rustc`/`cargo`. - Changing the semantics, contents, or ordering of the linker command line relative to the current implementation.

issue_title: Implement PlatformView support on Windows
requirement: **Requirement: PlatformView Support on Windows**  The framework shall provide support for embedding native Windows platform views within the application's rendering hierarchy.  **Details:**  - The Windows embedder shall allow developers to host native Windows UI controls as platform views that are composited together with framework-rendered content. - Platform views shall be created, updated, resized, and disposed through the existing platform view API used on other supported platforms, so that application code remains platform-agnostic. - Platform view layout and positioning shall stay synchronized with the Flutter widget tree, including scrolling, clipping, and transformations applied by the framework. - Input events (pointer, keyboard, and focus) shall be routed correctly between the framework and the embedded native views, with focus transitions handled in both directions. - Platform views shall render correctly under the Windows compositing pipeline, preserving z-ordering relative to framework-drawn content. - The implementation shall handle device pixel ratio scaling and window resizing so that embedded views remain aligned at all supported DPI settings. - Errors during platform view creation or lifecycle operations shall be reported to the Dart side without crashing the application. - Behavior shall be documented and covered by automated tests on the Windows platform.

issue_title: Add "refactor" tooling to rename symbols in the script editor
requirement: **REQ-EDITOR-REFACTOR-001: Symbol Rename Refactoring in Script Editor**  **Statement:** The script editor shall provide a "Rename Symbol" refactoring command that enables users to rename any symbol (variable, function, class, or parameter) and automatically updates its declaration and all references throughout the script in a single, atomic operation.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  1. The rename command shall be invocable via a context menu (right-click on the symbol), a keyboard shortcut, and the editor command palette. 2. When invoked, the editor shall present an inline editable field (or dialog) pre-populated with the current symbol name. 3. Upon confirmation, all occurrences of the symbol — including its declaration and all in-scope references — shall be updated consistently across the script. 4. The rename operation shall be scope-aware: identical symbol names in unrelated scopes shall remain unaffected. 5. The editor shall validate that the new name is a legal identifier and shall reject renames that would conflict with an existing symbol in the same scope, reporting the conflict without applying partial changes. 6. Where a reference to the symbol cannot be resolved with certainty (e.g., dynamic or string-based access), the user shall be warned prior to applying the change. 7. The rename operation shall be atomic — either all occurrences are updated or none are — and shall be reversible through the editor's standard undo functionality. 8. A summary of the number and location of modified occurrences shall be made available to the user after the operation completes.

issue_title: x/tools/gopls: support for bazel-based projects
requirement: **REQ-GOPLS-BAZEL-001**: Support for Bazel-Based Go Projects  **Description**: The gopls language server shall detect and provide full language server capabilities (navigation, diagnostics, completion, refactoring) within Go projects that use Bazel as their build system, mapping Bazel build targets to Go packages and resolving dependencies across Bazel-managed workspaces and external repositories.  **Functional Requirements**:  1. **Workspace Detection**: gopls shall identify a Bazel workspace root by detecting any of: `WORKSPACE`, `WORKSPACE.bazel`, `WORKSPACE.bazel.tmpl`, `MODULE.bazel`, `REPO.bazel`, or `.bazelversion` files.  2. **Build Target Analysis**: gopls shall parse `BUILD.bazel` and `BUILD` files to extract Go rule definitions (`go_library`, `go_binary`, `go_test`, `go_proto_library`, etc.), including `srcs`, `deps`, `embed`, `importpath`, and `visibility` attributes.  3. **Label Resolution**: gopls shall resolve Bazel labels (e.g., `//foo/bar:lib`, `@repo//baz:target`) to file system paths and Go import paths, enabling cross-target navigation within the same workspace and to external repositories.  4. **Generated Source Support**: gopls shall include generated Go files declared as outputs of Bazel rules (e.g., `genrule` outputs, `go_proto_library` generated sources) in package loading and analysis.  5. **Dependency Mapping**: gopls shall resolve standard Go import paths to their corresponding Bazel targets, supporting both legacy `WORKSPACE`-based external dependencies and modern `bzlmod` module extensions, including vendored dependencies managed by Bazel.  6. **Gazelle Compatibility**: gopls shall correctly interpret BUILD files generated by Gazelle, respecting `importpath` attributes and default package naming conventions.  7. **File Exclusion**: gopls shall exclude files not included in any Bazel target (as defined by `srcs` globs) from package analysis unless explicitly configured otherwise, or treat directories without BUILD files as standalone Go packages based on user settings.  **Acceptance Criteria**:  - [ ] gopls initializes successfully in a Bazel workspace root without incorrectly falling back to GOPATH or Go Modules mode. - [ ] "Go to Definition" navigates from a source file in one Bazel package to symbols defined in a dependency target (e.g., `//pkg/foo:lib`) within the same workspace. - [ ] "Go to Definition" and "Find References" work across external Bazel repositories (e.g., `@com_github_example_repo//pkg:lib`). - [ ] Diagnostics (syntax errors, type errors, unused imports) are accurately reported for files included in Bazel `go_library` or `go_test` targets. - [ ] Code completion suggests exported symbols from Bazel-managed dependencies. - [ ] Rename refactoring updates references across multiple Bazel targets. - [ ] gopls functions correctly in monorepos containing multiple Bazel modules or nested workspaces. - [ ] Startup time for workspaces with up to 1,000 Bazel targets increases by no more than 500ms compared to non-Bazel projects.  **Constraints**: - Must support Bazel versions 5.x through 7.x (both WORKSPACE and bzlmod modes). - Must not require Bazel to be installed or running; parsing shall be static based on BUILD file contents.

issue_title: [video_player] Support DRM content
requirement: **Requirement: DRM-Protected Content Playback in the Video Player**  The video player shall support playback of DRM-protected (digital rights managed) video content.  **Details:**  1. **License acquisition:** The player shall request and obtain decryption licenses from a configurable license server URL, using the DRM system appropriate to the platform (e.g., Widevine, FairPlay, PlayReady). 2. **Content specification:** The application shall be able to supply DRM configuration, including the DRM scheme, license server URL, and any required HTTP headers or license request parameters, when initializing a video source. 3. **Playback:** Encrypted media segments shall be decrypted and rendered without exposing the decrypted content to the application layer. 4. **Error handling:** The player shall report DRM-related failures (e.g., unsupported DRM scheme, license acquisition failure, expired or invalid license, insufficient output protection) through its error-reporting mechanism with distinguishable error codes. 5. **Platform support:** DRM playback shall be available on each supported platform where the underlying platform provides a compatible DRM system; the player shall indicate when a requested DRM scheme is unsupported on the current device. 6. **Compatibility:** Existing non-DRM playback behavior shall remain unchanged.

Running `brew install --cask flutter` on a supported macOS version installs the Flutter SDK without manual download or path configuration. 2. After installation, `flutter --version` and `dart --version` execute successfully in a new terminal session. 3. issue_title: [RFC] RPC Based Distributed Model Parallel
requirement: **Requirement: RPC-Based Distributed Model Parallelism**  The framework shall support model parallel training by partitioning a single model's submodules across multiple worker processes, possibly on different hosts, and coordinating their execution through a remote procedure call (RPC) mechanism.  The framework shall:  1. Allow a user to place individual submodules or layers on specific workers and reference them remotely without manually managing inter-process communication. 2. Execute forward passes on remote submodules via RPC, passing activations between workers as needed to compute the full model output. 3. Propagate gradients backward across worker boundaries so that a single distributed backward pass computes correct gradients for all parameters, regardless of where they reside. 4. Provide remote references to module instances and their parameters so that the caller can invoke methods, retrieve values, and access parameters on remote workers. 5. Support synchronous and asynchronous RPC invocation so that independent computations on different workers can overlap. 6. Integrate with the existing optimizer interface so that parameters distributed across workers can be updated, with each worker applying updates to its local parameters. 7. Handle worker failures and RPC errors by surfacing them as exceptions to the caller rather than hanging or silently producing incorrect results. 8. Be usable with a standard training loop with minimal changes to single-process model code.

issue_title: Add support for nullable static types in GDScript
requirement: **Requirement ID:** FR-GDSCRIPT-001 **Title:** Nullable Static Types in GDScript **Type:** Functional **Priority:** High  **Requirement Statement:** The GDScript language shall extend its static type system to support explicitly nullable types, enabling developers to declare variables, function parameters, return types, and container element types as either holding a value of the specified base type or null.  **Rationale:** GDScript's current static type system cannot formally express optionality. Developers must rely on untyped variables, sentinel values, or unchecked runtime assumptions, which prevents the analyzer from detecting null-related errors at compile time. Explicit nullable types improve type safety, code clarity, and error detection.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **FR-1 — Nullable Type Syntax:** GDScript shall provide a syntax for marking any static type as nullable (e.g., a `?` suffix such as `int?`, `Node2D?`), usable in variable declarations, function parameters, function return types, and as element types of typed arrays and dictionaries. 2. **FR-2 — Null Assignment:** A variable declared with a nullable type shall accept both values of its base type and `null`. 3. **FR-3 — Non-Nullable Enforcement:** Assigning `null` to a variable whose declared type is non-nullable shall be rejected or flagged by the static analyzer/compile-time checks. 4. **FR-4 — Analyzer Support:** The static analyzer shall report diagnostics when a nullable value is used in a context requiring a non-null value, unless the code explicitly performs a null check or safe-unwrap prior to use. 5. **FR-5 — Backward Compatibility:** Nullable annotations shall be opt-in; all existing GDScript code that does not use nullable annotations shall compile and behave without modification. Existing implicitly-nullable behavior for Object-derived types shall remain unchanged unless an explicit annotation is applied. 6. **FR-6 — Editor Tooling:** The script editor shall provide syntax highlighting, code completion, and error highlighting consistent with nullable type declarations and their usage.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - **AC-1:** `var x: int? = null` parses, type-checks, and accepts both integer values and `null` at runtime. - **AC-2:** A function declared with a nullable return type (e.g., `-> String?`) may return `null`; calling a method or accessing a member directly on its result without a preceding null check produces an analyzer diagnostic. - **AC-3:** Assigning `null` to a variable declared as `var y: int` produces a compile-time or analyzer-reported error/warning per project configuration. - **AC-4:** A project containing no nullable annotations compiles and runs identically before and after the feature is introduced.

issue_title: Investigate Swift Package Manager for Swift plugins
requirement: # Requirement: Swift Package Manager (SwiftPM) Command Plugin Support  ## 1. Objective  Assess the feasibility of using Swift Package Manager command plugins (SE-0273, Swift 5.6+) within the project and, subject to the feasibility outcome, enable the project to discover, invoke, and supervise SwiftPM plugins as part of its automated build/verification workflow.  ## 2. Background  SwiftPM allows a package to declare executable command plugins under `Plugins/<PluginName>/`, conforming to `PackagePlugin.CommandPlugin`. Such plugins are invoked with `swift package <plugin-name> [arguments…]`, run inside SwiftPM's sandbox, and may request permissions (e.g., tool execution, writing to the package directory, network access). The project currently has no integration with SwiftPM's plugin mechanism and relies exclusively on ad-hoc script execution.  ## 3. Scope  ### 3.1 Phase 1 — Investigation (mandatory deliverable)  Produce a written assessment that:  - Confirms the minimum supported Swift toolchain/SwiftPM version required (Swift 5.6+; document behavior differences across 5.6 → current). - Documents the plugin authoring API surface (`PackagePlugin`, `PluginContext`, `pluginWorkDirectory`, `packageDirectory`, `context.tool(named:)`), the manifest/package layout expectations, and the invocation contract and exit-code semantics. - Documents SwiftPM's permission model and the command-line flags used to grant or deny it (e.g., `--allow-writing-to-package-directory`, `--allow-writing-to-directory`, `--disable-sandbox`, `--skip-update`), including how each is surfaced to users in non-interactive/CI environments. - Documents how plugins are enumerated (e.g., `swift package plugin --list` where available; otherwise parsing of `Package.swift`/`Plugins/` and `swift package describe --type json`), and their limitations. - Identifies environmental constraints in CI and containerized environments (sandboxing, toolchain availability, working-directory assumptions, plugin caching/work-directory lifetime). - Compares the approach against alternatives (direct subprocess invocation of package executables, `swift run`, Make/Xcode build phases) and states a clear recommendation with rationale and risks. - Outlines a proposed invocation API and configuration surface for the project, including how a user selects a plugin and passes arguments.  The assessment is accepted when it is linked from the issue and reviewed by a maintainer, and a decision (proceed / proceed with changes / do not proceed) is recorded.  ### 3.2 Phase 2 — Implementation (conditional on a "proceed" decision)  **Functional requirements**  - **FR-1 Toolchain detection:** The project shall locate the Swift toolchain on the host, determine the Swift and SwiftPM versions, and fail with an actionable, user-facing error message when the toolchain is absent or older than the minimum supported version. - **FR-2 Plugin discovery:** The project shall enumerate the command plugins declared by a target Swift package and expose them (by name and description) to callers. - **FR-3 Invocation:** The project shall invoke a selected plugin by executing `swift package --package-path <package-dir> <plugin-name> [args…]`, forwarding caller-supplied arguments verbatim and preserving argument boundaries (including spaces and empty strings). - **FR-4 Environment and working directory:** The project shall support configuring the plugin's working directory, environment variables, and additional SwiftPM command-line options; unset variables shall not leak from the parent process unless explicitly requested. - **FR-5 Permissions:** The project shall support an explicit permission policy for plugin execution — `deny` (default in non-interactive runs), `allow` (all requested permissions pre-granted via the corresponding SwiftPM flags), or `prompt` (interactive only) — and shall report precisely which permissions were requested and which were denied. - **FR-6 Result reporting:** The project shall propagate the plugin's exit code, capture and expose stdout and stderr separately, and treat a non-zero exit code as a plugin failure. Plugin output shall be streamed or buffered according to the invocation mode and be attributable to the plugin invocation. - **FR-7 Isolation:** The project shall not modify the target package's sources, manifest, or resolved state as a side effect of invoking a plugin, except where the plugin is explicitly permitted to write. - **FR-8 Idempotency and repeatability:** Repeated invocations with identical inputs shall produce identical results, and the project shall not rely on state that persists only in an interactive session. - **FR-9 Diagnostics:** Failures due to SwiftPM errors (unresolved dependencies, malformed manifest, unknown plugin name) shall be surfaced with the underlying SwiftPM message preserved. - **FR-10 Configuration and documentation:** The new capability shall be configurable via the project's configuration mechanism and documented, including a usage example showing how to invoke a plugin and pass arguments.  **Non-functional requirements**  - **NFR-1 Compatibility:** Support macOS and Linux on supported architectures; align with the project's existing minimum operating system and Swift version policies. - **NFR-2 Performance:** Plugin discovery shall complete within an acceptable bound (target ≤ 5 s) for a typical package, and shall be cacheable with an explicit invalidation strategy. - **NFR-3 Security:** Plugin execution shall never run with escalated permissions by default; sandbox-related SwiftPM flags shall only be applied when explicitly configured. - **NFR-4 Maintainability:** The integration shall be implemented in a dedicated module with unit tests, and shall not introduce a hard dependency on SwiftPM internals that are not part of the public CLI/`PackagePlugin` surface. - **NFR-5 Observability:** Plugin invocations shall be logged (plugin name, package path, permissions granted/denied, duration, exit code) at a level consistent with existing logging conventions.  ## 4. Acceptance Criteria  1. A reviewed investigation document exists that covers the items in §3.1, and the issue records a proceed/do-not-proceed decision. 2. Given a package declaring at least one command plugin, when plugin discovery runs, the plugin names and descriptions are returned; when no plugins are declared, an empty result is returned without error. 3. Given a valid plugin name and arguments, when the plugin is invoked, the plugin executes under `swift package`, receives the arguments verbatim, and the plugin's stdout, stderr, and exit code are surfaced to the caller. 4. Given a plugin that requests a permission while the policy is `deny`, when the plugin is invoked, the invocation fails with a clear message naming the requested permission, and no privileged operation is performed. 5. Given the policy is `allow` in a non-interactive (CI) environment, when a permission-requesting plugin is invoked, the invocation completes without a hang or an interactive prompt. 6. Given a toolchain older than the minimum supported version or no toolchain, when discovery or invocation is attempted, the operation fails with an actionable error identifying the detected version. 7. Given a plugin that exits non-zero, when the invocation completes, the project reports failure and propagates the plugin's exit code. 8. Given the same package and plugin are invoked twice with the same arguments, when the package contents are unchanged, both invocations yield the same result. 9. Unit tests cover discovery, argument forwarding, permission policies, exit-code propagation, and error handling for missing/unsupported toolchains.  ## 5. Out of Scope  - Authoring new SwiftPM plugins on behalf of the project (only discovery and invocation are in scope). - Build-tool plugins (SE-0272) and macro plugins (Swift 5.9+), which shall be evaluated separately. - Modifications to SwiftPM itself or to third-party packages' plugin implementations. - Automatic granting of permissions without an explicit user/config opt-in.

issue_title: Add support for splitting linker invocation to a second execution of `rustc`
requirement: **Requirement: Split Linker Invocation into a Separate `rustc` Execution**  `rustc` shall support splitting a single compilation into two sequential invocations: a first invocation that performs compilation and emits all object files and the metadata needed for linking, and a second invocation that performs only the link step using those artifacts.  1. **Invocation control:** The user shall be able to request the split through a command-line option (for example, a flag that emits linker inputs and skips linking in the first run, and a flag that performs only linking in the second run). The exact flag names shall follow `rustc`'s existing option conventions. 2. **Artifact handoff:** The first invocation shall write all information required by the linker (object file paths, native library requirements, linker arguments, and crate metadata) to a well-defined, documented location or manifest that the second invocation reads without needing the original source files or compilation state. 3. **Equivalence:** The output produced by the two-step process shall be functionally identical to the output of a single-step invocation with the same inputs and options, including the final binary or library, its symbols, and its exit status on failure. 4. **Error handling:** The second invocation shall fail with a clear diagnostic if the handoff artifacts are missing, incomplete, or produced by an incompatible `rustc` version, and it shall not produce partial or silently incorrect output. 5. **Build-system compatibility:** The split shall work with build systems that run steps in separate processes, including preserving relative or absolute paths in the handoff data so that artifacts can be moved within the same build directory without breaking the link. 6. **Stability:** The feature may be initially gated behind an unstable flag, but its behavior and the handoff format shall be documented and covered by automated tests that verify the two-step output matches the single-step output on supported targets. 7. **No regression:** Existing single-invocation compilation behavior and performance shall remain unchanged when the split option is not used.

issue_title: Obfuscate GDScript in production export
requirement: Godot’s export pipeline shall provide an **Obfuscate GDScript** option for production export presets. When enabled, all GDScript resources included in the export shall be stored in a non-plaintext, obfuscated form so the original source cannot be read directly from the exported files. Obfuscation shall preserve script behavior, public APIs, signals, dependencies, and runtime error handling. The option shall be configurable per export preset and shall not affect editor use or debug exports. Obfuscated projects shall export, import, and run successfully without requiring additional tools or manual steps.

issue_title: Add support for global plugins/universal addons
requirement: ## Requirement: Global Plugins / Universal Addons  The platform shall support globally scoped plugins, also referred to as universal addons. A global plugin/addon shall be installed and enabled once, then discovered and loaded in every authorized project, workspace, and tenant context without requiring separate per-context installations.  ### Acceptance Criteria  - Global plugins/addons can be installed, configured, enabled, disabled, updated, and removed through the platform’s existing extension-management interfaces. - The management interface clearly identifies each plugin/addon’s scope and current status. - Existing project- or workspace-scoped plugins/addons retain their current behavior. Any migration to global scope must be explicit. - Global and context-scoped plugins/addons may coexist. Where they provide the same capability or extension point, the platform shall apply deterministic, documented precedence and shall not load or execute the same global extension more than once in a context. - Global configuration is stored centrally and applied consistently. Context-specific overrides are permitted only where defined by the platform’s configuration model. - Only authorized users may manage global plugins/addons, and global extensions must respect tenant boundaries, permissions, and other access controls. - Global plugin/addon registrations and configuration persist across restarts. - Failures in a global plugin/addon are surfaced through existing diagnostics and must not prevent unrelated plugins/addons from loading. - Automated tests cover scope-aware discovery, loading, precedence, access control, and backward compatibility. - User or administrator documentation explains global installation, activation, configuration, precedence, and troubleshooting.

issue_title: [Poll] Support DistributedDataParallel (DDP) in PyTorch C++ API (libtorch)
requirement: **Requirement ID:** REQ-LIBTORCH-DDP-001 **Title:** DistributedDataParallel (DDP) Support in PyTorch C++ API (LibTorch)  **Description:** The PyTorch C++ frontend (libtorch) shall provide full DistributedDataParallel functionality equivalent to the Python API, enabling users to perform distributed data-parallel training using native C++ code.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. The system shall expose a `torch::distributed::DistributedDataParallel` class within the `torch::distributed` namespace that accepts a `std::shared_ptr<torch::nn::Module>` and configures it for multi-process gradient synchronization. 2. The API shall support process group initialization via `torch::distributed::init_process_group` with support for NCCL, Gloo, and MPI backends, accepting parameters for backend type, world size, rank, and store configuration. 3. The DDP wrapper shall automatically all-reduce gradients across all participating processes during the backward pass without requiring manual gradient aggregation calls from the user. 4. The implementation shall support configurable DDP options including: device_ids (for GPU/CPU placement), broadcast_buffers, bucket_cap_mb (gradient bucketing size), find_unused_parameters, gradient_as_bucket_view, and static_graph mode. 5. The API shall support both single-node multi-device and multi-node distributed training topologies. 6. The C++ interface shall provide methods for querying module parameters, accessing the underlying wrapped module, and joining/closing the process group.  **Non-Functional Requirements:** 1. The C++ DDP implementation shall achieve performance parity with the Python implementation, with communication overhead not exceeding 5% of the Python baseline. 2. Memory consumption shall be equivalent to the Python DDP implementation for identical model architectures. 3. The API shall maintain ABI stability with existing libtorch interfaces and support C++17 standard compliance.  **Acceptance Criteria:** 1. A C++ application using libtorch successfully initializes a process group across multiple processes/GPUs and wraps a `torch::nn::Module` with `DistributedDataParallel`. 2. Forward and backward passes execute without error across all processes, with gradients verified to be synchronized (all-reduced) across all ranks. 3. Training a model (e.g., ResNet or simple MLP) in C++ using DDP produces loss values and model weights identical (within 1e-6 tolerance) to the equivalent Python DDP training run after the same number of iterations. 4. All configuration flags (bucket_cap_mb, find_unused_parameters, broadcast_buffers, etc.) are settable via the C++ API and demonstrably affect training behavior (e.g., bucket size affects communication volume). 5. Static analysis and unit tests verify that the C++ API throws appropriate exceptions for invalid configurations (e.g., wrapping an already-wrapped module, mismatched device IDs). 6. Documentation includes a complete C++ example demonstrating multi-process DDP training initialization and execution.

issue_title: [RFC] PT2-Friendly Traceable, Functional Collective Communication APIs
requirement: **Requirement: PT2-Compatible Functional Collective Communication APIs**  The distributed collective communication APIs shall be provided as functional, traceable operations that are fully compatible with the PyTorch 2 compiler stack (TorchDynamo, AOTAutograd, and TorchInductor).  1. **Functional semantics:** Each collective (e.g., all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, all-to-all, broadcast) shall return a new output tensor and shall not mutate its inputs in place, so that the operation can be functionalized and reasoned about by the compiler. 2. **Traceability:** Collectives shall be representable as nodes in an FX graph under `torch.compile` and shall not cause graph breaks for supported process group configurations. 3. **Asynchronous execution:** Asynchronous collectives shall return a tensor-like handle whose completion is explicitly expressed in the graph through a wait operation, allowing the compiler to schedule and overlap communication with computation without relying on opaque Python-side futures. 4. **Process group handling:** Process groups shall be referenced in a form that is serializable and traceable (e.g., by stable identifiers or registered group objects), so that compiled graphs remain valid across tracing and execution. 5. **Autograd support:** Each functional collective shall define its backward behavior so that gradients propagate correctly through AOTAutograd-generated graphs. 6. **Backend lowering:** Functional collectives shall be lowerable to backend-specific communication implementations (e.g., NCCL) by TorchInductor and the eager runtime, producing numerically equivalent results to the existing eager collective APIs. 7. **Compatibility:** The existing eager distributed APIs shall remain available and behaviorally unchanged; the functional variants are additive.

issue_title: [RFC] DeepSpeed + PT Distributed Integration
requirement: ## Requirement: DeepSpeed–PyTorch Distributed Integration  The system shall support interoperable distributed training when DeepSpeed and PyTorch’s `torch.distributed` are used within the same application, including jobs launched through `torchrun`.  ### Functional requirements  1. **Process-group initialization**    - Reuse an existing `torch.distributed` process group when one has already been initialized.    - Allow DeepSpeed initialization to initialize the required process group when none exists.    - Avoid creating duplicate default process groups and shall report invalid or conflicting initialization configurations clearly.  2. **Rank and device coordination**    - Maintain consistent global rank, local rank, world size, backend, and device assignments across DeepSpeed and `torch.distributed`.    - Support `torchrun`-provided environment variables and DeepSpeed-provided distributed configuration.    - Detect and report mismatches in rank, world size, backend, or device configuration before training begins.  3. **Collective communication**    - Ensure communication operations used during training, including barrier, broadcast, all-reduce, and all-gather, execute correctly across all participating ranks.    - Synchronize collective participation and completion so that no rank proceeds with incompatible operations.  4. **Gradient synchronization**    - Define a single owner for gradient synchronization when DeepSpeed and PyTorch distributed components are both active.    - Prevent unintended duplicate gradient all-reduce operations.    - Report actionable errors when conflicting gradient-synchronization configurations are detected.  5. **Lifecycle and persistence**    - Preserve correct distributed state through training shutdown and restart.    - Support DeepSpeed checkpoint save, load, and resume with consistent rank, world-size, backend, and device validation.    - Provide clear diagnostics for unsupported checkpoint or topology combinations.  6. **Documentation and compatibility**    - Document supported initialization orders, backends, configuration precedence, and known limitations.    - Clearly identify any advanced interoperability features that are not supported.  ### Acceptance criteria  - A multi-process `torchrun` job using a valid DeepSpeed configuration completes forward, backward, and optimizer steps without hanging or rank desynchronization. - Training results and gradient synchronization match an equivalent DeepSpeed-only run. - Collective communication initiated through either library produces correct results across all ranks. - Existing-process-group initialization and DeepSpeed-first initialization both complete successfully. - Unsupported backend, rank, world-size, device, or checkpoint combinations fail with an actionable error message. - Automated tests cover CPU/process-group scenarios and GPU/NCCL scenarios where the required hardware is available.

issue_title: Feature request: Use 'trampolines' to make most of the body of a generic function non-generic
requirement: ### Requirement: Shared generic-function bodies using trampolines  The compiler shall automatically lower eligible generic functions into:  1. A single shared, non-generic implementation containing all body logic that is independent of the function’s type parameters. 2. Type-specific trampolines containing only operations whose behavior, representation, overload/type-class resolution, or dispatch depends on those parameters.  Each concrete instantiation shall use the corresponding trampoline for every type-dependent operation. The compiler shall not duplicate type-independent logic for additional instantiations. A generic function with no type-dependent operations shall produce only one implementation regardless of the number of instantiations.  The transformation shall support direct calls, calls through function values, and recursive or mutually recursive generic functions. If a function cannot be safely partitioned, it may retain the existing specialization strategy without changing its behavior.  The optimization shall be transparent to source code and shall preserve type checking and inference, generic constraints, visibility, evaluation order, exception and error behavior, and return values. Type-dependent values crossing the shared implementation boundary shall retain sound runtime representations and shall never be dispatched to a trampoline for an incompatible instantiation.  Acceptance criteria shall include tests demonstrating that:  - Multiple instantiations share one type-independent implementation. - Type-dependent operations dispatch to the correct trampoline. - Entirely type-independent generic bodies are emitted once. - Existing generic-function behavior and diagnostics remain unchanged.

issue_title: Add array unpacking/destructuring to GDScript
requirement: **Requirement ID:** REQ-GDSCRIPT-DESTRUCTURING-001 **Title:** Array Unpacking and Destructuring Assignment **Priority:** High **Description:** GDScript shall support array destructuring (unpacking) syntax that allows multiple variables to be initialized or assigned from the elements of an array in a single statement, improving code concision and readability when working with structured array data.  **Functional Requirements:**  FR-1: The parser shall accept destructuring declarations of the form `var [pattern_list] = array_expression` and destructuring assignments of the form `[pattern_list] = array_expression` (without `var`), where `array_expression` evaluates to a value of type `Array`.  FR-2: Each element in `pattern_list` shall support the following forms: - **Identifier:** A variable name to receive the element at the corresponding index (e.g., `a`). - **Elision:** A comma with no identifier to skip the element at that index (e.g., `var [a, , c] = [1, 2, 3]`). - **Rest pattern:** The spread token `...` followed by an identifier as the final element in the list, which collects all remaining elements from the current index into a new `Array` (e.g., `var [first, ...rest] = [1, 2, 3]` yields `first=1`, `rest=[2, 3]`). - **Nested pattern:** A nested destructuring list (e.g., `var [[x, y], z] = [[1, 2], 3]`). - **Default value:** An identifier followed by `=` and an expression, used when the array index is out of bounds (e.g., `var [a, b = 10] = [1]` yields `b=10`).  FR-3: Evaluation shall proceed left-to-right; the right-hand side expression shall be evaluated exactly once, and elements shall be assigned to targets corresponding to array indices 0, 1, 2, etc.  FR-4: If `array_expression` does not evaluate to type `Array`, the system shall raise a runtime type error.  FR-5: If a non-default, non-rest, non-elided target requires an element at an index greater than or equal to the array's size, the system shall raise a runtime "index out of bounds" error.  FR-6: Variables declared via destructuring shall have their static type inferred from the source array's element type when the array is statically typed (e.g., `Array[int]`), or default to `Variant` otherwise.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  NFR-1: The implementation shall compile destructuring operations to efficient bytecode, avoiding unnecessary array allocations or copies, particularly when using the rest pattern.  NFR-2: The syntax shall be unambiguously distinguishable from array literals in expression contexts; the parser shall resolve ambiguity based on whether the construct appears in a declaration/assignment target position versus a value expression position.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  AC-1: `var [a, b, c] = [1, 2, 3]` results in `a == 1`, `b == 2`, `c == 3`. AC-2: `var [a, , c] = [1, 2, 3]` results in `a == 1` and `c == 3`. AC-3: `var [first, ...rest] = [1, 2, 3, 4]` results in `first == 1` and `rest == [2, 3, 4]`. AC-4: `var [a, b = 99] = [1]` results in `a == 1` and `b == 99`. AC-5: `var [[x, y], z] = [[1, 2], 3]` results in `x == 1`, `y == 2`, `z == 3`. AC-6: Given pre-declared `var a; var b;`, executing `[a, b] = [5, 6]` updates `a == 5` and `b == 6`. AC-7: Executing `var [a, b] = [1]` raises a runtime error indicating index out of bounds. AC-8: Executing `var [a] = {"key": "value"}` raises a runtime type error indicating expected `Array`.

issue_title: Add support for `#[doc(since="version")]` attribute
requirement: ## Requirement: Support `#[doc(since = "version")]` attributes  The documentation tooling must recognize `#[doc(since = "VERSION")]` on documented items and expose the specified version as item documentation metadata.  ### Functional requirements  1. The attribute parser must accept the nested `doc` attribute in the form `#[doc(since = "VERSION")]`, with optional whitespace around `=`. 2. `VERSION` must be supplied as a non-empty string literal. The value must be preserved exactly as written, without normalization or semantic-version validation. 3. The parsed version must be associated with the annotated item and retained in the documentation metadata model so that documentation renderers can display it. 4. Human-readable documentation must present the version using the established version-availability format, equivalent to `Available since VERSION`. 5. The attribute must not add text to the item’s main documentation body and must not affect the item’s stability, deprecation status, feature gating, visibility, exports, or runtime behavior. 6. Existing documentation attributes and comments, including `#[doc = "..."]`, `#[doc(alias = "...")]`, and ordinary `///` or `/** */` documentation, must continue to work unchanged. 7. Malformed usage must be rejected with a targeted diagnostic identifying the invalid attribute, including:    - `#[doc(since)]`    - `#[doc(since = 1.0)]`    - `#[doc(since = version)]`    - `#[doc(since = "")]` 8. Multiple `since` values on the same item must be rejected as ambiguous rather than silently selecting one value.  ### Acceptance criteria  - A function, type, trait, module, or other supported item annotated with `#[doc(since = "1.2.3")]` exposes `1.2.3` in its documentation metadata and displays `Available since 1.2.3`. - Values such as `"1.0"` are preserved verbatim. - The attribute itself is not rendered as part of the item’s prose. - Invalid and duplicate attribute usages produce clear diagnostics and do not produce partially rendered documentation. - Automated tests cover valid attributes, malformed attributes, duplicate attributes, multiple supported item kinds, and combinations with other documentation attributes.

issue_title: AVIF codec support
requirement: ## AVIF Codec Support  The image-codec framework shall support the AV1 Image File Format (AVIF) for both encoding and decoding through the existing public APIs.  - AVIF files shall be detected by their container signature and decoded using a standards-compliant AVIF decoder. - The public API shall expose AVIF encoding with configurable quality or compression settings and sensible defaults. - Decoded images shall preserve dimensions, orientation, color profile, and EXIF metadata when present in the source file and supported by the underlying codec. - Invalid, truncated, corrupted, or unsupported AVIF data shall produce clear codec-specific errors without crashing the application. - AVIF handling shall integrate with existing format detection and file I/O paths without regressing existing codecs. - Automated tests shall cover valid-file decoding, encode/decode round trips, invalid-input handling, and metadata preservation. - Documentation shall describe AVIF usage, configuration options, and any required build dependencies or platform limitations.

issue_title: Provide a means of turning iterators into fixed-size arrays
requirement: REQ-001: The system shall provide a public API for converting an iterator into a fixed-size array. The API shall accept any iterator whose yielded element type matches the array's element type, consume exactly N elements from the iterator, and produce an array of length N, where N is specified as a compile-time constant. If the iterator terminates before yielding N elements, the API shall return a well-defined error condition (rather than panicking or producing uninitialized values) without consuming or discarding the remaining elements of any underlying collection. If the iterator yields more than N elements, the API shall consume only the first N and define deterministic behavior for any remaining elements. The conversion shall be zero-cost where possible, performing no heap allocation and no unnecessary copying of elements.

issue_title: [webview_flutter] Add Windows support
requirement: **Requirement ID:** WF-WIN-001 **Title:** Windows Platform Support for webview_flutter Plugin  **Description:** The webview_flutter plugin shall extend its platform support to include Microsoft Windows, enabling Flutter applications to render web content using the native Windows WebView2 control (Microsoft Edge Chromium) while maintaining full API compatibility with existing iOS, Android, and Web implementations.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. The plugin shall implement all platform interface classes (`PlatformWebViewController`, `PlatformWebViewWidget`, `PlatformWebViewCookieManager`) for Windows using WebView2 as the underlying rendering engine. 2. The Windows implementation shall expose an identical Dart API surface to other platforms, requiring zero breaking changes in application code when targeting Windows. 3. Core WebView operations shall be supported: URL loading (`loadUrl`, `loadRequest`, `loadHtmlString`, `loadFlutterAsset`, `loadFile`), navigation history (`goBack`, `goForward`, `canGoBack`, `canGoForward`, `reload`), JavaScript execution (`runJavaScript`, `runJavaScriptReturningResult`), and state queries (`currentUrl`, `getTitle`). 4. JavaScript Channels shall be supported for bidirectional Dart-JavaScript communication via `addJavaScriptChannel` and `removeJavaScriptChannel`. 5. Cookie management shall be supported via `getCookies`, `setCookie`, and `clearCookies`. 6. Custom HTTP request headers and WebView settings (JavaScript mode, user agent, debugging, background color) shall be configurable through `WebViewController`. 7. All standard lifecycle events shall be emitted: `onWebViewCreated`, `onPageStarted`, `onPageFinished`, `onProgress`, `onWebResourceError`, `onNavigationRequest`, `onUrlChange`, and `onConsoleMessage`. 8. Additional controller methods shall function: `clearCache`, `clearLocalStorage`, scroll position controls (`getScrollX`, `getScrollY`, `scrollTo`, `scrollBy`), and `setOnPlatformWebViewCreated`.  **Technical Requirements:** 1. **Minimum OS:** Windows 10 version 1809 (Build 17763) or later with the WebView2 Evergreen Runtime installed. 2. **Architecture:** x64 (AMD64) shall be supported; ARM64 is optional for the initial implementation. 3. **Implementation:** Native code shall be written in C++/WinRT or C# utilizing WebView2 Win32 APIs, communicating with Dart via Flutter Platform Channels (MethodChannel/EventChannel). 4. **Window Management:** The implementation shall properly handle Win32 window embedding, resizing, DPI awareness, and keyboard focus within the Flutter view hierarchy. 5. **Runtime Detection:** The plugin shall detect WebView2 Runtime availability at initialization and throw a descriptive `PlatformException` if missing, including guidance for runtime installation.  **Acceptance Criteria:** 1. The `webview_flutter` example application compiles and executes on Windows 10/11 without Dart code modifications. 2. All example app features (navigation, JavaScript channels, cookies, custom headers, settings) behave identically to iOS/Android implementations. 3. The plugin passes the existing automated platform interface test suite when run on a Windows CI environment. 4. Bidirectional JavaScript-Dart messaging completes successfully with message delivery latency <100ms. 5. Documentation is updated to designate Windows as a supported platform and explicitly state the WebView2 Runtime prerequisite. 6. No regressions occur in existing iOS, Android, or Web platform implementations.

issue_title: [libs] Add `TcpStream::keepalive` and `TcpStream::set_keepalive`
requirement: ## Requirement: Add `TcpStream::keepalive` and `TcpStream::set_keepalive`  ### Summary Extend the library's `TcpStream` type with two public methods for inspecting and configuring TCP keepalive behavior, bringing it in line with the keepalive APIs already offered by the underlying socket layer.  ### API  ```rust impl TcpStream {     /// Returns the currently configured TCP keepalive idle interval.     ///     /// * `Ok(Some(duration))` – keepalive is enabled and probes are sent after     ///   the given period of inactivity.     /// * `Ok(None)` – keepalive is disabled.     /// * `Err(_)` – the underlying socket option could not be read.     pub fn keepalive(&self) -> io::Result<Option<Duration>>;      /// Enables or disables TCP keepalive on this stream.     ///     /// * `Some(duration)` – enable keepalive probes, sent after the given     ///   period of inactivity.     /// * `None` – disable keepalive probes.     ///     /// Returns an `io::Error` if the socket options could not be applied.     pub fn set_keepalive(&self, keepalive: Option<Duration>) -> io::Result<()>; } ```  ### Functional requirements 1. `set_keepalive` must be able to both enable and disable keepalive on an already-connected `TcpStream`, and must be effective without re-connecting or re-binding the socket. 2. `keepalive` must reflect the state last requested through `set_keepalive` (or the state inherited from the socket), returning the idle interval that the operating system actually applies. 3. Implementation must use the standard `SO_KEEPALIVE` socket option to enable/disable keepalive, combined with the platform-specific idle-time option (e.g. `TCP_KEEPIDLE` on Linux, `TCP_KEEPALIVE` on macOS/BSD, the Windows SIO_KEEPALIVE_VALS/`TCP_KEEPALIVE` equivalent) to express the duration. 4. Platform limitations (e.g. an OS that does not expose a configurable idle time) must be handled gracefully: the methods should return an error or `None` rather than panic, and the behaviour must be documented per platform. 5. All OS-level failures must be surfaced as `io::Error` with the original error code/kind preserved. 6. The methods must borrow `&self` and must not consume, close, or otherwise invalidate the stream; they must be safe to call concurrently with reads/writes on the same stream. 7. The new methods must be exposed in the crate's public API surface (re-exported/prelude as appropriate) and documented with examples, including the OS-level caveats of enabling keepalive.  ### Acceptance criteria * A `TcpStream` on which `set_keepalive(Some(d))` was called reports `keepalive() == Ok(Some(d))` (subject to platform rounding of the interval) and `keepalive() == Ok(None)` after `set_keepalive(None)`. * Enabling keepalive on a socket results in the OS sending probes for a connection whose peer has stopped responding, and disabling it stops that behaviour. * Errors from `setsockopt`/`getsockopt` are propagated to the caller as `io::Error`. * Unit/integration tests cover: default state (keepalive disabled → `None`), enabling with a duration, reading back the value, disabling again, and error propagation for an invalid/unsupported configuration.

issue_title: [feature request] Global GPU Flag
requirement: **REQ-GPU-001: Global GPU Enablement Flag**  **Statement:** The system shall provide a single global flag that lets users enable or disable GPU acceleration for all supported components from one setting, without requiring per-component configuration.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. The system shall expose the global GPU flag through at least one of: a command-line option, an environment variable, or a configuration file entry. 2. The flag shall accept explicit enable and disable values, and shall default to a documented value (disabled unless the hardware and drivers are detected, or as specified by the maintainers). 3. When the flag is set to disabled, all components that support GPU execution shall use CPU execution paths only, and no GPU device shall be initialized. 4. When the flag is set to enabled and a compatible GPU is detected, all supported components shall use the GPU. 5. When the flag is set to enabled and no compatible GPU or driver is detected, the system shall either fall back to CPU execution and log a warning, or fail with a clear error message, as defined by a documented configuration option. 6. Per-component settings, if they exist, shall take precedence over the global flag only where explicitly documented. 7. The active GPU status (enabled/disabled, device selected, or fallback reason) shall be reported at startup in the logs or verbose output.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - Setting the flag to disabled results in zero GPU device allocations across all supported components, verified by test or by device monitoring. - Setting the flag to enabled on a system with a supported GPU results in GPU execution for all supported components, verified by test. - Setting the flag to enabled on a system without a supported GPU produces the behavior defined in item 5, and no crash occurs unless fail-fast mode is configured. - The flag is documented in user-facing documentation, including its default value, accepted values, and precedence rules. - Existing behavior is unchanged when the flag is not specified, unless the default is intentionally changed and noted in the release notes.

issue_title: Add support for visionOS
