AC-1: The project compiles successfully for visionOS with zero errors and no new warnings. - AC-2: The existing test suite passes when run against the visionOS destination. - AC-3: A sample application targeting visionOS integrates the project and exercises core functionality without runtime errors. - AC-4: Existing supported platforms show no behavioral or build regressions. - AC-5: Release metadata explicitly lists visionOS as a supported platform.

issue_title: crypto/tls: add PSK support
requirement: # Requirement: `crypto/tls` — Pre-Shared Key (PSK) Support  ## 1. Summary  The `crypto/tls` package shall provide support for TLS 1.3 pre-shared key (PSK) key exchange as specified in RFC 8446 §4.2.11, including external PSKs (§4.2.11.2). A client and a server shall be able to establish an authenticated, encrypted TLS 1.3 connection using a pre-provisioned shared secret instead of certificate-based server authentication, in both `psk_ke` (PSK-only) and `psk_dhe_ke` (PSK plus ephemeral (EC)DHE) modes.  ## 2. Scope  **In scope** - TLS 1.3 `pre_shared_key` extension, client and server sides. - External PSKs provisioned by the application (identity, key material, hash algorithm). - Binder generation and verification, PSK-based key schedule, `psk_ke` and `psk_dhe_ke` handshake flows. - Configuration API, connection-state reporting, documentation, and tests.  **Out of scope** - TLS 1.2 static-PSK cipher suites (RFC 4279). - 0-RTT/early data with external PSKs. - Key provisioning, storage, distribution, rotation, or lifecycle management for PSKs. - Any change to existing certificate-based or session-resumption behavior when no PSK is configured.  ## 3. Configuration API  The package shall expose an API that permits an application to:  - Configure one or more PSKs on a client, each consisting of an opaque identity, secret key material, and the hash algorithm to be used with that PSK (defaulting to SHA-256 when unspecified). - Configure PSKs on a server, either as a static set or through a lookup function invoked with the identity received from the client, returning the matching key material and hash algorithm. The lookup function shall be safe for concurrent use and shall not be permitted to return PSK key material in error text. - Observe, after a successful handshake, whether a PSK was negotiated and which identity was selected (for example, via fields on `ConnectionState`).  The API shall be additive: existing `Config` usage, defaults, and behavior shall remain unchanged when no PSK is configured.  ## 4. Client Requirements  1. When a PSK is configured, the client shall include a `pre_shared_key` extension in the ClientHello as the **last** extension, containing the offered identity and an `obfuscated_ticket_age` of zero for external PSKs. 2. The client shall compute the binder over the partial ClientHello transcript (all bytes up to and including the identities field, with binder-list length fields computed as if the list were empty), using the PSK's hash algorithm and the binder key derived per RFC 8446 §7.1. 3. The client shall offer a key share so that `psk_dhe_ke` can be negotiated, and shall tolerate a server that selects `psk_ke` (no key share in ServerHello). 4. Upon receiving a ServerHello containing `pre_shared_key`, the client shall:    - Verify that the extension is the last extension in the ServerHello; otherwise, abort with an `illegal_parameter` alert.    - Verify that the selected identity is one the client offered; otherwise, abort with an `illegal_parameter` alert.    - Verify the binder; on mismatch, abort with a `decrypt_error` alert. 5. The client shall derive handshake, master, and traffic secrets using the PSK-based key schedule (early secret derived from the PSK, `derived` secret for the handshake, etc.) as specified in RFC 8446 §7.1. 6. The client shall not offer an external PSK and a session-resumption PSK under the same identity namespace; external PSK identities and resumption identities shall remain distinguishable.  ## 5. Server Requirements  1. On receiving a `pre_shared_key` extension, the server shall look up the offered identity in the configured static set or via the lookup function. 2. If a matching PSK is found, the server shall verify the binder using the PSK's hash algorithm. If verification fails, the server shall abort the handshake with a `decrypt_error` alert and shall not fall back to a certificate-based handshake after having selected the PSK. 3. If no identity matches, the server shall not select a PSK; it shall either continue with a certificate-based handshake or, when configured for PSK-only operation, abort with an `unknown_psk_identity` alert. This behavior shall be documented. 4. The server shall select a TLS 1.3 cipher suite whose KDF hash matches the selected PSK's hash algorithm; if no such suite exists, the server shall not select the PSK. 5. The server shall support both modes:    - `psk_dhe_ke`: selected when the client supplied a key share and the server supports (EC)DHE; the (EC)DHE shared secret is combined with the PSK per the key schedule.    - `psk_ke`: selected when no usable key share is available or when configured; ServerHello contains no key share. 6. When a PSK is selected, the server shall not send a Certificate message (server authentication is provided by the PSK). The server may still request and verify a client certificate if configured to do so. 7. The server shall include the `pre_shared_key` extension in the ServerHello as the **last** extension, containing the selected identity and `selected_obfuscated_ticket_age` of zero.  ## 6. Wire Compatibility and Interoperability  1. Encoding and decoding of the `pre_shared_key` extension shall conform to RFC 8446 §4.2.11 (including the OfferedPSK, ServerPreSharedKey, and PskBinderEntry structures). 2. The implementation shall interoperate with other TLS 1.3 stacks that support external PSKs (e.g., OpenSSL 3.x and BoringSSL) in both `psk_ke` and `psk_dhe_ke` modes, with matching transcript hashes and key schedules. 3. A Go client and Go server shall interoperate with each other using PSKs, and each shall interoperate with a non-Go peer.  ## 7. Security Requirements  1. PSK key material shall be at least as long as the output size of the associated hash algorithm (e.g., 32 bytes for SHA-256); shorter keys shall be rejected with a clear, non-sensitive error. 2. Binder comparisons shall be performed in constant time. 3. PSK key material, binder values, and binder-derived secrets shall never appear in error messages, panic output, or log records, and shall not be written to `Config.KeyLogWriter`. 4. A resumption ticket identity shall never be accepted as an external PSK identity, and an external PSK identity shall never be accepted as a resumption ticket. 5. PSK use shall not weaken existing protections: certificate validation, downgrade protection, and the existing alert and error-handling conventions shall be preserved.  ## 8. Documentation  1. `Config` and any new exported types/functions shall have GoDoc describing usage, hash-algorithm constraints, cipher-suite/hash matching requirements, and the `psk_ke`/`psk_dhe_ke` selection behavior. 2. Package documentation and release notes shall describe PSK support and its limitations.  ## 9. Acceptance Criteria  1. A Go TLS 1.3 client and server configured with a shared PSK complete a handshake successfully in both `psk_ke` and `psk_dhe_ke` modes, and the negotiated connection reports that a PSK was used along with the selected identity. 2. Handshakes succeed against OpenSSL 3.x and BoringSSL peers configured with the same external PSK, in both modes, and derived secrets match the peer. 3. Negative cases behave as specified and do not panic or leak key material:    - Incorrect key → `decrypt_error`.    - Unknown identity → documented behavior (`unknown_psk_identity` in PSK-only mode, otherwise no PSK selected).    - Hash algorithm mismatch between PSK and selected cipher suite → PSK not selected or handshake failure, never a silently invalid handshake.    - Server selects an identity the client did not offer, or the `pre_shared_key` extension is not last → `illegal_parameter`. 4. Binder computation and the PSK key schedule are validated against known-answer test vectors (e.g., published RFC/BoringSSL vectors). 5. The existing `crypto/tls` test suite continues to pass unchanged, and the new API is backwards compatible (no breaking changes to existing exported identifiers or behavior). 6. `go vet` and `go test` complete cleanly, and the new code is covered by unit and integration tests.

issue_title: Initializing array of Option<T> using [None; n] syntax should not require std::marker::Copy for T
requirement: **Requirement: Array Initialization of Option<T> Without Copy Bound**  The language/library shall allow initializing an array of `Option<T>` using the repeat-expression syntax `[None; N]` without requiring `T: Copy`.  **Details:**  - The expression `[None; N]`, where `None` is of type `Option<T>` for any type `T`, shall compile and produce an array of `N` `None` values. - The trait bound `T: std::marker::Copy` shall not be imposed as a requirement for this initialization form. - The behavior shall be consistent for any `N` that is a valid constant array length. - Existing behavior for types that are `Copy` shall remain unchanged.  **Rationale:**  `None` carries no value of type `T`, so duplicating it does not require `T` to be copyable. Requiring `Copy` unnecessarily restricts array initialization for non-Copy types such as `String`, `Vec<T>`, or user-defined structs.

issue_title: Implement a Rendering Compositor
requirement: ## REQ-COMP-001: Rendering Compositor  **Description**  The system shall provide a rendering compositor: a component that combines multiple rendered layers (surfaces) into a single final output frame for presentation to the display. The compositor shall be responsible for layer management, transformation, blending, damage tracking, and frame presentation, and shall expose a documented public API for client integration.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **Layer Management** — The compositor shall accept and manage a hierarchy of composited layers, each representing a rendered surface (bitmap, texture, or render target), and shall support add, remove, reorder, and reparent operations via its public API. 2. **Transformations** — Each layer shall support per-layer position, size, scale, rotation, opacity, and z-order, applied by the compositor during composition. 3. **Blending** — The compositor shall perform alpha blending of overlapping layers using the source-over operator by default, with per-layer opacity; additional blend modes (e.g., source-in, additive) shall be supported as configurable options. 4. **Damage Tracking** — The compositor shall track dirty (damaged) regions between frames and re-composite only affected regions, unless a full-frame recomposition is explicitly requested or forced by structural changes to the layer tree. 5. **Frame Presentation** — The compositor shall produce a complete composited frame and present it to the display/swap chain, synchronizing with the display refresh rate (vsync) where available. 6. **GPU Acceleration with Software Fallback** — The compositor shall support GPU-accelerated composition via the platform graphics API (e.g., Direct3D, Metal, Vulkan, or OpenGL) and shall automatically fall back to CPU (software) composition when GPU resources are unavailable, with no functional regression. 7. **Public API** — The compositor shall expose a documented API enabling clients to: (a) create and destroy layers, (b) update layer content and properties, (c) request composition on a scheduled or on-demand basis, and (d) register callbacks for frame-completed notifications. 8. **Thread Safety** — All public compositor APIs shall be safe to invoke from the client thread, with internal synchronization protecting compositor state. 9. **Clipping** — The compositor shall support rectangular and path-based clipping of layers to arbitrary bounds.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  1. **Performance** — Composition of a typical scene (≤ 100 layers) shall complete within one display frame budget (≤ 16.6 ms at 60 Hz) on supported hardware; damaged-region recomposition shall outperform full-frame recomposition. 2. **Correctness** — Composited output shall match the defined compositing model (source-over alpha blending, sRGB color space) and shall be verified against reference renders in automated tests. 3. **Robustness** — The compositor shall handle empty layer trees, zero-size layers, and out-of-bounds geometry without errors or undefined behavior. 4. **Portability** — The compositor shall build and pass the test suite on all platforms supported by the project.  **Acceptance Criteria**  1. A test scene of overlapping, transformed, semi-transparent layers composites correctly and matches the reference output. 2. Updating a single layer triggers recomposition of only the damaged region, verified by instrumentation. 3. The compositor runs with GPU acceleration when available and degrades gracefully to software rendering when it is not. 4. All public APIs are documented, with automated test coverage for layer management, transformations, blending, and damage tracking. 5. Benchmarks demonstrate composition within the stated frame budget on target hardware.  **Out of Scope (initial implementation)**  Hardware video overlay planes, non-affine (3D perspective) layer transforms, and animated property timelines; these may be addressed in follow-up requirements.

issue_title: Add support for variadic functions (varargs) to GDScript
requirement: **Requirement ID:** REQ-GDSCRIPT-042 **Title:** Native Variadic Function (Varargs) Support in GDScript **Priority:** High **Status:** Proposed  **Description:** GDScript shall provide first-class syntactic and semantic support for declaring and invoking variadic functions that accept a variable number of arguments at the call site, with integrated type safety and reflection capabilities.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **Declaration Syntax:** The language shall support a distinct syntax for variadic parameters (e.g., `...args` or `args: Array` marked as variadic), permitting a function signature of the form `func identifier(required_params..., ...variadic_param)` where the variadic parameter is syntactically distinguished from standard collection parameters.  2. **Argument Count Flexibility:** A variadic function shall accept zero or more arguments at the variadic position during invocation without requiring the caller to construct an explicit Array.  3. **Static Type Safety:** When a type annotation is applied to the variadic parameter (e.g., `...values: int`), the compiler shall enforce at compile-time that every argument passed at the variadic position conforms to the specified type. Untyped variadic parameters shall accept arguments of any type, subject to standard GDScript dynamic typing rules.  4. **Internal Access Semantics:** Within the function body, the variadic arguments shall be accessible as an ordered, read-only collection (exposed as an `Array`) containing all arguments passed at the variadic position, preserving invocation order.  5. **Parameter Composition:** Functions shall support mixing required positional parameters, optional parameters with default values, and exactly one variadic parameter, with the constraint that the variadic parameter must appear last in the parameter list.  6. **Inheritance Compatibility:** Variadic methods shall be overridable in derived classes. An override shall be valid if its variadic parameter type is identical to or a supertype of the base class's variadic type, or if both are untyped.  7. **Reflection and Introspection:** The GDScript reflection API (e.g., `ClassDB`, `MethodInfo`) shall expose metadata indicating whether a method is variadic, the index of the variadic parameter, and the minimum number of required arguments.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  8. **Performance:** Variadic function invocation shall not incur performance overhead exceeding 5% compared to an equivalent manually constructed Array argument.  9. **Backward Compatibility:** The introduction of variadic syntax shall not alter the parsing, semantics, or runtime behavior of existing GDScript source code.  **Constraints:**  10. The variadic parameter shall be restricted to the final position in the function signature. 11. The feature shall function correctly in both statically-typed (`static func`) and dynamically-typed contexts. 12. Variadic parameters shall be compatible with existing GDScript calling conventions, including named argument invocation where applicable.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - **AC-1:** Given `func log(level: String, ...messages)`, the call `log("INFO", "a", "b")` shall execute successfully with `messages` bound to `["a", "b"]` inside the function body. - **AC-2:** Given `func sum(...nums: int)`, the call `sum(1, 2, "three")` shall be rejected by the static type checker with a type mismatch error. - **AC-3:** Given a variadic method in a base class, a derived class override with the same variadic signature shall compile and execute correctly, with polymorphic dispatch functioning as expected. - **AC-4:** `MethodInfo.is_variadic()` (or equivalent) shall return `true` for variadic functions and `false` otherwise; `MethodInfo.args` shall reflect the total parameter count including the variadic collection. - **AC-5:** Calling a variadic function with zero variadic arguments (e.g., `log("INFO")`) shall be valid and bind the variadic parameter to an empty Array.

issue_title: Enable "hot reload" (not just "hot restart") for Flutter Web
requirement: **Requirement: Hot Reload Support for Flutter Web**  The Flutter Web development workflow shall support hot reload, in addition to the existing hot restart capability, so that developers can apply Dart source code changes to a running web application without losing its current application state.  **Functional Requirements**  1. The `flutter run -d chrome` (and `flutter run -d web-server`) command shall accept the interactive hot reload key (`r`) and the IDE hot reload action, and apply code changes to the running web application. 2. Hot reload shall preserve the current application state, including widget tree state, navigation stack, and in-memory variables, where the changed code is compatible with the existing state. 3. When a hot reload cannot be applied (for example, due to changes to global initializers, `main()`, or class structure that the Dart web compiler cannot patch), the tool shall report a clear message to the developer and indicate that a hot restart (`R`) is required. 4. Hot reload on Flutter Web shall use the Dart Development Compiler (DDC) incremental compilation and module reloading mechanism so that only changed modules are recompiled and reloaded in the browser. 5. Hot reload shall complete within a target latency comparable to mobile and desktop targets (under approximately 2 seconds for typical incremental changes in a medium-sized project), and the duration shall be reported to the developer. 6. Hot reload shall be supported in Chrome and Edge, and for any other browser the Flutter tool officially supports for debugging. 7. The developer shall be able to disable hot reload for web targets through a documented flag or configuration option, falling back to hot restart only. 8. Hot reload status, success, and failure events shall be visible in the console output and in the IDE integration (VS Code and Android Studio/IntelliJ) through the existing Flutter daemon protocol.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  1. Hot reload shall not introduce regressions in the behavior of hot restart or in the production build output (`flutter build web`). 2. The feature shall be covered by automated integration tests in the Flutter tool test suite that verify reload success, reload rejection with a fallback message, and state preservation. 3. Documentation shall be updated to describe hot reload behavior, limitations on Flutter Web, and the relevant commands and keyboard shortcuts.  **Acceptance Criteria**  - Running `flutter run -d chrome`, modifying a widget's build method, and pressing `r` updates the browser view without a full page reload and retains the current widget state. - Modifying `main()` or a top-level initializer and pressing `r` results in a clear message instructing the developer to use `R`. - The IDE hot reload action triggers the same behavior as the `r` key.

issue_title: Improve the performance of the GDScript VM
requirement: **Requirement ID:** REQ-GDSCRIPT-VM-PERF-001  **Title:** Improve Execution Performance of the GDScript Virtual Machine  **Type:** Non-functional requirement (Performance / Efficiency)  **Description:** The GDScript Virtual Machine (VM) interprets compiled GDScript bytecode at runtime. Its current execution overhead can degrade performance in script-intensive scenarios — such as per-frame game logic, large loops, frequent function calls, and heavy Variant operations — negatively affecting frame rates and application responsiveness.  **Requirement Statement:** The system shall optimize the GDScript Virtual Machine to reduce the runtime execution overhead of interpreted GDScript code, delivering measurably improved script execution performance relative to the current baseline implementation, while preserving full correctness, language semantics, and backward compatibility.  **Acceptance Criteria:** 1. The average execution time of representative GDScript benchmark workloads — including loops, function calls, property/member access, arithmetic and Variant operations, and coroutine/await handling — shall be reduced by at least 10% compared to the baseline implementation, with no individual workload regressing by more than 5%. 2. All existing GDScript unit, integration, and language conformance tests shall pass without modification, confirming unchanged language behavior. 3. Optimizations shall be transparent to developers; no changes to existing GDScript source code shall be required. 4. Debugger functionality (breakpoints, stepping, stack traces) and runtime error reporting for GDScript shall continue to operate correctly. 5. Peak and steady-state memory consumption of the VM shall not increase by more than 5% as a result of the optimizations. 6. Performance outcomes shall be validated using standardized benchmark suites and profiling on supported reference platforms, with before/after results documented.  **Constraints and Assumptions:** - Optimizations shall remain compatible with the existing GDScript module architecture and bytecode/project formats unless explicitly approved otherwise. - Improvements shall not introduce platform-specific behavioral divergences. - Correctness and stability take precedence over performance gains; no optimization may compromise defined language semantics.  **Priority:** High

issue_title: Add support for variadic functions (varargs) to GDScript
requirement: **Requirement: Variadic Function Support in GDScript**  GDScript shall support variadic functions, allowing a function to accept a variable number of arguments in a single call.  1. **Declaration:** A function shall be declarable with a variadic parameter (e.g., a rest/varargs parameter prefixed by a defined marker such as `...`) that must be the final parameter in the signature.  2. **Collection:** When called, all arguments supplied beyond the fixed parameters shall be collected into an array-like value bound to the variadic parameter, preserving argument order.  3. **Zero arguments:** If no extra arguments are supplied, the variadic parameter shall be bound to an empty array rather than causing an error.  4. **Type handling:** Variadic arguments shall accept values of any Variant type unless a type constraint is explicitly declared, in which case mismatched arguments shall produce a compile-time error where statically determinable and a runtime error otherwise.  5. **Spreading:** A call site shall be able to pass an existing array as the variadic portion using a spread operator, expanding its elements as individual arguments.  6. **Validation:** The compiler shall reject declarations where the variadic parameter is not the last parameter, or where more than one variadic parameter is declared, with a clear diagnostic message.  7. **Default values:** Fixed parameters preceding the variadic parameter may retain default values; the variadic parameter itself shall not accept a default value.  8. **Compatibility:** Existing GDScript functions and call semantics shall remain unchanged; the feature shall not alter behavior of functions without a variadic parameter.  9. **Reflection:** Variadic functions shall be identifiable as such through the engine's method introspection APIs (e.g., `get_method_list()`), indicating the variadic flag in the method's metadata.  10. **Documentation:** The language reference shall document the syntax, semantics, and examples for variadic functions.

issue_title: Initializing array of Option<T> using [None; n] syntax should not require std::marker::Copy for T
requirement: **REQ-001 — Array repeat initialization with `Option<T>` shall not require `T: Copy`**  When an array with element type `Option<T>` is initialized using the repeat-expression syntax `[None; n]` (equivalently `[Option::<T>::None; n]`), the compiler shall accept the expression for all types `T`, including types that do not implement `std::marker::Copy`, and shall not emit a missing-`Copy` trait-bound error for such expressions. The resulting array shall be semantically equivalent to an array whose elements are all the `None` variant of `Option<T>`. This exemption shall apply only to repeat expressions whose repeated operand is the `None` variant of `Option<T>`; repeat expressions with any other non-`Copy` operand (e.g., `[Some(value); n]`) shall continue to be subject to the existing `Copy` or constant-operand requirements.

issue_title: Implement PlatformView support on macOS
requirement: # Requirement: PlatformView Support on macOS  ## 1. Background  Flutter's `platform_views` framework allows a Flutter application to embed native platform views (an `NSView` on macOS, a `UIView` on iOS, an `AndroidView` on Android) directly inside the Flutter widget hierarchy, positioned, sized, z-ordered, and hit-tested by the Flutter compositor.  Today, iOS and Android provide the native half of this contract:  * **Dart/Flutter layer** — `UiKitView` / `AndroidView` widgets built on the generic `PlatformViewLink` widget and the `PlatformViewFactory` callback API. * **Embedder layer** — a `FlutterPlatformViewsController` that owns registered view factories, a `FlutterPlatformViewFactory` protocol implemented by the embedder to instantiate the native view, and a compositor that can place platform views into the Flutter scene.  The macOS embedder (`shell/platform/darwin/macos`) implements none of this. As a result:  * There is no macOS equivalent of `UiKitView`; no public Dart API can request an `NSView` be embedded. * The macOS embedder does not own a platform-views controller, so no view factories can be registered, and the engine has no place to route `flutter/platform_views` create/dispose/set-parameter messages. * The macOS scene graph/compositing path has no platform-view layer support, so even a natively created `NSView` could not be positioned or composited relative to Flutter content.  ## 2. Goal  Provide end-to-end support for embedding native AppKit `NSView`s inside Flutter applications on macOS, so that a Flutter developer can write:  ```dart MacOSView(   viewType: 'macos_text_field',   creationParams: const {'placeholder': 'Type here'},   onPlatformViewCreated: (id) { /* id is an opaque handle to the native view */ }, ) ```  and see a live, interactive native view rendered at the correct position inside the Flutter scene.  ## 3. Scope  ### 3.1 In scope  1. A public Dart widget for macOS platform views, plus any supporting Dart plumbing. 2. Routing of the platform-view protocol messages (`create`, `dispose`, `set parameters`) on the macOS embedder. 3. A platform-views controller in the macOS embedder that owns view factories and their lifetime. 4. A macOS implementation of the embedder-side platform-view factory protocol that creates and owns an `NSView`. 5. Composition, layout, clipping, opacity, and z-ordering of platform views relative to Flutter content on macOS. 6. Hit testing and input forwarding (mouse, keyboard, and Flutter-declared gesture recognizers) to the native view. 7. Lifecycle integration: engine detach, window/Flutter-view teardown, hot restart, and app termination. 8. Documentation and a runnable example.  ### 3.2 Out of scope  1. **Hybrid composition** (rendering the native view into a texture and forwarding a separate touch stream). Only the standard, non-hybrid platform-view composition is required. 2. Changes to iOS, Android, Windows, or Linux platform-view behavior, except where shared code must be refactored to be platform-neutral (such refactoring must not change existing platform behavior). 3. A general-purpose `NSView` → Flutter texture bridge unrelated to the `platform_views` protocol. 4. New capabilities for the Windows embedder.  ## 4. Functional Requirements  ### FR-1 — Dart platform-view widget  * **FR-1.1** The Flutter framework shall expose a public widget for macOS native views (proposed name: `MacOSView`), exported from `package:flutter/widgets.dart` alongside `UiKitView` and `AndroidView`. * **FR-1.2** The widget shall be implemented on top of the existing generic `PlatformViewLink` widget and `PlatformViewFactory` API so that the same creation/parameter/dispose protocol is used on all platforms. * **FR-1.3** The widget shall accept, at minimum:   * `viewType` (String) — identifies the registered native factory;   * `creationParams` (Object?) and `creationParamsCodec` (MessageCodec?) — passed to the native factory at creation;   * `onPlatformViewCreated` (callback) — invoked once the native view has been created and the engine has acknowledged it;   * `hitTestBehavior` — one of `transparent`, `opaque`, `translucent`, mirroring `UiKitView`;   * `gestureRecognizers` — Dart-side gesture recognizers forwarded to the native view. * **FR-1.4** Like `UiKitView`, the widget shall assert that `defaultTargetPlatform == TargetPlatform.macOS` and fail with a descriptive assertion error when used on another platform. * **FR-1.5** The widget shall support being placed inside scrollables, slivers, and other layout constraints; the native view shall track the widget's position, size, and clipping rectangle on every frame in which they change. * **FR-1.6** The `viewType` namespace used by macOS shall be distinct from the iOS namespace so that a shared Dart codebase can register both an iOS `UiKitView` factory and a macOS factory without collisions (e.g., an explicit platform prefix applied by the macOS widget).  ### FR-2 — Protocol plumbing  * **FR-2.1** The macOS embedder shall register the platform-view service channel/extension so that `flutter/platform_views` messages originating from the Dart `PlatformViewLink` are delivered to the engine's platform-view handling path. * **FR-2.2** Creation requests shall carry the `viewType` and the creation parameters encoded with the codec supplied by the Dart caller; the default `StandardMessageCodec` shall be used when none is specified. * **FR-2.3** The embedder shall send the "platform view created" acknowledgement back to Dart after the native view has been instantiated and installed, so that `onPlatformViewCreated` fires exactly once per platform view. * **FR-2.4** Parameter updates sent from Dart after creation shall be delivered to the native view/factory instance, in order, on the platform (main) thread.  ### FR-3 — Platform-views controller and factory registration  * **FR-3.1** The macOS embedder shall provide a platform-views controller, owned by the `FlutterEngine`, that:   * allows a client to register a view factory for a given view type;   * creates a platform view when a creation message arrives;   * disposes a platform view when a dispose message arrives;   * tears down all platform views when the engine is detached or shut down. * **FR-3.2** Registration APIs shall be public API of the macOS framework (headers shipped with the embedder), and shall be callable from Objective-C and Swift. * **FR-3.3** Registering a factory for a `viewType` that already has a factory shall replace the previous factory deterministically, log a warning, and dispose any live views created by the replaced factory — behavior consistent with the existing iOS embedder. * **FR-3.4** All controller, factory, and view operations shall be executed on the main/platform thread.  ### FR-4 — Native view creation  * **FR-4.1** The macOS embedder shall implement the embedder-side platform-view factory protocol (proposed: `FlutterPlatformViewFactory`) with a creation method equivalent to `createWithFrame:args:` returning an object that exposes the created `NSView`. * **FR-4.2** The factory shall receive the creation arguments as a dictionary decoded by the codec negotiated with Dart (default: `StandardMessageCodec`). * **FR-4.3** The created `NSView` shall be retained by the platform-view wrapper object, added to the Flutter view hierarchy as a subview, and positioned according to the layout information supplied by the engine. * **FR-4.4** The native view must not be added to the view hierarchy until the engine has supplied a valid frame; the first applied frame shall be the correct one. * **FR-4.5** If the factory returns `nil`, throws, or the view type is unregistered, the embedder shall report a structured error to Dart (via the platform-view channel / `FlutterError` reporting) rather than crashing the app.  ### FR-5 — Disposal and lifetime  * **FR-5.1** On a dispose message, the embedder shall remove the `NSView` from its superview, release it, and drop all references held by the embedder and the engine. * **FR-5.2** On engine detach/shutdown and on `FlutterView` teardown, all outstanding platform views shall be disposed as in FR-5.1. * **FR-5.3** Disposal shall be idempotent; a double dispose shall not crash. * **FR-5.4** Dart-side removal of the widget shall result in a native dispose message; the Dart widget shall not leak its `RenderObject` or callbacks.  ### FR-6 — Composition and rendering  * **FR-6.1** The platform view shall be composited into the Flutter scene by the macOS embedder's compositor/layer tree so that its content is visible on screen and interleaved with Flutter-drawn content at the correct z-order. * **FR-6.2** Position, size, and opacity of the native view shall be updated whenever the corresponding Flutter widget's layout changes, with no visible tearing or stale placement. * **FR-6.3** Clipping induced by Flutter ancestors (e.g., a `ClipRect` or a scroll viewport) shall be honored by the platform view. * **FR-6.4** The native view shall be composited by the platform (AppKit/Core Animation), not rasterized into a Flutter texture. Hybrid composition is explicitly out of scope (see §3.2). * **FR-6.5** The embedder shall not block the Flutter raster thread while creating, moving, or resizing a platform view.  ### FR-7 — Input, hit testing, and gestures  * **FR-7.1** Mouse clicks, drags, scroll wheel, and keyboard input shall be delivered to the native view when the pointer is over it. * **FR-7.2** `hitTestBehavior` shall be honored:   * `opaque` — the platform view absorbs all pointer events in its bounds;   * `transparent` — pointer events pass through to Flutter content behind the view;   * `translucent` — the platform view and the Flutter content behind it both receive events. * **FR-7.3** Flutter gesture recognizers declared on the widget shall be registered with the native view so that Flutter-level gestures (e.g., a Flutter-implemented drag) continue to work over the platform view. * **FR-7.4** Focus shall move to and from the native view correctly when it is tapped and when it is removed.  ### FR-8 — Accessibility and semantics  * **FR-8.1** The native view shall remain accessible to macOS assistive technologies through the normal AppKit accessibility hierarchy. * **FR-8.2** Platform views shall not appear as opaque nodes in the Flutter semantics tree, matching iOS/Android behavior.  ### FR-9 — Error reporting and diagnostics  * **FR-9.1** Unregistered `viewType`, factory failure, and malformed creation parameters shall surface as `FlutterError`s that reach `FlutterError.onError` / the Flutter error handler with a message identifying the view type. * **FR-9.2** The embedder shall log creation, disposal, and errors at a level consistent with the rest of the macOS embedder, and shall not log creation parameters that may contain sensitive data at default log levels.  ## 5. Non-Functional Requirements  | ID | Requirement | |----|-------------| | NFR-1 | The feature shall support all macOS deployment targets already supported by the macOS embedder (no increase in the minimum deployment target). | | NFR-2 | Creating a platform view shall not drop more than one frame at 60 Hz in the reference example; scrolling a Flutter list containing a platform view shall sustain 60 fps on supported hardware. | | NFR-3 | Repeated create/dispose cycles (≥ 1000) shall not leak native memory, and shall not leave orphaned subviews in the Flutter view hierarchy. | | NFR-4 | The implementation shall be thread-safe with respect to the platform thread; all AppKit operations occur on the main thread. | | NFR-5 | Public API additions shall follow the Flutter framework's API conventions (documentation, `@Since`/version annotations, null-safety, and API tests) and the macOS framework's existing header/visibility conventions. | | NFR-6 | The implementation shall not regress existing macOS functionality: rendering, input, text input, menus, window management, and hot restart must behave as before. |  ## 6. Deliverables  1. **Flutter framework (Dart)** — the macOS platform-view widget and any required adjustments to `PlatformViewLink`/`PlatformViewFactory` to make the mechanism multi-platform. 2. **Flutter engine (C++)** — any shared platform-view code changes required to support the macOS embedder (no behavior change for other platforms). 3. **macOS embedder (Objective-C/Objective-C++)** — platform-views controller, factory protocol and default implementation, layer/compositor support for platform views, input routing, and lifetime management. 4. **Public macOS framework headers** — the registration and factory protocols, documented and consumable from Objective-C and Swift. 5. **Example** — a macOS example app demonstrating at least two distinct native view types (e.g., an `NSTextField` and an `NSButton` or a custom `NSView` with drawing) inside scrolling and overlapping Flutter content. 6. **Documentation** — a macOS platform-view page describing registration of factories, creation parameters, hit-test behavior, and known limitations. 7. **Tests** — Dart unit/widget tests, and macOS embedder integration tests covering creation, parameter update, disposal, and error paths.  ## 7. Acceptance Criteria  | # | Criterion | |---|-----------| | AC-1 | A macOS app that registers a factory for view type `X` and places `MacOSView(viewType: 'X')` displays the corresponding native `NSView` on screen, correctly positioned and sized within the Flutter hierarchy. | | AC-2 | The native view is interactive: it accepts clicks and typed text, and Flutter content behind it remains interactive per the chosen `hitTestBehavior`. | | AC-3 | Moving and resizing the Flutter widget updates the native view's frame in the same frame, with no flicker or misplaced content. | | AC-4 | Removing the widget from the tree removes the native view from the view hierarchy and releases it; no `NSView` subviews remain after the widget is disposed. | | AC-5 | Creating and disposing a platform view 1000 times in a loop produces no memory growth detectable by Instruments and no crash. | | AC-6 | Multiple simultaneous platform views are composited with the correct relative z-order, including interleaving with Flutter-drawn content. | | AC-7 | Requesting an unregistered `viewType` produces a `FlutterError` delivered to the app's error handler; the app does not crash. | | AC-8 | Closing the window or detaching the engine disposes all platform views without leak or crash. | | AC-9 | Hot restart does not crash and does not leave stale platform views on screen. | | AC-10 | The example app builds and runs on all macOS deployment targets supported by the embedder, and the existing macOS example and integration tests continue to pass unchanged. |  ## 8. Definitions  * **Platform view** — a native view instance embedded in the Flutter widget hierarchy, addressed on the Dart side by an opaque integer id and on the native side by an `NSView` wrapper. * **View factory** — a native callback registered for a `viewType` that instantiates platform views of that type. * **Hybrid composition** — rendering native content into a Flutter texture and separately forwarding input; explicitly excluded here.  ## 9. References  * Flutter `platform_views` framework: `packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/platform_view.dart`, `PlatformViewLink`, `PlatformViewFactory`, `PlatformViewCreationParams`. * iOS embedder analogues: `FlutterPlatformViewsController`, `FlutterPlatformViewFactory`, `FlutterPlatformView` in `shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Headers` and `Source`. * macOS embedder: `shell/platform/darwin/macos/framework/Source` (`FlutterEngine`, `FlutterView`, `FlutterViewController`) and its `Headers`. * Engine platform-view infrastructure: `shell/common/platform_view.h`, `shell/common/platform_view_registry.*`.

issue_title: Table > TableRow > TableCell colspan
requirement: REQ-TABLE-001: TableCell colspan Support  The Table component shall support the `colspan` attribute on TableCell elements nested within TableRow components. The system shall allow a TableCell to span multiple columns by specifying a positive integer value for the `colspan` property (e.g., `<TableCell colspan={2}>`), causing the cell to occupy the specified number of columns in the table grid layout.  Constraints: 1. The `colspan` property shall default to `1` when not specified. 2. The `colspan` value shall be rendered as the corresponding `colspan` HTML attribute on the underlying `<td>` element. 3. The sum of `colspan` values across a TableRow shall not exceed the total number of columns defined in the Table; the system shall validate or gracefully handle rows where the total exceeds the column count. 4. The `colspan` property shall be compatible with existing TableCell properties (e.g., alignment, padding, styling) and shall not affect column width calculations for other rows.  Acceptance criteria: - A TableCell with `colspan={N}` renders as `<td colspan="N">` and visually spans N columns. - A TableCell without an explicit `colspan` value renders with a default span of 1 column. - Table headers and body rows both support `colspan` consistently.

issue_title: rustdoc: `--enable-index-page` integration with cargo?
requirement: ## Requirement: Support rustdoc's index page when building documentation with Cargo  ### Background  `rustdoc` has an (unstable) `--enable-index-page` flag that makes it emit an `index.html` page at the root of the generated documentation, listing the crates/modules it knows about so that a reader landing on the documentation root has an entry point into the whole set of docs. Today this flag is only usable by invoking `rustdoc` directly (and only on nightly with `-Z unstable-options`), so users who build documentation through `cargo doc` — including workspaces with several crates — have no such index and no way to discover the other crates from the root of `target/doc`.  ### Requirement  1. **`cargo doc` must accept an `--enable-index-page` option.**    - `cargo doc --enable-index-page` enables index-page generation for the documentation produced by the invocation.    - The option must be accepted on the stable toolchain (i.e. Cargo enables the corresponding unstable rustdoc behavior itself and does not require the user to pass `-Z unstable-options`); if stability is not achievable, Cargo must clearly report that the option requires nightly and point at the tracking issue.    - The option must be usable together with the existing `cargo doc` flags (`-p`, `--workspace`, `--all`, `--no-deps`, `--open`, `--target-dir`, etc.).  2. **Cargo must forward the request to rustdoc correctly.**    - Cargo must arrange for exactly one index page to be produced at the root of the output directory (`target/doc/index.html`), even when documenting multiple packages in one invocation.    - rustdoc invocations that Cargo makes for individual crates must not each overwrite or conflict with the shared index page.  3. **Contents of the index page.**    - The index must list every crate that was documented as part of the invocation, with a link to each crate's own documentation root.    - When documenting a workspace with several members, all members that were documented must appear, so that a user can navigate from the index to any of them.    - Crates excluded from the build (e.g. via `-p` selection or `--no-deps` for non-workspace dependencies) must not be listed.    - The page must be valid HTML, consistent with rustdoc's existing styling/assets, and must not break the `--open` behavior of `cargo doc` (i.e. opening the docs should show a usable landing page).  4. **Configuration and documentation.**    - The behavior should also be reachable through a Cargo configuration key (e.g. `[doc] index-page = true`) so it can be enabled persistently, consistent with other Cargo configuration options.    - `cargo doc --help` and the Cargo documentation must describe the new option, its stability, and its interaction with `--no-deps`, `-p`/`--workspace`, and `--all`.  5. **Non-goals / compatibility.**    - Existing `cargo doc` behavior and output layout must be unchanged when the option is not passed (no `index.html` is added to `target/doc`).    - The change must not alter the output of `rustdoc` when invoked directly.

issue_title: Implement namespaces in GDScript
requirement: Requirement: Namespace Support in GDScript  1. Overview GDScript shall support namespaces so that classes, functions, constants, and other named declarations can be grouped under a hierarchical qualifier to avoid naming collisions and to organize code across scripts.  2. Functional Requirements 2.1 A namespace declaration shall group named members under a single identifier, and may be nested within other namespaces. 2.2 Members of a namespace shall be accessible from outside the namespace using qualified names (e.g., `NamespaceName.MemberName`), with nested access using dot-separated paths. 2.3 Namespaces shall be definable within a single script file and, where applicable, across multiple script files that contribute to the same namespace. 2.4 Within a namespace, members shall be referenceable by their unqualified names without requiring the qualifier. 2.5 An import or using-style mechanism shall allow bringing a namespace's members into the current scope without full qualification, with explicit handling of ambiguous names. 2.6 Namespace identifiers shall participate in the existing scope and name-resolution rules, and a namespace name shall not conflict with a local variable, function, or class name in the same scope without a diagnostic error.  3. Compatibility Requirements 3.1 Existing GDScript code that does not use namespaces shall continue to compile and execute with unchanged behavior. 3.2 Existing class_name declarations shall remain valid and globally accessible as before.  4. Tooling Requirements 4.1 The GDScript parser shall report clear compile-time errors for undefined namespaces, duplicate member names within the same namespace, and circular namespace nesting. 4.2 The language server shall provide autocompletion and go-to-definition for namespace members.  5. Non-Functional Requirements 5.1 Namespace resolution shall occur at compile time where possible and shall not introduce measurable runtime overhead for member access. 5.2 Documentation shall be updated to describe namespace syntax, scoping rules, and migration guidance.

issue_title: Add procedural and parametrizable audio support
requirement: The system shall support procedural, parametrizable audio generation, enabling audio to be synthesized programmatically at runtime (e.g., via oscillators, noise generators, and synthesis primitives) rather than relying solely on pre-recorded audio assets. It shall be possible to define and instantiate sounds by specifying parameters such as frequency/pitch, amplitude/volume, waveform type, duration, envelope (attack/decay/sustain/release), and effects (e.g., filtering, modulation), and these parameters shall be modifiable dynamically at runtime, including on a per-instance basis. The feature shall expose a clean API (callable from code and/or configurable via data files) so that developers can create, configure, and update sounds without requiring pre-baked audio files, while remaining compatible with existing audio playback functionality.

issue_title: plugin: add Windows support
requirement: **Requirement: Windows Platform Support for the Plugin**  The plugin shall be installable, loadable, and fully functional on Microsoft Windows operating systems (Windows 10 and later, 64-bit), with behavior equivalent to the existing supported platforms (Linux and macOS).  Specifically, the plugin shall:  1. **Installation:** Install successfully via the project's standard installation methods on Windows, including handling of Windows-specific paths, file permissions, and executable extensions. 2. **Runtime compatibility:** Load and execute without errors on Windows, using path separators, line endings, and file system semantics appropriate to Windows. 3. **Feature parity:** Provide all functionality available on existing platforms, or explicitly document any platform-specific limitations. 4. **Dependencies:** Use only dependencies that are available and supported on Windows, or provide documented alternatives. 5. **Build and packaging:** Produce Windows-compatible build artifacts and include Windows in the project's continuous integration test matrix. 6. **Documentation:** Document Windows installation steps, prerequisites, and any known limitations.  **Acceptance criteria:** - The automated test suite passes on Windows in CI. - A clean Windows installation can install and run the plugin by following the documented steps without manual workarounds. - No functionality regresses on Linux or macOS as a result of the Windows support changes.

issue_title: Add ability to ignore tests at runtime.

Ignored tests should be clearly reported as skipped, along with an optional reason, so that test results accurately distinguish ignored tests from passed or failed ones.

issue_title: Support home and lock screen widgets
requirement: **Requirement: Home Screen and Lock Screen Widget Support**  **ID:** REQ-WIDGET-001 **Priority:** Should Have **Status:** Proposed  **Description:** The application shall provide widgets that can be placed on the device's home screen and lock screen. Widgets shall display key application information at a glance and allow users to perform defined quick actions without fully opening the application.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. The system shall offer at least one widget type for the home screen and at least one for the lock screen, using the platform's native widget framework. 2. Users shall be able to add, resize (where the platform supports it), configure, and remove widgets through the standard platform widget picker or gallery. 3. Widgets shall display current data from the application and refresh automatically at a defined interval and upon relevant data changes. 4. Tapping a widget shall open the application to the relevant screen or item. 5. Widgets shall support at least one quick action where the platform permits it, such as marking an item complete. 6. Widgets shall provide a configuration option to select the displayed content when the platform supports widget configuration. 7. Widgets shall display a placeholder or preview in the widget picker.  **Non-Functional Requirements:** 1. Widget data refresh shall not exceed the platform's background update limits and shall not noticeably reduce battery life. 2. Widgets shall render within 1 second of being placed or refreshed under normal conditions. 3. Sensitive data shall not be displayed on the lock screen unless the user explicitly enables it in settings. Lock screen widgets shall show a generic or redacted state when the device is locked and the user has not opted in. 4. Widgets shall respect the system light, dark, and accessibility text size settings. 5. Widgets shall provide accessible labels for screen readers.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - A user can add a home screen widget and a lock screen widget from the platform's widget picker. - Widget content matches application data within the defined refresh interval. - Tapping a widget opens the correct screen in the app. - Lock screen widgets hide sensitive content by default and display it only after the user opts in. - Widgets function on the minimum supported OS version, and the feature degrades gracefully on platforms without lock screen widget support. - Widgets pass automated UI tests for rendering across light and dark themes and at the largest accessibility text size.  **Out of Scope:** - Third-party widget plugins or a custom widget SDK. - Widgets on platforms without native widget frameworks.
