issue_title: cmd/compile: implement powerpc 32-bit backend (ppc32)
requirement: # Requirement: `cmd/compile` — Implement a 32-bit PowerPC (`ppc32`) Backend  **ID:** REQ-COMP-PPC32 **Type:** New architecture port / major compiler feature **Component:** Go toolchain (`cmd/compile`, `cmd/internal/obj`, `cmd/link`, `cmd/dist`, `cmd/go`, runtime, stdlib) **Status:** Draft for implementation  ---  ## 1. Summary  Add support for a new 32-bit, big-endian PowerPC architecture, identified by the `GOARCH` name `ppc`, to the Go toolchain. The deliverable is a complete, self-hosting-capable backend in `cmd/compile` (the `gc` compiler) together with the minimum surrounding toolchain, runtime, and standard-library support required to build, link, and test Go programs for `ppc`.  The backend is expected to be derived from the existing 64-bit big-endian PowerPC backend (`ppc64`) by introducing a distinct 32-bit ABI and word size while reusing the PowerPC instruction encodings, register numbering, and instruction-selection knowledge already present in the tree.  ---  ## 2. Problem Statement  The Go toolchain currently supports `ppc64` (big-endian 64-bit PowerPC) and `ppc64le` (little-endian 64-bit PowerPC) but provides no support for 32-bit PowerPC. Users deploying Go software to legacy 32-bit PowerPC systems (older AIX/Power Macintosh hardware, embedded and telecom PowerPC boards, and long-life server SKUs such as POWER4/POWER5-based appliances running 32-bit Linux) cannot build Go programs for these targets.  32-bit PowerPC remains a relevant target because:  - It supports the full Go programming model with a smaller address space, matching memory-constrained embedded devices. - The 32-bit ABI is a prerequisite for several legacy/embedded deployments and for parity with the existing 32-bit ports (`386`, `arm`, `mips`, `mipsle`, `wasm`). - It exercises the "narrow word" code paths in the compiler and runtime that are already required for `386`/`arm`.  No partial or experimental support exists today: `GOARCH=ppc` is unknown to `cmd/compile`, `cmd/link`, and `cmd/dist`.  ---  ## 3. Scope  ### 3.1 In Scope  1. A new 32-bit PowerPC object-code/assembler backend usable by `cmd/compile` and `cmd/internal/obj`. 2. A new `cmd/compile/internal/ssa` backend for `ppc32`, including generated rewrite rules, register allocation, and legalization of 64-bit operations on a 32-bit target. 3. Runtime support (including 32-bit assembly) sufficient to build and execute Go programs on `ppc`. 4. Minimal standard-library ports and adjustments required for `ppc` to compile cleanly and pass `go test all`. 5. Linker, build-system, and distribution integration (`cmd/link`, `cmd/dist`, `cmd/go`, `cmd/api`, `cmd/compile` test lists). 6. Automated test execution and CI wiring for the new architecture. 7. Documentation updates describing the new port.  ### 3.2 Out of Scope (Explicit Non-Goals)  - Performance parity with `ppc64` or with the C toolchain. Correctness and completeness are the goals of this requirement; optimization work is follow-on. - Little-endian 32-bit PowerPC (`ppcle`). Only big-endian `ppc` is in scope. (The naming `ppc` for big-endian mirrors the existing `ppc64`/`ppc64le` convention.) - New language features, changes to the Go language specification, or changes to the `gc` compiler architecture-independent framework. - Changes to `gccgo`. - Backporting `ppc` support to release branches; this targets the development branch only. - Assembler support for inline assembly written for 32-bit PowerPC by third parties is desirable but not a gate; the port must not regress existing `ppc64` inline assembly. - Vector (`AltiVec`/`VMX`) acceleration of the standard library beyond what is required for correctness.  ---  ## 4. Target Platform Definition ("`ppc32`" profile)  The following platform characteristics are normative for this port.  | Property | Value | |---|---| | `GOARCH` | `ppc` | | `GOOS` supported | `linux`, `netbsd`, `freebsd`, `openbsd` (each must build and pass tests) | | Endianness | Big-endian | | Word size | 32 bits (`int`, `uint`, `uintptr`, pointers = 4 bytes) | | Register size | 32-bit GPRs (`r0`–`r31`); 64-bit FPRs (`f0`–`f31`); 128-bit VRs available but not required for correctness | | Alignment | 4-byte maximum guaranteed alignment for all types; no 8-byte alignment guarantee | | `int` range | −2³¹ … 2³¹−1 | | Integer division | Native 32-bit `divw`/`divwu`; 64-bit division must be emulated | | 64-bit atomic ops | **Not available** in hardware — must be implemented via runtime helpers with locking, as on other 32-bit ports | | 64-bit multiply | `mullw`/`mullwo` provide low word; full 64-bit product requires runtime helper | | 64-bit shifts/rotates | `rldicl`/`rldicr`/`rldic`/`rldimi` operate on 64-bit registers only; 32-bit forms (`slw`, `srw`, `sraw`, `srawi`, `rlwinm`) are required for 32-bit shifts | | Floating point | IEEE-754 single and double; hardware FP supported; FMA optional | | C ABI | ELF32 PowerPC System V ABI (`linux/ppc`); SysV for BSDs | | Stack | Stack-based (ABI0) argument passing initially, matching `ppc64`'s current ABI posture; register ABI (ABIInternal) is a separate, later effort | | Maximum address space | 2 GiB user address space (per 32-bit process limits) |  **Constraint:** The target must not assume any 64-bit-only hardware instruction is available without a correct software fallback.  ---  ## 5. Functional Requirements  ### 5.1 Compiler Backend — `cmd/internal/obj` (new `ppc` package)  - **FR-1.1** The compiler must accept `GOARCH=ppc` and select a dedicated 32-bit PowerPC backend, distinct from the `ppc64` backend, that emits ELF32 (or the appropriate object format per `GOOS`) PowerPC objects. - **FR-1.2** The backend must implement the `obj.Prog` interface (`Preprocess`, `Rewrite`, `Assemble`, `progString`, `Arch`, `canMergeSym`, etc.) and register itself in the architecture dispatch tables (`cmd/internal/obj/arch.go`). - **FR-1.3** The backend must provide correct relocation and symbol handling for the supported `GOOS` values, including `R_ADDR32`, `R_CALL`, `R_PCREL*`, and any architecture-specific TLS relocations required by `linux/ppc`. - **FR-1.4** The backend must support the full instruction set required by the compiler backend, including:   - Integer: `add`, `addc`, `addi`, `addic`, `subf`, `subfic`, `neg`, `mullw`, `mulli`, `mullwo`, `divw`, `divwu`, `and`, `andc`, `oris`, `ori`, `xor`, `xori`, `nand`, `nor`, `eqv`, `extsb`, `extsh`, `cntlzw`, `slw`, `srw`, `sraw`, `srawi`, `rlwinm`, `rlwimi`, `cmpw`, `cmplw`, `cmpiw`.   - 64-bit helper-equivalent sequences (emulated) for `divd`, `divdu`, `mod`, `modu`, `mul` (64-bit product), and 64-bit shifts when expressed on 32-bit registers.   - Floating point: `fadd`, `fsub`, `fmul`, `fdiv`, `fmadd`/`fmsub`/`fnmadd`/`fnmsub`, `fmr`, `fabs`, `fneg`, `fctiw`, `fctiwz`, `fcfid`/`fcfid` (double↔int), `fctid`/`fctidz`, `fcmpo`, `fcmpu`, `frsp`, `mffs`/`mtfsf`, `lfs`, `lfd`, `stfs`, `stfd`.   - Memory: `lbz`, `lbzu`, `lbzx`, `stb`, `stbu`, `stbx`, `lhz`, `lhzu`, `lhzx`, `sth`, `sthu`, `sthx`, `lwz`, `lwzu`, `lwzx`, `stw`, `stwu`, `stwx`, `lfs`, `lfsx`, `lfd`, `lfdx`, `stfs`, `stfsx`, `stfd`, `stfdx`, `lmw`, `stmw`.   - Atomic: `lwarx`/`stwcx.` (and `lharx`/`sthcx.` where applicable) for 32-bit atomics.   - Branch: `b`, `bl`, `bc`, `bclr`, `bct`, `bcctr`, `blrl`, `mtlr`, `mtctr`, `mflr`, `isync`, `sync`, `lwsync`. - **FR-1.5** The backend must implement 32-bit PowerPC calling-convention handling: argument/result placement in stack frames, save/restore of callee-saved registers (`r14`–`r31`, `f14`–`f31`, `lr`, `ctr`, `xer`, `cr` fields), frame pointer and stack-map (pointer maps for GC) maintenance, and correct handling of the `R_CALL`/`R_PCREL` call sequence used by the linker. - **FR-1.6** The backend must emit correct DWARF or Go-specific unwind/frame metadata (`pclntab`, `funcdata`) sufficient for stack traces, `runtime.Callers`, and panic unwinding to work on `ppc`. - **FR-1.7** The backend must implement `obj.Link`/`obj.AddUser`/sym-datum handling such that `-S` assembly output, symbol dumps, and `go tool objdump` work.  ### 5.2 SSA Backend — `cmd/compile/internal/ssa`  - **FR-2.1** A new SSA backend package (`cmd/compile/internal/ssa/_gen/ppc32.rules` plus supporting code) must be created for the `ppc32` architecture, registered in the architecture switch in `cmd/compile/internal/ssa/compile.go`. - **FR-2.2** The SSA backend must define the `ppc32` `Arch` description: `ArchFamily = "ppc"`, `ArchWordSize = 4`, `ArchBigEndian = true`, `ArchHasFloat32/64 = true`, `ArchLinkPtrSize = 4`, and the correct `Arch` register mapping for integer, float, and (optional) vector registers. - **FR-2.3** Rewrite rules must be generated and checked in (`go generate ./cmd/compile/internal/ssa/_gen`), and `cmd/compile/internal/ssa/_gen/generic.rules` rewrites must apply correctly to `ppc32`. - **FR-2.4** The backend must legalize all 64-bit integer operations available in the SSA IR onto 32-bit hardware:   - 64-bit `ADD`/`SUB`/`AND`/`OR`/`XOR`/`NOT` — decomposed into 32-bit half-word operations with correct carry/borrow propagation.   - 64-bit `MUL` — via `mullw`/`mullwo` plus shift-add, or via a runtime helper, producing an exact 64-bit result.   - 64-bit `DIV`/`DIVU`/`MOD`/`MODU` — via runtime helper routines (software 64-bit division) that are correct for all inputs, including sign handling, division by zero (`panic` with `runtime.Error` of type `runtime.Error` / integer divide by zero), and `MinInt64 / -1` overflow (must panic, not silently wrap).   - 64-bit `LSHL`/`LSHR`/`ASHR` — decomposed using 32-bit shift instructions plus branchless conditional correction for shift counts ≥ 32.   - 64-bit `CMP`/`CMPQ` — decomposed into high/low half comparison.   - 64-bit `Extend`/`SignExtend`/`Trunc` conversions between 32-bit and 64-bit types. - **FR-2.5** Float↔int conversions must handle the full 32-bit ranges correctly, and 64-bit integer ↔ `float64` conversions must use helper routines that are correct at the boundaries (e.g., values above 2⁵³, and `MinInt64`). - **FR-2.6** The register allocator must be correct under register pressure: the `ppc32` backend must not require more than 32 simultaneously live integer values; spills must be correct. The implementation should avoid emitting `R_NONE`/unassigned registers. - **FR-2.7** The backend must support the Go 1.17+ "register ABI" framework gracefully: if `ppc32` initially uses the stack-based ABI (ABI0) exclusively, the SSA backend must emit code that is ABI0-only and must reject or correctly handle ABIInternal argument passing until the register ABI is implemented (a clear, explicit decision is required, documented in the code). - **FR-2.8** Memory operations in SSA must respect 4-byte alignment assumptions, and the backend must not introduce unaligned 64-bit loads/stores; `runtime.memmove`, `runtime.memclr`, and bulk copy paths must be used where alignment is not guaranteed. - **FR-2.9** Bounds-check elimination and other generic SSA optimizations must remain enabled and must not produce incorrect code for `ppc32`.  ### 5.3 Runtime Support  - **FR-3.1** Runtime assembly for 32-bit PowerPC must be provided: `runtime/asm_ppc.s` (or an equivalently named file), including the bootstrap sequence, `mstart`, `rt0_go`, `gogo`, `mcall`, `morestack`, `badmorestack`, `panic`, `goPanic`, `goPanicIndex`, `goPanicSlice`, `mapassign`, `mapaccess`, `mapdelete`, `mapiterinit`, `mapiternext`, `mapiternextkey`, typed memory operations, and GC support stubs as applicable for the chosen GC mode. - **FR-3.2** The runtime must provide correct implementations of 64-bit arithmetic helper functions used by the compiler backend: 64-bit signed/unsigned division and modulo, 64-bit multiplication, and any 64-bit shift helpers. - **FR-3.3** `sync/atomic` 64-bit operations (`AddInt64`, `LoadInt64`, `StoreInt64`, `CompareAndSwapInt64`, etc.) must be implemented correctly on `ppc` using the standard 32-bit-port strategy (mutex-protected helpers in `runtime` or `sync/atomic` with the platform-specific files added), including correct alignment handling. - **FR-3.4** The garbage collector must correctly trace and scan `ppc` stacks and globals, including correct pointer maps and `runtime.KeepAlive`/`runtime.SetFinalizer` semantics. - **FR-3.5** `runtime.memmove`, `runtime.memclr`, `runtime.duffcopy`, and `runtime.duffzero` must be implemented for `ppc`. - **FR-3.6** The runtime must support `GOMAXPROCS` > 1 correctly, including correct handling of the 32-bit `runtime·sched` structures and memory ordering (`sync/atomic` fences) — note that 32-bit PowerPC Linux typically requires explicit `sync`/`isync` barriers around critical sections where the kernel or hardware does not provide them. - **FR-3.7** Signals, `os/signal`, and `runtime/debug` must function: the runtime must install a signal trampoline in 32-bit PowerPC System V ABI and correctly convert signal frames to Go frames for `panic` reporting. - **FR-3.8** The runtime must implement `runtime.osyield`, `runtime.procyield`, and `runtime.check()` correctly with 32-bit PowerPC instructions (`or 1,1,1` style yield, `isync`/`sync` as appropriate). - **FR-3.9** The runtime must provide `runtime.vdsoCall*`/`clock_gettime` fast paths or a documented fallback if the 32-bit PowerPC vDSO is unavailable or insufficient. - **FR-3.10** If the selected GC implementation depends on architecture-specific assembly (e.g., write barriers, `gcWriteBarrier`), that assembly must be ported to 32-bit PowerPC, or the port must use the generic (non-assembly) implementation.  ### 5.4 System Calls and OS Interface  - **FR-4.1** `syscall` package support must be added for `linux/ppc` (and any additional supported `GOOS`), including `syscall.Syscall`, `syscall.RawSyscall`, `syscall.Syscall6`, `syscall.RawSyscall6`, `syscall.Getrlimit`, `syscall.Setrlimit`, `syscall.Setrlimit`, `syscall.Getrusage`, `syscall.Sysinfo`, `syscall.Getpid`, and `syscall.Exec`-family entry points. - **FR-4.2** `syscall` constants and structures must be defined for 32-bit PowerPC (e.g., `SYS_*` numbers for the `ppc` syscall table, `Stat_t`, `Rlimit`, `Timespec`, `Tms`, `Waitmsg`, `Sigset_t`, `Flock_t`, `Dirent` sizes, `Getdirentries`, `Epoll`/`EpollEvent` layout, `Fadvise`, `Fallocate`, `Pselect6`, `Ppoll`, `Uname`, `Utsname`). - **FR-4.3** `os`, `os/exec`, `net`, `net/http`, `time`, `internal/poll` must build and function for `ppc`; `os/user` and `os/exec` lookups must be correct given the 32-bit `getpwuid`/`getgrgid` ABI. - **FR-4.4** `internal/syscall/unix` must provide `linux/ppc`-specific implementations where the shared generic code is insufficient. - **FR-4.5** `syscall` package must not be marked unsupported for the supported `GOOS` values.  ### 5.5 Standard Library Ports  - **FR-5.1** Architecture-specific standard-library files must be added or adapted for `ppc`, at minimum for:   - `internal/bytealg` (compare, equal, index, count, etc.)   - `math/big` (native 64-bit word assembly or pure-Go fallback; must be correct on 32-bit)   - `crypto/*` (e.g., `crypto/sha256`, `crypto/sha1`, `crypto/aes`, `crypto/elliptic` fallback), `crypto/rand`   - `encoding/binary` (pure Go, no changes needed), `hash/*`, `compress/*`   - `internal/cpu` feature detection for PowerPC (e.g., `IsPOWER8`, `IsPOWER9`, `HasVMX`) exposed via `internal/cpu` and `crypto/aes`/`crypto/sha*` where beneficial; must be correct and conservative.   - `unicode` tables, `regexp` — must build.   - `sync/atomic` — 64-bit operations per FR-3.3.   - `time` — timezone loading and monotonic clock must work.   - `runtime/cgo` — must compile and link for `linux/ppc` (32-bit PowerPC glibc/musl ABI), including `libc` symbol naming differences and the requirement of `_init`/`_thread` handling. - **FR-5.2** Any standard-library package that currently uses `//go:build` constraints keyed on the set of supported 32-bit architectures (e.g., `386 || arm || mips || mipsle || wasm`) must be updated to include `ppc`, or given a `ppc`-specific implementation where semantics differ (notably `math/bits`, `strconv`, `internal/itoa`, `reflect`, `unsafe`, `runtime`'s `map` implementation with 64-bit keys). - **FR-5.3** `reflect` must correctly report `PtrSize = 4` and handle `unsafe.Pointer` and `uintptr` semantics on 32-bit. - **FR-5.4** The `unsafe` package and `runtime` must correctly reject or handle pointer arithmetic that overflows 32 bits (e.g., `unsafe.Pointer` arithmetic, `uintptr` round-tripping through `syscall.Syscall`).  ### 5.6 Toolchain and Build-System Integration  - **FR-6.1** `cmd/link` must support the `ppc` architecture: correct address-size handling (32-bit relocation application, `R_ADDR32` sign extension), ELF32 output for `linux/ppc` and the appropriate formats for other supported `GOOS`, correct `pclntab` and `moduledata` layout for 32-bit, and correct handling of the `ELF32` header fields. - **FR-6.2** `cmd/dist` must build a `ppc` toolchain (including `compile`, `link`, `asm`, `pack`, `cgo`, `buildid`) and produce `go tool dist list` output containing the `ppc` targets. - **FR-6.3** `cmd/go` must support `GOARCH=ppc` for `go build`, `go test`, `go run`, `go install`, `go vet`, `go tool` operations, module handling, and `GOOS`/`GOARCH` cross-compilation checks (`go tool dist` / `cmd/go/internal/work` `knownOS/knownArch` tables, `cmd/go/internal/load` `badArch`/`sizes` tables). - **FR-6.4** The `cmd/go` internal `sizes` table must be extended with a `ppc` entry: `Sizes: "gc", "ppc", "ppc", 4, 4, 4, 0` — i.e., `WordSize 4`, `MaxAlign 4` (or 8 if 8-byte alignment is guaranteed; must be stated explicitly and consistent with the runtime), `PtrSize 4`. - **FR-6.5** `cmd/compile/internal/sys` (or its successor) must define `ArchFamily = "ppc"` for `ppc32`, mapping to the correct system call numbers and `ArchFamily` distinction from `ppc64` where required by the runtime. - **FR-6.6** `cmd/api` and `cmd/compile` API checks must not break when the new architecture is added. - **FR-6.7** `cmd/compile/internal/base`/`flag` handling must support the new architecture name and produce a clear error message for unsupported `GOOS`/`GOARCH` combinations (e.g., `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=ppc` must be rejected with a helpful message).  ### 5.7 Testing and CI  - **FR-7.1** `src/cmd/internal/testdir` (or the current equivalent of `src/test`) must include a `ppc` test directory with tests exercising the port, e.g.:   - `test/fixedbugs/` regressions specific to 32-bit PowerPC codegen.   - `test/typeparam/` — run on `ppc` with `GOARCH=ppc`.   - `cmd/compile/internal/ssa/_gen` "exhaustive" rule-checking test (`TestRewrite`) must pass for `ppc32` with **no unchecked rules** remaining, or with an explicitly documented, justified list of remaining rules. - **FR-7.2** `cmd/internal/testenv` / `cmd/compile` internal tests must be extended so that `GOARCH=ppc` compile-only tests run in CI. - **FR-7.3** `cmd/dist` builder configuration must include at least one `ppc` builder (emulated via QEMU `ppc` if real hardware is unavailable) to run `all.bash` (or the current `cmd/dist` test target) including `go test std`, `go test cmd`, and the `race`/`vet` suites where supported. - **FR-7.4** `cmd/go` "dist test" and `go test all` must pass for `ppc`. - **FR-7.5** The port must pass the `cmd/compile/internal/ssa` "TestOptimizes" and "TestGen" harnesses with all rules verified. - **FR-7.6** Benchmarks and `-race` support: the race detector requires 64-bit atomics; the race detector's `ppc32` support must either be implemented or explicitly documented as unsupported with a clear, actionable error message rather than a silent miscompile. **The race detector must never be silently incorrect.** - **FR-7.7** A `ppc` entry must be added to the "supported platforms" test matrix in `doc/` and to any `src/cmd/dist/build.go` `toolchain` cross-compile lists (e.g., `cmd/dist` cross-toolchain builds for `linux/ppc` must succeed).  ### 5.8 Documentation  - **FR-8.1** `doc/install/source.html` (or successor) must document `ppc` as a supported port with the list of supported operating systems. - **FR-8.2** `doc/go_spec.html` must mention 32-bit PowerPC in the list of architectures with `int`/`uint` of 32 bits. - **FR-8.3** `README.md`/`doc/` "portable" notes must be updated where the supported architecture list appears. - **FR-8.4** The `ppc32` implementation must include a design note (e.g., `src/cmd/internal/obj/ppc/README` or an internal doc) recording: the ABI decision (stack-based vs. register), the 64-bit legalization strategy, and the reasons for any deviation from the `ppc64` backend.  ---  ## 6. Non-Functional Requirements  - **NFR-1 (Correctness):** No miscompilation is acceptable. All of `go test std`, `go test cmd`, `go test all`, and the compiler's rule-verification tests must pass on `ppc` with zero failures. - **NFR-2 (No regression):** The `ppc64` and `ppc64le` backends, and all other architectures, must continue to pass all existing tests unchanged. Shared code refactoring must not alter `ppc64` codegen output in a semantically significant way; any intentional change must be accompanied by justification. - **NFR-3 (Portability of the port):** The implementation should minimize duplication with the `ppc64` backend where it can be done without entangling 32-bit and 64-bit assumptions. A clear boundary (separate packages, or well-isolated shared helpers) must exist so that future `ppcle` support is feasible. - **NFR-4 (Maintainability):** The backend must follow the conventions of existing architectures: use `cmd/internal/obj`'s `Prog` API, `ssa` `_gen` rules generated via `go generate`, `//go:build` constraints, and the `internal/goarch`/`internal/goexperiment` conventions of the branch. - **NFR-5 (Build hygiene):** The port must build with the toolchain's own `GOARCH=ppc` (self-hosting is not strictly required, but `cmd/compile` for `ppc` must be buildable by a `ppc64`/`amd64` toolchain and produce identical results). - **NFR-6 (Diagnostics):** Compiler and linker errors on `ppc` must be as informative as on other architectures; unsupported `GOOS`/`GOARCH` pairs must fail early with actionable messages. - **NFR-7 (Performance baseline):** The generated code should not be pathologically slow relative to `ppc64`; in particular, 64-bit arithmetic must not be implemented by repeated function calls in the common path where an inline sequence is possible. Performance tuning is not a release gate. - **NFR-8 (Security):** The port must not introduce exploitable memory-safety issues; in particular, 64-bit atomics and the GC must not have torn-read/torn-write windows.  ---  ## 7. Acceptance Criteria  The feature is considered complete when all of the following hold:  1. `GOOS=linux GOARCH=ppc go build std` succeeds. 2. `GOOS=linux GOARCH=ppc go test std` passes with zero failures on a `ppc` (or emulated `ppc`) target. 3. `GOOS=linux GOARCH=ppc go test cmd` passes. 4. `GOOS=linux GOARCH=ppc go test all` passes. 5. `cmd/compile/internal/ssa`'s rule-verification test passes for `ppc32` with no unaccounted-for rules. 6. `GOOS=linux GOARCH=ppc go build -race` either works correctly or fails with an explicit, documented "race detector not supported on ppc" error. 7. `cmd/dist` produces working `ppc` toolchain binaries, and `go tool dist list` includes `linux/ppc`, `netbsd/ppc`, `freebsd/ppc`, `openbsd/ppc`. 8. `cmd/link` produces working ELF32 `ppc` binaries that execute correctly, including correct `runtime` panics with usable stack traces. 9. 64-bit integer arithmetic (`int64`/`uint64`) is verified correct against `math/big` reference results across a randomized test suite, including boundary values (`MinInt64`, `MaxInt64`, `0`, `−1`, shifts by 0/31/32/63/64, division by `−1`, `MinInt64 / −1`). 10. `sync/atomic` 64-bit operations are verified correct under `-race`-free stress with concurrent accessors. 11. `ppc64`/`ppc64le` test results are unchanged (no regressions). 12. Documentation updates (FR-8.1–FR-8.3) are merged.  ---  ## 8. Dependencies and Prerequisites  - **`ppc64` backend availability:** The 32-bit backend depends on the existing `cmd/internal/obj/ppc` code for instruction encodings and the `cmd/compile/internal/ssa/_gen/ppc64.rules` for instruction-selection knowledge. These must exist and be in a maintainable state. - **`ppc64le` precedent:** The `ppc64le` port (introduced as a separate 32/64-bit-independent endianness variant) provides a precedent for how a new PowerPC variant was introduced and integrated. - **Emulation infrastructure:** QEMU user-mode `ppc` (`qemu-ppc`) is required for CI testing if physical 32-bit PowerPC hardware is unavailable. This is a hard prerequisite for automated test execution. - **Cross C toolchain:** A 32-bit PowerPC cross-compiler (e.g., `powerpc-linux-gnu-gcc`) is required for `cgo`-enabled builds and for `cmd/dist`'s cgo tests. - **Go release process:** The port must be proposed through the Go project's porting process, including assignment of a port owner/maintainer, per the project's contribution guidelines.  ---  ## 9. Risks and Mitigations  | Risk | Impact | Mitigation | |---|---|---| | 64-bit arithmetic legalization produces subtly incorrect code (especially shifts ≥ 32 and signed division) | Miscompilation, data corruption | Randomized differential testing against `math/big`; exhaustive testing over shift counts 0–63; explicit overflow tests | | 32-bit atomics absent → torn 64-bit reads | Memory corruption, security issue | Implement 64-bit atomics via locked helper routines (as `386`/`arm` do), never via naive load/store pairs | | Missing 8-byte alignment guarantee | SIGBUS on some platforms | Avoid 64-bit loads/stores unless alignment is known; use `memmove`/byte-wise access otherwise | | PowerPC memory model ordering (`isync` vs. `sync` vs. `lwsync`) differs from x86 | Rare, hard-to-debug concurrency bugs | Follow the Linux kernel's 32-bit PowerPC barrier requirements; document chosen barriers in the design note | | Substantial duplication with `ppc64` backend increases maintenance burden | Long-term cost | Isolate shared instruction-encoding tables; keep 32-bit-specific logic in a separate package; document the boundary | | Emulated CI is slow or flaky | Delayed feedback, CI instability | Run a fast "compile-only" subset per commit and the full suite nightly; pin QEMU version | | Race detector unavailable on `ppc32` | Reduced testing capability | Explicitly reject `-race` with a clear message until supported; do not ship a silently broken detector | | Register ABI (ABIInternal) not implemented | Lower performance, ABI divergence from other architectures | Acceptable for initial port (matches `ppc64`'s current state); track as follow-on work |  ---  ## 10. Open Questions  1. **ABI:** Should the initial `ppc32` port use only the stack-based ABI0 (matching current `ppc64` posture) or attempt ABIInternal from the start? *Recommendation: ABI0 only, with an explicit follow-on issue for the register ABI.* 2. **Naming:** Confirm `GOARCH=ppc` for big-endian 32-bit, reserving `ppcle` for little-endian 32-bit. Confirm consistency with `mips`/`mipsle` naming. 3. **Vector support:** Should `AltiVec`/`VMX` be exposed in the initial port, or deferred? *Recommendation: defer; expose only if the SSA backend requires it for correctness.* 4. **GC mode:** Use the current default GC for the branch, or opt into the newer GC if the branch has one? This affects the amount of 32-bit assembly required. 5. **Scope of `GOOS`:** Is `linux/ppc` sufficient for the initial milestone, with BSDs added afterwards, or must all four listed `GOOS` values ship together? 6. **`internal/cpu` feature detection:** Which PowerPC ISA levels (POWER6/7/8/9) should be detected and exposed, and to which `crypto` implementations should they be wired?  ---  ## 11. Definition of Done  - All functional requirements in §5 are implemented or explicitly waived in writing by the port owner. - All acceptance criteria in §7 are met and verified on a `ppc` target (real or emulated). - The design note (FR-8.4) is written and reviewed. - A port maintainer/owner is identified and recorded in the project documentation. - The port is announced in the project's release notes as a supported architecture.

issue_title: Implement a Set primitive to complement Dictionary and Array
requirement: **Requirement: Add a Set Primitive Data Structure**  **Summary:** Introduce a native Set primitive that stores a collection of unique values, complementing the existing Dictionary and Array primitives.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **Creation:** The system shall allow users to create an empty Set and a Set initialized from an existing collection (e.g., an Array or iterable). 2. **Uniqueness:** The Set shall store each value at most once. Adding a value that already exists shall leave the Set unchanged. 3. **Membership Test:** The system shall provide an operation to determine whether a given value is contained in the Set, returning a boolean result. 4. **Insertion:** The system shall provide an operation to add a value to the Set, returning the Set (or a success indicator) to support chaining. 5. **Removal:** The system shall provide an operation to remove a specified value from the Set, returning whether the value was present. 6. **Size:** The system shall provide a read-only property or operation returning the number of elements in the Set. 7. **Clearing:** The system shall provide an operation to remove all elements from the Set. 8. **Iteration:** The system shall support iteration over Set elements in insertion order, compatible with the language's existing iteration protocol used by Array and Dictionary. 9. **Conversion:** The system shall provide a conversion from Set to Array, and from Array (or iterable) to Set, for interoperability. 10. **Set Operations:** The system shall provide union, intersection, and difference operations that return a new Set without mutating the operands. 11. **Equality Semantics:** Value uniqueness shall use the same equality semantics as Dictionary key comparison, so that values considered equal by Dictionary keys are treated as duplicates in a Set.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  12. **Performance:** Membership tests, insertions, and removals shall have average-case time complexity of O(1). 13. **Consistency:** The Set API naming and behavior shall follow the conventions already used by the Array and Dictionary primitives. 14. **Documentation:** The Set type shall be documented with API reference entries and usage examples alongside the existing primitives. 15. **Testing:** Unit tests shall cover creation, uniqueness, membership, insertion, removal, iteration order, conversion, set operations, and edge cases (empty Set, duplicate inputs, mixed value types). 16. **Serialization:** If Dictionary and Array support serialization, the Set shall serialize and deserialize with the same guarantees.  **Out of Scope:** - Ordered set variants beyond insertion-order iteration. - Multiset or bag semantics.

issue_title: x/tools/gopls: support change signature refactoring
requirement: ### gopls change-signature refactoring  gopls shall provide a user-invoked **Change signature** source-code action, advertised with the LSP `refactor` code-action kind, for Go function and method declarations, including generic declarations. When invoked on a supported declaration, the action shall allow the user to specify a replacement parameter and result list.  The refactoring shall support:  - Adding, removing, renaming, and reordering parameters and results. - Changing parameter and result types. - Updating parameter and result identifiers, including naked returns, within the declaration body. - Updating all affected call sites known to the workspace, including calls in deferred and goroutine expressions, variadic calls, method calls, method expressions, function-valued uses, and tests. - Updating interface method declarations and their implementations when those declarations are affected. - Requiring caller-supplied expressions for newly added parameters rather than inventing argument values. - Adapting call-site result contexts when results are added, removed, or changed.  The action shall calculate the affected references using Go type information and return the declaration and reference edits as a single coordinated `WorkspaceEdit`. Applying the refactoring must not introduce new Go type-checking or compilation errors. Where a requested change cannot be represented unambiguously or would discard observable values, gopls shall leave all files unchanged and return an actionable diagnostic identifying the conflicting declaration or reference.  The implementation shall include unit tests for signature parsing and edit generation and integration tests that verify action discovery, coordinated updates to declarations and call sites, successful type-checking after application, and clear failures for unsupported changes. The feature and its limitations shall be documented, and existing gopls tests shall continue to pass.

issue_title: plugin: add Windows support
requirement: ## Requirement: Windows Support for the Plugin System  ### Summary The plugin framework currently assumes a Unix-like host operating system and therefore cannot be built, installed, or run on Windows. Windows must be recognized as a first-class supported platform for plugins.  ### Motivation Plugins are the primary extension mechanism of the project. Excluding Windows makes the plugin ecosystem unavailable to a large share of users and prevents contributors from publishing Windows-compatible plugins. Supporting Windows also unifies behavior across all supported platforms so that plugin authors need not maintain separate code paths per OS.  ### Functional Requirements  **1. Platform detection** - The plugin runtime must detect the host operating system at startup and expose the result to plugins (e.g., via a platform/OS identifier in the plugin API and in the resolved plugin metadata). - Platform-specific behavior must be selected at runtime rather than at compile time, so a single distributable artifact runs correctly on Linux, macOS, and Windows.  **2. Filesystem and path handling** - All plugin-related paths (plugin directories, manifest/config files, search paths, cache directories) must be built with a platform-aware path API; string concatenation with `/` must not be used. - Path comparison, canonicalization, and "is this path inside the plugin directory" checks must be case-insensitive on Windows and case-sensitive elsewhere, and must handle Windows path separators, drive letters, and UNC paths. - Symlink-based plugin linking must not be required: on Windows, plugins may be installed by copying, and any symlink usage must degrade gracefully with a clear error or fallback.  **3. Plugin discovery, installation, and lifecycle** - Discovery must walk plugin directories on Windows using native APIs (or equivalent abstractions) and must tolerate Windows-specific filesystem characteristics such as file locks, hidden/system attributes, and long paths. - Installation/uninstallation of plugins must work on Windows, including removal of plugin directories containing read-only files (attributes must be cleared before deletion) and of running plugin processes. - Plugin manifest parsing and validation must behave identically on all platforms; line endings (CRLF) in manifest files must be accepted.  **4. Process execution and IPC** - Launching plugin processes (e.g., language-server or helper binaries shipped by plugins) must use the correct executable resolution on Windows (`.exe`, `.cmd`, `.bat`, `.ps1` handling) and must not assume POSIX shell syntax. - Arguments containing spaces or non-ASCII characters must be passed without shell re-parsing surprises; quoting rules must follow the Windows command-line convention when the target is a native executable. - Environment variables, `PATH` lookup, home directory, and temp directory must be resolved using the Windows conventions (`%APPDATA%`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, `%TEMP%`, `%USERPROFILE%`). - Stdin/stdout/stderr piping, process termination, and orphan-process cleanup must work on Windows, including terminating a process tree.  **5. Build, packaging, and installation** - The plugin host and its build configuration must compile and pass the full test suite on Windows CI runners. - Release artifacts (binaries, archives, installers) must include a Windows variant, and archives must use a format that preserves the executable bit where applicable or otherwise restore it at install time on Windows. - Installation scripts and documentation must provide Windows-specific instructions (PowerShell and/or Command Prompt), and the Windows install path must be exercised by automated tests.  **6. Configuration and documentation** - Any plugin-related configuration file locations, default paths, and environment variable names must be documented for Windows. - The developer documentation must state that Windows is a supported platform and list the known limitations (e.g., no symlink-based plugin linking, feature parity notes).  ### Non-Functional Requirements - No regression on existing Linux/macOS behavior; existing plugin tests must pass unchanged on those platforms. - Platform-specific code must be isolated behind clearly named abstractions/modules so that platform logic is not scattered through the plugin implementation. - Cross-platform behavior must be covered by automated tests, including at least one Windows CI job running the plugin test suite.  ### Acceptance Criteria 1. The plugin system builds and its test suite passes on a Windows CI runner. 2. A plugin can be discovered, enabled, invoked, and uninstalled on Windows using the documented Windows paths and commands. 3. Plugins shipping helper executables are launched correctly on Windows, including executables with spaces in their path. 4. The documentation includes Windows installation and usage instructions and explicitly lists Windows as supported. 5. No POSIX-only API (e.g., `fork`, `chmod`-based semantics, `os.symlink` requirement, `/proc` access) is used in plugin code paths without an implemented Windows equivalent or a documented fallback.

issue_title: rustdoc: `--enable-index-page` integration with cargo?
requirement: # Requirement: Cargo Integration for rustdoc's `--enable-index-page`  ## 1. Background / Motivation  rustdoc provides an `--enable-index-page` option that, in addition to the per-crate documentation output, emits a top-level `index.html` page enumerating every crate included in the generated documentation set (the analogue of the crate index on docs.rs).  The option is currently only reachable when rustdoc is invoked directly. Users who build documentation through Cargo — the overwhelmingly common path, and the only path that documents a whole dependency graph or workspace at once — have no way to enable it. Every workaround today involves manually locating Cargo's target directory, re-invoking rustdoc by hand with the correct `--extern`/`-L` flags and crate list, and hand-assembling the index page.  Cargo should therefore support enabling rustdoc's index-page generation as a first-class, documented feature of `cargo doc`.  ## 2. Scope  **In scope** - `cargo doc` gains a way to request that rustdoc generate the index page. - The flag must be propagated to every rustdoc invocation Cargo makes in the build (all crates in the selected packages/workspace and their documented dependencies). - The behavior must be selectable both ad hoc (command line) and persistently (Cargo configuration), consistent with how other rustdoc-affecting Cargo options are handled. - Documentation and diagnostics (help text, unstable-feature gating if applicable) must be updated.  **Out of scope** - Changes to rustdoc's index-page rendering, layout, or the set of crates it lists. - `cargo doc --open` / docs.rs-style index behavior beyond enabling the existing rustdoc feature. - Any new indexing, search, or cross-referencing functionality.  ## 3. Functional Requirements  ### FR-1: Command-line interface `cargo doc` must accept a boolean option that enables index-page generation, e.g.  ``` cargo doc --enable-index-page ```  The option: - Applies to the whole invocation, not to a single crate. - Is accepted together with the existing `--no-deps`, `--document-private-items`, `--all-features`, `--workspace`, etc. - Must not be silently ignored when a package selection (`-p`) narrows the build.  ### FR-2: Propagation to rustdoc When the option is enabled, Cargo must pass the corresponding rustdoc flag to **every** rustdoc process it spawns during the build, including: - the selected package(s) / workspace members, - dependency crates that are documented because `--no-deps` was not passed.  When the option is not enabled, Cargo's rustdoc invocation must be byte-for-byte identical to today's behavior (no new flag, no changed flag ordering that would alter output).  ### FR-3: Configuration-file support The option must be settable in Cargo configuration so users do not need to repeat it on every invocation: - `.cargo/config.toml` under a `[doc]` table (e.g. `enable-index-page = true`), and/or - `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`-style metadata if that is deemed the more appropriate home.  Precedence must follow Cargo's standard rule: command-line flags override environment variables, which override config files, which override built-in defaults. The default is `false`.  ### FR-4: Interaction with rustdoc's own requirements rustdoc may require additional information to build a complete index (for example, the set of crates participating in the build, or knowledge that it is part of a multi-crate documentation build). Cargo is responsible for supplying this information via the mechanism rustdoc defines (additional flags, environment variables, or JSON input), and the two sides must agree on the contract. If rustdoc cannot construct a meaningful index for the current build (e.g. a single-crate build with no documented dependencies), Cargo/rustdoc must degrade gracefully rather than fail the build.  ### FR-5: Stability and gating If the underlying rustdoc option is nightly-only, the Cargo-side option must either: - be gated behind the same nightly-feature mechanism (e.g. `-Z` namespace / `cargo-features` declaration) and emit a clear, actionable error when used on stable, or - be stabilized in lockstep with rustdoc's option.  In all cases, using the option must never produce a confusing "unrecognized option" error from rustdoc.  ### FR-6: Diagnostics and errors - `cargo doc --help` must list the new option with a short description. - If the option is used in a context where it cannot take effect, Cargo must emit a `cargo`-level warning or error explaining why, rather than letting rustdoc fail with an obscure message.  ### FR-7: Output correctness With the option enabled, the generated documentation directory must contain a working `index.html` at its root that: - links to every documented crate's documentation, - is reachable from the documentation root of each crate, - does not break existing navigation, search, or redirect logic.  ### FR-8: Documentation - The Cargo book chapter on `cargo doc` must document the option, its config-file equivalent, its interaction with `--no-deps`, and its stability status. - The option must be included in the reference documentation and completion/help output where applicable.  ## 4. Non-functional Requirements - Zero measurable regression in `cargo doc` build times or output when the option is disabled. - The implementation must not require rustdoc to be re-run a second time or to be invoked outside Cargo's normal dependency-tracking model. - Must work on all platforms Cargo supports and must not introduce new external dependencies.  ## 5. Acceptance Criteria 1. `cargo doc --enable-index-page` in a workspace with two member crates produces a documentation tree whose root contains an `index.html` listing both crates and linking to each crate's docs. 2. The same command with `--no-deps` produces an index listing only the selected package(s). 3. Setting `enable-index-page = true` under `[doc]` in `.cargo/config.toml` produces the same result as the command-line flag; the command-line flag overrides a `false` config value. 4. `cargo doc` without the flag and without the config setting produces output identical to the pre-change behavior (verified by snapshot comparison of the generated directory listing). 5. `cargo doc --enable-index-page` on stable Cargo, when the underlying rustdoc option is unstable, fails with a clear message naming the required nightly flag/feature rather than an opaque rustdoc error. 6. `cargo doc --help` mentions the option; the Cargo book documents it. 7. Unit/integration tests exist covering: flag propagation to all rustdoc invocations, config precedence, `--no-deps` interaction, and the "no indexable crates" edge case.  ## 6. Open Questions - Should the option be named `--enable-index-page` (mirroring rustdoc) or use a Cargo-idiomatic name such as `--index`? The name should be decided in the Cargo/rustdoc joint tracking issue and kept aligned across Cargo, the book, and rustdoc. - Is a single "index page" concept sufficient, or should Cargo also expose rustdoc's per-section/module index options? - Should `[package.metadata.docs.rs]` be the canonical configuration location (matching docs.rs behavior) instead of `[doc]`?

issue_title: encoding/xml: add support for xml version 1.1
requirement: Requirement: XML 1.1 Support in encoding/xml  The encoding/xml package shall support XML 1.1 documents in addition to XML 1.0.  1. Parsing: When an XML declaration specifies version="1.1", the decoder shall accept and correctly process documents conforming to XML 1.1, including:    - The extended set of characters permitted in names and character data as defined by XML 1.1.    - Character references and line-end normalization rules specific to XML 1.1 (including treatment of NEL U+0085 and LINE SEPARATOR U+2028 as line-end characters).    - Character references to characters previously disallowed in XML 1.0 (such as U+0001 through U+001F, excluding U+0000) when written as numeric character references.  2. Version handling: The decoder shall recognize the version pseudo-attribute in the XML declaration and apply the rules for the declared version. Documents declaring version="1.0" shall continue to be processed under XML 1.0 rules, and unsupported version values shall produce a descriptive error.  3. Encoding: The encoder (Encoder/Marshal) shall be able to emit an XML declaration with version="1.1" when requested, and shall escape or encode content such that the produced output is well-formed under XML 1.1 rules.  4. Compatibility: Existing behavior for XML 1.0 documents shall remain unchanged, and no public API breakage shall be introduced; any new configuration for version selection shall be opt-in or inferred from the document's declaration.  5. Testing: The package shall include tests covering XML 1.1 parsing of extended names, line-end normalization, restricted character references, version-specific error cases, and round-trip encoding under XML 1.1.

issue_title: cmd/go: allow verifying vendored code
requirement: **Requirement: Verification of Vendored Dependencies by the `go` Command**  The `go` command shall provide a mechanism to verify that the contents of the `vendor` directory are consistent with the module requirements recorded in `vendor/modules.txt` and with the checksums recorded in `go.sum`.  **Functional Requirements**  1. The `go` command shall provide a verification operation (for example, `go mod vendor -verify` or `go vendor verify`) that checks the integrity of the vendored tree without modifying it. 2. For each vendored module, the verification shall confirm that:    - the module path and version listed in `vendor/modules.txt` match the corresponding entry in `go.mod`;    - the files present under `vendor/<module path>` match the content of the module as it would be obtained from the module cache or module proxy, using the hashes recorded in `go.sum`;    - no extra files or directories exist in the vendor tree that are not accounted for by `vendor/modules.txt`, and no expected files are missing. 3. The verification shall detect and report each discrepancy with the offending module path, the nature of the mismatch (missing, extra, modified, or version mismatch), and the file path where applicable. 4. The command shall exit with a non-zero status if any discrepancy is found and with status zero if the vendor tree is fully consistent. 5. The verification shall operate offline when the module cache already contains the required modules, and shall fail with a clear error rather than silently passing when required module data is unavailable. 6. The verification shall not alter the `vendor` directory, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, or `vendor/modules.txt`.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  1. Verification of a vendor tree shall complete in time proportional to the size of the vendored content, without requiring network access in the common case. 2. Output shall be deterministic so that it can be used in CI pipelines and reproducibility checks. 3. The feature shall be documented in the `go` command reference and be covered by tests for consistent, modified, missing, extra, and version-mismatched vendor trees.

issue_title: x/tools/gopls: support change signature refactoring
requirement: **Requirement: Change Signature Refactoring Support in gopls**  gopls shall provide a "change signature" code action that allows a user to modify the parameters and return values of a Go function, method, or interface method, and shall update all affected declarations and call sites across the workspace accordingly.  **Functional requirements:**  1. **Invocation:** The refactoring shall be available as a code action when the cursor is on a function or method name, or within its signature, in supported LSP clients.  2. **Supported operations:** The user shall be able to:    - Add a parameter, specifying its name, type, and position, and an argument expression to use at existing call sites.    - Remove a parameter, with all corresponding arguments removed from call sites.    - Reorder parameters.    - Rename a parameter.    - Change a parameter's type.    - Add, remove, or change return values.  3. **Call site updates:** All direct call sites of the target function or method in the workspace shall be updated to match the new signature. Where an added parameter has no supplied argument expression, the refactoring shall use the zero value of the type or request user input, and shall not silently produce non-compiling code.  4. **Method and interface consistency:** When the target is a method that satisfies or is part of an interface, the refactoring shall either update all implementing methods and interface declarations consistently or report a conflict and refuse to apply, rather than leave the program in a non-compiling state.  5. **Preview:** The refactoring shall present the set of proposed edits to the user before applying them, consistent with other gopls refactorings.  6. **Conflict detection:** The refactoring shall detect and report conflicts, including name collisions with existing parameters or identifiers, removal of parameters still referenced in the function body (unless the user confirms), and calls that cannot be rewritten automatically (such as function values passed by reference, reflection-based calls, or calls through interfaces with unknown implementations). Such cases shall be reported to the user rather than silently skipped.  7. **Correctness:** The resulting workspace shall compile, with the same package-level type-check results as before aside from the intended signature change, for all affected packages. Generated code and files excluded by build constraints shall be handled as documented.  8. **Formatting:** Modified declarations and call sites shall be formatted in accordance with gofmt conventions, and comments attached to changed parameters shall be preserved or moved with their parameters.  9. **Protocol:** The feature shall be implemented using standard LSP code action and workspace edit mechanisms, so that it works in any LSP client that supports them, without requiring client-specific extensions.  **Non-functional requirements:**  - The refactoring shall complete within a reasonable time on large workspaces, and shall run asynchronously with progress reporting where supported. - Test coverage shall include unit tests for each supported operation, multi-package call-site updates, interface/method consistency cases, and conflict-detection cases, using the existing gopls marker-test framework. - Documentation shall be added to the gopls refactoring reference describing the supported operations, limitations, and conflict behavior.

issue_title: Statically checked tensor shapes
requirement: **REQ-SHAPE-001: Static Tensor Shape Validation**  **Description:** The system shall perform compile-time (or static analysis-time) verification of tensor shapes across all operations to detect dimensional incompatibilities, invalid broadcasting, and shape mismatches prior to runtime execution.  **Priority:** High  **Acceptance Criteria:**  1. The system shall statically infer tensor shapes through data flow analysis and report compile-time errors when operations receive incompatible dimensions (e.g., matmul dimension mismatches, invalid broadcast rules, reshape size conflicts).  2. When static inference is impossible (e.g., dynamic input shapes), the system shall require explicit shape annotations or symbolic shape constraints, and shall validate operations against these constraints during static analysis.  3. Error diagnostics shall specify the exact operation node, the expected shape signature, and the actual inferred shape at the point of failure, with references to source code locations.  4. The static checker shall support symbolic dimensions (e.g., batch size `N`, sequence length `L`) to enable validation of operations involving dynamic shapes while ensuring compatibility of static dimensions.  5. The system shall integrate with language servers/IDEs to provide real-time shape validation feedback during code authoring, without requiring program execution.  6. Existing dynamic shape checking behavior shall remain as a runtime fallback for cases where static analysis cannot resolve shapes, ensuring no regression in runtime safety.

issue_title: cmd/compile: implement powerpc 32-bit backend (ppc32)
requirement: **Requirement: Add a 32-bit PowerPC (ppc32) Compiler Backend for the Go Toolchain**  The Go toolchain (`cmd/compile`, `cmd/asm`, `cmd/link`, and the runtime) shall support a 32-bit big-endian PowerPC target, selected with `GOARCH=ppc`, as a first-class architecture alongside the existing ppc64 and ppc64le targets.  **Functional requirements:**  1. **Compiler (SSA backend):** The compiler shall provide a ppc32 SSA backend that lowers Go SSA to 32-bit PowerPC instructions. This includes instruction selection, register allocation over the PowerPC register file, and block/branch lowering. 2. **Assembler:** `cmd/asm` shall accept ppc32 assembly syntax and encode instructions for the 32-bit PowerPC ISA, including the Go assembler conventions used by existing PowerPC backends. 3. **Linker:** `cmd/link` shall produce ELF32 big-endian executables and position-appropriate relocations for the ppc32 target, with correct handling of the TOC-free PowerPC 32-bit ABI. 4. **Calling convention and ABI:** The backend shall define and implement a register-based or stack-based calling convention compatible with the runtime, including argument/result layout, stack frame layout, and closure context register usage. 5. **Runtime:** The runtime shall support ppc32, including goroutine stack management, stack growth and split checks, the scheduler's context switching, signal handling, atomic operations, and memory allocation with 32-bit address space and pointer size. 6. **Floating point:** Hardware floating-point operations shall be supported. The backend shall also define behavior for a software floating-point mode if the target CPU lacks an FPU, or document its absence explicitly. 7. **Build constraints and platform support:** The `go/build` package and build tags shall recognize `ppc` as a valid GOARCH value. At minimum, linux/ppc shall be supported as a target OS/architecture pair. 8. **Standard library:** Packages that contain architecture-specific code (including `math`, `sync/atomic`, `internal/bytealg`, `syscall`, `os`, and `reflect`) shall provide ppc32 implementations or safe generic fallbacks.  **Non-functional requirements:**  9. **Correctness:** The `go test` suite (including `cmd/compile` codegen tests, `runtime` tests, and the standard library tests) shall pass on linux/ppc with no new failures compared with other 32-bit targets. 10. **Testing infrastructure:** The builders (`dashboard` / `misc/ports`) shall include at least one ppc32 builder that runs the core test suite on hardware or an emulator (such as QEMU user-mode or system-mode). 11. **Performance:** Generated code shall avoid unnecessary spills and redundant moves in common cases, and performance shall be measured against a baseline (such as the compiled output of comparable C code) using the standard benchmark suite. 12. **Documentation:** The port shall be documented in the Go release notes, the `GOARCH` list in the `go` command documentation, and the port status page, including supported OS targets, minimum CPU level, and known limitations. 13. **Maintainability:** The implementation shall follow the structure of existing backends (for example `cmd/compile/internal/ppc64`), keep architecture-specific code isolated behind build tags, and include sufficient code comments and tests to support future maintenance.  **Acceptance criteria:**  - `GOARCH=ppc go build` succeeds for a representative set of programs, and resulting binaries run correctly on a ppc32 Linux target or emulator. - `GOARCH=ppc go test std` passes on the designated ppc32 builder. - The `go tool dist list` output includes `linux/ppc`. - Codegen tests in `cmd/compile/internal/ssagen` and the `test/` directory pass for the ppc32 target.

issue_title: database/sql: missing escape functions
requirement: **Requirement: Add standardized SQL value escaping/quoting support to `database/sql`**  **Problem Statement** The `database/sql` package provides no API for safely escaping or quoting user-supplied values when constructing SQL statement strings. Although parameterized queries (placeholders) are the recommended approach, there are legitimate cases where placeholders cannot be used (e.g., identifiers, `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` clauses, dynamic DDL, drivers or stored procedures lacking placeholder support). Developers must currently implement escaping themselves or use third-party packages, creating inconsistent and potentially insecure behavior that can lead to SQL injection vulnerabilities.  **Functional Requirements** 1. The `database/sql` package shall expose an API for escaping string values destined for inclusion in SQL statements. 2. Escaping shall be delegated to the underlying driver via a new optional interface in `database/sql/driver` (e.g., a method such as `EscapeValue`), so dialect-specific rules are honored: quote characters, backslash handling, charset-specific sequences (e.g., GBK/Big5 multibyte injection), and null bytes. 3. If the active driver does not implement the escaping interface, the escape function shall return a well-defined error (e.g., "driver does not support escaping"); it must not silently apply a generic escaping algorithm that may be unsafe for the target database. 4. The escaping implementation shall correctly handle embedded quotes, backslashes, newlines, control characters, null bytes, empty strings, and non-ASCII/multibyte character sequences according to the driver's dialect. 5. Identifier quoting (table and column names) shall either be supported through the same mechanism or explicitly documented as out of scope. 6. Package documentation shall state when escaping is required, its limitations, and that parameterized queries remain the preferred defense against SQL injection.  **Constraints** - The change must be backward compatible: existing driver implementations remain valid; the new capability is opt-in via an optional driver interface. - Escaping semantics must match the target database's canonical escaping behavior (e.g., MySQL driver behavior equivalent to `mysql_real_escape_string`). - The escape function shall run in O(n) time relative to input length, with no unnecessary allocations beyond the escaped output.  **Acceptance Criteria** - For a driver implementing the escaping interface, a test corpus of adversarial inputs (quotes, backslashes, newlines, null bytes, multibyte sequences) is escaped such that the resulting SQL executes correctly and safely on the target database. - For a driver not implementing the interface, the escape function returns the documented error and never returns incorrect output. - Examples and security guidance are included in the package documentation.

issue_title: Add a Trait system for GDScript
requirement: **Requirement: Trait System for GDScript**  **Summary** GDScript shall support traits as reusable, composable units of behavior (methods, properties, and signals) that a class can incorporate without using inheritance. This allows code sharing across unrelated class hierarchies while keeping GDScript's single-inheritance model unchanged.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **Trait declaration:** The language shall provide a declaration construct (e.g., `trait Name`) in a GDScript file that may define methods, member variables, constants, and signals. 2. **Trait composition:** A script or inner class shall be able to incorporate one or more traits (e.g., `use TraitName` or `with TraitName`). Incorporated members shall be available on instances as if they were declared in the using class. 3. **Multiple traits:** A class shall be able to use multiple traits in a single declaration. 4. **Conflict detection:** If two incorporated traits, or a trait and the class body, define a member with the same name, the parser shall emit a compile-time error that identifies the conflicting names and sources. Resolution rules (such as explicit aliasing or exclusion) may be specified in a follow-up requirement. 5. **Override precedence:** A member defined directly in the class shall take precedence over an identical member supplied by a trait only if an explicit override marker is used. Otherwise, the conflict shall be reported per requirement 4. 6. **Abstract requirements:** A trait may declare method signatures without bodies. Any class using the trait must implement them, or the parser shall emit a compile-time error. 7. **Inheritance compatibility:** Traits shall work with `extends` in any combination. A class may extend a base class and use traits, and the base class's members shall be accessible from trait methods through `self`. 8. **Type and reflection support:** Methods and properties provided by traits shall be visible to `has_method()`, `get()`, `set()`, `get_property_list()`, and the editor's script inspection. 9. **Static analysis:** The GDScript analyzer and language server shall resolve trait members for autocompletion, go-to-definition, and type inference. 10. **Traits cannot be instantiated:** Attempting to instantiate a trait directly shall produce a compile-time error. 11. **Trait nesting:** Traits may use other traits. Cyclic trait usage shall produce a compile-time error. 12. **Runtime behavior:** Trait-provided methods shall execute with the same semantics as native class methods, including access to `self`, signals, and exported variables. Trait-provided exported variables shall appear in the Inspector for the using class.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  - No change to the behavior of existing GDScript code that does not use the new keywords. - Trait resolution shall occur at parse time where possible, with no measurable runtime overhead for method dispatch compared to equivalent hand-written methods. - Error messages shall include file, line, and column of the conflicting declarations.  **Acceptance Criteria**  - A script using two traits with non-overlapping members compiles and runs; all members are callable on instances. - A script with a name collision between two traits fails to compile with an error naming both traits and the member. - A trait requiring an abstract method fails to compile when a using class omits it, and compiles when implemented. - Autocompletion in the Godot script editor lists trait members on instances of using classes. - Existing GDScript test suite passes without modification.  **Out of Scope (for this requirement)**  - Conflict resolution syntax (aliasing or exclusion operators). - Traits in C# or GDExtension bindings. - Trait-based dependency injection or runtime trait application to existing instances.

Struct types shall integrate with GDScript's static typing system (typed variables, function parameters, and return types), support editor autocompletion and compile-time errors for unknown or mistyped fields, and be clearly represented in the debugger and serialization, distinct from Dictionaries and Objects.

issue_title: [RFC] TorchStore - A Shared-Memory Tensor Store
requirement: **Requirement: Shared-Memory Tensor Store (TorchStore)**  **Summary:** Provide a process-shared key-value store for PyTorch tensors that lets multiple processes on the same host publish and retrieve tensors through shared memory, without serializing tensor data through pickling or copying it through IPC pipes.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **FR-1 Store creation:** The system shall allow a user to create a named TorchStore instance with a configurable maximum capacity in bytes. 2. **FR-2 Attachment:** The system shall allow other processes on the same host to attach to an existing named store by name, with no data copy at attach time. 3. **FR-3 Put:** The system shall accept a `torch.Tensor` with a string key and store it in shared memory. Supported dtypes shall include all standard CPU dtypes supported by PyTorch (float16, bfloat16, float32, float64, int8–int64, uint8, bool). 4. **FR-4 Get:** The system shall return a `torch.Tensor` view over the shared memory region for a given key, without copying the underlying data, and shall raise a defined `KeyError`-equivalent exception if the key does not exist. 5. **FR-5 Delete and existence check:** The system shall support deleting a key and checking whether a key exists. 6. **FR-6 Overwrite semantics:** A put to an existing key shall replace the stored tensor atomically from the perspective of concurrent readers, meaning a reader sees either the old or the new tensor in full, never a partial write. 7. **FR-7 Metadata:** Each entry shall record shape, stride, dtype, and byte size, retrievable without reading tensor data. 8. **FR-8 Capacity enforcement:** A put that would exceed configured capacity shall fail with a defined exception and leave existing entries intact. 9. **FR-9 Cleanup:** The system shall provide an explicit `close` and `unlink` operation, and shall release shared memory segments when the creating process unlinks the store.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  1. **NFR-1 Performance:** Get of a tensor shall be O(1) in tensor size with respect to data copying (zero-copy). Put shall incur at most one memcpy of the tensor data. 2. **NFR-2 Concurrency:** The store shall support concurrent readers and writers across processes, using a documented locking or lock-free scheme. Readers shall not block other readers. 3. **NFR-3 Crash safety:** If a writer process terminates mid-put, existing committed entries shall remain readable and the store shall not become corrupted. 4. **NFR-4 Platform:** The initial implementation shall support Linux using POSIX shared memory (`/dev/shm` or `shm_open`). 5. **NFR-5 Compatibility:** The API shall work with `torch.multiprocessing` spawn and fork start methods. 6. **NFR-6 Device scope:** The initial version shall support CPU tensors only. CUDA tensor support is out of scope and shall raise a clear error if attempted.  **Acceptance Criteria**  - A test spawns at least two processes; one puts a tensor and the other retrieves it with values matching bit-for-bit. - A retrieved tensor's `data_ptr()` lies within the shared memory mapping, demonstrating zero-copy. - Concurrent overwrite and read stress test (for example, 10,000 iterations across 4 processes) produces no torn reads. - Killing a writer with SIGKILL during a put leaves prior entries readable on subsequent attach. - Put exceeding capacity raises the defined exception and existing keys are unchanged. - Documentation covers API, supported dtypes, lifecycle (create, attach, close, unlink), and known limitations.

issue_title: Support soft hyphenation (line breaks at U+00AD plus rendering a hyphen at the end of the line)
requirement: # Requirement: Soft Hyphen (U+00AD) Support in Text Shaping and Line Breaking  ## 1. Description  The text layout engine shall support the Unicode **SOFT HYPHEN** character (`U+00AD`) as an *optional* line-break opportunity. When a line break is taken at a soft hyphen, the engine shall emit a visible hyphen glyph at the end of the preceding line. When no break is taken at that position, the soft hyphen shall render as nothing (zero advance width, no visible mark).  This enables authors to mark preferred hyphenation points in text without hard-coding line breaks, and allows the layout engine to break a word only when it does not fit on the line.  ## 2. Functional Requirements  | ID | Requirement | |----|-------------| | FR-1 | `U+00AD` shall be recognized as an optional break opportunity located **immediately before** the character (i.e. a break may be inserted between the preceding character and the soft hyphen). | | FR-2 | When a line break is inserted at a soft hyphen, the soft hyphen shall be **replaced** by a visible hyphen glyph rendered at the end of the broken line, and shall not appear at the start of the following line. | | FR-3 | When no break is inserted at a soft hyphen, the character shall be rendered as zero-width/invisible and shall not contribute to the measured advance width of the line. | | FR-4 | The break opportunity shall be inserted into the line-breaking candidate set so that the line-breaking algorithm (greedy, Knuth–Plass, or equivalent) may select it according to the configured penalty/justification rules. It shall be subject to the same line-breaking constraints (e.g. minimum line length, no break before/after disallowed characters) as other break opportunities. | | FR-5 | The visible hyphen glyph used at a break shall be drawn with the same font, size, style, and color as the surrounding text. If the primary font lacks a glyph for `U+00AD`, the engine shall fall back, in order, to `U+2010` (HYPHEN) and then `U+002D` (HYPHEN-MINUS). The fallback choice shall be configurable. | | FR-6 | The hyphen glyph shall participate in line justification and alignment exactly like any other glyph on the line (i.e. it must be included in the line's measured width). | | FR-7 | Support shall be controlled by a configuration option (e.g. `soft_hyphen: enabled \| disabled`), defaulting to **enabled**. When disabled, `U+00AD` shall be treated as a zero-width, non-breaking, invisible character. | | FR-8 | Shaping/measurement of a paragraph containing soft hyphens shall remain consistent: the engine shall be able to produce different break decisions for the same text at different widths without re-requiring the caller to supply pre-broken lines. | | FR-9 | Consecutive soft hyphens shall each be treated independently as an optional break opportunity; at most one shall be rendered as a visible hyphen per break. A soft hyphen at the very start or end of a paragraph/line shall never produce a visible hyphen unless a break is actually taken there. | | FR-10 | The feature shall not alter the content model of the source document: `U+00AD` shall remain present in the text buffer, and any text-extraction or copy API shall be able to return it either verbatim or stripped, per configuration. |  ## 3. Non-Goals  - Automatic (dictionary-based or algorithmic) hyphenation of words that do not contain an explicit `U+00AD`. - Support for other discretionary-hyphen-like codepoints or for `U+00AD` semantics in other Unicode scripts beyond the standard behavior described above. - Changes to the document/text-input layer (insertion of `U+00AD` into source text is the author's responsibility).  ## 4. Acceptance Criteria  1. **Break taken:** Given the string `"Soft\u{00AD}hyphen"` laid out in a width that forces exactly one break between `Soft` and `hyphen`, the output shall be two lines rendering as `Soft-` and `hyphen`. The first line's measured width shall include the hyphen glyph's advance. 2. **No break taken:** Given the same string laid out in a width where the whole word fits, the output shall be a single line rendering as `Softhyphen`, with the soft hyphen contributing zero width, and the rendered pixels shall be identical to those of the string `"Softhyphen"`. 3. **Glyph fallback:** Given a font with no `U+00AD` glyph, breaking at the soft hyphen shall still render a visible hyphen (via `U+2010`/`U+002D` fallback). 4. **Disabling:** With the feature disabled, `"Soft\u{00AD}hyphen"` shall never break at the soft hyphen and no hyphen shall ever be rendered. 5. **Justification:** In a justified paragraph containing a soft-hyphen break, the visible hyphen shall be stretched/positioned as part of the justified line and shall not overflow the line box. 6. **Round trip:** Text extraction from a laid-out paragraph shall preserve or strip `U+00AD` according to configuration, and shall never yield a stray hyphen character inserted into the extracted text.

issue_title: A new compiler flag: "link everything statically or die, dammit!"
requirement: ## Requirement: Add a compiler driver flag to force fully static linking  ### Summary The compiler driver shall provide a flag (proposed spelling: `-static`, with a long alias `--static`) that instructs the build to link the produced executable against static libraries only, so that the resulting binary contains no dynamic-library dependencies. If a required library or symbol cannot be satisfied from a static archive, the tool must fail loudly rather than silently falling back to a dynamic link.  ### Motivation Currently producing a self-contained, statically linked binary from the compiler driver requires the user to manually invoke the linker with the appropriate static archives and to know which objects/archives are available in static form. This is error prone: a single missing static archive results in a binary with unexpected runtime dependencies, or in a confusing link failure deep in the build. A first-class driver flag makes reproducible, hermetic, distribution-friendly builds a one-line change.  ### Functional requirements 1. **Flag accepted by the driver.** `-static` / `--static` must be accepted on the compiler command line and must be applicable to the link step of the compilation. 2. **Static resolution of all libraries.** When the flag is present, the driver must pass the equivalent of the linker's static-link mode (e.g. `-static`) to the linker so that:    - the C/C++ runtime (libc, libm, libpthread, libdl, etc.) is linked statically where static variants exist;    - any user-specified libraries (`-lfoo`, archive/object arguments) are resolved from static archives when available. 3. **No dynamic dependencies in output.** The produced executable must not require any shared object at runtime (verifiable via the platform's dynamic-dependency inspection facility). Any dynamic loader/`ld.so`-style dependency is a defect. 4. **Hard failure on unsatisfiable dependencies.** If a requested library has no static counterpart, or if a symbol required by the program exists only in a shared object, the driver must terminate with a non-zero exit status and a diagnostic that names the offending library/symbol and explains that static linking was requested. The driver must not silently downgrade to dynamic linking, and must not emit a partially-dynamic binary. 5. **Interaction with shared-only libraries.** Linking a library that exists only as a shared object under `-static` must produce the clear error described in (4), not a link crash or an internal toolchain error. 6. **Platform applicability.** On targets where a fully static link is not supported at all, the flag must be rejected with a clear "not supported on this target/platform" diagnostic and a non-zero exit status. 7. **Compatibility.** The flag must be composable with the rest of the existing command line (optimization, debug info, LTO, other linker options, `--sysroot`, custom library paths) and must not change the semantics of the compiled code. 8. **Pass-through of user linker options.** Existing mechanisms for passing raw arguments to the linker must remain available and must take precedence where they conflict with the flag, with a warning emitted.  ### Non-functional requirements - Deterministic and reproducible output for a given input set and toolchain. - The flag's behavior and limitations must be documented in the compiler's user documentation, including a note that static linking may affect licensing, security updates, and the size/debuggability of the resulting binary.  ### Acceptance criteria - `cc -static hello.c -o hello` produces a binary with zero dynamic dependencies that runs on a machine without the development toolchain installed. - `cc -static hello.c -lonlyshared -o hello` fails with a non-zero status and a message identifying `onlyshared` as lacking a static version. - On a platform without static-link support, `cc -static hello.c` fails with a clear "unsupported" diagnostic. - Existing test suites continue to pass with the flag absent, and a new test covers the success and failure cases above.

The existing unqualified `-u` behavior shall remain unchanged and continue to upgrade both direct and indirect dependencies.
