requirement: **REQ-GDSCRIPT-TRAIT-001: Trait System for GDScript**  **Overview:** Implement a Trait system in GDScript to enable composition-based code reuse, allowing classes to inherit concrete implementations and abstract contracts from multiple independent sources while maintaining single inheritance for the class hierarchy.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **Trait Declaration:** The language shall provide a `trait` keyword to define reusable behavior units containing concrete method implementations, abstract method signatures, member variables (with initialization), and signal declarations.  2. **Composition Syntax:** Classes shall compose one or more traits via a `with` clause (e.g., `extends CharacterBody2D with Movable, Damageable, Saveable`) or equivalent syntax, injecting all trait members into the class namespace.  3. **Host Access:** Trait methods shall access the composing instance via `self`, with full access to the host class's properties, signals, and other composed trait members, subject to standard visibility modifiers (`private`, `protected`).  4. **Conflict Resolution:** When multiple composed traits define members with identical names, the system shall enforce explicit resolution through: (a) override declarations in the composing class, (b) qualified access syntax (e.g., `TraitName.method()`), or (c) compile-time error requiring disambiguation, preventing silent precedence ambiguity.  5. **Type System Integration:** Traits shall serve as first-class types for static type hints (e.g., `var entity: Movable`), supporting nominal or structural typing with `is` operator runtime checks and `as` casting.  6. **Method Resolution Order:** The system shall define a deterministic MRO (Method Resolution Order) for `super()` calls within traits, enabling trait methods to chain to parent class implementations or other trait implementations predictably.  7. **Abstract Contracts:** Traits shall support abstract method declarations that composing classes must implement, enforced by the compiler with clear error messages indicating missing implementations.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  1. **Performance:** Trait composition shall compile to direct method dispatch (virtual table entries or equivalent) with zero runtime reflection overhead for method calls; property access shall match native class member performance.  2. **Backward Compatibility:** Existing GDScript codebases without traits shall compile and execute identically without modification; the `trait` keyword shall be contextually reserved without breaking existing identifiers.  3. **Static Analysis:** The GDScript parser, static type checker, and language server shall fully parse and validate trait constructs, providing autocomplete, go-to-definition, refactoring support, and compile-time error detection for trait misuse (circular composition, unimplemented abstract methods, etc.).  4. **Serialization & Export:** Trait member variables shall support `@export` annotations and participate in the scene serialization system identically to class member variables.  **Constraints:** - Must interoperate with Godot's node system, signals, and `super()` inheritance chain. - Must support tool mode (`tool` scripts) and hot-reloading for editor workflows. - Must function correctly with both GDScript VM execution and any future ahead-of-time compilation paths.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - A class composing multiple traits successfully inherits and executes methods from all traits. - Static type checker validates trait-typed variables and rejects incompatible types at compile time. - Conflicting trait members require explicit resolution without runtime ambiguity. - Performance benchmarks show trait method calls within 5% of native class method call performance.

issue_title: CPU version of PyTorch on PyPI
requirement: ## Requirement: CPU-Only PyTorch Builds Published on PyPI  ### Background Installing PyTorch via `pip install torch` currently pulls in large NVIDIA CUDA runtime wheels (cuDNN, cuBLAS, NCCL, etc.), resulting in multi-gigabyte downloads and installation failures on machines without a compatible NVIDIA GPU/driver, or on platforms where those wheels are unavailable.  ### Requirement PyTorch must publish CPU-only build artifacts to the public PyPI package index so that CPU-only users can install PyTorch with a standard `pip install` command and get a working CPU distribution without requiring CUDA-capable hardware or NVIDIA driver libraries.  ### Details 1. **CPU wheel availability:** The `torch` package on PyPI must provide a CPU-only wheel for every supported Python version and operating system (Linux x86_64, macOS x86_64/arm64, Windows x86_64, and any other currently supported targets), in addition to any existing CUDA-enabled wheels. 2. **Dependency behavior:** Installing a CPU wheel must not pull in `nvidia-*` (cuDNN, cuBLAS, NCCL, etc.) or other GPU-only runtime dependencies. 3. **Package metadata:** Wheel metadata and the package description must make the CPU/CUDA build variant identifiable (e.g., via local version or build-tag labels and documented index URLs) so users and automation can select the desired variant unambiguously. 4. **Documentation:** Installation instructions must state which index URL / package name to use for the CPU-only build versus the CUDA build, and note the minimum supported driver/Python requirements. 5. **Platform support:** Where CPU-only wheels cannot be produced for a platform, that limitation must be documented rather than silently omitted.  ### Acceptance Criteria - `pip install torch` (or the documented CPU-specific index/package name) succeeds on a machine with no NVIDIA GPU and no NVIDIA drivers installed. - The resolved dependency set contains no CUDA/GPU runtime packages. - Download size of the CPU installation is substantially smaller than the CUDA-enabled installation. - The installed package passes the standard smoke test: `import torch; torch.zeros(2,3).matmul(torch.zeros(3,4))` executes successfully on CPU, and `torch.cuda.is_available()` returns `False` without raising. - CPU wheels are available for all officially supported Python/OS/architecture combinations listed in the project documentation.

issue_title: DataLoader with option to re-use worker processes
requirement: The DataLoader should provide a configurable option to reuse worker processes across iterations (e.g., successive epochs) instead of spawning and terminating a fresh set of workers for each iteration. When enabled, worker processes must persist for the lifetime of the DataLoader and be reused for subsequent iterations, with per-iteration state (e.g., seeding and shuffling) correctly re-initialized and worker processes gracefully shut down when the DataLoader is exhausted or destroyed. When the option is not enabled, the existing behavior of creating new workers per iteration must be preserved.

issue_title: [RFC] Add tar-based IterableDataset implementation to PyTorch
requirement: # Requirement: Tar-Based `IterableDataset` Implementation for PyTorch  **Status:** RFC / Feature Request **Component:** `torch.utils.data` **Type:** New public API (Python), additive change; no breaking changes to existing APIs.  ---  ## 1. Motivation / Problem Statement  Large-scale model training increasingly consumes data packaged as **tar archives** (e.g., `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.xz`). This packaging is used because it:  - yields high throughput on POSIX filesystems (sequential reads, no per-file inode/metadata overhead), - allows a single file to be copied to object storage or shipped across nodes, - groups many small samples (image + label + metadata) under a common key.  PyTorch currently offers no first-party way to consume such archives for training:  - `torch.utils.data.IterableDataset` requires users to write their own tar parsing, sharding, shuffling, and transform logic. - `torch.utils.data.Dataset` (map-style) requires one file per sample and does not work with archives. - Existing third-party solutions (e.g., MosaicML IterableDataset, WebDataset) add a dependency, are not maintained with PyTorch, and often diverge from PyTorch's sharding, seeding, and `DataLoader` semantics (e.g., `set_epoch`, `worker_init_fn`, `get_worker_info`).  As a result, users re-implement the same logic, make inconsistent choices about sharding across ranks and workers (causing duplicate or missing samples), and cannot rely on PyTorch's documented determinism guarantees.  ## 2. Goals  1. Provide a **tar-backed `IterableDataset`** in `torch.utils.data` that yields samples drawn from tar archives. 2. Support **both sequential/streaming consumption** (memory-bounded, works for arbitrarily large archives) and **indexed random access** (enables true random shuffling). 3. Provide **correct, documented sharding** across distributed ranks and `DataLoader` workers, with no duplicated and no missing samples under supported configurations. 4. Provide **deterministic, reproducible shuffling** that integrates with `set_epoch()` and `torch.manual_seed`. 5. Support **composite (multi-file) samples** keyed by a shared prefix, plus single-file samples. 6. Support **pluggable transforms** at the sample level (bytes → tensors) without taking a hard dependency on `torchvision`. 7. Provide **robust error handling** (corrupt archives, truncated members, unsupported compression) with configurable strictness. 8. Achieve **competitive throughput** with a documented, reproducible benchmark.  ## 3. Non-Goals  - No new C++/CUDA kernels; implementation is Python-level in `torch/utils/data`. - No built-in network/HTTP(S) tar fetching, S3/GCS/Azure URIs, or authentication. Remote archives are out of scope for this RFC (may be layered later via a user-supplied file-like object or a `fsspec`-style plugin hook — see §8). - No replacement or deprecation of `ImageFolder`, `DatasetFolder`, or `WebDataset`-style third-party packages. - No implicit image/audio decoding; decoding is the responsibility of a user-supplied transform (with an optional, separately-imported convenience helper). - No attempt to preserve exact byte-for-byte tar format semantics beyond what the `tarfile` module guarantees.  ---  ## 4. Public API  ### 4.1 `torch.utils.data.TarIterableDataset`  ```python class TarIterableDataset(IterableDataset[Sample]):     def __init__(         self,         archives: str | os.PathLike | Sequence[str | os.PathLike],         *,         # sample construction         sample_key: str | None = None,          # grouping strategy key         transform: Callable[[Sample], Any] | None = None,         target_transform: Callable[[Any], Any] | None = None,         # access mode         mode: Literal["stream", "index"] = "stream",         # ordering         shuffle: bool = False,         shuffle_buffer_size: int = 0,         seed: int = 0,         # sharding         num_shards: int | None = None,         shard_id: int | None = None,         shard_strategy: Literal["contiguous", "strided", "hash"] = "strided",         # limits & robustness         limit: int | None = None,         on_error: Literal["raise", "skip"] = "raise",         max_retries: int = 0,         # misc         compression: Literal["infer", "none", "gzip", "bz2", "xz"] = "infer",         drop_invalid: bool = False,         **kwargs,     ) -> None: ...      def set_epoch(self, epoch: int) -> None: ...      # reshuffles deterministically     def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[Sample]: ...     def __len__(self) -> int: ...                    # defined iff length is known ```  - `Sample` is a `dict[str, Any]` mapping member name (or member stem, depending on grouping) to `bytes` by default. A reserved key `"__key__"` holds the group key when grouping is enabled. - When `mode="index"` and all archives are uncompressed (or compressed with a seekable decoder), the dataset builds an in-memory index of `(archive, offset, size, key)` and supports **random access**, hence `__len__` is defined and `shuffle=True` performs a true global shuffle.  ### 4.2 `torch.utils.data.TarFileDataset` (map-style sibling)  ```python class TarFileDataset(Dataset[Sample]):     """Map-style dataset over tar archives, indexed by member.""" ```  - Exposes `__getitem__(int)` returning the same `Sample` structure. - Shares the transform, grouping, error-handling, and sharding semantics with `TarIterableDataset` where applicable. - Rationale: many training loops prefer map-style datasets for `DistributedSampler` compatibility and `__len__`.  ### 4.3 Helper: `torch.utils.data.tar_utils`  - `infer_compression(path) -> str | None` - `is_tarfile(path) -> bool` - `group_members(members, key_fn) -> list[Sample]` - Publicly documented, importable, and unit-tested.  ### 4.4 Backward/forward compatibility  - Additive only. No signature changes to `DataLoader`, `IterableDataset`, `DistributedSampler`, or `get_worker_info`. - The new symbols must be exported from `torch.utils.data` and appear in `torch.utils.data.__all__`. - The API must be considered **experimental for at least one release** (documented via a warning-free "experimental" note in docs) with a stated stabilization plan before the next release cycle.  ---  ## 5. Functional Requirements  ### FR-1: Archive discovery and reading - **FR-1.1** Accept one or more local filesystem paths to tar archives. A path may be a file or a directory:   - If a directory, all files matching a documented glob (default `*.tar`, `*.tar.gz`, `*.tar.bz2`, `*.tar.xz`, `*.tgz`) are collected, recursively or not (configurable, default non-recursive), and sorted deterministically (lexicographic by absolute path). - **FR-1.2** Support uncompressed tar, gzip, bzip2, and xz/lzma. Compression is inferred from the file extension by default and can be overridden via `compression=`. - **FR-1.3** In `mode="stream"`, archives are read sequentially and members are yielded as encountered; the implementation must not require the full archive index to be materialized in memory (memory usage must be O(shuffle_buffer_size + max_sample_size)). - **FR-1.4** In `mode="index"`, the dataset builds an index by scanning member headers only; member payloads must not be loaded during indexing. - **FR-1.5** The dataset must not hold an open file handle across `__iter__` boundaries; handles are opened lazily in the worker process and closed on iterator exhaustion or exception.  ### FR-2: Sample construction - **FR-2.1** Support **single-file samples**: each tar member is one sample. Default output: `{"<filename>": bytes}` or, with a documented option, the raw `bytes` payload. - **FR-2.2** Support **grouped (composite) samples**: members sharing a key are yielded together as one sample. Grouping keys are derived by one of:   - `"prefix"` — key is the member path up to and including the last `.` (i.e., `dir/000123.jpg` and `dir/000123.txt` → key `dir/000123`). This is the common convention.   - `"stem"` — key is the member path with its final extension removed.   - `"dir"` — key is the containing directory.   - A user-supplied callable `sample_key_fn(name: str) -> str`. - **FR-2.3** A group is emitted only when the archive scan is complete for that group, i.e., the implementation must correctly handle interleaved and out-of-order member placement within an archive (members of a group need not be contiguous). The implementation must document whether interleaved groups are supported in `mode="stream"` and provide a fallback (e.g., deferring incomplete groups to the end of the archive) if exact grouping cannot be guaranteed while streaming. - **FR-2.4** Sample-level metadata (member name, size, mtime, mode) must be available to the transform. A documented convention for exposing metadata (e.g., a separate `"__meta__"` entry or a `Sample` dataclass with `.data`/`.meta`) must be chosen and stable. - **FR-2.5** Transforms:   - `transform` receives the full sample mapping and returns the yielded object.   - `target_transform` optionally receives the value at a documented reserved key (e.g., `"__target__"`) for label-specific processing.   - Transforms are applied in the worker process (not in the main process) when `num_workers > 0`.   - Transform exceptions must be handled per `on_error` semantics.  ### FR-3: Sharding (ranks and workers) - **FR-3.1** Explicit sharding: `shard_id` in `[0, num_shards)` and `num_shards >= 1`. `num_shards=1`/`shard_id=0` is the default and yields all samples. - **FR-3.2** Automatic sharding via `torch.utils.data.get_worker_info()` when `num_shards` is not specified: each `DataLoader` worker is a shard, and the worker must receive a distinct shard id. The dataset must combine `worker_info.id` with any externally supplied `shard_id` such that the **effective shard id = global_shard_id * num_workers + worker_id** and **effective num_shards = num_shards * num_workers**. - **FR-3.3** `shard_strategy`:   - `"contiguous"` — shard *i* receives a contiguous block of samples.   - `"strided"` (default) — shard *i* receives every *n*-th sample; provides better balance for heterogeneous sample costs.   - `"hash"` — shard membership determined by a stable hash of the sample key, giving content-addressed, load-balanced sharding independent of ordering. - **FR-3.4** With `shuffle=False` and `shard_strategy="contiguous"` or `"strided"`, the union of shards must equal the full dataset, and shard intersections must be empty (verified by test). - **FR-3.5** In `mode="index"` with `shuffle=True`, the global shuffle permutation must be generated over the whole dataset and then partitioned by shard, guaranteeing each sample appears exactly once globally and exactly once per epoch across all ranks/workers.  ### FR-4: Shuffling and determinism - **FR-4.1** `shuffle=True` in `mode="index"` performs a full random permutation of samples. - **FR-4.2** `shuffle=True` in `mode="stream"` uses a bounded shuffle buffer of size `shuffle_buffer_size` (default `1000`); samples are drawn randomly from the buffer, and the buffer is refilled as it drains. `shuffle_buffer_size=0` with `shuffle=True` is invalid and must raise a clear error. - **FR-4.3** Randomness is derived from a combination of the user-provided `seed`, the dataset's `set_epoch(epoch)` value, the shard id, and the worker id, such that:   - different shards/workers produce different orderings,   - the same `(seed, epoch, shard_id, worker_id)` reproduces the same order exactly across runs and machines. - **FR-4.4** `set_epoch(epoch)` must change the ordering for `epoch != previous_epoch` and be a no-op for repeated calls with the same epoch. - **FR-4.5** When the user has not called `set_epoch`, the dataset must use the current global `torch` RNG state (or a documented equivalent) so that `torch.manual_seed(...)` controls reproducibility.  ### FR-5: Limits and filtering - **FR-5.1** `limit: int | None` — emit at most `limit` samples per shard (after sharding and shuffling), enabling quick smoke tests. - **FR-5.2** `drop_invalid: bool` — if `True`, samples whose key group is incomplete or whose payload fails to decode are silently dropped (counted); if `False` (default), the behavior follows `on_error`. - **FR-5.3** Provide a documented way to filter samples by member name (e.g., `member_filter: Callable[[str], bool]`) and by key.  ### FR-6: Error handling and robustness - **FR-6.1** `on_error="raise"` (default): any I/O error, tar parsing error, decompression error, or transform exception propagates to the caller with an informative message including the archive path and member name. - **FR-6.2** `on_error="skip"`: the offending member/sample is skipped, a warning is emitted (rate-limited to avoid log flooding — documented cap), and the error is counted. The dataset must expose the count of skipped samples (e.g., `dataset.num_skipped`) after iteration. - **FR-6.3** Truncated or corrupted archives must not cause silent data loss: the dataset must detect truncation and either raise (default) or skip the trailing incomplete member and record it. - **FR-6.4** `max_retries: int` — number of times a failed archive read is retried (with the file handle reopened) before the error is escalated. - **FR-6.5** Empty archives, archives containing zero yieldable samples, and non-existent paths must produce clear, actionable errors (including a suggestion of the resolved absolute path).  ### FR-7: `DataLoader` integration - **FR-7.1** Must be usable directly with `DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=B, num_workers=N)` without any wrapper class. - **FR-7.2** Must work with `collate_fn` (including the default `default_collate`) for sample types that are dicts of tensors/ints/strings, and with `sampler` being `None` (an `IterableDataset` may not take a `sampler`). - **FR-7.3** Must work with `pin_memory`, `persistent_workers`, `prefetch_factor`, `drop_last`, and `timeout` without modification to `DataLoader`. - **FR-7.4** Worker processes must not inherit open file descriptors from the parent for archives; each worker opens its own handles (or uses documented `fork`-safe re-open logic).  ### FR-8: `DistributedSampler` / DDP compatibility - **FR-8.1** Provide documented guidance (in the docstring and tutorial) for use with `DistributedDataParallel`: either use the dataset's built-in `num_shards`/`shard_id` with `torch.arange(rank, world_size)`, or use `TarFileDataset` (map-style) with `DistributedSampler`. - **FR-8.2** The built-in sharding must produce a partition that is disjoint and exhaustive across ranks for a fixed `world_size`.  ---  ## 6. Non-Functional Requirements  - **NFR-1 (Performance):** For an uncompressed tar of 10,000 samples read with `num_workers=8`, single-sample decode-free iteration throughput must be within 20% of a hand-written baseline using `tarfile` directly, measured by the provided benchmark script. - **NFR-2 (Memory):** In `mode="stream"`, peak RSS must be independent of archive size (bounded by `shuffle_buffer_size` and largest sample). In `mode="index"`, index memory must be documented (bytes per entry) and must not include payload bytes. - **NFR-3 (Startup latency):** `mode="index"` must build the index lazily on first access in the worker and must not block the main process for the entire dataset build more than necessary; a documented `num_workers>0` recommendation must be provided. - **NFR-4 (No new hard dependencies):** The implementation must depend only on the Python standard library plus `torch`. Optional integrations (e.g., image decoding) must be implemented in a separate, optional module guarded by `importlib` checks and must not import `torchvision` at package import time. - **NFR-5 (Portability):** Must work on Linux and macOS; Windows support is best-effort and documented (path/permission caveats). - **NFR-6 (Typing & lint):** Full type annotations; the new module must pass the repository's `mypy`/`flake8` configuration and the PyTorch public-API surface test (`test_public_api`) must be updated to include the new symbols. - **NFR-7 (Documentation):** Must include an API reference entry in `docs/source/data.rst`, an "experimental" note, and a tutorial section in `docs/source/data.rst` or a dedicated `docs/source/notes/*.rst` demonstrating end-to-end usage (creating a tar, iterating, sharding across 2 ranks, shuffling, transform). - **NFR-8 (Security):** Must not extract members to disk; must not be vulnerable to path traversal since no extraction occurs; must not allocate buffers based on untrusted declared sizes without a documented cap (e.g., `max_sample_bytes`).  ---  ## 7. Acceptance Criteria  1. `TarIterableDataset` and `TarFileDataset` are importable from `torch.utils.data` and constructible with a single tar path and a list of tar paths. 2. A tar containing 1,000 single-file samples yields exactly 1,000 samples; a tar containing 500 image/label pairs yields exactly 500 samples with 2 entries each. 3. With `num_shards=4, shard_id=i`, the union of the four shards equals the full sample set, with no duplicates and no omissions; verified for both `contiguous` and `strided` strategies. 4. With `DataLoader(..., num_workers=4)` and no explicit `num_shards`, the union of all worker outputs equals the full sample set with no duplicates. 5. `shuffle=True, seed=42` produces identical ordering across two separate runs; `set_epoch(1)` produces a different ordering; `set_epoch(1)` called twice produces the same ordering. 6. `mode="index"` reports a correct `len(dataset)`; `mode="stream"` reports `len(dataset)` only when the total is known (otherwise raises a documented `TypeError`/`NotImplementedError` with a clear message). 7. A truncated tar raises a descriptive exception under `on_error="raise"` and yields the intact prefix plus a warning and an incremented `num_skipped` under `on_error="skip"`. 8. A transform that raises on a specific sample is handled per `on_error` semantics without crashing other workers. 9. A benchmark script exists in `benchmarks/` (or `torch/utils/data/benchmark/`) reporting samples/sec and throughput for stream and index modes. 10. Unit tests exist covering: tar creation fixtures (single/composite/interleaved groups), all compression formats, all sharding strategies, all error modes, `limit`, `set_epoch`, transform behavior, and `DataLoader` integration; all tests pass in CI on Linux. 11. `test_public_api.json` / `__all__` expectations are updated and pass. 12. Documentation renders the new API with the experimental note and a runnable tutorial example.  ---  ## 8. Open Questions / Future Work  - **Q-1:** Should remote/object-store archives be supported directly (e.g., `s3://` URIs) or only via a user-supplied file-like object? *Proposed: only via file-like object or a `fsspec`-style `opener` callable in a later iteration.* - **Q-2:** Should `TarFileDataset` be merged into `TarIterableDataset` via a `mode` argument to reduce API surface? *Proposed: keep both for map-style ergonomics; share an internal base class.* - **Q-3:** Exact grouping semantics for interleaved members in streaming mode (see FR-2.3) — defer-to-end-of-archive vs. requiring contiguous groups (fail fast with a clear error). - **Q-4:** Should `sample_key` be a reserved keyword, and what is the canonical metadata exposure mechanism (`"__meta__"` key vs. a `Sample` dataclass)? - **Q-5:** Stability timeline: how many releases before the API is declared stable and the experimental note removed? - **Q-6:** Should a `torch.compile`-friendly variant (no Python-side randomness) be provided for GPU-side data pipelines?

issue_title: Replace GridMap with an improved TileMap3D node (inspired by the new 2D TileMap)
requirement: **Requirement: Replace GridMap with an Improved TileMap3D Node**  **ID:** REQ-TILEMAP3D-001  **Summary:** The engine shall provide a `TileMap3D` node that supersedes `GridMap` and adopts the design patterns of the 2D `TileMap` node, including its TileSet-based workflow, layered data model, and editor tooling.  **Description:** `GridMap` stores 3D tile data in a limited, mesh-library-based model that lacks the flexibility of the 2D `TileMap`. `TileMap3D` shall offer a comparable workflow in 3D: tile definitions are authored once in a shared resource, placed on a grid through the editor and through code, and organized into layers. The node shall support the common 3D tile use cases (modular level construction, voxel-like terrain, and grid-aligned props) without requiring users to manage separate mesh libraries.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **TileSet resource:** Tile definitions shall be stored in a `TileSet3D` resource that can be shared across multiple `TileMap3D` nodes. Each tile shall define at least one mesh or scene, an optional material override, and an orientation set. 2. **Atlas and source support:** Tiles shall be selectable from a source, analogous to 2D atlas sources, so that sets of meshes can be referenced by ID and coordinate. 3. **Layers:** A `TileMap3D` shall support multiple layers, each with independent enable, visibility, and collision/navigation settings. 4. **Cell addressing:** Cells shall be addressed by integer 3D coordinates. Each cell shall store a source ID, atlas/tile coordinate, and orientation (rotation and flip in the grid's 24 axis-aligned orientations, or an equivalent set). 5. **Orientation:** Tiles shall be rotatable and flippable in 90-degree increments, with transforms applied consistently to rendering, collision, and navigation data. 6. **Physics:** Tiles shall support optional collision shapes defined in the TileSet, with per-layer collision layer and mask settings. 7. **Navigation:** Tiles shall support optional navigation data defined in the TileSet, usable by the navigation system. 8. **Custom data:** Tiles shall support user-defined custom data layers, readable at runtime via the API. 9. **Terrain/autotiling:** The system shall provide a rule-based terrain or autotile mechanism to select tile variants based on neighboring cells. This may be delivered in a later phase, but the data model shall not preclude it. 10. **Runtime API:** The node shall expose methods to set, get, and erase cells; query cells by region; convert between local and map coordinates; and clear layers. All mutating operations shall emit change signals or notifications. 11. **Editor support:** The editor shall provide a tile palette, paint, erase, rectangle-fill, pick, and rotate tools, plus a preview of the active tile and its orientation. 12. **Rendering:** Tiles shall be batched or instanced so that large maps render with draw-call counts comparable to or better than `GridMap` for equivalent content. 13. **Serialization:** Map data shall be saved in the scene file in a compact, diff-friendly format, and shall remain stable across engine minor versions.  **Migration Requirements:**  14. A conversion tool shall import an existing `GridMap` node and its MeshLibrary into an equivalent `TileMap3D` and `TileSet3D`, preserving cell positions, orientations, and mesh references. 15. `GridMap` shall be marked deprecated in the next minor release with a documented migration path, and it shall remain functional until the subsequent major release. 16. The API documentation shall map each `GridMap` method and property to its `TileMap3D` counterpart.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  17. Setting or erasing a single cell shall complete in constant time with respect to total map size. 18. The editor shall remain responsive (no frame drops below 30 FPS on reference hardware) when painting or filling regions of at least 10,000 cells. 19. The feature shall include unit tests for cell storage, orientation transforms, serialization round-trips, and migration from `GridMap`.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - A user can create a `TileSet3D` with at least three tile types and paint them into a `TileMap3D` in the editor without writing code. - A scene saved with `TileMap3D` reloads with identical cell data, orientations, and layer settings. - A `GridMap` scene converted with the migration tool renders visually identical output and produces identical physics collisions. - Rotating a tile updates its rendered mesh, collision shape, and navigation data together. - All functional requirements have corresponding passing tests.

issue_title: Implement `numpy.random.choice` equivalent
requirement: **REQ-RAND-001: Random Choice Sampling Function**  **Description** Implement a random sampling function `choice()` equivalent to `numpy.random.choice` that selects elements from a finite population with configurable replacement semantics and optional probability weights.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **Population Input (`a`)**: Accept either a 1-dimensional array-like object or a positive integer `n` (equivalent to `arange(n)`). 2. **Output Shape (`size`)**: Accept an optional integer or tuple of integers defining the output dimensions. If `None`, return a single scalar sample. 3. **Replacement Control (`replace`)**: Accept a boolean (default `True`).    - `True`: Samples are drawn with replacement (elements may repeat).    - `False`: Samples are drawn without replacement; raise `ValueError` if the total requested samples (product of `size`) exceeds the population cardinality. 4. **Probability Distribution (`p`)**: Accept an optional 1-D array-like of floats with length equal to the population size.    - All values must be non-negative.    - Values must sum to 1 (within tolerance `1e-8`); if not, normalize to sum to 1.    - If `None`, perform uniform random sampling. 5. **Reproducibility (`random_state`/`seed`)**: Accept an optional integer seed or random number generator instance to produce deterministic, repeatable sequences. 6. **Return Value**: Return sampled elements with the same dtype as the input population `a`, shaped according to `size`.  **Error Handling** - Raise `ValueError` if `a` is empty or not 1-dimensional. - Raise `ValueError` if `p` is provided but its length does not match the population size. - Raise `ValueError` if `p` contains negative values or NaN. - Raise `ValueError` if `replace=False` and the requested sample size exceeds the population size. - Raise `ValueError` if `size` contains negative values.  **Non-Functional Requirements** - Weighted sampling setup shall be O(n) where n is population size; drawing k samples shall be O(k) average case. - Behavior and return types shall be consistent with `numpy.random.choice` for all valid inputs.  **Acceptance Criteria** - `choice(5, size=3, random_state=0)` returns a sequence of 3 integers in range [0, 4]. - `choice([10, 20, 30], size=(2, 2), replace=False)` returns a 2×2 array containing 4 unique values from the population. - `choice(['a', 'b'], p=[0.9, 0.1], size=1000)` yields approximately 900 'a's and 100 'b's. - `choice(3, size=5, replace=False)` raises `ValueError`. - Identical calls with the same `random_state` produce identical outputs.

issue_title: Make `pub` in a binary equivalent to `pub(crate)` for diagnostics
requirement: For binary crate targets, the `pub` visibility modifier shall be treated as equivalent to `pub(crate)` when generating diagnostics, so that visibility lints (e.g., `unreachable_pub`) do not flag `pub` items as unreachable within a binary crate.

issue_title: Add procedural and parametrizable audio support
requirement: ### Procedural and Parameterizable Audio Support  The audio subsystem shall allow users and API callers to synthesize audio procedurally without requiring pre-recorded assets. Each synthesis definition shall expose named, typed parameters with documented defaults and valid ranges, including parameters for sound characteristics such as waveform, duration, frequency, envelope, and gain. Parameter values shall be configurable before generation and changeable during playback where supported. Procedurally generated audio shall be usable through the same playback, mixing, streaming, and export interfaces as static audio assets. Generation shall be deterministic for identical definitions, parameter values, and engine versions. Invalid parameters shall produce clear validation errors, and existing static-audio functionality shall remain backward compatible.

issue_title: Support soft hyphenation (line breaks at U+00AD plus rendering a hyphen at the end of the line)
requirement: **Requirement: Soft Hyphen (U+00AD) Support for Line Breaking and Rendering**  **Description:** The system shall support soft hyphens (U+00AD, SOFT HYPHEN) as optional line-break opportunities within text. A soft hyphen shall be invisible when its position is not used as a line break. When the line-breaking algorithm selects a soft hyphen as the break point, the system shall break the line at that position and render a visible hyphen-minus (U+002D) glyph at the end of the line preceding the break.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **Break opportunity:** The line-breaking algorithm shall treat each U+00AD character as a permitted break opportunity, with the break occurring after the soft hyphen's preceding character. 2. **Invisible when unbroken:** When a line containing a U+00AD is not broken at that position, the soft hyphen shall produce no visible glyph and shall occupy no advance width. 3. **Visible hyphen on break:** When a line is broken at a soft hyphen, the system shall render a hyphen glyph (U+002D or the font's hyphen glyph) at the end of the first line, after the last visible character before the break, and shall include its width in the line-width calculation. 4. **Break selection:** Soft hyphens shall be considered only as break opportunities alongside existing break rules; the system shall not force a break at a soft hyphen when the text fits on the current line. 5. **Multiple soft hyphens:** The system shall support any number of U+00AD characters within a single word, selecting the appropriate one(s) based on the line-breaking result. Only the selected break shall render a hyphen. 6. **Line-width accounting:** The width of the rendered hyphen shall be considered when determining whether the preceding text fits on the line, so that the rendered hyphen does not overflow the line's maximum width. 7. **Justification and alignment:** Rendered hyphens at line ends shall be respected by justified and aligned text layouts, with the hyphen treated as part of the line's final content. 8. **Copy/paste and text extraction:** Soft hyphens shall be preserved in the underlying character data and shall not be introduced as visible characters in extracted text unless the consumer requests raw content; the rendered end-of-line hyphen shall not be included in extracted text. 9. **Hyphenation at existing hyphens:** Soft hyphens shall coexist with existing hard hyphens (U+002D) and break rules; a hard hyphen shall not be duplicated by a soft hyphen break. 10. **Non-breaking contexts:** Soft hyphens within words marked as non-breaking (e.g., by U+2060 WORD JOINER or equivalent constructs) shall not create break opportunities.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  - The behavior shall conform to the Unicode Standard Annex #14 (UAX #14) treatment of U+00AD (class BA). - Soft hyphen processing shall not measurably degrade line-breaking performance for documents without soft hyphens.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - Given the string "hyphen\u00ADation" in a narrow column where "hyphen" fits but "hyphenation" does not, the output shows "hyphen-" on the first line and "ation" on the second. - Given the same string in a column wide enough to hold "hyphenation," no hyphen is rendered and no extra space appears. - Extracted text from the rendered output does not contain a spurious hyphen at the break point. - Unit tests cover single, multiple, and zero soft hyphens, plus justified, left, right, and centered alignment.

issue_title: Add literal quoted strings with embedded variables (f-strings) to GDScript
requirement: GDScript should support f-string literals, allowing variables embedded in quoted strings using `{}` and interpolated when the string is evaluated.

issue_title: Add support for multiple displays/screens/monitors in Godot editor
requirement: The system shall support multiple displays/monitors, enabling the editor interface to span across or be distributed on multiple screens.

issue_title: Add a "Mask2D" node (and/or a "mask_parent" property for Sprite2D)
requirement: The system shall provide 2D masking capability to clip rendered content to a defined mask region, implemented either as a dedicated "Mask2D" node that restricts the visibility of its child nodes within the scene tree based on the mask's shape or texture, or as a "mask_parent" property on "Sprite2D" nodes that designates a parent node to serve as the mask source for that sprite, or both.

issue_title: rustdoc support for per-parameter documentation
requirement: Rustdoc should support documenting individual function parameters and display each parameter’s documentation in the generated API documentation.

issue_title: Proc macros: ability to refer to a specific crate/symbol (something similar to `$crate`)
requirement: Procedural macros must provide a hygiene mechanism equivalent to the `$crate` metavariable that allows macro-generated code to unambiguously reference the defining crate and specific symbols within it, ensuring emitted paths resolve correctly even when the proc-macro crate is renamed or aliased at the invocation site.

issue_title: SliverAppBar flexibleSpace with height depending on children
requirement: The Flutter `SliverAppBar` widget should support sizing its `flexibleSpace` area based on the intrinsic height of its child widget(s) rather than requiring a manually specified `expandedHeight`. When this behavior is used, the app bar's expanded height should be automatically computed from the `flexibleSpace` content's own height, allowing the flexible space to adapt dynamically to varying or data-dependent children and ensuring the entire child content is displayed without hardcoding a fixed height value.

issue_title: Apple CarPlay / Android Auto support?
requirement: **Requirement: Apple CarPlay and Android Auto Support**  The application shall provide an integration with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto so that users can access its core functionality through a vehicle's infotainment display while driving. The integration shall:  1. Be detected and launched automatically when a compatible iOS device or Android device connects to a supported vehicle head unit via wired or wireless connection. 2. Present a driver-optimized interface that follows the CarPlay and Android Auto human-machine interface guidelines, including large touch targets, simplified navigation, and limited text entry. 3. Support voice control and steering-wheel or head-unit controls for primary actions, as permitted by the platform. 4. Restrict or defer non-driving-safe features, such as lengthy text input or complex menus, while the vehicle is in motion. 5. Synchronize relevant data with the phone-side application in real time, so that changes made in the car are reflected on the phone and vice versa. 6. Continue to function when the connection is interrupted, and resume the session automatically upon reconnection. 7. Comply with the current Apple CarPlay and Android Auto developer certification and distribution requirements.

issue_title: Feature Requst: Add regex support to test filters
requirement: ## Requirement: Regular-Expression Support for Test Filters  The test-selection mechanism shall support opt-in regular-expression filters through all interfaces that currently accept test filters.  ### Functional Requirements  - Users shall identify a regular-expression filter using the explicit prefix `re:<pattern>`, for example `re:^tests/unit/.*_test$`. - The pattern shall be evaluated using the implementation language’s standard regular-expression engine and matched against the complete test identifier used by the existing filtering mechanism, including applicable suite, module, and parameterization components. - Matching shall use search semantics; users shall be able to use anchors such as `^` and `$` when exact matching is required. - All tests whose identifiers match the expression shall be selected. A valid expression that matches no tests shall result in an empty selection rather than an error. - Existing literal, wildcard, inclusion, and exclusion filter behavior shall remain unchanged. Regular expressions shall not be inferred from unprefixed filters. - Multiple filters, including combinations of regular-expression and existing filter types, shall follow the filter-combination and precedence semantics already in use. - Patterns shall be compiled once before test execution rather than once per test. - An invalid regular expression shall cause the filtering operation to fail before test execution with a clear error identifying the invalid pattern and the reason for failure. Invalid expressions shall not be silently ignored or treated as literal strings.  ### Documentation and Verification  - User documentation shall describe the `re:` syntax, matching behavior, available examples, and error handling. - Automated tests shall cover matching and non-matching patterns, anchored expressions, special characters, filters combined with existing filter types, backward compatibility of existing filters, and invalid-pattern errors. - Command-line usage shall return a non-zero exit status when an invalid regular-expression filter is supplied.

issue_title: x/pkgsite: generate static docs
requirement: **Requirement**: Implement static documentation generation capability for x/pkgsite to export rendered Go package documentation as static HTML files deployable without the dynamic backend.  **Scope**: A new CLI subcommand (e.g., `pkgsite generate`) that accepts module paths with optional version specifiers (e.g., `github.com/user/repo@v1.2.3`, `@latest`) and produces an output directory containing a complete static website.  **Acceptance Criteria**: 1. The command shall generate an `index.html` for each package page at a path mirroring the dynamic site's URL structure (e.g., `output/github.com/user/repo@v1.2.3/index.html`), containing fully rendered package overview, symbol documentation, examples, and source file listings. 2. All static assets (CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts) shall be included in the output and referenced via relative paths to ensure the site functions correctly when served from static hosting providers (S3, GitHub Pages, Netlify) or opened via `file://` protocol. 3. The system shall generate a client-side search index file (e.g., `search_index.json`) containing package names, symbols, and descriptions to enable search functionality without server-side processing. 4. The command shall support batch processing of multiple modules and versions in a single invocation, generating a hierarchical directory tree for all specified targets. 5. A manifest file (e.g., `manifest.json`) shall be generated recording the generation timestamp, source module versions, and content hashes for each page to support incremental updates and cache invalidation. 6. Generated documentation shall preserve all client-side interactive features (syntax highlighting, collapsible navigation, search) while omitting server-dependent features (dynamic version resolution, real-time updates).

issue_title: x/crypto: add BLAKE3 support
requirement: Implement the BLAKE3 cryptographic hash function in package `x/crypto/blake3`, exposing a `hash.Hash`-compatible interface and supporting standard hashing, keyed hashing, and key derivation (XOF) modes in accordance with the official BLAKE3 specification.

issue_title: Add support for splitting linker invocation to a second execution of `rustc`
requirement: The compiler shall support splitting the linker invocation into a separate secondary execution of `rustc`, wherein the primary `rustc` process performs compilation and delegates the final linking step to a secondary `rustc` instance configured as a linker wrapper; the secondary instance shall receive all object files, crate metadata, library dependencies, and linker arguments from the primary process, subsequently invoke the actual system linker (or configured alternative), and propagate exit codes, error messages, and diagnostic output back to the primary process, while maintaining full compatibility with all existing linker flavors, target specifications, and build configurations; this behavior shall be activatable via a dedicated command-line flag or environment variable.

issue_title: Server-side rendering for Flutter web
requirement: Requirement: The system shall support server-side rendering (SSR) for Flutter web applications.

issue_title: Add structs in GDScript
requirement: The GDScript language shall support user-defined structs as lightweight value types, enabling declarations with named typed fields, literal construction, field access and assignment, pass-by-value semantics, equality based on all fields, and use in variables, functions, arrays, and dictionaries, while preserving existing GDScript compatibility.

issue_title: Support multiple windows for desktop shells
requirement: The system shall support multiple windows when running in desktop shell mode, enabling users to open, display, and interact with multiple application windows simultaneously. Each window shall function independently with its own content and state, windows may be created and closed individually, and the application shall terminate only when all windows have been closed.

issue_title: cmd/go: allow serving module under the subdirectory of git repository
requirement: The `go` command must support modules whose `go.mod` and source files are in a subdirectory of a Git repository, correctly locating and serving the module’s files and versions from that subdirectory.

issue_title: Support for `uint16`, `uint32`, and `uint64`
requirement: The system shall support `uint16`, `uint32`, and `uint64` as unsigned integer types, preserving their values across the supported input, processing, and output operations and enforcing their respective ranges: 0–65,535, 0–4,294,967,295, and 0–18,446,744,073,709,551,615.

issue_title: rustdoc support for per-parameter documentation
requirement: The system shall support per-parameter documentation in rustdoc.

requirement: The system shall provide a Vec::contains_ref method that is less restrictive than Vec::contains, even though it may be worse for type inference.

issue_title: cmd/go: allow verifying vendored code
requirement: The `go mod verify` command must support verifying vendored dependencies in addition to modules in the module cache. Vendored modules must be checked against the main module’s declared versions, replacements, and integrity metadata; verification must fail with a nonzero status and identify any missing, modified, or inconsistent vendored content, and succeed only when all vendored dependencies are intact.

requirement: The system shall support the playback of DRM-protected content.

issue_title: runtime: implement WASM-GC
requirement: The runtime shall support loading, validating, instantiating, and executing WebAssembly modules that use the WebAssembly GC proposal, including GC-managed structs and arrays, reference types, and GC instructions, while correctly managing object allocation, reachability, and reclamation and preserving compatibility with modules that do not use GC features.

issue_title: [Proposal] Data reading framework for PyTorch (Hive, MySQL, S3 etc.)
