requirement: Requirement: The system shall support splitting the linker invocation across a second execution of `rustc`, allowing the linker to be invoked in multiple stages.

issue_title: Investigate Swift Package Manager for Swift plugins
requirement: **Requirement: Evaluate Swift Package Manager (SwiftPM) Plugins for Swift Tooling Integration**  **Summary:** The project shall investigate whether Swift Package Manager plugins can replace or supplement the current tooling integration mechanisms for Swift code, and shall document a recommendation with supporting evidence.  **Background:** SwiftPM supports two plugin types: build tool plugins, which generate sources or run tools during the build, and command plugins, which expose custom commands invoked through `swift package`. The project needs to determine whether these plugin types fit its build, code generation, linting, or formatting workflows.  **Scope of Investigation:** 1. Identify the current tooling tasks (e.g., code generation, linting, formatting, resource processing) that could be implemented as SwiftPM plugins. 2. Document the SwiftPM plugin APIs relevant to those tasks, including build tool plugins and command plugins, with the minimum supported Swift tools version for each. 3. Build a prototype plugin for at least one representative task in a sandboxed test package. 4. Verify plugin behavior on all supported platforms (macOS, Linux, and any others the project targets) and with the supported Xcode and Swift toolchain versions. 5. Assess plugin sandboxing and permission requirements, including network access, file system access outside the package, and the need for user approval of plugin execution. 6. Compare the plugin approach against the current mechanism on build time, incremental build behavior, reproducibility, IDE integration (Xcode and SourceKit-LSP), and contributor onboarding effort. 7. Identify limitations, including restrictions on executable dependencies, binary tool distribution, and the lack of plugin-to-plugin dependencies.  **Deliverables:** - A written findings document in the repository (for example, `docs/investigations/swiftpm-plugins.md`) covering the scope items above. - A working prototype plugin in a branch or example directory, with instructions to reproduce it. - A recommendation stating whether to adopt, partially adopt, or reject SwiftPM plugins for each evaluated task, with rationale. - A list of follow-up issues for any recommended adoption.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - The findings document addresses every scope item and states the minimum Swift tools version and platforms tested. - The prototype builds and runs successfully with `swift build` and, where applicable, `swift package <command>` on each targeted platform, in a clean checkout. - The comparison includes measured build times for the current mechanism and the plugin approach on the same machine, with a clear description of the test conditions. - The recommendation is reviewed and approved by at least one project maintainer.

issue_title: database/sql: missing escape functions
requirement: The `database/sql` package shall provide standard APIs or driver interfaces for safely escaping and quoting SQL literals and identifiers to support safe dynamic query construction.

issue_title: Support home and lock screen widgets
requirement: The application shall provide configurable home screen and lock screen widgets that display up-to-date key application information directly from either surface.

issue_title: cmd/compile: coverage instrumentation for fuzzing
requirement: **Requirement Statement:**  The Go compiler (`cmd/compile`) shall support a code coverage instrumentation mode that enables the collection of coverage data during fuzz testing, in accordance with the following specifications:  1. **Instrumentation Trigger:** The compiler shall provide a build flag that, when enabled, instruments the compiled code with coverage counters at the basic block level (or equivalent fine-grained granularity) suitable for use by the fuzzing engine.  2. **Coverage Data Output:** The instrumented code shall expose coverage information through a runtime-accessible interface, allowing the fuzzing engine (e.g., `go test -fuzz`) to query which code paths were executed during a given fuzz test iteration.  3. **Runtime Integration:** The coverage instrumentation shall integrate with the `testing` package's fuzzing infrastructure so that the fuzzing engine can use coverage feedback to guide the generation of new test inputs (coverage-guided fuzzing).  4. **Performance Overhead:** The instrumentation shall impose minimal runtime overhead when the fuzzing engine is not actively running, and shall not alter the behavior or semantics of the instrumented program.  5. **Compatibility:** Coverage instrumentation shall be compatible with the standard Go toolchain workflows, including `go build`, `go test`, and cross-compilation, and shall not require changes to existing test code.  6. **Fallback Behavior:** If the fuzzing engine is not present or coverage feedback is unavailable, instrumented code shall behave identically to non-instrumented code, with coverage data simply not being collected.  7. **Determinism:** Coverage collection shall be deterministic and thread-safe, producing correct results under concurrent execution of the fuzz target.

issue_title: [Feature request] Let DistributedSampler take a Sampler as input
requirement: ## Requirement: `DistributedSampler` must accept an existing `Sampler` as input  ### Background When distributed training is enabled, the data pipeline always builds a `DistributedSampler` that generates its own index permutation (`torch.randperm`-based shuffling) over the dataset. There is no way for a user to supply their own index-ordering strategy (e.g. `SequentialSampler`, `RandomSampler`, or a length-grouped / Megatron-style sampler) in a distributed run, because the distributed sampler silently replaces it with its internal ordering.  ### Requirement Extend the distributed sampler implementation so that it can wrap a user-provided `torch.utils.data.Sampler`.  1. **New optional parameter**    - `DistributedSampler(dataset, ..., sampler: Optional[torch.utils.data.Sampler] = None)`.    - If a non-`Sampler` object is passed, raise a clear `TypeError`/`ValueError` indicating that a `torch.utils.data.Sampler` instance is required.  2. **Index generation delegates to the wrapped sampler**    - When `sampler` is provided, `__iter__` must shard the wrapped sampler's index order across `num_replicas` (rank `r` receives indices `i` where `i % num_replicas == r`, consistent with existing distributed behavior) instead of creating its own permutation.    - `__len__` must equal the number of indices yielded by the wrapped sampler, adjusted by `drop_last` exactly as for the non-wrapped case.    - The wrapped sampler's `__iter__` must be materialized once per epoch and reused for all ranks so that every rank shards the *same* global ordering; the ordering must be identical across ranks for a given epoch.  3. **Epoch handling**    - `set_epoch(epoch)` must continue to be supported and must forward the epoch to the wrapped sampler when it defines `set_epoch`, so that samplers which re-shuffle per epoch behave correctly.    - When `shuffle=True` and no wrapped sampler is given, the current per-epoch `torch.randperm` behavior (seeded by `seed` + `epoch`) must be preserved unchanged.  4. **Backwards compatibility**    - When `sampler` is not provided, the sampler's observable behavior (index order, `__len__`, `drop_last`, `set_epoch`, `shuffle`/`seed` semantics) must be identical to the current implementation.    - The class must remain a `torch.utils.data.Sampler` subclass and remain directly usable as `DataLoader(sampler=...)`.  5. **Integration**    - The training/data-loading entry point must forward a user-configured sampler (if any) to the distributed sampler, so that specifying a custom sampler in a single-process run and in a distributed run yields the same index-ordering strategy.    - Custom samplers operating on dataset items with variable lengths (e.g. length-grouped samplers) must be supported without additional user-side workarounds.  ### Acceptance criteria - A user can pass `LengthGroupedSampler`-style custom sampler to `DistributedSampler` in a multi-process run and observe grouped, length-aware batches with no duplicated or missing indices. - Ranks receive disjoint index shards derived from the wrapped sampler's ordering. - Existing tests and single-process behavior remain unaffected when the new parameter is omitted.

issue_title: Expose a zero allocation API to Godot C# bindings
requirement: The system shall provide a zero-allocation API for the Godot C# bindings.

issue_title: Use mold as default linker?
requirement: The build system shall use mold as the default linker on supported platforms unless overridden by configuration or unavailable.

issue_title: Feature Request: Easier to extend base RNN implementation
requirement: The system shall provide an extensible base RNN implementation to facilitate custom implementations.

issue_title: x/tools/gopls: support for bazel-based projects
requirement: gopls shall provide first-class language support for Go packages built with Bazel. When a Bazel workspace is detected or explicitly configured, gopls shall use Bazel build metadata to map targets to Go packages, load source and dependency information, and include relevant generated and external-repository Go files. Standard Go language features—including diagnostics, completion, hover, navigation, references, document symbols, formatting, and rename—shall work consistently across Bazel source files and dependencies. Target-to-package mappings that cannot be inferred shall be configurable, Bazel output and unrelated directories shall be excluded, and failures to query Bazel or resolve a target shall produce actionable diagnostics without crashing the language server. Existing behavior for non-Bazel Go workspaces shall remain unchanged.

issue_title: Enable "hot reload" (not just "hot restart") for Flutter Web
requirement: The Flutter development tooling shall support hot reload for Flutter Web applications, allowing developers to apply changed Dart code to a running web session in the browser without a full restart and update the UI while preserving existing application state where feasible.

issue_title: Struct initializer `..x` syntax should work for other structs with structurally equal subset of fields
requirement: The system shall allow struct initializer `..x` syntax to be used with any struct whose fields are a structurally equal subset of the fields of `x`.

issue_title: [webview_flutter] Add Windows support
requirement: The `webview_flutter` package shall provide first-class Windows support through a registered Windows platform implementation. Flutter applications running on Windows shall be able to use the existing `WebViewController` and `WebViewWidget` APIs to display web content in a WebView2-based view, including URL and HTML loading, navigation and reload controls, JavaScript execution, progress and navigation callbacks, and controller disposal. The implementation shall declare its WebView2 Runtime prerequisites in the package documentation, include tests covering Windows controller behavior and widget lifecycle, and preserve existing behavior on all currently supported platforms.

issue_title: cmd/compile: implement powerpc 32-bit backend (ppc32)
requirement: The system shall provide a 32-bit PowerPC (ppc32) backend in the Go compiler (cmd/compile) that generates correct machine code for the GOARCH=ppc target.

issue_title: [video_player] Support DRM content
requirement: The video player shall support playback of DRM-protected content.

issue_title: Add proper and complete support for multi-pass shaders
requirement: The rendering system shall provide complete support for multi-pass shaders, allowing a single material/shader definition to specify multiple sequential rendering passes. Each pass must support its own shader program, render state settings (e.g., blending, depth testing, culling, stencil operations), and texture bindings. The renderer shall execute all passes in the defined order for each affected object, correctly accumulating their results (e.g., via additive blending or framebuffers). Shader definitions and the public API must expose the ability to declare, configure, and iterate over passes, and the implementation must handle per-pass state changes and resource management without errors or undefined behavior.

issue_title: Customizable project structure (platforms)
requirement: **Requirement: Configurable Project Structure per Target Platform**  The system shall allow users to define, select, and customize the project directory structure and layout for each supported target platform (for example, Android, iOS, Web, Desktop) during project creation and in existing projects.  **Functional Requirements**  1. Users shall be able to select one or more target platforms when creating a project, and the system shall generate the directory structure, configuration files, and scaffolding specific to each selected platform. 2. Each platform definition shall specify its directory layout, required and optional files, and naming conventions. These definitions shall be editable through a configuration file (e.g., YAML or JSON) without modifying core source code. 3. Users shall be able to add, rename, or remove directories and files within a platform template, and override default paths for individual platforms. 4. The system shall ship with a default structure for each built-in platform that is used when no customization is provided. 5. Users shall be able to share and reuse custom platform templates across projects, including importing templates from a local path or remote repository. 6. When a project already exists, the system shall support adding a new platform or restructuring an existing one without overwriting user-modified files, and shall report any conflicts for user resolution. 7. The system shall validate custom structure definitions before applying them and report specific errors for malformed, conflicting, or incomplete definitions.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  1. Changes to a project structure shall be reversible or shall produce a preview of changes before application. 2. Custom structure definitions shall be backward compatible with existing project configurations and shall not break builds for projects that use default structures. 3. Documentation shall describe the schema for platform definitions, with at least one worked example.  **Acceptance Criteria**  - A user can create a project targeting two or more platforms and receive the correct default structure for each. - A user can modify a platform's structure via the configuration file, regenerate the project, and see the changes reflected without code changes. - Importing a valid custom template produces the expected structure; an invalid template produces a descriptive validation error and no partial output. - Adding a platform to an existing project creates only new files and leaves existing user-modified files unchanged. - All existing automated tests pass with default structures unchanged.

issue_title: Statically checked tensor shapes
requirement: The system shall provide static checking for tensor shapes to validate dimensional compatibility and detect shape mismatch errors prior to runtime execution.

issue_title: Replace GridMap with an improved TileMap3D node (inspired by the new 2D TileMap)
requirement: **Requirement: Replace GridMap with an improved TileMap3D node**  **Statement:** The engine shall replace the legacy GridMap node with a new TileMap3D node whose architecture, resource model, editor workflow, and API are aligned with the redesigned 2D TileMap system, providing equivalent or superior functionality for 3D grid-based level construction.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. Introduce a `TileMap3D` node that places 3D tiles (meshes and associated resources) on a 3D grid, covering all use cases currently supported by GridMap. 2. Base tile data on a `TileSet`-style resource model consistent with the new 2D TileMap (tile definitions with physics, navigation, occlusion, and custom data layers), replacing the `MeshLibrary`-based approach. 3. Support multiple tile map layers per TileMap3D node, with per-layer enable/disable, visibility, and modification flags, mirroring 2D TileMapLayer behavior. 4. Provide a terrain/autotiling system adapted to 3D tiles, consistent with the 2D terrain sets and peering-bit model. 5. Provide editor tools in the 3D viewport equivalent to the 2D TileMap editor: paint, erase, rectangle fill, pick, rotation, mirroring, and grid previews. 6. Expose a runtime API (get/set cells, erase, layer management, tile data access) that is consistent in naming and behavior with the 2D TileMap API. 7. Deprecate GridMap: hide it from the node creation dialog, mark it as deprecated in documentation, and provide an automated GridMap → TileMap3D scene conversion/migration path for existing projects.  **Non-Functional Requirements:** 1. Performance shall scale to large 3D tile grids (quadrant-based culling/batching of tile instances) comparable to the 2D TileMap's rendering strategy. 2. Editor interaction performance shall remain responsive with tile sets containing hundreds of tiles.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - A GridMap scene can be reproduced in TileMap3D with no loss of functionality (meshes, collisions, transforms, per-cell overrides). - 3D terrain autotiling can be configured and painted via the editor. - The 2D and 3D tile map APIs are documented and demonstrably consistent. - Existing GridMap projects can be migrated via the provided conversion tool, and GridMap is marked deprecated.

issue_title: Obfuscate GDScript in production export
requirement: When building a production export, GDScript source files should be obfuscated so that the original code cannot be easily read or reverse-engineered from the exported package. The export process shall apply an obfuscation step to all GDScript files (e.g., by stripping comments, minifying, renaming, and/or encrypting scripts), while ensuring the exported game runs identically to a non-obfuscated build. Debug builds should retain readable scripts, and the obfuscation behavior should be configurable via export options.

issue_title: x/crypto: add BLAKE3 support
requirement: The golang.org/x/crypto module shall provide standards-compliant BLAKE3 support through a dedicated package, exposing APIs for creating, updating, finalizing, and resetting BLAKE3 hashes, including support for optional key, salt, personalization, extendable output, and conformance testing against official BLAKE3 vectors.

issue_title: format_args! is slow
requirement: **Requirement: Improve the Performance of `format_args!` Expansion and Evaluation**  **Description:** The `format_args!` macro is reported to be slow. The system shall reduce the cost of `format_args!` so that formatting-related code compiles and executes with lower overhead, without changing its observable output or its accepted syntax.  **Scope:** - Compile-time cost: time and memory the compiler spends parsing, expanding, type-checking, and lowering `format_args!` invocations. - Runtime cost: time and allocations incurred when constructing and consuming the resulting `fmt::Arguments` value.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. `format_args!` shall produce output identical to the current implementation for all valid format strings and arguments. 2. All existing valid invocations, including implicit named arguments, positional and named arguments, width/precision parameters, and format traits, shall continue to compile. 3. Invalid format strings shall continue to produce diagnostics at the same locations, with equivalent error messages.  **Performance Requirements:** 1. The compile-time cost of a representative benchmark suite of `format_args!`-heavy code shall decrease by at least 15% relative to the baseline, measured on the same hardware and toolchain configuration. 2. The runtime construction cost of `fmt::Arguments` for representative invocations shall not regress and shall decrease measurably in the benchmark suite. 3. Generated code size for `format_args!` expansions shall not increase for the benchmark suite.  **Verification:** - Run the existing test suite, including UI/diagnostic tests, with no new failures. - Add benchmarks covering small, large, and nested format invocations, and report before/after results. - Confirm no regressions in the `core::fmt` and `std::fmt` test suites.

issue_title: Initializing array of Option<T> using [None; n] syntax should not require std::marker::Copy for T
requirement: `[None; N]` should be allowed to initialize an array of type `[Option<T>; N]` without requiring `T` or `Option<T>` to implement `Copy`.

issue_title: Improve the indexability (SEO) of Flutter apps on the web
requirement: **Requirement: Improve Search Engine Indexability of Flutter Web Applications**  Flutter web applications must produce content and metadata that search engine crawlers can discover, render, and index, without requiring crawlers to execute the Flutter runtime to read the page's primary content.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **Crawlable HTML output:** The build pipeline must provide an option to generate static HTML for each public route that contains the route's visible text content, headings, and links as plain DOM elements, not only as canvas-drawn output. 2. **Per-route metadata:** Developers must be able to define, for each route, a `<title>`, `<meta name="description">`, canonical URL (`<link rel="canonical">`), and Open Graph and Twitter card tags. Metadata must update on client-side navigation and must also be present in the statically generated HTML. 3. **Semantic and accessible structure:** The framework must emit semantic HTML elements (`h1`–`h6`, `nav`, `main`, `article`, `a href`) for widgets that represent headings, navigation, and links, and must keep the Flutter semantics tree synchronized with these elements. 4. **Crawlable links and URLs:** Routes must use clean, path-based URLs (no hash fragments required for content) with real `<a href>` links so crawlers can follow navigation. Each public route must return an HTTP 200 response with its own content when requested directly. 5. **Sitemap and robots support:** The tooling must generate a `sitemap.xml` from the declared public routes and allow a `robots.txt` to be generated or supplied, including a `Sitemap:` directive. 6. **Structured data:** Developers must be able to embed JSON-LD structured data (schema.org) per route. 7. **Render-status handling:** For routes whose content depends on asynchronous data, the framework must provide a mechanism to wait for or prerender that data before the static snapshot is captured, and must return appropriate HTTP status codes (e.g., 404) for unknown routes.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  8. Enabling SEO features must not change the behavior of existing apps that do not opt in. 9. Static HTML generation must complete for a 500-route site within a reasonable build time (target: under 5 minutes on a standard CI runner). 10. Generated pages must pass Google's Rich Results Test and Lighthouse SEO audit with no critical failures for the included metadata. 11. Documentation must describe the setup, supported hosting configurations, and known limitations (such as content rendered only inside the canvas without a semantic counterpart).  **Acceptance Criteria**  - A sample app with three public routes produces three HTML files containing the correct `<title>`, `<meta description>`, canonical link, and visible text, verifiable with `curl` without executing JavaScript. - Navigating between routes in the browser updates `document.title` and the meta description. - `sitemap.xml` lists all declared public routes and excludes routes marked private. - Lighthouse SEO score is 90 or higher on the sample app.

issue_title: Feature request: INT4 format support
requirement: The software shall support the INT4 data format, enabling users to create, read, validate, convert, and process INT4-encoded data through the existing interfaces, with appropriate documentation and clear error handling for unsupported or malformed input.

issue_title: Feature request: Use 'trampolines' to make most of the body of a generic function non-generic
requirement: The compiler shall transform generic functions by extracting their type-independent logic into a shared, non-generic implementation that is invoked through lightweight generic trampoline functions.

issue_title: Support multiple windows for desktop shells
requirement: The system shall support multiple windows for desktop shells.

issue_title: Implement PlatformView support on macOS
requirement: Add PlatformView support on macOS so native macOS platform views can be embedded within the application UI and behave consistently with PlatformView implementations on other supported platforms.

issue_title: Initializing array of Option<T> using [None; n] syntax should not require std::marker::Copy for T
requirement: Requirement: The system shall allow initializing an array of Option<T> using the [None; n] syntax without requiring T to implement std::marker::Copy.

issue_title: [feature request] Simple and Efficient way to get gradients of each element of a sum
requirement: **Requirement: Efficient Per-Term Gradient Computation for Summed Outputs**  The system shall provide a simple, public API that computes the gradient of each individual term of a summed output with respect to a specified set of inputs, in a single backward pass.  **Functional requirements**  1. Given a computation whose output is a sum of N terms, `y = Σᵢ fᵢ(x)`, the system shall return the N per-term gradients `∇ₓ fᵢ(x)` without requiring N separate backward calls from the user. 2. The API shall accept a tensor or array of summed terms and a set of input variables, and return the per-term gradients in a structure indexed by term (for example, a stacked tensor with a leading term dimension). 3. The API shall support an optional flag or parameter to select whether the gradients are returned for all terms or for a subset of terms specified by index or mask. 4. The API shall be composable with existing automatic differentiation features, including higher-order derivatives and use within `vmap`/batched execution where the underlying framework supports it. 5. The API shall raise a clear error if the input is not a sum-reducible output or if the requested inputs are not differentiable.  **Non-functional requirements**  6. The computation shall have time and memory cost no worse than a constant factor over a single standard backward pass for the same graph, and shall avoid recomputing the forward pass per term. 7. The API shall be documented with at least one minimal usage example and one example involving a batched or vectorized computation. 8. Existing gradient, backward, and autograd behavior shall remain unchanged for code that does not use the new API.  **Acceptance criteria**  - For a test function `y = Σᵢ fᵢ(x)` with known analytic gradients, the returned per-term gradients match the analytic values to within floating-point tolerance. - The number of backward graph traversals for N terms is 1, verified by instrumentation or profiling. - Unit tests cover scalar, vector, and multi-dimensional inputs, as well as subset selection and error cases.

issue_title: Add array unpacking/destructuring to GDScript
requirement: GDScript should support array unpacking/destructuring in variable declarations and assignments, allowing array values to be assigned to multiple variables (including nested arrays) with clear syntax and runtime errors for incompatible array shapes or lengths.

issue_title: Add support for `#[doc(since="version")]` attribute
requirement: ## Requirement: Support for the `#[doc(since = "...")]` attribute  ### Summary The documentation generator shall recognize and process a `since` documentation attribute so that authors can declare the version in which a documented item (module, struct, enum, function, trait, method, macro, etc.) became available.  ### Motivation Currently there is no way to record or display the release/version in which a given API was introduced. This information is valuable for library users to determine whether an item is available in their version of the crate, and for maintainers to keep track of API evolution across releases.  ### Functional Requirements  1. **Attribute parsing**    - The parser shall accept `#[doc(since = "<version>")]` applied to any item that may carry doc attributes.    - The attribute shall be recognized in all positions where `#[doc(...)]` attributes are already supported, including on items, on `impl` blocks and trait items, and inside nested modules.    - The version value shall be captured as a string literal; the value is otherwise opaque to the tool (no semantic validation of format, ordering, or comparison is required).    - Multiple `since` attributes on the same item shall be handled without error (the last occurrence shall take precedence, or otherwise be resolved deterministically).    - `#[doc(since = "...")]` shall not be emitted verbatim into the rendered documentation output.  2. **Rendering**    - Generated documentation shall display the declared version for the annotated item, e.g. as an "Available since version `<version>`" / "Since: `<version>`" note associated with the item's heading or signature.    - The note shall appear in every output format the tool produces (for example HTML and Markdown), consistently with how other doc attributes are rendered.    - Items without the attribute shall render exactly as they do today, with no "since" note.  3. **Interaction with existing behavior**    - The attribute shall not affect item ordering, visibility filtering, link resolution, search indexing beyond the added text, or intra-doc link rewriting.    - The attribute shall be ignored (or treated as unsupported) when applied to positions where doc attributes are not meaningful, without causing the build to fail.  4. **Error handling**    - Malformed usage (e.g. a non-string literal value) shall produce a clear, user-facing error message identifying the offending item and attribute, rather than a panic or generic failure.  ### Acceptance Criteria - `#[doc(since = "1.0.0")]` on an item produces visible output containing `1.0.0` in the generated documentation. - The same source compiles and renders without the "since" text when the attribute is removed. - The feature is covered by tests (unit and/or integration/snapshot) for parsing, rendering, and malformed input.

issue_title: Need negative trait bound
requirement: The system shall support negative trait bounds to specify that a generic type must not implement a particular trait.

issue_title: Support home and lock screen widgets
requirement: **Requirement: Home Screen and Lock Screen Widget Support**  The application shall provide widgets that can be placed on the device's home screen and lock screen. Users shall be able to add, configure, resize (where supported by the platform), and remove these widgets without launching the full application. Widgets shall display relevant, up-to-date information from the application and refresh automatically at appropriate intervals or when underlying data changes. Tapping a widget shall open the application to the corresponding content or view. Widgets shall respect the device's system theme and accessibility settings, and shall display a sensible placeholder or fallback state when data is unavailable or the user is not signed in. Widget support shall conform to the widget APIs of each supported platform and shall not degrade device battery life or application performance.

issue_title: RFC: Introduce `setup`, `teardown`, and `fixture` attributes for `cargo test`
requirement: **Requirement Statement:**  The Rust test harness (`cargo test`) shall introduce three new attributes for test lifecycle and context management:  1. `#[setup]` — Marks a function to be executed automatically before each test in its enclosing module, used to initialize test state and prepare the test environment. 2. `#[teardown]` — Marks a function to be executed automatically after each test in its enclosing module, used for cleanup; teardown must run even if the associated test fails or panics. 3. `#[fixture]` — Marks a function or type as a reusable fixture whose value can be requested as a parameter by test functions, providing shared, lazily-initialized test context.  Additional constraints: - Failures in setup or teardown shall be reported as test failures with clear diagnostics identifying the failing hook. - The new attributes shall compose with existing test attributes (e.g., `#[test]`, `#[should_panic]`, `#[ignore]`) and with async test functions. - Fixtures shall support configurable scoping, allowing a fresh instance per test or a shared instance across tests within a module, selectable via attribute arguments.

issue_title: reflect: NamedOf
requirement: The `reflect` package shall provide a `NamedOf(pkgpath, name string, underlying Type) Type` function that dynamically creates and returns a defined (named) `reflect.Type` with the specified package path, type name, and underlying type.

issue_title: Rework the Tilemap terrain system to improve its usability
requirement: The Tilemap terrain system shall be reworked to improve usability by streamlining the terrain authoring and editing workflow, enhancing editor intuitiveness and visual feedback, and simplifying the programming interface to reduce implementation complexity and configuration errors during terrain setup and runtime manipulation.

issue_title: Initializing array of Option<T> using [None; n] syntax should not require std::marker::Copy for T
requirement: The system shall allow initializing an array of Option<T> using the [None; N] syntax without requiring T to implement std::marker::Copy.

issue_title: Scan is overly specialized
requirement: The scan operation shall be generalized so it is not limited to a single use case, data type, or input format. Callers shall be able to configure its behavior, such as the traversal strategy, filtering criteria, and output format, through documented parameters or extension points. Existing scan behavior shall remain available as a default configuration, and existing callers shall continue to work without modification.

issue_title: Investigate Swift Package Manager for Swift plugins
requirement: **Requirement — Investigation: Swift Package Manager Support for Swift Plugins**  The project shall perform a structured technical investigation of Swift Package Manager (SPM) as a mechanism for developing, building, packaging, and distributing plugins written in Swift.  **Evaluation Scope:** 1. Determine how Swift-based plugins can be declared, built, and packaged using SPM, including `Package.swift` manifest structure, target definitions, and product types relevant to plugins. 2. Assess SPM's support for resolving plugin dependencies, semantic versioning, and distribution via public and private package repositories. 3. Evaluate compatibility of SPM-built plugins with the existing plugin architecture, runtime loading/integration, and the current build and release pipeline, including CI. 4. Identify technical constraints and risks, including minimum toolchain/Xcode version requirements, Swift–Objective-C interop, resource and binary dependency handling, and static versus dynamic linking behavior. 5. Compare SPM against the current plugin build and dependency management approach in terms of maintainability, build performance, and developer experience.  **Deliverables:** - A feasibility report documenting findings, limitations, risks, and a go/no-go recommendation for adopting SPM for Swift plugins. - If deemed feasible, a working proof-of-concept demonstrating a Swift plugin defined, built, and consumed via SPM within the existing plugin workflow. - A migration plan outlining adoption steps, estimated effort, and risk mitigation for transitioning Swift plugins to SPM.

issue_title: x/pkgsite: API for pkg.go.dev
requirement: Expose a stable, documented HTTP API from x/pkgsite for pkg.go.dev that allows clients to programmatically retrieve package and module metadata, documentation, search results, and version information, with machine-readable responses, clear error handling, rate limiting, and versioned endpoints.

issue_title: SliverAppBar flexibleSpace with height depending on children
requirement: ## Requirement: Child-driven sizing for `SliverAppBar.flexibleSpace`  ### 1. Problem / Motivation  `SliverAppBar` currently always expands its `flexibleSpace` to fill the entire available region between the top of the app bar and the bottom of the expanded app bar (bounded by `expandedHeight`). This is required by `FlexibleSpaceBar`, which stretches its background and animates its title over the full expanded height.  However, developers who supply a **custom** `flexibleSpace` (for example a `Column` of an image, a badge row, or a chart) have no way to make the flexible space's height match the natural height of that content. Consequences today:  - The custom flexible space content is stretched or must be manually padded/positioned to look correct. - Developers must hard-code the content height (duplicating `expandedHeight`) or use `IntrinsicHeight`/`SizedBox` hacks that do not survive dynamic content (localized text, async-loaded images, font scaling). - Content taller than `expandedHeight` overflows unpredictably; content shorter than the expanded region leaves an unexplained gap.  ### 2. Requirement Statement  `SliverAppBar` shall provide an opt-in mode in which the height of the `flexibleSpace` is derived from the natural (intrinsic) height of its child content, clamped to the valid range for the app bar, instead of always filling the expanded region.  **Functional requirements:**  - **FR-1 — Opt-in, backwards compatible.** The new behavior shall be opt-in via an explicit API on `SliverAppBar`. When the API is not used, `SliverAppBar` shall behave exactly as it does today (flexible space fills the expanded region, `FlexibleSpaceBar` animation unchanged). - **FR-2 — Intrinsic measurement.** In child-sizing mode, the app bar shall measure the desired height of the `flexibleSpace` child and use that value as the height of the flexible space region.   - The measurement shall use the child's intrinsic height when the child supports intrinsic dimension reporting (`RenderBox.getMaxIntrinsicHeight` / `IntrinsicHeight`).   - If the child does not report a usable intrinsic height (e.g. `FlexibleSpaceBar`, `Column` with unbounded children, `CustomPaint` without `computeMaxIntrinsicHeight`), the app bar shall fall back to the current expand-to-fill behavior rather than collapsing to zero. - **FR-3 — Clamping.** The resolved flexible space height shall be clamped to:   - lower bound: `toolbarHeight` (+ `bottom` widget height, if any),   - upper bound: `expandedHeight`.   If the child's desired height is below the lower bound, the lower bound is used and the content is clipped/overflowed per FR-6. If it is above the upper bound, the upper bound is used. - **FR-4 — Alignment.** The flexible space content shall be aligned within the expanded region according to an explicit alignment parameter, defaulting to **bottom** (i.e., the content sits directly above the toolbar, matching the visual position of a bottom-aligned `FlexibleSpaceBar` background). - **FR-5 — Scroll/collapse behavior.** As the app bar collapses (`shrinkOffset` increases), the flexible space shall scale/clamp proportionally with the rest of the app bar exactly as today, and shall reach the toolbar height when fully collapsed. The app bar's scroll extent (`maxScrollExtent`) shall remain derived from `expandedHeight` and shall not change between the two modes, so switching modes does not change the scroll geometry of an existing screen. - **FR-6 — Overflow handling.** When the resolved flexible space height is smaller than the child's natural height, the overflow shall be clipped at the flexible space boundary (no unbounded overflow errors, no painted content bleeding over the toolbar or outside the app bar). - **FR-7 — Dynamic content.** If the child's desired height changes after the first layout (e.g. an image finishes loading, text is localized, or the user changes the text scale factor), the app bar shall re-measure and update the flexible space height, subject to FR-3 clamping, and shall not throw layout exceptions or trigger unbounded rebuild loops. - **FR-8 — Performance.** Measurement shall not introduce a per-frame layout pass when the child's desired height is unchanged. The resolved height shall be cached and only invalidated when the child's measured height, `expandedHeight`, `toolbarHeight`, or the bottom widget's height changes.  ### 3. Proposed API (indicative)  ```dart enum FlexibleSpaceSizing {   /// Current behavior: the flexible space fills the expanded region.   expanded,    /// The flexible space is sized to the natural height of its child,   /// clamped to [toolbarHeight, expandedHeight].   child, }  class SliverAppBar extends StatelessWidget {   const SliverAppBar({     super.key,     this.flexibleSpace,     this.flexibleSpaceSizing = FlexibleSpaceSizing.expanded,     this.flexibleSpaceAlignment = Alignment.bottomCenter,     // ... existing parameters   });    final Widget? flexibleSpace;   final FlexibleSpaceSizing flexibleSpaceSizing;   final AlignmentGeometry flexibleSpaceAlignment; } ```  Alternative equivalent forms (e.g. a dedicated `FlexibleSpace`/`IntrinsicFlexibleSpace` wrapper widget, or a `FlexibleSpaceBuilder` that hands the resolved height to the child) are acceptable provided they satisfy FR-1 through FR-8 and preserve source compatibility.  ### 4. Acceptance Criteria  1. **Default behavior unchanged:** An existing app using `SliverAppBar(flexibleSpace: FlexibleSpaceBar(...))` produces pixel-identical output before and after the change; `FlexibleSpaceBar` continues to expand to `expandedHeight`. 2. **Child-sized region:** With `flexibleSpaceSizing: FlexibleSpaceSizing.child` and a `flexibleSpace` whose natural height is `H` where `toolbarHeight < H < expandedHeight`, the flexible space occupies exactly `H` pixels, bottom-aligned by default, and the remaining `expandedHeight - H` pixels are not painted by the flexible space. 3. **Clamping — too tall:** A child with natural height `> expandedHeight` renders within a region of exactly `expandedHeight` pixels and its overflow is clipped; no overflow exception is logged. 4. **Clamping — too short:** A child with natural height `< toolbarHeight` renders within a region of exactly `toolbarHeight` pixels and is clipped; the toolbar and app bar title remain fully visible and unobstructed. 5. **Fallback:** With `flexibleSpaceSizing: FlexibleSpaceSizing.child` and a child that reports no intrinsic height (e.g. `FlexibleSpaceBar`), the flexible space fills the expanded region (equivalent to `FlexibleSpaceSizing.expanded`). 6. **Alignment:** Passing `flexibleSpaceAlignment: Alignment.topCenter` positions the child at the top of the expanded region, and the remaining space at the bottom is not painted by the flexible space. 7. **Dynamic update:** A child whose height changes from `H1` to `H2` (e.g. via `setState` or a loaded image) results in the flexible space region being `H2` after the next frame, with no layout exception and no more than one additional layout pass per actual height change. 8. **Collapse:** Scrolling the app bar from fully expanded to fully collapsed shrinks the flexible space proportionally, matching the current visual behavior; at full collapse the flexible space contributes zero additional height beyond the toolbar. 9. **Scroll extent:** `maxScrollExtent` of the enclosing `CustomScrollView` is identical for `FlexibleSpaceSizing.expanded` and `FlexibleSpaceSizing.child` given the same `expandedHeight`. 10. **Tests:** The framework includes unit/widget tests covering criteria 1–9, and existing `SliverAppBar`/`FlexibleSpaceBar`/`AppBar` tests continue to pass unmodified.  ### 5. Constraints and Edge Cases  - `expandedHeight` remains the single source of truth for the app bar's expanded height; the child-driven height never increases it. - `primary: true` app bars shall account for `MediaQuery.padding.top` consistently with the current implementation. - App bars with a `bottom` widget shall include the bottom widget's height in the lower-bound calculation and shall not overlap the flexible space with it. - The feature shall work with `SliverAppBar` in pinned, floating, and standard variants. - Text scale factor changes shall trigger re-measurement (FR-7).  ### 6. Non-Goals  - Changing `FlexibleSpaceBar`'s own layout or animation semantics. - Automatically animating the flexible space height when the child resizes (a jump cut is acceptable; animated transitions are out of scope). - Supporting non-intrinsically-sized children (e.g. children that require unbounded height) beyond the fallback defined in FR-2. - Modifying the scroll extent or the collapse physics of the app bar.

issue_title: Support soft hyphenation (line breaks at U+00AD plus rendering a hyphen at the end of the line)
requirement: The text layout and rendering engine shall support soft hyphens (U+00AD) by treating the character as an eligible line-break opportunity during text wrapping; when a line breaks at a soft hyphen, the system shall render a visible hyphen glyph at the end of the line preceding the break, and when no line break occurs at the soft hyphen, the character shall remain invisible and occupy zero width.

issue_title: reflect: NamedOf
requirement: The `reflect` package should provide a `NamedOf` function that creates a new defined (named) type at runtime, given a type name and an underlying type, analogous to how `reflect.StructOf` constructs struct types at runtime. The returned type should be a distinct named type equivalent to one declared in source code (e.g., `type MyInt int`), including support for defining methods on it where the runtime permits, and it should be usable for type assertions, type switches, and other reflective operations.

issue_title: Support multiple windows for desktop shells
requirement: The system shall support opening and managing multiple windows within the desktop shell.

issue_title: compress/bzip2: implement bz2 encoder
requirement: **Requirement: Add a bzip2 compression (encoder) implementation to the `compress/bzip2` package**  **Summary:** The `compress/bzip2` package currently supports decompression only. Add a streaming bzip2 encoder that produces output compatible with the bzip2 file format and with standard bzip2 decompressors.  **Functional requirements:**  1. **API:** Provide `NewWriter(w io.Writer) *Writer` and `NewWriterLevel(w io.Writer, level int) (*Writer, error)`, where `level` is an integer from 1 to 9 (block size of 100k × level), matching the bzip2 command-line `-1` through `-9` options. `NewWriter` uses level 9 by default. `Writer` implements `io.WriteCloser` and an explicit `Flush` method if needed for stream completion semantics. 2. **Format compliance:** Output must conform to the bzip2 format specification, including the stream header ("BZh" plus block size digit), block headers and magic numbers, Burrows-Wheeler transform, move-to-front and Huffman coding, block and stream CRCs, and the end-of-stream marker. 3. **Interoperability:** Output must be decompressible by the reference `bzip2` tool (`bzip2 -d`) and by the package's existing `bzip2.NewReader`. Round-trip tests must pass for all levels 1–9. 4. **Streaming:** The encoder must process input incrementally, buffering at most one block (up to the configured block size) in memory, and must not require the entire input to be available up front. 5. **Close semantics:** `Close` must flush all pending data, write the final block and end-of-stream marker with stream CRC, and must not close the underlying `io.Writer`. Calling `Write` after `Close` must return an error. Repeated `Close` calls must be safe and return nil after the first successful close. 6. **Error handling:** Write errors from the underlying writer must be propagated to the caller and leave the writer in a failed state where subsequent calls return the same error. 7. **Empty input:** Closing a writer with no data written must produce a valid empty bzip2 stream that the reference tool decompresses to zero bytes.  **Non-functional requirements:**  8. **Determinism:** Given identical input and level, output must be byte-for-byte deterministic. 9. **Performance:** Compression throughput should be within a reasonable factor (target: no more than 2× slower) of the reference `bzip2` C implementation at the same level on standard benchmark corpora (e.g., Canterbury/Silesia). 10. **Dependencies:** Use only the Go standard library; no cgo or external modules. 11. **Documentation:** Public identifiers must have GoDoc comments, and the package documentation must state that the package now supports both compression and decompression.  **Acceptance criteria:**  - Unit tests cover all levels 1–9, empty input, single-byte input, input exactly equal to a block boundary, highly repetitive input (e.g., runs of a single byte exercising the RLE1 stage), random incompressible input, and multi-block input. - Round-trip tests pass: `Writer` output decoded by `NewReader` returns the original bytes. - Cross-validation tests pass against the reference `bzip2` binary for compression and decompression, where available, and are skipped otherwise. - Fuzz tests run without crashes or round-trip mismatches. - Writing to a failing `io.Writer` returns an error and does not panic.

issue_title: crypto/tls: add PSK support
requirement: Requirement: Pre-Shared Key (PSK) Support in crypto/tls  The crypto/tls package shall support Pre-Shared Key (PSK) authentication for TLS connections, allowing both client and server endpoints to establish a session using a shared secret key and identity instead of certificate-based authentication.  Specifically:  1. Configuration: Users shall be able to supply PSK credentials through the tls.Config structure, including a client-side identity and key, and a server-side mapping from identity to key, with an optional callback to resolve keys dynamically per identity.  2. Protocol support: The implementation shall support TLS PSK cipher suites as defined for TLS 1.2 (RFC 4279) and TLS 1.3 (RFC 8446, using the pre_shared_key extension and psk_key_exchange_modes), including session resumption-style PSK negotiation where applicable.  3. Negotiation: During the handshake, the client shall offer PSK identities and the server shall select a matching identity; the handshake shall fail with a descriptive error if no matching identity or key is available or if the negotiated parameters are invalid.  4. Compatibility: PSK-based and certificate-based authentication shall coexist. Enabling PSK shall not change behavior for connections that do not use it, and existing APIs shall remain backward compatible.  5. Security: Keys shall be handled as sensitive material and not logged or exposed through error messages. Implementations shall enforce minimum key lengths consistent with the negotiated cipher suite's hash requirements and shall preserve forward-secrecy options where the cipher suite supports them.  6. Testing: The feature shall include unit tests and handshake interoperability tests covering successful PSK handshakes in TLS 1.2 and 1.3, identity mismatch failures, and mixed PSK/certificate configurations.

Unix path types shall enforce forward-slash (`/`) as the sole separator and support arbitrary byte sequences (including non-UTF-8), while Windows path types shall support both backslash (`\`) and forward-slash separators, drive letters (e.g., `C:`), UNC prefixes (`\\server\share`), and UTF-16-compatible encoding (WTF-8). Both type families shall provide a path manipulation API equivalent to native `Path`/`PathBuf` (including component iteration, extension handling, parent/ancestor access, and joining operations). The system shall provide fallible conversion methods between these explicit types and the native `Path`/`PathBuf`, as well as between Unix and Windows variants, returning typed errors that specify when a path representation is invalid for the target platform's semantics (e.g., a Windows path containing a drive letter cannot be losslessly converted to a native Unix path).

issue_title: x/crypto: add BLAKE3 support
requirement: ## Requirement: Add BLAKE3 support to `golang.org/x/crypto`  ### Summary  Introduce a new package `golang.org/x/crypto/blake3` providing a pure-Go implementation of the BLAKE3 cryptographic hash function, following the conventions of the existing hash packages in `x/crypto` (`blake2b`, `blake2s`, `sha3`).  ### Functional Requirements  **Core hashing** - Implement the BLAKE3 hash function as specified by the BLAKE3 reference implementation, producing a 256-bit (32-byte) digest by default. - Provide a one-shot API: `blake3.Sum256(data []byte) [32]byte` returning the digest of the input. - Provide a streaming API: `blake3.New()` returning a `hash.Hash` that supports incremental `Write` calls and `Sum`/`Sum(nil)`/`Reset`, with `Size() == 32` and `BlockSize() == 64`. - Correctly handle input of any length, including empty input, and inputs spanning many blocks, matching the published BLAKE3 test vectors.  **Extended output** - Provide `blake3.NewXOF(size uint32) (hash.Hash, error)` (or equivalent) supporting arbitrary-length extendable output via the `Read` method of the returned hash, and a one-shot helper for extended output digests. - Provide support for BLAKE3's keyed hashing mode (32-byte key) and/or key derivation mode through an explicit constructor or option, exposed in a manner consistent with the package's public API.  **Serialization** - Implement `encoding.BinaryMarshaler` / `encoding.BinaryUnmarshaler` on the hash state so that a hash's internal state can be saved and restored, consistent with the behavior of `blake2b`/`blake2s`.  ### API and Package Conventions  - Package name `blake3`, import path `golang.org/x/crypto/blake3`. - Exported identifiers must be documented with Go doc comments; the package must pass `go vet` and the repository's standard linting. - Provide a `LICENSE`-compatible attribution to the BLAKE3 reference implementation if any upstream code is adapted, and state the algorithm's licensing clearly in the package documentation.  ### Testing  - Include unit tests that verify digest values against the official BLAKE3 test vector files (unkeyed, keyed, and derive-key contexts as applicable). - Include tests for the streaming API producing the same result as the one-shot API for equivalent input, for incremental writes split at arbitrary boundaries. - Include tests for extended output lengths and for marshal/unmarshal round-tripping.  ### Non-functional Requirements  - Pure Go implementation with no cgo or external dependencies beyond the Go standard library and `golang.org/x/crypto` internals already present. - Performance should be within a reasonable factor of the reference implementation and must not regress other `x/crypto` packages; benchmark functions should be included. - The implementation must be safe for concurrent use of distinct hash instances, and free of data races. - Must build and pass tests on all platforms supported by `x/crypto` (at minimum linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, windows/amd64) with `GOARCH`/`GOOS` independent code where required (e.g., use `math/bits` for portable operations). - Should be added to the `x/crypto` module and released under the module's existing versioning and API-stability policy.

issue_title: DataLoader with option to re-use worker processes
requirement: **Software Requirement: Persistent Worker Processes for DataLoader**  The DataLoader shall implement an optional persistent worker mode that maintains worker processes across multiple epochs or iterations to eliminate process creation overhead. The implementation shall satisfy the following requirements:  **Functional Requirements** 1. The DataLoader constructor shall accept a boolean parameter `persistent_workers` (default: `False`). 2. When `persistent_workers=True` and `num_workers > 0`, worker processes shall be spawned once upon the first iteration and reused for all subsequent iterations until the DataLoader instance is explicitly closed, deleted, or garbage collected. 3. When `persistent_workers=False`, the DataLoader shall retain existing behavior of spawning fresh worker processes for each epoch and terminating them upon epoch completion. 4. Persistent workers shall correctly reset per-epoch state (e.g., dataset indices, internal buffers) between iterations while maintaining process identity and PID stability. 5. The implementation shall provide reliable shutdown mechanisms to terminate persistent workers upon DataLoader teardown, preventing orphaned processes. 6. The feature shall support both map-style and iterable-style datasets and function correctly across all supported multiprocessing start methods (spawn, fork, forkserver).  **Constraints & Edge Cases** 7. The parameter shall only take effect when `num_workers > 0`; setting `persistent_workers=True` with `num_workers=0` shall either be ignored or raise a configuration warning. 8. Memory usage shall remain bounded across epochs; persistent workers shall not accumulate unbounded state or memory leaks. 9. Exception handling and error propagation from worker processes shall maintain semantics identical to the non-persistent mode. 10. Backward compatibility shall be preserved: existing code omitting the new parameter shall exhibit identical behavior to prior versions.  **Acceptance Criteria** - A DataLoader configured with `persistent_workers=True` and `num_workers=N` shall maintain exactly N distinct worker PIDs across 100 consecutive epochs. - Worker processes shall terminate within 5 seconds of DataLoader garbage collection or explicit shutdown. - Iterating over multiple epochs with `persistent_workers=True` shall demonstrate measurably reduced per-epoch latency compared to `persistent_workers=False` when dataset size per epoch is small relative to process startup cost.

issue_title: reflect: NamedOf
requirement: ## Requirement: `reflect.NamedOf`  ### Summary Add a new exported helper `NamedOf` to the `reflect` package that resolves the *name* of the named type underlying an arbitrary value or type.  ### Motivation Callers frequently hold a value whose static type is a wrapper (pointer, slice, array, map, channel, function) and need the name of the concrete named type it ultimately refers to — e.g. to look up a registry entry, a schema field, or to produce a human-readable label. Today this requires hand-written type-unwrapping loops at every call site. A single, panic-free helper centralizes this logic.  ### API  ```go func NamedOf(v any) string ```  - `v` may be any value, including `nil`, a typed nil pointer, a `reflect.Type`, or a `reflect.Value`. - Returns the name of the underlying named type, or `""` when no named type can be determined.  ### Behavior 1. **Unwrapping**: starting from the dynamic type of `v`, `NamedOf` transparently dereferences pointer types and unwraps slice, array, map, chan, and func types (including their element types) until a named type is reached. 2. **Named type found**: return `Type.Name()` of that type (e.g. `"Config"`, `"time.Time"`). 3. **No named type**: return `""` for unnamed types (e.g. `struct{ A int }`, `int`, `string`, `[]int`). 4. **Nil input**: `NamedOf(nil)` returns `""`. 5. **Typed nil pointer** (e.g. `(*Config)(nil)`): returns `"Config"`. 6. **Never panics**: invalid inputs yield `""` instead of a runtime panic.  ### Acceptance criteria - `reflect.NamedOf` is exported from the `reflect` package and documented. - All cases above are covered by unit tests, including table-driven tests for pointer-to-pointer, slice-of-pointer-to-named-struct, map values, interfaces holding concrete values, and `nil`. - Implementation reuses existing `reflect` primitives and does not introduce dependencies on unrelated packages. - Existing `reflect` package behavior is unchanged (no regressions in the existing test suite).

This equivalence shall apply only to diagnostic generation; the actual visibility semantics (name resolution, privacy checking, and item reachability rules) shall remain unchanged.  **Acceptance criteria:** 1. A `pub` item in a binary crate that is not used anywhere within the crate shall trigger the `dead_code` lint, with behavior identical to the same item declared `pub(crate)`. 2. Library crates (`lib` crate type) and other crate types shall be unaffected; `pub` items in libraries continue to be treated as externally reachable for diagnostics. 4. No new warnings shall be emitted for `pub` items in binary crates that are used within the crate, solely as a result of this change.

issue_title: x/vuln: add support for suppressing vulnerabilities by ID
requirement: Requirement: Vulnerability ID Suppression for x/vuln  The tool shall support suppressing specific vulnerabilities by their identifier so that they are excluded from reported results. Specifically:  1. Users shall be able to specify one or more vulnerability IDs (e.g., Go vulnerability IDs such as GO-YYYY-NNNN, and CVE/GHSA aliases where applicable) to be suppressed. 2. Suppressed vulnerabilities shall not appear in the default text, JSON, or SARIF output of a scan. 3. Suppression shall be configurable through a command-line option and/or a configuration file, and multiple IDs may be specified in a single invocation or configuration. 4. When an identifier supplied for suppression does not match any known vulnerability, the tool shall emit a warning and continue the scan rather than failing. 5. Suppression shall match an alias of a vulnerability (such as a CVE or GHSA identifier) so that suppressing any known alias of a vulnerability suppresses the corresponding Go vulnerability entry. 6. The tool shall indicate in its output (for example, a summary line) how many vulnerabilities were suppressed, so that suppression is not silent. 7. issue_title: Proc macros: ability to refer to a specific crate/symbol (something similar to `$crate`)
requirement: **Requirement: Stable crate-relative path references in procedural macro output**  Procedural macros must be able to generate tokens that refer to a specific crate or item by a path that resolves correctly regardless of how the invoking crate has named, renamed, or re-exported that dependency. This should work similarly to `$crate` in `macro_rules!`, which expands to a path pointing at the defining crate.  **Acceptance criteria:**  1. The `proc_macro` API (or an accompanying standard facility) provides a way to produce a path token that resolves to a named crate's item (e.g., `some_crate::module::Item`) independent of the invoking crate's `Cargo.toml` dependency name, including renamed dependencies (`package = "..."` / `extern crate ... as ...`). 2. The generated path resolves correctly when the macro is used in a crate that does not directly depend on the target crate but receives it through a re-export from another crate, provided the macro's own crate has a defined dependency on it. 3. The generated path is not shadowed by local items, `use` declarations, or generic parameter names in the invoking scope with the same identifier as the crate. 4. The mechanism works for both item-level and expression-level output, and for `#[derive]`, attribute, and function-like proc macros. 5. Hygiene is preserved: the path does not require the end user to have the target crate in scope under its canonical name. 6. Documentation describes the mechanism with examples, and the existing workaround (e.g., the `proc-macro-crate` approach of inspecting `Cargo.toml`) is no longer necessary for the common case. 7. Existing proc macros that hardcode crate paths continue to compile unchanged (no breaking change).

issue_title: Return attention weights in nn.Transformer
requirement: **Requirement: Support Returning Attention Weights from `nn.Transformer`**  **Feature ID:** REQ-NN-TRANSFORMER-ATTN-001  **Summary:** The `torch.nn.Transformer` module and its submodules (`nn.TransformerEncoder`, `nn.TransformerDecoder`, and their internal layers) shall provide an opt-in mechanism to return the attention weights computed during the forward pass, enabling users to inspect, analyze, and visualize attention patterns for model interpretability and debugging.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. `forward()` methods of `nn.Transformer`, `nn.TransformerEncoder`, and `nn.TransformerDecoder` shall accept a boolean keyword argument `need_weights` (default: `False`) that controls whether attention weights are collected and returned. 2. When `need_weights=True`:    - The module shall return the attention weights alongside the standard output tensor.    - Weights shall be provided for all applicable attention operations: encoder self-attention, decoder self-attention, and decoder cross-attention.    - Weights shall expose per-head granularity (with an option to average across heads), with a documented shape, e.g., `(num_layers, batch_size × num_heads, tgt_len, src_len)` for self-attention and `(num_layers, batch_size × num_heads, tgt_len, src_len)` for cross-attention. 3. When `need_weights=False` (default), the return signature and behavior shall remain identical to the current implementation, ensuring full backward compatibility with existing code. 4. Attention weights shall only be computed and stored when explicitly requested, to avoid unnecessary memory and computation overhead.  **Constraints:** - Enabling `need_weights=True` shall not alter the numerical results of the module's primary output. - Memory usage when the option is disabled shall be unchanged.  **Acceptance Criteria:** 1. A call to `nn.Transformer.forward(..., need_weights=True)` returns attention weights covering every layer and head, matching the documented shapes. 2. Existing code invoking `forward()` without the new argument produces identical results to the previous version. 3. Returned weights can be directly used to generate per-layer, per-head attention heatmaps for a given input.
