issue_title: [RFC] PT2-Friendly Traceable, Functional Collective Communication APIs
requirement: # Software Requirement Specification  **REQ-ID:** REQ-DIST-001 **Title:** PyTorch 2-Compatible Traceable, Functional Collective Communication APIs **Source:** [RFC] PT2-Friendly Traceable, Functional Collective Communication APIs **Priority:** High — prerequisite for first-class `torch.compile` support of distributed training workloads  ---  ## 1. Problem Statement  Existing `torch.distributed` collective operations (e.g., `all_reduce`, `all_gather`, `reduce_scatter`, `broadcast`) mutate their input tensors in place, are opaque to PyTorch's tracing and compilation stack (TorchDynamo, AOTAutograd, FX, `torch.export`), and hide the ordering constraints between communication and computation. Consequently, distributed programs using collectives cannot be faithfully captured, transformed, or optimized by PyTorch 2 tooling, forcing users into graph breaks or manual synchronization.  ## 2. Requirement Description  Introduce a new family of collective communication APIs in `torch.distributed` that follow **functional semantics**, are **fully traceable** by PyTorch 2 tracing and compilation systems, and preserve the correctness guarantees of the existing c10d collectives.  ## 3. Functional Requirements  - **FR-1 — Functional semantics:** Provide functional variants of the core collectives — at minimum `all_reduce`, `all_gather` (including `all_gather_into_tensor`), `reduce_scatter` (including `reduce_scatter_tensor`), `broadcast`, `gather`, and `scatter` — that return new result tensors (or tensor lists) and do not mutate their inputs. - **FR-2 — Asynchronous execution:** Each functional collective may execute asynchronously and must return a tensor-like object that remains valid to trace. Any subsequent operation that reads the result must implicitly force completion of the underlying communication work ("force-wait"), eliminating data races without user-inserted synchronization. - **FR-3 — Traceability:** The APIs must be capturable by TorchDynamo without graph breaks, must trace into FX graphs via AOTAutograd/`make_fx` with collectives represented as explicit, reorderable traceable ops, and must produce reproducible graphs under `torch.export`. - **FR-4 — Composability:** The APIs must compose with PT2 features, including `torch.compile`, functional tensor APIs (functorch/vmap where applicable), DTensor/tensor-parallel usage, and autocast/mixed precision. - **FR-5 — Eager-mode equivalence:** The APIs must work in eager mode with numerically equivalent results to the corresponding legacy in-place collectives, given identical inputs, process group, and backend. - **FR-6 — Backend coverage:** The APIs must support the standard c10d backends (NCCL, Gloo; MPI where available) and existing process-group initialization without requiring users to change how process groups are created. - **FR-7 — Ordering and safety:** The implementation must guarantee that all ranks issue matching collectives in a consistent order and that tracing/compilation preserves collective ordering (no mismatched collectives or deadlocks in traced form). - **FR-8 — Error handling:** Unsupported combinations (backend, dtype, device, invalid process group) must raise clear, actionable errors in both eager and traced/compiled contexts. - **FR-9 — Interoperability:** Provide a documented migration/interop path with the legacy in-place APIs, including equivalents of `async_op=True` work handles where relevant.  ## 4. Non-Functional Requirements  - **NFR-1 — Performance:** Eager-mode overhead relative to legacy in-place collectives must be negligible (target ≤ 5% end-to-end); in compiled mode, end-to-end performance must be equal to or better than eager mode by enabling communication/computation overlap and fusion opportunities. - **NFR-2 — Backward compatibility:** Existing in-place collectives must remain unchanged; the new APIs are additive and opt-in. - **NFR-3 — Testability:** Deliver unit and integration tests covering multi-rank correctness, eager/traced/compiled result equivalence, all supported backends, and force-wait race safety. - **NFR-4 — Documentation:** Provide public API documentation and a migration guide (in-place → functional).  ## 5. Acceptance Criteria  - **AC-1:** A distributed workload using the new collectives compiles with `torch.compile` with no graph breaks attributable to the collectives. - **AC-2:** Traced FX graphs contain explicit representations of the collectives, and `torch.export` output is reproducible. - **AC-3:** Reading a returned result tensor before communication completes triggers implicit synchronization; no data races are reported under race-detection checks. - **AC-4:** Results match the corresponding legacy collectives (bitwise for supported dtypes on NCCL/Gloo) for equivalent invocations. - **AC-5:** The covered collective types work on CPU (Gloo) and CUDA (NCCL).  ## 6. Assumptions and Out of Scope  - **Out of scope (initial release):** object-based collectives (`all_gather_object`, `gather_object`, `scatter_object_list`) and barrier-style synchronization ops; point-to-point primitives. - **Assumptions:** Existing c10d process-group infrastructure and backends remain available and unchanged.

issue_title: Code Push / Hot Update / out of band updates
requirement: ## Feature Requirement: Over-the-Air Code Push / Hot Updates  ### Summary The system shall allow application code and static resources to be updated on deployed clients **out of band** — i.e., without requiring a full app-store release and install cycle, and without the user performing any manual download or update action.  ### Functional Requirements  1. **Update Delivery**    - A build server (or update manifest endpoint) shall publish versioned update packages containing executable code and/or static assets.    - Clients shall poll or subscribe for update availability on app start, on resume, and at a configurable interval in the background.    - Updates shall be distributed over the network using standard HTTP(S), with support for resuming interrupted downloads and delta/patch-sized payloads.  2. **Client-Side Application**    - Upon detecting a newer version, the client shall download the update package, validate it, stage it locally, and atomically swap it into the active runtime on the next restart or, where supported, on the next app resume.    - The hot-swapped version must be usable by all subsequent code paths without requiring a process restart.    - The previously active version shall remain on disk so the client can fall back to it.  3. **Versioning & Rollback**    - Each release shall carry a monotonically increasing version identifier and a minimum-compatible-client version.    - Updates that fail validation, fail to boot, or cause a runtime crash immediately after activation shall be automatically rolled back to the last known-good version.    - The server shall be able to mark a release as revoked/halted, and clients shall then discard it and return to the previous release.  4. **Compatibility & Targeting**    - Updates shall be targetable by platform, OS version, app version, locale, device capability, and arbitrary runtime device properties.    - The client shall refuse packages whose compatibility constraints are not satisfied and remain on its current version.  5. **Data & State Safety**    - Updates shall not alter persisted user data schemas in an incompatible way; any schema migration requirements shall be declared in the manifest.    - In-flight user sessions shall be preserved across a hot swap.  6. **Security**    - Packages shall be cryptographically signed, and clients shall verify the signature against a bundled public key or trusted key set before activation.    - Plaintext HTTP transport shall be disallowed by default in release builds.    - Failed or unverifiable packages shall never be activated.  7. **User Control & Observability**    - Update behaviour shall be configurable: automatic silent application, or prompt-and-confirm (opt-in).    - The application shall expose the current active version, pending update version, download progress, and last update result via a programmatic API and a developer-facing status surface.    - Usage and failure metrics (check, download success/failure, activation, rollback, crash-after-update) shall be reported to the update service.  ### Non-Goals - Delivery of native binary changes that require re-linking or re-signing by the platform (subject to platform policy); such changes must continue to use the standard store release path. - Replacement of the application's business logic or server-side behaviour.  ### Acceptance Criteria - A newly published update is detected and applied on a connected client without a store submission and without user action beyond the app being opened. - An update containing a deliberate runtime error is detected by the client's stability check and automatically reverted, leaving the client fully functional. - A signed package with a tampered payload is rejected and reported. - A client on an incompatible platform or OS version does not receive, and cannot activate, the update. - The application reports the active version matching the expected manifest version after activation.

issue_title: Add proper and complete support for multi-pass shaders
requirement: **Requirement: Complete Multi-Pass Shader Support**  The system shall support multi-pass shader effects, in which a shader definition contains an ordered sequence of two or more render passes, and each pass consumes the outputs of prior passes as inputs.  1. **Pass definition:** A shader shall be able to declare an ordered list of passes. Each pass shall specify its own vertex and fragment (or equivalent) programs, render state (blend, depth, stencil, cull mode), and render target.  2. **Pass execution order:** Passes shall execute strictly in the declared order within a single shader invocation. Execution of pass N+1 shall not begin until pass N has completed.  3. **Intermediate render targets:** Each pass may write to an intermediate render target (texture or framebuffer) that is allocated by the system, or to the final output. Intermediate targets shall be sized and formatted as specified per pass, with support for relative sizing (e.g., 1/2 or 1/4 of the viewport) and absolute sizing.  4. **Inter-pass data flow:** A pass shall be able to bind the output of any earlier pass in the same shader as a named texture input. References to a pass's output shall be validated at shader load time, and references to undefined or later-ordered passes shall produce a descriptive error.  5. **Feedback handling:** The system shall support optional feedback from a previous frame's output of a pass, with explicit double-buffering so that a pass never reads and writes the same resource in the same frame.  6. **Resource management:** Intermediate targets shall be created, reused, and released without leaking GPU memory. Targets shall be reallocated when the viewport or output size changes.  7. **Parameters:** Uniform and parameter values shall be settable per pass and shared across passes where declared, with a defined precedence rule when the same name is declared in multiple scopes.  8. **Validation and errors:** Malformed multi-pass definitions (cyclic dependencies, missing shader programs, mismatched formats between producer and consumer, unsupported pass counts beyond a documented limit) shall be rejected at load time with an error identifying the shader, pass, and cause. The system shall not crash or render partially on invalid input.  9. **Backward compatibility:** Existing single-pass shaders shall continue to load and render with identical output and no required changes to their definitions.  10. **Performance:** Pass count and intermediate target count shall be bounded by a documented limit. Shaders with a single pass shall incur no measurable overhead from the multi-pass code path.  **Acceptance criteria:** - A shader with three chained passes (e.g., blur horizontal, blur vertical, composite) renders output matching a reference image within a defined tolerance. - A pass referencing a later pass's output fails to load with a specific error message. - A pass with feedback from the previous frame renders correctly across at least 60 consecutive frames with no read-write hazards. - Resizing the output viewport reallocates intermediate targets and renders correctly without restart. - All existing single-pass shader tests pass unchanged. - Documentation covers the pass syntax, data-flow rules, limits, and at least one complete example.

issue_title: Implement method overloading in GDScript
requirement: **Requirement: Support Method Overloading in GDScript**  **Summary** GDScript shall allow multiple functions in the same scope to share a name when their parameter lists differ in arity or static parameter types. The compiler or analyzer shall resolve each call to exactly one overload, and shall report an error when resolution is ambiguous or no overload matches.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **Declaration:** A script, including inner classes, shall permit multiple `func` declarations with the same identifier if their parameter signatures differ by number of parameters or by declared parameter types. 2. **Duplicate detection:** Two declarations with the same name and an identical signature (same parameter count and types, ignoring parameter names and return type) shall produce a compile-time error that identifies both declaration locations. 3. **Static resolution:** When the argument types are statically known or inferable, the analyzer shall select the overload at compile time using the following rules, in order:    a. Exact match on arity and types.    b. Match requiring only implicit, lossless conversions (for example, `int` to `float`).    c. Match using default parameter values to fill omitted arguments.    If more than one candidate remains at the same rank, the analyzer shall report an ambiguity error. 4. **Dynamic resolution:** When argument types are not statically known (for example, `Variant` values), the call shall be dispatched at runtime by matching the actual argument count and runtime types to the candidate signatures, using the same ranking rules. If no candidate matches, the runtime shall raise an error that lists the available signatures and the received argument types. 5. **Untyped parameters:** Overloads that differ only in untyped parameters shall be distinguished by arity. Two untyped overloads with the same arity shall be a compile-time error. 6. **Return types:** Overloads shall be permitted to declare different return types. Return type alone shall not distinguish overloads. 7. **Inheritance:** A subclass method that matches an inherited overload's full signature shall override that overload. A subclass method with a new signature shall add an overload without hiding inherited overloads of the same name. Overriding rules shall be documented. 8. **Reflection:** `has_method()`, `call()`, `callv()`, and `Object.get_method_list()` shall behave consistently with overloaded names. `call()` and `callv()` shall dispatch using the same runtime rules as item 4. 9. **Signals and callables:** Callables referencing an overloaded name (for example, `Callable(self, "name")`) shall resolve to the overload matching the expected signature or raise an error if the match is ambiguous. 10. **Backward compatibility:** All existing valid GDScript code shall compile and run with unchanged behavior. Scripts that currently produce a duplicate-function error for differing signatures shall compile after this change.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  - Statically resolved calls shall have no measurable runtime overhead compared with non-overloaded calls. - Runtime dispatch overhead shall be documented and kept within a defined bound relative to a direct call (target to be set by maintainers). - Error messages shall include the candidate signatures and the reason for failure. - The language reference and the editor's autocomplete and documentation tooling shall display all overloads of a name.  **Acceptance Criteria**  - A test script defines `func add(a: int, b: int)` and `func add(a: float, b: float, c: float)`, and calls to `add(1, 2)`, `add(1.0, 2.0, 3.0)` each resolve correctly at compile time. - A test script with two `func f(x)` declarations produces a compile error. - A call with an untyped `Variant` argument that matches one overload at runtime executes that overload; a call matching none raises a runtime error listing the signatures. - An existing test suite in the repository passes unchanged. - Documentation, including the GDScript reference, describes overload resolution rules and examples.

issue_title: Add support for multiple displays/screens/monitors in Godot editor
requirement: **Requirement ID:** EDITOR-MULTI-DISPLAY-001 **Title:** Multi-Monitor Display Support for Godot Editor  **Description:** The Godot Editor shall fully support operation across multiple physical displays, enabling users to distribute editor components across screens, maintain persistent per-monitor layouts, and handle heterogeneous display configurations (varying resolutions and DPI scales).  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **Cross-Monitor Window Movement:** The editor main window shall be movable and resizable across monitor boundaries without automatic constraint to a single display or snapping back to the primary monitor.  2. **Detachable Panels:** The system shall allow detaching of editor panels (Inspector, Scene Tree, FileSystem Dock, Script Editor, Asset Library, etc.) into independent floating windows that can be positioned, resized, and maximized on any connected physical monitor.  3. **Layout Persistence:** The editor shall save and restore window positions, sizes, and dock states keyed to specific monitor configurations (identified by resolution, position, and OS display ID), restoring the exact arrangement when the same monitor setup is reconnected.  4. **Per-Monitor DPI Awareness:** When monitors utilize different DPI scale factors (e.g., 100% vs. 150% vs. 200%), the editor shall render text, icons, and UI elements sharply on each display without blurring, and shall maintain accurate mouse/touch input coordinates on all monitors.  5. **Fullscreen Modes:** The editor shall support:    - a) Borderless fullscreen spanning the entire virtual desktop (all monitors combined)    - b) Fullscreen constrained to a user-selected specific monitor    - c) Standard windowed mode on any single monitor  6. **Viewport Flexibility:** The 2D/3D editor viewport shall be resizable to span multiple monitors when in docked mode, or occupy a specific monitor when undocked as a floating window.  7. **Popup Localization:** Context menus, tooltips, dropdowns, and modal dialogs shall appear on the same physical monitor as their parent window, never defaulting to the primary display when invoked from a secondary monitor.  8. **Hot-Plug Handling:** The system shall gracefully handle monitor connection/disconnection events, automatically repositioning any windows or panels that fall outside the remaining visible display area onto the nearest available monitor without losing content or state.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  - **Performance:** Window move, resize, and detach operations shall complete without frame drops or input lag, maintaining interactive frame rates (≥60 FPS) during transitions. - **Platform Support:** Feature shall function on Windows 10/11 (per-monitor DPI aware v2), macOS 12+, and Linux (X11 and Wayland compositors). - **Data Integrity:** Window layout state shall be persisted to editor settings and survive editor crashes or forced termination.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - Given a dual-monitor setup with differing resolutions (e.g., 2560×1440 primary and 1920×1080 secondary), when the user drags the editor window across the boundary, then the window shall remain fully interactive and visible on the target monitor with correct rendering. - Given detached panels positioned on a secondary monitor, when the editor is closed and relaunched with the same monitor configuration, then all floating windows shall restore to their exact previous positions on the correct monitor. - Given monitors configured with different OS-level DPI scaling, when the editor spans both displays, then all UI text shall be legible and crisp on each screen, and mouse clicks shall register at the correct coordinates without offset. - Given an active editor session with panels on a secondary monitor, when that monitor is physically disconnected, then affected windows shall automatically migrate to the primary monitor and remain fully functional without data loss. - Given a triple-monitor arrangement, when the user selects "Fullscreen (All Monitors)" mode, then the editor shall occupy the total combined resolution as a single borderless window with seamless mouse movement across monitor boundaries.

issue_title: Allow explicitly defining interfaces in GDScript
requirement: The system shall provide a mechanism in GDScript for developers to explicitly define interfaces — abstract declarations of method and property signatures that classes can choose to implement — so that the engine can verify whether a class conforms to a declared interface and produce compile-time or editor-time errors when required methods or properties are missing or have mismatched signatures. This feature should allow classes to declare which interfaces they implement, enable type checking against interface types (e.g., in variable declarations, function parameters, and return types), and work independently of inheritance hierarchies, allowing unrelated classes that satisfy the same interface to be used interchangeably where that interface type is expected.

issue_title: [FR][RFC] Build a serving framework to host and serve trained PyTorch models
requirement: **Requirement ID:** REQ-SRV-001 **Title:** PyTorch Model Serving Framework  **Requirement Statement:** The system shall provide a model serving framework that enables users to host, manage, and serve inference requests for trained PyTorch models through a production-ready server.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **Model Packaging:** The framework shall accept trained PyTorch models packaged in a standardized archive format containing the serialized model (e.g., TorchScript), model metadata, and any user-defined handler code for preprocessing and postprocessing.  2. **Inference API:** The framework shall expose HTTP/REST and gRPC endpoints that accept inference requests (supporting JSON and binary tensor inputs) and return model predictions in a structured response format.  3. **Multi-Model Hosting:** The framework shall support hosting multiple models concurrently within a single server instance, with each model addressable by name and version.  4. **Model Management:** The framework shall allow users to register, update, list, scale (adjust worker count), and remove models and model versions at runtime without requiring a server restart.  5. **Versioning:** The framework shall support serving multiple versions of the same model simultaneously and designating a default version per model.  6. **Request Batching:** The framework shall support configurable dynamic batching of incoming inference requests to improve throughput, with user-defined batch size and timeout parameters.  7. **Custom Handlers:** The framework shall allow users to supply custom preprocessing, inference, and postprocessing logic to be executed on each request.  8. **Hardware Configuration:** The framework shall support inference on both CPU and GPU devices, with device assignment configurable per model.  9. **Metrics and Observability:** The framework shall collect and expose runtime metrics (e.g., request latency, throughput, error rates, queue depth, resource utilization) via a monitoring endpoint compatible with standard metrics systems (e.g., Prometheus).  10. **Logging:** The framework shall produce structured logs for inference requests, model lifecycle events, and server errors.  11. **Deployment:** The framework shall be deployable as a standalone process and as a containerized (Docker) service suitable for orchestration platforms (e.g., Kubernetes), with a command-line interface and configuration file for startup and model registration.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  1. The framework shall add no more than 10 ms of per-request overhead (excluding model compute time) at the 99th percentile under standard load. 2. The framework shall support horizontal scaling by running multiple stateless server instances behind a load balancer. 3. The framework shall operate on Linux and macOS environments with supported PyTorch versions.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - A user can package a trained PyTorch model, start the server, register the model via the management API or configuration, and receive correct predictions through the inference endpoint. - A new model version can be registered and promoted to default without server downtime. - Runtime metrics are retrievable from the monitoring endpoint during active inference traffic. - The same model archive runs identically on CPU-only and GPU-enabled deployments with only configuration changes.

issue_title: [feature request] Global GPU Flag
requirement: ## Requirement: Global GPU Flag  **Summary** Provide a single, project-wide switch that enables GPU acceleration for all GPU-capable operations in the system, without requiring users to enable GPU settings individually for each component (experiment, worker, dataset, model, etc.).  **Motivation** Today GPU usage is configured per-component/per-job, which is repetitive and error-prone when a user wants every run on a machine to use the GPU (e.g., on a shared GPU workstation or in CI). A global flag lets users opt into GPU execution once and have it apply consistently.  **Details** 1. The system must expose a global GPU enable/disable setting available at the top-level configuration and/or as an environment variable (e.g., `GLOBAL_GPU=true`). 2. When the global flag is enabled:    - All GPU-capable components (experiments, training jobs, workers, tasks, inference/evaluation runs) default to GPU execution, even if their individual configuration does not explicitly request a device.    - Individual component settings may still override the global default (an explicit per-component device/setting takes precedence), so power users retain control. 3. When the global flag is disabled or unset, behavior remains unchanged: devices are selected according to existing per-component configuration and CLI arguments. 4. The effective resolution order must be deterministic and documented: explicit per-component/per-run override → global flag → system default (typically CPU). 5. If a component requests GPU but no usable GPU is available at runtime, the system must fail loudly with a clear, actionable error message (naming the component and the underlying cause), rather than silently falling back to CPU, unless the user has explicitly opted into an allowed fallback. 6. The resolved device (GPU vs. CPU, including GPU index/type when applicable) must be reported in logs and surfaced in run metadata/status output for each job so users can confirm the flag took effect. 7. The flag must work consistently across all entry points (CLI, configuration file, programmatic/API use) and must not require code changes in individual components to be honored.  **Acceptance Criteria** - Setting the global flag to enabled causes every GPU-capable component in a run to execute on GPU with no per-component edits. - Leaving the flag unset reproduces current behavior exactly. - A per-component explicit override still wins over the global flag. - A run configured for GPU on a machine with no available GPU fails with a descriptive error instead of silently running on CPU. - Logs/run metadata show the resolved device for each component. - The flag and its precedence rules are documented in the user-facing documentation.

issue_title: cmd/link: support msvc object files
requirement: # Requirement: cmd/link — Support MSVC Object Files  **ID:** REQ-CMDLINK-MSVC-001 **Source Request:** "cmd/link: support msvc object files"  ## Background  On Windows, the Go internal linker (cmd/link) cannot consume COFF object files produced by the Microsoft Visual C++ (MSVC) toolchain. Users who must link Go programs against C/C++ libraries built with MSVC are forced to recompile those libraries with a GCC-compatible toolchain (e.g., MinGW-w64) or fall back to external linking. This requirement closes that gap by extending cmd/link to accept MSVC-produced object files.  ## Requirement Statement  The Go linker (cmd/link) shall support parsing and linking COFF object files produced by the MSVC toolchain in internal linking mode, enabling Go programs on Windows to link against MSVC-compiled C/C++ code without requiring a GCC-compatible toolchain.  ## Functional Requirements  1. **FR-1 — Object parsing:** cmd/link shall parse MSVC-generated COFF object files (`.obj`) for all supported Windows architectures (386, amd64, arm64). 2. **FR-2 — Symbol handling:** cmd/link shall correctly read MSVC symbol tables and name decorations (e.g., `__imp_` import thunks, stdcall `@N` suffixes) and resolve symbols between Go/cgo code and MSVC-compiled objects in both directions. 3. **FR-3 — Relocations:** cmd/link shall process all relocation types emitted by MSVC for each supported architecture, including section-relative and architecture-specific relocations. 4. **FR-4 — COMDAT support:** cmd/link shall handle COMDAT sections (including selection and associative semantics) without producing spurious duplicate-symbol errors. 5. **FR-5 — Static archives:** cmd/link shall link COFF static archives (`.lib`) whose members are MSVC-produced object files. 6. **FR-6 — Diagnostics:** when an MSVC object contains a construct cmd/link cannot process, the linker shall emit an error identifying the input file, the unsupported section/symbol/feature, and a suggested workaround (e.g., `-linkmode=external`). 7. **FR-7 — cgo integration:** object files and static libraries produced by MSVC shall be consumable through standard cgo mechanisms (`#cgo` directives, package-provided `.syso`/`.lib` inputs) without manual conversion.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - **AC-1:** A cgo program calling a function defined in an MSVC-compiled `.obj`/`.lib` builds and runs successfully with `go build` (default internal linking) on windows/amd64, windows/386, and windows/arm64. - **AC-2:** Go-exported functions are correctly resolved when referenced by MSVC-compiled code (callbacks). - **AC-3:** Objects containing COMDAT sections link cleanly where selection semantics permit. - **AC-4:** Unsupported constructs produce actionable diagnostics per FR-6. - **AC-5:** Existing cmd/link test suites pass without regressions; new tests cover MSVC object parsing, relocation application, COMDAT handling, and error cases on each supported architecture.  ## Scope and Constraints  - Applies to `GOOS=windows` targets only. - In scope: COFF object files and static archives produced by supported MSVC toolsets (Visual Studio 2015 and later). - Out of scope: PDB debug information consumption; C++ ABI features (exceptions, RTTI) beyond what the Go runtime already supports. - Internal linking of MinGW/GCC-produced COFF objects must not regress.

issue_title: rustdoc support for per-parameter documentation
requirement: ## Requirement: Per-Parameter Documentation Support in rustdoc  ### 1. Summary  rustdoc shall support attaching and rendering documentation for individual function and method parameters, so that callers can read a description, type semantics, and usage notes for each argument directly on the API documentation page of the function that owns it.  ### 2. Background / Problem Statement  Currently, rustdoc renders a single block of documentation for a function as a whole. Documentation for a specific argument can only be expressed indirectly:  - Comments placed above the parameter in the source are ordinary `//`/`/* */` comments and are discarded by the compiler and never reach rustdoc. - `///` (or `/** */`) doc comments written in parameter position are syntactically accepted as attributes on the parameter expression (e.g. `fn f(#[doc = "text"] x: u32)`), but rustdoc does not collect, associate, or render them; the information is silently lost from the generated documentation. - There is no structured place in the output where per-argument information can appear, so the "what does this argument mean?" question can only be answered by prose in the function-level doc comment, which is not machine-readable, cannot be validated against the signature, and is not reusable for tooling (e.g. IDEs, doc generators, API consumers).  ### 3. Goal  Enable Rust users to document each parameter in a structured way and have rustdoc:  1. Collect parameter-level documentation from the source. 2. Render it on the function's documentation page in a clearly identifiable, per-parameter form. 3. Keep the association between the documentation and the specific parameter unambiguous, including for functions with same-named parameters, destructured patterns, `self` receivers, methods, and trait/impl items. 4. Expose the information in a machine-readable form in rustdoc's JSON output.  ### 4. Functional Requirements  **FR-1 — Source-level syntax for parameter documentation.** rustdoc shall recognize doc comments written in parameter position as documentation belonging to that parameter. The following must be supported:  - `///` outer doc comments preceding a parameter. - `/** ... */` outer doc comments preceding a parameter. - `#[doc = "..."]` attributes on a parameter.  Documentation in parameter position shall be attributed to the immediately following parameter in the function signature.  **FR-2 — Collection into the documentation model.** Parameter documentation collected during compilation shall be stored on the corresponding `FnDecl`/`FnKind`/argument representation used by rustdoc, associated by parameter index, and carried through to the rendering and JSON stages.  **FR-3 — Rendering on the function page.** For every documented parameter, rustdoc shall render a dedicated "Arguments" (or equivalent) section in the function's documentation body, listing each parameter with:  - The parameter's name as written in the signature (or a canonical rendering for patterns, e.g. `a: u32`). - The parameter's type. - The parameter's documentation text, rendered with the same Markdown/HTML pipeline as all other rustdoc documentation (code blocks, links, intra-doc links, footnotes, etc.).  The section shall:  - Appear after the function's summary/description and before (or clearly distinguished from) the return-value section. - Include only parameters that have documentation, unless an explicit "show all parameters" mode is enabled (see FR-7). - Be emitted in parameter declaration order. - Use a stable, documented heading and structure so that downstream consumers and tests can rely on it.  **FR-4 — Return-value documentation consistency.** If a parameter documentation mechanism is introduced, rustdoc's existing handling of `-> T` return-value documentation (e.g. `# Returns` sections) shall continue to work unchanged and shall not conflict with the new per-parameter rendering.  **FR-5 — Interaction with existing doc conventions.** Parameter documentation shall not interfere with:  - Function-level doc comments, including `# Examples`, `# Panics`, `# Safety`, `# Errors` sections, which continue to apply to the function as a whole. - Intra-doc links and disambiguators, which shall resolve identically inside parameter documentation. - Attributes that are meaningful on parameters (e.g. `#[cfg]`, `#[allow]`, `#[cfg_attr]`): a `cfg`/`cfg_attr` that removes a parameter shall also remove its documentation, and documentation shall not resurrect a `cfg`-disabled parameter.  **FR-6 — Trait, impl, and method contexts.** Parameter documentation shall be collected and rendered for:  - Free functions. - Methods, including the `self` receiver (a `self` receiver may carry its own documentation, e.g. via a documented `self` parameter). - Associated functions in inherent and trait impls. - Function pointers, `Fn`/`FnMut`/`FnOnce` trait implementations, and closures where rustdoc exposes signatures. - Items generated by macros: documentation originating from macro expansion shall be handled consistently with rustdoc's existing macro-expansion behavior (i.e., preserved when the expansion is inlined, and reported with the usual span caveats otherwise).  **FR-7 — Configurable behavior.** rustdoc shall provide a configuration flag (e.g. `--document-parameter-docs` / a lint or cfg-style option) that controls whether per-parameter documentation is collected and rendered, so that:  - The behavior can be enabled for a project without affecting other crates' rendered output by default. - Users can opt out where per-parameter documentation is not desired or where existing parameter-position doc attributes were used for other purposes. - The default value of the flag shall be documented and shall be stated explicitly in the requirement and in rustdoc's `--help` output.  **FR-8 — JSON output.** rustdoc's JSON output format shall include, for each function-like item, an ordered list of parameter objects, each containing at minimum:  - `name` (string, as written in the signature). - `type` (the parameter's type as a string reference or rendered type). - `doc` (the parameter's documentation string, or `null`/absent when undocumented).  The JSON schema version shall be bumped, and the change shall be documented in the JSON output format documentation.  **FR-9 — Lint for misplaced or missing parameter documentation.** A rustdoc lint (opt-in by default within the enabling flag, or separately configurable) shall be able to warn when:  - A parameter-position doc comment/attribute exists but rustdoc cannot associate it with a parameter (e.g. dangling documentation, or documentation on a pattern binding that is not representable). - A parameter is undocumented while the function has parameter documentation on other parameters, if the "require all parameters documented" behavior is enabled.  ### 5. Non-Goals  - Changing Rust's ownership, name resolution, or the semantics of doc comments in non-parameter positions. - Providing parameter documentation for struct fields (already supported) or enum variants (already supported). - Generating parameter names automatically for unnamed/`_` parameters; `_` parameters may be documented but shall not be rendered with a synthesized name. - Supporting documentation attached to individual arguments at call sites.  ### 6. Edge Cases and Acceptance Criteria  The implementation is accepted when:  1. Given:    ```rust    /// Adds two numbers.    ///    /// # Examples    /// ```    /// assert_eq!(add(1, 2), 3);    /// ```    pub fn add(        /// The first addend.        a: i32,        /// The second addend.        b: i32,    ) -> i32 { a + b }    ```    the rendered page contains an "Arguments" section listing `a: i32` with "The first addend." and `b: i32` with "The second addend.", in that order, before any "Returns" section.  2. A parameter documented with `/** ... */` and one documented with `#[doc = "..."]` render equivalently to one documented with `///`.  3. A function with mixed documented and undocumented parameters lists only the documented ones by default, and all parameters when the "include all parameters" option is enabled.  4. A method with a documented `self` receiver renders the receiver's documentation alongside the other parameters.  5. Intra-doc links inside parameter documentation resolve to the same targets as links in function-level documentation.  6. A parameter removed by `#[cfg]` does not appear in the rendered page and its documentation does not appear either.  7. rustdoc JSON output for the `add` function above contains two parameter entries with the expected `name`, `type`, and `doc` fields.  8. `--document-parameter-docs` appears in `rustdoc --help` with a documented default value, and enabling/disabling it changes the rendered output as described.  9. Existing rustdoc test suites (including doc tests, `#[doc]` attribute tests, and JSON output tests) continue to pass, with new tests added covering parameter documentation collection, rendering, JSON serialization, and the `cfg`-interaction edge cases.  ### 7. Documentation Deliverables  - rustdoc book page (or equivalent) section describing how to document parameters, with examples, the enabling flag, and the interaction with existing `# Arguments`-style conventions. - Update to the rustdoc JSON output format documentation reflecting the new fields and the schema version bump. - Release notes / changelog entry describing the new behavior, the flag, and any migration guidance for code that previously used `#[doc]` attributes on parameters for unrelated purposes.

issue_title: [libs] Add `TcpStream::keepalive` and `TcpStream::set_keepalive`
requirement: Requirement: Add keepalive accessors to TcpStream  The `TcpStream` type in the libs component shall provide two methods for managing TCP keepalive behavior on the underlying socket:  1. `TcpStream::keepalive(&self) -> io::Result<Option<Duration>>` (or equivalent signature) shall return the currently configured TCP keepalive idle time for the stream. It shall return `None` when keepalive is disabled, and `Some(duration)` with the configured idle interval when it is enabled.  2. `TcpStream::set_keepalive(&self, keepalive: Option<Duration>) -> io::Result<()>` shall enable TCP keepalive with the given idle interval when passed `Some(duration)`, and disable keepalive on the socket when passed `None`.  Both methods shall: - Operate on the underlying OS socket using the platform's standard keepalive mechanism (e.g., SO_KEEPALIVE and the appropriate idle-time option such as TCP_KEEPIDLE on Linux or TCP_KEEPALIVE on macOS). - Propagate any OS-level errors as `io::Error` values rather than panicking. - Be available on all platforms where the underlying socket API supports keepalive, and document any platform-specific limitations or behavior differences. - Preserve the stream's other socket state and not affect read/write behavior beyond keepalive probing.

issue_title: Support multiple windows for desktop shells
requirement: **Requirement: Multi-Window Support for Desktop Shells**  The desktop shell must support opening and managing multiple application windows simultaneously. Specifically:  1. The shell shall allow more than one window to be open at the same time for the same application and across different applications. 2. Each window shall be independently created, focused, moved, resized, minimized, maximized, and closed without affecting other open windows. 3. The shell shall maintain a consistent registry of all open windows, including their identifiers, owning applications, and current state (focused, minimized, maximized, etc.). 4. The shell shall provide a means for users to switch between open windows (e.g., via taskbar, keyboard shortcut, or window list). 5. The shell shall correctly handle window stacking order, ensuring that the most recently activated window appears on top and that z-order is preserved when windows are restored or reordered. 6. Closing one window shall not terminate other windows belonging to the same application unless the application itself requests termination. 7. The shell shall persist and restore window positions and sizes across sessions where supported by the platform configuration. 8. Multi-window behavior shall not degrade shell responsiveness or cause resource leaks as the number of open windows increases.

issue_title: compress/bzip2: implement bz2 encoder
requirement: **Requirement: Implement a Bzip2 Encoder in the compress/bzip2 Package**  The Go standard library package `compress/bzip2` shall provide a bzip2 encoder that writes the bzip2 compressed file format, complementing the existing bzip2 decoder.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. The package shall expose a `Writer` type that implements the `io.WriteCloser` interface, accepting uncompressed data via `Write` and producing bzip2-compressed output on the underlying `io.Writer`.  2. `Writer` shall be constructed via `NewWriter(w io.Writer)` (default compression level) and `NewWriterLevel(w io.Writer, level int)`, where `level` is a valid integer in the range 1–9 (matching the convention of `compress/flate` and `compress/gzip`); invalid levels shall return an error.  3. The encoder shall produce output that is fully conformant with the bzip2 file format specification, including:    - The stream header (`BZh` magic bytes followed by the block-size digit).    - The per-block magic number (pi digits).    - Huffman/RLE encoding, MTF (move-to-front) transformation, and the Burrows–Wheeler block sorting as required by the format.    - The final CRC32 checksum block and the end-of-stream magic number.  4. `Close` shall flush all buffered data, write the final block and checksum, and mark the writer as complete. Additional writes after `Close` shall return an error (`ErrClosed`).  5. A `Reset(w io.Writer)` method shall be provided to allow reuse of the writer for a new stream, discarding the previous state.  6. Output produced by the encoder shall be decompressible by the existing `compress/bzip2` decoder and by reference bzip2 implementations, ensuring interoperability and round-trip fidelity.  **Quality Requirements:**  7. The encoder's compression ratio shall be comparable to the reference bzip2 implementation at the same compression level, with a maximum deviation that does not materially degrade compression performance.  8. The encoder shall include a complete set of unit tests, including round-trip tests (encode → decode) across varying input sizes, data patterns, and compression levels, and tests validating error handling for invalid levels and closed writers.  9. The implementation shall be added to the `compress/bzip2` package and shall follow the Go standard library's code style, documentation conventions, and error-handling patterns.

issue_title: net/http: support HTTP/3
requirement: Requirement: HTTP/3 Support in net/http  The net/http package shall support HTTP/3 as both a client and a server protocol, in addition to the existing HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 support.  Specifically:  1. Client support: http.Client and http.Transport shall be able to issue requests over HTTP/3 when the peer supports it, using QUIC as the underlying transport. 2. Server support: http.Server shall be able to accept and serve HTTP/3 requests over QUIC, using the same Handler interface used for other HTTP versions. 3. Protocol negotiation: The implementation shall support discovery of HTTP/3 availability, such as via Alt-Svc headers, and shall fall back to HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 when HTTP/3 is unavailable or fails. 4. TLS requirements: HTTP/3 connections shall use TLS 1.3 as required by the QUIC specification, and shall respect existing http.Transport and http.Server TLS configuration options where applicable. 5. API compatibility: Existing public APIs shall remain backward compatible; any new configuration options for HTTP/3 shall be additive. 6. Standards compliance: The implementation shall conform to RFC 9114 (HTTP/3) and RFC 9000 (QUIC transport). 7. Resource handling: Request and response semantics, including headers, trailers, body streaming, cancellation via context, and connection lifecycle management, shall behave consistently with the HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 implementations in net/http.

issue_title: Use mold as default linker?
requirement: **Requirement: Use mold as the default linker when available**  The build system shall use the mold linker by default for linking on supported platforms (Linux, x86-64 and AArch64), provided that mold is installed.  1. **Default selection:** When the user has not explicitly configured a linker, the build shall invoke mold for the link step on supported platforms. 2. **Detection:** The build shall detect mold on the system `PATH` or at a user-configured location. If it is not found, the build shall fall back to the platform's default linker without failing and shall log an informational message stating that mold was not found and which linker is being used. 3. **Override:** Users shall be able to select a different linker (including the system default `ld`/`ld.bfd`/`gold`/`lld`) through a documented build option or environment variable. An explicit user selection shall take precedence over the default. 4. **Platform scope:** On unsupported platforms (for example, macOS and Windows), the build shall keep its existing linker behavior unchanged. 5. **Functional equivalence:** Binaries linked with mold shall pass the full existing test suite with no functional regressions. 6. **Documentation:** The build and installation documentation shall state that mold is the default linker on supported platforms, describe the fallback behavior, and explain how to override the default.  **Acceptance criteria:** - On a Linux system with mold installed and no overrides set, the link step invokes mold, verified by build logs or verbose output. - On a Linux system without mold, the build succeeds using the fallback linker and logs an informational message. - Setting the override option or environment variable to a different linker uses that linker and ignores the mold default. - On macOS and Windows, the linker invocation is unchanged from the previous release. - The full test suite passes with the mold default enabled in CI.

issue_title: Add a "Mask2D" node (and/or a "mask_parent" property for Sprite2D)
requirement: The engine shall provide a 2D masking mechanism to restrict the visible region of rendered 2D content using a mask texture or geometric shape. This shall be implemented via one or both of the following interfaces: (1) a `Mask2D` node class inheriting from `Node2D` that clips the rendering of all descendant `CanvasItem` nodes to the opaque areas of its assigned mask source, and/or (2) a `mask_parent` property on `Sprite2D` (and other applicable 2D visual nodes) referencing a `Mask2D` instance, causing the node's output to be clipped by the referenced mask. The mask source shall be defined by a `Texture2D` (utilizing its alpha channel) or a vector path. Masking operations shall occur during the 2D rendering pipeline, preserving the transform hierarchy of masked content, and shall support multiple masked items referencing the same mask instance without affecting physics, collision detection, or the logical scene graph structure.

issue_title: Support Firefox as a browser in flutter run
requirement: **Feature: Firefox Browser Support for `flutter run` (Web Target)**  **Description:** The `flutter run` command must support Mozilla Firefox as a target browser when running Flutter web applications. Users should be able to select Firefox as the browser for development sessions in the same way they can select Chrome or Edge.  **Requirements:**  1. **Browser Selection:** `flutter run -d web-server` and related web device targets must allow Firefox to be launched automatically when the user specifies it (e.g., via a `--browser` option or equivalent configuration). 2. **Browser Detection:** The Flutter tool must detect an installed Firefox executable on supported platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux) using standard installation paths and environment configuration. 3. **Custom Path Override:** Users must be able to specify a custom Firefox executable path if it is not found automatically, via an environment variable or configuration setting. 4. **Debugging Integration:** Hot reload, hot restart, and the Dart DevTools connection must function for Flutter web apps running in Firefox, to the same extent as with Chrome. 5. **Error Handling:** If Firefox is requested but not installed or cannot be launched, the tool must display a clear, actionable error message indicating the missing component and how to resolve it. 6. **Compatibility:** Existing behavior for Chrome and Edge must remain unchanged. 7. **Documentation:** Flutter documentation must be updated to list Firefox as a supported browser for `flutter run` and describe how to select it.

issue_title: rustdoc: `--enable-index-page` integration with cargo?
requirement: **REQ-CARGO-RUSTDOC-001 — `cargo doc` support for rustdoc `--enable-index-page`**  The `cargo doc` command shall provide a first-class option to enable rustdoc's index-page generation, so that users can produce a documentation index page without resorting to workarounds such as `RUSTDOCFLAGS="--enable-index-page"`.  Sub-requirements:  1. **Option exposure:** `cargo doc` shall accept an `--enable-index-page` option. When specified, cargo shall pass `--enable-index-page` to every rustdoc invocation it performs for the documentation build, including workspace-wide builds (`--workspace`/`--all`). 2. **Expected behavior:** When the option is enabled, the build shall produce an index page (`index.html`) in the documentation output directory (e.g., `target/doc`) that indexes the documented items generated by the build, so the index is reachable through the normal `cargo doc --open` entry point. 3. **Default behavior:** When the option is absent, `cargo doc` behavior shall be unchanged and no index page shall be generated. 4. **Stability gating:** While rustdoc's `--enable-index-page` remains unstable, the cargo option shall be gated behind nightly-only unstable options (i.e., require `-Z unstable-options`). When used on a stable toolchain or without `-Z unstable-options`, cargo shall abort with a clear, non-zero-exit error message that names the unstable feature and explains how to enable it. 5. **Toolchain compatibility:** If the selected toolchain's rustdoc does not recognize `--enable-index-page`, cargo shall surface a diagnostic identifying the unsupported option; the failure shall not be silently ignored, and no partially generated documentation index shall be presented as success. 6. **Parity guarantee:** `cargo doc --enable-index-page` shall produce the same rustdoc invocations (with respect to the index-page flag) as `RUSTDOCFLAGS="--enable-index-page" cargo doc`, ensuring no behavioral divergence between the two mechanisms. 7. **Documentation:** The option shall be documented in the cargo command reference, including its stability status, its effect on single-crate versus workspace documentation builds, and its interaction with related options such as `--document-private-items` and `--open`.  Acceptance criteria:  - On nightly with `-Z unstable-options`, `cargo doc --enable-index-page` succeeds and generates `target/doc/index.html` containing links to the built crate's documented items. - `cargo doc --enable-index-page` without `-Z unstable-options` (or on stable) exits with an explanatory error and generates no index page. - `cargo doc` without the option produces output identical to current behavior (no `index.html` generated). - A rustdoc version lacking the flag results in a clear diagnostic rather than silent omission of the index page.

issue_title: Implement method overloading in GDScript
requirement: ## Requirement: GDScript method overloading  GDScript shall allow multiple methods with the same name in a class when their parameter counts or declared parameter types differ. For example:  ```gdscript func process(value: int) -> void func process(value: String) -> void ```  - Overload resolution shall consider required, optional, and variadic parameters. - Exact type matches shall be preferred over matches requiring implicit GDScript type conversions. - Calls with statically known argument types shall be validated during analysis whenever possible. - Calls involving `Variant` or other dynamically typed arguments shall be resolved at runtime using the runtime value’s type. - A call that matches no overload or matches multiple equally suitable overloads shall produce an error identifying the available signatures. - Two methods with identical parameter lists remain invalid as duplicate definitions; return type alone does not distinguish overloads. - Inherited overloads shall remain available according to existing method-lookup and override rules. - Editor tooling, documentation, and automated tests shall cover overloaded declarations, calls, inheritance, ambiguity, and missing matches.

issue_title: Struct initializer `..x` syntax should work for other structs with structurally equal subset of fields
requirement: Rust shall allow functional record update syntax (`Target { field: value, ..base }`) to use a `base` expression of a different struct type when the base contains every target field omitted from the initializer with the same field name and type. Explicitly initialized fields retain their supplied values, while omitted fields are populated from the base using existing ownership, move, and copy semantics. Extra fields in the base are permitted but are not copied. The compiler shall reject the expression when an omitted field is missing from the base or has an incompatible type.  For example, given `struct Common { x: i32, y: i32 }` and `struct Extended { x: i32, y: i32, z: bool }`, `Extended { z: true, ..common }` shall be valid when `common` has type `Common`.

issue_title: Add WebGPU support
requirement: **Requirement: Add WebGPU Support**  The software shall support WebGPU as a graphics and compute backend, enabling it to run in environments that expose the WebGPU API (e.g., modern web browsers and native WebGPU implementations), in addition to any existing backends.  **Functional requirements:**  1. Detect WebGPU availability at runtime and enumerate adapters/devices, including feature and limit queries. 2. Implement full lifecycle management of WebGPU resources: buffers, textures, samplers, bind groups, command encoders, and render/compute pipelines, with shaders authored in or translated to WGSL as needed. 3. Achieve functional parity with existing backends: all currently supported rendering and compute features shall produce correct results when running on WebGPU. 4. Integrate backend selection into the existing configuration/API, allowing WebGPU to be explicitly requested or automatically selected when available. 5. Degrade gracefully on platforms without WebGPU support by falling back according to existing backend-selection policy or reporting a clear, actionable error. 6. Provide diagnostics/logging for initialization failures and unsupported feature combinations under WebGPU.  **Acceptance criteria:**  - Examples, tests, or demos run successfully with the WebGPU backend on at least one mainstream browser or native WebGPU implementation. - Visual/compute output is verified correct against results from existing backends. - Environments lacking WebGPU continue to function without crashes or silent failures. - Documentation describes how to enable and select the WebGPU backend, along with any known limitations.

The plugin should compile and run when targeting web, providing sensible behavior for its APIs (e.g., returning temporary paths or throwing appropriate `UnsupportedError` exceptions for paths that do not apply on web), so that applications depending on `path_provider` do not need to add conditional imports or platform-specific workarounds.

issue_title: Include images in rustdoc output
requirement: **REQ-RUSTDOC-001: Image Inclusion in rustdoc Output**  **Statement:** The rustdoc tool shall support embedding images in generated documentation. When a documentation comment contains a Markdown image reference of the form `![alt-text](path)`, rustdoc shall render the image in the corresponding documentation page.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  1. Relative image paths shall be resolved against the source file containing the documentation comment (including `///`, `//!`, and `#[doc = "..."]` forms); remote URLs (`http`/`https`) shall be passed through unchanged and not downloaded. 2. Referenced local image files shall be copied into the documentation output directory, preserving the relative directory structure needed for the rendered page to display the image, without modifying or re-encoding file contents. 3. At minimum, the following formats shall be supported: PNG, JPEG, GIF, SVG, and WebP; unrecognized file types shall be copied as-is. 4. Images shall be rendered in all documentation contexts, including item-level docs (modules, structs, enums, functions, traits, etc.), crate-level docs, and docs generated from standalone Markdown files. 5. If a referenced local image file is missing, unreadable, or of an unsupported location, rustdoc shall emit a warning identifying the file path and the originating source location, and shall render the alt text in place of the image. A missing image shall not cause documentation generation to fail. 6. Image files originating from different source locations shall be copied to non-colliding output paths, and clean builds shall not leave stale copies of previously referenced images in the output directory.

issue_title: Implement `numpy.random.choice` equivalent
requirement: ## Random Choice Sampling  Implement a public `choice(a, size=None, replace=True, p=None)` API equivalent to `numpy.random.choice`.  - Interpret `a` as either a non-negative integer population, equivalent to `range(a)`, or a one-dimensional sequence or array of selectable elements. - Return uniformly sampled elements when `p` is omitted. - When `p` is provided, perform probability-weighted sampling. The probabilities must:   - Have the same length as the population.   - Be finite and non-negative.   - Sum to 1 within the implementation’s floating-point tolerance. - Support sampling with replacement when `replace=True` and sampling without replacement when `replace=False`. - When sampling without replacement, select distinct population positions and raise a validation error if `size` exceeds the number of available positions. - Support `size=None`, an integer, or a tuple of integers:   - `size=None` returns one selected element.   - An integer size produces a one-dimensional result.   - A tuple size produces a result with the corresponding shape.   - A zero size produces an empty result with the requested shape. - Preserve the sampled values and the population’s data type. - Integrate with the existing random-number generator so configured seeds and random state produce reproducible results. - Reject invalid population sizes, output sizes, replacement settings, and probability vectors with clear errors consistent with the project’s public API conventions.

issue_title: [RFC] Add tar-based IterableDataset implementation to PyTorch
requirement: The system shall provide an `IterableDataset` implementation within `torch.utils.data` that sequentially streams and yields samples directly from single or multiple POSIX tar archives (including `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, and `.tar.bz2` formats) without requiring prior extraction to disk. The dataset must support:  1. Accepting local file paths, file-like objects, or network stream inputs. 2. Partitioning/sharding archive iteration across distributed processes and multi-process `DataLoader` workers via `torch.utils.data.get_worker_info()`. 3. Grouping associated files sharing common prefixes/keys within an archive into unified data samples. 4. Custom sample filtering, parsing, and transform pipelines. 5. Configurable error-handling modes (e.g., raise, warn, or ignore) when encountering corrupted or truncated tar records.

issue_title: Add literal quoted strings with embedded variables (f-strings) to GDScript
requirement: **REQ-FSTR-001 — Formatted String Literals (f-strings) in GDScript**  GDScript shall support formatted string literals ("f-strings"): string literals prefixed with `f` (case-insensitive) in which brace-delimited embedded expressions are evaluated at runtime, converted to `String` using `str()` semantics, and substituted into the resulting string.  1. **Syntax.** The `f` prefix may precede any regular String literal (single-quoted, double-quoted, or triple-quoted multiline), e.g. `f"Hello, {player_name}! Score: {score}"`. It shall not apply to StringName (`&"…"`) or NodePath (`^"…"`) literals. The combined prefixes `rf`/`fr` shall be supported, with raw-string escape rules applying to backslashes while interpolation remains active.  2. **Interpolation semantics.** Each `{expression}` shall be evaluated in left-to-right order, in the scope where the literal appears, each time the literal is evaluated. Arbitrary valid GDScript expressions are permitted, including member access, indexing, arithmetic, and function calls.  3. **Escaping.** `{{` and `}}` shall render literal `{` and `}` characters, respectively.  4. **Error handling.** Unbalanced braces, empty expressions `{}`, or syntactically invalid embedded expressions shall be reported as parse-time errors with accurate line/column information. Runtime failures within an embedded expression (e.g., an invalid property access) shall behave identically to the same expression evaluated as a standalone statement.  5. **Compatibility.** Existing string literals, the `%` formatting operator, and `String.format` shall be unaffected. An f-string containing no braces shall be valid and behave as an ordinary String.  6. **Out of scope (initial version).** Python-style format specifiers (e.g., `{x:.2f}`), dictionary literals inside embedded expressions (due to brace-delimiter ambiguity), and embedded expressions containing the string's own delimiter quote character.

issue_title: Add procedural and parametrizable audio support

issue_title: cmd/go: add 'go get' options to update direct and indirect dependencies separately
requirement: **Requirement: Separate Update Options for Direct and Indirect Dependencies in `go get`**  The `go get` command shall provide options to update direct dependencies and indirect dependencies independently, so that a user can update one set without changing the other.  1. **Direct-only update:** When the user invokes `go get` with the direct-dependency option (for example, `-direct`), the command shall update only the module requirements that are direct dependencies of the main module, meaning those listed without `// indirect` in `go.mod`. Indirect requirements shall remain at their currently selected versions unless a version change is required to satisfy a direct dependency's updated requirements.  2. **Indirect-only update:** When the user invokes `go get` with the indirect-dependency option (for example, `-indirect`), the command shall update only the module requirements marked `// indirect` in `go.mod`. Direct dependencies shall remain at their currently required versions.  3. **Compatibility with existing update flags:** The new options shall work with the existing update modes (`-u`, `-u=patch`) and shall not change the behavior of `go get` when neither new option is specified.  4. **Dependency consistency:** The command shall preserve a consistent build list. If an update to one set requires a change to the other to satisfy the module graph, the command shall apply the minimum necessary change and report it to the user.  5. **Go module files:** After execution, `go.mod` and `go.sum` shall reflect only the changes permitted by the selected option, and the `// indirect` markers shall be correctly maintained.  6. **Output and diagnostics:** The command shall report which modules were updated, which were left unchanged, and any indirect or direct modules that were changed due to a constraint from the other set.  7. **Documentation:** The `go help get` output and the Go Modules Reference shall describe the new options, their interaction with `-u` and `-t`, and examples of their use.  8. **Testing:** Automated tests shall cover direct-only updates, indirect-only updates, combined use with `-u` and `-u=patch`, cases where a forced change in one set propagates to the other, and the unchanged default behavior.

issue_title: x/tools/gopls: support for bazel-based projects
requirement: **Requirement: Bazel-Based Project Support in gopls**  gopls shall support Go projects built with Bazel. Specifically:  1. gopls shall detect Bazel workspaces (identified by a `WORKSPACE` or `MODULE.bazel` file at the root) and treat them as valid project roots. 2. gopls shall load Go packages in Bazel workspaces so that code navigation, completion, diagnostics, and other language features work for Bazel-built code. 3. gopls shall use package metadata provided by Bazel (such as Go package and import path information from build rules) when Go's native build system cannot resolve a package, avoiding reliance on `go list` alone where it fails. 4. gopls shall allow users to configure Bazel-specific behavior, including the Bazel executable path and build/query arguments, through its settings. 5. gopls shall handle Bazel-generated files and external repository dependencies so that imports resolve correctly to their Bazel-managed locations. 6. gopls shall keep Bazel-derived package information up to date when BUILD files or Go sources change, without requiring a restart of the editor or language server. 7. When Bazel is unavailable or a query fails, gopls shall fall back to standard Go tooling behavior and report a clear, non-fatal diagnostic to the user.

issue_title: Server-side rendering for Flutter web
requirement: **Requirement: Server-Side Rendering Support for Flutter Web**  The Flutter web framework shall provide a supported mechanism to render Flutter web application content on the server and deliver the resulting HTML to the client, so that initial page content is visible before client-side JavaScript loads and executes.  **Functional requirements**  1. The framework shall generate HTML markup for the initial application view on the server, given a route and application state. 2. The server-rendered output shall be hydrated by the Flutter web client without a visible flash or layout shift, preserving the rendered state. 3. The framework shall support server-side rendering of routed pages, including the ability to resolve the requested URL path to the corresponding view. 4. The framework shall expose an API for applications to supply server-side data (such as initial state) that is serialized into the page and consumed by the client during hydration. 5. The framework shall allow rendering to be executed in a non-browser runtime (e.g., a Dart VM process) without requiring a DOM or browser APIs. 6. The framework shall provide a fallback to client-side rendering when server rendering fails or is not configured.  **Non-functional requirements**  1. Server-rendered responses shall produce valid HTML5 that passes standard validation. 2. Server rendering of a representative page shall complete within a configurable time budget (default: 200 ms on reference hardware) and shall fail gracefully with a logged error if exceeded. 3. Server-rendered output shall be deterministic for identical inputs (route, state, and locale). 4. The feature shall not degrade client-side rendering performance or increase the client bundle size for applications that do not opt in.  **Acceptance criteria**  1. A sample application can be rendered to HTML on the server for at least three distinct routes, and each response contains the expected text content in the HTML body without executing client JavaScript. 2. The client hydrates the server-rendered page with no console errors and no visible re-render of content on first load. 3. Applications that do not enable server rendering produce the same build output as before this feature is introduced. 4. Documentation describes setup, supported platforms, known limitations (such as unsupported plugins or platform channels), and migration steps. 5.
