issue_title: Implement a code formatter for GDScript in the script editor
requirement: # Requirement: GDScript Code Formatter in the Script Editor  ## Summary The Godot script editor shall provide a built-in code formatter that reformats GDScript source code to a consistent, configurable style without changing program behavior.  ## User Story As a GDScript developer, I want to automatically format my script in the script editor so that my code follows a consistent style and I spend less time on manual whitespace and layout adjustments.  ## Functional Requirements  1. **Invocation**    1.1. The formatter shall be invocable from the script editor via a menu item (e.g., Edit or Script menu) and a configurable keyboard shortcut.    1.2. The formatter shall be invocable on the entire script or on the current selection.    1.3. The formatter may optionally run automatically on save, controlled by an editor setting that is disabled by default.  2. **Formatting Rules**    2.1. Indentation shall use the project's configured indent style (tabs or spaces) and indent size.    2.2. The formatter shall normalize spacing around operators, after commas, after colons in dictionaries, and inside parentheses and brackets according to the style rules.    2.3. The formatter shall normalize blank lines between functions, class declarations, and top-level statements to a configurable count (default: two blank lines between top-level functions and classes, one blank line otherwise).    2.4. The formatter shall remove trailing whitespace and ensure a single newline at end of file.    2.5. The formatter shall wrap or align multi-line array, dictionary, and function call expressions consistently.    2.6. The formatter shall preserve the content and position of comments, including inline comments and `##` documentation comments.    2.7. The formatter shall preserve line continuations and multi-line string literals without altering their contents.  3. **Semantic Preservation**    3.1. The formatter shall not change the semantics of the script. The token sequence after formatting, ignoring whitespace and layout, shall be identical to the token sequence before formatting.    3.2. The formatter shall not modify identifiers, string literal contents, or numeric literal values.  4. **Error Handling**    4.1. If the script contains a syntax error, the formatter shall not modify the script and shall display a message identifying the error location.    4.2. The formatter shall report failures without corrupting or truncating the file contents.  5. **Editor Integration**    5.1. A single formatting operation shall be undoable with one undo action.    5.2. Caret position and scroll position shall be preserved as closely as possible after formatting.    5.3. Formatting shall not mark unrelated portions of the file as changed.  6. **Configuration**    6.1. Formatting options (indent style, indent size, blank lines between functions, trailing newline) shall be configurable in Editor Settings.    6.2. Settings shall be persisted per user, with optional project-level overrides.  ## Non-Functional Requirements - **Performance:** Formatting a script of 2,000 lines shall complete within 200 ms on reference hardware. - **Idempotency:** Formatting an already formatted script shall produce no changes. - **Reliability:** The formatter shall be covered by automated tests, including a corpus of valid GDScript files and round-trip semantic checks. - **Compatibility:** The formatter shall support all GDScript syntax supported by the current Godot release, including static typing, annotations, lambdas, and inner classes.  ## Acceptance Criteria - AC1: Given a script with mixed tab and space indentation, when the user runs the formatter, then all indentation matches the configured style. - AC2: Given a script with syntax errors, when the user runs the formatter, then the file remains unchanged and an error message identifies the line and column of the first error. - AC3: Given a formatted script, when the formatter runs again, then the file content is byte-identical to the prior result. - AC4: Given any valid script, when formatted, then its token sequence (excluding whitespace) is unchanged. - AC5: Given a formatting operation, when the user presses Undo once, then the script returns to its exact pre-format state. - AC6: Given "format on save" is enabled, when the user saves a script, then the formatter runs before the file is written. - AC7: Given a selection, when the formatter runs on the selection, then only the selected lines are modified.  ## Out of Scope - Enforcing lint rules or refactoring code structure (e.g., reordering members or renaming symbols). - Formatting non-GDScript files such as shader or C# scripts. - Formatting across multiple files in a single operation.

issue_title: Flutter support for Apple Watch
requirement: **Requirement: Native watchOS Platform Support for Flutter Framework**  **Overview:** Extend the Flutter engine, framework, and tooling to enable full development, compilation, deployment, and debugging of Flutter applications targeting Apple Watch (watchOS), including seamless bidirectional communication with companion iOS applications.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. **Platform Target Support:** The Flutter engine MUST compile and run on watchOS (versions 7.0+), supporting both arm64_32 (Series 4-7) and arm64 (Series 8+, Ultra) architectures. 2. **Tooling Integration:** The Flutter CLI MUST support `flutter create --platforms=ios,watchos`, `flutter build watchos`, and `flutter run --device-id <watch-device-id>` for direct deployment to physical Apple Watch devices. 3. **UI Framework Adaptation:** The widget framework MUST provide watch-specific layout constraints, navigation patterns (hierarchical and flat), and input handling optimized for 38mm–49mm displays, including Digital Crown and gesture support. 4. **Inter-Device Communication:** Platform channels MUST support reliable data exchange between a Flutter watchOS app and its companion Flutter iOS app via WatchConnectivity framework, including background transfers and real-time messaging. 5. **Plugin Architecture:** The plugin system MUST support watch-specific plugins (watchOS extensions) and allow existing iOS plugins to expose watch-compatible APIs. 6. **Development Experience:** Hot reload MUST function on watchOS targets when the watch is connected to a Mac via the companion iPhone, with debug logging routed through the iOS tethering connection.  **Non-Functional Requirements:** - **Performance:** Watch applications MUST achieve cold launch times under 2 seconds on Apple Watch Series 6 and later. - **Resource Efficiency:** The engine memory footprint MUST be optimized to operate within watchOS memory constraints (≤ 1GB RAM), with aggressive asset caching strategies for limited storage. - **Power Management:** Rendering and animation pipelines MUST implement frame-skipping and low-power modes to minimize battery impact during active use. - **Accessibility:** Full support for VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, and Reduce Motion accessibility settings native to watchOS.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - [ ] A developer can generate a Flutter project with watchOS support using standard CLI commands - [ ] Sample watch application renders correctly across all supported watch sizes (38mm, 40mm, 41mm, 42mm, 44mm, 45mm, 49mm) with appropriate safe-area handling - [ ] Bidirectional messaging between Flutter iOS and watchOS apps completes with < 100ms latency for small payloads (< 1KB) - [ ] Watch apps pass Apple App Store validation including required companion iOS app pairing - [ ] Hot reload updates UI changes on watch within 1 second of code modification - [ ] Memory usage remains under 200MB during standard UI interaction on Series 6 hardware  **Constraints & Dependencies:** - watchOS applications REQUIRE a companion iOS app; standalone watch-only Flutter apps are not supported by Apple's architecture - Development requires Xcode 14+ with watchOS SDK and a paired iPhone running iOS 15+ - Background execution is limited to watchOS background app refresh intervals and complications - Input is restricted to touch, Digital Crown rotation/click, and side button (no keyboard input)

issue_title: Implement Terrain
requirement: **REQ-TERRAIN-001: Terrain Generation, Rendering, and Editing Subsystem**  The system shall provide a complete terrain subsystem capable of generating, rendering, manipulating, and persisting three-dimensional terrain surfaces derived from heightmap data or procedural algorithms.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. The system shall import heightmap data from standard image formats (PNG, TIFF, RAW) and geospatial formats (GeoTIFF, HGT) to generate triangle mesh geometry with configurable vertex spacing. 2. The system shall implement procedural terrain generation using fractal noise algorithms (Perlin, Simplex, or Worley) with user-configurable parameters including octaves, persistence, lacunarity, scale, and random seed for deterministic output. 3. The system shall generate renderable mesh geometry with automatic Level-of-Detail (LOD) management, supporting at least 4 LOD levels with configurable transition distances to maintain rendering performance. 4. The system shall provide real-time terrain editing tools including height modification (raise/lower), smoothing, flattening, and noise brushes with adjustable radius, strength, and falloff. 5. The system shall support multi-texture splatting based on height ranges, slope angles, and custom blend masks, allowing a minimum of 4 simultaneous surface materials. 6. The system shall implement spatial partitioning (quadtree or octree) with frustum and occlusion culling to render terrains up to 4096×4096 resolution while maintaining 60 FPS on target hardware. 7. The system shall provide accurate collision detection and raycasting against terrain geometry for physics engines and interaction systems. 8. The system shall serialize terrain state (height data, texture masks, LOD settings) to a native binary format and/or standard interchange format (OBJ, PLY) for save/load operations.  **Non-Functional Requirements:** 1. The terrain subsystem shall operate within a memory budget of 2 GB for a 4096×4096 resolution terrain including textures and collision data. 2. Initial terrain generation for a 1024×1024 heightmap shall complete within 5 seconds on reference hardware. 3. LOD transitions shall be geometrically seamless without visible popping, cracking, or texture swimming. 4. The implementation shall be renderer-agnostic, supporting both forward and deferred rendering pipelines with standard PBR shader models.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - Given a valid 16-bit heightmap file, when imported, then the generated mesh vertices match the height data within a tolerance of ±0.001 units. - Given identical procedural generation parameters and seed values, when generating terrain twice, then the resulting geometry shall be bitwise identical. - Given a 2048×2048 terrain with 4 LOD levels, when rendering with a camera traversing the scene, then the frame rate shall remain ≥60 FPS on a NVIDIA GTX 1060 or equivalent. - Given terrain editing operations applied via the API or editor, when the terrain is saved and subsequently loaded, then all height modifications and texture masks shall be preserved exactly.

issue_title: Initializing array of Option<T> using [None; n] syntax should not require std::marker::Copy for T
requirement: Requirement: Array repeat-expression initialization for Option<T>  The Rust compiler and standard library shall permit array initialization of the form `[None; N]` for any element type `Option<T>`, where `T` is an arbitrary type that does not implement `Copy` (and no `Clone` bound is imposed on `T` by this syntax).  Acceptance criteria:  1. The expression `let a: [Option<T>; N] = [None; N];` compiles successfully for any type `T`, including non-`Copy` types such as `String`, `Vec<U>`, and user-defined structs without `Copy` or `Clone` implementations. 2. The resulting array has length `N` and every element is `None`. 3. The array repeat-expression form is accepted in both `const` and non-`const` contexts when the element expression is the constant `None`. 4. The compiler does not emit an error stating that `Option<T>: Copy` or `T: Copy` is unsatisfied for this expression. 5. Existing behavior for `[Some(x); N]` and other repeat expressions involving non-`Copy` element types is unchanged, i.e., those forms continue to require `Copy` (or a `const` item operand) as before. 6. The change introduces no new unsound behavior: each element is independently initialized to `None` without aliasing or double-drop. 7. Documentation for array repeat expressions and `Option` is updated to describe when `[None; N]` is permitted without `Copy`.

issue_title: cmd/compile: implement powerpc 32-bit backend (ppc32)
requirement: ## Requirement: Implement a 32-bit PowerPC backend (`ppc32`) in `cmd/compile`  ### Summary `cmd/compile` shall gain a new code-generation backend targeting 32-bit PowerPC (`ppc32`), enabling the Go toolchain to build and run programs for that architecture.  ### Motivation The compiler currently supports only 64-bit PowerPC (`ppc64`) plus the other 32-bit targets (`386`, `arm`, `mips`, `mipsle`, …). A 32-bit PowerPC target is required so that Go programs can be built for 32-bit PowerPC systems (e.g. older/embedded PowerPC hosts and cross-compilation targets), matching the feature set already available on `ppc64`.  ### Functional Requirements  1. **Architecture support**    - Add `ppc32` as a recognized compiler architecture (e.g. `GOARCH=ppc32` in `cmd/internal/obj`, `cmd/internal/sys`, `cmd/dist`, `cmd/internal/goarch`, and the internal `objabi`/`ssagen` plumbing).    - The backend shall be selectable through the standard `-S`, `-m`, and cross-compilation build paths, and `go build`/`go test` for `GOARCH=ppc32` shall work end to end.  2. **Code generation**    - Implement instruction selection, register allocation, stack-frame layout, and prologue/epilogue generation for the 32-bit PowerPC ISA, mirroring the structure of the existing `ppc64` backend while using 32-bit encodings and register conventions.    - Support the full Go language feature set required for the architecture: all integer and floating-point types supported by the target, slices, maps, channels, goroutines, closures, deferred calls, panic/recover, interface conversion, and `unsafe` operations.    - Emit correct position-independent and non-PIC code as required by the target, including correct handling of external (dynamic-linking) symbol references.  3. **ABI and runtime compatibility**    - Define and implement the calling convention (argument/result passing, stack alignment, frame size, return values) for `ppc32`, including the register-based calling-convention variant used by the Go runtime (`ABIInternal` / `ABI0` as applicable).    - Provide the runtime support needed by the backend: goroutine stack switching, `g`/`m` register access, `morestack` handling, write barriers, and any architecture-specific assembly support files.    - The resulting binaries shall interoperate with the Go runtime and standard library for the target.  4. **Build and tooling integration**    - Add the architecture to the toolchain's target lists so that `go tool dist list`, `go env`, cross-compilation, and `cmd/dist` bootstrap for `ppc32` function correctly.    - Ensure `cmd/compile` builds cleanly for the host and that `cmd/internal/obj` accepts `ppc32` as a valid `-S`/architecture argument.  5. **Testing**    - The compiler's architecture-independent test suites shall pass for `ppc32` (e.g. `go test` of the toolchain's own tests under `GOARCH=ppc32`, where runnable).    - Add architecture-specific tests covering calling conventions, floating-point behaviour, integer overflow/division semantics, struct passing, and goroutine/closure behaviour.  ### Non-Goals - Support for 64-bit-only instructions or features that cannot be expressed in 32-bit PowerPC. - Changes to the language specification or to the semantics of existing architectures. - Optimization beyond what is already implemented for comparable 32-bit backends, except where required for correctness.  ### Acceptance Criteria - `GOARCH=ppc32 go build` succeeds for the standard library and representative sample programs. - The compiler's test suite passes for `ppc32`, and the backend produces code that is accepted by the assembler/linker for the target. - `ppc32` appears in the toolchain's supported architecture lists and can be selected via `-S` in `cmd/compile`.

The function shall: - Return the input unchanged in meaning if it is already absolute. - Prepend the current working directory to relative paths. - Not require the path to exist on the file system. - Not resolve symbolic links. - Not normalize or collapse path components such as `.` and `..` unless explicitly specified (i.e., behavior is distinct from canonicalization).  This function is distinct from canonicalization, which resolves symbolic links and returns the real physical path and typically requires the path to exist.

The obfuscation option shall be disabled by default, shall be available per export preset, and shall not affect debug builds or projects run from the editor. issue_title: [RFC] DeepSpeed + PT Distributed Integration
requirement: **Requirement: Integrate DeepSpeed with PyTorch Distributed**  The system shall integrate DeepSpeed with the PyTorch distributed package (`torch.distributed`) so that DeepSpeed uses PyTorch's process groups, communication backends (NCCL, Gloo), and rank/world-size discovery without requiring a separate initialization path or duplicated process-group management.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  1. DeepSpeed shall initialize from an existing `torch.distributed` process group when one is already initialized, and shall initialize its own process group using `torch.distributed.init_process_group` when none exists. 2. DeepSpeed shall derive local rank, global rank, and world size from `torch.distributed` and from standard launcher environment variables (`RANK`, `LOCAL_RANK`, `WORLD_SIZE`), consistent with `torchrun`. 3. All DeepSpeed collective operations (all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, broadcast) used by ZeRO stages 1–3 and pipeline/tensor parallel components shall execute through `torch.distributed` APIs and the process groups passed to them. 4. Users may supply custom process groups to DeepSpeed components (e.g., data-parallel, model-parallel, and expert-parallel groups), and DeepSpeed shall respect those groups without creating conflicting groups. 5. Training with DeepSpeed under `torchrun` shall produce results (loss curves and final parameters within numerical tolerance) equivalent to a reference run using native `torch.distributed` data parallelism for the same seed, batch size, and model. 6. Backend selection (NCCL, Gloo, and others supported by PyTorch) shall follow the backend configured in `torch.distributed` unless explicitly overridden in the DeepSpeed configuration. 7. Existing DeepSpeed user code that calls `deepspeed.init_distributed()` shall continue to function without modification, with a deprecation path documented for future versions. 8. Failures in process-group initialization or rank mismatch shall raise a descriptive error that identifies the mismatched configuration (world size, rank, or backend). 9. Unit and integration tests shall cover single-node multi-GPU and multi-node launches via `torchrun`, with CI coverage for NCCL and Gloo backends. 10. Documentation shall describe the initialization order, process-group ownership, and migration steps for users currently relying on DeepSpeed-managed process groups.

issue_title: [RFC] PT2-Friendly Traceable, Functional Collective Communication APIs
requirement: **REQ-DIST-FUNC-001: PT2-Compatible Functional Collective Communication API**  The distributed communication subsystem shall provide a functional, traceable API layer for collective operations (all_reduce, all_gather, broadcast, reduce_scatter, all_to_all, barrier) that enables seamless integration with PyTorch 2.0 (PT2) compilation pipelines (`torch.compile`/Dynamo) without graph breaks, while supporting asynchronous execution and backend agnosticism.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **Traceability**: Collective operations shall be implemented as pure, traceable Python functions that do not access hidden global state, perform blocking Python I/O, or mutate communicator objects, ensuring compatibility with Dynamo graph capture and FX symbolic tracing without requiring `@torch._dynamo.disable` or `allow_in_graph` decorators.  2. **Functional Semantics**: The API shall adhere to functional programming principles: process groups/communicators must be passed as explicit arguments; operations must return new tensor handles or work futures rather than mutating input tensors in-place; and no mutable global registries shall track pending operations.  3. **Asynchronous Execution**: Each collective shall provide an asynchronous variant returning a work handle supporting explicit `wait()`/`synchronize()` methods, enabling the PT2 compiler to schedule communication concurrently with computation kernels within a single captured graph.  4. **Compilation Safety**: The functional APIs must execute correctly under `@torch.compile` (including `mode="reduce-overhead"` and CUDA Graphs capture) with results numerically identical to eager mode, requiring zero fallback to eager execution for the collective operation itself.  5. **Backend Abstraction**: The interface shall abstract over communication backends (NCCL, Gloo, MPI, UCC) through unified functional signatures, with backend selection confined to process group initialization.  6. **Memory Lifetime Management**: Returned handles shall explicitly manage tensor lifetimes to prevent use-after-free in compiled CUDA graphs, avoiding reliance on Python garbage collection for CUDA memory safety.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  - Performance overhead versus existing imperative APIs shall not exceed 5%. - API signatures shall remain stable across minor versions to ensure reproducibility of compiled artifacts.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  - All collectives pass unit tests under `torch.compile` with zero graph breaks (verified via `torch._dynamo.utils.counters["graph_break"]`). - Strict tracing mode (`torch._dynamo.config.traceable=True`) confirms no global mutable state access. - Async work handles can be chained (e.g., `handle = all_reduce(t, group); handle.wait()`) within a single compiled function. - Numerical equivalence with eager mode is verified across all supported data types, device types, and process group topologies.

issue_title: [RFC] DeepSpeed + PT Distributed Integration
requirement: **Requirement ID:** REQ-DIST-DS-001 **Title:** Native DeepSpeed + PyTorch Distributed Integration  **Requirement Statement:** The framework shall provide first-class integration between DeepSpeed and PyTorch Distributed (`torch.distributed`), enabling DeepSpeed's ZeRO-based optimizations (Stages 1–3, mixed precision, offloading, activation checkpointing) to run on top of PyTorch Distributed's process-group management, launch tooling, and model preparation APIs, so that users can enable DeepSpeed through standard PyTorch distributed workflows without duplicate communicator initialization or incompatible glue code.  **Functional Sub-Requirements:**  - **FR-1 (Process-Group Reuse):** When a `torch.distributed` process group is already initialized, DeepSpeed shall adopt it (rank, world size, backend) rather than creating a separate communicator; DeepSpeed may initialize the process group when absent and expose it for subsequent PyTorch usage. - **FR-2 (Launcher Compatibility):** DeepSpeed-configured training shall be launchable via `torchrun`/`torch.distributed.run`, including elastic start and restart semantics, with behavior equivalent to the native `deepspeed` launcher. - **FR-3 (Composability):** ZeRO Stages 1–3 shall be usable with models prepared via `DistributedDataParallel` or `FullyShardedDataParallel` in a documented, supported configuration matrix; unsupported combinations shall fail fast with actionable error messages. - **FR-4 (Unified Configuration):** A single configuration surface shall govern both PyTorch Distributed parameters (backend, timeout, device assignment) and DeepSpeed parameters (ZeRO stage, offload, micro-batch size), with precedence rules explicitly documented. - **FR-5 (Checkpoint Interoperability):** Checkpoints written in integrated mode shall round-trip within the integrated stack and, for model weights, remain loadable by vanilla PyTorch and standalone DeepSpeed runtimes. - **FR-6 (Backward Compatibility):** Existing public APIs of both stacks shall remain unchanged; integration shall be strictly opt-in via configuration flag until declared stable.  **Acceptance Criteria:**  1. A reference training workload produces statistically equivalent loss/metric trajectories (tolerance agreed per test plan) under (a) the native `deepspeed` launcher and (b) `torchrun` with the integration, on at least two multi-GPU/multi-node configurations. 2. All ZeRO stages execute in integrated mode with verified gradient and optimizer-state sharding behavior. 3. Checkpoint round-trips pass for FR-5 scenarios. 4. An elastic `torchrun` restart resumes from the latest checkpoint without rank/world-size mismatch errors. 5. Throughput in integrated mode does not regress more than 5% versus standalone DeepSpeed on the reference benchmark. 6. Nightly CI validates the configuration matrix against the latest stable and prior-minor PyTorch releases.  **Constraints:** Supported communication backends shall include NCCL and Gloo; all new public APIs shall be typed and documented.  **Exclusions:** Performance tuning of CPU/NVMe offload, pipeline/tensor parallelism extensions, and Windows platform support are out of scope for this requirement.

issue_title: Add literal quoted strings with embedded variables (f-strings) to GDScript
requirement: GDScript should support literal quoted strings with embedded expressions (f-strings), allowing developers to interpolate variables and expressions directly into string literals. An f-string should be prefixed appropriately (e.g., `f"..."`) and any expression placed inside braces `{}` within the string literal should be evaluated at runtime, with the resulting value converted to its string representation and inserted into the final string. This eliminates the need for verbose concatenation or format calls (e.g., `"Value: " + str(var)` or `"Value: %s" % var`) and should support nested braces, escaping of literal braces via `{{` and `}}`, and type conversion consistent with existing `str()` behavior.

issue_title: Implement similar PyTorch function as model.summary() in keras?
requirement: **Requirement: Add a PyTorch-style model summary utility to Keras**  The Keras library shall provide a public function (e.g., `keras.utils.model_summary` or an equivalent API) that generates a layer-by-layer summary of a given model, comparable to the summaries produced by PyTorch utilities such as `torchsummary.summary` and `torchinfo.summary`, and shall meet the following criteria:  1. **Input:** The function accepts a Keras model and an optional input size or example input. When the model is not built, the function shall use the provided input specification to build it, or raise a descriptive error if no input shape is available. 2. **Per-layer output:** The summary shall list each layer's name, layer type, output shape, and number of parameters, in the order the layers execute. 3. **Parameter counts:** The summary shall report trainable parameters, non-trainable parameters, and total parameters, both per layer and aggregated for the model. 4. **Size estimate:** The summary shall include an estimated memory footprint for parameters and forward-pass activations, based on the dtype of each tensor. 5. **Nested models:** Nested models and sub-models shall be expanded or summarized hierarchically, with an option to control the depth of expansion. 6. **Subclassed models:** The function shall work with subclassed models, Functional models, and Sequential models, and shall handle layers whose output shapes are dynamic by reporting them as unknown or `None`. 7. **Output format:** The function shall print a formatted table by default and return a structured object (e.g., a dict or dataclass) containing the same data, so the results can be consumed programmatically. 8. **Backend compatibility:** The function shall run on all Keras-supported backends (TensorFlow, JAX, and PyTorch) without requiring any backend-specific dependency. 9. **Existing behavior:** The function shall not alter the model's state, weights, or training configuration, and it shall not change the behavior of the existing `model.summary()` method. 10. **Documentation:** The function shall include a docstring, an entry in the API reference, and unit tests covering Sequential, Functional, subclassed, and nested models.

issue_title: cmd/go: add 'go get' options to update direct and indirect dependencies separately

issue_title: x/crypto: add BLAKE3 support
requirement: The golang.org/x/crypto module shall provide a new package implementing the BLAKE3 cryptographic hash function in accordance with the official BLAKE3 specification. The package shall expose an incremental (streaming) hashing API consistent with the standard library's hash.Hash interface, and shall support: (1) the default 32-byte digest as well as arbitrary-length extendable output (XOF); (2) keyed hashing mode; and (3) the key derivation (derive_key) mode. The implementation shall be pure Go with a portable fallback, may include architecture-specific optimized code paths (e.g., AVX2, SSE4.1, ARM NEON) that produce bit-identical results, and shall pass the official BLAKE3 test vectors. Separate hasher instances shall be safe for concurrent use, and the package shall include documentation and usage examples consistent with other packages in the module.

issue_title: Feature Requst: Add regex support to test filters

issue_title: [FR][RFC] Build a serving framework to host and serve trained PyTorch models
requirement: # Requirement: Serving Framework for Trained PyTorch Models  ## 1. Summary  Build a standalone, production-oriented **model serving framework** that hosts trained PyTorch models behind a network API so that downstream applications can send inference requests and receive predictions without embedding the model or PyTorch runtime in their own process.  The framework must be able to serve one or many models simultaneously, expose them over HTTP (and optionally gRPC), handle batching and concurrency efficiently, and provide the operational tooling (configuration, health checks, metrics, logging) expected of a deployable service.  ## 2. Goals  - Allow a trained `torch.nn.Module` (and TorchScript / exported artifacts) to be registered and served with minimal code changes. - Provide a stable, well-documented request/response contract for inference. - Maximize inference throughput via dynamic batching and efficient GPU/CPU utilization while controlling latency. - Be containerizable and horizontally scalable, with stateless or explicitly stateful request handling. - Be extensible: users can add custom pre-/post-processing, model backends, and transport protocols.  ## 3. Functional Requirements  ### 3.1 Model Management - **FR-1 Model loading:** Load a model from a local path, a URL, or a model registry/artifact store at start-up or on demand (hot-loading without restarting the service). - **FR-2 Model registry:** Maintain a registry of served models keyed by a unique model name/version (e.g., `resnet50:v3`), supporting multiple concurrent versions of the same model and staged/canary rollout of a new version. - **FR-3 Lifecycle:** Support explicit load, unload, reload, and graceful draining of models; unload must wait for in-flight requests to complete or reject new ones according to policy. - **FR-4 Backend abstraction:** Define a pluggable backend interface with at least a PyTorch eager-mode backend and a TorchScript backend; additional backends (ONNX Runtime, TensorRT) may be added behind the same interface. - **FR-5 Configuration:** Serve models and their settings (device, batch size limits, timeouts, metadata, dependencies) from a declarative configuration file (YAML/JSON) and/or command-line flags, with environment-variable overrides. - **FR-6 Metadata:** Each model exposes metadata describing name, version, signature/input and output schema, framework version, and any required auxiliary files (tokenizers, label maps, vocabulary).  ### 3.2 Inference API - **FR-7 Prediction endpoint:** Provide an HTTP endpoint that accepts inference requests and returns predictions. The request format must support:   - Binary tensor payloads (e.g., `application/octet-stream`) with metadata describing tensor name, shape, and dtype.   - JSON payloads for simple/scalar inputs and for structured (non-tensor) request bodies.   - Multiple named inputs per request where the model signature declares them. - **FR-8 Output format:** Return results in a binary tensor payload and/or JSON, according to the model's declared output schema; responses must be correlatable to requests via a request ID. - **FR-9 Protocol support:** HTTP/JSON and HTTP/binary are mandatory; gRPC with protobuf service definitions generated from the model signature is optional but must be architecturally supported. - **FR-10 Health and readiness:** Expose liveness and readiness endpoints; readiness must be `false` while a model is loading or draining and `true` only when at least one model is able to serve. - **FR-11 Error handling:** Return structured errors with meaningful HTTP status codes (bad request, model not found, model unavailable, inference timeout, internal error) and human-readable messages; internal errors must not leak stack traces to clients but must be logged. - **FR-12 Synchronous and asynchronous modes:** Support blocking single-request inference and asynchronous submission with client-supplied or server-assigned request IDs and result retrieval/polling.  ### 3.3 Pre-/Post-Processing - **FR-13 Pre-processing hooks:** Allow registering a preprocessing function per model (e.g., image decode and resize, tokenization, normalization) that converts the raw request body into model inputs. - **FR-14 Post-processing hooks:** Allow registering a postprocessing function per model (e.g., softmax, top-k, label decoding) that converts model outputs into the response payload. - **FR-15 Default handlers:** Provide sensible default implementations (identity tensor conversion, JSON encoding) so that models can be served with no custom code.  ### 3.4 Batching, Concurrency, and Performance - **FR-16 Dynamic batching:** Group concurrently arriving requests into a single batched forward pass within a configurable maximum batch size and maximum wait/queue delay. - **FR-17 Queueing and backpressure:** Bound the internal request queue; apply configurable overflow behaviour (reject with 429/503, block, or drop-oldest) and return queue-wait metrics. - **FR-18 Concurrency:** Support concurrent request handling with configurable worker/thread or async concurrency, and model-level locking so that a single model instance is not executed concurrently unless explicitly allowed. - **FR-19 Device placement:** Support CPU and CUDA execution, with configurable device selection, optional automatic fallback to CPU, and support for multi-GPU (data-parallel) serving. - **FR-20 Precision:** Support configurable inference precision (FP32, FP16, BF16) including automatic mixed precision. - **FR-21 Model warm-up:** Run configurable warm-up inference passes at load time so that the first real request is not penalised by lazy initialization, CUDA graph capture, or memory allocation. - **FR-22 Timeouts and cancellation:** Enforce configurable request timeouts and propagate client disconnects/cancellation to abort queued or in-flight work where possible.  ### 3.5 Observability - **FR-23 Metrics:** Expose Prometheus-compatible metrics (or equivalent) including request count, error count, latency histogram (queue time, inference time, end-to-end), batch size distribution, and per-model GPU/CPU utilization and memory. - **FR-24 Logging:** Structured, configurable logging with per-request correlation IDs and configurable levels; no prediction payloads logged by default. - **FR-25 Tracing (optional but supported):** Allow propagation of OpenTelemetry trace context so inference spans appear in distributed traces.  ### 3.6 Deployment and Operations - **FR-26 Containerization:** Provide a Docker image and documentation/build files for running the service in a container. - **FR-27 Horizontal scaling:** Support running multiple service instances behind a load balancer; instances must be stateless with respect to request data, and model versions must be consistent across instances (configurable via shared config or coordinated rollout). - **FR-28 Configuration-driven startup:** The service must start, validate its configuration, and become ready without requiring code changes for common deployment scenarios. - **FR-29 Graceful shutdown:** On `SIGTERM`, stop accepting new requests, drain in-flight requests within a grace period, release model resources, and exit cleanly.  ## 4. Non-Functional Requirements  - **NFR-1 Performance:** Sustain a documented target throughput/latency on a stated reference workload (e.g., ≥ X requests/second at p99 ≤ Y ms for a given model and hardware) and demonstrate that dynamic batching improves throughput over unbatched serving. - **NFR-2 Efficiency:** Avoid unnecessary per-request allocations and copies; reuse pre-allocated buffers where practical. - **NFR-3 Portability:** Support Linux and macOS on CPU; CUDA support on Linux. Python 3.9+ with PyTorch 2.x. - **NFR-4 Reliability:** A model load failure must not crash the whole service; the service must remain healthy and report the model as unavailable. - **NFR-5 Security:** Bind to configurable host/port; support optional API-key or token authentication and TLS termination; no unauthenticated administrative endpoints by default. - **NFR-6 Testability:** Provide unit tests for handlers, batching, registry, and configuration, plus integration tests that start the server, issue requests, and assert on responses. - **NFR-7 Documentation:** Provide user documentation covering quick start, configuration reference, API specification, custom pre-/post-processing, and troubleshooting, plus at least one end-to-end example.  ## 5. Out of Scope (initial release)  - Training, fine-tuning, or hyperparameter management. - A hosted control plane/UI for model management (a registry abstraction and CLI/API are sufficient). - Online/batch feature-store integration and complex request routing/ensembling beyond model versioning.  ## 6. Acceptance Criteria  1. A user can start the service with a configuration file that references a locally saved PyTorch model, and the service reports ready within a bounded startup time. 2. `POST`ing a valid input to the model's prediction endpoint returns a prediction matching the model's output within a documented tolerance. 3. A request to an unknown model name returns a structured `404`; a malformed request returns a structured `400`. 4. With dynamic batching enabled, concurrent requests are observed to be executed in batches larger than one, and metrics report the achieved batch sizes. 5. Loading a second model version and switching traffic to it can be performed without restarting the process, and the previous version can be unloaded afterwards. 6. Metrics and health endpoints are scrapeable and reflect request counts, errors, and latencies. 7. The service handles `SIGTERM` by draining in-flight requests and exiting with status 0. 8. The automated test suite (unit + integration) passes in CI.

issue_title: Flutter support for Apple Watch
requirement: **Requirement ID:** REQ-PLAT-001 **Title:** Native watchOS (Apple Watch) Platform Support for Flutter  **Requirement Statement:** The Flutter framework SHALL provide first-class, native support for the watchOS platform, enabling developers to create, build, run, debug, and distribute Flutter applications on Apple Watch devices and watchOS simulators.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. The Flutter toolchain SHALL support watchOS as a target platform for `flutter create`, `flutter run`, `flutter build`, and `flutter attach`. 2. The Flutter engine SHALL compile and execute on ARM64 watchOS hardware and simulators, rendering Flutter UI natively on Apple Watch displays. 3. Flutter projects SHALL support a watchOS companion app embedded within an existing iOS host application, packaged in accordance with Apple's watch app distribution requirements. 4. The framework SHALL expose platform channels enabling interoperability with native watchOS APIs (e.g., HealthKit, complications, notifications, workouts). 5. Flutter SHALL provide widgets and layout primitives adapted to small wearable displays and watchOS input paradigms (Digital Crown, tap interaction, always-on display states). 6. Core development workflows — hot reload, hot restart, debugging, and profiling — SHALL function against watchOS simulators and physical Apple Watch devices. 7. The build system SHALL produce App Store–ready watchOS artifacts consistent with Apple's submission requirements.  **Non-Functional Requirements:** 1. App launch time SHALL comply with Apple's watchOS application response deadline guidance. 2. Memory footprint and battery consumption SHALL remain within limits appropriate for wearable hardware. 3. Supported platform versions SHALL follow the minimum watchOS version defined in Flutter's platform support policy (e.g., watchOS 9.0+).  **Acceptance Criteria:** 1. `flutter create --platforms=watchos` generates a valid, runnable watchOS project template. 2. A minimal Flutter application builds, deploys, and runs correctly on both a watchOS simulator and a physical Apple Watch. 3. Hot reload reflects UI changes on a connected watchOS target. 4. A watchOS companion app can be built and released alongside an iOS Flutter application using standard Flutter tooling. 5. A documented sample demonstrates platform channel communication with a native watchOS API.

issue_title: proposal: database/sql: support a way to perform bulk actions
requirement: The database/sql package shall provide a standard, driver-agnostic API for performing bulk database operations—such as inserting, updating, deleting, or copying many rows in a single call or round trip—so that applications no longer need to hand-construct vendor-specific multi-row SQL statements or execute statements one row at a time. The API shall integrate naturally with existing database/sql types (DB, Tx, Conn, prepared statements), shall permit drivers to implement bulk operations using native backend mechanisms where available, and shall specify well-defined behavior when a driver or database does not support bulk execution (e.g., an explicit error or a documented fallback). Results of bulk operations, including rows affected and any per-row or batch-level errors, shall be reported consistently with existing database/sql semantics.

issue_title: Support Windows kernel mode for driver development
requirement: Requirement: The system shall support Windows kernel mode for driver development.

issue_title: Scan is overly specialized
requirement: **Requirement:** The scan capability shall be generalized so that it supports multiple scan targets, detection types, and configurable options, rather than being limited to a single hardcoded use case. Users shall be able to select or configure scan scope, rules, and output through documented parameters or configuration, with the default behavior preserved for existing users.

issue_title: Implement a Rendering Compositor
requirement: The system shall provide a rendering compositor that combines one or more rendered surfaces into a single frame, honoring each surface’s visibility, stacking order, position, and opacity, and presents the composed frame at the configured output dimensions.

issue_title: OpenCL 3.0 support: support every GPU on earth through rusticl
requirement: Requirement: OpenCL 3.0 Support in Rusticl  The Rusticl OpenCL implementation shall provide conformant OpenCL 3.0 functionality so that it can be used on any GPU supported by the underlying Gallium3D drivers.  Specifically:  1. Rusticl shall advertise and implement the OpenCL 3.0 platform and device version, including the mandatory and optional features defined by the OpenCL 3.0 specification. 2. Rusticl shall expose OpenCL 3.0 functionality on all GPU hardware for which a supported Gallium3D driver is available, without requiring vendor-specific code paths in the OpenCL layer. 3. Feature support that depends on hardware capabilities shall be reported accurately through the standard OpenCL device query interface, so applications can detect unsupported features at runtime. 4. Rusticl shall pass the applicable OpenCL conformance test suite for OpenCL 3.0 on supported hardware, or document any gaps in conformance. 5. Driver-level requirements (such as required memory, atomic, and image capabilities) shall be checked during device initialization, and devices that cannot meet the minimum OpenCL 3.0 requirements shall be excluded or reported with an appropriate reduced version.

issue_title: Improve the performance of the GDScript VM
requirement: Optimize the GDScript virtual machine (VM) to reduce script execution time and runtime overhead while preserving identical runtime behavior and full backward compatibility with existing GDScript code. Optimization efforts shall focus on the interpreter's core execution path (e.g., bytecode dispatch, opcode handling, and memory access patterns), and improvements must be validated through benchmarks demonstrating measurable performance gains on representative workloads without introducing regressions in correctness, stability, or debuggability.

issue_title: Implement a Set primitive to complement Dictionary and Array
requirement: The system shall implement a native `Set` collection primitive to complement the existing `Array` and `Dictionary` types, providing an iterable collection of unique elements with constant-time average complexity for insertion, deletion, and membership lookup, along with standard set operations including union, intersection, difference, and subset evaluation.

issue_title: x/net/http2: support consuming PUSH_PROMISE streams in the client
requirement: **Requirement: HTTP/2 Client Support for Consuming Server Push (PUSH_PROMISE) Streams**  The `golang.org/x/net/http2` client implementation shall accept, process, and expose server-initiated pushed streams that the server announces via PUSH_PROMISE frames, so that applications can retrieve pushed responses without issuing a separate request.  Specifically, the client shall:  1. **Accept PUSH_PROMISE frames** on client connections in which server push is enabled (SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH = 1), validating the promised stream ID, the associated stream ID, and the pseudo-header fields of the promised request (`:method`, `:scheme`, `:authority`, `:path`) per RFC 7540 §8.2.  2. **Reject invalid pushes** by sending RST_STREAM (with an appropriate error code such as PROTOCOL_ERROR or REFUSED_STREAM) for any PUSH_PROMISE that is malformed, references an unknown or closed associated stream, uses a non-cacheable or unsafe request method, or is otherwise non-conformant. The client shall also treat a PUSH_PROMISE as a connection error when it is received while SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH is 0 or when the promised stream ID is not valid.  3. **Expose pushed responses to the application** through a public API that allows the caller to:    - Determine whether a pushed resource is available for a given associated request.    - Receive the promised request and the pushed response headers and body as a readable stream, independently of the associated response.    - Cancel or refuse an individual pushed stream (via RST_STREAM with CANCEL or REFUSED_STREAM).  4. **Support a configurable push-handling policy**, allowing the application to enable or disable push per client or per request, and optionally to supply a handler that decides whether each incoming push is accepted, refused, or cached.  5. **Manage resources** so that pushed streams count toward the connection's concurrent-stream accounting (SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS), buffered push data is bounded by a configurable limit, and unconsumed pushes are discarded and their streams reset when the connection closes or when the push is refused by the policy.  6. **Maintain compatibility** with existing client behavior: when push is disabled or no handler is registered, the client shall continue to advertise SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH = 0 (or equivalent default) and existing request/response semantics shall be unchanged.  7. **Be covered by tests** including: valid push delivery, malformed PUSH_PROMISE rejection, push refusal by policy, concurrency limit enforcement, buffer-limit enforcement, connection close with outstanding pushes, and interoperability with a server that emits pushes.

issue_title: [web] Support compute on separate thread in Flutter Web
requirement: On Flutter Web, `compute()` shall execute its callback on a background worker thread, keeping the UI thread responsive while preserving the existing API and returning the callback’s result or error to the caller.

issue_title: Allow release mode builds to run on simulators
requirement: The system shall allow release mode builds to run on simulators.

issue_title: cmd/compile: thread support for webassembly
requirement: The Go compiler and runtime for the WebAssembly target (GOOS=js, GOARCH=wasm) shall support multithreading in accordance with the WebAssembly threads and shared memory proposals. This requires: (1) compiler support for emitting WebAssembly atomic and synchronization instructions (e.g., atomics, wait/notify) used by the runtime and sync package; (2) support for shared linear memory so multiple WebAssembly instances can operate in the same address space; and (3) runtime scheduler integration that allows goroutines to be scheduled and run in parallel on multiple native WebAssembly threads in hosts that support threading (e.g., browsers, Node.js). Until the underlying WebAssembly proposal is standardized and universally enabled, thread support may be exposed as an opt-in build or environment configuration.

issue_title: plugin: add Windows support
requirement: The system shall support plugins on the Windows operating system.

issue_title: Feature request: INT4 format support
requirement: The system shall support INT4 (4-bit integer) quantized format for model weights, enabling loading, inference, serialization, and conversion of models using 4-bit integer precision to reduce memory footprint and computational overhead while maintaining acceptable accuracy.

issue_title: Feature request: Use 'trampolines' to make most of the body of a generic function non-generic
requirement: For eligible generic functions, the compiler shall generate type-specific trampolines that delegate to a shared, non-generic implementation for the type-independent portion of the function body, preserving behavior while reducing duplicated generated code.

issue_title: plugin: Add support for closing plugins
requirement: The plugin system shall allow plugins to be closed at runtime by invoking their close hook, removing them from the active plugin registry, releasing any resources they hold, and preventing any further plugin callbacks or event handling.

issue_title: Feature Requst: Add regex support to test filters
requirement: **Requirement: Regular Expression Support for Test Filtering**  The test runner shall support regular expressions as a pattern-matching syntax for filtering test execution, allowing selection of tests based on complex naming patterns beyond simple exact matches or wildcards.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. **Syntax:** When a filter value is delimited by forward slashes (e.g., `/^module\..*_test$/`) or when using a dedicated `--filter-regex` option, the system shall compile and apply the enclosed string as a regular expression against the fully qualified test identifier (package/module + class + method name). 2. **Flags:** The system shall support standard regex flags (e.g., `i` for case-insensitive) appended after the closing delimiter (e.g., `/pattern/i`). 3. **Validation:** Upon startup, the system shall validate all provided regex patterns. If a pattern is syntactically invalid, the runner shall terminate with a non-zero exit code and output a specific error message identifying the pattern and syntax error (e.g., "Invalid regex '/[unclosed': missing closing bracket"). 4. **Compatibility:** Existing filter syntax (literal strings, glob patterns) shall remain fully functional and shall not be interpreted as regex unless explicitly delimited or when using the regex-specific flag. 5. **Performance:** Each regex pattern shall be compiled exactly once during initialization and cached; the compiled pattern shall be reused when evaluating every test case to avoid recompilation overhead.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - Executing the test suite with `--filter-regex "^test_integration_.*"` runs only those tests whose identifiers begin with `test_integration_`. - Providing the invalid pattern `/test(.*/` causes immediate failure with a clear error message before any test execution begins. - A filter combining standard syntax (`--filter "test_exact"`) and regex syntax (`--filter-regex "/_slow$/"`) executes the union of matching tests. - Regex matching respects the standard semantics of the runtime's regex engine (supporting character classes, quantifiers, anchors, and alternation).

issue_title: Implement a Set primitive to complement Dictionary and Array
requirement: The system shall provide a Set primitive to complement Dictionary and Array.

issue_title: database/sql: missing escape functions
requirement: Requirement: Provide escape utilities in the database/sql package  The database/sql package shall provide standard functions that escape or quote values and identifiers for use in SQL statements, so that callers can safely construct dynamic SQL text where placeholder parameters cannot be used (for example, table names, column names, and other identifiers).  Specifically, the package shall:  1. Provide a function that escapes or quotes an SQL identifier (table, column, schema names) according to the target driver's identifier quoting rules, returning a string safe for direct inclusion in a query. 2. Provide a function that escapes string literal values for inclusion in SQL text, handling embedded quote characters and other driver-relevant special characters. 3. Allow the escaping behavior to be driven by the connected driver's dialect, so that identifiers and literals are escaped correctly for each supported database, with a sensible default when the driver does not supply its own rules. 4. Expose these capabilities through a driver-optional interface, so that existing drivers continue to compile and operate unchanged, and drivers may opt in to custom escaping. 5. Document the escaping guarantees and limitations clearly, stating that escaping is not a substitute for parameterized queries for data values, and that callers should prefer placeholders wherever the driver supports them. 6. Return an error when input cannot be safely escaped (for example, invalid or empty identifiers, or values containing unsupported characters), rather than silently producing unsafe output.

issue_title: non-negative least squares solver feature request
requirement: ## Requirement: Non-Negative Least Squares Solver  The project shall provide a publicly accessible non-negative least squares (NNLS) solver.  ### Functional Requirements  - Given a real matrix \(A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}\) and vector \(b \in \mathbb{R}^m\), the solver shall compute:  \[ x^* = \arg\min_{x \ge 0} \frac{1}{2}\|Ax-b\|_2^2 \]  - The public API shall accept:   - Input matrix \(A\)   - Target vector \(b\)   - Optional convergence tolerance   - Optional maximum iteration count - The solver shall return:   - The computed solution vector \(x\)   - The final residual norm \(\|Ax-b\|_2\)   - The objective value \(\frac{1}{2}\|Ax-b\|_2^2\)   - Convergence status   - Number of iterations performed - All returned solution components shall be non-negative, with negligible negative numerical artifacts clamped to zero. - The solver shall support:   - Overdetermined and underdetermined systems   - Rank-deficient matrices   - Zero vectors and matrices containing zeros   - Ill-conditioned but finite inputs - The solver shall report invalid input clearly, including mismatched dimensions, empty unsupported inputs, and NaN or infinite values. - If the maximum iteration count is reached before convergence, the solver shall return the best feasible result with a non-converged status. - The implementation shall be deterministic and shall not depend on randomized initialization.  ### Quality and Documentation Requirements  - Automated tests shall compare results against established NNLS reference solutions for representative small, random, overdetermined, underdetermined, and rank-deficient cases. - Tests shall verify non-negativity, objective-value consistency, residual consistency, and correct handling of invalid inputs. - Documentation shall describe the API, constraints, return values, tolerance behavior, convergence criteria, and an example.  ### Acceptance Criteria  - For supported valid inputs, the solver returns a feasible solution whose objective value and residual agree with the returned diagnostics. - On a feasible reference problem, the computed objective is no greater than that of the zero solution and is within the configured numerical tolerance of a trusted reference implementation. - Invalid inputs produce documented errors rather than crashes or undefined results. - The complete automated test suite passes without requiring network access.

issue_title: Flutter support for Apple Watch

issue_title: Include images in rustdoc output
requirement: **Requirement: Include Images in Rustdoc Output**  When `cargo doc` generates HTML documentation, images referenced from a crate's documentation comments (for example, Markdown image syntax `![alt](path)` in doc comments or `#[doc = ...]` attributes) must be included in the generated output and render correctly in the browser.  Specifically:  1. Relative paths to local image files referenced in doc comments must be resolved relative to the source file or crate root, as specified by the documentation author. 2. Referenced local image files must be copied into the generated documentation directory, and the emitted HTML must reference the copied files using paths that work when the documentation is opened locally or served from a web server. 3. Images referenced by absolute URLs (e.g., `https://...`) must be left unchanged and not copied. 4. If a referenced local image file does not exist or cannot be read, `rustdoc` must emit a warning identifying the missing file and the doc comment where it was referenced, without aborting documentation generation. 5. Image files shared across multiple items or crates must not be duplicated unnecessarily in the output where a single copy suffices. 6. Behavior must be consistent across supported platforms, with path separators and case sensitivity handled correctly.

issue_title: Need negative trait bound
requirement: The compiler shall provide syntax and semantics for negative trait bounds, allowing generic items (functions, structs, and trait implementations) to declare that a type parameter must not implement a specified trait (e.g., `T: !Send`). The type checker shall enforce this constraint at compile time, rejecting any monomorphization where the concrete type implements the forbidden trait with a descriptive error message. issue_title: reflect: NamedOf
requirement: **Requirement: Add `reflect.NamedOf` function to the Go `reflect` package**  The `reflect` package shall provide a new function `NamedOf(name string, pkgPath string, t Type) Type` that creates a named type at runtime with the given type name, package path, and underlying type.  1. **Signature and behavior**    - `func NamedOf(name string, pkgPath string, t Type) Type`    - The returned `Type` must be a named type whose `Name()` returns `name` and whose `PkgPath()` returns `pkgPath`.    - The underlying type of the returned type must be the type `t` (which may itself be a named or unnamed type).  2. **Input constraints**    - `name` must be a valid Go exported or unexported identifier (non-empty, no spaces, no invalid characters). If `name` is invalid, the function must panic.    - `pkgPath` must be a non-empty string representing a valid package path. If `pkgPath` is empty, the resulting type is treated as a builtin-style type name (e.g., `int`, `error`), and `name` must be a valid predeclared type name context; otherwise the function must panic.    - `t` must not be nil. If `t` is nil, the function must panic.  3. **Restrictions**    - The underlying type `t` must be a type that can be used as an underlying type: it must not be a pointer type, interface constraint, or a type whose kind is `UnsafePointer`. If `t` is invalid (e.g., a `reflect.Type` of kind `Invalid`), the function must panic.    - `NamedOf` must not be used to redefine types that already exist in the runtime package set; creating a name that collides with an existing package-local type name is permitted (the new type is distinct from the existing one), but implementations must not attempt to merge or alias them.  4. **Type identity and compatibility**    - Two types created by `NamedOf` with the same name and pkgPath must be considered distinct types (each call creates a new named type), except where the runtime implementation can guarantee canonicalization.    - The returned type must support all standard `reflect.Type` operations, including `Implements`, `AssignableTo`, `ConvertibleTo`, and use in `reflect.New`, `reflect.ValueOf`, and `reflect.StructTag` lookups.    - Values created with the returned type must be usable in `reflect.Value.Set`, type assertions, and interface conversion consistent with Go's assignability rules for named types.  5. **Implementation constraints**    - The implementation must not require runtime compiler support; it must be implemented using existing runtime type-creation facilities (e.g., internal runtime APIs such as `runtime.NewNamed`).    - The function must be safe for concurrent use from multiple goroutines.  6. **Documentation**    - The function must be documented in the `reflect` package documentation, including its panics, restrictions, and a note that it is intended for creating types for serialization, code generation, and testing purposes, and that it cannot be used to create types that are indistinguishable from compile-time types.

issue_title: Implement `numpy.random.choice` equivalent
requirement: The system shall implement a random sampling function equivalent to `numpy.random.choice` that generates random samples from a given 1D array-like object or integer range. The implementation must fulfill the following specifications:  1. **Function Signature and Parameters:**    - `a`: 1D array-like or integer. If an integer is provided, the sampling population shall be `range(a)`.    - `size`: (Optional) Integer or tuple of integers defining the output shape. If not specified, a single scalar value must be returned.    - `replace`: (Optional) Boolean flag indicating whether sampling is with replacement. Default is `True`.    - `p`: (Optional) 1D array-like of float probabilities corresponding to each entry in `a`. Default is `None` (uniform distribution).  2. **Functional and Algorithmic Requirements:**    - When `replace=True`, elements may be selected multiple times.    - When `replace=False`, elements must be sampled without replacement.    - When `p` is provided, elements must be selected according to the specified probability distribution.    - The function must integrate with the library's existing pseudorandom number generator (PRNG) state to ensure deterministic reproducibility when seeded.  3. **Input Validation and Error Handling:**    - Raise a `ValueError` if `replace=False` and the total number of requested samples (`size`) exceeds the population size of `a`.    - Raise a `ValueError` if `p` is provided and its length does not match the length of `a`.    - Raise a `ValueError` if any value in `p` is negative, or if the sum of probabilities in `p` does not equal 1 (within standard floating-point tolerance).    - Raise a `ValueError` if `a` is an integer less than or equal to 0, or if `a` is an array-like object with dimension greater than 1.  4. **Return Value:**    - Return an array of the specified `size` (or a scalar if `size=None`) containing sampled elements with a data type consistent with `a` (or integer dtype if `a` is an integer).

issue_title: [RFC] DataLoader architecture updates and TarDataset implementation
requirement: **Requirement: DataLoader Architecture Updates and TarDataset Implementation**  **1. Summary** Update the DataLoader architecture to support pluggable dataset types and streaming access patterns, and add a `TarDataset` that reads samples directly from tar archives without requiring extraction to disk.  **2. Background** The current DataLoader couples data access tightly to in-memory or indexed datasets, which makes it difficult to add sources that are sequential or stored in archive formats. Users who store training data in tar archives (common for large-scale and webdataset-style workflows) must extract archives to disk first, which increases storage use and setup time.  **3. Functional Requirements**  3.1 DataLoader architecture - FR-1: The DataLoader shall accept any dataset that implements a defined base interface, either map-style (indexed by integer or key) or iterable-style (sequential). - FR-2: The DataLoader shall support both map-style and iterable-style datasets through the same batching, shuffling, and collation pipeline. - FR-3: Sampling, batching, and collation shall be separable components that can be replaced without modifying the dataset implementation. - FR-4: Existing DataLoader public APIs and default behavior shall remain backward compatible. Any breaking change must be documented and gated behind a deprecation period.  3.2 TarDataset - FR-5: `TarDataset` shall accept one or more local tar file paths (including `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, and `.tar.bz2`) and expose each archive member file as a sample. - FR-6: `TarDataset` shall build a member index on initialization so that random access by index is supported for uncompressed `.tar` files. - FR-7: For compressed archives, `TarDataset` shall support sequential iteration and shall document that random access may be slow or unsupported. - FR-8: `TarDataset` shall return samples as raw bytes by default and accept a user-supplied decode function to convert bytes to tensors or other objects. - FR-9: `TarDataset` shall be usable in multi-worker DataLoader configurations. Each worker shall open its own file handle, and samples shall not be duplicated or dropped across workers. - FR-10: `TarDataset` shall support sharding across distributed ranks so that each rank reads a disjoint subset of archive members. - FR-11: Archive members that are not regular files (directories, symlinks, device files) shall be skipped by default, with an option to include them. - FR-12: Malformed or truncated archives shall raise a descriptive error that identifies the archive path and offset where reading failed.  **4. Non-Functional Requirements** - NFR-1: Reading a sample from an uncompressed tar shall not require scanning the full archive after the index is built. - NFR-2: Memory usage shall not scale with archive size; only the index and the current sample(s) shall be held in memory. - NFR-3: Behavior shall be consistent across Linux, macOS, and Windows. - NFR-4: All new components shall include unit tests with coverage for uncompressed, compressed, multi-worker, and distributed cases.  **5. Acceptance Criteria** - AC-1: A DataLoader using a map-style custom dataset and an iterable-style dataset produces identical batch structure when given equivalent content. - AC-2: `TarDataset` on a 10 GB uncompressed archive produces the same samples, in the same order, as extracting the archive and reading files from disk. - AC-3: With `num_workers=4`, the union of samples across workers equals the full set of archive members with no duplicates. - AC-4: With `world_size=2`, the two ranks read disjoint sets of members whose union equals the full set. - AC-5: A truncated archive raises an error naming the file and the failing offset. - AC-6: All existing DataLoader tests pass without modification.  **6. Out of Scope** - Remote object storage access (S3, GCS, HTTP) for the initial release. - Writing or modifying tar archives. - Automatic decoding of image, audio, or video formats beyond the user-provided decode hook.  **7. Open Questions** - Final base interface names and signatures for map-style and iterable-style datasets. - Whether the member index is cached to disk and, if so, its invalidation rules. - Priority of compressed-archive random access versus the initial sequential-only support.

issue_title: DataLoader with option to re-use worker processes

issue_title: Struct initializer `..x` syntax should work for other structs with structurally equal subset of fields
requirement: **Requirement: Functional Base Struct Expressions Across Compatible Struct Types**  The language shall extend the functional update syntax (`..base`) in struct initializer expressions such that the base expression may be an instance of a different struct type than the struct being constructed, provided that the field types of the base struct are compatible with the corresponding fields of the target struct that are not explicitly specified.  Specifically:  1. When constructing an instance of struct `S` using the initializer syntax `S { field1: value1, ..base }`, the expression `base` may evaluate to any struct type `T` (including `S` itself), provided that every field of `S` not explicitly listed in the initializer exists on `T` with a type compatible (via the applicable implicit conversion/subtyping rules of the language) with the corresponding field type of `S`.  2. Fields of `S` that are explicitly specified in the initializer shall not be required to exist on `T`.  3. Type checking shall be performed statically at compile time; the expression shall be rejected with a diagnostic error if `T` lacks any required field or if any required field's type is incompatible with the corresponding field type of `S`.  4. If no fields of `S` are explicitly specified, the syntax `S { ..base }` shall be valid only when `T` provides all fields of `S` with compatible types, in which case the expression shall be equivalent to a conversion of `base` into `S`.  5. Existing behavior for base expressions of the same struct type shall remain unchanged and continue to compile without modification.

issue_title: runtime: implement WASM-GC
requirement: Implement support for the WebAssembly Garbage Collection (WasmGC) proposal in the runtime, enabling WebAssembly modules to define and manipulate garbage-collected heap objects. The implementation shall include: support for GC type definitions (struct and array types) and reference heap types (anyref, eqref, i31ref, structref, arrayref, and their nullable/non-nullable variants) with proper subtyping and recursive type group validation; parsing and execution of all WasmGC instructions including struct.new, struct.new_default, struct.get, struct.set, array.new, array.new_default, array.new_fixed, array.get, array.set, array.len, array.fill, array.copy, ref.test, ref.cast, ref.as_non_null, ref.is_null, ref.null, ref.func, br_on_null, and br_on_non_null; binary encoding/decoding of GC-related type sections and opcodes; and integration with the host runtime's garbage collector to manage allocation, tracking, and reclamation of Wasm heap objects. The implementation shall conform to the standardized WebAssembly GC specification and pass the corresponding WebAssembly spec test suite for GC features.

issue_title: [RFC] RPC Based Distributed Model Parallel
requirement: **Requirement: RPC-Based Distributed Model Parallelism**  **Summary** The framework shall support model parallelism across multiple processes and hosts by using a remote procedure call (RPC) mechanism to execute model components on remote workers and exchange tensors and gradients between them.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **Remote module placement:** Users shall be able to assign a model submodule or layer to a specific remote worker identified by a name or rank. 2. **Remote execution:** The forward pass of a placed submodule shall execute on its assigned worker, with input tensors transferred via RPC and output tensors returned to the caller. 3. **Distributed autograd:** Gradients shall propagate backward across RPC boundaries so that a single backward call computes gradients for parameters on all participating workers. 4. **Distributed optimizer:** The framework shall provide an optimizer that updates parameters residing on multiple remote workers, invoked from a single coordinating process. 5. **Parameter references:** Remote parameters shall be accessible through reference handles (RRefs) that can be read, updated, or passed to other remote calls without copying the full tensor to the caller. 6. **Pipeline composition:** The API shall allow chaining remote submodules into a sequential or pipelined model, with activations transferred between consecutive workers. 7. **Device support:** Remote workers shall support CPU and CUDA devices, including transfer of tensors between devices on different hosts. 8. **Initialization:** Workers shall initialize RPC through a documented entry point that takes worker name, rank, world size, and an init method (e.g., TCP or environment variable rendezvous), and shall shut down cleanly.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  1. **Performance:** RPC overhead per remote call shall be measurable and documented; tensor transfers shall avoid unnecessary serialization copies where the transport permits. 2. **Fault handling:** Failure of a remote worker shall raise a catchable exception in the coordinating process within a configurable timeout, rather than hanging indefinitely. 3. **Compatibility:** The API shall integrate with existing `nn.Module` definitions with minimal changes and shall not break single-process execution. 4. **Thread safety:** Concurrent RPC calls from multiple threads on the same worker shall be supported. 5. **Observability:** Timing and error information for RPC calls shall be available through logging or profiling hooks.  **Acceptance Criteria**  - A two-worker example splits a sequential model across processes and produces outputs and gradients numerically equal (within floating-point tolerance) to the single-process reference. - A single `backward()` call on the coordinator updates parameters on all workers, verified by the distributed optimizer step. - Killing a worker mid-training causes the coordinator to raise a timeout or RPC error within the configured interval. - Unit tests cover placement, forward/backward across boundaries, RRef access, and shutdown on CPU; CUDA tests run on multi-GPU CI. - Public API and usage guide are documented with a runnable example.

issue_title: Implement method overloading in GDScript
requirement: **Requirement: Method Overloading in GDScript**  GDScript shall allow multiple methods with the same name in the same class scope, provided each declaration has a distinct parameter signature.  1. **Signature distinction:** Two overloads are distinct if they differ in parameter count or in the declared types of at least one parameter. Overloads that differ only in return type, or whose parameter lists are identical, shall be rejected at parse time with a clear error message identifying the conflicting declarations.  2. **Call resolution:** When a method call matches multiple overloads, the engine shall select the overload whose parameter types most closely match the argument types, using the following precedence: exact match, then implicit widening conversion (such as `int` to `float`), then `Variant`. If no overload matches or the match is ambiguous, a parse-time error shall be raised when types are statically known, and a runtime error shall be raised otherwise.  3. **Untyped arguments:** Parameters without type annotations shall be treated as `Variant`. Overload resolution for untyped calls shall fall back to runtime argument-type inspection and shall produce a runtime error if no single overload is applicable.  4. **Default arguments:** An overload with default parameter values shall be callable with any argument count between its required and total parameter counts. Overload resolution shall not select an ambiguous overload set created by default arguments; such declarations shall be rejected at parse time.  5. **Inheritance:** A subclass may declare overloads of a method inherited from a parent class. An overriding declaration shall match a parent overload by exact signature. Overloads not overridden remain callable through the subclass.  6. **Signals, callables, and reflection:** `Callable` references to an overloaded name shall bind to a specific overload based on the signature supplied. `has_method()` shall return true if any overload exists with the given name.  7. **Backward compatibility:** Existing scripts that do not declare duplicate method names shall behave identically. Duplicate declarations with identical signatures shall continue to produce a compile error.  8. **Performance:** Overloads resolved statically at compile time shall incur no runtime dispatch overhead beyond a direct call to the selected function.  9. **Documentation:** The GDScript reference shall document overload rules, resolution order, and error conditions, with examples.
