issue_title: Support home and lock screen widgets
requirement: ## Requirement: Home Screen and Lock Screen Widget Support  ### 1. Overview  The application shall provide users with glanceable, at-a-glance access to their most important information directly from the device home screen and lock screen, without requiring the user to launch the app. Users shall be able to place, configure, and remove widgets in multiple sizes and positions, with data refreshed automatically in the background so that information remains current even when the app is not running.  ### 2. Functional Requirements  **FR-1 — Widget Types** - The app shall ship the following widget types:   - **Summary widget:** a single headline metric or status (e.g., primary count/value, progress toward a goal, current status).   - **List widget:** a scrollable list of the top N (default 5, configurable) user-relevant items (e.g., recent activity, upcoming items, ranked entries).   - **Interactive/action widget:** a widget supporting at least one action button or toggle that mutates state without opening the app (e.g., mark complete, toggle favorite, increment counter). - Each widget type shall be offered in the platform-standard small (approx. 2×2), medium (approx. 4×2), and large (approx. 4×4) sizes, adapting content layout accordingly.  **FR-2 — Widget Gallery and Placement** - The app shall register all widget types with the platform widget gallery so users can add, resize, and reposition widgets from the home screen. - Adding, removing, and rearranging widgets shall be performed entirely through the platform's native widget management UI; the app itself shall not implement its own home-screen editor. - Lock screen widgets (where supported by the platform) shall be available for compatible widget types, using lock-screen-appropriate presentation (glanceable, low-color, privacy-aware).  **FR-3 — Configuration and Personalization** - Users shall be able to configure a widget instance before or after adding it by selecting which data source/account/category the widget displays (e.g., which list, which metric, which time range). - Configuration shall be persisted per widget instance and per app, and shall survive app updates and device reboots. - Users shall be able to reset a widget to defaults and re-open configuration at any time via the platform's "Edit Widget" affordance.  **FR-4 — Data Refresh and Background Updates** - Widget data shall be refreshed on a periodic background schedule (target: at least every 30 minutes while the system permits) and opportunistically whenever the app's underlying data changes. - Widgets shall display the timestamp of the last successful refresh, or a stale-data indicator, when data cannot be refreshed within the platform's background execution limits. - Refreshes shall be resilient: transient network or data-source failures shall not clear or blank an existing widget; the last-known good data shall be retained and marked as stale. - If no data exists (e.g., new account with no items), the widget shall render a platform-standard empty state with a call to action to open the app.  **FR-5 — Deep Linking and Navigation** - Tapping a widget, or any interactive element within it, shall deep-link into the corresponding in-app screen for the displayed data item, with the correct context and state restored. - Tapping a widget header/footer area designated as an entry point shall open the app's default home screen. - All deep links shall be handled without a login prompt when a valid session exists, and shall route to an authentication flow when the session has expired.  **FR-6 — Interactive Actions** - Supported widget actions shall complete the underlying mutation, update the shared data store, and trigger a widget timeline reload so all instances reflect the new state. - Actions shall be confirmed (via the platform's standard interaction affordance) for destructive or irreversible operations.  **FR-7 — Privacy and Lock Screen Behavior** - Lock screen widgets shall not display sensitive content by default (e.g., amounts, titles, names). Sensitive values shall be masked unless the user explicitly opts in via a per-widget setting or the platform's "Show on lock screen" privacy toggle. - On Android, the app shall declare and support the platform's lock-screen ("keyguard") widget category where the widget type is applicable.  **FR-8 — Theming and Accessibility** - Widgets shall adapt to the system light/dark theme and to the user's accent color settings. - All widget text and interactive elements shall meet platform accessibility requirements, including Dynamic Type / font scaling support, minimum touch-target sizes for interactive elements, and VoiceOver/TalkBack labels and hints describing the displayed value and the action's result.  ### 3. Non-Functional Requirements  - Widget rendering shall not exceed the platform's widget memory and CPU budgets; widgets shall not run continuous foreground processes. - Adding a widget or completing a widget action shall produce visible UI feedback within 1 second of user interaction (excluding platform animation durations). - Widget data loads shall not block the main app launch path; widget data shall be sourced from a locally cached store when offline. - The implementation shall not degrade the app's startup time or battery consumption beyond platform-recommended limits for background widget updates. - Widget types shall be covered by automated tests verifying rendering, deep-link routing, and configuration persistence.  ### 4. Out of Scope  - The app shall not provide its own home screen or launcher. - Live Activity / real-time streaming updates (e.g., second-by-second counters) are excluded from this release. - Cross-device widget synchronization of layout arrangement (content synchronization is in scope; exact widget placement is not).  ### 5. Acceptance Criteria  1. Every supported widget type appears in the platform widget gallery and can be added to the home screen in all offered sizes. 2. A configured widget renders correct data matching the in-app equivalent and updates within the platform's standard refresh window without the app being foregrounded. 3. Tapping any widget element opens the correct in-app screen with the correct item selected. 4. An interactive widget action mutates data, is reflected in the app, and updates all widget instances of that type. 5. Widget configuration persists across app restart, app update, and device reboot. 6. Lock screen widgets mask sensitive content by default and respect the user's opt-in setting. 7. Widgets remain legible and operable at the user's maximum font scale and in both light and dark themes. 8. With no data present, the widget displays an empty state with a working call to action rather than an error or blank view. 9. With the device offline, the widget displays last-known data with a stale indicator and does not crash or clear.

issue_title: Allow Hero widgets to have transitions within the same screen
requirement: # Requirement: Same-Screen Hero Transitions  ## 1. Overview  The `Hero` widget currently animates only as part of a route transition (a `Navigator` push/pop). It is therefore impossible to use a Hero animation to morph one widget into another widget that lives in the **same** screen/route — for example, tapping a small card and having it expand into a full-screen details view that is already built in the same widget tree, or collapsing a modal back into its thumbnail without navigating.  This requirement extends the Hero mechanism so that a Hero flight can be executed **between two `Hero` widgets within the same route**, triggered by application state changes rather than by route push/pop.  ## 2. Motivation / Use Cases  - **Expand/collapse in place:** a list item is tapped and expands into a larger overlay/dialog that is already present in the same screen. - **Gallery/masonry transitions:** a thumbnail grows into an enlarged image that is part of the same page (e.g., a `PageView` or an animated overlay layer). - **Tab / segmented-control morphing:** a selected chip morphs into a floating action button or a bottom sheet. - **Filter/search morphing:** a category chip morphs into the filter panel header. - **Reordering / re-parenting visuals:** an avatar moves from one container to another container on the same screen.  ## 3. Functional Requirements  ### 3.1 Core capability - **FR-1:** The framework shall provide a supported way to run a Hero flight between two `Hero` widgets that are located in the **same route (screen)**, without pushing or popping a route. - **FR-2:** The flight shall be explicitly triggered by application code (e.g., in response to a tap, gesture, or state change), and shall not require any `Navigator` mutation. - **FR-3:** The in-screen flight shall reuse the existing Hero rendering model (overlay-based flight, `Rect` tweening, `createRectTween`, `flightShuttleBuilder`, `placeholderBuilder`) so that the visual result is consistent with route-based Hero transitions.  ### 3.2 Triggering and control - **FR-4:** The framework shall expose a controller/scope abstraction (e.g., a `HeroScope`/`HeroController` pair, or an equivalent mechanism) that allows a widget to:   - request a flight identified by the **source** and **destination** `heroTag` values;   - observe the lifecycle of the flight (started, completed, aborted);   - cancel or supersede an in-flight transition. - **FR-5:** The API shall allow the caller to specify the direction of the flight (source → destination, e.g. "expand"; or destination → source, e.g. "collapse/revert"). - **FR-6:** Multiple independent flights shall be permitted to run concurrently, each identified by its own pair of tags; a flight request must not affect unrelated Heroes on the screen. - **FR-7:** If a flight is requested while an identical flight is already running, the framework shall either no-op or replace the existing flight deterministically (documented behavior); it shall never produce a duplicate overlay or a crash.  ### 3.3 Hero participation semantics - **FR-8:** A `Hero` participating in an in-screen flight shall be identified by its `heroTag`, which must remain unique among simultaneously mounted Heroes in the tree, exactly as today. - **FR-9:** During the flight:   - the **source** Hero shall be hidden from the tree's painting and replaced by its `placeholderBuilder` (if provided) once the flight begins;   - the **destination** Hero shall be hidden until the flight lands, then shown in its final position;   - the **flight shuttle** (the animating overlay) shall be painted above the participating Heroes and below any overlay/modal that contains them. - **FR-10:** If a participating Hero has `enabled: false` via `HeroMode`, it shall not participate in the flight and the flight shall be aborted gracefully (no exception). - **FR-11:** If either the source or destination Hero cannot be found at the moment the flight is requested, the framework shall abort the flight cleanly, leaving the UI in a consistent state (no orphaned overlay, no lingering hidden Hero). - **FR-12:** If a participating Hero is removed from the tree mid-flight (e.g., due to a rebuild triggered by the same state change), the flight shall settle gracefully to the destination position (or to the placeholder) without leaking overlays, timers, or throwing exceptions.  ### 3.4 Interoperability with navigation - **FR-13:** Existing route-based Hero behavior shall be **completely unchanged**; no regression in push, pop, `popRoute`, `onPopPage`, and `Navigator` gesture-driven Hero animations. - **FR-14:** A route transition and an in-screen flight must not be able to claim the same `heroTag` concurrently; conflicts shall be resolved deterministically (in-flight flights take precedence; the route flight for that tag is skipped or aborted, per documented policy). - **FR-15:** In-screen flights shall work on all platforms, including those with limited GPU/memory, using the same overlay/rendering path as route-based transitions.  ### 3.5 Customization - **FR-16:** `createRectTween`, `flightShuttleBuilder`, and `placeholderBuilder` supplied on the participating Heroes shall be honored for in-screen flights. - **FR-17:** `Hero` widgets shall continue to support `transitionOnUserGestures` semantics for route transitions; for in-screen flights the framework shall define and document whether gesture-based interruption is supported, and if not, allow the caller to abort explicitly. - **FR-18:** The system shall respect the platform's reduced-motion / accessibility settings (`MediaQuery.disableAnimations`) by completing the flight instantly (no animation) when animations are disabled.  ## 4. Non-Functional Requirements  - **NFR-1 (Performance):** The flight shall be driven by the same animation/overlay machinery as route transitions, avoiding per-frame layout of the underlying widgets; no measurable jank regression on the reference devices for a 4-hero concurrent flight. - **NFR-2 (Compatibility):** The change shall be source-compatible and behavior-compatible for existing `Hero` usage; no required changes to existing applications. - **NFR-3 (Testability):** The feature shall be unit/widget-testable without pumping a `Navigator` route transition (i.e., a test can trigger and assert an in-screen flight in a single `pumpWidget` tree). - **NFR-4 (Documentation):** The API shall be documented in the `Hero` widget dartdoc and the framework's widget documentation, including a code sample demonstrating expand and collapse usage, and guidance on tag uniqueness and conflict rules. - **NFR-5 (Sample):** A framework sample application shall be updated or added that demonstrates a same-screen Hero transition on at least one platform.  ## 5. Acceptance Criteria  1. **AC-1:** Given a screen containing a small `Hero(tag: 'thumb')` and a large `Hero(tag: 'detail')` in the same route, when the application triggers a transition from `'thumb'` to `'detail'`, then the small Hero is replaced by its placeholder, an animated overlay flies from the thumbnail's rect to the detail's rect over the specified duration, and the large Hero becomes visible only when the flight completes. 2. **AC-2:** The same scenario with `createRectTween` (e.g., Material `RectTween`), `flightShuttleBuilder`, and `placeholderBuilder` set on the Heroes produces the corresponding custom shuttle and placeholder during the in-screen flight. 3. **AC-3:** Triggering a reverse flight (destination → source) animates the overlay back to the thumbnail's rect and leaves the thumbnail visible at rest. 4. **AC-4:** Two or more flights with distinct tag pairs can be in progress simultaneously; each overlay animates independently and each lands correctly. 5. **AC-5:** Requesting a flight with an unknown source or destination tag results in no exception, no leftover overlay, and both Heroes remain visible and unchanged. 6. **AC-6:** Removing the destination Hero from the tree one frame into the flight results in the overlay being disposed and the source Hero being restored/settled, with no "setState() called after dispose" or overflow errors in the test output. 7. **AC-7:** A `Hero` wrapped in `HeroMode(enabled: false)` is not animated by an in-screen flight and the flight aborts cleanly. 8. **AC-8:** All existing `Hero` widget tests and Navigator Hero transition tests continue to pass unmodified. 9. **AC-9:** A push/pop transition in an app that also uses in-screen flights animates correctly and is not disturbed by the presence of the in-screen Hero controller. 10. **AC-10:** With `MediaQuery.disableAnimations: true`, the flight completes immediately (single frame) rather than animating. 11. **AC-11:** The public API is documented with dartdoc, and the feature is demonstrated in at least one framework sample.  ## 6. Out of Scope  - Automatic detection of "which two Heroes should morph" without an explicit trigger (the caller must specify source and destination). - Hero flights across **different** routes that are not part of a `Navigator` transition (e.g., between separate `Overlay`s) beyond what already exists. - Changes to the visual design or default tweening of existing route-based Hero transitions. - Reverse-engineering or back-porting of third-party packages that implement similar behavior.

issue_title: Add support for variadic functions (varargs) to GDScript
requirement: The system shall support variadic functions (varargs) in GDScript, allowing functions to accept a variable number of arguments.

issue_title: Feature request: Use 'trampolines' to make most of the body of a generic function non-generic
requirement: The compiler shall generate generic function bodies as non-generic shared functions accessed through thin trampolines: for each instantiated generic function, emit only a trampoline that forwards arguments and type or value metadata to a single non-generic implementation of the function body, and use this path wherever the body does not require monomorphized specialization due to inlining, code size, or platform constraints.

issue_title: cmd/link: support msvc object files
requirement: The Go linker (`cmd/link`) shall support loading, resolving, and linking Windows Common Object File Format (PE/COFF) object files (`.obj`) generated by the Microsoft Visual C++ (MSVC) compiler, including the proper handling of MSVC-specific section headers, symbol types, linker directives (e.g., `.drectve`), and relocation types across supported Windows architectures.

issue_title: Inclusive version of take_while
requirement: The library shall provide an inclusive variant of `take_while` that yields elements from a sequence as long as a specified predicate returns true, and additionally yields the first element for which the predicate evaluates to false before terminating.

issue_title: Add ability to ignore tests at runtime.
requirement: **Requirement: Runtime Test Ignoring**  The test framework shall provide a mechanism to mark individual tests as ignored during execution, such that:  1. A test can be conditionally or unconditionally skipped at runtime from within the test body or setup code, without requiring a change to its static declaration. 2. An ignored test is not executed, and its body and assertions are not evaluated. 3. Ignored tests are reported in the test results as "ignored" (or "skipped") and are counted separately from passed, failed, and errored tests. 4. The ignore mechanism accepts an optional reason message, which is included in the test report output. 5. The ignore decision can be made dynamically based on runtime state, such as environment variables, configuration values, or resource availability. 6. The ignored status does not cause the overall test run to fail. 7. The mechanism is available through the framework's public API and is documented alongside existing test annotation or assertion features.

issue_title: Feature Request: Easier to extend base RNN implementation
requirement: The base RNN class shall expose clearly defined extension points (such as overridable methods for the recurrent cell computation or pluggable cell interfaces) that allow developers to easily subclass and customize RNN behavior for custom variants, without requiring modification of the internal sequence iteration loop or hidden state management logic.

issue_title: [webview_flutter] Add Windows support
requirement: Add Windows support to the webview_flutter plugin so that Flutter applications can embed, display, and interact with a native Windows WebView through the plugin’s existing API.

issue_title: cmd/go: allow verifying vendored code
requirement: The system shall allow users to verify the integrity of vendored code.

issue_title: non-negative least squares solver feature request
requirement: The system shall provide a Non-Negative Least Squares (NNLS) solver that computes the vector $x$ minimizing the objective function $\|Ax - b\|_2$ subject to the non-negativity constraint $x \ge 0$, given an input matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ and an observation vector $b \in \mathbb{R}^m$.  The implementation shall meet the following specifications: 1. **Input Parameters:**    - `A`: A 2D numeric array of shape `(m, n)`.    - `b`: A 1D numeric array of shape `(m,)`.    - `max_iter` (optional): An integer defining the maximum number of iterations (default: $3 \times n$).    - `tol` (optional): A positive floating-point scalar defining the convergence tolerance for the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) optimality conditions.  2. **Outputs:**    - A solution vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ where $x_i \ge 0$ for all $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$.    - The final Euclidean residual norm $\|Ax - b\|_2$.  3. **Validation & Error Handling:**    - Raise a `ValueError` if the number of rows in $A$ does not match the length of $b$, or if input dimensions are invalid.    - Raise a `ConvergenceError` (or return an explicit convergence status flag) if the active-set algorithm does not converge within `max_iter` iterations.    - Gracefully handle rank-deficient matrices $A$ without unhandled numeric exceptions.

issue_title: [Desktop] - Splash screen or background color customization
requirement: The system shall provide an option to customize the splash screen or background color on the desktop.

issue_title: PyPy support
requirement: The system shall support running under the PyPy interpreter.

issue_title: CPU version of PyTorch on PyPI
requirement: Provide a CPU-only PyTorch distribution on PyPI so that users can install and use PyTorch without requiring NVIDIA CUDA or GPU-specific dependencies.

issue_title: DataLoader with option to re-use worker processes
requirement: The system shall provide an option in the DataLoader to re-use worker processes.

issue_title: x/vuln: add support for suppressing vulnerabilities by ID
requirement: The system shall allow users to suppress vulnerabilities by ID.

issue_title: Return index of the first visible item in ListView
requirement: The system shall provide a method to return the index of the first visible item in the ListView.

issue_title: Let flutter be installable via homebrew
requirement: The Flutter SDK shall be distributed as an official Homebrew formula (or cask) available in the Homebrew core repository or a dedicated Flutter-maintained tap, enabling users to install, upgrade, and manage the Flutter SDK via standard Homebrew commands (e.g., `brew install flutter`, `brew upgrade flutter`). The package shall automatically install all required system dependencies, add the Flutter `bin` directory to the user's `PATH`, default to the stable channel, and support switching between release channels (stable, beta, dev) through Homebrew-standard command-line options or subcommands.

issue_title: Support Firefox as a browser in flutter run
requirement: Requirement: The system shall support Firefox as a target browser for the `flutter run` command.

issue_title: [RFC] Add tar-based IterableDataset implementation to PyTorch
requirement: ## Requirement: Tar‑based `IterableDataset` for PyTorch  ### 1. Motivation / Purpose  PyTorch currently offers no first‑party dataset that streams samples directly out of tar archives. Users who store data in tar shards (a common pattern for large, web‑dataset‑style corpora served over HTTP) must manually extract archives, write custom `IterableDataset` subclasses, and re‑implement member‑name parsing, sample key extraction, rank/worker sharding, and remote streaming. This results in duplicated, error‑prone code and poor default performance (e.g. serial, unbuffered reads).  PyTorch shall provide a maintained, well‑tested, tar‑based `IterableDataset` implementation that yields samples lazily from tar archives, whether the archives are local files or remote objects (e.g. HTTP/HTTPS URLs), without requiring users to write custom dataset code.  ### 2. Scope  In scope:  - A new public `IterableDataset` subclass for reading samples from tar archives. - Support for local filesystem paths and remote URLs. - Member‑name–based sample keying, optional per‑sample decoding/transform, and deterministic sharding across processes/ranks. - Unit tests, documentation, and an example script.  Out of scope:  - Automatic dataset format inference beyond tar (e.g. zip, parquet shards). - Writing/compressing archives. - Built‑in label/classification semantics; the dataset is format‑agnostic and returns raw member bytes plus a key.  ### 3. Proposed API  ```python class TarDataset(IterableDataset):     def __init__(         self,         urls: Union[str, List[str], Iterable[str]],         *,         transform: Optional[Callable[[bytes], Any]] = None,         decoder: Optional[Callable[[bytes], Any]] = None,   # alias/extension point         key_transform: Optional[Callable[[str], str]] = None,         extensions: Optional[List[str]] = None,             # member suffix filter         shuffle: bool = False,         buffer_size: int = 0,         chunk_size: int = 1024 * 1024,         timeout: float = 30.0,         download_mode: str = "stream",                        # "stream" | "download"     ): ...      def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[Tuple[str, Any]]:         """Yield (key, sample) pairs."""      def __len__(self) -> int:  # optional, only when cheaply known         ...      def set_epoch(self, epoch: int) -> None: ... ```  - `transform`: applied to the raw bytes of each member, producing the yielded sample. - `decoder`: optional semantic alias for `transform`, for symmetry with `torchvision` conventions; exactly one of the two may be provided. - `extensions`: if provided, only members whose name ends with one of the listed suffixes are yielded. - `key_transform`: applied to the derived sample key. - `download_mode="stream"`: the archive is read incrementally and members are yielded as they are encountered; `"download"`: the whole archive is fetched to a temporary local file first, then read.  ### 4. Functional Requirements  **FR‑1 Archive enumeration and reading**  - FR‑1.1 The dataset shall accept a single URL/path or an iterable of URLs/paths, and shall process them in the order given (subject to optional shuffling). - FR‑1.2 The implementation shall open each tar archive in streaming (non‑seeking) mode and shall not require the full archive to be present locally when `download_mode="stream"`. - FR‑1.3 Members shall be yielded in the order in which they appear in the archive. - FR‑1.4 Non‑file members (directories, symlinks, hardlinks, device files) shall be skipped silently. - FR‑1.5 The dataset shall yield one `(key, sample)` tuple per eligible member, where `sample` is the raw member bytes passed through `transform`/`decoder` if supplied.  **FR‑2 Key derivation**  - FR‑2.1 The default key shall be the member's path within the archive, normalized to use `/` as separator, with the archive's base filename removed and any leading directory components stripped according to a documented, configurable rule. - FR‑2.2 `key_transform` shall be applied to the default key to produce the final yielded key. - FR‑2.3 Keys shall be unique within a single archive; duplicate keys across archives are permitted.  **FR‑3 Filtering**  - FR‑3.1 When `extensions` is provided, members not matching any listed suffix shall be skipped. - FR‑3.2 Suffix matching shall be case‑insensitive and shall consider the full member path.  **FR‑4 Sharding and parallelism**  - FR‑4.1 When used with `torch.utils.data.DataLoader` with `num_workers > 0`, the dataset shall divide the set of archives among workers such that each archive is processed by exactly one worker, and each worker yields a disjoint subset of samples. - FR‑4.2 Assignment of archives to workers shall be deterministic for a fixed worker count and dataset configuration. - FR‑4.3 The dataset shall expose `set_epoch(epoch)`; when `shuffle=True`, the archive order (and therefore sample order) shall be re‑randomized per epoch using a seed derived from the epoch number, so that all workers agree on the permutation while still partitioning archives among themselves. - FR‑4.4 When used with `DistributedDataParallel`/`DataLoader` under `torch.distributed`, the dataset shall support being wrapped in `torch.utils.data.distributed.DistributedSampler` semantics or, if a dedicated distributed wrapper is provided, each rank shall receive a disjoint subset of archives.  **FR‑5 Streaming and performance**  - FR‑5.1 Reading shall be buffered: the implementation shall read at least `chunk_size` bytes per I/O operation and shall not perform one read syscall per member for archives with many small members. - FR‑5.2 The implementation shall not load the entire archive into memory at any point. - FR‑5.3 The dataset shall be re‑iterable: multiple epochs over the same instance shall re‑open and re‑read the archives rather than caching samples in memory.  **FR‑6 Error handling**  - FR‑6.1 Non‑existent local paths and unreachable/invalid remote URLs shall raise a clear error (subclass of `RuntimeError`/`ValueError`) that includes the offending URL/path. - FR‑6.2 Corrupt tar archives shall raise an informative error rather than silently yielding partial data; the error message shall identify the archive. - FR‑6.3 A failed individual member read (e.g. truncated member) shall either skip the member with a warning or raise, according to a documented policy. - FR‑6.4 Network operations shall honour `timeout` and shall surface timeouts as an informative exception.  **FR‑7 Usage with `DataLoader`**  - FR‑7.1 The dataset shall be usable with `DataLoader(batch_size=..., num_workers=..., collate_fn=default_collate)` for byte‑tensor samples, and with user‑supplied `collate_fn` for arbitrary sample types. - FR‑7.2 The dataset shall support `pin_memory`, `prefetch_factor`, and persistent workers without additional user code.  ### 5. Non‑Functional Requirements  - NFR‑1 The implementation shall live in a dedicated module within `torch.utils.data` (e.g. `torch.utils.data.tar`) and be importable from a stable, documented public path. - NFR‑2 Public API shall be documented in the PyTorch documentation alongside other `Dataset`/`IterableDataset` classes, including a usage example, parameter semantics, and error behavior. - NFR‑3 Unit tests shall cover: key derivation, extension filtering, transform application, multi‑archive iteration, worker sharding determinism, epoch shuffling determinism, error cases (missing file, corrupt archive), and compatibility with `DataLoader` at `num_workers=0` and `num_workers>0`. - NFR‑4 The implementation shall not introduce new mandatory runtime dependencies; optional remote‑URL support may rely on an optional extra. - NFR‑5 The code shall pass the project's lint/format/type‑check standards and shall include type annotations. - NFR‑6 Performance of the streaming path shall be within a reasonable factor of a plain sequential read of the same archive (target: overhead of the dataset layer shall not dominate I/O time for archives with many small members).  ### 6. Acceptance Criteria  1. A user can construct `TarDataset(["https://host/shard_000.tar", "https://host/shard_001.tar"])` and iterate it with a `DataLoader` to obtain batches of decoded samples keyed by member name, without any manual extraction or custom dataset code. 2. With `num_workers=4`, the union of samples yielded across workers equals the full sample set with no duplicates and no omissions. 3. `set_epoch()` combined with `shuffle=True` yields a different archive order per epoch while remaining consistent across workers. 4. All error cases in FR‑6 produce actionable, documented exceptions. 5. Unit tests, documentation, and an example script are merged and pass CI.

issue_title: Implement `numpy.random.choice` equivalent
requirement: Implement a public `random.choice` function that provides equivalent behavior to NumPy's `numpy.random.choice`, allowing elements to be sampled from a 1-D array-like input with optional parameters for probabilities (`p`), output shape (`size`), sampling with or without replacement (`replace`), and axis selection, while matching NumPy's input validation, return types, and random generation semantics.

issue_title: Initializing array of Option<T> using [None; n] syntax should not require std::marker::Copy for T
requirement: The system shall allow initialization of arrays of Option<T> using [None; n] syntax without requiring T to implement the Copy trait.

issue_title: PyPy support
requirement: The system shall support execution under PyPy, the alternative Python implementation with a JIT compiler, such that the library installs, imports, and passes its test suite on supported PyPy versions that correspond to the supported CPython version range, with any unavoidable behavioral differences documented.

issue_title: Implement PlatformView support on macOS
requirement: The system shall implement PlatformView support on macOS, enabling applications to embed native macOS (AppKit/NSView-based) views within the framework-rendered UI. Native views shall be created, positioned, resized, layered, and disposed in synchronization with the framework's widget lifecycle and rendering pipeline, and shall support input event handling, hit-testing, clipping, and correct z-order compositing. The macOS implementation shall expose the same cross-platform PlatformView APIs available on other supported platforms, so that existing embedder and application code requires no platform-specific changes beyond view registration.

issue_title: x/vuln: add support for suppressing vulnerabilities by ID
requirement: The x/vuln tool must allow users to suppress individual vulnerability findings by vulnerability ID. Any reported vulnerability matching a configured or specified ID must be omitted, while non-suppressed vulnerabilities continue to be reported normally.

issue_title: Need negative trait bound
requirement: **Requirement: Support Negative Trait Bounds**  The language shall allow generic type parameters and where-clauses to specify that a type does not implement a given trait, using syntax of the form `T: !Trait`.  1. A negative bound `T: !Trait` shall be satisfied only when the concrete type substituted for `T` does not implement `Trait`. 2. The compiler shall reject instantiations where the concrete type implements a trait that appears in a negative bound, and shall report an error identifying the violated bound. 3. Negative bounds shall be usable in generic function signatures, generic type definitions, impl blocks, and where-clauses. 4. Negative bounds shall be combinable with positive bounds (e.g., `T: Clone + !Copy`). 5. Overlapping implementations shall be permitted to be disambiguated through negative bounds, so that an impl constrained by `T: !Trait` does not conflict with an impl constrained by `T: Trait`. 6. Auto traits and marker traits shall be eligible for negative bounds on the same terms as ordinary traits. 7. Negative bounds shall not change the runtime behavior of generated code; they affect only type checking and trait resolution.

issue_title: x/tools/gopls: annotations for implementations of interfaces
requirement: Add code lens annotations to gopls that display the count of implementations for Go interfaces and interface methods, enabling navigation from interface declarations to their concrete implementing types.

issue_title: Add support for global plugins/universal addons

issue_title: Add proper and complete support for multi-pass shaders
requirement: **REQ-GFX-001: Multi-Pass Shader Execution Support**  **Description:** The rendering system shall provide a complete framework for defining and executing multi-pass shader pipelines, enabling a single render operation to execute two or more sequential shader passes where each pass may utilize distinct shader programs, render targets, pipeline states, and resource bindings, with controlled and synchronized data flow between passes.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. The system shall expose an API to define an ordered sequence of shader passes, wherein each pass independently specifies: (a) a shader program or stage combination, (b) input resource bindings (textures, storage buffers, uniform buffers), (c) output render targets or storage images, and (d) complete pipeline state configuration (blend mode, depth/stencil test, rasterization state, viewport/scissor). 2. The system shall automatically manage intermediate render targets and storage buffers required between passes, including their allocation, format validation, binding, and lifecycle cleanup. 3. The system shall enable data transfer between consecutive passes through: (a) sampling of previous pass outputs as texture inputs, (b) read/write access to storage buffers with appropriate memory barriers, and (c) per-pass uniform or push constant updates. 4. The system shall guarantee sequential execution order of passes and insert necessary pipeline barriers and memory synchronization to prevent data races and ensure correct visibility of writes between passes. 5. The system shall validate multi-pass configurations at compile/initialization time, detecting and reporting: (a) format incompatibilities between pass outputs and subsequent pass inputs, (b) unbound required resources, (c) resource dependency cycles, and (d) unsupported stage combinations for the target graphics backend. 6. The system shall support all applicable shader stages (vertex, tessellation control/evaluation, geometry, fragment, and compute) within multi-pass pipelines, subject to hardware and API constraints. 7. The system shall provide mechanisms for conditional pass execution, pass skipping, or early pipeline termination based on query results or application-defined predicates.  **Non-Functional Requirements:** 1. Multi-pass execution shall incur no overhead beyond the aggregate cost of individual pass executions when passes operate on independent resources. 2. Intermediate resources shall be pooled and reused across frames when dimensions and formats match to minimize allocation overhead and fragmentation. 3. The implementation shall provide consistent behavior and visual results across all supported graphics backends (e.g., Vulkan, OpenGL, DirectX 12, Metal).  **Acceptance Criteria:** 1. A developer can define a three-pass pipeline (e.g., geometry generation → lighting accumulation → post-processing) where each pass utilizes a distinct shader program, and the rendered output of pass N is automatically bound as a sampled input to pass N+1 without manual intermediate texture management. 2. Per-pass pipeline states (e.g., additive blending in pass 2, alpha-to-coverage in pass 3) apply correctly without leaking into adjacent passes. 3. Attempting to bind a resource as input to pass N+1 that was not written by pass N or any prior pass results in a descriptive validation error at pipeline creation time. 4. Memory profiling confirms zero leakage of intermediate render targets or buffers after multi-pass execution and pipeline destruction. 5. An identical multi-pass shader definition executes successfully on at least two distinct graphics backends producing visually equivalent output within acceptable tolerance.

issue_title: x/tools/gopls: annotations for implementations of interfaces
requirement: ## Requirement: Implementations annotations for interfaces in `x/tools/gopls`  ### Background `gopls` currently offers "Find Implementations" only for interface *methods* (via `gopls implementations` / alt-click on a method name). There is no way to look at an interface type declaration and see which concrete types in the code base actually satisfy it. Users want an inline annotation (code lens) that surfaces implementers directly in the source file.  ### Functional requirements  1. **Code lens on interface declarations**    - When the cursor is inside (or on the name of) a named interface type declaration, `gopls` must display a code lens annotation summarizing the implementations of that interface, e.g. `3 implementations`.    - Expanding the lens must list each implementing type by name (qualified where needed), sorted deterministically (e.g. by package path then type name), with a maximum number of entries shown inline (the remainder summarized, e.g. `…and 5 more`).  2. **Navigation**    - Each listed implementer must be navigable: applying the lens entry jumps to the implementer's type declaration, positioned at the type name.    - Navigation must work across packages within the module and, where applicable, to types in dependencies.  3. **Correctness of implementation detection**    - A type counts as implementing an interface if it is a non-interface type (or interface type, when asked) whose method set is a superset of the interface's method set, using assignability rules.    - Detection must handle:      - embedded interfaces and embedded struct fields promoted into the method set,      - generic types and generic interfaces (with type parameters instantiated/substituted),      - type aliases and defined types based on other types,      - pointer vs. value receivers,      - types from imported packages in the same module and in dependencies.    - The lens must not be computed from stale data: results must reflect the current state of the workspace.  4. **Matching existing behavior**    - The set of types reported by the annotation must be consistent with the existing `gopls implementations` command applied to the interface's methods, so that a user finding one implementer by method search finds the same type in the annotation.  5. **Command/API surface**    - `gopls` must expose an operation to list the implementations of an *interface type* (not just a method), usable from the editor's "Go to Implementation"-style commands and from the command line, returning the list of implementing type declarations.    - The existing per-method implementation lookup must continue to work unchanged.  6. **Configuration and performance**    - The annotation must be disableable through a `gopls` setting (e.g. an `annotations`/`codelenses` option) and must be off or silent where it cannot be computed cheaply.    - Implementation lookup must be performed asynchronously and must not block or degrade the responsiveness of the editor; lenses are updated as the workspace changes.  7. **Non-goals / limits**    - The feature is an aid for discovery; it does not attempt to prove that non-implementing types will never implement the interface, and incomplete or ambiguous information is acceptable when types are not analyzable (e.g. due to build errors), provided the annotation is omitted rather than incorrect.

issue_title: reflect: NamedOf
requirement: **Requirement: Runtime Creation of Named Types via `reflect.NamedOf`**  The `reflect` package shall provide a function `NamedOf(pkgPath string, name string, underlying reflect.Type) reflect.Type` that returns a new defined (named) type at runtime.  1. **Inputs:**    - `pkgPath`: the package path identifying the type's origin. An empty string is permitted.    - `name`: a non-empty identifier for the type. An invalid identifier causes the function to panic with a descriptive message.    - `underlying`: a non-nil `reflect.Type` that serves as the underlying type. Interface types and named types are not permitted as the underlying type, and the function shall panic if either is supplied.  2. **Output:** A `reflect.Type` whose `Kind()` equals `underlying.Kind()`, whose `Name()` returns `name`, whose `PkgPath()` returns `pkgPath`, and whose underlying type is identical to `underlying`. The returned type is distinct from `underlying` and from any other named type.  3. **Identity:** Calling `NamedOf` repeatedly with the same `pkgPath`, `name`, and `underlying` shall return the same `reflect.Type` value, so that type comparisons using `==` succeed.  4. **Method set:** The created type has no methods. Methods cannot be attached through this function.  5. **Compatibility:** Values of the created type can be created with `reflect.New`, `reflect.Zero`, and `reflect.MakeSlice` (and similar constructors), and converted to and from the underlying type using `Value.Convert`, provided the conversion is valid under Go's assignability and conversion rules.  6. **Documentation:** The function's documentation shall state that the created type has no methods and that the type's identity is determined by the combination of `pkgPath`, `name`, and `underlying`.

issue_title: [Desktop] - Splash screen or background color customization
requirement: The desktop application shall allow users to customize the splash screen displayed during application startup by either selecting a custom background color (via color picker interface, hex code, or RGB input) or uploading a custom image file (supported formats: PNG, JPEG, SVG; maximum file size: 5 MB). These customization options shall be accessible through the application's Settings/Preferences menu, validated to reject invalid color codes or unsupported file formats with appropriate error messaging, persisted in local user configuration across application sessions, and applied during the startup sequence, with a "Reset to Default" function provided to restore the original splash screen appearance.

issue_title: Table > TableRow > TableCell colspan
requirement: Requirement: Support the colspan attribute on table cells within the Table component.  The Table, TableRow, and TableCell components must allow a TableCell to span multiple columns by accepting a colspan property. When colspan is set to a value greater than 1, the rendered cell must occupy that many columns in the table grid, and the table layout must remain aligned with the header and other rows. The default colspan must be 1, preserving existing behavior when the property is omitted. Invalid values (non-positive or non-integer) must be handled gracefully, either by falling back to 1 or by surfacing a clear error.

issue_title: Return attention weights in nn.Transformer
requirement: When invoking the `forward` method of `nn.Transformer`, `nn.TransformerEncoder`, and `nn.TransformerDecoder`, the API shall optionally return the per-layer attention weight matrices in addition to the output sequence. This shall be controlled by a boolean parameter (e.g., `need_weights`) that defaults to `False` to preserve backward compatibility. When enabled, the method shall return a tuple `(output, attention_weights)` where `attention_weights` is a list or tuple containing the attention matrices for each encoder layer, decoder self-attention layer, and decoder cross-attention layer (as applicable), with each matrix having shape `[batch_size, num_heads, target_sequence_length, source_sequence_length]`, enabling interpretability and visualization of token-to-token attention patterns.

issue_title: Add procedural and parametrizable audio support
requirement: **Requirement: Procedural and Parametrizable Audio Support**  **ID:** REQ-AUDIO-001 **Priority:** Should Have **Status:** Proposed  **Description** The system shall provide support for generating audio procedurally at runtime from user-defined parameters, without requiring pre-recorded audio assets. Audio generation shall be parametrizable so that output characteristics (such as pitch, frequency, amplitude, duration, waveform type, envelope, and modulation) can be controlled through a defined set of inputs, and changed during playback without restarting the audio stream.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **FR-1 Waveform Generation:** The system shall generate at least the following waveform types: sine, square, sawtooth, triangle, and white/pink noise. 2. **FR-2 Parameter Interface:** Each procedural audio source shall expose a named set of parameters (e.g., frequency, amplitude, phase, duty cycle, envelope attack/decay/sustain/release times) that can be set at creation and modified at runtime. 3. **FR-3 Real-Time Parameter Updates:** Parameter changes shall take effect within one audio buffer period (or less) without causing audible discontinuities such as clicks or pops. Smoothing (e.g., linear or exponential ramping over a configurable time) shall be applied to continuous parameters. 4. **FR-4 Modulation:** The system shall support modulating any numeric parameter with another procedural source (LFO or envelope) and with a parameter-driven control input. 5. **FR-5 Composition:** Procedural sources shall be composable, including mixing multiple sources and routing one source's output as the modulation input of another. 6. **FR-6 Determinism:** Given identical parameters, sample rate, and random seed, the system shall produce bit-identical output across runs on the same platform. 7. **FR-7 Serialization:** Procedural audio definitions (parameters, graph structure, and seed) shall be serializable to and deserializable from a human-readable format (e.g., JSON or YAML). 8. **FR-8 Integration:** Procedural audio shall integrate with the existing audio playback pipeline, including volume, panning, spatialization, and playback start/stop/pause controls, so that it is handled identically to file-based audio from the caller's perspective.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  1. **NFR-1 Performance:** Generating and mixing up to 32 concurrent procedural voices at a 48 kHz sample rate shall consume no more than 10% of one CPU core on the reference platform. 2. **NFR-2 Latency:** Parameter changes made from the main thread shall be applied on the audio thread without blocking it (lock-free or equivalent mechanism). 3. **NFR-3 Memory:** Procedural sources shall not preallocate sample buffers larger than the audio engine's configured block size. 4. **NFR-4 Sample Rate Independence:** Output shall be correct at all supported sample rates (minimum 22.05 kHz to 96 kHz), with frequency-based parameters expressed in Hz independent of sample rate.  **Acceptance Criteria**  - AC-1: A sine source at 440 Hz produces a spectrum with its dominant peak within ±1 Hz of 440 Hz, verified by FFT on rendered output. - AC-2: Changing frequency from 440 Hz to 880 Hz during playback produces no sample-to-sample discontinuity exceeding the configured smoothing tolerance. - AC-3: Rendering the same definition with the same seed twice yields byte-identical PCM output. - AC-4: A serialized definition loaded in a fresh session reproduces the same output as the original. - AC-5: An LFO modulating a sine source's amplitude at 5 Hz produces a measurable 5 Hz amplitude envelope in the output. - AC-6: The benchmark in NFR-1 passes on the reference platform and is included in the automated test suite. - AC-7: Procedural sources can be played, paused, stopped, panned, and spatialized using the same API calls used for file-based audio, with no API changes required for existing callers. - AC-8: Documentation includes a parameter reference for every built-in waveform and modulator, and at least one example definition.  **Out of Scope**  - Physical modeling synthesis, granular synthesis, and neural audio generation. - A graphical node editor (the requirement covers the programmatic and data-driven interface only). - Recording or exporting procedural output to disk (may be addressed in a follow-up requirement).

issue_title: Provide a means of turning iterators into fixed-size arrays
requirement: # Requirement: Convert Iterators into Fixed-Size Arrays  ## 1. Summary  The library shall provide a public, allocation-free API for materializing an iterator into a fixed-size array whose element count is known at compile time (referred to throughout this document as `Array<T, N>`, where `N` is a const-generic length). Users must be able to build such an array directly from any `IntoIterator`, with explicit, well-defined handling of length mismatches.  ## 2. Problem Statement  Currently, converting a sequence of elements into a fixed-size array requires the caller to:  - manually index into a mutable buffer and track a write cursor, - rely on `unsafe` pointer writes or `MaybeUninit` juggling, or - collect into a heap-allocated intermediate container (`Vec`, `Box<[T]>`, etc.) and then copy/convert into the fixed-size array.  All of these approaches are either unsafe, allocate on the heap, are verbose, or do not verify that the element count matches the array's declared size. There is no supported, safe, allocation-free way to express "take these `N` elements and give me a fixed-size array," which is needed whenever data arrives from an iterator (e.g., parsing, protocol decoding, numeric kernels, interop with C FFI structures) and the destination size is fixed by the type system or ABI.  ## 3. Scope and Assumptions  - The library exposes a fixed-size array type with a compile-time-known element count and length (const-generic `N`). - The conversion must not perform heap allocation. - The element type `T` and the length `N` are not known by this requirement; the API must be generic over both. - Existing invariants of `Array<T, N>` (length always exactly `N`, contiguous storage, `Drop` of contained elements) must be preserved. - This requirement covers construction from iterators only; it does not alter iteration, indexing, mutation, or comparison behavior of the existing type.  ## 4. Functional Requirements  **FR-1 — Construction from an iterator.** The library shall provide an associated constructor on the fixed-size array type that accepts any `IntoIterator`:  ```rust impl<T, const N: usize> Array<T, N> {     pub fn from_iter<I>(iter: I) -> Self     where         I: IntoIterator<Item = T>; } ```  **FR-2 — Length validation and mismatch behavior.** The constructor shall consume the iterator and verify that it yields exactly `N` elements.  - If the iterator yields **fewer** than `N` elements, the constructor shall fail with a clear panic (or an error, per FR-3) that reports the expected length and the actual number of elements produced. - If the iterator yields **more** than `N` elements, the constructor shall fail with a clear panic (or an error, per FR-3) that reports the expected length and the actual number of elements produced. Excess elements must still be dropped correctly (i.e., `Drop` implementations of `T` must run for any elements produced beyond `N`), and dropping must not cause a double-drop of the retained elements.  **FR-3 — Fallible variant.** The library shall provide a non-panicking counterpart that reports length mismatches as a typed error:  ```rust impl<T, const N: usize> Array<T, N> {     pub fn try_from_iter<I>(iter: I) -> Result<Self, ArrayFromIterError>     where         I: IntoIterator<Item = T>; }  pub enum ArrayFromIterError {     TooFew { expected: usize, actual: usize },     TooMany { expected: usize, actual: usize }, } ```  `ArrayFromIterError` shall implement `Debug`, `Display`, `std::error::Error`, `Clone`, `Copy`, `PartialEq`, and `Eq`.  **FR-4 — Interaction with the `FromIterator` / `TryFromIterator` traits.** The library shall implement the standard collection traits so that the idiomatic `collect()` form works:  - `impl<T, const N: usize> FromIterator<T> for Array<T, N>` — panics on length mismatch, consistent with the convention used by the standard library for fixed-size collections; it must not silently truncate or zero-fill. - If a dedicated `TryFromIterator` trait is not available in the target toolchain, `try_from_iter` (FR-3) is the sanctioned fallible entry point, and the `FromIterator` implementation shall document that it panics.  **FR-5 — Borrowed element sources.** The library shall support building an array from an iterator of references to `Copy` elements (e.g. `iter().copied()`, `&[T]`), either via a dedicated constructor or via a trait bound of the form `I::Item: Borrow<T>` such that no cloning beyond what the caller requests is performed.  **FR-6 — Known-length iterators.** When the iterator implements `ExactSizeIterator`, the implementation shall use the reported length to validate the element count up front (before consuming elements) and shall report a mismatch without first filling the array. The behavior on mismatch must be identical to the general case in FR-2/FR-3.  **FR-7 — Safety and memory correctness.** - The implementation shall not require `unsafe` code at the call site. - No element may be leaked, double-dropped, or left uninitialized. - The implementation shall not read or write outside the bounds of the array. - The implementation shall not allocate on the heap.  **FR-8 — Const-context support.** The library shall provide a `const fn` constructor usable in const evaluation that accepts an array-producing closure of the form `FnMut(usize) -> T` (equivalent to the standard library's `array::from_fn`), so that fixed-size arrays can still be built in const contexts where iterators are unavailable.  **FR-9 — Trait coherence.** `Array<T, N>` shall continue to satisfy all traits it currently implements (`Debug`, `Display` where applicable, `Clone`, `Copy` when `T: Copy`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `PartialOrd`, `Ord`, `Hash`, `Default` when `T: Default`, `Send`, `Sync`, `Unpin`, etc.). Adding the new APIs shall not introduce conflicting or overlapping trait implementations, and shall not break downstream users' trait bounds.  **FR-10 — Documentation.** The new APIs shall be documented with rustdoc including: a description of the length-mismatch behavior, a panic section (for the panicking variants), at least one worked example, and a `# Errors` section for the fallible variant.  ## 5. Non-Functional Requirements  - **Performance:** The conversion shall be zero-cost with respect to allocation: no heap allocation, no hidden buffering. For `Copy` element types the conversion should compile to a simple loop; the implementation should be benchmarked against a manual `MaybeUninit` fill to confirm no regression. - **Portability:** The implementation shall rely only on stable, portable Rust features; no architecture-specific or nightly-only APIs. - **MSRV:** The minimum supported Rust version shall not be increased by this feature, or, if const generics require a newer version, that change shall be documented in the changelog. - **Code quality:** The implementation shall be `unsafe`-free where practical, and any internal `unsafe` shall be `// SAFETY:` annotated and covered by `cargo miri` in CI. - **Consistency:** Naming, error types, and doc style shall match the conventions already used elsewhere in the library.  ## 6. Acceptance Criteria  1. `Array::from_iter` builds an array from `Vec`, arrays, ranges, and any custom `Iterator` yielding exactly `N` elements. 2. `Array::from_iter` on an iterator yielding `N - 1` elements panics with a message naming the expected and actual lengths; the partially built elements are dropped exactly once. 3. `Array::from_iter` on an iterator yielding `N + 1` elements panics with a message naming the expected and actual lengths; all produced elements are dropped exactly once. 4. `Array::try_from_iter` returns `Err(ArrayFromIterError::TooFew { .. })` / `Err(..::TooMany { .. })` for the same inputs, with correct `expected`/`actual` values, and `Ok` for an exact-length iterator. 5. The error type satisfies `std::error::Error` and is displayable as a human-readable message. 6. `let a: Array<u8, 4> = iter.collect();` compiles and behaves as specified in FR-4. 7. `Array::try_from_iter` on an `ExactSizeIterator` with an incorrect length reports the mismatch without consuming/validating elements one-by-one (verifiable by an iterator that increments a counter). 8. A `Drop`-tracking element type demonstrates no leaks and no double-drops in the success, too-few, and too-many cases. 9. No heap allocation occurs during conversion (verifiable via a custom global allocator that counts allocations). 10. A `const` array is constructible in a `const` context via the `const fn` constructor (FR-8). 11. Existing tests continue to pass; new unit tests cover all of the above, and the crate builds without new warnings under `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`.  ## 7. Non-Goals  - Building fixed-size arrays from a dynamically sized source with a runtime-determined length (that is the role of a growable/heap-backed type). - Changing the representation or layout of the existing fixed-size array type. - Providing iterator adapters (e.g., `map`/`filter` over the array's own elements) beyond what already exists. - Providing `unsafe` or "trust me" variants that skip length validation, unless already present in the library's API surface.

issue_title: Return index of the first visible item in ListView
requirement: The ListView shall provide a method or property to return the index of the first item currently visible in the viewport.

issue_title: Obfuscate GDScript in production export
requirement: The export system shall provide a configurable option to obfuscate GDScript code when generating production or release build exports.

issue_title: Using std::io::{Read, Write, Cursor} in a nostd environment
requirement: The library shall support `Read`, `Write`, and `Cursor` I/O traits and types when compiled in a `no_std` environment.

issue_title: Add array unpacking/destructuring to GDScript
requirement: GDScript shall support array destructuring (unpacking) syntax, enabling elements of an array to be unpacked and assigned directly to multiple distinct variables within assignment and variable declaration statements.

issue_title: cmd/go: 'go mod why' should have an answer for every module in 'go list -m all'
requirement: **Requirement: `go mod why` shall provide an explanation for every module reported by `go list -m all`**  **R1 (Coverage).** For every module M whose path appears in the output of `go list -m all`, invoking `go mod why` with M as an argument (in module mode, e.g., `go mod why -m M`) shall exit with status 0 and produce a non-empty dependency path that originates at the main module and terminates at M.  **R2 (Import-reachable modules).** When M is needed because one of its packages is imported, directly or transitively, by a package in the main module, the command shall report the package import chain, preserving the current output format.  **R3 (Module-graph-only modules).** When M is included in the build list solely through go.mod requirements of other modules (i.e., no package in the main module's import graph imports any of M's packages), the command shall report a chain of module requirements through the module graph — indicating which module's go.mod file requires which module — that originates at the main module and terminates at M. The command shall not, in this case, report that the main module does not need M.  **R4 (Message semantics).** The message "(main module does not need module X)" shall be produced only for module paths that do not appear in the build list (i.e., not in `go list -m all`) and for which no dependency path from the main module exists.  **R5 (Consistency invariant).** The set of modules for which `go mod why` produces an explanatory path shall be exactly equal to the set of modules printed by `go list -m all`. For every module M in `go list -m all`, the last element of the path reported by `go mod why -m M` shall be M.  **R6 (Multiple arguments).** When multiple module paths are supplied, the command shall independently produce a compliant explanation for each argument, consistent with current per-argument output behavior.  **R7 (Module graph modes).** The requirement shall hold in both pruned (Go 1.17+) and unpruned module graph configurations; in pruned mode the reported chain may be limited to information available in the pruned graph but must still account for every module in `go list -m all`.  **Acceptance criteria.** 1. For all M in `go list -m all`: `go mod why -m M` exits 0, and its output is a path from the main module to M (R1, R5). 2. No module in `go list -m all` receives a "does not need" response (R3, R4). 3. A regression test exists that iterates over the output of `go list -m all` and verifies criteria 1–2.

issue_title: Expo like tool for flutter
requirement: The tool shall provide an Expo-style managed workflow for Flutter, enabling developers to create and configure projects, preview them on iOS and Android devices with live reload, build and distribute signed applications through a hosted service, and deliver Dart code and asset updates over the air where platform policies permit.

issue_title: Add support for multiple displays/screens/monitors in Godot editor
requirement: ## Requirement: Multi-Monitor Support in the Godot Editor  The desktop Godot Editor shall support multi-monitor environments by:  - Detecting all connected displays and allowing users to select the target display for the main editor window, additional editor windows, and detached editor panels. - Allowing editor windows to be moved and resized across display boundaries, including placing different windows on different monitors simultaneously. - Providing a display-selection option when entering fullscreen mode. - Persisting each window’s target display, position, and size, and restoring that placement when the editor is reopened. - Repositioning windows whose saved display is no longer available so that their title bars, menus, and controls remain accessible. - Handling monitor connection, disconnection, resolution, and per-monitor scale changes without requiring an editor restart or causing off-screen windows, crashes, or incorrect mouse-input coordinates. - Using monitor-specific coordinate and scaling information when calculating window geometry.  This requirement applies to editor window management and shall not alter the runtime display behavior of projects.

issue_title: cmd/go: add 'go get' options to update direct and indirect dependencies separately
requirement: Requirement: Separate control of direct and indirect dependency updates in `go get`  The `go get` command shall provide options that allow users to update direct dependencies (those explicitly required by the main module) and indirect dependencies (those required only transitively) independently of one another.  Specifically:  1. A user shall be able to request updates limited to direct dependencies only, leaving indirect dependency versions unchanged unless required by the update. 2. A user shall be able to request updates limited to indirect dependencies only, leaving direct dependency versions unchanged. 3. The options shall be usable with the existing package patterns and version suffixes supported by `go get`, and shall not change behavior when they are not specified. 4. The resulting `go.mod` file shall reflect the selected updates, with `// indirect` annotations kept accurate for each requirement. 5. The command shall report an error for invalid combinations of options or arguments, and shall document the options in `go help get`.

issue_title: rustdoc support for per-parameter documentation
requirement: The `rustdoc` documentation tool shall support per-parameter documentation by parsing doc comments and attributes attached to individual parameters of functions, methods, closures, and function pointers, and rendering the parameter descriptions alongside their corresponding identifiers and types in generated documentation outputs (HTML and JSON), with optional compiler diagnostic lints to detect undocumented, mismatched, or nonexistent parameter names.

issue_title: Implement a Set primitive to complement Dictionary and Array
requirement: The system shall provide a Set primitive that maintains a collection of unique elements, complementing the existing Dictionary and Array primitives.

issue_title: rustdoc: `--enable-index-page` integration with cargo?
requirement: The system shall provide an option to pass the `--enable-index-page` flag to rustdoc when building documentation through cargo.

issue_title: Add a "Mask2D" node (and/or a "mask_parent" property for Sprite2D)
requirement: Implement a "Mask2D" node and/or a "mask_parent" property for the "Sprite2D" node to enable 2D masking and clipping of sprites.

issue_title: [Proposal] Data reading framework for PyTorch (Hive, MySQL, S3 etc.)
requirement: The system shall provide a unified, pluggable data reading framework for PyTorch that enables direct ingestion of training data from heterogeneous external data sources—including but not limited to Hive, MySQL, and Amazon S3—through a common API. The framework shall integrate with PyTorch's Dataset/DataLoader abstractions, allow users to declaratively specify what data to read (e.g., SQL queries or object store paths), support extensibility for additional backend connectors, and provide efficient, parallelizable (sharded and batched) reading suitable for large-scale and distributed training workloads.

issue_title: Return index of the first visible item in ListView
requirement: The system shall return the index of the first visible item in a ListView.

issue_title: Rework the Tilemap terrain system to improve its usability
requirement: The system shall rework the Tilemap terrain system to provide a more intuitive and user-friendly terrain authoring and editing experience.

issue_title: Parallel Associative Scan
requirement: The system shall provide a parallel associative scan (prefix scan) API that computes cumulative reductions across input sequences or multidimensional arrays along a specified axis. The implementation shall:  1. Support both inclusive and exclusive scan operations. 2. Accept any binary operator satisfying associativity ($a \circ (b \circ c) = (a \circ b) \circ c$), including standard arithmetic/logical operators and user-defined functions. 3. Execute concurrently across available parallel compute backends (multi-threaded CPU and/or GPU) using a work-efficient parallel scan algorithm with $O(N)$ total work and $O(\log N)$ step complexity. 4. Support arbitrary input sequence lengths, including non-power-of-two sizes, single-element collections, and empty inputs. 5. Provide support for both in-place and out-of-place array operations, accepting an optional identity element when executing exclusive scans.

issue_title: Zero-copy on shared memory of NVIDIA Jetson devices
requirement: The system shall support zero-copy data transfer using NVIDIA Jetson shared memory to reduce CPU overhead and improve performance.

issue_title: Add function to make paths absolute, which is different from canonicalization
requirement: Requirement: The system shall provide a function that converts a given path to an absolute path, distinct from the existing path canonicalization function.

issue_title: x/pkgsite: API for pkg.go.dev
requirement: The system shall provide a documented, versioned API that allows external clients to programmatically retrieve package information from pkg.go.dev.

issue_title: Implement `numpy.random.choice` equivalent
requirement: The system shall provide a function equivalent to `numpy.random.choice` for generating random samples.

issue_title: cmd/go: subcommand as git merge tool for go.mod merge conflicts
requirement: **Requirement: Add `go mod merge` subcommand to serve as a git merge driver for go.mod files**  **Description:** The `cmd/go` tool shall provide a new subcommand (e.g., `go mod merge`) that resolves merge conflicts in `go.mod` files, enabling it to be registered as a custom git merge driver.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **CLI Interface:** The command shall accept the standard git merge driver argument convention: `go mod merge <base> <current> <other>`, where `<base>` is the common ancestor version, `<current>` is the current branch's version, and `<other>` is the incoming branch's version of the go.mod file.  2. **Conflict Resolution:** The command shall semantically merge the three input go.mod files rather than performing line-based merging, correctly handling:    - Added, removed, and upgraded/downgraded module requirements in `require` blocks (including `// indirect` markers).    - Added or removed `replace`, `exclude`, and `retract` directives.    - Changes to the `go` directive (selecting the higher version when both sides change).    - Duplicate or conflicting entries by applying deterministic resolution rules consistent with MVS (Minimal Version Selection) semantics.  3. **Output:** The command shall write the merged result to the path given as the current file argument and exit with status 0 upon successful merge.  4. **Failure Handling:** If a semantic conflict cannot be resolved automatically, the command shall exit with a non-zero status and emit a diagnostic message identifying the conflicting directives, allowing git to fall back to manual conflict resolution.  5. **Documentation:** The command documentation shall include instructions for registering the merge driver via `git config` (e.g., `git config merge.gomod.driver "go mod merge %O %A %B"`) and associating it with go.mod files via `.gitattributes`.  **Non-Functional Requirements:**  1. The merge operation shall complete without network access and without modifying the module cache or any files other than the specified output file.  2. Merge results shall be deterministic: identical inputs shall always produce identical output, including directive ordering consistent with `go mod tidy` formatting conventions.

issue_title: Crate local state for procedural macros?
requirement: **Requirement: Crate-Local State for Procedural Macros**  Procedural macros must be able to store and retrieve state that is scoped to the crate currently being compiled. This state must:  1. Persist across multiple macro invocations within the same crate compilation session. 2. Be isolated from other crates, so one crate's macro state is not visible to or affected by another crate's expansions. 3. Be discarded or reset when compilation of that crate completes, so that state does not leak across separate compilations. 4. Be accessible through a stable, documented API available to procedural macro authors, without requiring global mutable state, external files, or environment variables.

issue_title: Implement method overloading in GDScript
requirement: **Requirement ID:** REQ-GDS-001 **Title:** Method Overloading in GDScript  **Statement:** The GDScript language shall support method overloading, allowing developers to declare multiple methods with the same name within a single class, provided each declaration has a distinct parameter signature (differing in the number of parameters or the declared type of at least one parameter). The engine shall select and invoke the correct overload based on the arguments supplied at the call site.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. The GDScript parser shall accept multiple method declarations with the same name in the same class if and only if their parameter lists differ in parameter count or in the declared type of at least one parameter. 2. Overload resolution shall be performed at compile time when all argument types are statically determinable; otherwise, resolution shall be performed at runtime using the actual argument types. 3. The most specific applicable overload shall be selected. Calls that are ambiguous (match multiple overloads equally) shall be rejected with a compile-time error; calls that match no overload shall produce a compile-time or runtime error identifying the class, method name, and supplied argument types. 4. Overloads shall integrate with inheritance: a subclass shall inherit all overloads defined by its superclass, may declare additional overloads, and may override an inherited overload's implementation without affecting other overloads of the same name. 5. Default parameter values shall be permitted within overload declarations and shall be accounted for during overload resolution. 6. Redeclaring a method with an identical signature shall remain a parse error.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - A GDScript class declaring two or more same-named methods with distinct parameter lists compiles and dispatches calls to the correct implementation. - Statically typed calls resolve at compile time; dynamically typed calls resolve correctly at runtime. - Ambiguous and unmatched calls produce clear, actionable error messages. - All previously valid GDScript projects continue to compile and execute without modification (backward compatibility).

issue_title: cmd/link: support msvc object files
requirement: ## Requirement: `cmd/link` support for MSVC object files  The Go linker (`cmd/link`) shall accept Microsoft Visual C++ (MSVC)-generated COFF object files (`.obj`) as linker inputs. It shall correctly process object sections, symbol definitions and references, and relocation records; combine MSVC objects with Go object files and other linker inputs; and resolve cross-object symbol references.  A successful link shall produce a valid executable or shared library containing the MSVC object code and data. Malformed objects or COFF constructs that the linker does not support shall result in an explicit diagnostic identifying the affected input file and the invalid or unsupported construct; the linker shall not silently omit such content.  Automated tests shall cover, at minimum, linking an MSVC-generated object containing code and data, cross-object symbol resolution and relocation, and rejection of malformed or unsupported input.

issue_title: compress/bzip2: implement bz2 encoder
requirement: Requirement: Implement a bzip2 compressor in the compress/bzip2 package.  Scope and behavior:  - Provide a streaming encoder that implements io.WriteCloser, wrapping an io.Writer and producing a valid bzip2 stream. - Expose a constructor (e.g., NewWriter) accepting an io.Writer and a compression level parameter (block size 1 to 9, corresponding to 100k to 900k blocks), with a default level when unspecified. - Output must be decodable by the existing compress/bzip2 reader and by the reference bzip2 tool. - The encoder must perform the standard bzip2 pipeline: initial run-length encoding (RLE1), Burrows-Wheeler transform, move-to-front transform, run-length encoding of zeros (RLE2), and Huffman coding with multiple tables selected per 50-symbol group, followed by the stream header, per-block CRC (CRC32 in bzip2's big-endian polynomial variant), and stream-level combined CRC. - Close must flush any buffered data, write the end-of-stream marker and combined CRC, and pad the final byte; it must not close the underlying writer. - Flush must emit pending data as a complete block without ending the stream. - Errors from the underlying writer must be propagated to the caller of Write, Flush, or Close. - Empty input must produce a valid empty bzip2 stream. - Behavior must be deterministic for identical input and level. - Include unit tests that round-trip data through the encoder and the existing decoder, and tests verifying interoperability with the system bzip2 tool where available, covering empty input, single-byte input, runs of repeated bytes, random data, and inputs spanning multiple blocks.
